entries.zh: 乃命衆軍卽日上道，沿江至建康，凡磯、浦、村落，軍行宿次、立頓處所，弘策逆爲圖測，皆在目中。
entries.en: He ordered the armies to march at once; from the river to Jiankang, every ford, beach, and hamlet where men camped or halted, Hongce had charted beforehand and held it all in mind.
entries.literal: He then ordered the host to march that very day; along the river to Jiankang, every ford, harbor, and village—where the army halted, encamped, or pitched its posts—Hongce had mapped in advance, all within his eye.

entries.zh: 義師至新林，王茂、曹景宗等於大航方戰，高祖遣弘策持節勞勉，衆咸奮厲。
entries.en: At Xinlin, Wang Mao and Cao Jingzong fought at the Great Crossing; Gaozu sent Hongce with staff to hearten them, and all fought the harder.
entries.literal: When the righteous army reached Xinlin, Wang Mao and Cao Jingzong were fighting at the Great Crossing; Gaozu sent Hongce with staff insignia to encourage them, and the host was everywhere roused.

entries.zh: 是日，仍破朱雀軍。
entries.en: That same day they broke the Vermilion Bird force again.
entries.literal: That day they again broke the Vermilion Bird army.

entries.zh: 高祖入頓石頭城，弘策屯門禁衛，引接士類，多全免。
entries.en: Gaozu encamped at Shitou; Hongce held the gates, received scholars and gentry, and saved many from harm.
entries.literal: Gaozu entered and encamped at Shitou city; Hongce garrisoned the gates in guard, received and guided men of rank, and many were wholly spared.

entries.zh: 城平，高祖遣弘策與呂僧珍先入清宮，封檢府庫。
entries.en: When the city fell, Gaozu sent Hongce and Lü Sengzhen first into the inner palace to seal the treasuries.
entries.literal: When the city was pacified, Gaozu sent Hongce and Lü Sengzhen ahead to clear the inner palace and seal and inspect the treasuries.

entries.zh: 于時城內珍寶委積，弘策申勒部曲，秋毫無犯。
entries.en: Treasures lay piled within the walls; Hongce forbade his men strictly, and nothing was touched.
entries.literal: At the time treasures within the walls lay heaped; Hongce strictly warned his command, and not a hair was taken.

entries.zh: 遷衛尉卿，加給事中。
entries.en: He was made commandant of the guards and also attendant within the yellow gates.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Commandant of the Guards, with additional appointment as Attendant Within the Yellow Gates.

entries.zh: 天監初，加散騎常侍，洮陽縣侯，邑二千二百戶。
entries.en: Early in Tianjian he was also made scattered cavalry attendant and marquis of Taoyang with two thousand two hundred households.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he was given additional title as Scattered Cavalry Attendant and Marquis of Taoyang county with a fief of two thousand two hundred households.

entries.zh: 弘策盡忠奉上，知無不爲，交友故舊，隨才薦拔，搢紳皆趨焉。
entries.en: Hongce served with full loyalty and left nothing undone; he raised friends and old ties by their gifts, and the gentry gathered to him.
entries.literal: Hongce gave loyal service above and knew nothing he would not do; with friends and old acquaintances he promoted each according to talent, and the gentry all flocked to him.

entries.zh: 時東昏餘黨初逢赦令，多未自安，數百人因運荻炬束仗，得入南北掖作亂，燒神虎門、總章觀。
entries.en: Dong Hun's remnant followers had just been pardoned and many still feared for their lives; several hundred, under cover of reed transport, smuggled torches and arms through the side gates, burned Shenhu Gate and Zongzhang View, and rose in revolt.
entries.literal: At the time the remnant partisans of Dong Hun had just received an amnesty and many were still uneasy; several hundred men, using reed transport, bundled torches and weapons, entered the Southern and Northern Side Gates to make trouble, burning Shenhu Gate and Zongzhang View.

entries.zh: 前軍司馬呂僧珍直殿內，以宿衛兵拒破之，盜分入衛尉府，弘策方救火，盜潛後害之，時年四十七。
entries.en: Front army chief clerk Lü Sengzhen held the inner palace with the night guard and broke them; robbers slipped into the commandant's quarters while Hongce fought the blaze—a thief crept behind and killed him. He was forty-seven.
entries.literal: Front Army Chief Clerk Lü Sengzhen was on duty within the palace and, with the night guard, repelled and broke them; the robbers split and entered the Commandant of the Guards' office—Hongce was then fighting the fire, and a robber stole behind and killed him, aged forty-seven.

entries.zh: 高祖深慟惜焉。
entries.en: Gaozu grieved for him bitterly.
entries.literal: Gaozu mourned him deeply.

entries.zh: 給第一區，衣一襲，錢十萬，布百匹，蠟二百斤。
entries.en: He granted a house in the first ward, a suit of robes, one hundred thousand cash, one hundred bolts of cloth, and two hundred jin of wax.
entries.literal: He granted one residence in the first ward, one suit of clothes, one hundred thousand cash, one hundred bolts of cloth, and two hundred jin of wax.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「亡從舅衛尉，慮發所忽，殞身祅豎。
entries.en: An edict said, "My late maternal uncle, commandant of the guards, was cut down in a careless hour by wicked men.
entries.literal: An edict said: "The late maternal uncle, Commandant of the Guards, was struck down in a moment of heedlessness by evil minions.

entries.zh: 其情理清貞，器識淹濟，自籓升朝，契闊夷阻。
entries.en: His mind was clear and his conduct straight; his talent ran deep; from the provinces he came to court and shared every trial.
entries.literal: His reason and bearing were pure and upright, his talent and insight broad and deep; from the provinces he rose to court, sharing hardship through distant trials.

entries.zh: 加外氏凋衰，饗嘗屢絕，興感《渭陽》，情寄斯在。
entries.en: My mother's kin had dwindled and rites were often broken; reading the Wei-yang, I fixed my heart on him.
entries.literal: Moreover, on my mother's side the line had withered and sacrifices were often broken; stirred by the 'Wei-yang' ode, my feeling rested on him.

entries.zh: 方賴忠勳，翼宣寡薄，報效無徵，永言增慟。
entries.en: I meant to lean on his loyal service to shore my slender reign; he answered with no sign, and my sorrow deepens.
entries.literal: I was about to rely on his loyal merit to support my slight virtue; he gave no sign of repayment, and my grief only grows.

entries.zh: 可贈散騎常侍、車騎將軍。
entries.en: Grant him posthumously scattered cavalry attendant and general of cavalry and chariots.
entries.literal: He may be posthumously granted Scattered Cavalry Attendant and General of Cavalry and Chariots.

entries.zh: 給鼓吹一部。
entries.en: Grant one suite of drums and pipes.
entries.literal: Grant one suite of drums and pipes.

entries.zh: 諡曰愍。」
entries.en: Posthumous name Lamented."
entries.literal: Posthumous name Lamented."

entries.zh: 五年秋，明帝崩，遺詔以高祖爲雍州刺史，乃表弘策爲錄事參軍，帶襄陽令。
entries.en: In autumn of year five Mingdi died; by his final edict Gaozu became inspector of Yongzhou and named Hongce recording secretary with concurrent charge of Xiangyang.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year Mingdi died; the testamentary edict made Gaozu inspector of Yongzhou, and he memorialized Hongce as Recording Secretary and concurrent magistrate of Xiangyang.

entries.zh: 高祖睹海內方亂，有匡濟之心，密爲儲備，謀猷所及，惟弘策而已。
entries.en: Gaozu saw chaos spread across the land and meant to rescue it; he stocked supplies in secret and weighed every plan with Hongce alone.
entries.literal: Gaozu saw the realm falling into disorder and bore a heart to set it right; he secretly made stores and laid plans—and in all of this only Hongce was consulted.

entries.zh: 時長沙宣武王罷益州還，仍爲西中郎長史，行郢州事。
entries.en: The Xuanwu Prince of Changsha had just left Yizhou and again held the Western Zhonglang long-term staff post, acting for Ying province.
entries.literal: At the time the Xuanwu Prince of Changsha had left Yizhou and returned, and again served as Western Zhonglang long-term staff officer with acting charge of Ying province affairs.

entries.zh: 高祖使弘策到郢，陳計于宣武王，語在《高祖紀》。
entries.en: Gaozu sent Hongce to Ying to present the plan to the prince, as told in the Annals of Gaozu.
entries.literal: Gaozu sent Hongce to Ying to lay the plan before the Xuanwu Prince—the account is in the Annals of Gaozu.

entries.zh: 弘策因說王曰：「昔周室旣衰，諸侯力爭，齊桓蓋中人耳，遂能一匡九合，民到于今稱之。
entries.en: Hongce urged the prince, "When Zhou waned, lords fought for power; Duke Huan of Qi was no more than an ordinary man, yet he united the realm nine times, and men still praise him.
entries.literal: Hongce then urged the prince: "When the Zhou house had declined, the feudal lords strove for power; Duke Huan of Qi was only a middling man, yet he was able to unite the realm in nine gatherings, and the people to this day praise him.

entries.zh: 齊德告微，四海方亂，蒼生之命，會應有主。
entries.en: Qi's virtue is spent; the four seas are in turmoil; the people must have their ruler.
entries.literal: Qi's virtue is nearly spent; the four seas are in disorder; the fate of the living must find its lord.

entries.zh: 以郢州居中流之要，雍部有戎馬之饒，卿兄弟英武，當今無敵，虎據兩州，參分天下，糾合義兵，爲百姓請命，廢昏立明，易於反掌。
entries.en: Ying lies at the midstream's hinge; Yong is rich in war-horses; you and your brother are heroes without peer—hold two provinces like tigers, split the realm, raise righteous arms, plead for the people, topple the dark and set up the bright: as easy as turning your palm.
entries.literal: Ying province stands at the heart of the midstream; Yong holds horses in abundance; you and your brother are heroic and unmatched today—tiger-like over two provinces, you may divide the realm, gather righteous troops, plead for the people, cast down the benighted and raise the enlightened: it is easier than turning the hand.

entries.zh: 如此，則桓、文之業可成，不世之功可建。
entries.en: Do that, and the deeds of Huan and Wen are yours, and glory beyond the age is within reach.
entries.literal: Thus the work of Huan and Wen may be achieved, and an unworldly merit established.

entries.zh: 無爲豎子所欺，取笑身後。
entries.en: Do not let some stripling fool you and make you a jest in later ages.
entries.literal: Do not be duped by a petty fellow and become a laughingstock after death.

entries.zh: 雍州揣之已熟，願善圖之。」
entries.en: Yongzhou has thought this through; plan wisely."
entries.literal: Yongzhou has weighed this to the full; I beg you to plan well."

entries.zh: 王頗不懌而無以拒也。
entries.en: The prince was ill pleased but could not refuse.
entries.literal: The prince was quite displeased yet had no way to refuse.

entries.zh: 永元末，高祖起兵，遣書招域。
entries.en: At the end of Yongyuan Gaozu rose in arms and wrote to summon Yu.
entries.literal: At the end of Yongyuan Gaozu rose in arms and wrote to summon Yu.

entries.zh: 西台建，以爲寧朔將軍，領行選，從高祖東下。
entries.en: When the western headquarters was set up, he was made pacify-the-north general with acting charge of selection and followed Gaozu east.
entries.literal: When the western headquarters was set up, he was made pacify-the-north general with acting charge of selection and followed Gaozu east.

entries.zh: 師次楊口，和帝遣御史中丞宗夬銜命勞軍。
entries.en: At Yangkou, Emperor He sent imperial censor Zong Guai to comfort the armies.
entries.literal: At Yangkou, Emperor He sent imperial censor Zong Guai to comfort the armies.

entries.zh: 域乃諷夬曰：「黃鉞未加，非所以總率侯伯。」
entries.en: Yu pressed Guai: "Without the yellow battle-ax you cannot command the lords."
entries.literal: Yu pressed Guai: "Without the yellow battle-ax you cannot command the lords."

entries.zh: 夬反西臺，卽授高祖黃鉞。
entries.en: Guai went back to the western headquarters, and the yellow battle-ax was given to Gaozu at once.
entries.literal: Guai went back to the western headquarters, and the yellow battle-ax was given to Gaozu at once.

entries.zh: 蕭穎胄旣都督中外諸軍事，論者謂高祖應致牋，域爭不聽，乃止。
entries.en: When Xiao Yingzhou became area commander of all armies, some said Gaozu should send a formal letter of submission; Yu objected and the idea was dropped.
entries.literal: When Xiao Yingzhou became area commander of all armies, some said Gaozu should send a formal letter of submission; Yu objected and the idea was dropped.

entries.zh: 郢城平。
entries.en: Ying city fell.
entries.literal: Ying city fell.

entries.zh: 域及張弘策議與高祖意合，卽命衆軍便下。
entries.en: Yu and Zhang Hongce argued as Gaozu wished, and the armies marched downstream at once.
entries.literal: Yu and Zhang Hongce argued as Gaozu wished, and the armies marched downstream at once.

entries.zh: 每獻謀畫，多被納用。
entries.en: Plans he offered were usually taken.
entries.literal: Plans he offered were usually taken.

entries.zh: 霸府初開，以爲諮議參軍。
entries.en: When the hegemon's headquarters opened, he became an advisory staff officer.
entries.literal: When the hegemon's headquarters opened, he became an advisory staff officer.

entries.zh: 天監初，封廣牧縣子，後軍司馬。
entries.en: Early in Tianjian he was made viscount of Guangmu and rear army chief clerk.
entries.literal: Early in Tianjian he was made viscount of Guangmu and rear army chief clerk.

entries.zh: 出爲寧朔將軍、巴西、梓潼二郡太守。
entries.en: He went out as pacify-the-north general and administrator of Brazil and Zitong.
entries.literal: He went out as pacify-the-north general and administrator of Brazil and Zitong.

entries.zh: 梁州長史夏侯道遷舉州叛降魏，魏騎將襲巴西，域固守百餘日，城中糧盡，將士皆齕草食土，死者太半，無有離心。
entries.en: Xiahou Daoqian, Liang's long-term staff officer, rebelled and surrendered the province to Wei; Wei cavalry struck Brazil; Yu held more than a hundred days; grain ran out and men ate grass and earth--more than half died--yet none wavered.
entries.literal: Xiahou Daoqian, Liang's long-term staff officer, rebelled and surrendered the province to Wei; Wei cavalry struck Brazil; Yu held more than a hundred days; grain ran out and men ate grass and earth--more than half died--yet none wavered.

entries.zh: 魏軍退，詔增封二百戶，進爵爲伯。
entries.en: When Wei withdrew, an edict added two hundred households to his fief and raised him to earl.
entries.literal: When Wei withdrew, an edict added two hundred households to his fief and raised him to earl.

entries.zh: 六年，卒於郡。
entries.en: In the sixth year, he died in the commandery.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, he died in the commandery.

entries.zh: 張弘策，字真簡，范陽方城人，文獻皇后之從父弟也。
entries.en: Zhang Hongce, styled Zhenjian, came from Fangcheng in Fanyang—a younger paternal cousin of Empress Wenxian.
entries.literal: Zhang Hongce, styled Zhenjian, was a native of Fangcheng in Fanyang, a younger paternal cousin of Empress Wenxian.

entries.zh: 幼以孝聞。
entries.en: As a boy he was known for filial devotion.
entries.literal: From childhood he was famed for filial piety.

entries.zh: 母嘗有疾，五日不食，弘策亦不食。
entries.en: When his mother fell ill she refused food for five days, and Hongce refused food as well.
entries.literal: Once when his mother fell ill, for five days she would not eat, and Hongce would not eat either.

entries.zh: 母強爲進粥，乃食母所餘。
entries.en: She made him swallow porridge; he ate only what remained of hers.
entries.literal: His mother forced him to take gruel; only then did he eat what she had left.

entries.zh: 遭母憂，三年不食鹽菜，幾至滅性。
entries.en: In mourning for his mother he took no salt or greens for three years, almost to death.
entries.literal: In mourning for his mother, for three years he ate neither salt nor vegetables, nearly to the point of destroying his life.

entries.zh: 兄弟友愛，不忍暫離，雖各有室，常同臥起，世比之姜肱兄弟。
entries.en: The brothers loved one another and hated to part even briefly; though each had a home, they usually slept and rose together—the age likened them to the Jiang Gong brothers.
entries.literal: The brothers were affectionate and could not bear brief separation; though each had his own household, they often slept and rose together, and the age compared them to the Jiang Gong brothers.

entries.zh: 起家齊邵陵王國常侍，遷奉朝請、西中郎江夏王行參軍。
entries.en: He began as an attendant in Qi's Prince of Shaoling kingdom, then became court attendant and acting staff officer to the Western Zhonglang General, Prince of Jiangxia.
entries.literal: He first entered office as Attendant of the Prince of Shaoling's kingdom in Qi, and was transferred to Court Attendant and Acting Staff Officer to the Western Zhonglang General, Prince of Jiangxia.

entries.zh: 高祖臨司州，命爲中兵參軍，領長流，因是厚自結附。
entries.en: When Gaozu held Sizhou, he made Shaoshu Middle Army Aide in charge of the long patrol, and Shaoshu thereafter attached himself closely.
entries.literal: When Gaozu took charge of Sizhou, he appointed Shaoshu Middle Army Aide, with charge of the long patrol, and from then on Shaoshu bound himself closely to him.

entries.zh: 高祖罷州還京師，謝遣賓客，紹叔獨固請願留。
entries.en: When Gaozu left the province for the capital and released his guests, Shaoshu alone insisted on remaining.
entries.literal: When Gaozu left the province and returned to the capital, he dismissed his guests with thanks; Shaoshu alone pressed hard to be allowed to stay.

entries.zh: 高祖謂曰：「卿才幸自有用，我今未能相益，宜更思他塗。」
entries.en: Gaozu told him, "Your talent will surely serve somewhere; I cannot help you yet. You should look elsewhere."
entries.literal: Gaozu said to him, "Your talent will surely find use; I cannot benefit you yet—you should seek another path."

entries.zh: 紹叔曰：「委質有在，義無二心。」
entries.en: Shaoshu said, "I have pledged myself. My loyalty knows no second allegiance."
entries.literal: Shaoshu said, "Having pledged myself, my loyalty admits no second heart."

entries.zh: 高祖固不許，於是乃還壽陽。
entries.en: Gaozu still refused, and Shaoshu went back to Shouyang.
entries.literal: Gaozu firmly would not agree, and so Shaoshu returned to Shouyang.

entries.zh: 刺史蕭遙昌苦引紹叔，終不受命。
entries.en: Inspector Xiao Yaochang pressed him repeatedly, yet Shaoshu never accepted command.
entries.literal: Inspector Xiao Yaochang pressed him hard to serve, but in the end Shaoshu would not accept the post.

entries.zh: 遙昌怒，將囚之，救解得免。
entries.en: Yaochang flew into a rage and meant to imprison him, but others intervened and he was spared.
entries.literal: Yaochang grew angry and was about to imprison him; rescue and mediation won his release.

entries.zh: 及高祖爲雍州刺史，紹叔間道西歸，補甯蠻長史、扶風太守。
entries.en: When Gaozu took Yongzhou, Shaoshu stole west by back roads and was made Chief of Ningman and Administrator of Fufeng.
entries.literal: When Gaozu became Inspector of Yongzhou, Shaoshu came west by hidden routes and was appointed Chief of Ningman and Administrator of Fufeng.

entries.zh: 東昏旣害朝宰，頗疑高祖。
entries.en: Once Donghun had slain the court's leading ministers, his suspicion of Gaozu deepened.
entries.literal: After Donghun had killed the chief ministers of state, he grew quite suspicious of Gaozu.

entries.zh: 紹叔兄植爲東昏直後，東昏遣至雍州，託以候紹叔，實潛使爲刺客。
entries.en: Shaoshu's brother Zhi was Donghun's rear-palace attendant; Donghun sent him to Yongzhou under the pretense of visiting Shaoshu, while secretly ordering him to kill Gaozu.
entries.literal: Shaoshu's elder brother Zhi served as Donghun's personal attendant in the rear palace; Donghun sent him to Yongzhou, ostensibly to visit Shaoshu, but in truth to set him on Gaozu as an assassin.

entries.zh: 紹叔知之，密以白高祖。
entries.en: Shaoshu learned the plot and secretly told Gaozu.
entries.literal: Shaoshu learned of it and secretly reported the matter to Gaozu.

entries.zh: 植旣至，高祖于紹叔處置酒宴之，戲植曰：「朝廷遣卿見圖，今日閑宴，是見取良會也。」
entries.en: When Zhi came, Gaozu feasted him at Shaoshu's house and said in jest, "The court sent you to kill me. This leisurely banquet is your finest opening."
entries.literal: When Zhi arrived, Gaozu set wine for him at Shaoshu's quarters and jested with Zhi, saying, "The court sent you to plot against me. Today's idle feast is your best chance to take me."

entries.zh: 賓主大笑。
entries.en: Host and guest burst out laughing.
entries.literal: Host and guest laughed aloud together.

entries.zh: 令植登臨城隍，周觀府署，士卒、器械、舟艫、戰馬，莫不富實。
entries.en: He sent Zhi up on the ramparts to tour the compound: troops, arms, boats, and horses were all lavishly supplied.
entries.literal: He had Zhi climb the city wall and look about the offices; soldiers, weapons, boats, and war-horses—nothing was not ample and strong.

entries.zh: 植退謂紹叔曰：「雍州實力，未易圖也。」
entries.en: On leaving, Zhi told Shaoshu, "Yongzhou is not a prize easily seized."
entries.literal: Zhi withdrew and said to Shaoshu, "Yongzhou's strength is not easily taken."

entries.zh: 紹叔曰：「兄還，具爲天子言之。
entries.en: Shaoshu said, "Go back and report all of this faithfully to the throne.
entries.literal: Shaoshu said, "Brother, when you return, tell the Son of Heaven everything plainly.

entries.zh: 兄若取雍州，紹叔請以此衆一戰。」
entries.en: If you come for Yongzhou, I will meet your army in open battle with these men."
entries.literal: If brother means to take Yongzhou, I ask only to meet your host with these troops in a single battle."

entries.zh: 送兄于南峴，相持慟哭而別。
entries.en: He sent his brother off at South Xian, and the two held each other, weeping, before they separated.
entries.literal: He saw his brother off at South Xian; they clung to each other and wept as they parted.

entries.zh: 義師起，爲冠軍將軍，改驍騎將軍，侍從東下江州，留紹叔監州事，督江、湘二州糧運，事無闕乏。
entries.en: When the righteous army rose, Shaoshu was made General of the Champions, then General of Valiant Cavalry; accompanying the eastern advance to Jiangzhou, he was left to oversee the province and supervise grain transport for Jiang and Xiang, without a single lapse.
entries.literal: When the righteous army rose, he was made General of the Champions, then changed to General of Valiant Cavalry; he followed east to Jiangzhou, while Shaoshu was left to oversee the province and supervise grain transport for Jiang and Xiang—nothing fell short.

entries.zh: 天監初，入爲衛尉卿。
entries.en: In early Tianjian he entered court as Minister of the Guards.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he entered the capital as Minister of the Guards.

entries.zh: 紹叔忠於事上，外所聞知，纖毫無隱。
entries.en: Shaoshu served with absolute loyalty; whatever reached him from outside, he concealed nothing.
entries.literal: Shaoshu was loyal in serving his lord; of all he heard abroad, not the slightest thread was hidden.

entries.zh: 每爲高祖言事，善則曰：「臣愚不及，此皆聖主之策。」
entries.en: When he reported good news to Gaozu, he said, "I am too dull for praise; this is the sagely lord's doing alone."
entries.literal: Whenever he spoke to Gaozu of affairs, if they went well he said, "I am too dull to deserve credit; these are all the sagely lord's measures."

entries.zh: 其不善，則曰：「臣慮出淺短，以爲其事當如是，殆以此誤朝廷，臣之罪深矣。」
entries.en: If matters went wrong, he said, "My judgment was shallow. I thought it should be done this way and nearly led the court astray. The fault is mine."
entries.literal: If they went ill, he said, "My counsel was shallow; I thought the matter should be thus, and nearly misled the court thereby—my fault is grave."

entries.zh: 高祖甚親信之。
entries.en: Gaozu cherished and relied on him utterly.
entries.literal: Gaozu trusted and favored him deeply.

entries.zh: 母憂去職。
entries.en: He left office to mourn his mother.
entries.literal: On his mother's death he left office for mourning.

entries.zh: 紹叔有至性，高祖常使人節其哭。
entries.en: Shaoshu's filial devotion ran deep; Gaozu repeatedly sent attendants to restrain his grief.
entries.literal: Shaoshu's nature was utmost in filial piety; Gaozu often sent men to moderate his weeping.

entries.zh: 頃之，起爲冠軍將軍、右軍司馬，封營道縣侯，邑千戶。
entries.en: Soon he returned as General of the Champions and Right Army Major, enfeoffed Marquis of Yingdao with a thousand-household fief.
entries.literal: Before long he was recalled as General of the Champions and Right Army Major, enfeoffed as Marquis of Yingdao with a fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 俄復爲衛尉卿，加冠軍將軍。
entries.en: He was soon again Minister of the Guards, also bearing the rank General of the Champions.
entries.literal: Shortly after he was again Minister of the Guards, with the additional title General of the Champions.

entries.zh: 以營道縣戶凋弊，改封東興縣侯，邑如故。
entries.en: As Yingdao's households had withered, his title was shifted to Marquis of Dongxing, the fief unchanged.
entries.literal: Because the households of Yingdao county were depleted and in distress, his enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Dongxing, the fief remaining as before.

entries.zh: 初，紹叔少失父，事母及祖母以孝聞，奉兄恭謹。
entries.en: From youth he had lost his father; he was famed for honoring mother and grandmother, and deferential toward his elder brother.
entries.literal: Earlier, Shaoshu had lost his father young; he served his mother and grandmother with a filial name, and toward his elder brother he was reverent and careful.

entries.zh: 及居顯要，祿賜所得及四方貢遺，悉歸之兄室。
entries.en: In high rank, every stipend, gift, and tribute went straight to his brother's house.
entries.literal: Once he stood in high office, his salary, gifts, and tribute from all quarters he sent entirely to his brother's household.

entries.zh: 六年，徵爲左將軍，加通直散騎常侍，領司、豫二州大中正。
entries.en: In year six he was recalled as Left General, also Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and chief rectifier of Si and Yu.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he was summoned as Left General, with the additional office Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and chief rectifier of Si and Yu provinces.

entries.zh: 紹叔至家疾篤。
entries.en: By the time Shaoshu reached home, he was desperately ill.
entries.literal: When Shaoshu reached home his illness was grave.

entries.zh: 詔於宅拜授，輿載還府，中使醫藥，一日數至。
entries.en: The throne invested him at his house, had him borne back to office in a litter, and sent physicians from court several times a day.
entries.literal: An edict appointed him at his dwelling; he was carried back to his office in a litter, and palace envoys with medicine came several times in a single day.

entries.zh: 七年，卒於府舍，時年四十五。
entries.en: In year seven he died at his government house, forty-five years old.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he died in his official residence, aged forty-five.

entries.zh: 高祖將臨其殯，紹叔宅巷狹陋，不容輿駕，乃止。
entries.en: Gaozu wished to visit the bier, but Shaoshu's alley was too cramped for the imperial coach, and he desisted.
entries.literal: Gaozu meant to attend his lying-in-state, but Shaoshu's lane and courtyard were too narrow for the imperial carriage, and so he stopped.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「追往念功，前王所篤；
entries.en: The edict said, "To honor the dead and reward merit is what former kings treasured;
entries.literal: The edict read: "To recall the dead and honor merit is what former kings held dear;

entries.zh: 在誠惟舊，異代同規。
entries.en: to hold fast to old loyalty across ages is one law for every dynasty.
entries.literal: to keep faith with the loyal across ages is the same rule in every time.

entries.zh: 通直散騎常侍、右衛將軍、東興縣開國侯紹叔，立身清正，奉上忠恪，契闊籓朝，情績顯著。
entries.en: Shaoshu, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Right Guard General, and founding Marquis of Dongxing, was upright in conduct and utterly loyal; from long service on the frontier his devotion and deeds shone clear.
entries.literal: Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Right Guard General, and Marquis of Dongxing, Shaoshu, stood upright and pure in person, loyal and earnest in serving his lord; through long service at the frontier court his merit and feeling were plain to see.

entries.zh: 爰及義始，寔立茂勳，作牧疆境，效彰所莅。
entries.en: From the first rising of the righteous cause he won great merit; governing the marches, his achievements where he served were evident.
entries.literal: From the righteous beginning he truly raised lofty achievement; as shepherd of the borderlands the good he wrought where he ruled was manifest.

entries.zh: 方申任寄，協贊心膂；
entries.en: He was on the verge of greater trust, to stand at the ruler's right hand;
entries.literal: He was just then to receive further trust and share in the work of the heart and backbone;

entries.zh: 奄至殞喪，傷痛於懷。
entries.en: when suddenly he fell—grief cuts to the bone.
entries.literal: suddenly he fell to death and ruin, and grief pierced the breast.

entries.zh: 宜加優典，隆茲寵命。
entries.en: Let him receive added honors and this lofty posthumous grace.
entries.literal: He should receive added honors and this exalted bestowal.

entries.zh: 可贈散騎常侍、護軍將軍，給鼓吹一部，東園秘器，朝服一具，衣一襲，凶事所須，隨由資給。
entries.en: Posthumously: Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General of the Guards, with one set of martial music, Eastern Garden burial vessels, one court robe, one suit of garments, and whatever the funeral required supplied as needed.
entries.literal: He may be posthumously made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General of the Guards, with one set of martial music, Eastern Garden secret rites, one court robe, one suit of garments, and whatever the funeral requires supplied as needed.

entries.zh: 諡曰忠。」
entries.en: His posthumous name was Loyal."
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Loyal."

entries.zh: 紹叔卒後，高祖嘗潸然謂朝臣曰：「鄭紹叔立志忠烈，善則稱君，過則歸己，當今殆無其比。」
entries.en: After Shaoshu died, Gaozu once told the court through tears, "Zheng Shaoshu lived for loyalty; in success he praised his lord, in failure he blamed himself. I doubt we shall see his like again."
entries.literal: After Shaoshu's death, Gaozu once said tearfully to the court, "Zheng Shaoshu set his will on loyal fierceness; when things went well he praised his lord, when they went ill he took the blame on himself—today there is scarcely his equal."

entries.zh: 其見賞惜如此。
entries.en: So deeply was he valued and mourned.
entries.literal: Such was the measure of his esteem and regret.

entries.zh: 子貞嗣。
entries.en: His son Zhen succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Zhen inherited the title.

entries.zh: 建武二年，魏大舉南侵，五道並進。
entries.en: In Jianwu year two, Wei invaded south on a great scale, five armies advancing together.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jianwu, Wei launched a great southern invasion on five routes at once.

entries.zh: 高祖率師援義陽，僧珍從在軍中。
entries.en: Gaozu marched to relieve Yiyang, and Sengzhen went with the host.
entries.literal: Gaozu led troops to relieve Yiyang; Sengzhen followed in the army.

entries.zh: 長沙宣武王時爲梁州刺史。
entries.en: The Prince of Changsha, the Xuanwu King, then held Liangzhou.
entries.literal: The Prince of Changsha, Xuanwu King, was then Inspector of Liangzhou.

entries.zh: 魏圍守連月，間諜所在不通，義陽與雍州路斷。
entries.en: Wei besieged month after month; no spy could get through, and the road from Yiyang to Yongzhou was severed.
entries.literal: Wei besieged for months on end; spies could not pass anywhere, and the road between Yiyang and Yongzhou was cut.

entries.zh: 高祖欲遣使至襄陽，求梁州問，衆皆憚，莫敢行，僧珍固請充使，卽日單舸上道。
entries.en: Gaozu meant to send someone to Xiangyang for news of Liangzhou; all shrank from the road, but Sengzhen insisted and that same day sailed alone upstream.
entries.literal: Gaozu wished to send an envoy to Xiangyang to seek word of Liangzhou; all feared the journey and none dared go, but Sengzhen pressed to go as envoy and that very day set out alone in a single boat.

entries.zh: 旣至襄陽，督遣援軍，且獲宣武王書而反，高祖甚嘉之。
entries.en: At Xiangyang he drove the relief forces, secured the Xuanwu King's letter, and returned; Gaozu commended him in the highest terms.
entries.literal: Once he reached Xiangyang he hurried the relief armies and also obtained the Xuanwu King's letter before returning; Gaozu praised him highly.

entries.zh: 事寧，補羽林監。
entries.en: After peace he was made Supervisor of the Forest of Feathers.
entries.literal: When the affair was settled, he was appointed Supervisor of the Forest of Feathers.

entries.zh: 東昏卽位，司空徐孝嗣管朝政，欲與共事，僧珍揣不久安，竟弗往。
entries.en: When Donghun succeeded, Xu Xiaosi ran the government and sought his help; Sengzhen guessed the ground would not hold and never went.
entries.literal: When Donghun took the throne, Minister of Works Xu Xiaosi managed court affairs and wished to work with him; Sengzhen judged that security would not last and in the end did not go.

entries.zh: 時高祖已臨雍州，僧珍固求西歸，得補邔令。
entries.en: Gaozu already held Yongzhou; Sengzhen begged to go west and was made Magistrate of Qi.
entries.literal: By then Gaozu already held Yongzhou; Sengzhen pressed hard to return west and was appointed Magistrate of Qi.

entries.zh: 旣至，高祖命爲中兵參軍，委以心膂。
entries.en: On arrival Gaozu made him Middle Army Aide and trusted him as his right hand.
entries.literal: Once he arrived, Gaozu appointed him Middle Army Aide and entrusted him as heart and backbone.

entries.zh: 僧珍陰養死士，歸之者甚衆。
entries.en: Sengzhen quietly gathered men who would die for him, and a great host rallied.
entries.literal: Sengzhen secretly nurtured men willing to die for him; those who came to him were very many.

entries.zh: 高祖頗招武猛，士庶響從，會者萬餘人，因命按行城西空地，將起數千間屋，以爲止舍，多伐材竹，沈於檀溪，積茅蓋若山阜，皆不之用。
entries.en: Gaozu drew fierce fighters until more than ten thousand gathered; he had the open ground west of the wall surveyed for thousands of lodgings, cut timber and bamboo and sank it in Tan Creek, and piled thatch into hillocks—yet used none of it.
entries.literal: Gaozu gathered many fierce fighters; scholars and commoners answered the call, and those who assembled were more than ten thousand. He therefore ordered a survey of open ground west of the city wall, intending to raise several thousand rooms as lodging, felling much timber and bamboo and sinking it in the Tanxi, heaping thatch in mounds like hills—all unused.

entries.zh: 僧珍獨悟其旨，亦私具櫓數百張。
entries.en: Sengzhen alone understood the plan and privately stockpiled hundreds of oars.
entries.literal: Sengzhen alone grasped the intent and on his own also prepared several hundred oars.

entries.zh: 義兵起，高祖夜召僧珍及張弘策定議，明旦乃會衆發兵，悉取檀溪材竹，裝爲艛艦，葺之以茅，並立辦。
entries.en: When the righteous army rose, Gaozu called Sengzhen and Zhang Hongce at night to decide; at dawn the host moved out, pulled up the Tanxi timber and bamboo, rigged them as warships roofed with thatch, and had all in an instant.
entries.literal: When the righteous army rose, Gaozu summoned Sengzhen and Zhang Hongce by night to fix the plan; at dawn he mustered the host and marched, taking all the Tanxi timber and bamboo, fitting it as war-boats and thatching them with straw—everything ready at once.

entries.zh: 衆軍將發，諸將果爭櫓，僧珍乃出先所具者，每船付二張，爭者乃息。
entries.en: As the armies prepared to sail, the generals fought over oars; Sengzhen brought out his hidden store, two oars per vessel, and the dispute died.
entries.literal: As the armies were about to march, the generals indeed quarreled over oars; Sengzhen then produced those he had prepared beforehand, giving two to each boat, and the quarrel ceased.

entries.zh: 高祖以僧珍爲輔國將軍、步兵校尉，出入臥內，宣通意旨。
entries.en: Gaozu made him Supporting-the-State General and Colonel of Footmen, entering the inner quarters to speak the ruler's mind.
entries.literal: Gaozu made Sengzhen Supporting-the-State General and Colonel of the Footmen; he went in and out of the sleeping quarters, conveying the lord's intent.

entries.zh: 師及郢城，僧珍率所領頓偃月壘，俄又進據騎城。
entries.en: At Ying, Sengzhen encamped his men at Crescent Fortress, then pressed forward and took Qicheng.
entries.literal: When the army reached Ying city, Sengzhen led his command to camp at the Crescent Fortress; soon after he advanced and seized Qicheng.

entries.zh: 郢州平，高祖進僧珍爲前鋒大將軍。
entries.en: After Ying fell, Gaozu promoted him to Grand General of the Vanguard.
entries.literal: When Yingzhou was pacified, Gaozu advanced Sengzhen to Grand General of the Vanguard.

entries.zh: 大軍次江寧，高祖令僧珍與王茂率精兵先登赤鼻邏。
entries.en: The army stopped at Jiangning; Gaozu sent Sengzhen and Wang Mao with elite troops to take the Red Nose picket first.
entries.literal: The great host halted at Jiangning; Gaozu ordered Sengzhen and Wang Mao to lead picked troops to seize the Red Nose picket first.

entries.zh: 其日，東昏將李居士與衆來戰，僧珍等要擊，大破之。
entries.en: That day Donghun's general Li Jushi brought his force to battle; Sengzhen intercepted and shattered them.
entries.literal: That day, Donghun's general Li Jushi came with his host to fight; Sengzhen and the others intercepted and broke them utterly.

entries.zh: 乃與茂進軍于白板橋築壘，壘立，茂移頓越城，僧珍獨守白板。
entries.en: He and Mao pushed to Whiteboard Bridge and built a fort; when it stood, Mao shifted to Yuecheng and Sengzhen held Whiteboard alone.
entries.literal: Then he and Mao advanced to Whiteboard Bridge and raised a fortress; once the ramparts stood, Mao moved his camp to Yuecheng while Sengzhen alone held Whiteboard.

entries.zh: 李居士密覘知衆少，率銳卒萬人，直來薄城。
entries.en: Li Jushi spied and saw how thin the garrison was; he led ten thousand elite men straight against the walls.
entries.literal: Li Jushi secretly reconnoitered and knew the defenders were few; he led ten thousand crack troops and came straight to press the wall.

entries.zh: 僧珍謂將士曰：「今力旣不敵，不可與戰；
entries.en: Sengzhen told the troops, "We are too few to fight them head-on;
entries.literal: Sengzhen told his officers and men, "Our strength cannot match them now; we must not give battle;

entries.zh: 亦勿遙射，須至塹裏，當並力破之。」
entries.en: and we must not loose arrows from afar. When they reach the ditch, we break them together."
entries.literal: nor shoot at them from afar—wait until they reach the moat, then strike with combined force and break them."

entries.zh: 俄而皆越塹拔柵，僧珍分人上城，矢石俱發，自率馬步三百人出其後，守隅者復踰城而下，內外齊擊，居士應時奔散，獲其器甲不可勝計。
entries.en: Soon they crossed the moat and wrenched down the stakes; Sengzhen put men on the wall with stones and arrows raining, led three hundred horse and foot around their rear, and had the corner guards leap down as well—inner and outer struck as one, Jushi fled instantly, and arms taken were beyond reckoning.
entries.literal: Before long they all crossed the ditch and tore up the palisade; Sengzhen sent men up on the wall, stones and arrows flying together, while he himself led three hundred horse and foot out behind them; the defenders on the corners also leaped down from the wall, and inner and outer struck together—Jushi scattered at once, and captured arms and armor beyond counting.

entries.zh: 僧珍又進據越城。
entries.en: Sengzhen pressed on and took Yuecheng.
entries.literal: Sengzhen again advanced and seized Yuecheng.

entries.zh: 東昏大將王珍國列車爲營，背淮而陣。
entries.en: Donghun's great general Wang Zhenguo formed chariot encampments with his back to the Huai.
entries.literal: Donghun's great general Wang Zhenguo drew up chariots as camps, with their backs to the Huai in battle array.

entries.zh: 王茂等衆軍擊之，僧珍縱火車焚其營。
entries.en: Wang Mao and the allied armies struck; Sengzhen rolled fire-chariots against the camps and burned them.
entries.literal: Wang Mao and the other hosts attacked; Sengzhen sent fire-chariots to burn their camps.

entries.zh: 卽日瓦解。
entries.en: That same day the enemy host dissolved.
entries.literal: That same day the enemy lines collapsed.

entries.zh: 建康城平，高祖命僧珍率所領先入清宮，與張弘策封檢府庫，卽日以本官帶南彭城太守，遷給事黃門侍郎，領虎賁中郎將。
entries.en: When Jiankang fell, Gaozu had Sengzhen lead his men first into the inner palace; with Zhang Hongce he sealed and checked the treasury. That day he kept his rank as acting Nan Pengcheng administrator, was made Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate, and held the Tiger guards colonelcy.
entries.literal: When Jiankang was pacified, Gaozu ordered Sengzhen to lead his troops first into the inner palace; with Zhang Hongce he sealed and inspected the treasury. That same day he kept his current post as acting Administrator of Nan Pengcheng, was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate, and concurrently Colonel of the Valiant Cavalry of the Tiger guards.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，以爲冠軍將軍、前軍司馬，封平固縣侯，邑一千二百戶。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, he was made Champion General and front army marshal, enfeoffed as Marquis of Pinggu with twelve hundred households.
entries.literal: When Gaozu accepted the abdication, he was made Champion General and front army marshal, enfeoffed as Marquis of Pinggu district with a fief of twelve hundred households.

entries.zh: 尋遷給事中、右衛將軍。
entries.en: Soon he became Attending Within and Right Guard General.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Attending Within and Right Guard General.

entries.zh: 頃之，轉左衛將軍，加散騎常侍，入直秘書省，總知宿衛。
entries.en: Before long he became Left Guard General, was made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, took regular duty in the Secretariat, and oversaw the palace guard.
entries.literal: Before long he was transferred to Left Guard General, added Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, entered regular duty at the Secretariat, and had overall charge of palace guard service.

entries.zh: 天監四年冬，大舉北伐，自是軍機多事，僧珍晝直中書省，夜還秘書。
entries.en: In winter of Tianjian year 4 the court launched a major northern campaign; military business piled up, and Sengzhen spent his days at the Central Secretariat and his nights back at the Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the winter of the fourth year of Tianjian a great northern campaign was launched; from then on military affairs multiplied, and Sengzhen by day was on duty at the Central Secretariat and by night returned to the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 五年夏，又命僧珍率羽林勁勇出梁城。
entries.en: In summer of year 5 he was again ordered to lead crack Feathered Forest troops from Liangcheng.
entries.literal: In the summer of the fifth year he was again ordered to lead elite Feathered Forest troops out from Liangcheng.

entries.zh: 其年冬旋軍，以本官領太子中庶子。
entries.en: That winter the army came home; he kept his post and was made concurrent crown prince's assistant in the palace.
entries.literal: That winter the army returned; he kept his current post and was made concurrent Crown Prince's Assistant in the Palace.

entries.zh: 僧珍去家久，表求拜墓。
entries.en: Long away from home, Sengzhen petitioned to visit his family graves.
entries.literal: Sengzhen had been away from home long and submitted a memorial asking to visit his ancestral tombs.

entries.zh: 高祖欲榮之，使爲本州，乃授使持節、平北將軍、南兗州刺史。
entries.en: Gaozu meant to honor him with his home province and appointed him Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the North, and Southern Yanzhou inspector.
entries.literal: Gaozu wished to honor him and made him governor of his native province, granting him Bearer of the Staff with credentials, General Who Pacifies the North, and Southern Yanzhou Inspector.

entries.zh: 僧珍在任，平心率下，不私親戚。
entries.en: In office Sengzhen was even-handed with subordinates and never favored relatives.
entries.literal: In office Sengzhen treated subordinates fairly and showed no favor to kin.

entries.zh: 從父兄子先以販蔥爲業，僧珍旣至，乃棄業欲求州官。
entries.en: A son of his father's elder brother had sold scallions for a living; when Sengzhen came to the province, the man quit the trade to seek an official post.
entries.literal: His father's elder brother's son had earlier made his living selling scallions; when Sengzhen arrived, he abandoned the trade to seek a provincial post.

entries.zh: 僧珍曰：「吾荷國重恩，無以報效，汝等自有常分，豈可妄求叨越，但當速反蔥肆耳。」
entries.en: Sengzhen said, "I owe the state a heavy debt I cannot repay; you each have your proper place—how can you seek promotion rashly? Go back to your scallion stall at once."
entries.literal: Sengzhen said: "I bear the state's heavy grace and have no means to repay it; you each have your proper station—how can you rashly seek to overstep? You should quickly return to the scallion shop."

entries.zh: 僧珍舊宅在市北，前有督郵廨，鄉人咸勸徒廨以益其宅。
entries.en: Sengzhen's old house stood north of the market, with the postal inspector's office in front; neighbors all urged moving the office to enlarge his home.
entries.literal: Sengzhen's old house stood north of the market; before it was the postal inspector's office, and fellow townsmen all urged moving the office to enlarge his residence.

entries.zh: 僧珍怒曰：「督郵官廨也，置立以來，便在此地，豈可徙之益吾私宅！」
entries.en: Sengzhen snapped, "The postal inspector's office is a government building; it has stood here since it was built—how can you move it to enlarge my private house!"
entries.literal: Sengzhen said angrily: "The postal inspector's office is a government building; since it was established it has stood here—how can it be moved to enlarge my private house!"

entries.zh: 姊適于氏，住在市西，小屋臨路，與列肆雜處，僧珍常導從鹵簿到其宅，不以爲恥。
entries.en: His elder sister had married a Yu and lived west of the market in a little house on the street amid the shops; Sengzhen often led his full guard escort to her door and felt no shame.
entries.literal: His elder sister had married into the Yu clan and lived west of the market in a small house facing the road, mixed among shop stalls; Sengzhen often led his full guard retinue to her home and was not ashamed.

entries.zh: 在州百日，徵爲領軍將軍，尋加散騎常侍，給鼓吹一部，直秘書省如先。
entries.en: After a hundred days in the province he was recalled as Commandant of the Guards, soon made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, given ceremonial drums and pipes, and kept his Secretariat duty as before.
entries.literal: After a hundred days in the province he was summoned as Commandant of the Guards; soon he was added Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, given one set of ceremonial drums and pipes, and held Secretariat duty as before.

entries.zh: 僧珍有大勳，任總心膂，恩遇隆密，莫與爲比。
entries.en: Sengzhen had great merit, stood at the heart of power, and enjoyed favor so close that none could match him.
entries.literal: Sengzhen had great merit, held overall charge of the ruler's inner circle, and enjoyed favor so dense that none could compare.

entries.zh: 性甚恭慎，當直禁中，盛暑不敢解衣。
entries.en: Deeply respectful and cautious by nature, on palace duty he would not loosen his clothes even in fierce summer heat.
entries.literal: By nature he was very respectful and cautious; when on duty in the palace, even in great heat he dared not loosen his clothing.

entries.zh: 每侍御座，屏氣鞠躬，果食未嘗舉箸。
entries.en: Whenever he attended the throne he held his breath and bowed low; he never once touched the fruit set before him.
entries.literal: Whenever he attended the imperial seat he held his breath and bowed; he never once raised his chopsticks to the fruit set before him.

entries.zh: 嘗因醉後，取一柑食之。
entries.en: Once, drunk, he took a mandarin and ate it.
entries.literal: Once, when drunk, he took a mandarin orange and ate it.

entries.zh: 高祖笑謂曰：「便是大有所進。」
entries.en: Gaozu laughed and said, "That is real progress."
entries.literal: Gaozu laughingly said to him: "That is a great advance."

entries.zh: 祿俸之外，又月給錢十萬；
entries.en: Beyond his salary he also received a hundred thousand cash a month;
entries.literal: Beyond his salary he was also given a hundred thousand cash each month;

entries.zh: 其餘賜賚不絕于時。
entries.en: and other gifts and rewards never stopped.
entries.literal: other gifts and rewards were unceasing.

entries.zh: 十年，疾病，車駕臨幸，中使醫藥，日有數四。
entries.en: In year 10 he fell ill; the emperor came in person, and palace envoys brought medicine several times daily.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he fell ill; the imperial carriage visited him, and palace emissaries brought medicine several times a day.

entries.zh: 僧珍語親舊曰：「吾昔在蒙縣，熱病髮黃，當時必謂不濟，主上見語，『卿有富貴相，必當不死，尋應自差』，俄而果愈。
entries.en: Sengzhen told kin, "Once in Meng county I had fever and turned yellow and was sure I would die. His Majesty said, 'You have a nobleman's look—you will not die and will soon recover'—and I did.
entries.literal: Sengzhen told relatives and friends: "I was once in Meng county with fever and turned yellow; then I surely thought I would not survive. The lord said to me, 'You have the look of wealth and rank—you will surely not die and should soon recover on your own'—and indeed I soon recovered.

entries.zh: 今已富貴而復髮黃，所苦與昔正同，必不復起矣。」
entries.en: Now that I am wealthy and honored I have turned yellow again with the same illness as then—I will not get up again."
entries.literal: Now, having wealth and rank, I have turned yellow again; the affliction is exactly the same as before—I surely will not rise again."

entries.zh: 竟如其言。
entries.en: In the end it was as he said.
entries.literal: In the end it was as he said.

entries.zh: 卒於領軍府舍，時年五十八。
entries.en: He died at the Commandant of the Guards residence at fifty-eight.
entries.literal: He died at the Commandant of the Guards residence, aged fifty-eight.

entries.zh: 高祖卽日臨殯，詔曰：「思舊篤終，前王令典；
entries.en: Gaozu came to the mourning hall that same day. The edict said, "Cherishing the old and honoring the dead is the ancient kings' model;
entries.literal: Gaozu that same day came to the mourning hall. The edict said: "Thinking fondly of the old and honoring the end—the former kings' fine model;

entries.zh: 追榮加等，列代通規。
entries.en: adding posthumous glory is the rule of every age.
entries.literal: pursuing glory with added rank—the rule of every dynasty.

entries.zh: 散騎常侍、領軍將軍、平固縣開國侯僧珍，器思淹通，識宇詳濟，竭忠盡禮，知無不爲。
entries.en: Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commandant of the Guards, and Marquis of Pinggu Sengzhen had broad talent and penetrating thought, detailed knowledge and accomplished bearing, gave exhaustive loyalty and full ritual, and left nothing undone.
entries.literal: Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commandant of the Guards, and Marquis of Pinggu district Sengzhen—his talent and thought were broad and penetrating, his knowledge and bearing detailed and accomplished; he exhausted loyalty and full ritual and knew nothing he would not do.

entries.zh: 與朕契闊，情兼屯泰。
entries.en: He shared our hardships, his heart holding both hard times and good.
entries.literal: With us in shared hardship, his feelings embraced both adversity and ease.

entries.zh: 大業初構，茂勳克舉。
entries.en: When the great enterprise was first raised, he won splendid merit.
entries.literal: When the great undertaking was first built, splendid merit was achieved.

entries.zh: 及居禁衛，朝夕盡誠。
entries.en: In palace guard service he gave his utmost morning and evening.
entries.literal: When he held palace guard duty, morning and evening he gave full sincerity.

entries.zh: 方參任台槐，式隆朝寄；
entries.en: Just as he was to take his place among the highest ministers and bear the court's heavy trust,
entries.literal: Just as he was to share responsibility at the high ministries and elevate the court's trust,

entries.zh: 奄致喪逝，傷慟于懷。
entries.en: he suddenly died—grief filled our hearts.
entries.literal: he suddenly met death and loss—grief filled the breast.

entries.zh: 宜加優典，以隆寵命。
entries.en: Let superior rites be added to honor his service.
entries.literal: Superior rites should be added to exalt the favored mandate.

entries.zh: 可贈驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司，常侍、鼓吹、侯如故。
entries.en: Posthumously grant him General of Fast Cavalry and an office equal to the Three Excellencies in staff; his cavalier attendant rank, drums and pipes, and marquisate remain as before.
entries.literal: He may posthumously be granted General of Fast Cavalry and Office equaling the Three Excellencies in Staff; Cavalier Attendant, drums and pipes, and marquisate as before.

entries.zh: 給東園秘器，朝服一具，衣一襲，喪事所須，隨由備辦。
entries.en: Grant eastern-garden funeral vessels, one court robe, and one suit of clothes; prepare whatever the funeral requires.
entries.literal: Eastern garden secret vessels are given, one set of court robes and one suit of clothes; whatever the funeral requires shall be prepared as needed.

entries.zh: 諡曰忠敬侯。」
entries.en: Posthumous title: Loyal and Respectful Marquis."
entries.literal: Posthumous title: Marquis Zhongjing."

entries.zh: 高祖痛惜之，言爲流涕。
entries.en: Gaozu grieved deeply and wept as he spoke.
entries.literal: Gaozu grieved deeply and spoke with tears streaming.

entries.zh: 長子峻早卒，峻子淡嗣。
entries.en: His eldest son Jun died young; Jun's son Dan inherited.
entries.literal: His eldest son Jun died early; Jun's son Dan succeeded.

entries.zh: 張弘策
entries.en: Zhang Hongce
entries.literal: Zhang Hongce

entries.zh: 柳惔 弟忱 席闡文 韋叡 族弟愛
entries.en: Liu Tan; his younger brother Chen; Xi Chanwen; Wei Rui; and clan cousin Ai
entries.literal: Liu Tan; younger brother Chen; Xi Chanwen; Wei Rui; clan cousin Ai

entries.zh: 柳惔，字文通，河東解人也。
entries.en: Liu Tan, styled Wentong, came from Jie in Hedong.
entries.literal: Liu Tan, styled Wentong, was a native of Jie in Hedong.

entries.zh: 父世隆，齊司空。
entries.en: His father Shilong had been Qi's minister of works.
entries.literal: His father Shilong was Minister of Works in Qi.

entries.zh: 惔年十七，齊武帝爲中軍，命爲參軍，轉主簿。
entries.en: At seventeen, with Emperor Wu of Qi as central army commander, Tan became his retainer, then chief clerk.
entries.literal: At seventeen, when Emperor Wu of Qi was Central Army commander, Tan was appointed a retainer, then transferred to chief clerk.

entries.zh: 齊初，入爲尚書三公郎，累遷太子中舍人，巴東王子響友。
entries.en: Early in Qi he entered the secretariat as three-ducal attendant, rose to crown prince gentleman companion, and was made Friend of the Prince of Badong, Zi Xiang.
entries.literal: Early in Qi he entered the Masters of Writing as attendant of the Three Ducal Officials, rose through posts to crown prince gentleman companion, and became Friend of the Prince of Badong, Zi Xiang.

entries.zh: 子響爲荊州，惔隨之鎮。
entries.en: When Zi Xiang went to Jing province, Tan followed him there.
entries.literal: When Zi Xiang took Jing province, Tan followed him to the post.

entries.zh: 子響昵近小人，惔知將爲禍，稱疾還京。
entries.en: Zi Xiang clung to petty men; Tan foresaw ruin, claimed illness, and went back to the capital.
entries.literal: Zi Xiang doted on petty men; Tan saw disaster coming, feigned illness, and returned to the capital.

entries.zh: 及難作，惔以先歸得免。
entries.en: When trouble came, Tan escaped because he had returned first.
entries.literal: When the crisis broke, Tan was spared because he had left early.

entries.zh: 歷中書侍郎，中護軍長史。
entries.en: He was gentleman of the secretariat and long-term staff officer to the central guard.
entries.literal: He served as gentleman of the Secretariat and long-term staff officer to the Central Guard.

entries.zh: 出爲新安太守，居郡，以無政績，免歸。
entries.en: He went out as Xin'an prefect, achieved nothing in office, and was sent home.
entries.literal: He went out as prefect of Xin'an; in the commandery he achieved nothing and was dismissed.

entries.zh: 久之，爲右軍諮議參軍事。
entries.en: Long afterward he became an advisory staff officer of the right army.
entries.literal: After a long interval he became advisory staff officer to the Right Army.

entries.zh: 建武末，爲西戎校尉、梁南秦二州刺史。
entries.en: At the end of Jianwu he was western rong colonel and inspector of Liang and Southern Qin.
entries.literal: At the end of Jianwu he was made Colonel of the Western Rong and inspector of Liang and Southern Qin provinces.

entries.zh: 及高祖起兵，惔舉漢中應義。
entries.en: When Gaozu rose in arms, Tan raised Hanzhong for the cause.
entries.literal: When Gaozu raised the army, Tan raised Hanzhong in support of the righteous cause.

entries.zh: 和帝卽位，以爲侍中，領前軍將軍。
entries.en: Emperor He made him attendant within and acting front army general.
entries.literal: When Emperor He took the throne, Tan was made Attendant Within and given acting charge as Front Army General.

entries.zh: 高祖踐阼，徵爲護軍將軍，未拜，仍遷太子詹事，加散騎常侍。
entries.en: Gaozu summoned him as protector of the army; before he took the post he became heir apparent household head and scattered cavalry attendant.
entries.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Tan was summoned as Protector of the Army General; before he accepted he was transferred to Household Head of the Heir Apparent with additional appointment as Scattered Cavalry Attendant.

entries.zh: 論功封曲江縣侯，邑千戶。
entries.en: For merit he was made marquis of Qujiang with one thousand households.
entries.literal: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qujiang with a fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 高祖因讌爲詩以貽惔曰：「爾實冠羣后，惟餘實念功。」
entries.en: At a feast Gaozu wrote a poem for Tan: "You alone crown the lords; only you keep my deeds in mind."
entries.literal: At a banquet Gaozu composed a poem and gave it to Tan, saying: "You truly crown the feudal lords; only you truly remember my merit."

entries.zh: 又嘗侍座，高祖曰：「徐元瑜違命嶺南，《周書》罪不相及，朕已宥其諸子，何如？」
entries.en: Another time at court Gaozu said, "Xu Yuanyu rebelled in Lingnan. The Book of Zhou says punishment does not chain to kin—I have pardoned his sons. What say you?"
entries.literal: On another occasion, while attending him, Gaozu said: "Xu Yuanyu defied orders in Lingnan—the Book of Zhou says crimes do not reach kin. I have already pardoned his sons. What do you think?"

entries.zh: 惔對曰：「罰不及嗣，賞延于世，今復見之聖朝。」
entries.en: Tan answered, "Punishment stops at the man; reward flows to his line—we see that again in this sage reign."
entries.literal: Tan replied: "Punishment does not reach heirs; reward extends through generations—today we see it again in the sage court."

entries.zh: 時以爲知言。
entries.en: Men called it words that knew the times.
entries.literal: The age regarded it as perceptive speech.

entries.zh: 尋遷尚書右僕射。
entries.en: He was soon made right vice director of the masters of writing.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 天監四年，大舉北伐，臨川王宏都督衆軍，以惔爲副。
entries.en: In Tianjian year four the court launched a great northern campaign; the Prince of Linchuan, Hong, commanded the armies with Tan as deputy.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Tianjian a great northern campaign was launched; the Prince of Linchuan, Hong, commanded the massed armies, with Tan as his deputy.

entries.zh: 軍還，復爲僕射。
entries.en: When the armies came home he was again vice director.
entries.literal: When the army returned, he again became vice director.

entries.zh: 以久疾，轉金紫光祿大夫，加散騎常侍，給親信二十人。
entries.en: Long illness moved him to golden crown and purple light grandee, scattered cavalry attendant, and twenty trusted retainers.
entries.literal: Because of long illness he was transferred to Golden Crown and Purple Light Grandee with additional appointment as Scattered Cavalry Attendant and twenty trusted retainers.

entries.zh: 未拜，出爲使持節、安南將軍、湘州刺史。
entries.en: Before he took office he went out with credentials as pacify-the-south general and Xiangzhou inspector.
entries.literal: Before he accepted the post he went out as envoy with credentials, Pacify the South General, and inspector of Xiang province.

entries.zh: 六年十月，卒于州，時年四十六。
entries.en: In the tenth month of year six he died in the province at forty-six.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of the sixth year he died in the province, aged forty-six.

entries.zh: 高祖爲素服舉哀。
entries.en: Gaozu wore undyed robes and mourned him.
entries.literal: Gaozu wore plain robes and raised lament for him.

entries.zh: 贈侍中、撫軍將軍，給鼓吹一部。
entries.en: Posthumously he was attendant within and pacify-the-army general, with one suite of drums and pipes.
entries.literal: He was posthumously granted Attendant Within and Pacify the Army General, with one suite of drums and pipes.

entries.zh: 諡曰穆。
entries.en: Posthumous name Mu.
entries.literal: Posthumous name: Mu.

entries.zh: 惔著《仁政傳》及諸詩賦，粗有辭義。
entries.en: Tan wrote Record of Benevolent Government and poems and fu with modest literary force.
entries.literal: Tan wrote the Record of Benevolent Government and various poems and rhapsodies, all with some literary merit.

entries.zh: 子照嗣。
entries.en: His son Zhao inherited the title.
entries.literal: His son Zhao succeeded him.

entries.zh: 忱字文若，惔第五弟也。
entries.en: Chen, styled Wenruo, was Tan's fifth brother.
entries.literal: Chen, styled Wenruo, was Tan's fifth younger brother.

entries.zh: 年數歲，父世隆及母閻氏時寢疾，忱不解帶經年。
entries.en: Still a child, he tended his father Shilong and mother Lady Yan through long illness without undoing his belt for a year.
entries.literal: When he was only a few years old, his father Shilong and his mother, Lady Yan, lay ill; Chen went without loosening his belt for a full year.

entries.zh: 及居喪，以毀聞。
entries.en: In mourning his grief was famed for wrecking his body.
entries.literal: In mourning he was famed for destroying his health.

entries.zh: 起家爲司徒行參軍，累遷太子中舍人，西中郎主簿，功曹史。
entries.en: He began on the minister of education's staff, rose to crown prince gentleman companion, western Zhonglang chief clerk, and merit-records officer.
entries.literal: He first entered office as a retainer on the Minister of Education's staff, rose through posts to crown prince gentleman companion, Western Zhonglang chief clerk, and merit-records officer.

entries.zh: 惔第四弟憕，亦有美譽，歷侍中、鎮西長史。
entries.en: Tan's fourth brother Cheng was also praised; he was attendant within and pacify-the-west long-term staff officer.
entries.literal: Tan's fourth younger brother Cheng also enjoyed a fine reputation; he served as Attendant Within and long-term staff officer to Pacify the West.

entries.zh: 天監十二年，卒，贈寧遠將軍、豫州刺史。
entries.en: In Tianjian year twelve he died and was posthumously pacify-the-distant general and Yuzhou inspector.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year of Tianjian he died; posthumously he was granted Pacify the Distant General and inspector of Yu province.

entries.zh: 齊東昏遣巴西太守劉山陽由荊襲高祖，西中郎長史蕭穎胄計未有定，召忱及其所親席闡文等夜入議之。
entries.en: Dong Hun sent Brazil prefect Liu Shanyang from Jing against Gaozu; Xiao Yingzhou, western Zhonglang long-term staff officer, had no plan yet and called Chen, Xi Chanwen, and others to a night council.
entries.literal: Dong Hun sent Liu Shanyang, prefect of Brazil, from Jing to strike Gaozu; the Western Zhonglang long-term staff officer Xiao Yingzhou had not settled on a plan and summoned Chen and his intimate Xi Chanwen and others to enter by night to discuss it.

entries.zh: 忱曰：「朝廷狂悖，爲惡日滋。
entries.en: Chen said, "The court is deranged and wicked, and its crimes swell daily.
entries.literal: Chen said: "The court is mad and wicked; its evils grow day by day.

entries.zh: 頃聞京師長者，莫不重足累息；
entries.en: Lately I hear that in the capital the old and honored dare not breathe aloud;
entries.literal: Of late I hear that elders in the capital—none do not walk on tiptoe, holding their breath;

entries.zh: 今幸在遠，得假日自安。
entries.en: we are lucky to be distant and may steal a day's peace.
entries.literal: we are fortunate to be far away and may take a day to rest in safety.

entries.zh: 雍州之事，且藉以相斃耳。
entries.en: As for Yongzhou, for now let it kill them for us.
entries.literal: The Yongzhou affair—let us for now rely on it to destroy one another.

entries.zh: 獨不見蕭令君乎？
entries.en: Have you not seen Commander Xiao?
entries.literal: Have you alone not seen Commander Xiao?

entries.zh: 以精兵數千，破崔氏十萬衆，竟爲羣邪所陷，禍酷相尋。
entries.en: A few thousand elite troops broke Cui's hundred thousand, yet villains trapped him and ruin followed ruin.
entries.literal: With a few thousand crack troops he shattered Cui's force of a hundred thousand, yet in the end was trapped by a pack of villains, calamity heaped upon calamity.

entries.zh: 前事之不忘，後事之師也。
entries.en: What came before, if remembered, teaches what comes after.
entries.literal: What is past and not forgotten is the teacher of what follows.

entries.zh: 若使彼凶心已逞，豈知使君不系踵而及？
entries.en: If their evil will is satisfied, do you think our lord will not be chained next?
entries.literal: If their wicked hearts have already had their way, do you suppose our lord will not be next in chains?

entries.zh: 且雍州士銳糧多，蕭使君雄姿冠世，必非山陽所能擬；
entries.en: Yongzhou has sharp troops and full granaries; Commander Xiao's heroism tops the age—Liu Shanyang cannot compare;
entries.literal: Moreover Yongzhou's soldiers are sharp and its grain abundant; Commander Xiao's heroic bearing crowns the age—he is surely not someone Liu Shanyang can match;

entries.zh: 若破山陽，荊州復受失律之責。
entries.en: break Liu Shanyang and Jingzhou again pays for failure in arms.
entries.literal: if you defeat Liu Shanyang, Jingzhou will again bear blame for losing discipline.

entries.zh: 進退無可，且深慮之。」
entries.en: Advance or retreat, there is no road—think hard on this."
entries.literal: Whether you advance or retreat there is no way—ponder this deeply."

entries.zh: 闡文亦深勸同高祖。
entries.en: Xi Chanwen too pressed hard for alliance with Gaozu.
entries.literal: Xi Chanwen also urged joining Gaozu in depth.

entries.zh: 穎胄乃誘斬山陽，以忱爲寧朔將軍。
entries.en: Yingzhou baited and killed Shanyang and made Chen pacify-the-north general.
entries.literal: Yingzhou then lured and killed Shanyang and made Chen Pacify the North General.

entries.zh: 高祖踐阼，以忱爲五兵尚書，領驍騎將軍。
entries.en: Gaozu made him minister of the five armies and acting valiant cavalry general.
entries.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Chen was made Minister of the Five Armies and given acting charge as Valiant Cavalry General.

entries.zh: 論建義功，封州陵伯，邑七百戶。
entries.en: For founding merit he was baron of Zhouling with seven hundred households.
entries.literal: For merit in founding the righteous cause he was enfeoffed as Baron of Zhouling with a fief of seven hundred households.

entries.zh: 天監二年，出爲安西長史、冠軍將軍、南郡太守。
entries.en: In Tianjian year two he was pacify-the-west long-term staff officer, champion general, and Nan commandery prefect.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianjian he went out as long-term staff officer to Pacify the West, Champion General, and prefect of Nan commandery.

entries.zh: 六年，徵爲員外散騎常侍、太子右衛率。
entries.en: In year six he was summoned as extraordinary scattered-cavalry attendant and heir apparent right guard commandant.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he was summoned as Extraordinary Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.

entries.zh: 未發，遷持節、督湘州諸軍事、輔國將軍、湘州刺史。
entries.en: Before he left he became credentialed envoy, Xiang military supervisor, supporting state general, and Xiangzhou inspector.
entries.literal: Before he set out he was transferred to envoy with credentials, supervisor of military affairs in Xiang province, Supporting State General, and inspector of Xiang province.

entries.zh: 八年，坐輒放從軍丁免。
entries.en: In year eight he was removed for freeing conscripts without leave.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he was dismissed for releasing conscript soldiers on his own authority.

entries.zh: 俄入爲秘書監，遷散騎常侍，轉祠部尚書，未拜遇疾，詔改授給事中、光祿大夫，疾篤不拜。
entries.en: Soon he was secretariat director, then scattered-cavalry attendant, then minister of sacrifices; illness came before he took office and an edict made him palace supervisor and splendid-light grandee, but he was too ill to accept.
entries.literal: Soon he entered the court as Director of the Secretariat, was transferred to Scattered Cavalry Attendant, then Minister of Sacrifices—but before he accepted he fell ill; an edict changed his appointment to Supervisor of the Palace and Grandee of Splendid Light; his illness was severe and he did not accept.

entries.zh: 十年，卒於家，時年四十一。
entries.en: In year ten he died at home at forty-one.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he died at home, aged forty-one.

entries.zh: 追贈中書令，諡曰穆。
entries.en: Posthumously he was director of the secretariat; posthumous name Mu.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was granted Director of the Secretariat; posthumous name: Mu.

entries.zh: 子範嗣。
entries.en: His son Fan inherited the line.
entries.literal: His son Fan succeeded him.

entries.zh: 席闡文，安定臨涇人也。
entries.en: Xi Chanwen came from Linjing in Anding.
entries.literal: Xi Chanwen was a native of Linjing in Anding.

entries.zh: 少孤貧，涉獵書史。
entries.en: Orphaned and poor in youth, he read widely in books and histories.
entries.literal: Orphaned young and poor, he ranged widely through books and histories.

entries.zh: 齊初，爲雍州刺史蕭赤斧中兵參軍，由是與其子穎胄善。
entries.en: Early in Qi he was central army retainer to Yongzhou inspector Xiao Chifu and grew close to his son Yingzhou.
entries.literal: Early in Qi he was a central army retainer to Xiao Chifu, inspector of Yong province, and through this became close to Chifu's son Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 復歷西中郎中兵參軍，領城局。
entries.en: He later was western Zhonglang central army retainer and held the city bureau.
entries.literal: He later served as central army retainer in the Western Zhonglang headquarters and held charge of the city bureau.

entries.zh: 高祖之將起義也，闡文深勸之，穎胄同焉，仍遣田祖恭私報高祖，并獻銀裝刀，高祖報以金如意。
entries.en: As Gaozu prepared to rise, Chanwen urged him hard; Yingzhou agreed and sent Tian Zugong secretly to Gaozu with a silver-mounted knife—Gaozu answered with a gold ruyi.
entries.literal: When Gaozu was about to raise the righteous army, Chanwen urged him deeply; Yingzhou agreed and sent Tian Zugong in secret to report to Gaozu, also presenting a silver-mounted knife—Gaozu replied with a gold ruyi scepter.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，除都官尚書、輔國將軍。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne Chanwen was minister of punishments and supporting state general.
entries.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Chanwen was made Minister of Punishments and Supporting State General.

entries.zh: 封山陽伯，邑七百戶。
entries.en: He was baron of Shanyang with seven hundred households.
entries.literal: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Shanyang with a fief of seven hundred households.

entries.zh: 出爲東陽太守，又改封湘西，戶邑如故。
entries.en: He went out as Dongyang prefect, then was re-enfeoffed as baron of Xiangxi with the same fief.
entries.literal: He went out as prefect of Dongyang and was later re-enfeoffed as Baron of Xiangxi, his household fief unchanged.

entries.zh: 視事二年，以清白著稱，卒於官。
entries.en: In two years in office his integrity was famed; he died there.
entries.literal: In two years of office he was famed for integrity and died in his post.

entries.zh: 詔賻錢三萬，布五十匹。
entries.en: An edict granted thirty thousand cash and fifty bolts of cloth.
entries.literal: An edict granted thirty thousand cash and fifty bolts of cloth for his funeral.

entries.zh: 諡曰威。
entries.en: Posthumous name Wei.
entries.literal: Posthumous name: Wei.

entries.zh: 宋永光初，袁顗爲雍州刺史，見而異之，引爲主簿。
entries.en: In Song's first Yongguang year Yuan Yan was Inspector of Yongzhou; he saw Rui, marveled, and made him chief clerk.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongguang of Song, Yuan Yan was Inspector of Yongzhou; he saw Rui and was struck with wonder, and took him as chief clerk.

entries.zh: 顗到州，與鄧琬起兵，叡求出爲義成郡，故免顗之禍。
entries.en: Yan reached his post and rose with Deng Wan; Rui secured an exit as administrator of Yicheng and missed Yan's downfall.
entries.literal: When Yan reached his province he joined Deng Wan in raising troops; Rui asked to go out as Administrator of Yicheng and so escaped the ruin that overtook Yan.

entries.zh: 後爲晉平王左常侍，遷司空桂陽王行參軍，隨齊司空柳世隆守郢城，拒荊州刺史沈攸之。
entries.en: He became regular attendant to the Prince of Jinping, then staff officer to the Prince of Guiyang under the Minister of Works, and followed Liu Shilong in the defense of Yingcheng against Shen Youzhi.
entries.literal: Later he was Regular Attendant to the Prince of Jinping, then a staff officer on the Prince of Guiyang's suite under the Minister of Works; he followed Qi Minister of Works Liu Shilong in holding Yingcheng against Jingzhou Inspector Shen Youzhi.

entries.zh: 攸之平，遷前軍中兵參軍。
entries.en: After Youzhi's defeat he was made army aide of the van.
entries.literal: When Youzhi was pacified, he was promoted to Army Aide of the Van.

entries.zh: 久之，爲廣德令。
entries.en: In time he became magistrate of Guangde.
entries.literal: After some time he was made magistrate of Guangde.

entries.zh: 累遷齊興太守、本州別駕、長水校尉、右軍將軍。
entries.en: He advanced through administrator of Qixing, provincial aide, colonel of the Long River, and general of the right.
entries.literal: He rose repeatedly to Administrator of Qixing, provincial aide of his native prefecture, Colonel of the Long River, and General of the Right.

entries.zh: 齊末多故，不欲遠鄉里，求爲上庸太守，加建威將軍。
entries.en: Qi's last days were full of upheaval; he did not wish to leave his native hills and asked for Shangyong, with the added title general who establishes might.
entries.literal: At the end of Qi turmoil was everywhere; unwilling to leave his home country, he asked to be Administrator of Shangyong, with the additional rank General Who Establishes Might.

entries.zh: 俄而太尉陳顯達、護軍將軍崔慧景頻逼京師，民心遑駭，未有所定，西土人謀之於叡。
entries.en: Soon Chen Xianda and Cui Huijing harried the capital repeatedly; fear ran wild and the west turned to Rui for a plan.
entries.literal: Before long Grand Marshal Chen Xianda and Protector of the Army Cui Huijing pressed the capital again and again; the people's hearts were frantic and nothing was settled, and the men of the western lands looked to Rui for counsel.

entries.zh: 叡曰：「陳雖舊將，非命世才；
entries.en: Rui said, "Chen is a veteran, yet not a man born for the times;
entries.literal: Rui said, "Chen is an old commander, but no man of the age;

entries.zh: 崔頗更事，懦而不武。
entries.en: Cui has weathered many storms, yet he is soft and no soldier.
entries.literal: Cui has seen much, but he is timid and no warrior.

entries.zh: 其取赤族也，宜哉！
entries.en: They deserve the extinction of their houses—of course they do!
entries.literal: That their clans should be wiped to the last man is only fitting!

entries.zh: 天下真人，殆興於吾州矣。」
entries.en: The man Heaven favors will probably rise from our province."
entries.literal: The true lord of the realm will likely rise from our province."

entries.zh: 乃遣其二子，自結於高祖。
entries.en: With that he sent his two sons to bind themselves to Gaozu.
entries.literal: He then sent his two sons to attach themselves to Gaozu.

entries.zh: 義兵檄至，叡率郡人伐竹爲筏，倍道來赴，有衆二千，馬二百匹。
entries.en: The call to arms came; Rui had his district cut bamboo rafts, marched night and day, and arrived with two thousand foot and two hundred horse.
entries.literal: When the righteous army's manifesto arrived, Rui led the people of his command to cut bamboo for rafts, came by forced marches, and brought two thousand men and two hundred horses.

entries.zh: 高祖見叡甚悅，拊几曰：「他日見君之面，今日見君之心，吾事就矣。」
entries.en: Gaozu rejoiced at the sight of him and smote the table: "I might have met your face another day; today I meet your heart—my work is done."
entries.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased when he saw Rui and struck the table, saying, "Another day I would have seen your face; today I see your heart—my cause is assured."

entries.zh: 義師克郢、魯，平加湖，叡多建謀策，皆見納用。
entries.en: The righteous army took Ying and Lu and pacified Jiahu; Rui's counsel was offered at every turn and taken.
entries.literal: The righteous army took Ying and Lu, pacified Jiahu Lake, and Rui offered many plans, all of which were adopted.

entries.zh: 大軍發郢，謀留守將，高祖難其人；
entries.en: The host marched from Ying and debated a garrison commander; Gaozu could find no fit man.
entries.literal: When the great army set out from Ying, they debated who should stay to guard it; Gaozu found no man equal to the task.

entries.zh: 久之，顧叡曰：「棄騏驥而不乘，焉遑遑而更索？」
entries.en: At length he looked at Rui and said, "To abandon a stallion and go begging for another mount—what sort of hurry is that?"
entries.literal: After a long while he turned to Rui and said, "To leave a thoroughbred unmounted and go running about for another—what folly is that?"

entries.zh: 卽日以爲冠軍將軍、江夏太守，行郢府事。
entries.en: That day he was made general of the champions, administrator of Jiangxia, and acting head of the Ying prefecture.
entries.literal: That same day he was made General of the Champions, Administrator of Jiangxia, and acting governor of the Ying prefecture.

entries.zh: 初，郢城之拒守也，男女口垂十萬，閉壘經年，疾疫死者十七八，皆積屍於床下，而生者寢處其上，每屋輒盈滿。
entries.en: When Ying had been besieged, nearly a hundred thousand people were trapped inside for a year; plague killed seven or eight in ten—they piled the dead beneath the beds and slept above, house after house packed to the rafters.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Ying city had held out under siege, the population within the walls had neared a hundred thousand; the gates were shut for a year, and of plague and sickness seven or eight in ten died—corpses were heaped under the beds while the living slept above them, and every house was packed full.

entries.zh: 叡料簡隱恤，咸爲營理，於是死者得埋藏，生者反居業，百姓賴之。
entries.en: Rui sorted the neglected and the suffering and set everything right; the dead were buried, the living went back to their work, and the people lived by his hand.
entries.literal: Rui sifted the hidden cases and showed compassion; he had all of it put in order, so the dead were buried and the living returned to their trades—the people relied on him.

entries.zh: 梁臺建，徵爲大理。
entries.en: When the Liang platform rose he was called to be grand judge.
entries.literal: When the Liang regime was established he was summoned as Grand Judge.

entries.zh: 高祖卽位，遷廷尉，封都梁子，邑三百戶。
entries.en: At Gaozu's accession he became minister of justice, enfeoffed viscount of Duliang with three hundred households.
entries.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, Rui was made Minister of Justice and enfeoffed as Viscount of Duliang with a fief of three hundred households.

entries.zh: 天監二年，改封永昌，戶邑如先。
entries.en: In Tianjian year 2 he was re-enfeoffed as Yongchang, fief and households unchanged.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianjian his enfeoffment was changed to Yongchang, the households and fief as before.

entries.zh: 東宮建，遷太子右衛率，出爲輔國將軍、豫州刺史、領歷陽太守。
entries.en: The eastern palace rose; he became right commandant of the crown prince's guard, then went out as general who assists the state, inspector of Yuzhou, and administrator of Liyang.
entries.literal: When the Eastern Palace was established he was made Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, then went out as General Who Assists the State, Inspector of Yuzhou, and concurrent Administrator of Liyang.

entries.zh: 三年，魏遣衆來寇，率州兵擊走之。
entries.en: In year 3 Wei raided; he led the province's soldiers and beat them back.
entries.literal: In the third year Wei sent armies to raid; he led the provincial troops and drove them off.

entries.zh: 四年，王師北伐，詔叡都督衆軍。
entries.en: In year 4 the court marched north; Rui was ordered to command the armies.
entries.literal: In the fourth year the imperial army marched north; an edict made Rui commander-in-chief of the massed forces.

entries.zh: 叡遣長史王超宗、梁郡太守馮道根攻魏小峴城，未能拔。
entries.en: He sent chief clerk Wang Chaozong and Liangjun administrator Feng Daogen against Xiaokeng; they failed to crack the walls.
entries.literal: Rui sent Chief Clerk Wang Chaozong and Administrator of Liangjun Feng Daogen to attack the Wei fort of Xiaokeng, but they could not take it.

entries.zh: 叡巡行圍柵，魏城中忽出數百人陳於門外，叡欲擊之，諸將皆曰：「向本輕來，未有戰備，徐還授甲，乃可進耳。」
entries.en: Rui toured the encirclement; hundreds of Wei soldiers burst from the gate and drew up outside. He meant to hit them, but his officers said, "We came lightly, without armor—fall back, arm, then fight."
entries.literal: Rui walked the siege lines; several hundred men suddenly sallied from the Wei city and formed ranks outside the gate. Rui meant to strike them, but the generals all said, "We came light, without battle gear—withdraw, arm, and then advance."

entries.zh: 叡曰：「不然。
entries.en: Rui said, "No.
entries.literal: Rui said, "Not so.

entries.zh: 魏城中二千餘人，閉門堅守，足以自保，無故出人於外，必其驍勇者也，若能挫之，其城自拔。」
entries.en: Two thousand-odd men behind barred gates can hold that place. If they come out without reason, these are their bravest; crush them and the city will take itself."
entries.literal: Within the Wei city are a little more than two thousand men, shut in behind closed gates—enough to hold themselves. For them to come out without cause means these must be their fiercest fighters; if we break them, the city will fall of itself.

entries.zh: 衆猶遲疑，叡指其節曰；
entries.en: The army still hung back; Rui pointed to his command baton and said:
entries.literal: The host still hesitated; Rui pointed to his staff of command and said:

entries.zh: 「朝廷授此，非以爲飾，韋叡之法，不可犯也。」
entries.en: "The throne gave me this, not for show. Wei Rui's law is not to be broken."
entries.literal: "The court gave this—not for ornament. Wei Rui's law admits no breach."

entries.zh: 乃進兵。
entries.en: He marched.
entries.literal: He advanced.

entries.zh: 士皆殊死戰，魏軍果敗走，因急攻之，中宿而城拔。
entries.en: The soldiers fought to the death; Wei broke and ran, and he pressed hard—before midnight the walls were his.
entries.literal: The men fought as if each meant to die; the Wei army broke and fled, and he pressed the assault—by midnight the city was his.

entries.zh: 遂進討合肥。
entries.en: Then he moved against Hefei.
entries.literal: He then marched to invest Hefei.

entries.zh: 先是，右軍司馬胡略等至合肥，久未能下，叡按行山川，曰：「吾聞『汾水可以灌平陽，絳水可以灌安邑』，卽此是也。」
entries.en: Hu Lue and the rest had besieged Hefei without success. Rui walked the ground and said, "They say 'the Fen flooded Pingyang and the Jiang flooded Anyi'—here is the same trick."
entries.literal: Earlier, Right Army Major Hu Lue and others had reached Hefei but long could not reduce it. Rui surveyed the rivers and hills and said, "I have heard that the Fen can flood Pingyang and the Jiang can flood Anyi—this is that same thing."

entries.zh: 乃堰肥水，親自表率，頃之，堰成水通，舟艦繼至。
entries.en: He dammed the Fei and led the work in person; soon the water flowed, and warships followed one after another.
entries.literal: He dammed the Fei River and worked at the head of the labor himself; before long the dam was done, the water ran through, and war-boats came up in succession.

entries.zh: 魏初分築東西小城夾合肥，叡先攻二城。
