entries.en: Wei had split Hefei with twin forts east and west; Rui struck those first.
entries.literal: Wei had first built eastern and western forts flanking Hefei; Rui attacked the two cities first.

entries.zh: 旣而魏援將揚靈胤帥軍五萬奄至，衆懼不敵，請表益兵。
entries.en: Then Yang Lingyin came with fifty thousand in relief; fear spread, and they asked to petition for more troops.
entries.literal: Then Wei's relief commander Yang Lingyin led fifty thousand men in a sudden arrival; the army feared it could not match them and asked to memorialize for reinforcements.

entries.zh: 叡笑曰：「賊已至城下，方復求軍，臨難鑄兵，豈及馬腹？
entries.en: Rui laughed: "The foe is at the wall and you want more men—to cast weapons mid-battle, will that reach the horse's belly?
entries.literal: Rui laughed and said, "The enemy is already at the walls and you ask for soldiers—who forges blades when the battle is on? Will that reach the horse's belly in time?

entries.zh: 且吾求濟師，彼亦徵衆，猶如吳益巴丘，蜀增白帝耳。
entries.en: If we beg for reinforcements, they will summon theirs too—Wu thickening Baqiu while Shu thickened White Emperor.
entries.literal: If we ask for help, they too will summon hosts—like Wu reinforcing Baqiu while Shu reinforced White Emperor.

entries.zh: 『師克在和不在衆』，古之義也。」
entries.en: 'The army wins by unity, not by mass'—so the ancients taught."
entries.literal: 'Victory lies in harmony, not in numbers'—that is the ancient teaching."

entries.zh: 因與戰，破之，軍人少安。
entries.en: He fought and routed them; the men drew breath again.
entries.literal: He gave battle and broke them; the army breathed a little easier.

entries.zh: 合肥旣平，高祖詔衆軍進次東陵。
entries.en: Hefei fell; Gaozu ordered the hosts forward to Dongling.
entries.literal: When Hefei was pacified, Gaozu ordered the armies to advance and encamp at Dongling.

entries.zh: 東陵去魏甓城二十里，將會戰，有詔班師。
entries.en: Dongling stood twenty li from Wei's Brick City; as battle neared, orders came to withdraw.
entries.literal: Dongling lay twenty li from Wei's Brick City; battle was about to join when an edict recalled the army.

entries.zh: 去賊旣近，懼爲所躡，叡悉遣輜重居前，身乘小輿殿后，魏人服叡威名，望之不敢逼，全軍而還。
entries.en: The foe was near; he sent wagons ahead and rode a small litter in the rear—Wei feared his name and would not close; the army came home whole.
entries.literal: The enemy was close; fearing pursuit, Rui sent all the baggage train ahead while he himself rode in a small litter at the rear—the Wei men revered Rui's name and dared not press him; the whole army returned intact.

entries.zh: 至是遷豫州於合肥。
entries.en: Then the seat of Yuzhou was shifted to Hefei.
entries.literal: At that time Yuzhou's seat was moved to Hefei.

entries.zh: 五年，魏中山王元英寇北徐州，圍刺史昌義之於鐘離，衆號百萬，連城四十餘。
entries.en: In year 5 Yuan Ying, prince of Zhongshan, struck North Xuzhou and penned Chang Yizhi at Zhongli—"a million" men, forty-odd camps chained together.
entries.literal: In the fifth year Wei's Prince of Zhongshan Yuan Ying raided North Xuzhou and besieged Inspector Chang Yizhi at Zhongli; they claimed a million men and more than forty linked camps.

entries.zh: 高祖遣征北將軍曹景宗，都督衆軍二十萬以拒之。
entries.en: Gaozu sent Cao Jingzong, general who pacifies the north, with two hundred thousand to meet them.
entries.literal: Gaozu sent Pacification-North General Cao Jingzong to command two hundred thousand men to resist.

entries.zh: 次邵陽洲，築壘相守，高祖詔叡率豫州之衆會焉。
entries.en: They held Shaoyang Isle behind fresh ramparts; Gaozu told Rui to bring Yuzhou's army to the rendezvous.
entries.literal: They encamped at Shaoyang Isle and built ramparts to hold each other; Gaozu ordered Rui to bring the forces of Yuzhou and join them.

entries.zh: 叡自合肥逕道由陰陵大澤行，值澗穀，輒飛橋以濟。
entries.en: He left Hefei by the straight track through Yinling's great bogs, bridging every gully as he came.
entries.literal: Rui came from Hefei by the direct road through the great marshes of Yinling; whenever he met ravines he threw flying bridges across.

entries.zh: 師人畏魏軍盛，多勸叡緩行。
entries.en: His men dreaded Wei's numbers and begged him to march slowly.
entries.literal: The soldiers feared the Wei host's strength and many urged Rui to go slowly.

entries.zh: 叡曰：「鐘離今鑿穴而處，負戶而汲，車馳卒奔，猶恐其後，而況緩乎！
entries.en: Rui said, "At Zhongli they burrow in the earth and haul water on their shoulders; chariots fly and runners dash, and still they fear they are late—shall we crawl?
entries.literal: Rui said, "At Zhongli they are digging holes to live in and carrying water on their backs; chariots race and runners sprint, and still they fear they come too late—how much less should we linger!

entries.zh: 魏人已墮吾腹中，卿曹勿憂也。」
entries.en: Wei is already in my gut—have no fear."
entries.literal: The Wei men are already in my belly—do not fret."

entries.zh: 旬日而至邵陽。
entries.en: In ten days he was at Shaoyang.
entries.literal: Within ten days he reached Shaoyang.

entries.zh: 初，高祖敕景宗曰：「韋叡，卿之鄉望，宜善敬之。」
entries.en: Gaozu had told Jingzong, "Wei Rui is the great man of your district—treat him with respect."
entries.literal: Earlier Gaozu had charged Jingzong, "Wei Rui is the leading man of your native place—you must honor him well."

entries.zh: 景宗見叡，禮甚謹。
entries.en: Jingzong received him with deep courtesy.
entries.literal: Jingzong received Rui with the utmost courtesy.

entries.zh: 高祖聞之，曰：「二將和，師必濟矣。」
entries.en: Gaozu heard and said, "Two generals in accord—the host will win."
entries.literal: When Gaozu heard of it he said, "When two generals are in harmony, the army will surely succeed."

entries.zh: 叡於景宗營前二十里，夜掘長塹，樹鹿角，截洲爲城，比曉而營立。
entries.en: Twenty li short of Jingzong's lines he dug a trench by night, planted stakes, and walled off the isle—by dawn a camp stood.
entries.literal: Twenty li before Jingzong's camp, Rui dug a long trench by night, set antlers, and cut the isle into a walled camp; by dawn the fort stood.

entries.zh: 元英大驚，以杖擊地曰：「是何神也！」
entries.en: Yuan Ying was thunderstruck and beat the earth with his staff: "What sorcery is this!"
entries.literal: Yuan Ying was greatly alarmed and struck the ground with his staff, crying, "What spirit is this!

entries.zh: 明旦，英自率衆來戰，叡乘素木輿，執白角如意麾軍，一日數合，英甚憚其強。
entries.en: At first light Ying came in person; Rui sat in a plain wooden litter, white ruyi in hand, and fought several rounds in a day—Ying dreaded his power.
entries.literal: At dawn Ying himself led the host to battle; Rui rode a plain wooden litter, white horn ruyi in hand to command the ranks, clashing several times in a day—Ying greatly feared his strength.

entries.zh: 魏軍又夜來攻城，飛矢雨集，叡子黯請下城以避箭，叡不許。
entries.en: Wei stormed the wall by night; arrows poured. His son An begged to come down; Rui refused.
entries.literal: The Wei army came again by night to storm the wall; arrows fell like rain. Rui's son An asked to leave the wall to escape the shafts; Rui would not allow it.

entries.zh: 軍中驚，叡於城上厲聲呵之，乃定。
entries.en: The ranks wavered; he roared from the battlements and they steadied.
entries.literal: Panic ran through the army; Rui shouted from the wall in a fierce voice and the host steadied.

entries.zh: 魏人先於邵陽洲兩岸爲兩橋，樹柵數百步，跨淮通道。
entries.en: Wei had bridged both shores of Shaoyang with palisades for hundreds of paces, a road across the Huai.
entries.literal: The Wei men had earlier built twin bridges on both banks of Shaoyang Isle, with palisades for several hundred paces, spanning the Huai as a road.

entries.zh: 叡裝大艦，使梁郡太守馮道根、廬江太守裴邃、秦郡太守李文釗等爲水軍。
entries.en: He fitted great ships and set Feng Daogen of Liangjun, Pei Sui of Lujiang, and Li Wenzhao of Qinjun over the fleet.
entries.literal: Rui fitted great warships and made Administrator of Liangjun Feng Daogen, Administrator of Lujiang Pei Sui, and Administrator of Qinjun Li Wenzhao command the river force.

entries.zh: 值淮水暴長，叡卽遣之，鬬艦競發，皆臨敵壘。
entries.en: The Huai swelled; he launched at once—tower-ships leaped forward and closed on the Wei lines.
entries.literal: The Huai suddenly rose in flood; Rui sent the fleet at once, tower-ships racing out, all bearing on the enemy ramparts.

entries.zh: 以小船載草，灌之以膏，從而焚其橋。
entries.en: Small craft heaped greased grass and fired the bridges in their wake.
entries.literal: Small boats carried grass soaked in grease and set the bridges ablaze behind them.

entries.zh: 風怒火盛，煙塵晦冥，敢死之士，拔柵斫橋，水又漂疾，倏忽之間，橋柵盡壞。
entries.en: Wind made a furnace of the sky; men who did not care for life wrenched down stakes and chopped bridges while the flood raced—bridges and palisades vanished in a breath.
entries.literal: Wind fed the flames until smoke and dust blotted the sky; death-defying men tore down palisades and hacked the bridges, while the current ran fierce—in an instant bridges and stakes were gone.

entries.zh: 而道根等皆身自搏戰，軍人奮勇，呼聲動天地，無不一當百，魏人大潰。
entries.en: Feng Daogen and the others fought in the van; the soldiers roared till heaven shook, each man worth a hundred—Wei broke completely.
entries.literal: Feng Daogen and the rest fought hand to hand themselves; the soldiers fought with fury, their cries shaking heaven and earth, none meeting less than a hundred—the Wei host collapsed utterly.

entries.zh: 元英見橋絕，脫身遁去。
entries.en: Yuan Ying saw the bridges destroyed and ran.
entries.literal: Yuan Ying saw the bridges gone and fled for his life.

entries.zh: 魏軍趨水死者十餘萬，斬首亦如之。
entries.en: Men drowning in the river ran to the hundred-thousands; heads heaped as high.
entries.literal: Wei soldiers rushing to the water drowned by the hundred-thousands; heads taken were as many.

entries.zh: 其餘釋甲稽顙，乞爲囚奴，猶數十萬。
entries.en: The rest dropped their armor and kowtowed, begging to become prisoners and slaves--still hundreds of thousands.
entries.literal: The rest cast off armor and bowed their foreheads, begging to be prisoners—still several hundred thousand.

entries.zh: 所獲軍實牛馬，不可勝紀。
entries.en: Booty in arms, cattle, and horses passed counting.
entries.literal: Arms, cattle, and horses captured could not be counted.

entries.zh: 叡遣報昌義之，義之且悲且喜，不暇答語，但叫曰：「更生！
entries.en: Rui sent to Chang Yizhi; Yizhi wept and laughed, unable to answer, and could only shout, "Born again!
entries.literal: Rui sent word to Chang Yizhi; Yizhi was by turns grieving and glad, too overwhelmed to answer, and could only cry, "Reborn!

entries.zh: 更生！」
entries.en: Born again!"
entries.literal: Reborn!"

entries.zh: 高祖遣中書郎周捨勞於淮上，叡積所獲於軍門，捨觀之，謂叡曰：「君此獲復與熊耳山等。」
entries.en: Gaozu sent Zhou She to comfort the Huai army; Rui heaped booty at the gate. She said, "This haul matches Bear-Ear Mountain."
entries.literal: Gaozu sent Palace Secretary Zhou She to reward and comfort the army on the Huai; Rui piled the spoils at the camp gate for him to see. She looked and said to Rui, "Your capture here rivals Bear-Ear Mountain."

entries.zh: 以功增封七百戶，進爵爲侯，徵通直散騎常侍、右衛將軍。
entries.en: His fief grew by seven hundred households, he became a marquis, and was called to court as regular attendant of direct transmission and right guard general.
entries.literal: For his merit his fief was increased by seven hundred households, he was advanced to marquis, and summoned as Regular Attendant of Direct Transmission and Right Guard General.

entries.zh: 十四年，出爲平北將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史。
entries.en: In year 14 he went out as General Who Pacifies the North, Pacify Barbarians Commandant, and inspector of Yongzhou.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year he went out as General Who Pacifies the North, Pacify Barbarians Commandant, and Inspector of Yongzhou.

entries.zh: 初，叡起兵鄉中，客陰儁光泣止叡，叡還爲州，儁光道候叡，叡笑謂之曰：「若從公言，乞食於路矣。」
entries.en: When Rui first raised troops at home, his guest Yin Junguang wept and tried to stop him; on returning as inspector, Junguang met him on the road, and Rui laughed and said, "Had I taken your advice, I would be begging along the highway."
entries.literal: Earlier, when Rui had raised troops in his home district, his guest Yin Junguang wept and tried to stop him; when Rui returned as inspector, Junguang met him on the road, and Rui laughed and said to him, "Had I followed your advice, I would be begging food on the highway."

entries.zh: 餉耕牛十頭。
entries.en: He gave him ten draft oxen.
entries.literal: He presented ten draft oxen.

entries.zh: 叡於故舊，無所遺惜，士大夫年七十以上，多與假板縣令，鄉里甚懷之。
entries.en: Toward old friends Rui was unstinting; for gentry over seventy he often gave acting county magistrate posts, and the district loved him for it.
entries.literal: Toward old friends Rui held nothing back; for scholar-officials over seventy he often granted acting county magistrate appointments, and the district thought warmly of him.

entries.zh: 十五年，拜表致仕，優詔不許。
entries.en: In year 15 he petitioned to retire; a gracious edict refused.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year he memorialized to retire; a gracious edict refused.

entries.zh: 十七年，徵散騎常侍、護軍將軍，尋給鼓吹一部，入直殿省。
entries.en: In year 17 he was summoned as Regular Attendant and Protector of the Army; soon he received martial pipes and drums and took regular duty in the Hall Department.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year he was summoned as Regular Attendant and Protector of the Army General; soon he was given one set of martial pipes and drums and entered regular duty in the Hall Department.

entries.zh: 居朝廷，恂恂未嘗忤視，高祖甚禮敬之。
entries.en: At court he was deferential and never met others' eyes; Gaozu treated him with great respect.
entries.literal: In court he was respectful and never met others' eyes directly; Gaozu greatly honored him.

entries.zh: 性慈愛，撫孤兄子過於己子，歷官所得祿賜，皆散之親故，家無餘財。
entries.en: Kind by nature, he raised his orphaned nephews more devotedly than his own sons and gave every salary and gift to kin and friends, leaving nothing at home.
entries.literal: By nature he was kindly; he raised his orphaned elder brother's sons more devotedly than his own, and whatever salary and gifts his offices brought he gave away to kin and friends, leaving nothing at home.

entries.zh: 後爲護軍，居家無事，慕萬石、陸賈之爲人，因畫之於壁以自玩。
entries.en: Later, idle at home as Protector of the Army, he admired the Wan Shi and Lu Jia and painted them on his wall for amusement.
entries.literal: Later, as Protector of the Army with nothing to do at home, he admired the conduct of the Wan Shi clan and Lu Jia and painted them on his wall for his own pleasure.

entries.zh: 時雖老，暇日猶課諸兒以學。
entries.en: Though old, on free days he still drilled his sons in learning.
entries.literal: Though old, on free days he still set lessons for his sons.

entries.zh: 第三子稜，尤明經史，世稱其洽聞，叡每坐棱使說書，其所發擿，稜猶弗之逮也。
entries.en: His third son Ling knew the classics and histories especially well and was called broadly learned. Rui always seated Ling and had him lecture on books; the points Rui raised, Ling still could not match.
entries.literal: His third son Ling was especially versed in the classics and histories; the age called him broadly learned. Rui would seat Ling and have him explain the books; the points Rui raised, Ling still could not match.

entries.zh: 高祖方銳意釋氏，天下咸從風而化；
entries.en: Gaozu was then intent on Buddhism, and the realm followed;
entries.literal: Gaozu was then keen on Buddhism, and all under heaven followed the fashion;

entries.zh: 叡自以信受素薄，位居大臣，不欲與俗俯仰，所行略如他日。
entries.en: Rui felt his faith had always been thin; as a great minister he would not bob with fashion, and lived much as before.
entries.literal: Rui felt his own faith had always been thin; holding a minister's rank, he did not wish to bob with the crowd, and his conduct stayed much as before.

entries.zh: 七年，遷左衛將軍，俄爲安西長史、南郡太守，秩中二千石。
entries.en: In year 7 he became left guard general, then chief clerk of Anxi and administrator of Nanjun at two-thousand-dan rank.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he was made Left Guard General, then soon Anxi Chief Clerk and Administrator of Nanjun at the salary of two thousand dan.

entries.zh: 會司州刺史馬仙琕北伐還軍，爲魏人所躡，三關擾動，詔叡督衆軍援焉。
entries.en: Ma Xianbi of Sizhou marched north and was chased home by Wei; the Three Passes trembled, and Rui was ordered to command the rescue.
entries.literal: When Sizhou Inspector Ma Xianbi marched north and returned, Wei pursued him; the Three Passes were shaken, and an edict made Rui commander of the relief armies.

entries.zh: 叡至安陸，增築城二丈餘，更開大塹，起高樓，衆頗譏其示弱。
entries.en: At Anlu he raised walls two zhang higher, dug a deep moat, and built tall towers—many sneered that he showed weakness.
entries.literal: Rui reached Anlu, raised the walls more than two zhang, opened a great trench, and built tall towers; many mocked him for showing fear.

entries.zh: 叡曰：「不然，爲將當有怯時，不可專勇。」
entries.en: Rui said, "No—a general must know fear; bravery alone will not do."
entries.literal: Rui said, "Not so—a commander must know when to be timid; courage alone is not enough.

entries.zh: 是時元英復追仙琕，將復邵陽之恥，聞叡至，乃退。
entries.en: Yuan Ying chased Xianbi again to avenge Shaoyang; hearing Rui had arrived, he retreated.
entries.literal: At that time Yuan Ying again pursued Xianbi, meaning to wash away the shame of Shaoyang; when he heard Rui had come, he withdrew.

entries.zh: 帝亦詔罷軍。
entries.en: The throne recalled the host.
entries.literal: The emperor also ordered the armies disbanded.

entries.zh: 明年，遷信武將軍、江州刺史。
entries.en: Next year he became trustworthy-war general and inspector of Jiangzhou.
entries.literal: The next year he was made Trustworthy-War General and Inspector of Jiangzhou.

entries.zh: 九年，徵員外散騎常侍、右衛將軍，累遷左衛將軍、太子詹事，尋加通直散騎常侍。
entries.en: In year 9 he was recalled as supernumerary regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and right guard general, then advanced through left guard general and supervisor of the crown prince's household, with the added title regular attendant of direct transmission.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he was summoned as Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Right Guard General, and rose repeatedly to Left Guard General and Supervisor of the Crown Prince's Household, then with the additional title Regular Attendant of Direct Transmission.

entries.zh: 十三年，遷智武將軍、丹陽尹，以公事免。
entries.en: In year 13 he was made Intelligent Martial General and intendant of Danyang, then dismissed on public business.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to Intelligent Martial General and Intendant of Danyang, then removed from office on public business.

entries.zh: 頃之，起爲中護軍。
entries.en: Soon he was recalled as Central Protector General.
entries.literal: Before long he was recalled as Central Protector General.

entries.zh: 普通元年夏，遷侍中、車騎將軍，以疾未拜。
entries.en: In summer of Putong year 1 he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of Chariots and Cavalry but did not take office because of illness.
entries.literal: In the summer of the first year of Putong he was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of Chariots and Cavalry, but because of illness did not accept the appointment.

entries.zh: 八月，卒于家，時年七十九。
entries.en: In the eighth month he died at home at seventy-nine.
entries.literal: In the eighth month he died at home, aged seventy-nine.

entries.zh: 遺令薄葬，斂以時服。
entries.en: He ordered a plain burial in seasonal dress.
entries.literal: His final instructions ordered a plain burial, enshrouded in seasonal dress.

entries.zh: 高祖卽日臨哭甚慟。
entries.en: Gaozu came to mourn that same day and wept bitterly.
entries.literal: Gaozu came that same day to mourn and wept bitterly.

entries.zh: 賜錢十萬，布二百匹，東園秘器，朝服一具，衣一襲，喪事取給於官，遣中書舍人監護。
entries.en: He received a hundred thousand cash, two hundred bolts of cloth, eastern-garden funeral vessels, one court robe and one suit of clothes; the offices supplied the funeral, and a Secretariat Gentleman oversaw it.
entries.literal: He was granted a hundred thousand cash, two hundred bolts of cloth, eastern-garden funeral vessels, one court robe, one suit of clothes; whatever the funeral required was to be supplied by the offices, and a Secretariat Gentleman was sent to oversee it.

entries.zh: 贈侍中、車騎將軍、開府儀同三司。
entries.en: Posthumously he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Acting Three Excellencies with Opening Office.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Acting Three Excellencies with Opening Office.

entries.zh: 諡曰嚴。
entries.en: Posthumous title: Yan.
entries.literal: Posthumous title: Yan.

entries.zh: 袁顗爲雍州刺史，辟爲主簿。
entries.en: Yuan Hao, inspector of Yongzhou, recruited him as chief clerk.
entries.literal: Yuan Hao was Inspector of Yongzhou and recruited him as chief clerk.

entries.zh: 遭母憂，廬於墓側，負土起墳。
entries.en: At his mother's death he built a hut by the tomb and carried earth for the mound.
entries.literal: When his mother died he built a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to raise the mound.

entries.zh: 高祖臨雍州，聞之，親往臨弔。
entries.en: When Gaozu held Yongzhou he heard and came in person to mourn.
entries.literal: When Gaozu held Yongzhou he heard of it and came in person to mourn at the site.

entries.zh: 服闋，引爲中兵參軍。
entries.en: When mourning ended he was made Central Army Aide.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he was brought in as Central Army Aide.

entries.zh: 義師之起也，以愛爲壯武將軍、冠軍南平王司馬，帶襄陽令。
entries.en: When the righteous army rose, Ai was made Valiant Martial General and major to the Prince of Nanping, Champion, with concurrent charge as magistrate of Xiangyang.
entries.literal: When the righteous army rose, Ai was made Valiant Martial General and Major to the Prince of Nanping, Champion, with concurrent charge as Magistrate of Xiangyang.

entries.zh: 時京邑未定，雍州空虛，魏興太守顏僧都等據郡反，州內驚擾，百姓攜貳。
entries.en: The capital was unsettled and Yongzhou empty; Wei Xing administrator Yan Sangdu and others held the commandery in revolt, and the province shook.
entries.literal: At that time the capital was not yet settled and Yongzhou was empty; Wei Xing Administrator Yan Sangdu and others held the commandery in revolt; within the province there was alarm and the people wavered.

entries.zh: 愛沉敏有謀，素爲州里信伏，乃推心撫御，曉示逆順；
entries.en: Ai was deep, keen, and trusted in the district; he won hearts with open care and showed who was loyal and who rebel;
entries.literal: Ai was deep, keen, and resourceful and had long been trusted by the district; he won hearts with open-handed care and made clear who was rebel and who loyal;

entries.zh: 兼率募鄉里，得千餘人，與僧都等戰於始平郡南，大破之，百姓乃安。
entries.en: he also recruited more than a thousand men locally and routed Sangdu south of Shiping commandery; the people were at peace.
entries.literal: he also led recruitment in the home district and got more than a thousand men; with Sangdu and the rest he fought south of Shiping commandery, routed them utterly, and the people were then at peace.

entries.zh: 黯字務直，性強正，少習經史，有文詞。
entries.en: An, styled Wuzhi, was forceful and upright; in youth he studied the classics and histories and wrote well.
entries.literal: An, styled Wuzhi, was by nature forceful and upright; in youth he studied the classics and histories and had literary skill.

entries.zh: 起家太子舍人，稍遷太僕卿，南豫州刺史，太府卿。
entries.en: He began as Heir Apparent's Household Attendant, rose to Minister of the Imperial Studs, inspector of South Yuzhou, and Minister of the Grand Storehouse.
entries.literal: He began his career as Household Attendant of the Heir Apparent, was gradually promoted to Minister of the Imperial Studs, Inspector of South Yuzhou, and Minister of the Grand Storehouse.

entries.zh: 侯景濟江，黯屯六門，尋改爲都督城西面諸軍事。
entries.en: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangzi, An held the Six Gates; soon he was made commander of the western defenses.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangzi, An garrisoned the Six Gates; soon he was made commander of all military affairs on the city's western face.

entries.zh: 時景於城外起東西二土山，城內亦作以應之，太宗親自負土，哀太子以下躬執畚鍤。
entries.en: Jing built east and west earthen mounds outside the wall and matching mounds within; Taizong personally carried earth, and the Lamenting Heir Apparent and those below him carried earth with shovel and basket.
entries.literal: At that time Jing raised east and west earthen mounds outside the wall, and within the city others were built to match; Taizong personally carried earth, and the Lamenting Heir Apparent and those below him personally took shovel and basket in hand.

entries.zh: 黯守西土山，晝夜苦戰，以功授輕車將軍，加持節。
entries.en: An held the western mound and fought day and night; for merit he was made General of Light Chariots with staff of authority.
entries.literal: An held the western mound, fighting bitterly day and night; for merit he was made General of Light Chariots with added staff of authority.

entries.zh: 卒於城內，贈散騎常侍、左衛將軍。
entries.en: He died in the city and was posthumously made Regular Attendant and Left Guard General.
entries.literal: He died within the city and was posthumously made Regular Attendant and Left Guard General.

entries.zh: 叡族弟愛。
entries.en: Rui's cousin Ai.
entries.literal: Rui's cousin by the clan Ai.

entries.zh: 中興二年，從和帝東下。
entries.en: In Zhongxing year 2 he followed Emperor He east.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhongxing he followed Emperor He east.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，進號輔國將軍，仍爲驍騎將軍，尋除寧蜀太守，與益州刺史鄧元起西上襲劉季連，行至公安，道病卒，贈衛尉卿。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Ai was advanced to General Who Assists the State, then kept as General of Valiant Cavalry, made administrator of Ning Shu, and with Yizhou inspector Deng Yuanqi went west against Liu Jilian; at Gong'an he died on the road and was posthumously made Minister of the Guard.
entries.literal: When Gaozu accepted the abdication, Ai's rank was advanced to General Who Assists the State; he remained General of Valiant Cavalry, was soon made Administrator of Ning Shu, and with Yizhou Inspector Deng Yuanqi went west to attack Liu Jilian; on reaching Gong'an he died of illness on the road and was posthumously made Minister of the Guard.

entries.zh: 子乾向，官至驍騎將軍，征北長史，汝陰、鐘離二郡太守。
entries.en: His son Ganxiang rose to General of Valiant Cavalry, chief clerk on the northern expedition, and administrator of Ruyin and Zhongli.
entries.literal: His son Ganxiang rose in office to General of Valiant Cavalry, Chief Clerk of the Army on the Northern Expedition, and Administrator of the two commanderies of Ruyin and Zhongli.

entries.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：昔竇融以河右歸漢，終爲盛族；
entries.en: Chen Minister of Personnel Yao Cha said: Dou Rong once submitted Hexi to Han and became a great clan;
entries.literal: Chen Minister of Personnel Yao Cha said: In old times Dou Rong submitted the lands west of the Yellow River to Han and in the end became a great clan;

entries.zh: 柳惔舉南鄭響從，而家聲弗霣，時哉！
entries.en: Liu Tan raised Nan Zheng in response and followed, yet his family name did not sink—the times favored it!
entries.literal: Liu Tan raised Nan Zheng in response and followed, yet his family's renown did not sink—the times were right!

entries.zh: 忱之謀畫，亦用有成，智矣。
entries.en: Liu Chen's plans too succeeded—how wise!
entries.literal: Liu Chen's planning too had its successes—how wise!

entries.zh: 韋叡起上庸以附義，其地比惔則薄，及合肥、邵陽之役，其功甚盛，推而弗有，君子哉！
entries.en: Wei Rui rose from Shangyong for the righteous cause; his base was poorer than Tan's, yet at Hefei and Shaoyang his merit was great, and he yielded without claiming it—a gentleman indeed!
entries.literal: Wei Rui rose from Shangyong to join the righteous cause; his territory was poorer than Tan's, yet at Hefei and Shaoyang his merit was very great, and he yielded without claiming it—a gentleman indeed!

entries.zh: 梁書卷第十二 列傳第六
entries.en: Book of Liang, Volume 12, Biographies 6
entries.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 12, Biographies 6

entries.zh: 齊初爲征虜記室，帶襄陽令，所奉之王，齊文惠太子也。
entries.en: At Qi's opening he was campaign recorder with Xiangyang on his belt—the prince was Crown Prince Wenhuì.
entries.literal: Early in Qi he was campaign-against-barbarians recorder, concurrent Xiangyang magistrate—the prince he served was Crown Prince Wenhuì.

entries.zh: 太子入居東宮，爲步兵校尉，管書記，直永壽省，校四部圖書。
entries.en: The heir moved east; he became infantry colonel, keeper of papers, stationed at Yongshou, collating the four library divisions.
entries.literal: When the crown prince moved to the Eastern Palace, he was infantry colonel, in charge of records, on duty at Yongshou office, collating the four sections of books.

entries.zh: 時東宮多士，約特被親遇，每直入見，影斜方出。
entries.en: The eastern palace teemed with talent, yet Yue alone was drawn close—he walked straight in and left only when the sun hung low.
entries.literal: Many scholars were at the Eastern Palace; Yue was specially favored, entering straight through each time and not leaving until his shadow slanted long.

entries.zh: 當時王侯到宮，或不得進，約每以爲言。
entries.en: Sometimes even kings and marquises were turned away at the gate, and Yue always pleaded their case.
entries.literal: At times princes and marquises coming to the palace could not get in—Yue always spoke up about it.

entries.zh: 太子曰：「吾生平懶起，是卿所悉，得卿談論，然後忘寢。
entries.en: The heir said, "You know how late I like to wake; only your talk makes me forget the bed.
entries.literal: The crown prince said: "I have been lazy to rise all my life, as you know; only when I talk with you do I forget sleep.

entries.zh: 卿欲我夙興，可恒早入。」
entries.en: If you want me at dawn, come early every day."
entries.literal: If you want me up early, come in early every day."

entries.zh: 遷太子家令，後以本官兼著作郎，遷中書郎，本邑中正，司徒右長史，黃門侍郎。
entries.en: He rose to eastern-palace household head, then added compilation gentleman, secretariat gentleman, native impartial judge, right chief of staff to the minister of works, and yellow-gate companion.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Eastern Palace Household Head, later combining that office with Compilation Gentleman, then Secretariat Gentleman, native-district impartial judge, Right Chief of Staff of the Minister of Works, and Yellow Gate Gentleman Companion.

entries.zh: 時竟陵王亦招士，約與蘭陵蕭琛、琅邪王融、陳郡謝朓、南鄉范雲、樂安任昉等皆遊焉，當世號爲得人。
entries.en: The Prince of Jingling too kept a salon; Yue moved with Xiao Chen, Wang Rong, Xie Tiao, Fan Yun, Ren Fang, and the rest—men of the age called them the company worth having.
entries.literal: The Prince of Jingling also gathered scholars; Yue with Xiao Chen of Lanling, Wang Rong of Langye, Xie Tiao of Chen commandery, Fan Yun of Nanxiang, Ren Fang of Le'an, and others all associated—at the time they were called the attained men.

entries.zh: 俄兼尚書左丞，尋爲御史中丞，轉車騎長史。
entries.en: Soon he doubled as left assistant in the Masters of Writing, then censor-in-chief, then chief clerk to the cavalry general.
entries.literal: Soon he concurrently served as Left Assistant Minister of the Masters of Writing, then became Censor-in-Chief, then Chief Clerk of the Cavalry General.

entries.zh: 隆昌元年，除吏部郎，出爲寧朔將軍、東陽太守。
entries.en: In the first Longchang year he took the personnel post, then left as pacify-the-north general and administrator of Dongyang.
entries.literal: In Longchang year 1, he was appointed Department of Personnel Attendant, then went out as Pacify-the-North General and Administrator of Dongyang.

entries.zh: 明帝卽位，進號輔國將軍，徵爲五兵尚書，遷國子祭酒。
entries.en: Ming's accession brought him the title assist-the-state; he was called to armaments minister, then made chancellor of the imperial academy.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, his title advanced to Assist-the-State General; he was summoned as Masters of Armaments Minister, then became Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.

entries.zh: 明帝崩，政歸塚宰，尚書令徐孝嗣使約撰定遺詔。
entries.en: When Ming died the regent held the reins; Xu Xiaosi ordered Yue to fix the final edict.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming died, power fell to the chamberlain; Minister Xu Xiaosi had Yue draft the death edict.

entries.zh: 遷左衛將軍，尋加通直散騎常侍。
entries.en: He became left guard general, soon with unimpeded transmission regular attendant added.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Left Guard General, soon with added Unimpeded Transmission Regular Attendant.

entries.zh: 永元二年，以母老表求解職，改授冠軍將軍、司徒左長史，征虜將軍、南清河太守。
entries.en: In Yongyuan year 2 he begged off for his mother's sake and was shifted to champion general, left chief of staff, campaign general, and administrator of Southern Qinghe.
entries.literal: In Yongyuan year 2, citing his mother's age he petitioned to leave office; reassigned as Champion General and Left Chief of Staff of the Minister of Works, Campaign General and Administrator of Southern Qinghe.

entries.zh: 迹平生之耿介，實有心於獨往。
entries.en: The track of my days was straight and hard; I meant to keep a heart that went alone.
entries.literal: The traces of my life's upright integrity—truly I kept a heart that walked alone.

entries.zh: 思幽人而軫念，望東臯而長想。
entries.en: I mourned the man apart from the world and turned my eyes to the eastern terrace in longing.
entries.literal: I thought of the reclusive man and felt deep pity; I gazed at the eastern ridge and longed.

entries.zh: 本忘情於徇物，徒羈絏於天壤。
entries.en: I was born to forget the world's goods, yet only wound in heaven's dust.
entries.literal: By nature I had forgotten feeling for outer things, only to be bound by heaven's dust.

entries.zh: 應屢歎於牽絲，陸興言於世網。
entries.en: Ying Pu-ke groaned at every tug of thread; Lu Ji named the net the age weaves.
entries.literal: Ying Pu-ke sighed again and again at threads that pulled; Lu Ji spoke of the world's net.

entries.zh: 事滔滔而未合，志悁悁而無爽。
entries.en: Business poured on without rest; my heart was tight but never bent.
entries.literal: Affairs ran on, ungathered; my will was anxious yet never lost its integrity.

entries.zh: 路將殫而彌峭，情薄暮而踰廣。
entries.en: The path was nearly spent and grew sharper; at evening my longing widened.
entries.literal: The road neared its end and grew steeper still; feeling at dusk spread ever wider.

entries.zh: 抱寸心其如蘭，何斯願之浩蕩。
entries.en: I carried a span of heart sweet as orchid—how wide this wish runs!
entries.literal: I held an inch of heart fragrant as orchids—how vast this longing's flood!

entries.zh: 詠歸歟而躑跼，眷岩阿而抵掌。
entries.en: I sang of going home yet could not move; I turned to the cliff and struck my palms.
entries.literal: I chanted "Returning!" yet stood rooted in place; I looked toward the rocky crags and clapped my hands.

entries.zh: 梁書卷第十三 列傳第七
entries.en: Book of Liang, Volume 13, Biographies 7
entries.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 13, Biographies 7

entries.zh: 會南東海太守陸澄丁艱，淹自謂郡丞應行郡事，景素用司馬柳世隆。
entries.en: When Southern Donghai prefect Lu Cheng began mourning, Yan assumed the aide should run the commandery; Jingsu gave the post to staff officer Liu Shilong.
entries.literal: When Southern Donghai prefect Lu Cheng entered mourning for his father, Yan thought that as commandery aide he should act as prefect; Jingsu appointed staff officer Liu Shilong instead.

entries.zh: 淹固求之，景素大怒，言於選部，黜爲建安吳興令。
entries.en: Yan insisted; Jingsu raged, spoke to personnel, and demoted him to Jian'an magistrate in Wu-xing.
entries.literal: Yan pressed his claim; Jingsu was furious and spoke to the selection office, demoting him to magistrate of Jian'an in Wu-xing.

entries.zh: 淹在縣三年。
entries.en: Yan served in the county three years.
entries.literal: Yan held the district three years.

entries.zh: 昇明初，齊帝輔政，聞其才，召爲尚書駕部郎、驃騎參軍事。
entries.en: At the start of Ascendant Bright, with Qi's emperor as regent, he heard of Yan and made him secretariat director of the imperial equipage and valiant-cavalry staff officer.
entries.literal: At the start of the Ascendant Bright era, when Qi's emperor held regency, he heard of Yan's talent and summoned him as Masters of Writing director of the imperial equipage and valiant-cavalry staff officer.

entries.zh: 俄而荊州刺史沈攸之作亂，高帝謂淹曰：「天下紛紛若是，君謂何如？」
entries.en: Soon Jing inspector Shen Youzhi rose in arms; Gaodi asked Yan, "The world is chaos like this—what is your view?"
entries.literal: Before long Jing inspector Shen Youzhi rebelled; Gaodi said to Yan, "The realm is in such turmoil—what do you think?"

entries.zh: 淹對曰：「昔項強而劉弱，袁衆而曹寡，羽號令諸侯，卒受一劍之辱，紹跨躡四州，終爲奔北之虜。
entries.en: Yan answered, "Once Xiang Yu was strong and Liu Bang weak, Yuan Shao had numbers and Cao Cao few; Yu ruled the lords yet died by one sword, Yuan held four provinces yet fled north in defeat.
entries.literal: Yan answered, "Of old Xiang was strong and Liu weak, Yuan had many men and Cao few; Yu commanded the feudal lords yet in the end suffered the shame of a single sword, Yuan straddled four provinces yet ended a fugitive north of the river.

entries.zh: 此謂『在德不在鼎』。
entries.en: That is what men mean by 'power lies in virtue, not in the tripod.'
entries.literal: This is what they call 'virtue, not the vessel.'

entries.zh: 公何疑哉？」
entries.en: What doubt remains for you?"
entries.literal: Why should you doubt?"

entries.zh: 帝曰：「聞此言者多矣，試爲慮之。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Many say the same—work it through for me."
entries.literal: The emperor said, "Many have spoken so—try to think it through."

entries.zh: 淹曰：「公雄武有奇略，一勝也；
entries.en: Yan said, "You are boldly martial with a singular plan—first victory;
entries.literal: Yan said, "Your Lordship is boldly martial with a strange design—one victory;

entries.zh: 寬容而仁恕，二勝也；
entries.en: tolerant and humane—second victory;
entries.literal: tolerant and humane—two victories;

entries.zh: 賢能畢力，三勝也；
entries.en: the worthy give all their strength—third victory;
entries.literal: the worthy exert all their strength—three victories;

entries.zh: 民望所歸，四勝也；
entries.en: the people's hopes rest on you—fourth victory;
entries.literal: the people's hopes turn to you—four victories;

entries.zh: 奉天子而伐叛逆，五勝也。
entries.en: you hold the Son of Heaven and punish rebellion—fifth victory.
entries.literal: you hold the Son of Heaven and strike the rebel—five victories.

entries.zh: 彼志銳而器小，一敗也；
entries.en: Their will is keen but their measure small—first defeat;
entries.literal: Their will is sharp but their vessel small—one defeat;

entries.zh: 有威而無恩，二敗也；
entries.en: they inspire fear but grant no grace—second defeat;
entries.literal: they have awe but no grace—two defeats;

entries.zh: 士卒解體，三敗也；
entries.en: their troops are slack—third defeat;
entries.literal: their soldiers are loosened—three defeats;

entries.zh: 搢紳不懷，四敗也；
entries.en: the gentry do not stand with them—fourth defeat;
entries.literal: the gentry do not cling to them—four defeats;

entries.zh: 懸兵數千里，而無同惡相濟，五敗也。
entries.en: they stretch an army a thousand li with no ally of one heart—fifth defeat.
entries.literal: they hang their army a thousand li away with none of like mind to aid them—five defeats.

entries.zh: 故雖豺狼十萬，而終爲我獲焉。」
entries.en: Though jackals number in the tens of thousands, in the end they are yours."
entries.literal: Though they have a hundred thousand wolves, in the end they will be ours."

entries.zh: 帝笑曰：「君談過矣。」
entries.en: The emperor laughed and said, "You overspeak."
entries.literal: The emperor laughed and said, "You talk too much."

entries.zh: 是時軍書表記，皆使淹具草。
entries.en: In those days every army dispatch and memorial passed through Yan's hand.
entries.literal: At that time military reports and memorials were all drafted by Yan.

entries.zh: 相國建，補記室參軍事。
entries.en: When the chief minister's office was set up, he became record-keeper on the staff.
entries.literal: When the chief minister's office was established, he was made record-keeper staff officer.

entries.zh: 建元初，又爲驃騎豫章王記室，帶東武令，參掌詔册，並典國史。
entries.en: At Jianyuan's opening he was again valiant-cavalry record-keeper to the Prince of Yuzhang, magistrate of Dongwu in addition, drafting edicts and patents and tending the national history.
entries.literal: At the start of Jianyuan he was again valiant-cavalry record-keeper to the Prince of Yuzhang, with concurrent magistrate of Dongwu, charged with edicts and patents and also keeper of the national history.

entries.zh: 尋遷中書侍郎。
entries.en: Soon he rose to secretariat gentleman.
entries.literal: Soon he was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman.

entries.zh: 永明初，遷驍騎將軍，掌國史。
entries.en: At Yongming's opening he became valiant cavalry general and still held the national history.
entries.literal: At the start of Yongming he was made Valiant Cavalry General and kept charge of the national history.

entries.zh: 出爲建武將軍、廬陵內史。
entries.en: He went out as general who establishes martial glory and Luling interior magistrate.
entries.literal: He went out as General Who Establishes Martial Glory and interior magistrate of Luling.

entries.zh: 視事三年，還爲驍騎將軍，兼尚書左丞，尋復以本官領國子博士。
entries.en: After three years he returned as valiant cavalry general and vice director of the masters of writing; soon he held the same rank and led the national university as erudite.
entries.literal: After three years in office he returned as Valiant Cavalry General and concurrent Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; soon he again held his former post with charge as Erudite of the National University.

entries.zh: 少帝初，以本官兼御史中丞。
entries.en: When the Depraved Emperor began his reign Yan kept his rank and also served as censor.
entries.literal: At the start of the Depraved Emperor's reign he held his former post with concurrent Censor.

entries.zh: 初，齊明帝旣廢郁林王，始爲侍中、中書監、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、揚州刺史、錄尚書事，封宣城郡公，加兵五千，使昉具表草。
entries.en: When Qi's Emperor Ming deposed the Emperor of Lin, he first took attendant, palace library director, agile-cavalry general with full staff, Yangzhou inspector, and recorder of the secretariat, was made duke of Xuancheng with five thousand more troops, and had Fang draft the memorial.
entries.literal: Early, after Qi Emperor Ming had deposed the Emperor of Lin, he first became Attendant, Palace Library Director, General of Agile Cavalry with full staff equal to the Three Ministries, Yangzhou Inspector, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, enfeoffed as Duke of Xuancheng with five thousand additional troops, and had Fang draft the memorial.

entries.zh: 其辭曰：「臣本庸才，智力淺短。
entries.en: It runs: "Your servant is a mediocrity, shallow in wit and short in strength.
entries.literal: Its words say: "Your servant is by nature mediocre, shallow in mind and short in strength.

entries.zh: 太祖高皇帝篤猶子之愛，降家人之慈；
entries.en: Grand Ancestor Gao cherished a nephew as a son and gave the kindness of kin under one roof;
entries.literal: Grand Ancestor Emperor Gao cherished the love due a nephew-son and granted the kindness shown within a household;

entries.zh: 世祖武皇帝情等布衣，寄深同氣。
entries.en: Ancestor Emperor Wu treated him as an equal of the robe and bound him with shared blood.
entries.literal: Ancestor Emperor Wu treated him as a commoner's equal and entrusted him with the bond of shared blood.

entries.zh: 武皇大漸，實奉詔言。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu lay dying, I truly received his charge in words.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu fell gravely ill, I truly received his charge in words.

entries.zh: 雖自見之明，庸近所蔽，愚夫一至，偶識量己，實不忍自固於綴衣之辰，拒違於玉幾之側，遂荷顧托，導揚末命。
entries.en: Though I saw my own light, the near blinded me—yet even a fool, once, may know his measure—and I could not harden myself at the hour of mourning dress nor turn away beside the jade throne; so I bore the trust and carried out the last command.
entries.literal: Though I saw my own light, the near and mean blinded me—yet when a fool arrives once, he happens to know his measure—and I truly could not steel myself at the hour of the embroidered robe nor refuse at the jade throne's side; thus I bore the entrustment and led the command of the final charge.

entries.zh: 雖嗣君棄常，獲罪宣德，王室不造，職臣之由。
entries.en: Though the heir abandoned the norm and was judged for upholding virtue, the royal house was broken—and the fault is mine.
entries.literal: Though the successor prince abandoned the norm and was condemned to uphold virtue, the royal house was undone—the fault lies with ministers like me.

entries.zh: 何者？
entries.en: Why is that?
entries.literal: Why?

entries.zh: 親則東牟，任惟博陸，徒懷子孟社稷之對，何救昌邑爭臣之譏。
entries.en: Kin was the Prince of Eastern Mou, the charge was Bolu's—he only kept Zimeng's answer for throne and altar; how could he spare Changyi the rebuke of contentious ministers?
entries.literal: Kinship was Eastern Mou's, the charge was Bolu's—he only harbored Zimeng's reply for state and altar, how could he save Changyi from the censure of contentious ministers?

entries.zh: 四海之議，於何逃責？
entries.en: The judgment of the four seas—how shall I escape blame?
entries.literal: The opinion of the four seas—how escape blame?

entries.zh: 陵土未乾，訓誓在耳，家國之事，一至於斯，非臣之尤，誰任其咎！
entries.en: The imperial tomb is not yet dry, the charge still rings in the ear—house and state have come to this; if not my fault, whose is it?
entries.literal: The imperial tomb not yet dry, instructions and warnings still in the ear—the affair of house and state has come to this; if not my fault, who bears the blame!

entries.zh: 將何以肅拜高寢，虔奉武園？
entries.en: How shall I bow at the high inner chamber and serve the martial park with devotion?
entries.literal: How shall I reverently bow at the high inner chamber and devoutly serve the martial park?

entries.zh: 悼心失圖，泣血待旦。
entries.en: A grieving heart has lost its map; I wait for dawn in tears of blood.
entries.literal: A grieving heart loses its plan; I wait for dawn weeping blood.

entries.zh: 寧容復徼榮於家恥，宴安於國危。
entries.en: How can I again seek glory on family shame and feast while the state is in peril?
entries.literal: How can I again seek glory atop family shame and feast in ease amid national peril?

entries.zh: 驃騎上將之元勳，神州儀刑之列岳，尚書是稱司會，中書實管王言。
entries.en: The founding merit of the agile-cavalry general, the model lord of the divine land—the secretariat is called steward of assemblies, the palace director truly holds the king's words.
entries.literal: The founding merit of the General of Agile Cavalry, the exemplar of the divine land's model lords—the Masters of Writing is called steward of assemblies, the Secretariat truly governs the king's words.

entries.zh: 且虛飾寵章，委成禦侮，臣知不愜，物誰謂宜。
entries.en: Yet empty ornaments of favor, entrusting the ward of insult—I know it will not satisfy; who would call it fitting?
entries.literal: Yet empty ornaments of favor, entrusting defense of insult—I know it does not satisfy; who of things would say it is fitting?

entries.zh: 但命輕鴻毛，責重山岳，存沒同歸，毀譽一貫。
entries.en: Yet life is lighter than a goose feather and duty heavier than mountains; alive or dead we go together, ruin and praise one thread.
entries.literal: But life is lighter than a goose feather, duty heavier than mountains; alive or dead we return together, ruin and praise one strand.

entries.zh: 辭一官不減身累，增一職已黷朝經。
entries.en: To refuse one office does not lighten the body's load; to add one post already stains the court's rule.
entries.literal: To refuse one office does not lessen the body's burden; to add one post already stains the court's rule.

entries.zh: 便當自同體國，不爲飾讓。
entries.en: I should then be one body with the state and not make a show of yielding.
entries.literal: I should then be of one body with the state and not make a show of yielding.

entries.zh: 至於功均一匡，賞同千室，光宅近甸，奄有全邦，殞越爲期，不敢聞命，亦願曲留降鑒，卽垂聽許。
entries.en: As for merit like one rectification and reward like a thousand households, shining over the nearby suburbs and holding the whole realm—for my life's term I dare not hear the command; yet I beg you bend your lowered gaze and grant it at once.
entries.literal: As for merit equal to one rectification and reward like a thousand households, shining over the nearby suburbs, covering the whole realm—for the term of my life I dare not hear the command; yet I also beg you bend your lowered discernment and grant hearing at once.

entries.zh: 鉅平之懇誠必固，永昌之丹慊獲申，乃知君臣之道，綽有餘裕，苟曰易昭，敢守難奪。」
entries.en: Juping's earnest plea must stand, Yongchang's cinnabar heart may be declared—then one knows the way of ruler and minister still has room; if change is plain, I dare keep what is hard to take."
entries.literal: Juping's earnest plea must stand firm, Yongchang's cinnabar loyalty may be declared—then one knows the way of ruler and minister has ample surplus; if you say change is manifest, I dare keep what is hard to wrest away."

entries.zh: 帝惡其辭斥，甚慍，昉由是終建武中，位不過列校。
entries.en: The emperor hated the rebuke in his words and was furious; from this Fang through all Jianwu never rose above colonel.
entries.literal: The emperor hated that his words rebuked him, was greatly angered—Fang from this for the whole Jianwu period never rose beyond colonel rank.

entries.zh: 時明帝作相，因謂淹曰：「君昔在尚書中，非公事不妄行，在官寬猛能折衷；
entries.en: Mingdi was regent and told Yan, "In the secretariat you never moved without public business; in office you could balance mercy and severity;
entries.literal: Mingdi was then chief minister and said to Yan, "When you were in the Masters of Writing you never acted without public cause; in office you balanced lenity and severity;

entries.zh: 今爲南司，足以震肅百僚。」
entries.en: now as southern inspector you can shake the hundred officials sober."
entries.literal: now as southern inspector you are enough to awe and sober the hundred officials."

entries.zh: 淹答曰：「今日之事，可謂當官而行，更恐才劣志薄，不足以仰稱明旨耳。」
entries.en: Yan answered, "Today's charge is to act as the post requires; I only fear my gift is small and my resolve thin for your clear command."
entries.literal: Yan answered, "Today's task may be called doing the office as it demands; I only fear talent too slight and will too thin to rise to your bright intent."

entries.zh: 於是彈中書令謝朏，司徒左長史王繢、護軍長史庾弘遠，並以久疾不預山陵公事；
entries.en: He then impeached secretariat director Xie Fei, minister of education left chief of staff Wang Ji, and protecting-army chief clerk Yu Hongyuan—for long illness and absence from the imperial tomb rites;
entries.literal: Thereupon he impeached Secretariat Director Xie Fei, Left Chief of Staff to the Minister of Education Wang Ji, and Protecting Army Chief Clerk Yu Hongyuan—all for long illness and failure to attend the mountain tomb rites;

entries.zh: 又奏前益州刺史劉悛、梁州刺史陰智伯，並贓貨巨萬，輒收付廷尉治罪。
entries.en: he also charged former Yi inspector Liu Jun and former Liang inspector Yin Zhibo with bribes in the tens of thousands and sent them straight to the court for judgment.
entries.literal: he also memorialized against former Yi province inspector Liu Jun and former Liang inspector Yin Zhibo, both for accepting bribes in the tens of thousands, and had them taken at once to the Court for punishment.

entries.zh: 臨海太守沈昭略、永嘉太守庾曇隆，及諸郡二千石幷大縣官長，多被劾治，內外肅然。
entries.en: Linhai prefect Shen Zhaolue, Yongjia prefect Yu Tanlong, and many two-thousand-bushel magistrates in great districts were impeached and punished; inside and outside the court turned severe.
entries.literal: Linhai prefect Shen Zhaolue, Yongjia prefect Yu Tanlong, and magistrates of two thousand bushels in many commanderies and great counties were largely impeached and disciplined; within and without the court grew stern.

entries.zh: 明帝謂淹曰：「宋世以來，不復有嚴明中丞，君今日可謂近世獨步。」
entries.en: Mingdi told Yan, "Since the Song there has been no censor this stern; you may be called alone in our age."
entries.literal: Mingdi said to Yan, "Since Song times there has been no stern censor like you; today you may be called unmatched in recent generations."

entries.zh: 昉雅善屬文，尤長載筆，才思無窮，當世王公表奏，莫不請焉。
entries.en: Fang excelled at prose, especially at the brush; his talent never ran dry—every king and duke of the age asked him for memorials.
entries.literal: Fang by nature excelled at composing prose, especially at wielding the brush; his talent never ceased—for that age kings and dukes' memorials, none did not ask him.

entries.zh: 昉起草卽成，不加點竄。
entries.en: Fang's drafts were done at once, without a dot changed.
entries.literal: Fang's drafts were finished at once, without a dot or stroke changed.

entries.zh: 沈約一代詞宗，深所推挹。
entries.en: Shen Yue, master of the age's words, prized him deeply.
entries.literal: Shen Yue, master of a generation's words, deeply esteemed him.

entries.zh: 明帝崩，遷中書侍郎。
entries.en: When Emperor Ming died he was made secretariat gentleman.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming died, promoted to Secretariat Gentleman.

entries.zh: 永元末，爲司徒右長史。
entries.en: At Yongyuan's end he was right chief of staff of the secretariat.
entries.literal: At Yongyuan's end, became Right Chief of Staff of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 明帝卽位，爲車騎臨海王長史。
entries.en: When Mingdi succeeded, Yan became chief of staff to the valiant-cavalry prince of Linhai.
entries.literal: When Mingdi took the throne, Yan was made chief of staff to the Valiant Cavalry Prince of Linhai.

entries.zh: 俄除廷尉卿，加給事中，遷冠軍長史，加輔國將軍。
entries.en: Soon he was court commandant and supplicator in addition, then champion chief of staff and assistant state general.
entries.literal: Soon he was made Court Commandant with additional appointment as Supplicator, then champion chief of staff with additional appointment as Assistant State General.

entries.zh: 出爲宣城太守，將軍如故。
entries.en: He went out as Xuancheng prefect, general's rank unchanged.
entries.literal: He went out as Xuan prefect with his general's rank unchanged.

entries.zh: 在郡四年，還爲黃門侍郎、領步兵校尉，尋爲秘書監。
entries.en: Four years in office, then back to court as yellow-gate gentleman and infantry colonel, soon keeper of the palace library.
entries.literal: After four years in the commandery he returned as Yellow Gate Gentleman, concurrently Infantry Colonel, soon made Palace Library Director.

entries.zh: 永元中，崔慧景舉兵圍京城，衣冠悉投名刺，淹稱疾不往。
entries.en: In Yongyuan, Cui Huijing besieged the capital; every gentleman sent his card, but Yan pleaded sickness and stayed away.
entries.literal: In Yongyuan, Cui Huijing raised troops and besieged the capital; officials all sent calling cards—Yan claimed illness and did not go.

entries.zh: 及事平，世服其先見。
entries.en: When the storm passed, the world praised his foresight.
entries.literal: When the affair was settled, the age admired his foresight.

entries.zh: 東昏末，淹以秘書監兼衛尉，固辭不獲免，遂親職。
entries.en: At the end of Donghun's reign, Yan, as Palace Library Director, was also made Commandant of the Guards. He firmly declined but could not be excused, and so took up the office himself.
entries.literal: At the end of Donghun's reign, Yan, as Palace Library Director, was also made Commandant of the Guards. He firmly declined but could not be excused, and so took up the office himself.

entries.zh: 謂人曰：「此非吾任，路人所知，正取吾空名耳。
entries.en: He told someone, "This is not a post suited to me; even passersby know it. They are simply using my empty name.
entries.literal: He told someone, "This is not a post suited to me; even passersby know it. They are simply using my empty name.

entries.zh: 且天時人事，尋當飜覆。
entries.en: Besides, the timing of Heaven and the affairs of men will soon be overturned.
entries.literal: Besides, the timing of Heaven and the affairs of men will soon be overturned.

entries.zh: 孔子曰：『有文事者必有武備。』
entries.en: Confucius said, 'Those who have civil affairs must also have military preparations.'
entries.literal: Confucius said, 'Those who have civil affairs must also have military preparations.'

entries.zh: 臨事圖之，何憂之有？」
entries.en: If one plans when events arrive, what is there to worry about?"
entries.literal: If one plans when events arrive, what is there to worry about?"

entries.zh: 頃之，又副領軍王瑩。
entries.en: Soon afterward he again served as deputy to Wang Ying, Commander of the Army.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he again served as deputy to Wang Ying, Commander of the Army.

entries.zh: 及義師至新林，淹微服來奔，高祖板爲冠軍將軍，秘書監如故，尋兼司徒左長史。
entries.en: When the righteous army reached Xinlin, Yan came over in plain clothes. Gaozu provisionally appointed him Champion General, leaving him as Palace Library Director as before, and soon made him concurrently left chief clerk to the Minister over the Masses.
entries.literal: When the righteous army reached Xinlin, Yan came over in plain clothes. Gaozu provisionally appointed him Champion General, leaving him as Palace Library Director as before, and soon made him concurrently left chief clerk to the Minister over the Masses.

entries.zh: 中興元年，遷吏部尚書。
entries.en: In Zhongxing 1, he was transferred to Minister of Personnel.
entries.literal: In Zhongxing 1, he was transferred to Minister of Personnel.

entries.zh: 二年，轉相國右長史，冠軍將軍如故。
entries.en: In the second year, he was moved to right chief clerk to the Chancellor of State, remaining Champion General as before.
entries.literal: In the second year, he was moved to right chief clerk to the Chancellor of State, remaining Champion General as before.

entries.zh: 天監元年，爲散騎常侍、左衛將軍，封臨沮縣開國伯，食邑四百戶。
entries.en: In Tianjian 1, he became Regular Attendant and Left Guard General, and was enfeoffed as founding Count of Linju county with a fief of four hundred households.
entries.literal: In Tianjian 1, he became Regular Attendant and Left Guard General, and was enfeoffed as founding Count of Linju county with a fief of four hundred households.

entries.zh: 淹乃謂子弟曰：「吾本素宦，不求富貴，今之忝竊，遂至於此。
entries.en: Yan then told his sons and younger kinsmen, "I was originally a plain official and did not seek wealth or rank. Now, through undeserved favor, I have reached this point.
entries.literal: Yan then told his sons and younger kinsmen, "I was originally a plain official and did not seek wealth or rank. Now, through undeserved favor, I have reached this point.

entries.zh: 平生言止足之事，亦以備矣。
entries.en: What I have said all my life about knowing when to stop is now fully satisfied.
entries.literal: What I have said all my life about knowing when to stop is now fully satisfied.

entries.zh: 人生行樂耳，須富貴何時。
entries.en: Life is only for taking one's pleasure; when does one need wealth and rank?
entries.literal: Life is only for taking one's pleasure; when does one need wealth and rank?

entries.zh: 吾功名旣立，正欲歸身草萊耳。」
entries.en: Now that my achievements and name are established, I simply wish to return myself to the fields."
entries.literal: Now that my achievements and name are established, I simply wish to return myself to the fields."

entries.zh: 其年，以疾遷金紫光祿大夫，改封醴陵侯。
entries.en: That year, because of illness, he was transferred to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, and his fief was changed to Marquis of Liling.
entries.literal: That year, because of illness, he was transferred to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, and his fief was changed to Marquis of Liling.

entries.zh: 四年卒，時年六十二。
entries.en: He died in the fourth year, aged sixty-two.
entries.literal: He died in the fourth year, aged sixty-two.

entries.zh: 高祖爲素服舉哀。
entries.en: Gaozu wore plain mourning dress and held a lamentation for him.
entries.literal: Gaozu wore plain mourning dress and held a lamentation for him.

entries.zh: 賻錢三萬，布五十匹。
entries.en: He granted funeral gifts of thirty thousand cash and fifty bolts of cloth.
entries.literal: He granted funeral gifts of thirty thousand cash and fifty bolts of cloth.

entries.zh: 諡曰憲伯。
entries.en: His posthumous title was Xianbo.
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Xianbo.

entries.zh: 高祖克京邑，霸府初開，以昉爲驃騎記室參軍。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the capital and the hegemon's office opened, Fang was staff officer and recorder to the agile-cavalry general.
entries.literal: When Gaozu took the capital, as the hegemon's office first opened, Fang was made Staff Officer and Recorder to the General of Agile Cavalry.

entries.zh: 始高祖與昉遇竟陵王西邸，從容謂昉曰：「我登三府，當以卿爲記室。」
entries.en: When Gaozu first met Fang at the Prince of Jingling's western residence, he said lightly, "When I reach the three offices, you shall be my recorder."
entries.literal: When Gaozu first met Fang at the Prince of Jingling's Western Residence, he said with ease: "When I rise to the three offices, I shall make you my recorder."

entries.zh: 昉亦戲高祖曰：「我若登三事，當以卿爲騎兵。」
entries.en: Fang joked back, "If I reach the three ministries, you shall be my cavalry officer."
entries.literal: Fang also joked to Gaozu: "If I rise to the three ministries, I shall make you my cavalry officer."

entries.zh: 謂高祖善騎也。
entries.en: He meant Gaozu rode well.
entries.literal: Meaning Gaozu was skilled at riding.

entries.zh: 至是故引昉，符昔言焉。
entries.en: Now he drew Fang in—keeping the old jest.
entries.literal: Now therefore he drew Fang in—matching the old words.

entries.zh: 昉奉牋曰：「伏承以今月令辰，肅膺典策，德顯功高，光副四海，含生之倫，庇身有地；
entries.en: Fang submitted a letter: "I humbly receive that on this appointed day you solemnly take the canonical charter—virtue bright, merit high, light over the four seas; every living kind has ground to shelter its body;
entries.literal: Fang submitted a letter saying: "I humbly receive that on this month's appointed day you solemnly accept the canonical charter—virtue manifest, merit high, light paired with the four seas; every class that lives has ground to shelter its body;

entries.zh: 況昉受教君子，將二十年，咳唾爲恩，眄睞成飾，小人懷惠，顧知死所。
entries.en: As for Fang, I have received a gentleman's teaching nearly twenty years—cough and spit were grace, a glance was ornament; the small man who cherishes favor knows where to die.
entries.literal: As for Fang, he received a gentleman's teaching for nearly twenty years—cough and spit were grace, a glance became ornament; the small man cherishing favor knows where to die.

entries.zh: 昔承清宴，屬有緒言，提挈之旨，形乎善謔，豈謂多幸，斯言不渝。
entries.en: Once at a clear banquet there was a thread of words, shaped in friendly jest; who thought such fortune—that those words would hold.
entries.literal: Once at a clear banquet there was a thread of words—its lift and carry shaped in friendly jest; who thought such fortune—those words unfailing.

entries.zh: 雖情謬先覺，而迹淪驕餌，湯沐具而非弔，大廈構而相驩。
entries.en: Though feeling erred in foresight, my tracks fell among proud bait—bath and wash stood ready yet no condolence came, the great hall was built yet we rejoiced together.
entries.literal: Though feeling erred in foresight, traces fell among proud bait—bath and wash were ready yet no condolence, the great hall was built yet we rejoiced together.

entries.zh: 明公道冠二儀，勳超邃古，將使伊周奉轡，桓文扶轂，神功無紀，化物何稱。
entries.en: My lord's Way crowns the two principles, merit passes the deepest past—you will make Yi and Zhou hold the reins, Huan and Wen steady the wheels; divine work beyond record, transforming beings beyond name.
entries.literal: My lord's Way crowns the Two Principles, merit surpasses the deepest past—he will make Yi and Zhou hold the reins, Huan and Wen steady the wheels; divine work beyond record, transforming beings beyond name.

entries.zh: 府朝初建，俊賢驤首，惟此魚目，唐突璵璠。
entries.en: As the office first rose, worthy men tossed their heads—only this fish's eye bumped the pearl jade by mistake.
entries.literal: As the office first rose, worthy men tossed their heads—only this fish's eye carelessly bumped the jade of pearls.

entries.zh: 顧己循涯，𢉴知塵忝，千載一逢，再造難答。
entries.en: Looking back at my own bank, I know how dust stains the frontier—a meeting once in a thousand ages, a rebirth hard to repay.
entries.literal: Looking back at my own bank, I know how dust clings to the frontier—a meeting once in a thousand ages, a rebirth hard to answer.

entries.zh: 雖則殞越，且知非報。」
entries.en: Though I overstep and die, I know it is not repayment."
entries.literal: Though I will overstep and die, I know it is not repayment."

entries.zh: 梁臺建，禪讓文誥，多昉所具。
entries.en: When the Liang terrace rose, the abdication documents were mostly Fang's work.
entries.literal: When the Liang terrace was raised, the abdication documents were mostly Fang's work.

entries.zh: 高祖踐阼，拜黃門侍郎，遷吏部郎中，尋以本官掌著作。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne he was yellow-gate gentleman, then personnel section director, soon in that post supervising the compilation office as well.
entries.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, appointed Yellow Gate Gentleman, promoted to Personnel Section Director, soon in that office he also supervised the Compilation Office.

entries.zh: 子蒍襲封嗣，自丹陽尹丞爲長城令，有罪削爵。
entries.en: His son Wei took the title, rose from Danyang aide to magistrate of Changcheng, then lost the fief for a crime.
entries.literal: His son Wei inherited the fief; from Assistant to the Danyang Intendant he became magistrate of Changcheng; for a crime his noble rank was stripped.

entries.zh: 普通四年，高祖追念淹功，復封蒍吳昌伯，邑如先。
entries.en: In Putong year 4 Gaozu remembered Yan's service and made Wei marquis of Wuchang again, with the old fief.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Putong, Gaozu recalled Yan's merit and re-enfeoffed Wei as Marquis of Wuchang, fief as before.

entries.zh: 六年春，出爲寧朔將軍、新安太守。
entries.en: In the sixth year's spring he went out as pacify-the-north general and administrator of Xin'an.
entries.literal: Sixth year spring, went out as Pacify-the-North General, Administrator of Xin'an.

entries.zh: 在郡不事邊幅，率然曳杖，徒行邑郭，民通辭訟者，就路決焉。
entries.en: In the commandery he did not trouble about dress; staff in hand, he walked the town on foot—whoever brought suit or plea, he judged on the road.
entries.literal: In the commandery he did not trouble about dress; simply trailing his staff, he walked the town on foot—people bringing suits and pleas, he judged on the road.

entries.zh: 爲政清省，吏民便之。
entries.en: His rule was pure and spare; officials and people found it easy.
entries.literal: His governance was pure and spare; officials and people found it easy.

entries.zh: 視事朞歲，卒於官舍，時年四十九。
entries.en: After a full year in office he died in the government house, at forty-nine.
entries.literal: After a full year in office, he died in the government house, age forty-nine.

entries.zh: 闔境痛惜，百姓共立祠堂於城南。
entries.en: The whole territory grieved; the people together built a shrine south of the city.
entries.literal: The whole territory grieved; the people together built a shrine south of the city.

entries.zh: 高祖聞問，卽日舉哀，哭之甚慟。
entries.en: When Gaozu heard, that very day he mourned and wept with extreme grief.
entries.literal: When Gaozu heard, that very day he held mourning and wept with extreme grief.

entries.zh: 追贈太常卿，諡曰敬子。
entries.en: Posthumously he was made grand master of ceremonies, posthumous title Jingzi.
entries.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of Ceremonies, posthumous title Jingzi.

entries.zh: 昉好交結，獎進士友，得其延譽者，率多升擢，故衣冠貴遊，莫不爭與交好，坐上賓客，恒有數十。
entries.en: Fang loved friendship and lifted scholar friends—those who won his praise mostly rose; so gentry and nobles all vied to know him, and guests at his seat were always several tens.
entries.literal: Fang loved to bind friendships and encourage scholar friends—those who gained his praise mostly rose in rank; thus the gentry and nobles all vied to befriend him; guests at his seat were always several tens.

entries.zh: 時人慕之，號曰任君，言如漢之三君也。
entries.en: Men of the age admired this and called him Lord Ren—as with the Three Lords of Han.
entries.literal: Men of the age admired this and called him Lord Ren—meaning like the Three Lords of Han.

entries.zh: 陳郡殷芸與建安太守到溉書曰：「哲人云亡，儀表長謝。
entries.en: Yin Yun of Chen commandery wrote to Dao Gai, administrator of Jian'an: "The wise man has passed; the compass fails.
entries.literal: Yin Yun of Chen commandery wrote to Administrator of Jian'an Dao Gai: "The wise man has passed; the compass fails.

entries.zh: 元龜何寄？
entries.en: To whom does the divine tortoise belong?
entries.literal: To whom does the divine tortoise belong?

entries.zh: 指南誰託？」
entries.en: Who will carry the lodestone?"
entries.literal: Who will carry the lodestone?"

entries.zh: 其爲士友所推如此。
entries.en: Thus gentlemen friends pushed him.
entries.literal: Thus was he pushed by gentlemen friends.

entries.zh: 昉不治生產，至乃居無室宅。
entries.en: Fang did not manage livelihood—so much so that he had no house.
entries.literal: Fang did not manage livelihood—so much so that he had no dwelling.

entries.zh: 世或譏其多乞貸，亦隨復散之親故。
entries.en: The world sometimes mocked him for much begging and borrowing, yet he at once gave it away to kin and friends.
entries.literal: The world sometimes mocked him for much begging and borrowing, yet he at once gave it away to kin and friends.

entries.zh: 昉常歎曰：「知我亦以叔則，不知我亦以叔則。」
entries.en: Fang often sighed, "Those who know me know me by Uncle Ze; those who do not know me also know me by Uncle Ze."
entries.literal: Fang often sighed: "Those who know me know me by Uncle Ze; those who do not know me also know me by Uncle Ze."

entries.zh: 昉墳籍無所不見，家雖貧，聚書至萬餘卷，率多異本。
entries.en: Fang had seen every book in the land—though his house was poor, his library held more than ten thousand scrolls, mostly rare editions.
entries.literal: Fang's library holdings he had seen everywhere—though the house was poor, books gathered to more than ten thousand scrolls, mostly rare editions.

entries.zh: 昉卒後，高祖使學士賀縱共沈約勘其書目，官所無者，就昉家取之。
entries.en: After Fang died, Gaozu had Academician He Zong and Shen Yue collate his catalog—what the office lacked, they took from Fang's house.
entries.literal: After Fang died, Gaozu had Academician He Zong together with Shen Yue collate his book catalog—what the office lacked, they took from Fang's house.

entries.zh: 昉所著文章數十萬言，盛行於世。
entries.en: Fang's writings ran to several hundred thousand words and flourished in the world.
entries.literal: Fang's compositions ran to several hundred thousand words and flourished in the world.

entries.zh: 永明初，衛將軍王儉領丹陽尹，復引爲主簿。
entries.en: Early in Yongming, Wang Jian of the guards, as Danyang intendant, drew him back as chief clerk.
entries.literal: Early Yongming, General of the Guards Wang Jian took Danyang as intendant and again recruited him as chief clerk.

entries.zh: 儉雅欽重昉，以爲當時無輩。
entries.en: Jian prized him deeply and said no man of the time matched him.
entries.literal: Jian deeply admired Fang and thought there was no equal in the age.

entries.zh: 遷司徒刑獄參軍事，入爲尚書殿中郎，轉司徒竟陵王記室參軍，以父憂去職。
entries.en: He rose to prison staff in the criminal office, then palace attendant in the secretariat, then recorder to the Prince of Jingling, and left for his father's mourning.
entries.literal: Promoted to Criminal Office Prison staff officer, entered as Attendant of the Palace Department in the Masters of Writing, then transferred to Staff Officer and Recorder to the Prince of Jingling of the Secretariat, left office for father's mourning.

entries.zh: 性至孝，居喪盡禮。
entries.en: He was filial to the bone; in mourning he kept every rite.
entries.literal: By nature most filial; in mourning he observed every rite.

entries.zh: 服闋，續遭母憂，常廬于墓側，哭泣之地，草爲不生。
entries.en: When that mourning ended, his mother died; he kept a hut by the grave, and where he wept the grass would not grow.
entries.literal: When mourning ended, he again suffered mother's mourning; he often lodged beside the tomb—in the place of his weeping grass would not grow.

entries.zh: 服除，拜太子步兵校尉、管東宮書記。
entries.en: When mourning ended he was heir-apparent infantry colonel, keeper of the eastern palace papers.
entries.literal: When mourning ended, appointed Heir Apparent Infantry Colonel, in charge of Eastern Palace records.

entries.zh: 馳鶩之俗，澆薄之倫，無不操權衡，秉纖纊。
entries.en: In the rushing-grouse age, the thin and shallow sort—none fails to hold the balance-scale and grasp gossamer.
entries.literal: In the rushing-grouse age, the thin and shallow sort, none fails to hold the balance-scale and grasp the gossamer.

entries.zh: 衡所以揣其輕重，纊所以屬其鼻息。
entries.en: The scale weighs heaviness and lightness; the gossamer tests their breath.
entries.literal: The scale weighs their heaviness and lightness; the gossamer tests their breath.

entries.zh: 若衡不能舉，纊不能飛，雖顏、冉龍翰鳳＜芻鳥＞，曾、史，蘭熏雪白，舒、向金玉，淵海卿、雲，黼黻河漢，視若遊塵。
entries.en: If the scale cannot lift and the gossamer cannot fly, though Yan and Ran had dragon sinews and phoenix pinions, Zeng and Shi orchid scent and snow-white, Shu and Xiang gold, jade, and the abyss-sea, Qing and Yun embroidery and the Milky Way—they are wandering dust.
entries.literal: If the scale cannot lift and the gossamer cannot fly, though Yan and Ran had dragon sinews and phoenix pinions, Zeng and Shi orchid scent and snow-white, Shu and Xiang gold, jade, and the abyss-sea, Qing and Yun embroidery and the Milky Way—they are seen as wandering dust.

entries.zh: 遇同土梗，莫肯費其半菽，罕有落其一毛。
entries.en: Met as clay puppets, none spends half a bean; rarely does one lose a single hair.
entries.literal: Met as clay puppets, none will spend half a bean; rarely does one lose a single hair.

entries.zh: 若衡重錙銖，纊微彯撇，雖共工之蒐慝，驩兜之掩義，南荊之跋扈，東陵之巨猾，皆爲匍匐委蛇，折枝舐痔，金膏翠羽將其意，脂韋便辟導其誠。
entries.en: If the scale weighs heavy as a cash-weight and the gossamer stirs the slightest breath, though Gong Gong's evil, Huan Dou's masked righteousness, southern Jing's arrogance, eastern mound's great knavery—all crawl and writhe, break branches and lick hemorrhoids; gold paste and kingfisher plumes suit their intent, grease and rush smooth their sincerity.
entries.literal: If the scale weighs heavy as a cash-weight and the gossamer stirs the slightest breath, though Gong Gong's search for evil, Huan Dou's masking of righteousness, the southern Jing's arrogance, the eastern mound's great knavery—all crawl and writhe, break branches and lick hemorrhoids; gold paste and kingfisher plumes suit their intent, grease and rush smooth the way to their sincerity.

entries.zh: 故輪蓋所遊，必非夷、惠之室；
entries.en: Thus wherever carriage wheels travel, it is not Bo Yi and Liu Xiahui's house;
entries.literal: Thus wherever carriage wheels travel, it cannot be Bo Yi and Liu Xiahui's house;

entries.zh: 苞苴所入，實行張、霍之家。
entries.en: wherever bribes enter, it is truly Zhang and Huo's home.
entries.literal: wherever bribes enter, it is truly Zhang and Huo's home.

entries.zh: 謀而後動，芒毫寡忒。
entries.en: They plot before they act—not a hair's error.
entries.literal: They plot before they act; not a hair's error.

entries.zh: 是曰量交，其流五也。
entries.en: This is measure friendship—the fifth current.
entries.literal: This is measure friendship—its current is the fifth.

entries.zh: 梁書卷第十四 列傳第八
entries.en: Book of Liang, Volume 14, Biographies 8
entries.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 14, Biographies 8

entries.zh: 謝朏字敬沖，陳郡陽夏人也。
entries.en: Xie Fei, styled Jingchong, came from Yangxia in Chen commandery.
entries.literal: Xie Fei, styled Jingchong, was a native of Yangxia in Chen commandery.

entries.zh: 祖弘微，宋太常卿，父莊，右光祿大夫，並有名前代。
entries.en: His grandfather Hongwei had been Song grand minister of ceremonies; his father Zhuang, right grand master of splendid happiness—both were celebrated in earlier ages.
entries.literal: His grandfather Hongwei was Song Grand Minister of Ceremonies; his father Zhuang was Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness—both were famed in earlier generations.

entries.zh: 朏幼聰慧，莊器之，常置左右。
entries.en: Fei was bright as a boy; Zhuang prized him and never let him leave his side.
entries.literal: Fei was clever from childhood; Zhuang treasured him and kept him always at his side.

entries.zh: 年十歲，能屬文。
entries.en: At ten he could write finished prose.
entries.literal: At ten he could compose literary pieces.

entries.zh: 莊游土山賦詩，使朏命篇，朏攬筆便就。
entries.en: When Zhuang toured Mount Tu and wrote verse, he gave Fei the theme; Fei took brush and finished on the spot.
entries.literal: When Zhuang visited Mount Tu and composed poetry, he set Fei a topic; Fei took up the brush and finished at once.

entries.zh: 琅邪王景文謂莊曰：「賢子足稱神童，復爲後來特達。」
entries.en: Prince Jing of Langye, Wang Jingwen, told Zhuang, "Your worthy son may be called a wonder child—a singular talent still to come."
entries.literal: Prince Jing of Langye, Wang Jingwen, said to Zhuang: "Your worthy son deserves the name wonder child; he will be a singular talent yet to come."

entries.zh: 莊笑，因撫朏背曰：「真吾家千金。」
entries.en: Zhuang laughed, stroked Fei's back, and said, "Truly the thousand gold of our house."
entries.literal: Zhuang laughed, stroked Fei's back, and said: "Truly the thousand gold of our house."

entries.zh: 孝武帝游姑孰，勑莊攜朏從駕，詔使爲《洞井贊》，於坐奏之。
entries.en: Emperor Xiaowu toured Gudu, ordered Zhuang to bring Fei in the train, and commanded an "Ode on the Cave Well," which Fei presented in the hall.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaowu toured Gudu; he ordered Zhuang to bring Fei in the entourage and commanded him to compose "Ode on the Cave Well," which he presented in the assembly.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「雖小，奇童也。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Small as he is, a wonder child."
entries.literal: The emperor said, "Small though he is, a wonder child."

entries.zh: 齊高帝爲驃騎將軍輔政，選朏爲長史，勑與河南褚炫、濟陽江斅、彭城劉俁俱入侍宋帝，時號爲天子四友。
entries.en: Qi Emperor Gao, as regent rapid-cavalry general, made Fei his chief of staff and sent him with Chu Xuan of Henan, Jiang Jiao of Jiyang, and Liu Hou of Pengcheng to attend the Song emperor—men called them the Son of Heaven's Four Friends.
entries.literal: Qi Emperor Gao, as Rapid Cavalry General assisting government, chose Fei as chief of staff and ordered him with Chu Xuan of Henan, Jiang Jiao of Jiyang, and Liu Hou of Pengcheng to attend the Song emperor—they were called the Son of Heaven's Four Friends.

entries.zh: 續拜侍中，並掌中書、散騎二省詔冊。
entries.en: He was further made attendant-in-ordinary and jointly managed secretariat and scattered-cavalry edicts.
entries.literal: He was further made Attendant-in-Ordinary, jointly managing the edicts of the Secretariat and Scattered Cavalry bureaus.

entries.zh: 高帝進太尉，又以朏爲長史，帶南東海太守。
entries.en: When Gao became grand marshal, he again made Fei chief of staff with Southern Donghai prefect in addition.
entries.literal: When Gao advanced to Grand Marshal, he again made Fei chief of staff with concurrent Southern Donghai prefect.

entries.zh: 高帝方圖禪代，思佐命之臣，以朏有重名，深所欽屬。
entries.en: Gao was plotting the abdication and wanted ministers to crown the change; Fei's great name made Gao admire and lean on him.
entries.literal: Gao was plotting to seize the throne and sought ministers who would aid the mandate; because Fei had great renown, he deeply admired and relied on him.

entries.zh: 論魏、晉故事，因曰：「晉革命時事久兆，石苞不早勸晉文，死方慟哭，方之馮異，非知機也。」
entries.en: Discussing Wei and Jin precedents, he said, "When Jin took the mandate the omen was old; Shi Bao did not urge Wen of Jin in time—he wept only at death. Set beside Feng Yi, that is not reading the hour."
entries.literal: Discussing Wei and Jin precedents, he said: "When Jin changed the mandate the signs were long visible; Shi Bao did not early urge Wen of Jin—he only wailed at death. Compared to Feng Yi, that is not knowing the moment."

entries.zh: 朏答曰：「昔魏臣有勸魏武卽帝位者，魏武曰：『如有用我，其爲周文王乎！』
entries.en: Fei answered, "Of old a Wei minister urged Martial Emperor of Wei to take the throne; Martial Emperor said, 'If Heaven would use me, would I not be King Wen of Zhou!'
entries.literal: Fei answered: "Of old among Wei ministers some urged Martial Emperor of Wei to take the throne; Martial Emperor said, 'If heaven would use me, would I not be like King Wen of Zhou!'

entries.zh: 晉文世事魏氏，將必身終北面；
entries.en: Wen of Jin served the house of Wei and was bound to end his days facing north;
entries.literal: Wen of Jin served the house of Wei and was bound to die facing north;

entries.zh: 假使魏早依唐虞故事，亦當三讓彌高。」
entries.en: had Wei early followed Yao and Shun, he would still have yielded three times to the utmost height."
entries.literal: had Wei early followed the model of Yao and Shun, he would still have thrice yielded to the highest degree."

entries.zh: 帝不悅。
entries.en: The emperor was displeased.
entries.literal: The emperor was displeased.

entries.zh: 更引王儉爲左長史，以朏侍中，領秘書監。
entries.en: He brought in Wang Jian as left chief of staff and kept Fei as attendant-in-ordinary directing the imperial library.
entries.literal: He brought in Wang Jian as left chief of staff and kept Fei as attendant-in-ordinary with charge of the Imperial Library.

entries.zh: 及齊受禪，朏當日在直，百僚陪位，侍中當解璽，朏佯不知，曰：「有何公事？」
entries.en: When Qi received the abdication, Fei was on duty; the hundred officials took their stations; the attendant-in-ordinary should unseal the seal. Fei played ignorant and said, "What business is there?"
entries.literal: When Qi received the abdication, Fei was on duty that day; all officials took their places; the attendant-in-ordinary should unseal the imperial seal. Fei pretended not to know and said, "What business is there?"

entries.zh: 傳詔云：「解璽授齊王。」
entries.en: The relay edict said, "Unseal and hand it to the King of Qi."
entries.literal: The relay edict said, "Unseal and transfer to the King of Qi."

entries.zh: 朏曰：「齊自應有侍中。」
entries.en: Fei said, "Qi ought to have its own attendant-in-ordinary."
entries.literal: Fei said, "Qi surely has its own attendant-in-ordinary."

entries.zh: 乃引枕臥。
entries.en: He fetched a pillow and lay down.
entries.literal: He took a pillow and lay down.

entries.zh: 傳詔懼，乃使稱疾，欲取兼人。
