entries.en: The relay messenger panicked and had him claim illness to bring in a stand-in.
entries.literal: The relay messenger was afraid; they had him feign illness to fetch a substitute.

entries.zh: 朏曰：「我無疾，何所道。」
entries.en: Fei said, "I am not ill; what is there to report?"
entries.literal: Fei said, "I have no illness; what is there to say?"

entries.zh: 遂朝服，步出東掖門，乃得車，仍還宅。
entries.en: He dressed in court robes, walked out the eastern side gate, found a carriage, and went home.
entries.literal: He put on court dress, walked out the eastern side gate, got a carriage, and returned home.

entries.zh: 是日遂以王儉爲侍中解璽。
entries.en: That day Wang Jian was made attendant-in-ordinary to unseal the seal.
entries.literal: That day Wang Jian was made attendant-in-ordinary to unseal the seal.

entries.zh: 旣而武帝言於高帝，請誅朏。
entries.en: Soon Emperor Wu of Qi spoke to Gao and asked to kill Fei.
entries.literal: Soon Emperor Wu of Qi spoke to Gao, asking to execute Fei.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「殺之則遂成其名，正應容之度外耳。」
entries.en: Gao said, "Kill him and you make his name; better to spare him beyond the pale."
entries.literal: Gao said, "Kill him and his name is made; better to tolerate him beyond the pale."

entries.zh: 遂廢于家。
entries.en: He was dismissed and kept at home.
entries.literal: He was dismissed and kept at home.

entries.zh: 覽爲人美風神，善辭令，高祖深器之。
entries.en: Lan had a handsome presence and gift for speech; the Founding Emperor prized him greatly.
entries.literal: Lan was a man of fine bearing and spirit, skilled in eloquence; Gaozu deeply valued him.

entries.zh: 嘗侍座，受敕與侍中王暕爲詩答贈。
entries.en: Once in attendance he was ordered, with Attendant Wang Jian, to compose answering verse for a gift exchange.
entries.literal: Once while attending in his seat, he received an edict to compose an answering poem with Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Jian in reply to an exchange of gifts.

entries.zh: 其文甚工。
entries.en: The piece was finely wrought.
entries.literal: His writing was very skilled.

entries.zh: 高祖善之，仍使重作，復合旨。
entries.en: The Emperor approved and asked for another; again it fit the wish.
entries.literal: Gaozu was pleased and had him write again; it again matched intent.

entries.zh: 乃賜詩云：「雙文旣後進，二少實名家；
entries.en: He granted a poem: "Twin Wen are latecomers yet rising; both young men are true great clans;
entries.literal: Then he bestowed a poem that read: "Both Wen are rising talents; the two youths are truly famous houses;

entries.zh: 豈伊止棟隆，信乃俱國華。」
entries.en: could they only lift the ridgebeam? Surely both are the realm's finest blossoms."
entries.literal: how could they merely bear up the ridgepole's height? Truly both are the state's finest flowers."

entries.zh: 以母憂去職。
entries.en: He left his post for mourning his mother.
entries.literal: On his mother's mourning he left office.

entries.zh: 服闋，除中庶子，又掌吏部郎事，尋除吏部郎，遷侍中。
entries.en: After mourning he became heir-apparent companion, handled Personnel bureau director duties, soon became director, then attendant.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he was made Palace Companion to the Heir Apparent, also handled the Bureau Director of Personnel's affairs, soon made Bureau Director, then promoted Attendant-in-Ordinary.

entries.zh: 覽頗樂酒，因醼席與散騎常侍蕭琛辭相詆毀，爲有司所奏。
entries.en: Lan loved wine; at a feast he and Regular Attendant Xiao Chen traded insults, and the authorities memorialized against them.
entries.literal: Lan was quite fond of wine; at a banquet with Regular Attendant of the Writes-on-the-Fast Xiao Chen they exchanged abusive words and were reported by the authorities.

entries.zh: 高祖以覽年少不直，出爲中權長史。
entries.en: The Emperor, holding Lan young and not upright, sent him out as Central Guards chief clerk.
entries.literal: Gaozu, because Lan was young and not straightforward, sent him out as Chief Clerk of the Central Guards.

entries.zh: 頃之，敕掌東宮管記，遷明威將軍、新安太守。
entries.en: Soon he was ordered to keep Eastern Palace records, promoted Bright Might general and Xin'an administrator.
entries.literal: Shortly after, he was ordered to manage Eastern Palace records, promoted General of Bright Might and Administrator of Xin'an.

entries.zh: 永明元年，起家拜通直散騎常侍，累遷侍中，領國子博士。
entries.en: In Yongming's first year he began as regular palace attendant-in-ordinary, rose to attendant-in-ordinary, and led the national university as erudite.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongming he began as Regular Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary, rose through offices to Attendant-in-Ordinary with charge as National University Erudite.

entries.zh: 五年，出爲冠軍將軍、義興太守，加秩中二千石。
entries.en: In the fifth year he went out as champion general and Yixing prefect with middle two-thousand-bushel rank.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he went out as Champion General and Yixing prefect, with rank of middle two thousand bushels.

entries.zh: 在郡不省雜事，悉付綱紀，曰：「吾不能作主者吏，但能作太守耳。」
entries.en: In the commandery he ignored routine business and gave it all to clerks, saying, "I cannot be the clerk in charge—I can only be the prefect."
entries.literal: In the commandery he did not oversee miscellaneous affairs, giving all to the clerks, and said, "I cannot be the clerk who runs things; I can only be the prefect."

entries.zh: 視事三年，徵都官尚書、中書令。
entries.en: After three years he was recalled as director of the court offices and palace secretariat director.
entries.literal: After three years in office he was recalled as Director of the Court Offices and Palace Secretariat Director.

entries.zh: 隆昌元年，復爲侍中，領新安王師。
entries.en: In Longchang's first year he was again attendant-in-ordinary, leading tutor to the prince of Xin'an.
entries.literal: In the first year of Longchang he was again Attendant-in-Ordinary, leading tutor to the Prince of Xin'an.

entries.zh: 未拜，固求外出。
entries.en: Before investiture he begged hard to go out on assignment.
entries.literal: Before taking the appointment he firmly sought to go out on assignment.

entries.zh: 仍爲征虜將軍、吳興太守，受召便述職。
entries.en: He was still made general who punishes barbarians and Wu-xing prefect; summoned, he took office at once.
entries.literal: He was still made General Who Punishes Barbarians and Wu-xing prefect; on summons he took office at once.

entries.zh: 時明帝謀入嗣位，朝之舊臣皆引參謀策。
entries.en: Mingdi was then plotting to enter the succession; old courtiers were all drawn into counsel.
entries.literal: Mingdi was then plotting succession to the throne; old ministers of the court were all drawn into counsel.

entries.zh: 朏內圖止足，且實避事。
entries.en: Fei inwardly sought enough and truly meant to avoid affairs.
entries.literal: Fei inwardly sought sufficiency and truly wished to avoid affairs.

entries.zh: 弟𤅢，時爲吏部尚書。
entries.en: His brother Yin was then director of the ministry of personnel.
entries.literal: His brother Yin was then Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 朏至郡，致𤅢數斛酒，遺書曰：「可力飲此，勿豫人事。」
entries.en: At the commandery he sent Yin several piculs of wine with a letter: "Drink this hard; keep out of men's business."
entries.literal: Arriving at the commandery, he sent Yin several piculs of wine with a letter that said, "Drink this with all your strength; do not meddle in human affairs."

entries.zh: 朏居郡每不治，而常務聚斂，衆頗譏之，亦不屑也。
entries.en: In the commandery Fei seldom governed yet always gathered revenue; many mocked him, and he did not care.
entries.literal: In the commandery Fei rarely governed yet constantly pursued levies; many criticized him, and he did not care.

entries.zh: 建武四年，詔徵爲侍中、中書令，遂抗表不應召。
entries.en: In Jianwu's fourth year an edict summoned him as attendant-in-ordinary and palace secretariat director; he memorialized and refused.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Jianwu an edict summoned him as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Palace Secretariat Director; he submitted a memorial refusing the summons.

entries.zh: 遣諸子還京師，獨與母留，築室郡之西郭。
entries.en: He sent his sons to the capital, stayed alone with his mother, and built a house west of the commandery wall.
entries.literal: He sent his sons back to the capital but stayed alone with his mother, building a house west of the commandery seat.

entries.zh: 明帝下詔曰：「夫超然榮觀，風流自遠；
entries.en: Mingdi issued an edict: "To stand beyond glory is to see the world from far off;
entries.literal: Mingdi issued an edict: "One who stands apart from glory views the world from afar;

entries.zh: 蹈彼幽人，英華罕值。
entries.en: to walk the hermit's way is to bloom in solitude.
entries.literal: one who treads the hermit's path is rarely met in full flower.

entries.zh: 故長揖楚相，見稱南國；
entries.en: hence the long bow of the Chu minister won praise in the southern states;
entries.literal: Hence the long bow to the Chu minister won praise in the southern states;

entries.zh: 高謝漢臣，取貴良史。
entries.en: the Han worthy's lofty refusal won honor from fine historians.
entries.literal: the Han worthy's high refusal won honor from fine historians.

entries.zh: 新除侍中、中書令朏，早藉羽儀，夙標清尚，登朝樹績，出守馳聲。
entries.en: The newly appointed attendant-in-ordinary and palace secretariat director Fei long wore court insignia and from youth bore a clear name; in court he built merit, abroad he made his name heard.
entries.literal: The newly appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and Palace Secretariat Director Fei long bore the court insignia and from youth bore a pure reputation; in court he built merit, going out he made his name heard.

entries.zh: 遂斂跡康衢，拂衣林沚，抱箕潁之餘芳，甘憔悴而無悶。
entries.en: Then he gathered his steps from the broad highway and shook dust from forest robes, keeping the after-scent of Jiqian and Ying, glad in lean exile without regret.
entries.literal: Then he gathered his steps from the broad highway and shook the dust from his forest robes, embracing the lingering fragrance of Jiqian and Ying, content in lean exile without regret.

entries.zh: 撫事懷人，載留欽想。
entries.en: Hearing his story, one keeps him in honored thought.
entries.literal: Hearing of his deeds one keeps him in honored thought.

entries.zh: 宜加優禮，用旌素概。
entries.en: Let added courtesy mark his plain integrity.
entries.literal: He should receive added courtesy to mark his plain integrity.

entries.zh: 可賜床帳褥席，俸以卿祿，常出在所。」
entries.en: Grant bed curtains and padded mats, salary at minister rank, always sent to his dwelling."
entries.literal: Grant bed curtains and padded mats, salary at minister rank, always provided at his dwelling."

entries.zh: 時國子祭酒廬江何胤亦抗表還會稽。
entries.en: At that time national university chancellor He Yin of Lujiang also memorialized to return to Kuaiji.
entries.literal: At that time National University Chancellor He Yin of Lujiang also submitted a memorial to return to Kuaiji.

entries.zh: 永元二年，詔徵朏爲散騎常侍、中書監，胤爲散騎常侍、太常卿，並不屈。
entries.en: In Yongyuan's second year an edict summoned Fei as regular palace attendant-in-ordinary and imperial library director, and Yin as regular palace attendant-in-ordinary and grand minister of ceremonies—neither came.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yongyuan an edict summoned Fei as Regular Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary and Imperial Library Director, and Yin as Regular Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Minister of Ceremonies—neither yielded.

entries.zh: 三年，又詔徵朏爲侍中、太子少傅，胤散騎常侍、太子詹事。
entries.en: In the third year another edict summoned Fei as attendant-in-ordinary and junior tutor to the crown prince, and Yin as regular palace attendant-in-ordinary and crown prince household superintendent.
entries.literal: In the third year another edict summoned Fei as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince, and Yin as Regular Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary and Crown Prince Household Superintendent.

entries.zh: 時東昏皆下在所，使迫遣之，值義師已近，故並得不到。
entries.en: By then Emperor Donghun was confined at the palace; messengers were sent to hurry them, but the righteous army was already near, so neither was reached.
entries.literal: By then Emperor Donghun was under house arrest at the palace; messengers were sent to hurry them, but the righteous army was already near, so neither could be fetched.

entries.zh: 十二年春，出爲吳興太守。
entries.en: In the twelfth year's spring he went out as Wuxing administrator.
entries.literal: In spring of year twelve he went out as Administrator of Wuxing.

entries.zh: 中書舍人黃睦之家居烏程，子弟專橫，前太守皆折節事之。
entries.en: Secretariat gentleman Huang Muzhi's house was in Wucheng; his kin bullied the circuit, and every prior administrator bowed to them.
entries.literal: Palace Secretariat Gentleman Huang Muzhi's family lived in Wucheng; his sons and nephews were overbearing, and former administrators all bent the knee to serve them.

entries.zh: 覽未到郡，睦之子弟來迎，覽逐去其船，杖吏爲通者。
entries.en: Before Lan arrived, Muzhi's kin came to meet him; he drove off their boats and whipped the clerks who had let them through.
entries.literal: Before Lan reached the commandery, Muzhi's kin came to welcome him; Lan drove off their boats and beat the clerks who had cleared the way for them.

entries.zh: 自是睦之家杜門不出，不敢與公私關通。
entries.en: After that Muzhi's clan stayed indoors and dared no public or private traffic.
entries.literal: From then on Muzhi's household shut their doors and did not venture out, daring no private or official dealings.

entries.zh: 郡境多劫，爲東道患，覽下車肅然，一境清謐。
entries.en: Robbery was rife and troubled the eastern roads; when Lan took office the whole district grew orderly and still.
entries.literal: The commandery had many robbers and was a scourge on the eastern route; when Lan took his carriage down the district grew stern and the whole region grew quiet.

entries.zh: 初，齊明帝及覽父綍、東海徐孝嗣，並爲吳興，號稱名守，覽皆欲過之！
entries.en: Once Qi Mingdi, Lan's father Fu, and Donghai's Xu Xiaosi had all ruled Wuxing as famed administrators—Lan meant to outdo them all!
entries.literal: Earlier Qi Mingdi, Lan's father Fu, and Xu Xiaosi of Donghai had all governed Wuxing and been called famed administrators—Lan wished to surpass them all!

entries.zh: 昔覽在新安頗聚斂，至是遂稱廉潔，時人方之王懷祖。
entries.en: Once in Xin'an he had been grasping; now he was called incorrupt, and the age compared him to Wang Huainzu.
entries.literal: Long ago in Xin'an Lan had greatly gathered wealth; now he was praised as pure and clean, and men compared him to Wang Huainzu.

entries.zh: 卒于官，時年三十七。
entries.en: He died in office at thirty-seven.
entries.literal: He died in office at age thirty-seven.

entries.zh: 詔贈中書令。
entries.en: He was posthumously made palace library director.
entries.literal: An edict posthumously made him Director of the Palace Library.

entries.zh: 子罕，早卒。
entries.en: His son Han died early.
entries.literal: His son Han died young.

entries.zh: 及高祖平京邑，進位相國，表請朏、胤曰：「夫窮則獨善，達以兼濟。
entries.en: When Gaozu pacified the capital and advanced to chancellor of state, he memorialized for Fei and Yin, saying, "In want one keeps to oneself; risen, one aids all.
entries.literal: When Gaozu pacified the capital and advanced to Chancellor of State, he memorialized requesting Fei and Yin, saying: "When poor, one keeps to oneself; when risen, one aids all.

entries.zh: 雖出處之道，其揆不同，用舍惟時，賢哲是蹈。
entries.en: Though the way of going out and staying in differs in measure, use and refusal follow the hour, and the wise tread it.
entries.literal: Though the way of going out and staying in differs in measure, timing decides employment, and the wise tread accordingly.

entries.zh: 前新除侍中、太子少傅朏，前新除散騎常侍、太子詹事、都亭侯胤，羽儀世胄，徽猷冠冕，道業德聲，康濟雅俗。
entries.en: The former newly appointed attendant-in-ordinary and junior tutor to the crown prince Fei, and the former newly appointed regular palace attendant-in-ordinary, crown prince household superintendent, and marquis of Duting Yin—feathered heirs of noble lines, emblem bearers of the crown, conduct and fame a balm to refined custom.
entries.literal: The former newly appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Fei, and the former newly appointed Regular Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary, Crown Prince Household Superintendent, and Marquis of Duting Yin—both are feathered scions of noble houses, emblem bearers of the crown, their conduct and fame a balm to refined custom.

entries.zh: 昔居朝列，素無宦情，賓客簡通，公卿罕預，簪紱未褫，而風塵擺落。
entries.en: In former days at court they had no taste for office; guests were few and grandees rarely met; rank sashes were not yet off when turmoil's dust brushed them away.
entries.literal: In former days at court they were without appetite for office; guests were few and grandees rarely met; their rank sashes were not yet removed when the dust of turmoil brushed them off.

entries.zh: 且文宗儒肆，互居其長；
entries.en: One was master of the Confucian grove;
entries.literal: One was master of the Confucian grove;

entries.zh: 清規雅裁，兼擅其美。
entries.en: the other combined elegant rule with refined judgment.
entries.literal: the other combined elegant rule with refined judgment.

entries.zh: 並達照深識，預睹亂萌，見庸質之如初，知貽厥之無寄。
entries.en: Each saw deep and judged early, foresaw chaos sprouting, knew vulgar quality at first glance, and knew there was nothing to pass to heirs.
entries.literal: Each saw deep and judged early, foresaw the sprouting chaos, knew vulgar quality at first glance, and knew there was nothing to pass on to heirs.

entries.zh: 拂衣東山，眇絕塵軌。
entries.en: They shook out robes on the eastern hills and cut dust from their tracks.
entries.literal: They shook out their robes on the eastern hills and cut the dust from their tracks.

entries.zh: 雖解組昌運，實避昏時。
entries.en: Though they surrendered seals in a prosperous age, they truly fled a benighted time.
entries.literal: Though they surrendered their seals in a prosperous age, they truly fled a benighted time.

entries.zh: 家膺鼎食，而甘茲橡艾；
entries.en: Families that ate from the tripod yet savored oak and mugwort;
entries.literal: Families that ate from the tripod yet savored oak and mugwort;

entries.zh: 世襲青紫，而安此懸鶉。
entries.en: lineages that inherited purple and blue yet rested easy as hanging quail.
entries.literal: lineages that inherited purple and blue yet rested easy as hanging quail.

entries.zh: 自澆風肇扇，用南成俗，淳流素軌，餘烈頗存。
entries.en: Since the shallow wind first stirred, the south became custom; the pure current and plain track still had force left.
entries.literal: Since the shallow wind first stirred, the south became custom; the pure current and plain track still had much force left.

entries.zh: 誰其激貪，功歸有道，康俗振民，朝野一致。
entries.en: Who stirs against greed—the merit returns to the Way; who revives custom and lifts the people makes court and countryside one.
entries.literal: Who stirs against greed—the merit returns to the Way; who revives custom and lifts the people makes court and countryside one.

entries.zh: 雖在江海，而勳同魏闕。
entries.en: Though they dwelt by rivers and sea, their merit matched the Wei audience hall.
entries.literal: Though they dwelt by rivers and sea, their merit matched the Wei audience hall.

entries.zh: 今泰運甫開，賤貧爲恥；
entries.en: Now the great fortune is just opening; to be poor and low is shame;
entries.literal: Now the great fortune is just opening; to be poor and low is shame;

entries.zh: 況乎久蘊瑚璉，暫厭承明，而可得求志海隅，永追松子。
entries.en: how much more those who long harbored jade and ritual vessels, who for a time loathed the Bright Hall—can they seek their will at the sea's edge and forever chase Master Chizi?
entries.literal: how much more those who long harbored jade and ritual vessels, who for a time loathed the Bright Hall—can they seek their will at the sea's edge and forever chase Master Chizi?

entries.zh: 臣負荷殊重，參贊萬機，寔賴羣才，共成棟幹。
entries.en: Your servant bears a singular burden and shares in the myriad affairs of state; he truly relies on many talents to raise the roof beam together.
entries.literal: Your servant bears a singular burden and shares in the myriad affairs of state; he truly relies on many talents to raise the roof beam together.

entries.zh: 思挹清源，取鏡止水。
entries.en: He wishes to draw from the clear spring and take still water as mirror.
entries.literal: He wishes to draw from the clear spring and take the still water as mirror.

entries.zh: 愚欲屈居僚首，朝夕諮諏，庶足以翼宣寡薄，式是王度。
entries.en: He wishes to bend them to the first rank among his staff, to consult morning and evening, that they may help spread his thin virtue and shape the kingly measure.
entries.literal: He wishes to bend them to the first rank among his staff, to consult morning and evening, that they may help spread his thin virtue and shape the kingly measure.

entries.zh: 請並補臣府軍諮祭酒，朏加後將軍。」
entries.en: Request that both be appointed military affairs adviser and libation officer in your servant's chancellery, with Fei additionally made rear general."
entries.literal: Request that both be appointed military affairs adviser and libation officer in your servant's chancellery, with Fei additionally made Rear General."

entries.zh: 並不至。
entries.en: Neither came.
entries.literal: Neither came.

entries.zh: 高祖踐阼，徵朏爲侍中、左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，胤散騎常侍、特進、右光祿大夫，又並不屈。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Fei was summoned as attendant-in-ordinary, left grand master of splendid happiness, and bearer of the golden halberd with protocol equal to the three excellencies; Yin as regular palace attendant-in-ordinary, special grandee, and right grand master of splendid happiness—they again both refused.
entries.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, Fei was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Bearer of the Golden Halberd with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies; Yin was summoned as Regular Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary, Special Grandee, and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness—they again both refused.

entries.zh: 仍遣領軍司馬王果宣旨敦譬。
entries.en: Palace guard staff officer Wang Guo was again sent to convey the edict with earnest persuasion.
entries.literal: Palace guard staff officer Wang Guo was again sent to convey the edict with earnest persuasion.

entries.zh: 明年六月，朏輕舟出，詣闕自陳。
entries.en: The next year, in the sixth month, Fei took a light boat and came to the palace to report in person.
entries.literal: The next year in the sixth month Fei took a light boat and came to the palace to report in person.

entries.zh: 旣至，詔以爲侍中、司徒、尚書令。
entries.en: On arrival an edict made him attendant-in-ordinary, grand marshal, and director of the masters of writing.
entries.literal: On arrival an edict made him Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Marshal, and Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 朏辭腳疾不堪拜謁，乃角巾肩輿，詣雲龍門謝。
entries.en: Fei pleaded leg ailment and could not kneel in audience; he wore kerchief and rode a shoulder carriage to Cloud Dragon Gate to give thanks.
entries.literal: Fei pleaded that leg ailment prevented kneeling in audience; he wore kerchief and shoulder carriage and came to Cloud Dragon Gate to give thanks.

entries.zh: 詔見於華林園，乘小車就席。
entries.en: An edict received him in Hualin Garden; he sat in a small carriage at the mat.
entries.literal: An edict received him in Hualin Garden; he sat in a small carriage at the mat.

entries.zh: 明旦，輿駕出幸朏宅，醼語盡歡。
entries.en: Next morning the imperial carriage visited Fei's house; they feasted and talked in full joy.
entries.literal: Next morning the imperial carriage went out to visit Fei's house; they feasted and talked in full joy.

entries.zh: 朏固陳本志，不許；
entries.en: Fei firmly stated his original intent; the emperor would not allow it;
entries.literal: Fei firmly stated his original intent; the emperor would not allow it;

entries.zh: 因請自還東迎母，乃許之。
entries.en: he then asked to go east himself to fetch his mother, and permission was granted.
entries.literal: he then asked to go east himself to fetch his mother, and permission was granted.

entries.zh: 臨發，輿駕復臨幸，賦詩餞別。
entries.en: On the eve of departure the imperial carriage again visited, composing poetry to see him off.
entries.literal: On the eve of departure the imperial carriage again came to visit, composing poetry to see him off.

entries.zh: 王人送迎，相望於道。
entries.en: Court envoys went out and escorted him back—processions met on the road.
entries.literal: Court envoys went out and escorted him back—one party's procession met the other's on the road.

entries.zh: 到京師，勑材官起府於舊宅，高祖臨軒，遣謁者於府拜授，詔停諸公事及朔望朝謁。
entries.en: On reaching the capital, an order had the materiel office raise a mansion at his old residence; the emperor came to the front hall and sent an usher to the mansion to invest him; an edict suspended all public business and new-moon and full-moon audiences.
entries.literal: On reaching the capital, an order had the materiel office raise a mansion at his old residence; the emperor came to the front hall and sent an usher to the mansion to invest him with office; an edict suspended all public business and the new-moon and full-moon audiences.

entries.zh: 覽字景滌，朏弟綍之子也。
entries.en: Lan, styled Jingdi, was the son of Fei's younger brother Fu.
entries.literal: Lan, styled Jingdi, was the son of Fei's younger brother Fu.

entries.zh: 選尚齊錢唐公主，拜駙馬都尉、秘書郎、太子舍人。
entries.en: He was selected to marry the Princess of Qiantang of Qi and was appointed Imperial Son-in-law Commandant, Palace Library Gentleman, and attendant to the crown prince.
entries.literal: He was selected to marry the Princess of Qiantang of Qi and was appointed Imperial Son-in-law Commandant, Palace Library Gentleman, and attendant to the crown prince.

entries.zh: 高祖爲大司馬，召補東閤祭酒，遷相國戶曹。
entries.en: When Gaozu was Grand Marshal, he summoned Lan to fill the post of libationer of the Eastern Lodge; Lan was then transferred to the household section of the Chancellor of State.
entries.literal: When Gaozu was Grand Marshal, he summoned Lan to fill the post of libationer of the Eastern Lodge; Lan was then transferred to the household section of the Chancellor of State.

entries.zh: 天監元年，爲中書侍郎，掌吏部事，頃之卽真。
entries.en: In Tianjian 1, Lan became Gentleman of the Secretariat and handled Personnel affairs; before long he took the office in his own right.
entries.literal: In Tianjian 1, Lan became Gentleman of the Secretariat and handled Personnel affairs; before long he took the office in his own right.

entries.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：謝朏之於宋代，蓋忠義者歟？
entries.en: Chen Minister of Personnel Yao Cha said: Was Xie Fei, in Song times, a man of loyalty and righteousness?
entries.literal: Chen Minister of Personnel Yao Cha said: In the Song age, was Xie Fei perhaps a man of loyalty and righteousness?

entries.zh: 當齊建武之世，拂衣止足，永元多難，確然獨善，其疏、蔣之流乎。
entries.en: In Qi Jianwu he held back his robes; amid Yongyuan's troubles he stood alone in the good—one of Shu and Jiang's kind?
entries.literal: In Qi Jianwu times he folded his robe and checked his step; in Yongyuan's many troubles he stood firm in doing good alone—is he not of the sort of Shu and Jiang?

entries.zh: 洎高祖龍興，旁求物色，角巾來仕，首陟台司，極出處之致矣！
entries.en: When Gaozu rose, he searched widely; Fei came in plain kerchief and first reached the high ministries—the full arc of public life!
entries.literal: When Gaozu's dragon fortune rose, he sought men on every hand; Fei came to serve in scholar's kerchief and first climbed the terraces of state—he had reached the utmost of entering and leaving office!

entries.zh: 覽終能善政，君子韙之。
entries.en: Lan could govern well to the end; gentlemen praised it.
entries.literal: Lan in the end could govern well; gentlemen approved him.

entries.zh: 梁書卷第十五 列傳第九
entries.en: Book of Liang, Volume 15, Biographies 9
entries.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 15, Biographies 9

entries.zh: 王亮字奉叔，琅邪臨沂人，晉丞相導之六世孫也。
entries.en: Wang Liang, styled Fengshu, came from Linyi in Langye—a sixth-generation descendant of Jin Chancellor Dao.
entries.literal: Wang Liang, styled Fengshu, was a native of Linyi in Langye; he was sixth-generation descendant of Jin Chancellor Dao.

entries.zh: 祖偃，宋右光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。
entries.en: His grandfather Yan had been Song right grand master of splendid happiness, opening the government with ritual equal to the three excellencies.
entries.literal: His grandfather Yan was Song Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, opening the government with ritual equal to the three excellencies.

entries.zh: 父攸，給事黃門侍郎。
entries.en: His father You was an attendant yellow gate gentleman.
entries.literal: His father You was Attendant Yellow Gate Gentleman.

entries.zh: 亮以名家子，宋末選尚公主，拜駙馬都尉、秘書郎，累遷桂陽王文學，南郡王友，秘書丞。
entries.en: As a son of a great house, at the end of Song he was matched to a princess, made commandant of the horse for the imperial son-in-law and secretary gentleman, and rose through literary scholar to the prince of Guiyang, friend to the prince of Nanjun, and secretary assistant.
entries.literal: Liang was a scion of a famous house; at the end of Song he was chosen to marry a princess, made Commandant of the Horse for the Imperial Son-in-law and Secretary Gentleman, and rose through Literary Scholar to the Prince of Guiyang, Friend to the Prince of Nanjun, and Secretary Assistant.

entries.zh: 齊竟陵王子良開西邸，延才俊以爲士林館，使工圖畫其像，亮亦預焉。
entries.en: When Qi's prince of Jingling opened the Western Lodge and gathered worthies for the Scholars' Grove Hall, artisans painted their likenesses—and Liang was among them.
entries.literal: Qi Prince of Jingling Zi Liang opened the Western Lodge, gathering talented men for the Scholars' Grove Hall and having artisans paint their portraits—Liang was among them.

entries.zh: 遷中書侍郎、大司馬從事中郎，出爲衡陽太守。
entries.en: He rose to secretariat gentleman and chief staff officer to the grand marshal, then went out as Hengyang governor.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman and Chief Staff Officer to the Grand Marshal, and went out as Governor of Hengyang.

entries.zh: 以南土卑濕，辭不之官，遷給事黃門侍郎。
entries.en: The south was low and damp; he declined the post and was made attendant yellow gate gentleman.
entries.literal: Because the southern land was low and humid, he declined the office and was transferred to Attendant Yellow Gate Gentleman.

entries.zh: 尋拜晉陵太守，在職清公有美政。
entries.en: Soon he was Jinling governor—pure in office, with a reputation for good rule.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Governor of Jinling; in office he was pure and public-spirited, with fine governance.

entries.zh: 時齊明帝作相，聞而嘉之，引爲領軍長史，甚見賞納。
entries.en: Qi Emperor Ming was then regent; hearing of him he praised him, made him chief of staff to the guard general, and favored him deeply.
entries.literal: At the time Qi Emperor Ming was acting as regent; hearing of this he praised him, brought him in as Chief Staff Officer to the Guard General, and greatly favored and received him.

entries.zh: 及卽位，累遷太子中庶子，尚書吏部郎，詮序著稱，遷侍中。
entries.en: When Ming took the throne, Liang rose to crown prince palace attendant and director of the ministry of personnel—his rankings won fame—and then to attendant.
entries.literal: When Ming took the throne, he rose through offices to Crown Prince Palace Attendant and Director of the Ministry of Personnel—his evaluations won renown—and was promoted to Attendant.

entries.zh: 齊永明中，爲剡縣令，略不視事，多爲山水遊。
entries.en: In Qi's Yongming era he was Shan county magistrate, scarcely overseeing affairs, often roaming mountains and waters.
entries.literal: In Qi's Yongming era he was Governor of Shan County, scarcely overseeing affairs, often roaming mountains and waters.

entries.zh: 會賊唐㝢之作亂，稷率厲縣人，保全縣境。
entries.en: When the bandit Tang Yuzhi rebelled, Ji led and encouraged the county people and preserved the county territory.
entries.literal: When the bandit Tang Yuzhi rebelled, Ji led and encouraged the county people and preserved the county territory.

entries.zh: 入爲太子洗馬，大司馬東曹掾，建安王友，大司馬從事中郎。
entries.en: He entered as crown prince purifier, eastern bureau staff officer to the grand marshal, friend to the prince of Jian'an, and chief staff officer to the grand marshal.
entries.literal: He entered office as Crown Prince Purifier, Eastern Bureau Staff Officer to the Grand Marshal, Friend to the Prince of Jian'an, and Chief Staff Officer to the Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 武陵王曅爲護軍，轉護軍司馬，尋爲本州治中。
entries.en: When the prince of Wuling was guard general, Ji was transferred to guard general staff officer, soon made chief administrator of his native province.
entries.literal: When Prince of Wuling Ye was Guard General, Ji was transferred to Guard General Staff Officer, soon made Chief Administrator of his native province.

entries.zh: 明帝領牧，仍爲別駕。
entries.en: When Emperor Ming held the governorship, Ji remained as vice governor.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming held the governorship, Ji remained as Vice Governor.

entries.zh: 時魏寇壽春，以稷爲寧朔將軍、軍主，副尚書僕射沈文季鎮豫州。
entries.en: At the time Wei raided Shouchun; Ji was made pacifying-the-north general and army commander, assisting right vice director Shen Wenji in guarding Yuzhou.
entries.literal: At the time Wei raided Shouchun; Ji was made Pacifying the North General and army commander, assisting Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Shen Wenji in guarding Yuzhou.

entries.zh: 魏衆稱百萬，圍城累日，時經略處分，文季悉委稷焉。
entries.en: Wei forces were said to number a million and besieged the city for many days; all planning and disposition Wenji wholly entrusted to Ji.
entries.literal: Wei forces were said to number a million and besieged the city for many days; all planning and disposition Wenji wholly entrusted to Ji.

entries.zh: 軍退，遷平西司馬、寧朔將軍、南平內史。
entries.en: When the army withdrew, he was promoted to pacifying-the-west staff officer, pacifying-the-north general, and Nanping interior governor.
entries.literal: When the army withdrew, he was promoted to Pacifying the West Staff Officer, Pacifying the North General, and Interior Governor of Nanping.

entries.zh: 魏又寇雍州，詔以本號都督荊、雍諸軍事。
entries.en: Wei again raided Yong province; an edict made him with his present title commander of military affairs in Jing and Yong.
entries.literal: Wei again raided Yong Province; an edict made him with his present title Commander of military affairs in Jing and Yong.

entries.zh: 時雍州刺史曹虎度樊城岸，以稷知州事。
entries.en: At the time Cao Hu, Inspector of Yong Province, crossed to the Fancheng bank, and Ji was put in charge of provincial affairs.
entries.literal: At the time Cao Hu, Inspector of Yong Province, crossed to the Fancheng bank, and Ji was made acting administrator of the province.

entries.zh: 魏師退，稷還荊州，就拜黃門侍郎，復爲司馬、新興、永寧二郡太守。
entries.en: When Wei forces withdrew, Ji returned to Jing province and was at once appointed yellow gate gentleman, again made staff officer and governor of Xinxing and Yongning.
entries.literal: When Wei forces withdrew, Ji returned to Jing Province and was at once appointed Yellow Gate Gentleman, again made Staff Officer and Governor of both Xinxing and Yongning commanderies.

entries.zh: 郡犯私諱，改永寧爲長寧。
entries.en: The commandery violated a private taboo, so Yongning was changed to Changning.
entries.literal: The commandery violated a private taboo, so Yongning was changed to Changning.

entries.zh: 尋遷司徒司馬，加輔國將軍。
entries.en: Soon he was promoted to grand marshal staff officer with additional assistant state general.
entries.literal: Soon he was promoted to Grand Marshal Staff Officer with additional Assistant State General.

entries.zh: 及江州刺史陳顯達舉兵反，以本號鎮歷陽、南譙二郡太守，遷鎮南長史、尋陽太守、輔國將軍、行江州事。
entries.en: When Jiangzhou inspector Chen Xianda raised troops in rebellion, with his present title he was made governor of Liyang and Nanqiao, promoted to pacifying-the-south chief staff officer, Xunyang governor, assistant state general, and acting Jiangzhou affairs.
entries.literal: When Jiangzhou Inspector Chen Xianda raised troops in rebellion, with his present title he was made Governor of both Liyang and Nanqiao commanderies, promoted to Pacifying the South Chief Staff Officer, Xunyang Governor, Assistant State General, and Acting Jiangzhou Affairs.

entries.zh: 尋徵還，爲持節、輔國將軍、都督北徐州諸軍事、北徐州刺史。
entries.en: Soon recalled, he became bearer of credentials, General Who Assists the State, area commander of North Xuzhou, and North Xuzhou inspector.
entries.literal: Soon he was recalled and made Bearer of Credentials, General Who Assists the State, Area Commander of all North Xuzhou military affairs, and North Xuzhou Inspector.

entries.zh: 出次白下，仍遷都督南兗州諸軍事、南兗州刺史。
entries.en: He posted at Baixia, then became area commander of South Yanzhou and South Yanzhou inspector.
entries.literal: He posted at Baixia, then was transferred to Area Commander of all South Yanzhou military affairs and South Yanzhou Inspector.

entries.zh: 俄進督北徐、徐、兗、青、冀五州諸軍事，將軍並如故。
entries.en: Soon he was advanced to command the five provinces North Xu, Xu, Yan, Qing, and Ji, with his general ranks unchanged.
entries.literal: Soon he was advanced to command military affairs in North Xu, Xu, Yan, Qing, and Ji—five provinces in all—while his general ranks remained as before.

entries.zh: 永元末，徵爲侍中，宿衛宮城。
entries.en: At the end of Yongyuan he was summoned as attendant within and guarded the palace city.
entries.literal: At the end of the Yongyuan era he was summoned as Attendant Within and guarded the palace city.

entries.zh: 義師至，兼衛尉江淹出奔。
entries.en: When the righteous army came, Concurrent Commandant of the Guard Jiang Yan fled.
entries.literal: When the Righteous Army arrived, Concurrent Commandant of the Guard Jiang Yan fled.

entries.zh: 稷兼衛尉，副王瑩都督城內諸軍事。
entries.en: Ji held the concurrent guard commandancy and assisted Wang Ying in commanding the city's forces.
entries.literal: Ji held the concurrent commandantship and assisted Wang Ying in commanding all military affairs within the city.

entries.zh: 齊高帝爲驃騎將軍，引爲從事中郎。
entries.en: When Qi Gaodi was Rapid Cavalry General, he brought Ying in as participation officer.
entries.literal: When Qi Gaodi was Rapid Cavalry General, he brought Ying in as participation officer.

entries.zh: 頃之，出爲義興太守，代謝超宗。
entries.en: Soon he went out as Yixing administrator, replacing Xie Chaozong.
entries.literal: Shortly after, he went out as Yixing Administrator, replacing Xie Chaozong.

entries.zh: 超宗去郡，與瑩交惡，旣還，間瑩於懋。
entries.en: Chaozong left the commandery on bad terms with Ying; back in the capital he slandered Ying to Mao.
entries.literal: When Chaozong left the commandery he and Ying had become enemies; once back in the capital he slandered Ying to Mao.

entries.zh: 懋言之於朝廷，以瑩供養不足，坐失郡廢棄。
entries.en: Mao raised it at court; Ying's upkeep of office was judged insufficient, and he lost his commandery and was cast aside.
entries.literal: Mao spoke of it at court; because Ying's support of his post was insufficient, he was dismissed from his commandery and cast aside.

entries.zh: 久之，爲前軍諮議參軍，中書侍郎，大司馬從事中郎，未拜，丁母憂。
entries.en: Long after, he became advisory staff officer of the Front Army, Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat, and Gentleman of the Grand Marshal's staff; before taking up the post, he went into mourning for his mother.
entries.literal: After a long while he was made Advisory Staff Officer of the Front Army, Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat, and Gentleman of the Grand Marshal's staff; before he could take up the post, he entered mourning for his mother.

entries.zh: 服闋，爲給事黃門郎，出爲宣城太守，遷爲驃騎長史。
entries.en: After mourning he became yellow gate attendant, went out as Xuancheng administrator, then rapid cavalry chief clerk.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he was made Yellow Gate Attendant, went out as Xuancheng Administrator, and was transferred to Rapid Cavalry Chief Clerk.

entries.zh: 復爲黃門侍郎、司馬、太子中庶子，仍遷侍中，父憂去職。
entries.en: He again became Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, Marshal, and Junior Mentor in the heir apparent's household, and soon became Attendant-in-Ordinary; he left office to mourn his father.
entries.literal: He was again made Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, Marshal, and Junior Mentor in the heir apparent's household, and soon transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary; he left office for his father's mourning.

entries.zh: 服闋，復爲侍中，領射聲校尉，又爲冠軍將軍、東陽太守。
entries.en: After mourning he again became attendant within and colonel of the archers' guard, then champion general and Dongyang administrator.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he was again made Attendant Within with concurrent Colonel of the Archers' Guard, then Champion General and Dongyang Administrator.

entries.zh: 居郡有惠政，遷吳興太守。
entries.en: In office he ruled with benevolence and was transferred to Wuxing administrator.
entries.literal: In the commandery he had benevolent government and was transferred to Wuxing Administrator.

entries.zh: 明帝勤憂庶政，瑩頻處二郡，皆有能名。
entries.en: Mingdi toiled over common government; Ying twice held commanderies and in both won a name for ability.
entries.literal: Mingdi labored anxiously over common government; Ying twice held commanderies and in both had a name for ability.

entries.zh: 甚見褒美。
entries.en: He was greatly praised.
entries.literal: He was greatly praised.

entries.zh: 還爲太子詹事、中領軍。
entries.en: On return he became crown prince grand tutor and central army commander.
entries.literal: On his return he was made Crown Prince Grand Tutor and Central Army Commander.

entries.zh: 義師至新林，內外百僚皆道迎，其未能拔者，亦間路送誠款，亮獨不遣。
entries.en: When the Righteous Army reached Xinlin, officials within and without went out to welcome them; those who could not leave still sent loyalty by back roads—only Liang sent no one.
entries.literal: When the Righteous Army reached Xinlin, officials inside and outside all went out to welcome them; those who could not break away still sent pledges of loyalty by side roads—only Liang sent no one.

entries.zh: 及城內旣定，獨推亮爲首。
entries.en: Once the city was settled, he alone was pushed forward as ringleader.
entries.literal: When the city was settled, he alone was singled out as ringleader.

entries.zh: 亮出見高祖，高祖曰：「顛而不扶，安用彼相。」
entries.en: Liang came out to see Gaozu. Gaozu said, "When the tottering man is not held up, what use is that minister!"
entries.literal: Liang came out to see Gaozu; Gaozu said: "When the toppling man is not supported, what use is that minister!"

entries.zh: 而弗之罪也。
entries.en: Yet he did not punish him.
entries.literal: Yet he did not punish him.

entries.zh: 霸府開，以爲大司馬長史、撫軍將軍、琅邪、清河二郡太守。
entries.en: When the supreme office opened, he was made chief of staff to the grand marshal, pacifying army general, and governor of Langye and Qinghe.
entries.literal: When the Supreme Office opened, he was made Chief Staff Officer to the Grand Marshal, Pacifying Army General, and Governor of both Langye and Qinghe commanderies.

entries.zh: 梁臺建，授侍中、尚書令，固讓不拜，乃爲侍中、中書監，兼尚書令。
entries.en: When the Liang regime was set up, he was offered attendant and director of the masters of writing; he refused firmly and was made attendant, director of the secretariat, with the masters of writing added.
entries.literal: When the Liang regime was established, he was appointed Attendant and Director of the Masters of Writing; he firmly refused; he was then made Attendant, Director of the Secretariat, and concurrently Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，遷侍中、尚書令、中軍將軍，引參佐命，封豫寧縣公，邑二千戶。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the mandate, Liang became attendant, director of the masters of writing, and central army general, drawn into founding the state, and was enfeoffed duke of Yuning with two thousand households.
entries.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, he was promoted to Attendant, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Central Army General, drawn into assisting the mandate, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yuning with two thousand households.

entries.zh: 天監二年，轉左光祿大夫，侍中、中軍如故。
entries.en: In Tianjian's second year he was transferred to left grand master of splendid happiness; attendant and central army were unchanged.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianjian he was transferred to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Attendant and Central Army unchanged.

entries.zh: 元日朝會萬國，亮辭疾不登殿，設饌別省，而語笑自若。
entries.en: On New Year's Day the myriad states met in court; Liang pleaded illness, did not mount the hall, dined in a side office, and talked and laughed as if at ease.
entries.literal: On New Year's Day the myriad states assembled in court; Liang pleaded illness and did not ascend the hall, set out food in a separate office, yet talked and laughed as if at ease.

entries.zh: 數日，詔公卿問訊，亮無疾色，御史中丞樂藹奏大不敬，論棄市刑。
entries.en: Days later an edict sent dukes and ministers to inquire; Liang showed no sickness; censor-in-chief Yue Ai memorialized gross disrespect and asked the death penalty in the marketplace.
entries.literal: Several days later an edict had the dukes and ministers inquire; Liang showed no sign of illness; Censor-in-Chief Yue Ai memorialized for gross disrespect, penalty of execution in the marketplace.

entries.zh: 詔削爵廢爲庶人。
entries.en: An edict stripped his rank and made him a commoner.
entries.literal: An edict stripped his rank and made him a commoner.

entries.zh: 四年夏，高祖讌於華光殿，謂羣臣曰：「朕日昃聽政，思聞得失。
entries.en: In summer of the fourth year Gaozu feasted at Huaguang Hall and told the ministers, "From noon I hear government, wishing to learn gain and loss.
entries.literal: In summer of the fourth year Gaozu feasted at Huaguang Hall and said to the assembled ministers: "From noon I hear affairs of state, wishing to learn gain and loss.

entries.zh: 卿等可謂多士，宜各盡獻替。」
entries.en: You are many scholars—each should offer full and frank counsel."
entries.literal: You may be called many scholars—each should fully offer candid counsel."

entries.zh: 尚書左丞范縝起曰：「司徒謝朏本有虛名，陛下擢之如此，前尚書令王亮頗有治實，陛下棄之如彼，是愚臣所不知。」
entries.en: Left assistant director Fan Zhen rose and said, "Grand Marshal Xie Fei had only empty fame, yet Your Majesty raised him so; former director Wang Liang had real governing merit, yet Your Majesty cast him off so—this dull minister cannot understand."
entries.literal: Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Fan Zhen rose and said: "Grand Marshal Xie Fei originally had only empty fame, yet Your Majesty raised him thus; former Director Wang Liang truly had governing merit, yet Your Majesty cast him off like that—this a dull minister cannot understand."

entries.zh: 高祖變色曰：「卿可更餘言。」
entries.en: Gaozu's color changed. "You may speak on other matters."
entries.literal: Gaozu's face changed: "You may speak on other matters."

entries.zh: 縝固執不已，高祖不悅。
entries.en: Zhen pressed on; Gaozu was displeased.
entries.literal: Zhen persisted without end; Gaozu was displeased.

entries.zh: 御史中丞任昉因奏曰：
entries.en: Censor-in-chief Ren Fang then memorialized:
entries.literal: Censor-in-Chief Ren Fang then memorialized:

entries.zh: 時東昏淫虐，義師圍城已久，城內思亡而莫有先發。
entries.en: Donghun was depraved and cruel; the righteous army had long besieged the city, and everyone inside wished to turn, yet none dared move first.
entries.literal: Donghun was then depraved and cruel; the Righteous Army had besieged the city for a long time, and within the walls all wished to rebel, yet none dared act first.

entries.zh: 北徐州刺史王珍國就稷謀之，乃使直閤張齊害東昏于含德殿。
entries.en: North Xuzhou inspector Wang Zhenguo plotted with Ji; Ji had Direct Attendant Zhang Qi kill Donghun in Hede Hall.
entries.literal: North Xuzhou Inspector Wang Zhenguo consulted with Ji; Ji then had Direct Attendant Zhang Qi kill Donghun in Hede Hall.

entries.zh: 稷召尚書右僕射王亮等列坐殿前西鐘下，謂曰：「昔桀有昏德，鼎遷于殷；
entries.en: Ji summoned Right Vice Director Wang Liang and others to sit before the western bell in the hall and said, "Of old Jie had dark virtue, and the tripod moved to Yin;
entries.literal: Ji summoned Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Liang and others to sit in a row before the western bell in the hall and said: "Of old Jie had dark virtue, and the tripod moved to Yin;

entries.zh: 商紂暴虐，鼎遷于周。
entries.en: Shang's Zhou was violent and cruel, and the tripod moved to Zhou.
entries.literal: Shang's Zhou was violent and cruel, and the tripod moved to Zhou.

entries.zh: 今獨夫自絕于天，四海已歸聖主，斯實微子去殷之時，項伯歸漢之日，可不勉哉！」
entries.en: Now the tyrant has cut himself off from Heaven; the four seas already belong to the sage lord—this is Weizi leaving Yin, Xiang Bo returning to Han. You must exert yourselves!"
entries.literal: Now the lone man has cut himself off from Heaven; the four seas already belong to the sage lord—this is truly the time of Weizi leaving Yin, Xiang Bo returning to Han. You must exert yourselves!"

entries.zh: 乃遣國子博士范雲、舍人裴長穆等使石頭城詣高祖，高祖以稷爲侍中、左衛將軍。
entries.en: Then he sent National University erudite Fan Yun, attendant Pei Changmu, and others to Stone City to see Gaozu; Gaozu made Ji attendant within and left palace guard general.
entries.literal: Then he sent National University Erudite Fan Yun, Attendant Pei Changmu, and others to Stone City to present themselves to Gaozu; Gaozu made Ji Attendant Within and Left Palace Guard General.

entries.zh: 高祖總百揆，遷大司馬左司馬。
entries.en: When Gaozu took charge of all affairs, Ji became the grand marshal's left staff officer.
entries.literal: When Gaozu oversaw all state affairs, Ji was transferred to Left Staff Officer of the Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 梁臺建，爲散騎常侍、中書令。
entries.en: When the Liang court was set up he became cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and director of the secretariat.
entries.literal: When the Liang regime was established he was made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，以功封江安縣侯，邑一千戶。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Ji was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiang'an for merit, with a fief of one thousand households.
entries.literal: When Gaozu accepted the abdication, Ji was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiang'an for his merit, with a fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 又爲侍中、國子祭酒，領驍騎將軍，遷護軍將軍、揚州大中正，以事免。
entries.en: He again became attendant within and chancellor of the National University, with concurrent rapid cavalry general; he became protector general and Yangzhou chief rectifier, then was dismissed over an affair.
entries.literal: He was again made Attendant Within and Chancellor of the National University, with concurrent Rapid Cavalry General; he was transferred to Protector General and Yangzhou Chief Rectifier, then dismissed over an affair.

entries.zh: 尋爲度支尚書、前將軍、太子右衛率，又以公事免。
entries.en: Soon he became minister of revenue, front general, and right crown prince palace guard commander, then was again dismissed over official business.
entries.literal: Soon he was made Minister of Revenue, Front General, and Right Crown Prince Palace Guard Commander, then again dismissed over an official matter.

entries.zh: 俄爲祠部尚書，轉散騎常侍、都官尚書、揚州大中正，以本職知領軍事。
entries.en: Soon he became minister of sacrificial affairs, then cavalier attendant, director of capital crimes, and Yangzhou chief rectifier, concurrently commanding guard-army affairs.
entries.literal: Soon he was made Minister of Sacrificial Affairs, then transferred to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of Capital Crimes, and Yangzhou Chief Rectifier, with this office concurrently in charge of guard-army affairs.

entries.zh: 尋遷領軍將軍，中正、侯如故。
entries.en: Soon he became guard army general, keeping his chief rectifier title and marquisate.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Guard Army General, his chief rectifier title and marquisate remaining as before.

entries.zh: 永元初，政由羣小，瑩守職而不能有所是非。
entries.en: At the start of Yongyuan petty men held power; Ying kept his post but could not speak on right and wrong.
entries.literal: At the start of Yongyuan, government lay with petty men; Ying kept his post but could not judge right and wrong.

entries.zh: 瑩從弟亮旣當朝，於瑩素雖不善，時欲引與同事。
entries.en: Cousin Liang was then in power; though never close to Ying, he now wished to draw him into shared office.
entries.literal: Ying's cousin Liang was then in power; though he had never been close to Ying, he now wished to draw him into shared office.

entries.zh: 遷尚書左僕射，未拜。
entries.en: He was transferred to left vice director but did not take up the post.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing but did not take up the post.

entries.zh: 會護軍崔慧景自京口奉江夏王入伐，瑩假節，率衆拒慧景於湖頭，夜爲慧景所襲，衆散，瑩赴水，乘榜入樂遊，因得還臺城。
entries.en: When Protector General Cui Huijing raised the Prince of Jiangxia from Jingkou, Ying held temporary credentials, led troops to resist Huijing at Hutou, was night-attacked, his host scattered, threw himself into the water, rafted into Le You, and so returned to the terrace city.
entries.literal: When Protector General Cui Huijing raised the Prince of Jiangxia from Jingkou in revolt, Ying was granted temporary credentials, led troops to resist Huijing at Hutou, was night-attacked by Huijing, his host scattered, and Ying threw himself into the water and entered Le You on a raft, thereby returning to the terrace city.

entries.zh: 慧景敗，還居領軍府。
entries.en: When Huijing was defeated, Ying returned to the defender-in-chief's residence.
entries.literal: When Huijing was defeated, Ying returned to the Defender-in-Chief's residence.

entries.zh: 義師至，復假節，都督宮城諸軍事。
entries.en: When the righteous army came, he again held temporary credentials and commanded palace-city forces.
entries.literal: When the Righteous Army arrived, he was again granted temporary credentials and made Area Commander of all palace-city military affairs.

entries.zh: 建康平，高祖爲相國，引瑩爲左長史，加冠軍將軍，奉法駕迎和帝于江陵。
entries.en: When Jiankang was pacified, Gaozu as chancellor of state brought Ying in as left chief clerk, advanced him to champion general, and had him escort the imperial carriage to welcome Emperor He from Jiangling.
entries.literal: When Jiankang was pacified, Gaozu as Chancellor of State brought Ying in as Left Chief Clerk, advanced him to Champion General, and had him escort the imperial carriage to welcome Emperor He from Jiangling.

entries.zh: 帝至南州，遜位于別宮。
entries.en: When the emperor reached Southern Province, he abdicated at a separate palace.
entries.literal: When the Emperor reached Southern Province, he abdicated at a separate palace.

entries.zh: 高祖踐阼，遷侍中、撫軍將軍，封建城縣公，邑千戶。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Ying became attendant within and pacification army general, enfeoffed as Duke of Jiancheng with a fief of one thousand households.
entries.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Ying was transferred to Attendant Within and Pacification Army General, enfeoffed as Duke of Jiancheng with a fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 尋遷尚書左僕射，侍中、撫軍如故。
entries.en: Soon he became Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, keeping his titles of Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Pacifies the Army.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, with Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Pacifies the Army as before.

entries.zh: 頃之，爲護軍將軍，復遷散騎常侍、中軍將軍、丹陽尹。
entries.en: Soon he became protector general, then cavalier attendant, central army general, and Danyang intendant.
entries.literal: Shortly after, he was made Protector General, then transferred to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Central Army General, and Danyang Intendant.

entries.zh: 視事三年，遷侍中、光祿大夫，領左衛將軍。
entries.en: After three years in office he became attendant within and grand master of splendid happiness, with concurrent left palace guard general.
entries.literal: After three years in office he was transferred to Attendant Within and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, with concurrent Left Palace Guard General.

entries.zh: 俄遷尚書令、雲麾將軍，侍中如故。
entries.en: Soon he became director of the Masters of Writing and Cloud-Banner general, keeping attendant within.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing and Cloud-Banner General, his attendant within title remaining as before.

entries.zh: 累進號左中權將軍，給鼓吹一部。
entries.en: He was repeatedly advanced to Left Central Authority general and granted one set of pipes and drums.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly advanced in title to Left Central Authority General and granted one set of martial pipes and drums.

entries.zh: 瑩性清慎，居官恭恪，高祖深重之。
entries.en: Ying was pure and cautious; in office he was respectful and earnest, and Gaozu valued him deeply.
entries.literal: Ying's nature was pure and cautious; in office he was respectful and earnest, and Gaozu valued him deeply.

entries.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：孔子稱「殷有三仁：微子去之，箕子爲之奴，比干諫而死。」
entries.en: Chen Minister of Personnel Yao Cha said: Confucius said, "Yin had three worthies: Weizi left; Jizi became a slave; Bigan remonstrated and died."
entries.literal: Chen Minister of Personnel Yao Cha said: Confucius said, "Yin had three worthies: Weizi left it; Jizi became its slave; Bigan remonstrated and died."

entries.zh: 王亮之居亂世，勢位見矣。
entries.en: Wang Liang's standing in chaotic times—rank and position were plain to see.
entries.literal: Wang Liang's standing in a chaotic age—his rank and position were plain to see.

entries.zh: 其于取捨，何與三仁之異歟？
entries.en: In what he took and rejected, how did he differ from the three worthies?
entries.literal: In what he took and rejected, how did he differ from the three worthies?

entries.zh: 及奉興王，蒙寬政，爲佐命，固將愧於心。
entries.en: Yet serving the Rising King under lenient rule and helping found the dynasty, he must have felt shame at heart.
entries.literal: Yet when he served the Rising King, he received lenient policy and helped found the dynasty—he must surely have felt shame at heart.

entries.zh: 乃自取廢敗，非不幸也。
entries.en: Then he brought ruin on himself—not misfortune.
entries.literal: Then he brought ruin on himself—not misfortune.

entries.zh: 《易》曰：「非所據而據之，身必危。」
entries.en: The Changes says, "Occupy what is not yours to occupy, and the body must be in peril."
entries.literal: The Changes says: "When one occupies what is not one's to occupy, the body must be in peril."

entries.zh: 亮之進退，失所據矣。
entries.en: In advance and retreat, Liang lost what he should have stood on.
entries.literal: In advance and retreat, Liang lost what he should have stood on.

entries.zh: 惜哉！
entries.en: Pity!
entries.literal: Pity!

entries.zh: 張稷因機制變，亦其時也。
entries.en: Zhang Ji seized the moment to shift course—that too was its time.
entries.literal: Zhang Ji seized the moment to shift course—that too was its time.

entries.zh: 王瑩印章六毀，豈神之害盈乎？
entries.en: Wang Ying's seal was cast six times and six times the tortoise was ruined—did a spirit punish excess?
entries.literal: Wang Ying's seal was cast six times and six times the tortoise was ruined—was it a spirit punishing fullness?

entries.zh: 詔聞可。
entries.en: Edict: Approved.
entries.literal: Edict: Approved.

entries.zh: 璽書詰縝曰：「亮少乏才能，無聞時輩，昔經冒入羣英，相與豈薄，晚節諂事江祏，爲吏部，末協附梅蟲兒、茹法珍，遂執昏政。
entries.en: An imperial letter reprimanded Zhen: "Liang in youth lacked talent and was unknown among his peers; formerly he rashly entered the ranks of worthies—we were not thin with one another; in his later years he flattered Jiang Shi; as director of personnel he finally joined Mei Chong'er and Ru Fazhen and held benighted government.
entries.literal: An imperial letter reprimanded Zhen: "Liang in youth lacked talent and was unknown among contemporaries; formerly he rashly entered the ranks of worthies—we with one another were not thin; in his later years he flattered Jiang Shi; as Director of Personnel he finally joined with Mei Chong'er and Ru Fazhen and so held benighted government.

entries.zh: 比屋罹禍，盡家塗炭，四海沸騰，天下橫潰，此誰之咎！
entries.en: Household upon household met disaster, whole families were scorched; the four seas seethed, the realm collapsed—whose fault is this!
entries.literal: Household upon household met disaster, whole families were scorched; the four seas seethed, the realm collapsed—whose fault is this!

entries.zh: 食亂君之祿，不死於治世。
entries.en: He ate the salary of a chaotic lord yet did not die in an age of order.
entries.literal: He ate the salary of a chaotic lord yet did not die in an age of order.

entries.zh: 亮協固凶黨，作威作福，靡衣玉食，女樂盈房，勢危事逼，自相吞噬。
entries.en: Liang joined the vicious faction, made might and made blessing, fine clothes and jade food, female musicians filling the rooms; when peril pressed and business forced, they devoured one another.
entries.literal: Liang solidified with the vicious faction, made might and made blessing, fine clothes and jade food, female musicians filling the rooms; when peril pressed and business forced, they devoured one another.

entries.zh: 建石首題，啓靡請罪。
entries.en: At Jianshi he put his head on the first draft, opened up, and asked only for punishment.
entries.literal: At Jianshi he put his head on the first draft, opened up, and asked only for punishment.

entries.zh: 朕錄其白旗之來，貰其旣往之咎。
entries.en: I recorded his coming under the white flag and pardoned his past fault.
entries.literal: I recorded his coming under the white flag and pardoned his past fault.

entries.zh: 亮反覆不忠，姦賄彰暴，有何可論！
entries.en: Liang was faithless and shifting, corruption and bribes openly violent—what is there to discuss!
entries.literal: Liang was faithless and shifting, corruption and bribes openly violent—what is there to discuss!

entries.zh: 妄相談述，具以狀對。」
entries.en: Rashly to talk and narrate such—report fully in a memorial for judgment."
entries.literal: Rashly to talk and narrate such—fully report by memorial for judgment."

entries.zh: 所詰十條，縝答支離而已。
entries.en: The ten points of censure—Zhen's answers were disjointed only.
entries.literal: The ten points of censure—Zhen's answers were disjointed only.

entries.zh: 亮因屏居閉掃，不通賓客。
entries.en: Liang then lived in seclusion, swept his quarters, and received no guests.
entries.literal: Liang then lived in seclusion, swept his quarters, and received no guests.

entries.zh: 遭母憂，居喪盡禮。
entries.en: When his mother died he observed mourning in full ritual.
entries.literal: When his mother died he observed mourning in full ritual.

entries.zh: 張稷字公喬，吳郡人也。
entries.en: Zhang Ji, styled Gongqiao, was a man of Wu commandery.
entries.literal: Zhang Ji, styled Gongqiao, was a native of Wu commandery.

entries.zh: 父永，宋右光祿大夫。
entries.en: His father Yong was Song right grand master of splendid happiness.
entries.literal: His father Yong was Song Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

entries.zh: 稷所生母遘疾歷時，稷始年十一，夜不解衣而養，永異之。
entries.en: Ji's birth mother had long been ill; when Ji was eleven he would not unbind his clothes to nurse her—Yong marveled at this.
entries.literal: Ji's birth mother had long been ill; when Ji was eleven he did not unbind his clothes to nurse her—Yong marveled at this.

entries.zh: 及母亡，毀瘠過人，杖而後起。
entries.en: When his mother died his grief-wasting exceeded others; he rose only with a staff's support.
entries.literal: When his mother died his grief-wasting exceeded others; he rose only with a staff's support.

entries.zh: 性疏率，朗悟有才略，與族兄充、融、卷等俱知名，時稱之曰：「充融卷稷，是爲四張。」
entries.en: By nature he was careless and open, bright with talent and stratagem; with his kinsmen Chong, Rong, and Juan he was all famed—the age called them, "Chong, Rong, Juan, and Ji—that is the Four Zhangs."
entries.literal: By nature he was careless and open, bright and perceptive with talent and stratagem; with his kinsmen Chong, Rong, and Juan he was all famed—the age called them: "Chong, Rong, Juan, and Ji—that is the Four Zhangs."

entries.zh: 起家著作佐郎，不拜，頻居父母憂，六載廬于墓側。
entries.en: He began as editorial assistant in the masters of writing but did not accept; he repeatedly sat parents' mourning, six years dwelling by the tomb.
entries.literal: He began office as Editorial Assistant in the Masters of Writing but did not accept; he repeatedly sat parents' mourning, six years dwelling by the tomb.

entries.zh: 服除，爲驃騎法曹行參軍，遷外兵參軍。
entries.en: When mourning ended he was rapid-cavalry law bureau acting staff officer, then outer army staff officer.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he was Rapid Cavalry Law Bureau Acting Staff Officer, promoted to Outer Army Staff Officer.

entries.zh: 稷長女楚瑗，適會稽孔氏，無子歸宗。
entries.en: Ji's eldest daughter Chu Yuan married the Kong clan of Kuaiji; childless, she returned to her clan.
entries.literal: Ji's eldest daughter Chu Yuan married into the Kong clan of Kuaiji; having no son, she returned to her clan.

entries.zh: 至稷見害，女以身蔽刃，先父卒。
entries.en: When Ji was killed, his daughter shielded him with her body and died before her father.
entries.literal: When Ji was killed, his daughter used her body to shield the blade and died before her father.

entries.zh: 稷子嵊，別有傳。
entries.en: Ji's son Song has a separate biography.
entries.literal: Ji's son Song has a separate biography.

entries.zh: 梁書卷第十六 列傳第十
entries.en: Book of Liang, Volume 16, Biographies 10
entries.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 16, Biographies 10

entries.zh: 珍國起家冠軍行參軍，累遷虎賁中郎將、南譙太守，治有能名。
entries.en: Zhenguo began as champion army acting staff officer, rose through tiger-guard commandant of the center and Nanqiao prefect, and won a name for able rule.
entries.literal: Zhenguo began office as champion army acting staff officer, rose through tiger-guard commandant of the center and Nanqiao prefect, and was famed for capable governance.

entries.zh: 時郡境苦饑，乃發米散財，以拯窮乏。
entries.en: The commandery was in bitter famine; he opened granaries and scattered wealth to save the poor.
entries.literal: At the time the commandery suffered bitter famine; he issued grain and scattered wealth to relieve the destitute.

entries.zh: 齊高帝手敕云：「卿愛人治國，甚副吾意也。」
entries.en: Qi Gaodi wrote by hand, "You love the people and govern the state—this suits my intent well."
entries.literal: Qi Gaodi wrote by hand: "You love the people and govern the state well—this suits my intent very well."

entries.zh: 永明初，遷桂陽內史，討捕盜賊，境內肅清。
entries.en: At the start of Yongming he became Guiyang interior governor, hunted bandits, and pacified the territory.
entries.literal: At the start of Yongming he was transferred to Guiyang interior governor, hunted down bandits and robbers, and the territory was pacified.

entries.zh: 罷任還都，路經江州，刺史柳世隆臨渚餞別，見珍國還裝輕素，乃歎曰：「此真可謂良二千石也！」
entries.en: When his term ended he returned to court; passing Jiangzhou, Inspector Liu Shilong came to the ford to see him off, saw his baggage light and plain, and sighed, "This is a true two-thousand-dan official!"
entries.literal: When his term ended he returned to the capital; passing through Jiangzhou, Inspector Liu Shilong came to the ford to bid farewell, saw Zhenguo's return baggage light and plain, and sighed: "This truly may be called a fine two-thousand-dan official!"

entries.zh: 還爲大司馬中兵參軍。
entries.en: On return he was made grand marshal central army staff officer.
entries.literal: On return he was made grand marshal central army staff officer.

entries.zh: 武帝雅相知賞，每歎曰：「晚代將家子弟，有如珍國者少矣。」
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Qi knew and prized him; he often sighed and said, "Among later generations of generals' houses, few sons are like Zhenguo."
entries.literal: Emperor Wu of Qi greatly knew and appreciated him; he often sighed and said: "Among later-age generals' sons, few are like Zhenguo."

entries.zh: 復出爲安成內史。
entries.en: He went out again as Ancheng interior governor.
entries.literal: He went out again as Ancheng interior governor.

entries.zh: 入爲越騎校尉，冠軍長史、鐘離太守。
entries.en: He entered as crossbow-and-horses commandant, champion chief of staff, and Zhongli prefect.
entries.literal: He entered office as crossbow-and-horses commandant, champion chief of staff, and Zhongli prefect.

entries.zh: 仍遷巴東、建平二郡太守。
entries.en: He was then transferred to prefect of Badong and Jianping.
entries.literal: He was then transferred to prefect of Ba and Ping commanderies.

entries.zh: 還爲遊擊將軍，以父憂去職。
entries.en: On return he was made raid general and left office for his father's mourning.
entries.literal: On return he was made raid general and left office for his father's mourning.

entries.zh: 建武末，魏軍圍司州，明帝使徐州刺史裴叔業攻拔渦陽，以爲聲援，起珍國爲輔國將軍，率兵助焉。
entries.en: Late in Jianwu, Wei besieged Si province; Emperor Ming sent Xuzhou inspector Pei Shuye to take Guoyang as a diversion and raised Zhenguo to supporting-the-state general to reinforce him.
entries.literal: Late in Jianwu, Wei forces besieged Si Province; Emperor Ming sent Xuzhou Inspector Pei Shuye to attack and capture Guoyang as a diversion, and raised Zhenguo to supporting-the-state general to lead troops in support.

entries.zh: 魏將楊大眼大衆奄至，叔業懼，棄軍走，珍國率其衆殿，故不至大敗。
entries.en: Wei general Yang Dayan's host suddenly arrived; Shuye in fear abandoned the army and fled; Zhenguo led the rearguard, so the defeat was not total.
entries.literal: Wei general Yang Dayan's great host suddenly arrived; Shuye in fear abandoned the army and fled; Zhenguo led his men as rearguard, so they did not suffer great defeat.

entries.zh: 永泰元年，會稽太守王敬則反，珍國又率衆距之。
entries.en: In Yongtai year one, Kuaiji prefect Wang Jingze rebelled; Zhenguo again led troops against him.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, Kuaiji prefect Wang Jingze rebelled; Zhenguo again led troops to resist.

entries.zh: 敬則平，遷寧朔將軍、青、冀二州刺史，將軍如故。
entries.en: When Jingze was pacified, he was made pacifying-the-north general and inspector of Qing and Ji, general as before.
entries.literal: When Jingze was pacified, he was made pacifying-the-north general and inspector of Qing and Ji, general as before.

entries.zh: 馬仙琕，字靈馥，扶風郿人也。
entries.en: Ma Xianpin, styled Lingfu, came from Mei in Fufeng.
entries.literal: Ma Xianpin, styled Lingfu, was a native of Mei in Fufeng.

entries.zh: 父伯鸞，宋冠軍司馬。
entries.en: His father Boluan was Song champion army acting chief of staff.
entries.literal: His father Boluan was Song champion army acting chief of staff.

entries.zh: 仙琕少以果敢聞，遭父憂，毀瘠過禮，負土成墳，手植松柏。
entries.en: From youth Xianpin was known for daring; when his father died his mourning exceeded ritual—he carried earth for the mound and planted pines and cypresses himself.
entries.literal: Xianpin from youth was known for daring and resolve; when his father died his grief-wasting exceeded ritual—he carried earth to make the mound and planted pines and cypresses with his own hands.

entries.zh: 起家郢州主簿，遷武騎常侍，爲小將，隨齊安陸王蕭緬。
entries.en: He began as Yezhou chief clerk, rose to martial-cavalry regular attendant, served as a junior officer, and followed Qi's prince of Anlu Xiao Mian.
entries.literal: He began office as Yezhou chief clerk, transferred to martial-cavalry regular attendant, served as a junior officer, and followed Qi Prince of Anlu Xiao Mian.

entries.zh: 緬卒，事明帝。
entries.en: When Mian died, he served Emperor Ming.
entries.literal: When Mian died, he served Emperor Ming.

entries.zh: 永元中，蕭遙光、崔慧景亂，累有戰功，以勳至前將軍。
entries.en: In Yongyuan, Xiao Yaoguang and Cui Huijing rebelled; he won repeated battle merit and rose to front general.
entries.literal: In Yongyuan, Xiao Yaoguang and Cui Huijing rebelled; he repeatedly had battle merit and through merit rose to front general.

entries.zh: 出爲龍驤將軍、南汝陰、譙二郡太守。
entries.en: He went out as dragon-prancing general and prefect of Nan Ruyin and Qiao.
entries.literal: He went out as dragon-prancing general and prefect of Nan Ruyin and Qiao.

entries.zh: 會壽陽新陷，魏將王肅侵邊，仙琕力戰，以寡克衆，魏人甚憚之。
entries.en: When Shouchun had newly fallen, Wei general Wang Su raided the border; Xianpin fought hard, the few overcame the many, and Wei greatly feared him.
entries.literal: When Shouchun had newly fallen, Wei general Wang Su invaded the border; Xianpin fought hard, with the few overcame the many, and Wei men greatly feared him.

entries.zh: 復以功遷寧朔將軍、豫州刺史。
entries.en: Again through merit he was transferred to pacifying-the-north general and Yuzhou inspector.
entries.literal: Again through merit he was transferred to pacifying-the-north general and Yuzhou inspector.

entries.zh: 義師起，東昏召珍國以衆還京師，入頓建康城。
entries.en: When the Righteous Army rose, Donghun summoned Zhenguo with his troops to the capital; he entered and garrisoned Jiankang.
entries.literal: When the Righteous Army rose, Donghun summoned Zhenguo with his troops back to the capital; he entered and garrisoned Jiankang city.

entries.zh: 義師至，使珍國出屯朱雀門，爲王茂軍所敗，乃入城。
entries.en: When the Righteous Army arrived, Donghun sent Zhenguo to camp at Zhuque Gate; Wang Mao's army defeated him and he re-entered the city.
entries.literal: When the Righteous Army arrived, Donghun had Zhenguo go out and camp at Zhuque Gate; he was defeated by Wang Mao's army and re-entered the city.

entries.zh: 仍密遣郄纂奉明鏡獻誠於高祖，高祖斷金以報之。
entries.en: He secretly sent Xi Zuan to present a bright mirror to Gaozu as pledge of loyalty; Gaozu broke gold in answer.
entries.literal: He then secretly sent Xi Zuan to present a bright mirror as pledge of loyalty to Gaozu; Gaozu broke gold to answer him.

entries.zh: 時城中咸思從義，莫敢先發，侍中、衛尉張稷都督衆軍，珍國潛結稷腹心張齊要稷，稷許之。
entries.en: Everyone in the city wished to turn to the righteous cause, yet none dared move first; attendant Zhang Ji as Ministry of Guard general commanded the host; Zhenguo secretly won over Ji's confidant Zhang Qi to sway Ji, and Ji agreed.
entries.literal: At the time everyone in the city wished to follow righteousness, yet none dared act first; Attendant Zhang Ji as Ministry of Guard general commanded all troops; Zhenguo secretly joined with Ji's trusted man Zhang Qi to win Ji over, and Ji agreed.

entries.zh: 十二月丙寅旦，珍國引稷於衛尉府，勒兵入自雲龍門，卽東昏於內殿斬之，與稷會尚書僕射王亮等於西鐘下，使中書舍人裴長穆等奉東昏首歸高祖。
entries.en: On the morning of day bingyin in the twelfth month, Zhenguo led Ji to the Ministry of Guard headquarters, mustered troops through Cloud Dragon Gate, and at once beheaded Donghun in the inner hall; with Ji he met right vice director Wang Liang and others below the western bell and had palace scribe Pei Changmu and others present Donghun's head to Gaozu.
entries.literal: On the morning of day bingyin in the twelfth month, Zhenguo led Ji to the Ministry of Guard headquarters, mustered troops entering by Cloud Dragon Gate, and at once beheaded Donghun in the inner hall; with Ji he met Right Vice Director Wang Liang and others below the western bell, and had Palace Scribe-in-Ordinary Pei Changmu and others present Donghun's head to Gaozu.

entries.zh: 以功授右衛將軍，辭不拜；
entries.en: For merit he was appointed right guard general; he declined;
entries.literal: For merit he was appointed right guard general; he declined and did not accept;

entries.zh: 又授徐州刺史，固乞留京師。
entries.en: Again appointed Xuzhou inspector; he firmly begged to stay in the capital.
entries.literal: Again appointed Xuzhou inspector; he firmly begged to remain in the capital.

entries.zh: 復賜金帛，珍國又固讓。
entries.en: Again granted gold and silk; Zhenguo again firmly declined.
entries.literal: Again granted gold and silk; Zhenguo again firmly declined.

entries.zh: 敕答曰：「昔田子泰固辭絹穀。
entries.en: An edict replied, "In old times Tian Zitai firmly declined silk and grain.
entries.literal: Edict replied: "In old times Tian Zitai firmly declined silk and grain.

entries.zh: 卿體國情深，良在可嘉。」
entries.en: Your care for the state runs deep—truly praiseworthy."
entries.literal: Your care for the state runs deep—truly praiseworthy."

entries.zh: 後因侍宴，帝問曰：「卿明鏡尚存，昔金何在？」
entries.en: Later at a feast the emperor asked, "Your bright mirror still exists—where is the gold of old?"
entries.literal: Later at a feast the emperor asked: "Your bright mirror still exists—where is the gold of old?"

entries.zh: 珍國答曰：「黃金謹在臣肘，不敢失墜。」
entries.en: Zhenguo answered, "The gold is carefully at my elbow; I dare not let it fall."
entries.literal: Zhenguo answered: "The gold is carefully at my elbow; I dare not let it fall."

entries.zh: 復爲右衛將軍，加給事中，遷左衛將軍，加散騎常侍。
entries.en: Again made right guard general with additional supervisory attendant; transferred to left guard general with additional scattered-cavalry attendant-in-ordinary.
entries.literal: Again made right guard general, with additional supervisory attendant; transferred to left guard general with additional scattered-cavalry attendant-in-ordinary.

entries.zh: 天監初，封灄陽縣侯，邑千戶。
entries.en: At the start of Tianjian he was enfeoffed marquis of Zhenyang with a thousand households.
entries.literal: At the start of Tianjian he was enfeoffed Marquis of Zhenyang with a thousand households.

entries.zh: 除都官尚書，常侍如故。
entries.en: Made director of the court for public works, attendant-in-ordinary as before.
entries.literal: Made Director of the Court for Public Works, attendant-in-ordinary as before.

entries.zh: 齊永元中，義師起，東昏徵稷歸，都督宮城諸軍事，居尚書省。
entries.en: In Qi Yongyuan, the righteous army rose; Donghun recalled Ji, made him commander of palace-city forces, and lodged him in the Masters of Writing complex.
entries.literal: In the Yongyuan era of Qi, the Righteous Army rose; Donghun summoned Ji back, made him Area Commander of all palace-city military affairs, and had him reside in the Masters of Writing complex.

entries.zh: 義兵至，周邊漸急，齊日造王珍國，陰與定計。
entries.en: As the righteous army drew near and the ring tightened, Qi visited Wang Zhenguo daily and secretly fixed their plan.
entries.literal: When the righteous army arrived, the siege around them grew pressing; Qi went daily to Wang Zhenguo and secretly settled plans with him.

entries.zh: 計定，夜引珍國就稷造膝，齊自執燭以成謀。
entries.en: When the plan was set, at night he brought Zhenguo to Ji for a knee-to-knee counsel; Qi himself held the candle while they plotted.
entries.literal: Once the plan was set, at night he led Zhenguo to Ji to join in deliberation knee to knee; Qi himself held the candle to complete the plot.

entries.zh: 明旦，與稷、珍國卽東昏於內殿，齊手刃焉。
entries.en: At dawn he, Ji, and Zhenguo seized Donghun in the inner hall; Qi himself killed him with his blade.
entries.literal: At dawn the next day, together with Ji and Zhenguo, he seized Donghun in the inner hall; Qi himself struck him dead with his blade.

entries.zh: 明年，高祖受禪，封齊安昌縣侯，邑五百戶，仍爲寧朔將軍、歷陽太守。
entries.en: Next year Gaozu took the throne; Qi was made Marquis of Anchang with five hundred households, retaining pacification north general and Liyang administrator.
entries.literal: The next year Gaozu received the abdication; Qi was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anchang county with a fief of five hundred households, and remained Pacification North General and Administrator of Liyang.

entries.zh: 齊手不知書，目不識字，而在郡有清政，吏事甚脩。
entries.en: Qi could neither write nor read, yet in office he ruled cleanly and managed affairs diligently.
entries.literal: Qi did not know writing by hand and could not read characters by sight, yet in his commandery he had pure governance and handled official business very well.

entries.zh: 義師起，四方多回應，高祖使仙琕故人姚仲賓說之，仙琕於軍斬仲賓以徇。
entries.en: When the Righteous Army rose, all quarters largely responded; Gaozu sent Xianpin's old friend Yao Zhongbin to win him over; Xianpin beheaded Zhongbin in camp to warn the host.
entries.literal: When the Righteous Army rose, all quarters largely responded; Gaozu sent Xianpin's old friend Yao Zhongbin to persuade him; Xianpin in the army beheaded Zhongbin to display to the host.

entries.zh: 義師至新林，仙琕猶持兵於江西，日鈔運漕，建康城陷，仙琕號哭經宿，乃解兵歸罪。
entries.en: When the Righteous Army reached Xinlin, Xianpin still held arms west of the river, daily requisitioning transport grain; when Jiankang fell, he wept all night, then laid down arms and came to submit his guilt.
entries.literal: When the Righteous Army reached Xinlin, Xianpin still held arms on the west of the river, daily requisitioning transport grain; when Jiankang fell, Xianpin wept and wailed a whole night, then laid down arms and came to submit his guilt.

entries.zh: 高祖勞之曰：「射鉤斬袪，昔人弗忌。
entries.en: Gaozu comforted him, saying, "Shooting the hook, cutting the sleeve—men of old did not resent such things.
entries.literal: Gaozu comforted him, saying: "Shooting the hook, cutting the sleeve—men of old did not resent such.

entries.zh: 卿勿以戮使斷運，苟自嫌絕也。」
entries.en: Do not, because you killed the envoy and cut off supply, needlessly estrange yourself."
entries.literal: Do not, because you killed the envoy and cut off supply, needlessly estrange yourself."

entries.zh: 仙琕謝曰：「小人如失主犬，後主飼之，便復爲用。」
entries.en: Xianpin apologized, "A petty man is like a stray dog without a master; when a new master feeds it, it serves again."
entries.literal: Xianpin apologized: "A petty man is like a stray dog without a master; when a new master feeds it, it will serve again."

entries.zh: 高祖笑而美之。
entries.en: Gaozu laughed and praised him.
entries.literal: Gaozu laughed and praised him.

entries.zh: 俄而仙琕母卒，高祖知其貧，賻給甚厚。
entries.en: Soon Xianpin's mother died; Gaozu knew he was poor and gave funeral gifts very generously.
entries.literal: Soon Xianpin's mother died; Gaozu knew he was poor and gave funeral gifts very generously.

entries.zh: 仙琕號泣，謂弟仲艾曰：「蒙大造之恩，未獲上報。
entries.en: Xianpin wept and said to his younger brother Zhong'ai, "Having received great creating grace, I have not yet repaid it.
