entries.literal: In Tianjian year two, when Ai went out to command the southern frontier, Facai stayed in the capital, was promoted to Director of the Treasury, and left office for his father's mourning.

entries.zh: 服闋，除中書通事舍人，出爲本州別駕。
entries.en: After mourning he handled Secretariat affairs and went out as native province chief clerk.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he was made Secretariat attendant who handles affairs and went out as chief clerk of his native province.

entries.zh: 入爲通直散騎侍郎，復掌通事，遷尚書右丞。
entries.en: He entered as Regular Attendant, again handled affairs, then became Right Director.
entries.literal: He entered as Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, again handled affairs, and was promoted Right Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 晉安王爲荊州，重除別駕從事史。
entries.en: When the Prince of Jin'an held Jingzhou, he was again chief clerk and staff officer.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Jin'an held Jingzhou, he was again made chief clerk and staff officer.

entries.zh: 復徵爲尚書右丞，出爲招遠將軍、建康令。
entries.en: Recalled as Right Director, he went out as general who invites from afar and Jiankang magistrate.
entries.literal: He was summoned again as Right Director, went out as general who invites from afar and magistrate of Jiankang.

entries.zh: 不受俸秩，比去任，將至百金，縣曹啟輸臺庫。
entries.en: He took no salary; near a hundred jin of gold had gathered when he left, and the county reported it to the central treasury.
entries.literal: He would not take salary; by the time he left office he had nearly a hundred jin of gold, and the county clerks reported it to the central treasury.

entries.zh: 高祖嘉其清節，曰：「居職若斯，可以爲百城表矣。」
entries.en: Gaozu prized his integrity and said, "To hold office like this is to be a model for a hundred cities.”
entries.literal: Gaozu prized his integrity and said: "To hold office like this is to stand as a model for a hundred cities.”

entries.zh: 卽日遷太府卿。
entries.en: That same day he was made grand chamberlain.
entries.literal: That same day he was transferred to Grand Chamberlain.

entries.zh: 尋除南康內史，恥以讓俸受名，辭不拜。
entries.en: Soon named Nankang interior administrator, he refused the post rather than accept a title earned by yielding his salary.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed interior administrator of Nankang; ashamed to accept the name of one who yielded his salary, he declined and did not take the post.

entries.zh: 俄轉雲騎將軍、少府卿。
entries.en: Before long he became cloud-cavalry general and minister of palace supplies.
entries.literal: Before long he was transferred to Cloud-Cavalry General and Minister of Palace Supplies.

entries.zh: 出爲信武長史、江夏太守。
entries.en: He went out as Trustworthy Martial chief clerk and Jiangxia administrator.
entries.literal: He went out as chief clerk on the Trustworthy Martial staff and Jiangxia administrator.

entries.zh: 因被代，表便道還鄉。
entries.en: Replaced in office, he asked leave to go home by the direct route.
entries.literal: When he was replaced, he memorialized to return home by the direct route.

entries.zh: 至家，割宅爲寺，棲心物表。
entries.en: At home he gave part of his house for a temple and turned his mind from the world.
entries.literal: At home he divided his residence to make a temple and lodged his heart beyond worldly affairs.

entries.zh: 皇太子以法才舊臣，累有優令，召使東下，未及發而卒，時年六十三。
entries.en: The crown prince, holding Facai an old servant, sent him generous summons east again and again; he died before he could leave, at sixty-three.
entries.literal: The crown prince, since Facai was an old retainer, repeatedly sent favorable orders summoning him east; before he could set out he died, aged sixty-three.

entries.zh: 天監初，遷驍騎將軍、領少府卿；
entries.en: At Tianjian's opening he was Raiding Cavalry General and palace workshop director;
entries.literal: At the start of Tianjian he was promoted to Raiding Cavalry General and Director of the Palace Workshop;

entries.zh: 俄遷御史中丞，領本州大中正。
entries.en: soon Censor-in-Chief and head of his province's great rectifiers.
entries.literal: soon he was Censor-in-Chief and head of the great rectifiers of his native province.

entries.zh: 初，藹發江陵，無故於船得八車輻，如中丞健步避道者，至是果遷焉。
entries.en: Leaving Jiangling he had found eight carriage hubs on the boat, like a censor stepping aside—and now the omen held.
entries.literal: When Ai had set out from Jiangling he found for no reason on the boat eight carriage hubs, like a censor's brisk step giving way on the road—and now the omen came true.

entries.zh: 藹性公強，居憲臺甚稱職。
entries.en: Fair and forceful, he shone at the censorate.
entries.literal: Ai's nature was fair and forceful; at the censorate he filled the post admirably.

entries.zh: 時長沙宣武王將葬，而車府忽於庫火油絡，欲推主者。
entries.en: King Xuanwu of Changsha was to be buried when the carriage office found lamp oil burning in the storehouse and sought a culprit.
entries.literal: At the time King Xuanwu of Changsha was to be buried, and the carriage office suddenly found lamp oil ablaze in the storehouse; they wished to impeach the keeper.

entries.zh: 藹曰：「昔晉武庫火，張華以爲積油萬石必然。
entries.en: Ai said, "When Jin's arsenal burned, Zhang Hua said ten thousand stone of piled oil made fire inevitable.
entries.literal: Ai said: "In Jin, when the arsenal caught fire, Zhang Hua held that ten thousand stone of oil piled up made it inevitable.

entries.zh: 今庫若有灰，非吏罪也。」
entries.en: If ash lies in the storehouse, no clerk is to blame."
entries.literal: If the storehouse now holds ash, it is no clerk's crime."

entries.zh: 旣而檢之，果有積灰。
entries.en: Inspection found piled ash.
entries.literal: On inspection there was indeed piled ash.

entries.zh: 時稱其博物弘恕焉。
entries.en: The age praised his learning and his large forgiveness.
entries.literal: The age praised his broad learning and large forgiveness.

entries.zh: 梁書卷第十九 列傳第十三
entries.en: Book of Liang, Volume 19, Biographies 13
entries.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 19, Biographies 13

entries.zh: 劉季連字惠續，彭城人也。
entries.en: Liu Lijian, styled Huixu, came from Pengcheng.
entries.literal: Liu Lijian, styled Huixu, was a native of Pengcheng.

entries.zh: 父思考，以宋高祖族弟顯於宋世，位至金紫光祿大夫。
entries.en: His father Sikao, kin to Song Gaozu, shone in the Song age and rose to Grand Master of Splendid Virtue with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
entries.literal: His father Sikao, as a cousin of Song's founding sovereign Gaozu, had been eminent in the Song age and rose to Grand Master of Splendid Virtue with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

entries.zh: 季連有名譽，早歷清官。
entries.en: Lijian was widely esteemed and early held clean posts.
entries.literal: Lijian had a fine reputation and early passed through pure offices.

entries.zh: 齊高帝受禪，悉誅宋室近屬，將及季連等，太宰褚淵素善之，固請乃免。
entries.en: When Qi Gaozu took the throne he meant to kill every near branch of Song; Lijian was next, but Chu Yuan, who had long favored him, pleaded until he was spared.
entries.literal: When Qi Gaozu accepted the abdication, he was set to slay all near kin of the Song house; Lijian's turn was coming, but the grand minister Chu Yuan, who had long favored him, pleaded hard and he was spared.

entries.zh: 建元中，季連爲尚書左丞。
entries.en: In Jianyuan he was Left Director in the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: In the Jianyuan era he was Left Director in the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 永明初，出爲江夏內史，累遷平南長沙內史，冠軍長史、廣陵太守，並行府州事。
entries.en: At Yongming's opening he was Jiangxia interior governor, then Pingnan and Changsha, champion staff officer and Guangling prefect, all running his seat.
entries.literal: At the opening of Yongming he went out as interior governor of Jiangxia, rose through interior governor of Pingnan and Changsha, champion staff officer and Guangling prefect, all while running his district seat.

entries.zh: 入爲給事黃門侍郎，轉太子中庶子。
entries.en: He entered as Yellow Gate attendant, then crown prince chief of staff.
entries.literal: He entered as Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gate who presents matters, then became crown prince chief of staff.

entries.zh: 建武中，又出爲平西蕭遙欣長史、南郡太守。
entries.en: In Jianwu he again went out as staff officer to Pingxi general Xiao Yaoqin and Nanjun prefect.
entries.literal: In the Jianwu era he again went out as staff officer to Pingxi general Xiao Yaoqin and prefect of Nanjun.

entries.zh: 時明帝諸子幼弱，內親則仗遙欣兄弟，外親則倚后弟劉暄、內弟江祏。
entries.en: The Ming Emperor's sons were still young; inside the palace he leaned on the Yaoqin brothers, outside on the empress's brother Liu Xuan and her brother-in-law Jiang Shi.
entries.literal: At that time the Ming Emperor's sons were young and weak; for kin within the palace he relied on the Yaoqin brothers, for kin without on the empress's brother Liu Xuan and her brother-in-law Jiang Shi.

entries.zh: 遙欣之鎮江陵也，意寄甚隆；
entries.en: When Yaoqin held Jiangling, trust in him ran deep;
entries.literal: When Yaoqin took his post at Jiangling his trust ran deep;

entries.zh: 而遙欣至州，多招賓客，厚自封殖，明帝甚惡之。
entries.en: but in the province he gathered guests and grew fat on graft, and the Ming Emperor came to hate him.
entries.literal: but once in the province he drew in many guests and fattened himself on graft, and the Ming Emperor came to hate him.

entries.zh: 季連族甥琅邪王會爲遙欣諮議參軍，美容貌，頗才辯，遙欣遇之甚厚。
entries.en: Lijian's clan nephew Wang Hui of Langya was Yaoqin's advising staff officer—handsome and sharp-tongued; Yaoqin favored him.
entries.literal: Lijian's clan nephew Wang Hui of Langya served as Yaoqin's advising staff officer—handsome, quick with words; Yaoqin favored him greatly.

entries.zh: 會多所慠忽，於公座與遙欣競侮季連，季連憾之，乃密表明帝，稱遙欣有異迹。
entries.en: Hui was insolent; before the assembly he and Yaoqin mocked Lijian together. Lijian nursed the grudge and secretly told the Ming Emperor that Yaoqin showed suspicious signs.
entries.literal: Hui was often insolent; at a public session he vied with Yaoqin to mock Lijian, who bore a grudge and secretly reported to the Ming Emperor that Yaoqin showed suspicious conduct.

entries.zh: 明帝納焉，乃以遙欣爲雍州刺史。
entries.en: The emperor believed him and made Yaoqin Yongzhou inspector.
entries.literal: The emperor took it in and made Yaoqin inspector of Yongzhou.

entries.zh: 明帝心德季連，四年，以爲輔國將軍、益州刺史，令據遙欣上流。
entries.en: Grateful to Lijian, in year four the emperor made him Supporting-the-State General and Yizhou inspector, set to hold the upper river against Yaoqin.
entries.literal: The emperor was grateful to Lijian; in year four he made him Supporting-the-State General and inspector of Yizhou, ordering him to hold the upper reaches against Yaoqin.

entries.zh: 季連父，宋世爲益州，貪鄙無政績，州人猶以義故，善待季連。
entries.en: His father had held Yizhou in Song times, greedy and without merit, yet the people, for old friendship's sake, still treated Lijian kindly.
entries.literal: Lijian's father in the Song age had held Yizhou, greedy and without good governance, yet the people, still for old friendship's sake, treated Lijian kindly.

entries.zh: 季連下車，存問故老，撫納新舊，見父時故吏，皆對之流涕。
entries.en: On taking office he asked after elders, comforted old and new ties, and wept with his father's former clerks.
entries.literal: When Lijian stepped down from his carriage he inquired of elders, comforted old and new ties, and when he saw his father's former clerks he wept openly with them.

entries.zh: 辟遂寧人龔愜爲府主簿。
entries.en: He made Gong Yi of Suining his chief clerical secretary.
entries.literal: He recruited Gong Yi of Suining as his chief clerical secretary.

entries.zh: 愜，龔穎之孫，累世有學行，故引焉。
entries.en: Yi was Gong Ying's grandson; learning and conduct ran in the line, so he was brought in.
entries.literal: Yi was grandson of Gong Ying; for generations the house had learning and conduct, so he was brought in.

entries.zh: 齊安陸王子敬爲南兗州，頗持兵自衛。
entries.en: Qi Prince of Anlu Zijing held Southern Yanzhou and kept many troops for self-defense.
entries.literal: Qi Prince of Anlu Zijing held Southern Yanzhou and kept many troops about him for self-defense.

entries.zh: 明帝遣廣之討子敬，廣之至歐陽，遣伯之先驅，因城開，獨入斬子敬。
entries.en: The Ming Emperor sent Guangzhi to punish Zijing; at Ouyang Guangzhi sent Bozhi ahead, and when the gates opened Bozhi went in alone and beheaded Zijing.
entries.literal: The Ming Emperor sent Guangzhi to punish Zijing; reaching Ouyang, Guangzhi sent Bozhi ahead, and when the gates opened Bozhi went in alone and beheaded Zijing.

entries.zh: 又頻有戰功，以勳累遷爲冠軍將軍、驃騎司馬，封魚復縣伯，邑五百戶。
entries.en: He won merit again and again, rose by battle honors to Champion General and Rapid Cavalry Marshal, and was enfeoffed Baron of Yufu with five hundred households.
entries.literal: He won merit again and again, rose by battle honors to Champion General and Rapid Cavalry Marshal, and was enfeoffed Baron of Yufu with five hundred households.

entries.zh: 伯之子虎牙，時爲直閤將軍，高祖手疏龍符罪，親付虎牙，虎牙封示伯之；
entries.en: Bozhi's son Huya was Direct Attendant general; Gaozu wrote Longfu's crimes in his own hand for Huya, and Huya showed his father;
entries.literal: Bozhi's son Huya was then Direct Attendant General; Gaozu wrote Longfu's crimes in his own hand and gave the note to Huya; Huya showed it to Bozhi;

entries.zh: 高祖又遣代江州別駕鄧繕，伯之並不受命。
entries.en: Gaozu also sent a replacement for vice-inspector Deng Shan; Bozhi refused both.
entries.literal: Gaozu also sent a man to replace Jiangzhou vice-inspector Deng Shan, and Bozhi refused both orders.

entries.zh: 答高祖曰：「龍符驍勇健兒，鄧繕事有績效，臺所遣別駕，請以爲治中。」
entries.en: He answered Gaozu, "Longfu is a bold fighter; Deng Shan has done real work. Let the court's vice-inspector serve as chief clerk instead."
entries.literal: He answered Gaozu, "Longfu is a fierce and valiant fighter; Deng Shan has real achievements. As for the vice-inspector the court sends, please make him chief clerk instead."

entries.zh: 繕於是日夜說伯之云：「臺家府庫空竭，復無器仗，三倉無米，東境饑流，此萬代一時也，機不可失。」
entries.en: Shan urged him day and night, "The court's treasuries are bare, its arsenals empty, the granaries dry, the east a river of refugees—this moment will not come again."
entries.literal: Shan then night and day urged Bozhi, saying, "The court's storehouses are empty and there are no weapons; the three granaries have no grain; the eastern lands are starving wanderers—this is a chance that comes once in ten thousand generations; the moment must not be lost."

entries.zh: 緭、永忠等每贊成之。
entries.en: Wei, Yongzhong, and the rest kept urging him on.
entries.literal: Wei, Yongzhong, and the rest kept seconding him.

entries.zh: 伯之謂繕：「今段啓卿，若復不得，便與卿共下使反。」
entries.en: Bozhi told Shan, "This time I back you; if I fail again, I march with you against the court."
entries.literal: Bozhi told Shan, "This time I raise you up; if I still fail, I will go down with you and rebel."

entries.zh: 高祖敕部內一郡處繕，伯之於是集府州佐史謂曰：「奉齊建安王教，率江北義勇十萬，已次六合，見使以江州見力運糧速下。
entries.en: Gaozu seized Shan in one commandery; Bozhi gathered his staff and said, "By Qi's Prince of Jian'an I lead a hundred thousand northern volunteers at Liuhe; an envoy orders Jiangzhou to haul grain south at once.
entries.literal: Gaozu ordered one commandery in the circuit to take Shan in; Bozhi then gathered the province's officers and clerks and said, "By the Prince of Jian'an's command of Qi I lead a hundred thousand righteous men of the north; they have halted at Liuhe. An envoy orders the Jiangzhou levies to haul grain south at once.

entries.zh: 我荷明帝厚恩，誓死以報。
entries.en: I owe Mingdi a great debt and swear to repay it with my life.
entries.literal: I owe Emperor Ming a deep grace and swear to die repaying it.

entries.zh: 今便纂嚴備辦。」
entries.en: We arm and prepare now."
entries.literal: We arm and make ready at once."

entries.zh: 使緭詐爲蕭寶夤書，以示僚佐。
entries.en: He had Wei forge a letter as from Xiao Baoyin and show the staff.
entries.literal: He had Wei forge a letter in Xiao Baoyin's name and show it to his staff.

entries.zh: 於廳事前爲壇，殺牲以盟。
entries.en: Before the hall he built an altar and slaughtered victims for the oath.
entries.literal: Before the hall he raised an altar and slew victims to swear the oath.

entries.zh: 伯之先飲，長史已下次第歃血。
entries.en: Bozhi drank first; the chief clerk and the rest pledged in turn.
entries.literal: Bozhi drank first; the chief clerk and those below took the blood in order.

entries.zh: 緭說伯之曰：「今舉大事，宜引衆望，程元沖不與人同心；
entries.en: Wei urged him, "A great rising needs men the troops trust. Cheng Yuanchong is not with us;
entries.literal: Wei urged Bozhi, "In a great undertaking you should lean on men the host admires. Cheng Yuanchong does not share our heart;

entries.zh: 臨川內史王觀，僧虔之孫，人身不惡，便可召爲長史，以代元沖。」
entries.en: Linchuan interior administrator Wang Guan, Sengqian's grandson, is not ill-favored—summon him as chief clerk for Yuanchong."
entries.literal: Linchuan interior administrator Wang Guan, grandson of Sengqian, is not ill-favored in person—call him in as chief clerk to replace Yuanchong."

entries.zh: 伯之從之。
entries.en: Bozhi agreed.
entries.literal: Bozhi followed this.

entries.zh: 仍以緭爲尋陽太守，加討逆將軍；
entries.en: He made Wei Xunyang administrator and Suppresses-Rebellion general;
entries.literal: He also made Wei administrator of Xunyang and gave him the added title Suppresses-Rebellion General;

entries.zh: 永忠輔義將軍；
entries.en: Yongzhong became Assists-the-Cause general;
entries.literal: Yongzhong was made Assists-the-Cause General;

entries.zh: 龍符爲豫州刺史，率五百人守大雷。
entries.en: Longfu became Yuzhou inspector with five hundred men to hold Dalei.
entries.literal: Longfu was made inspector of Yuzhou and led five hundred men to hold Dalei.

entries.zh: 大雷戍主沈慧休，鎮南參軍李延伯。
entries.en: Dalei was held by Shen Huixiu; Li Yanbo was Pacifies-the-South staff officer.
entries.literal: Dalei garrison commander Shen Huixiu and Pacifies-the-South staff officer Li Yanbo.

entries.zh: 又遣鄉人孫鄰、李景受龍符節度，鄰爲徐州，景爲郢州。
entries.en: He sent townsman Sun Lin and Li Jing under Longfu—Lin for Xuzhou, Jing for Yingzhou.
entries.literal: He also sent his townsman Sun Lin and Li Jing under Longfu's command—Lin for Xuzhou, Jing for Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 豫章太守鄭伯倫起郡兵距守。
entries.en: Yuzhang administrator Zheng Bolun raised commandery forces to resist.
entries.literal: Yuzhang administrator Zheng Bolun raised the commandery troops to hold him off.

entries.zh: 程元沖旣失職，於家合率數百人，使伯之典籤呂孝通、戴元則爲內應。
entries.en: Yuanchong, out of office, gathered hundreds at home and set Bozhi's recorders Lü Xiaotong and Dai Yuanze within.
entries.literal: Yuanchong, having lost his post, gathered several hundred men at home and had Bozhi's recorders Lü Xiaotong and Dai Yuanze act as inside agents.

entries.zh: 伯之每旦常作伎，日晡輒臥，左右仗身皆休息。
entries.en: Each dawn Bozhi held his entertainments; by afternoon he slept and his guards rested.
entries.literal: Each morning Bozhi would perform his entertainments; by late afternoon he would lie down and his bodyguards all rested.

entries.zh: 元沖因其解弛，從北門入，徑至廳事前。
entries.en: Yuanchong used the slack to enter the north gate and reach the hall.
entries.literal: Yuanchong used that slack hour to enter by the north gate and go straight to the hall.

entries.zh: 伯之聞叫聲，自率出蕩，元沖力不能敵，走逃廬山。
entries.en: Hearing the clamor, Bozhi rushed out himself; Yuanchong could not stand and fled to Mount Lu.
entries.literal: Hearing the outcry, Bozhi himself rushed out to fight; Yuanchong could not hold and fled to Mount Lu.

entries.zh: 時會稽人石文安字守休，隱居鄉里，專行禮讓，代季連爲尚書左丞，出爲江夏內史，又代季連入爲御史中丞，與季連相善。
entries.en: At that time Shi Wen'an of Kuaiji, styled Shouxiu, lived in seclusion practicing courtesy, had replaced Lijian as Left Director, gone out as Jiangxia interior governor, then replaced him again as Censor-in-Chief—and he and Lijian were friends.
entries.literal: At that time Shiwen'an of Kuaiji, styled Shouxiu, lived in seclusion in his district practicing courtesy and deference, had replaced Lijian as Left Director, gone out as Jiangxia interior governor, and again replaced Lijian as Censor-in-Chief—he and Lijian were on good terms.

entries.zh: 子仲淵字欽回，聞義師起，率鄉人以應高祖。
entries.en: His son Zhongyuan, styled Qinhui, hearing the Righteous Army had risen, led the district to answer Gaozu.
entries.literal: His son Zhongyuan, styled Qinhui, hearing the Righteous Army had risen, led the district men to answer Gaozu.

entries.zh: 天監初，拜郢州別駕，從高祖平京邑。
entries.en: At Tianjian's opening he was Yingzhou Bieyu and followed Gaozu to pacify the capital.
entries.literal: At the start of Tianjian he was made Bieyu of Yingzhou and followed Gaozu to pacify the capital.

entries.zh: 伯之與豫章人鄧繕、永興人戴永忠並有舊，繕經藏伯之息英免禍，伯之尤德之。
entries.en: He was old friends with Deng Shan of Yuzhang and Dai Yongzhong of Yongxing; Shan had once hidden his son Ying from harm, and Bozhi owed him deeply.
entries.literal: Bozhi was old friends with Deng Shan of Yuzhang and Dai Yongzhong of Yongxing; Shan had once hidden Bozhi's son Ying and saved him from harm, and Bozhi was deeply obliged.

entries.zh: 及在州，用繕爲別駕，永忠記室參軍。
entries.en: In the province he made Shan vice-inspector and Yongzhong his recorder.
entries.literal: In the province he made Shan vice-inspector and Yongzhong recorder on his staff.

entries.zh: 河南褚緭，京師之薄行者，齊末爲揚州西曹，遇亂居閭里；
entries.en: Chu Wei of Henan was a rake of the capital; at Qi's end he was Yangzhou western staff officer and, when chaos came, stayed in his lane;
entries.literal: Chu Wei of Henan was a loose man of the capital; at the end of Qi he was western staff officer of Yangzhou and, when turmoil came, lived in his lane;

entries.zh: 而輕薄互能自致，惟緭獨不達。
entries.en: while other rakes still found their way up, only Wei could not.
entries.literal: while other light fellows could still advance themselves, only Wei failed to rise.

entries.zh: 高祖卽位，緭頻造尚書范雲，雲不好緭，堅距之。
entries.en: After Gaozu took the throne Wei often visited Fan Yun, minister of personnel; Yun disliked him and kept him out.
entries.literal: After Gaozu took the throne Wei often called on the Minister of Personnel Fan Yun; Yun disliked him and firmly shut him out.

entries.zh: 緭益怒，私語所知曰：「建武以後，草澤底下，悉化成貴人，吾何罪而見棄。
entries.en: Wei grew furious and whispered to friends, "Since Jianwu every nobody has become a lord—what is my crime that I am thrown away?
entries.literal: Wei grew angrier and told those he knew in private, "Since Jianwu, every man from the grass roots has turned into a noble—what crime is mine that I am cast aside?

entries.zh: 今天下草創，饑饉不已，喪亂未可知。
entries.en: The realm is new, famine unending, and no one knows whether the turmoil will end.
entries.literal: The realm is newly founded, famine does not cease, and whether chaos will end is still unknown.

entries.zh: 陳伯之擁強兵在江州，非代來臣，有自疑意；
entries.en: Chen Bozhi holds Jiangzhou with a strong host; he is no hereditary minister and nurses doubts;
entries.literal: Chen Bozhi holds strong troops in Jiangzhou; he is no minister of long descent and bears private doubts;

entries.zh: 且熒惑守南斗，詎非爲我出。
entries.en: and the Sparkling One stands in the Southern Dipper—surely it moves for me.
entries.literal: and the Sparkling One guards the Southern Dipper—surely it rises for me.

entries.zh: 今者一行，事若無成，入魏，何遽減作河南郡。」
entries.en: If this venture fails, I enter Wei—why not become governor of Henan at once?"
entries.literal: If this one venture fails, I need only go to Wei—why should I not at once be made governor of Henan?"

entries.zh: 於是遂投伯之書佐王思穆，事之，大見親狎。
entries.en: So he joined Bozhi's clerk Wang Simu, served him closely, and won great favor.
entries.literal: So he threw in his lot with Bozhi's clerk Wang Simu, served him, and was soon treated with great intimacy.

entries.zh: 及伯之鄉人朱龍符爲長流參軍，並乘伯之愚闇，恣行姦險，刑政通塞，悉共專之。
entries.en: Zhu Longfu, Bozhi's townsman, became senior recorder; he and Wei preyed on Bozhi's ignorance and ran the province by fraud and force.
entries.literal: When Bozhi's townsman Zhu Longfu became senior recorder, together with Wei they rode Bozhi's dullness and ran wild with treachery; punishments and policy passed or failed as they alone willed.

entries.zh: 天監元年六月，元起至巴西，季連遣其將李奉伯等拒戰。
entries.en: In the sixth month of Tianjian year one Yuanqi reached Baxi; Lijian sent Li Fengbo and others to fight.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of Tianjian year one Yuanqi reached Baxi; Lijian sent his generals Li Fengbo and others to fight.

entries.zh: 兵交，互有得失，久之，奉伯乃敗退還成都。
entries.en: Battle swayed back and forth; after a long while Fengbo was beaten back to Chengdu.
entries.literal: Battle swayed back and forth; after a long while Fengbo was beaten back to Chengdu.

entries.zh: 季連驅略居人，閉城固守。
entries.en: Lijian drove out the inhabitants, shut the city, and held firm.
entries.literal: Lijian drove out the inhabitants, shut the city, and held firm.

entries.zh: 元起稍進圍之。
entries.en: Yuanqi slowly advanced and besieged him.
entries.literal: Yuanqi slowly advanced and besieged him.

entries.zh: 是冬，季連城局參軍江希之等謀以城降，不果，季連誅之。
entries.en: That winter staff officer Jiang Xizhi and others plotted to yield the city but failed; Lijian executed them.
entries.literal: That winter staff officer Jiang Xizhi and others plotted to yield the city but failed; Lijian executed them.

entries.zh: 蜀中喪亂已二年矣，城中食盡，升米三千，亦無所糴，餓死者相枕。
entries.en: Shu had known turmoil two years; food in the city was gone—a sheng of rice cost three thousand cash and could not be bought; the dead lay atop one another from hunger.
entries.literal: Shu had known turmoil two years; food in the city was gone—a sheng of rice cost three thousand cash yet could not be bought; the dead lay atop one another from hunger.

entries.zh: 其無親黨者，又殺而食之。
entries.en: Those without kin were killed and eaten.
entries.literal: Those without kin were killed and eaten.

entries.zh: 季連食粥累月，饑窘無計。
entries.en: Lijian ate gruel for months, hunger and straits without plan.
entries.literal: Lijian ate gruel for months, hunger and straits without plan.

entries.zh: 二年正月，高祖遣主書趙景悅宣詔降季連，季連肉袒請罪。
entries.en: In year two's first month Gaozu sent chief secretary Zhao Jingyue to announce an edict accepting Lijian's surrender; Lijian bared his torso and begged pardon.
entries.literal: In the first month of year two Gaozu sent chief secretary Zhao Jingyue to announce an edict accepting Lijian's surrender; Lijian bared his torso and begged pardon.

entries.zh: 元起遷季連於城外，俄而造焉，待之以禮。
entries.en: Yuanqi moved Lijian outside the walls and soon came to visit, treating him with courtesy.
entries.literal: Yuanqi moved Lijian outside the walls and soon came to visit, treating him with courtesy.

entries.zh: 季連謝曰：「早知如此，豈有前日之事。」
entries.en: Lijian said, "Had I known it would come to this, there would never have been what happened before."
entries.literal: Lijian said: "Had I known it would come to this, there would never have been what happened before."

entries.zh: 元起誅李奉伯幷諸渠帥，送季連還京師。
entries.en: Yuanqi executed Li Fengbo and the other ringleaders and sent Lijian back to the capital.
entries.literal: Yuanqi executed Li Fengbo and the other ringleaders and sent Lijian back to the capital.

entries.zh: 季連將發，人莫之視，惟龔愜送焉。
entries.en: As Lijian was about to set out, none would look at him; only Gong Yi saw him off.
entries.literal: As Lijian was about to set out, none would look at him; only Gong Yi saw him off.

entries.zh: 天監四年，詔太尉、臨川王宏率衆軍北討，宏命記室丘遲私與伯之書曰：
entries.en: In Tianjian year four an edict sent Grand Marshal Linchuan Wang Hong north; Hong had his recorder Qiu Chi write Chen Bozhi privately, saying:
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Tianjian an edict had Grand Marshal Linchuan Wang Hong lead the armies north; Hong ordered his recorder Qiu Chi to send Chen Bozhi a private letter, saying:

entries.zh: 季連旣至，詣闕謝，高祖引見之。
entries.en: When Lijian arrived he went to the palace to give thanks; Gaozu received him.
entries.literal: When Lijian arrived he went to the palace to give thanks; Gaozu received him.

entries.zh: 季連自東掖門入，數步一稽顙，以至高祖前。
entries.en: Lijian entered by the East Flank Gate, kowtowing every few steps until he stood before Gaozu.
entries.literal: Lijian entered by the East Flank Gate, kowtowing every few steps until he stood before Gaozu.

entries.zh: 高祖笑謂曰：「卿欲慕劉備而曾不及公孫述，豈無臥龍之臣乎。」
entries.en: Gaozu laughed and said, "You wished to rival Liu Bei yet could not even match Gongsun Shu—had you no Wolong at your side?"
entries.literal: Gaozu laughed and said: "You wished to rival Liu Bei yet could not even match Gongsun Shu—had you no Wolong at your side?"

entries.zh: 季連復稽顙謝。
entries.en: Lijian kowtowed again in thanks.
entries.literal: Lijian kowtowed again in thanks.

entries.zh: 赦爲庶人。
entries.en: He was pardoned to commoner status.
entries.literal: He was pardoned to commoner status.

entries.zh: 四年正月，因出建陽門，爲蜀人藺道恭所殺。
entries.en: In year four's first month, going out the Jianyang Gate, he was killed by the Shu man Lan Daogong.
entries.literal: In the first month of year four, going out the Jianyang Gate, he was killed by the Shu man Lan Daogong.

entries.zh: 季連在蜀，殺道恭父，道恭出亡，至是而報復焉。
entries.en: In Shu Lijian had killed Daogong's father; Daogong had fled and now took revenge.
entries.literal: In Shu Lijian had killed Daogong's father; Daogong fled and now took revenge.

entries.zh: 義師起，東昏假伯之節、督前驅諸軍事、豫州刺史，將軍如故。
entries.en: When the righteous army rose, Dong Hun lent Bozhi his staff, named him overseer of the vanguard, and inspector of Yuzhou; his rank stayed the same.
entries.literal: When the righteous army rose, Dong Hun lent Chen Bozhi his staff, made him overseer of the vanguard hosts, and inspector of Yuzhou; his generalship stood as before.

entries.zh: 尋轉江州，據尋陽以拒義軍。
entries.en: Soon he took Jiangzhou and held Xunyang against the righteous army.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Jiangzhou and held Xunyang to block the righteous army.

entries.zh: 郢城平，高祖得伯之幢主蘇隆之，使說伯之， 卽以爲安東將軍、江州刺史。
entries.en: When Ying fell, Gaozu took Bozhi's banner-master Su Longzhi to persuade him; Bozhi was named Pacifies-the-East general and Jiangzhou inspector.
entries.literal: When Ying city fell, Gaozu seized Bozhi's banner-master Su Longzhi and sent him to win Bozhi over; at once Bozhi was made Pacifies-the-East General and inspector of Jiangzhou.

entries.zh: 伯之雖受命，猶懷兩端，偽云「大軍未須便下」。
entries.en: Bozhi took the post but still hedged, claiming, "The great army need not march down yet."
entries.literal: Though Bozhi accepted the commission, he still wavered between two sides and pretended, saying, "The great army need not advance yet."

entries.zh: 高祖謂諸將曰：「伯之此答，其心未定，及其猶豫，宜逼之。」
entries.en: Gaozu told the generals, "That answer shows Bozhi's heart is not fixed; while he still wavers, press him."
entries.literal: Gaozu told the generals, "From this answer Bozhi's heart is unsettled; while he still hesitates, we should press him."

entries.zh: 衆軍遂次尋陽，伯之退保南湖，然後歸附。
entries.en: The armies halted at Xunyang; Bozhi withdrew to South Lake, then came over.
entries.literal: The hosts then halted at Xunyang; Bozhi fell back to guard South Lake, and only then submitted.

entries.zh: 進號鎮南將軍，與衆俱下。
entries.en: He was raised to Pacifies-the-South general and went down with the armies.
entries.literal: He was advanced to Pacifies-the-South General and marched down with the host.

entries.zh: 伯之頓籬門，尋進西明門。
entries.en: Bozhi camped at Fence Gate, then entered West Bright Gate.
entries.literal: Bozhi encamped at Fence Gate, then soon entered West Bright Gate.

entries.zh: 建康城未平，每降人出，伯之輒喚與耳語。
entries.en: While Jiankang still held out, each time a defector emerged Bozhi would pull him aside and whisper.
entries.literal: While Jiankang was not yet pacified, whenever a defector came out Bozhi would call him aside and speak into his ear.

entries.zh: 高祖恐其復懷翻覆，密語伯之曰：「聞城中甚忿卿舉江州降，欲遣刺客中卿，宜以爲慮。」
entries.en: Gaozu feared a fresh betrayal and told him privately, "I hear the city is enraged that you surrendered Jiangzhou; they will send assassins—take care."
entries.literal: Gaozu feared he might turn again and spoke to him in secret, saying, "I hear the city is furious that you raised Jiangzhou and surrendered; they mean to send assassins against you—you should take thought for that."

entries.zh: 伯之未之信。
entries.en: Bozhi did not believe him.
entries.literal: Bozhi did not believe it.

entries.zh: 會東昏將鄭伯倫降，高祖使過伯之，謂曰：「城中甚忿卿，欲遣信誘卿以封賞。
entries.en: When Dong Hun's general Zheng Bolun came over, Gaozu sent him to Bozhi, saying, "The city is furious with you and will try to lure you back with honors.
entries.literal: Then Dong Hun's general Zheng Bolun surrendered; Gaozu sent him past Bozhi with the words, "The city is very angry with you and means to lure you back with promises of rank and reward.

entries.zh: 須卿復降，當生割卿手腳；
entries.en: If you yield again they will cut off your hands and feet while you live;
entries.literal: If you surrender again they will flay you alive, limb by limb;

entries.zh: 卿若不降，復欲遣刺客殺卿。
entries.en: if you refuse, they will send assassins after you.
entries.literal: if you do not surrender, they will again send assassins to kill you.

entries.zh: 宜深爲備。」
entries.en: Guard yourself well."
entries.literal: You must guard yourself deeply."

entries.zh: 伯之懼，自是無異志矣。
entries.en: Bozhi was afraid, and from then on he held no second thought.
entries.literal: Bozhi was afraid; from then on he had no second thought.

entries.zh: 力戰有功。
entries.en: He fought fiercely and earned merit.
entries.literal: He fought hard and won merit.

entries.zh: 城平，進號征南將軍，封豊城縣公，邑二千戶，遣還之鎮。
entries.en: When the city fell he became Campaigns-the-South general, duke of Fengcheng with two thousand households, and returned to his post.
entries.literal: When the city fell he was advanced to Campaigns-the-South General, enfeoffed as Duke of Fengcheng with two thousand households, and sent back to his command.

entries.zh: 明年春，遣左右陳建孫送季連弟通直郎子淵及季連二子使蜀，喻旨慰勞。
entries.en: Next spring Gaozu sent close attendant Chen Jiansun to bring Lijian's younger brother Tongzhilang Ziyuan and Lijian's two sons into Shu with words of comfort.
entries.literal: The next spring Gaozu sent his close attendant Chen Jiansun to convey Lijian's younger brother Tongzhilang Ziyuan and Lijian's two sons into Shu with imperial words of comfort.

entries.zh: 季連受命，飭還裝。
entries.en: Lijian accepted the charge and prepared to return.
entries.literal: Lijian accepted the charge and prepared to return.

entries.zh: 高祖以西臺將鄧元起爲益州刺史。
entries.en: Gaozu made western headquarters general Deng Yuanqi Yizhou inspector.
entries.literal: Gaozu made western headquarters general Deng Yuanqi inspector of Yizhou.

entries.zh: 元起，南郡人。
entries.en: Yuanqi came from Nanjun commandery.
entries.literal: Yuanqi was a man of Nanjun commandery.

entries.zh: 季連爲南郡之時，素薄元起。
entries.en: When Lijian had held Nanjun he had always looked down on Yuanqi.
entries.literal: When Lijian had held Nanjun he had always looked down on Yuanqi.

entries.zh: 典簽朱道琛者，嘗爲季連府都錄，無賴小人，有罪，季連欲殺之，逃叛以免。
entries.en: Chief controller Zhu Daochen had once been head recorder in Lijian's office—a worthless rogue with crimes; Lijian meant to kill him but he fled and lived.
entries.literal: Chief controller Zhu Daochen had once been head recorder in Lijian's office—a worthless rogue with crimes; Lijian meant to kill him but he fled and lived.

entries.zh: 至是說元起曰：「益州亂離已久，公私府庫必多秏失，劉益州臨歸空竭，豈辦復能遠遣候遞。
entries.en: Now he told Yuanqi, "Yizhou has been torn apart for years; public and private treasuries must be drained. When Inspector Liu leaves he will empty everything—how could he still send escorts from afar?
entries.literal: Now he told Yuanqi: "Yizhou has been in disorder long; public and private treasuries must be drained. When Inspector Liu leaves he will empty everything—how could he still send escorts far away?

entries.zh: 道琛請先使檢校，緣路奉迎；
entries.en: Let me go first to inspect and along the road pay court and welcome you;
entries.literal: Let me first go to inspect, and along the road pay court and welcome you;

entries.zh: 不然，萬里資糧，未易可得。」
entries.en: otherwise supplies for ten thousand li will not come easy."
entries.literal: otherwise ten thousand li of supplies will not be easy to obtain."

entries.zh: 元起許之。
entries.en: Yuanqi agreed.
entries.literal: Yuanqi agreed.

entries.zh: 道琛旣至，言語不恭，又歷造府州人士，見器物輒奪之，有不獲者，語曰：「會當屬人，何須苦惜。」
entries.en: Once Daochen arrived his speech was rude; he went office to office among the district's men and seized whatever he saw, saying when refused, "Soon it will belong to someone else—why cling so hard?"
entries.literal: Once Daochen arrived his speech was disrespectful; he went from office to office among the district's men, and wherever he saw goods he seized them, saying when refused: "Soon it will belong to someone else—why cling so hard?"

entries.zh: 於是軍府大懼，謂元起至必誅季連，禍及黨與，競言之於季連。
entries.en: The military prefecture was terrified, saying when Yuanqi came he would punish Lijian and drag down everyone linked with him; they rushed to tell Lijian.
entries.literal: The military prefecture was terrified, saying when Yuanqi came he would surely punish Lijian and bring disaster on all linked with him; they rushed to tell Lijian.

entries.zh: 季連亦以爲然；
entries.en: Lijian believed it too;
entries.literal: Lijian believed it too;

entries.zh: 又惡昔之不禮元起也，益憤懣。
entries.en: and he hated his old rudeness to Yuanqi, which deepened his rage.
entries.literal: and he hated his old rudeness to Yuanqi, which deepened his rage.

entries.zh: 司馬朱士略說季連，求爲巴西郡，留三子爲質，季連許之。
entries.en: Marshal Zhu Shilve urged Lijian to ask for Baxi commandery and leave three sons as hostages; Lijian agreed.
entries.literal: Marshal Zhu Shilve urged Lijian to ask for Baxi commandery, leaving three sons as hostages; Lijian agreed.

entries.zh: 頃之，季連遂召佐史，矯稱齊宣德皇后令，聚兵復反，收朱道琛殺之。
entries.en: Before long Lijian summoned his clerks, forged an edict in the name of Qi's Virtuous-Pacifying empress dowager, gathered troops and rebelled again, seized Zhu Daochen and killed him.
entries.literal: Before long Lijian summoned his clerks, forged an edict in the name of Qi's Virtuous-Pacifying empress dowager, gathered troops and rebelled again, seized Zhu Daochen and killed him.

entries.zh: 書報朱士略，兼召李膺。
entries.en: He wrote Zhu Shilve and also summoned Li Ying.
entries.literal: He wrote to Zhu Shilve and also summoned Li Ying.

entries.zh: 膺、士略並不受使。
entries.en: Ying and Shilve both refused the summons.
entries.literal: Ying and Shilve both refused the summons.

entries.zh: 使歸，元起收兵于巴西以待之，季連誅士略三子。
entries.en: When the messengers returned, Yuanqi gathered troops in Baxi to wait; Lijian executed Shilve's three sons.
entries.literal: When the messengers returned, Yuanqi gathered troops in Baxi to wait; Lijian executed Shilve's three sons.

entries.zh: 初，元沖起兵，要尋陽張孝季，孝季從之。
entries.en: When Yuanchong first rose he called on Zhang Xiaoji of Xunyang; Xiaoji came.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Yuanchong raised troops he had asked Xunyang's Zhang Xiaoji to join; Xiaoji followed him.

entries.zh: 旣敗，伯之追孝季不得，得其母郎氏，蠟灌殺之。
entries.en: Defeated, he could not catch Xiaoji; he took Xiaoji's mother Lady Lang and killed her with molten wax.
entries.literal: After defeat Bozhi could not catch Xiaoji; he seized Xiaoji's mother, Lady Lang, and killed her by wax infusion.

entries.zh: 遣信還都報虎牙兄弟，虎牙等走盱眙，盱眙人徐安、莊興紹、張顯明邀擊之，不能禁，反見殺。
entries.en: He sent word to his sons at the capital; Huya and his brothers fled to Xuyi, where Xu An, Zhuang Xingshao, and Zhang Xianming ambushed them—failed to stop them and were killed instead.
entries.literal: He sent word back to the capital to his sons Huya and the rest; Huya and his brothers fled to Xuyi, where Xuyi men Xu An, Zhuang Xingshao, and Zhang Xianming waylaid them—could not hold them, and were themselves killed.

entries.zh: 高祖遣王茂討伯之。
entries.en: Gaozu sent Wang Mao to crush Bozhi.
entries.literal: Gaozu sent Wang Mao against Bozhi.

entries.zh: 伯之聞茂來，謂緭等曰：「王觀旣不就命，鄭伯倫又不肯從，便應空手受困。
entries.en: When he heard Mao was coming he told Wei, "Wang Guan would not come; Zheng Bolun would not follow—we are trapped with empty hands.
entries.literal: Hearing Mao was coming, Bozhi told Wei and the rest, "Wang Guan would not take the post; Zheng Bolun would not follow—so we should be trapped empty-handed.

entries.zh: 今先平豫章，開通南路，多發丁力，益運資糧，然後席捲北向，以撲饑疲之衆，不憂不濟也。」
entries.en: Take Yuzhang first, open the south road, levy labor and grain, then sweep north against starving troops—how could we fail?"
entries.literal: First pacify Yuzhang, open the southern road, levy many laborers, and haul more grain; then roll north in one sweep against starving, weary troops—how could we fail?"

entries.zh: 乃留鄉人唐蓋人守城，遂相率趣豫章。
entries.en: He left townsman Tang Gairen in the city and marched on Yuzhang.
entries.literal: He left his townsman Tang Gairen to hold the city and led his men toward Yuzhang.

entries.zh: 太守鄭伯倫堅守，伯之攻之不能下。
entries.en: Zheng Bolun held fast; Bozhi could not break the city.
entries.literal: Administrator Zheng Bolun held firm; Bozhi could not take it.

entries.zh: 王茂前軍旣至，伯之表裏受敵，乃敗走，間道亡命出江北，與子虎牙及褚緭俱入魏。
entries.en: Mao's vanguard came; caught between two fires, Bozhi fled by hidden paths north of the river and entered Wei with Huya and Chu Wei.
entries.literal: Wang Mao's vanguard arrived; caught front and rear, Bozhi was beaten and fled, stole out by bypaths north of the river, and with his son Huya and Chu Wei entered Wei together.

entries.zh: 魏以伯之爲使持節、散騎常侍、都督淮南諸軍事、平南將軍、光祿大夫、曲江縣侯。
entries.en: Wei gave him the staff, made him irregular attendant, overseer of Huainan armies, Pacifies-the-South general, grand master of splendid happiness, and marquis of Qujiang.
entries.literal: Wei made him bearer of the staff, irregular attendant, overseer of the Huainan armies, Pacifies-the-South General, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Marquis of Qujiang.

entries.zh: 梁書卷第二十 列傳第十四
entries.en: Book of Liang, Volume 20, Biographies 14
entries.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 20, Biographies 14

entries.zh: 長沙嗣王業 永陽嗣王伯游 衡陽嗣王元簡 桂陽嗣王象
entries.en: Ye, Heir Prince of Changsha; Boyou, Heir Prince of Yongyang; Yuanjian, Heir Prince of Hengyang; and Xiang, Heir Prince of Guiyang
entries.literal: Ye, Heir Prince of Changsha; Boyou, Heir Prince of Yongyang; Yuanjian, Heir Prince of Hengyang; Xiang, Heir Prince of Guiyang

entries.zh: 長沙嗣王業字靜曠，高祖長兄懿之子也。
entries.en: Ye, Heir Prince of Changsha, whose style was Jingkuang, was the son of Yi, elder brother of Emperor Wu.
entries.literal: Ye, Heir Prince of Changsha, styled Jingkuang, was the son of Yi, the High Ancestor's elder brother.

entries.zh: 懿字元達，少有令譽。
entries.en: Yi, styled Yuanda, enjoyed an excellent reputation from his youth.
entries.literal: Yi, styled Yuanda, in youth had fine repute.

entries.zh: 解褐齊安南邵陵王行參軍，襲爵臨湘縣侯。
entries.en: On entering office he served as a staff officer to the Prince of Shaoling of Qi, and inherited the title Marquis of Linxiang.
entries.literal: Upon leaving the cloth he became a staff officer to the Prince of Shaoling, acting as Annan, of Qi, and succeeded to the marquisate of Linxiang county.

entries.zh: 遷太子舍人、洗馬、建安王友。
entries.en: He was promoted to Crown Prince Attendant, Groom, and Companion to the Prince of Jian'an.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Crown Prince Attendant, Groom, and Companion to the Prince of Jian'an.

entries.zh: 出爲晉陵太守，曾未朞月，訟理人和，稱爲善政。
entries.en: Posted as governor of Jinling, within less than a month he had brought lawsuits to order and harmony among the people, and his rule was acclaimed as exemplary.
entries.literal: He went out as governor of Jinling; before a full month had passed, lawsuits were settled and the people were at peace, and it was called good government.

entries.zh: 入爲中書侍郎。
entries.en: He was recalled to the capital as Vice Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: He entered the capital as Vice Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 永明季，授持節、都督梁南北秦沙四州諸軍事、西戎校尉、梁、南秦二州刺史，加冠軍將軍。
entries.en: In the closing years of the Yongming era he received the staff of authority as Commander-in-Chief over Liang, North Qin, South Qin, and Sha, was appointed Western Rong Commandant and Governor of Liang and South Qin, and given the additional rank of General Who Establishes Might.
entries.literal: In the last years of Yongming he was given the staff of authority, made Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the four provinces Liang, North Qin, South Qin, and Sha, Western Rong Commandant, and Governor of Liang and South Qin, with the additional title General Who Establishes Might.

entries.zh: 是歲，魏人入漢中，遂圍南鄭。
entries.en: That year the Northern Wei invaded Hanzhong and laid siege to Nanzheng.
entries.literal: That year the Wei entered Hanzhong and then besieged Nanzheng.

entries.zh: 懿隨機拒擊，傷殺甚多，乃解圍遁去。
entries.en: Yi countered them as opportunities arose, inflicting heavy casualties, until the enemy lifted the siege and withdrew.
entries.literal: Yi met them as occasion demanded and repelled them, wounding and killing many; then they raised the siege and fled.

entries.zh: 懿又遣氐帥楊元秀攻魏歷城、皋蘭、駱谷、坑池等六戍，剋之。
entries.en: Yi also dispatched the Di chieftain Yang Yuanxiu against six Wei garrisons—Licheng, Gaolan, Luogu, Kengchi, and others—and took them all.
entries.literal: Yi also sent the Di chieftain Yang Yuanxiu to attack the six Wei garrisons of Licheng, Gaolan, Luogu, Kengchi, and others, and captured them.

entries.zh: 魏人震懼，邊境遂寧。
entries.en: The Wei were shaken with fear, and the frontier was thereafter secure.
entries.literal: The Wei were shaken with fear, and the borderlands were thereafter at peace.

entries.zh: 進號征虜將軍，增封三百戶，遷督益寧二州軍事、益州刺史。
entries.en: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, his fief was increased by three hundred households, and he was appointed to oversee military affairs in Yi and Ning and to serve as Governor of Yi.
entries.literal: His title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, his fief increased by three hundred households, and he was transferred to oversee military affairs of Yi and Ning and to be Governor of Yi.

entries.zh: 入爲太子右衛率、尚書吏部郎、衛尉卿。
entries.en: He was recalled as Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and Commandant of the Guard.
entries.literal: He entered the capital as Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and Commandant of the Guard.

entries.zh: 永元二年，裴叔業據豫州反，授持節、征虜將軍、督豫州諸軍事、豫州刺史，領歷陽南譙二郡太守，討叔業。
entries.en: In the second year of Yongyuan, Pei Shuye rebelled while holding Yuzhou. Yi received the staff of authority as General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, Commander-in-Chief of Yuzhou, and Governor of Yuzhou, and concurrently governed Liyang and Nanqiao, to suppress Shuye.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yongyuan, Pei Shuye held Yuzhou in rebellion; Yi was given the staff of authority, the title General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, command of all military affairs of Yuzhou, and the governorship of Yuzhou, and was made concurrent governor of Liyang and Nanqiao, to campaign against Shuye.

entries.zh: 叔業懼，降于魏。
entries.en: Shuye, in fear, surrendered to the Wei.
entries.literal: Shuye was afraid and surrendered to Wei.

entries.zh: 旣而平西將軍崔慧景入寇京邑，奉江夏王寶玄圍臺城。
entries.en: Soon afterward General Who Pacifies the West Cui Huijing invaded the capital, supporting Prince Bao Xuan of Jiangxia in a siege of the imperial city.
entries.literal: Thereafter the General Who Pacifies the West, Cui Huijing, invaded the capital region, supporting Prince Bao Xuan of Jiangxia in besieging the Terrace City.

entries.zh: 齊室大亂，詔徵懿。
entries.en: With the Qi court in turmoil, an edict summoned Yi to the capital.
entries.literal: The house of Qi was in great disorder, and an edict summoned Yi.

entries.zh: 懿時方食，投箸而起，率銳卒三千人援城。
entries.en: Yi was in the middle of a meal when the summons came; he threw down his chopsticks, rose at once, and led three thousand elite troops to relieve the capital.
entries.literal: Yi was then at his meal; he cast down his chopsticks, rose, and led three thousand crack troops to relieve the city.

entries.zh: 慧景遣其子覺來拒，懿奔擊，大破之，覺單騎走。
entries.en: Huijing sent his son Jue to block him; Yi charged headlong and routed the force completely, and Jue fled alone on horseback.
entries.literal: Huijing sent his son Jue to resist; Yi charged and struck, routing them utterly, and Jue fled alone on horseback.

entries.zh: 乘勝而進，慧景衆潰，追斬之。
entries.en: Pressing his advantage, Yi drove on until Huijing's army broke; Huijing was pursued and beheaded.
entries.literal: Pressing the victory forward, Huijing's host collapsed, and he was pursued and beheaded.

entries.zh: 授侍中、尚書右僕射，未拜。
entries.en: He was appointed Attendant-in-Chief and Vice Director of the Right of the Secretariat, but never took up the offices.
entries.literal: He was appointed Attendant-in-Chief and Vice Director of the Right of the Secretariat, but did not assume the posts.

entries.zh: 仍遷尚書令、都督征討水陸諸軍事，持節、將軍如故，增邑二千五百戶。
entries.en: He was then made Director of the Secretariat and Commander-in-Chief of all land and naval forces on campaign; his staff of authority and general's rank were unchanged, and his fief was increased by two thousand five hundred households.
entries.literal: He was then transferred to Director of the Secretariat and Commander-in-Chief of all land and water forces for punitive campaigns; his staff of authority and general's title remained as before, and his fief was increased by two thousand five hundred households.

entries.zh: 時東昏肆虐，茹法珍、王咺之等執政，宿臣舊將，並見誅夷，懿旣立元勳，獨居朝右，深爲法珍等所憚，乃說東昏曰：「懿將行隆昌故事，陛下命在晷刻。」
entries.en: At that time Emperor Donghun ruled with savage cruelty; Ru Fazhen, Wang Xuanzhi, and their faction held power, and veteran ministers and old generals were slaughtered one after another. Yi, who had won the founding merit, stood alone at the summit of the court and was deeply feared by Fazhen and his allies. They told Donghun, 'Yi is about to repeat what happened in the Longchang era—Your Majesty's life is measured in moments.'
entries.literal: At that time Emperor Donghun was wanton in cruelty; Ru Fazhen, Wang Xuanzhi, and others held power; veteran ministers and old generals were all put to death. Yi, having established the founding merit, stood alone at the right hand of the court and was deeply feared by Fazhen and the rest. They therefore said to Donghun, 'Yi is about to repeat the Longchang affair; Your Majesty's life hangs by a sun-dial's shadow.'

entries.zh: 東昏信之，將加酷害，而懿所親知之，密具舟江渚，勸令西奔。
entries.en: Donghun believed them and was about to have Yi killed. Those close to Yi learned of the plot, secretly prepared boats on the riverbank, and urged him to flee west.
entries.literal: Donghun believed them and was about to inflict cruel harm, but those close to Yi learned of it, secretly prepared boats on the riverbank, and urged him to flee west.

entries.zh: 懿曰：「古皆有死，豈有叛走尚書令耶？」
entries.en: Yi said, 'Since antiquity all men must die—has there ever been a Director of the Secretariat who fled in disgrace?'
entries.literal: Yi said, 'Since antiquity all men must die—how could there be a Director of the Secretariat who flees in rebellion?'

entries.zh: 遂遇禍。
entries.en: He met his death.
entries.literal: He then met with disaster.

entries.zh: 中興元年，追贈侍中、中書監、司徒。
entries.en: In the first year of Zhongxing he was posthumously appointed Attendant-in-Chief, Supervisor of the Secretariat, and Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhongxing he was posthumously given Attendant-in-Chief, Supervisor of the Secretariat, and Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 宣德太后臨朝，改贈太傅。
entries.en: When Empress Dowager Xuande assumed the regency, his posthumous rank was raised to Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: When Empress Dowager Xuande held court, his posthumous gift was changed to Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 天監元年，追崇丞相，封長沙郡王，諡曰宣武。
entries.en: In the first year of Tianjian he was posthumously honored as Chancellor, created Prince of Changsha, and given the posthumous title Xuanwu.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianjian he was posthumously honored as Chancellor and enfeoffed as Prince of Changsha commandery, with the posthumous title Xuanwu.

entries.zh: 給九旒、鸞輅、輼輬車，黃屋左纛，前後部羽葆鼓吹，輓歌二部，虎賁班劍百人，葬禮一依晉安平王故事。
entries.en: He was granted the full panoply of princely funeral honors—nine tassels, the imperial carriage, the funeral bier, the yellow canopy and left banner, front and rear escorts with feathered parasols and martial music, two sections of dirge singers, and a hundred Tiger Guards with ceremonial swords—and his burial followed entirely the precedent set for the Prince of Anping of Jin.
entries.literal: He was granted nine tassels, the imperial carriage, the funeral bier carriage, the yellow canopy and left banner, front and rear guard with feathered parasols and martial music, two sections of dirge singers, a hundred Tiger Guards with ceremonial swords, and his funeral rites followed entirely the precedent of the Prince of Anping of Jin.

entries.zh: 業幼而明敏，識度過人。
entries.en: From childhood Ye was bright and perceptive, his judgment surpassing that of others.
entries.literal: Ye from childhood was bright and keen, his discernment surpassing others.

entries.zh: 仕齊爲著作郎、太子舍人。
entries.en: Under the Qi he served as a Compiler and Crown Prince Attendant.
entries.literal: Serving Qi, he was a Compiler and Crown Prince Attendant.

entries.zh: 宣武之難，與二弟藻、象俱逃匿。
entries.en: When Prince Xuanwu met his death, he went into hiding together with his younger brothers Zao and Xiang.
entries.literal: At the disaster of Xuanwu, he fled into hiding together with his two younger brothers Zao and Xiang.

entries.zh: 高祖旣至，乃赴于軍，以爲寧朔將軍。
entries.en: Once Emperor Wu had arrived, he came to join the army and was appointed General Who Pacifies the North.
entries.literal: When the High Ancestor had arrived, he then came to the army and was made General Who Pacifies the North.

entries.zh: 中興二年，除輔國將軍、南琅邪清河二郡太守。
entries.en: In the second year of Zhongxing he was appointed General Who Assists the State and governor of South Langye and Qinghe.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhongxing he was appointed General Who Assists the State and governor of the two commanderies South Langye and Qinghe.

entries.zh: 天監二年，襲封長沙王，徵爲冠軍將軍，量置佐史，遷秘書監。
entries.en: In the second year of Tianjian he inherited the title Prince of Changsha, was summoned as General Who Establishes Might with an appropriate staff, and was appointed Supervisor of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianjian he succeeded to the princedom of Changsha, was summoned as General Who Establishes Might, was allotted staff officers as appropriate, and was transferred to Supervisor of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 四年，改授侍中。
entries.en: In the fourth year he was reassigned as Attendant-in-Chief.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was reassigned as Attendant-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 六年，轉散騎常侍、太子右衛率，遷左驍騎將軍，尋爲中護軍，領石頭戍軍事。
entries.en: In the sixth year he became Regular Attendant and Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, was promoted to General of the Left Rapid Cavalry, and soon after was made Central Guard General with command of the Shitou garrison.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Regular Attendant and Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, promoted to General of the Left Rapid Cavalry, and soon made Central Guard General in charge of the military affairs of the Shitou garrison.

entries.zh: 七年，出爲使持節、都督南兗兗徐青冀五州諸軍事、仁威將軍、南兗州刺史。
entries.en: In the seventh year he was posted with the emissary staff as Commander-in-Chief of South Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, General of Benevolent Might, and Governor of South Yan.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he went out with the emissary staff of authority as Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the five provinces South Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, General of Benevolent Might, and Governor of South Yan.

entries.zh: 八年，徵爲護軍。
entries.en: In the eighth year he was recalled as Protector of the Army.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he was summoned as Protector of the Army.

entries.zh: 九年，除中書令，改授安後將軍、鎮琅邪彭城二郡、領南琅邪太守。
entries.en: In the ninth year he was appointed Director of the Secretariat and reassigned as General Who Pacifies the Rear, charged with Langye and Pengcheng and concurrently governing South Langye.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Director of the Secretariat and reassigned as General Who Pacifies the Rear, with charge of the two commanderies Langye and Pengcheng and concurrent governorship of South Langye.

entries.zh: 十年，徵爲安右將軍、散騎常侍。
entries.en: In the tenth year he was recalled as General Who Pacifies the Right and Regular Attendant.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he was summoned as General Who Pacifies the Right and Regular Attendant.

entries.zh: 十四年，復爲護軍，領南琅邪彭城，鎮于琅邪。
entries.en: In the fourteenth year he again became Protector of the Army with charge of South Langye and Pengcheng, and took up his post at Langye.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year he again became Protector of the Army, with charge of South Langye and Pengcheng, stationed at Langye.

entries.zh: 復徵中書令，出爲輕車將軍、湘州刺史。
entries.en: He was again summoned as Director of the Secretariat, then posted as General of the Light Carriage and Governor of Xiangzhou.
entries.literal: He was again summoned as Director of the Secretariat, then went out as General of the Light Carriage and Governor of Xiangzhou.

entries.zh: 業性敦篤，所在留惠。
entries.en: Ye was by nature sincere and steadfast, and wherever he served he left a legacy of kindness.
entries.literal: Ye by nature was sincere and steadfast; wherever he served he left kindness behind.

entries.zh: 深信因果，篤誠佛法，高祖每嘉歎之。
entries.en: He was a devout believer in karmic retribution and sincerely devoted to the Buddhist teachings, which Emperor Wu often praised with admiration.
entries.literal: He deeply believed in cause and effect and was devoutly sincere toward the Buddhist Law; the High Ancestor often praised and sighed over this.

entries.zh: 普通三年，徵爲散騎常侍、護軍將軍。
entries.en: In the third year of Putong he was recalled as Regular Attendant and Protector General of the Army.
entries.literal: In the third year of Putong he was summoned as Regular Attendant and Protector General of the Army.

entries.zh: 四年，改爲侍中、金紫光祿大夫。
entries.en: In the fourth year he was reassigned as Attendant-in-Chief and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was changed to Attendant-in-Chief and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle.

entries.zh: 七年，薨，時年四十八。
entries.en: In the seventh year he died, at the age of forty-eight.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he died; he was forty-eight.

entries.zh: 諡曰元。
entries.en: He was given the posthumous title Yuan.
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Yuan.

entries.zh: 有文集行於世。
entries.en: His collected writings circulated in his lifetime.
entries.literal: He had a collection of writings in circulation in the world.

entries.zh: 子孝儼嗣。
entries.en: His son Xiaoyan succeeded him.
entries.literal: His son Xiaoyan succeeded.

entries.zh: 藻字靖藝，元王弟也。
entries.en: Zao, styled Jingyi, was the younger brother of Prince Yuan.
entries.literal: Zao, styled Jingyi, was the younger brother of Prince Yuan.

entries.zh: 少立名行，志操清潔。
entries.en: From youth he established a reputation for conduct, and his aspirations and integrity were pure.
entries.literal: From youth he established a reputation for conduct, and his aspirations and integrity were pure.

entries.zh: 齊永元初，釋褐著作佐郎。
entries.en: At the beginning of Qi's Yongyuan era, he entered office as Assistant Compiler.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qi's Yongyuan era, he entered office as Assistant Compiler.

entries.zh: 天監元年，封西昌縣侯，食邑五百戶。
entries.en: In Tianjian 1, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xichang county, with a fief of five hundred households.
entries.literal: In Tianjian 1, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xichang county, with a fief of five hundred households.

entries.zh: 出爲持節、都督益、寧二州諸軍事、冠軍將軍、益州刺史。
entries.en: He went out as Envoy Holding Credentials, commander of military affairs in Yi and Ning provinces, Champion General, and inspector of Yizhou.
entries.literal: He went out as Envoy Holding Credentials, commander of military affairs in Yi and Ning provinces, Champion General, and inspector of Yizhou.

entries.zh: 時天下草創，邊徼未安，州民焦僧護聚衆數萬，據郫、繁作亂。
entries.en: At the time the realm had only just been founded and the border regions were not yet settled. A provincial man, Jiao Senghu, gathered tens of thousands, occupied Pi and Fan, and rebelled.
entries.literal: At the time the realm had only just been founded and the border regions were not yet settled. A provincial man, Jiao Senghu, gathered tens of thousands, occupied Pi and Fan, and rebelled.

entries.zh: 藻年未弱冠，集僚佐議，欲自擊之。
entries.en: Zao was not yet twenty. He gathered his aides to deliberate and wanted to attack the rebels himself.
entries.literal: Zao was not yet twenty. He gathered his aides to deliberate and wanted to attack the rebels himself.

entries.zh: 或陳不可，藻大怒，斬于階側。
entries.en: Someone stated that this was impossible; Zao became furious and had him beheaded beside the steps.
entries.literal: Someone stated that this was impossible; Zao became furious and had him beheaded beside the steps.

entries.zh: 乃乘平肩輿，巡行賊壘。
entries.en: He then rode a level-shouldered litter and made a circuit of the rebel camps.
entries.literal: He then rode a level-shouldered litter and made a circuit of the rebel camps.

entries.zh: 賊弓亂射，矢下如雨，從者舉楯禦箭，又命除之，由是人心大安。
entries.en: The rebels loosed arrows wildly, and shafts fell like rain. His attendants raised shields against the arrows, but he ordered the shields removed, and the people's hearts were greatly calmed.
entries.literal: The rebels loosed arrows wildly, and shafts fell like rain. His attendants raised shields against the arrows, but he ordered the shields removed, and the people's hearts were greatly calmed.

entries.zh: 賊乃夜遁，藻命騎追之，斬首數千級，遂平之。
entries.en: The rebels then fled by night. Zao ordered cavalry to pursue them, took several thousand heads, and pacified them.
entries.literal: The rebels then fled by night. Zao ordered cavalry to pursue them, took several thousand heads, and pacified them.

entries.zh: 進號信威將軍，九年，徵爲太子中庶子。
entries.en: His title was advanced to General Who Inspires Trusting Awe, and in the ninth year he was summoned to be Household Attendant to the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: His title was advanced to General Who Inspires Trusting Awe, and in the ninth year he was summoned to be Household Attendant to the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 十年，爲左驍騎將軍、領南琅邪太守。
entries.en: In the tenth year, he became Left General of Agile Cavalry and acting administrator of South Langye.
entries.literal: In the tenth year, he became Left General of Agile Cavalry and acting administrator of South Langye.

entries.zh: 入爲侍中。
entries.en: He entered court as Attendant-in-Ordinary.
entries.literal: He entered court as Attendant-in-Ordinary.

entries.zh: 永陽嗣王伯游字士仁，高祖次兄敷之子。
entries.en: Boyou, Heir Prince of Yongyang, styled Shiren, was the son of Fu, Gaozu's second elder brother.
entries.literal: Boyou, Heir Prince of Yongyang, styled Shiren, was the son of Fu, Gaozu's second elder brother.

entries.zh: 敷字仲達，解褐齊後將軍、征虜行參軍，輔太子舍人，洗馬，遷丹陽尹丞。
entries.en: Fu, styled Zhongda, began office as acting staff officer to Qi's General of the Rear and General Who Subdues Captives, then served as assistant crown prince attendant and Groom, and was transferred to assistant Intendant of Danyang.
entries.literal: Fu, styled Zhongda, began office as acting staff officer to Qi's General of the Rear and General Who Subdues Captives, then served as assistant crown prince attendant and Groom, and was transferred to assistant Intendant of Danyang.

entries.zh: 入爲太子中舍人，除建威將軍、隨郡內史。
entries.en: He entered court as central household attendant to the crown prince and was appointed General Who Establishes Might and Interior Minister of Sui Commandery.
entries.literal: He entered court as central household attendant to the crown prince and was appointed General Who Establishes Might and Interior Minister of Sui Commandery.

entries.zh: 招懷遠近，黎庶安之，以爲前後之政莫之及也。
entries.en: He summoned and comforted people far and near, and the common people were at peace under him; they believed that no administration before or after matched his.
entries.literal: He summoned and comforted people far and near, and the common people were at peace under him; they believed that no administration before or after matched his.

entries.zh: 進號寧朔將軍，徵爲廬陵王諮議參軍。
entries.en: His title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the North, and he was summoned to be advisory army aide to the Prince of Luling.
entries.literal: His title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the North, and he was summoned to be advisory army aide to the Prince of Luling.

entries.zh: 建武四年，薨。
entries.en: In Jianwu 4, he died.
entries.literal: In Jianwu 4, he died.

entries.zh: 高祖即位，追贈侍中、司空，封永陽郡王，諡曰昭。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Fu was posthumously granted the offices of Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of Works, enfeoffed as Prince of Yongyang Commandery, and given the posthumous title Zhao.
entries.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, Fu was posthumously granted the offices of Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of Works, enfeoffed as Prince of Yongyang Commandery, and given the posthumous title Zhao.

entries.zh: 桂陽嗣王象字世翼，長沙宣武王第九子也。
entries.en: Xiang, Heir Prince of Guiyang, styled Shiyi, was the ninth son of Prince Xuanwu of Changsha.
entries.literal: Xiang, Heir Prince of Guiyang, styled Shiyi, was the ninth son of Prince Xuanwu of Changsha.

entries.zh: 初，叔父融仕齊至太子洗馬。
entries.en: Earlier, his uncle Rong served Qi and rose to Groom of the Crown Prince's Household.
entries.literal: Earlier, his uncle Rong served Qi and rose to Groom of the Crown Prince's Household.

entries.zh: 永元中，宣武之難，融遇害。
entries.en: During Yongyuan, in the disaster that befell Prince Xuanwu, Rong was killed.
entries.literal: During Yongyuan, in the disaster that befell Prince Xuanwu, Rong was killed.

entries.zh: 高祖平京邑，贈給事黃門侍郎。
entries.en: After Gaozu pacified the capital, Rong was posthumously granted the office of Yellow Gate Gentleman for Service.
entries.literal: After Gaozu pacified the capital, Rong was posthumously granted the office of Yellow Gate Gentleman for Service.

entries.zh: 天監元年，加散騎常侍、撫軍大將軍，封桂陽郡王。
entries.en: In Tianjian 1, he was additionally made Regular Attendant and Great General Who Pacifies the Army, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Guiyang Commandery.
entries.literal: In Tianjian 1, he was additionally made Regular Attendant and Great General Who Pacifies the Army, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Guiyang Commandery.

entries.zh: 諡曰簡。
entries.en: His posthumous title was Jian.
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Jian.

entries.zh: 無子，乃詔象爲嗣，襲封爵。
entries.en: He had no son, so an edict made Xiang his heir, and Xiang inherited the noble title.
entries.literal: He had no son, so an edict made Xiang his heir, and Xiang inherited the noble title.

entries.zh: 藻性謙退，不求聞達。
entries.en: Zao was by nature modest and retiring, seeking neither fame nor advancement.
entries.literal: Zao by nature was modest and retiring, not seeking fame or advancement.

entries.zh: 善屬文辭，尤好古體，自非公讌，未嘗妄有所爲，縱有小文，成輒棄本。
entries.en: He was skilled at literary composition and especially favored the ancient style. Except at formal gatherings he never wrote casually, and even when he produced a short piece he would discard the draft once it was done.
entries.literal: He was skilled at composing literary works and especially loved the ancient style; except at public banquets he never rashly produced anything, and even when he had a small piece, once finished he would discard the draft.

entries.zh: 十一年，出爲使持節、都督雍、梁、秦三州竟陵、隨二郡諸軍事、仁威將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史。
entries.en: In the eleventh year he was posted with the emissary staff as Commander-in-Chief of Yong, Liang, and Qin and of Jingling and Sui, General of Benevolent Might, Pacifier of the Barbarians Commandant, and Governor of Yong.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year he went out with the emissary staff of authority as Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the three provinces Yong, Liang, and Qin and the two commanderies Jingling and Sui, General of Benevolent Might, Pacifier of the Barbarians Commandant, and Governor of Yong.

entries.zh: 十二年，徵爲使持節、都督南兗兗徐青冀五州諸軍事、兗州刺史，軍號如故。
entries.en: In the twelfth year he was recalled with the emissary staff as Commander-in-Chief of South Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji and as Governor of Yan, his military rank unchanged.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year he was summoned with the emissary staff as Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the five provinces South Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji and as Governor of Yan; his military title remained as before.

entries.zh: 頻蒞數鎮，民吏稱之。
entries.en: He served repeatedly at several frontier posts, and both the people and officials praised his rule.
entries.literal: He repeatedly took up several garrison posts, and the people and officials praised him.

entries.zh: 推善下人，常如弗及。
entries.en: He deferred to others' virtues and humbled himself before all, always as though he fell short of them.
entries.literal: He advanced others' goodness and lowered himself before men, always as if he could not match them.

entries.zh: 徵爲太子詹事。
entries.en: He was recalled as Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: He was summoned as Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 普通三年，遷領軍將軍，加侍中。
entries.en: In the third year of Putong he was promoted to General of the Garrison Guards with the additional title Attendant-in-Chief.
entries.literal: In the third year of Putong he was transferred to General of the Garrison Guards and given the additional title Attendant-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 六年，爲軍師將軍，與西豊侯正德北伐渦陽，輒班師，爲有司所奏，免官削爵土。
entries.en: In the sixth year he served as General of the Army and joined the Marquis of Xifeng, Zhengde, on a northern campaign against Woyang, but abruptly withdrew his forces. The authorities impeached him, and he was stripped of office and fief.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he was made General of the Army and, with the Marquis of Xifeng, Zhengde, marched north against Woyang; he abruptly withdrew the army, was impeached by the responsible offices, and was stripped of office and fief.

entries.zh: 七年，起爲宗正卿。
entries.en: In the seventh year he was reappointed Director of the Imperial Clan.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he was raised up as Director of the Imperial Clan.

entries.zh: 八年，復封爵，尋除左衛將軍，領步兵校尉。
entries.en: In the eighth year his title was restored; soon after he was appointed General of the Left Guard and Commandant of Foot Soldiers.
entries.literal: In the eighth year his title was restored; soon he was appointed General of the Left Guard and made Commandant of Foot Soldiers.

entries.zh: 大通元年，遷侍中、中護軍。
entries.en: In the first year of Datong he was promoted to Attendant-in-Chief and Central Guard General.
entries.literal: In the first year of Datong he was transferred to Attendant-in-Chief and Central Guard General.

entries.zh: 時渦陽始降，乃以藻爲使持節、北討都督、征北大將軍，鎮于渦陽。
entries.en: Woyang had just surrendered, and Zao was appointed with the emissary staff as Northern Campaign Commander-in-Chief and General Who Conquers the North, with his headquarters at Woyang.
entries.literal: At that time Woyang had just surrendered, and Zao was made emissary with staff of authority, Northern Campaign Commander-in-Chief, and General Who Conquers the North, stationed at Woyang.

entries.zh: 二年，爲中權將軍、金紫光祿大夫，置佐史，加侍中。
entries.en: In the second year he was appointed General of Central Authority and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle with an appropriate staff, and given the additional title Attendant-in-Chief.
entries.literal: In the second year he was made General of Central Authority, Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle, with staff officers allotted, and given the additional title Attendant-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 中大通元年，遷護軍將軍，中權如故。
entries.en: In the first year of Zhongdatong he was promoted to Protector General of the Army while retaining his rank as General of Central Authority.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhongdatong he was transferred to Protector General of the Army; his title of Central Authority remained as before.

entries.zh: 三年，爲中軍將軍、太子詹事，出爲丹陽尹。
entries.en: In the third year he was appointed Central Army General and Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, then posted as Governor of Danyang.
entries.literal: In the third year he was made Central Army General and Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, then went out as Governor of Danyang.

entries.zh: 高祖每歎曰：「子弟並如迦葉，吾復何憂。」
entries.en: Emperor Wu often sighed and said, 'If all my sons and nephews were like Kaye, what would I have to worry about?'
entries.literal: The High Ancestor often sighed and said, 'If all my sons and younger kinsmen were like Kaye, what would I have to worry about?'

entries.zh: 迦葉，藻小名也。
entries.en: Kaye was Zao's childhood name.
entries.literal: Kaye was Zao's childhood name.

entries.zh: 入爲安左將軍、尚書左僕射，加侍中，藻固辭不就，詔不許。
entries.en: He was recalled as General Who Pacifies the Left and Vice Director of the Left of the Secretariat with the additional title Attendant-in-Chief. Zao firmly declined, but the edict would not allow it.
entries.literal: He entered the capital as General Who Pacifies the Left and Vice Director of the Left of the Secretariat, with the additional title Attendant-in-Chief; Zao firmly declined and would not accept, but the edict did not permit it.

entries.zh: 大同五年，遷中衛將軍、開府儀同三司、中書令，侍中如故。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Datong he was promoted to Central Guard General, Commander with honors equal to the Three Excellencies and his own staff, and Director of the Secretariat, while retaining his title as Attendant-in-Chief.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Datong he was transferred to Central Guard General, Commander with honor equal to the Three Excellencies and an office of his own, and Director of the Secretariat; his title as Attendant-in-Chief remained as before.

entries.zh: 伯游美風神，善言玄理。
entries.en: Boyou had an elegant bearing and was skilled in the discourse of metaphysics.
entries.literal: Boyou had fine bearing and spirit and was skilled at speaking of the dark principle.

entries.zh: 天監元年四月，詔曰：「兄子伯游，雖年識未弘，意尚粗可。
entries.en: In the fourth month of the first year of Tianjian an edict read, 'My elder brother's son Boyou, though still young in years and learning, shows promise of sound judgment.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Tianjian an edict said, 'My elder brother's son Boyou, though his years and knowledge are not yet broad, his intentions are still roughly acceptable.

entries.zh: 浙東奧區，宜須撫蒞，可督會稽東陽新安永嘉臨海五郡諸軍事、輔國將軍、會稽太守。」
entries.en: The vital region of eastern Zhe requires a steady hand; he is appointed Commander-in-Chief of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Yongjia, and Linhai, General Who Assists the State, and Governor of Kuaiji.'
entries.literal: The vital region of eastern Zhe must be soothed and overseen; he may be made Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the five commanderies Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Yongjia, and Linhai, General Who Assists the State, and Governor of Kuaiji.'

entries.zh: 二年，襲封永陽郡王。
entries.en: In the second year he inherited the title Prince of Yongyang.
entries.literal: In the second year he succeeded to the princedom of Yongyang commandery.

entries.zh: 五年，薨，時年二十三。
entries.en: In the fifth year he died, at the age of twenty-three.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he died; he was twenty-three.

entries.zh: 諡曰恭。
entries.en: He was given the posthumous title Gong.
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Gong.

entries.zh: 孝儼字希莊，聰慧有文才。
entries.en: Xiaoyan, styled Xizhuang, was clever and gifted in letters.
entries.literal: Xiaoyan, styled Xizhuang, was clever and had literary talent.

entries.zh: 射策甲科，除秘書郎、太子舍人。
entries.en: He placed in the top grade of the civil examination and was appointed Secretary and Crown Prince Attendant.
entries.literal: In the archery examination he placed in the top grade and was appointed Secretary and Crown Prince Attendant.

entries.zh: 從幸華林園，於座獻《相風烏》、《華光殿》、《景陽山》等頌，其文甚美，高祖深賞異之。
entries.en: On an imperial visit to Hualin Garden, he presented at the banquet his odes "The Wind-Measuring Bird," "Huaguang Hall," "Jingyang Mountain," and others. The writing was exquisite, and Emperor Wu admired it greatly.
entries.literal: Accompanying the emperor on a visit to Hualin Garden, he presented at the banquet his odes "The Wind-Measuring Bird," "Huaguang Hall," "Jingyang Mountain," and others; the writing was very fine, and the High Ancestor deeply admired and marveled at it.

entries.zh: 普通元年，薨，時年二十三。
entries.en: In the first year of Putong he died, at the age of twenty-three.
entries.literal: In the first year of Putong he died; he was twenty-three.

entries.zh: 諡曰章。
entries.en: He was given the posthumous title Zhang.
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Zhang.

entries.zh: 子慎嗣。
entries.en: His son Shen succeeded him.
entries.literal: His son Shen succeeded.

entries.zh: 藻性恬靜，獨處一室，床有膝痕，宗室衣冠，莫不楷則。
entries.en: Zao was tranquil by nature. He lived alone in a single room, and the marks of his knees were worn into his couch. Throughout the imperial clan and the gentry, all looked to him as a model.
entries.literal: Zao by nature was tranquil and still; he dwelt alone in a single room, and his couch bore the marks of his knees. Among the imperial clan and the gentry, none did not take him as a model.

entries.zh: 常以爵祿太過，每思摒退，門庭閑寂，賓客罕通，太宗尤敬愛之。
entries.en: He often felt his rank and stipend were too great and always thought of resigning. His household was quiet and still, and guests rarely called. Taizong especially revered and loved him.
entries.literal: He often felt his rank and stipend were excessive and always thought of withdrawing; his gates and courtyard were quiet and still, and guests rarely came. The Crown Prince especially revered and loved him.

entries.zh: 自遭家禍，恒布衣蒲席，不食鮮禽，非在公庭，不聽音樂。
entries.en: Since his family's tragedy he always wore plain cloth and sat on rush mats, ate no fresh meat or poultry, and listened to no music except on formal court occasions.
entries.literal: Since the family disaster he always wore plain cloth and sat on rush mats, ate no fresh poultry, and unless in the public court did not listen to music.

entries.zh: 高祖每以此稱之。
entries.en: Emperor Wu often praised him for this.
entries.literal: The High Ancestor often praised him for this.

entries.zh: 出爲使持節、督南徐州刺史。
entries.en: He was posted with the emissary staff as Governor of South Xuzhou.
entries.literal: He went out with the emissary staff of authority as overseer and Governor of South Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 侯景亂，藻遣長子彧率兵入援，及城開，加散騎常侍、大將軍。
entries.en: During Hou Jing's rebellion, Zao sent his eldest son Yu to lead troops to relieve the capital. When the city fell he was given the additional titles Regular Attendant and Great General.
entries.literal: In the disorder of Hou Jing, Zao sent his eldest son Yu to lead troops in relief; when the city was opened he was given the additional titles Regular Attendant and Great General.

entries.zh: 景遣其儀同蕭邕代之，據京口，藻因感氣疾，不自療。
entries.en: Hou Jing sent his officer Xiao Yong to replace him and seized Jingkou. Zao fell ill with a wasting disorder and refused to seek treatment.
entries.literal: Jing sent his Yitong Xiao Yong to replace him and seized Jingkou; Zao therefore fell ill with ch'i disorder and did not treat himself.

entries.zh: 或勸奔江北，藻曰：「吾國之台鉉，位任特隆，旣不能誅剪逆賊，正當同死朝廷，安能投身異類，欲保餘生。」
entries.en: Some urged him to flee north of the Yangzi. Zao said, 'I am a pillar of the state, my rank and responsibility exceptionally great. Having failed to destroy the rebels, I ought to die with the court. How could I cast my lot among alien peoples merely to preserve what life remains?'
entries.literal: Some urged him to flee north of the river; Zao said, 'I am a pillar of the state, my position and commission exceptionally lofty. Having failed to cut down the rebel bandits, I should rightly die together with the court—how could I cast myself among alien kinds to preserve what life remains?'

entries.zh: 因不食累日。
entries.en: He then refused food for many days.
entries.literal: He therefore did not eat for many days.

entries.zh: 太清三年，薨，時年六十七。
entries.en: In the third year of Taiqing he died, at the age of sixty-seven.
