entries.literal: In the third year of Taiqing he died; he was sixty-seven.

entries.zh: 衡陽嗣王元簡字熙遠，高祖第四弟暢之子。
entries.en: Yuanjian, Heir Prince of Hengyang, styled Xiyuan, was the son of Chang, Gaozu's fourth younger brother.
entries.literal: Yuanjian, Heir Prince of Hengyang, styled Xiyuan, was the son of Chang, Gaozu's fourth younger brother.

entries.zh: 暢仕齊至太常，封江陵縣侯，卒。
entries.en: Chang served Qi and rose to Chamberlain for Ceremonials; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiangling county and died.
entries.literal: Chang served Qi and rose to Chamberlain for Ceremonials; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiangling county and died.

entries.zh: 天監元年，追贈侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。
entries.en: In Tianjian 1, he was posthumously granted the offices of Attendant-in-Ordinary, Great General of Agile Cavalry, and Opening Office with Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies.
entries.literal: In Tianjian 1, he was posthumously granted the offices of Attendant-in-Ordinary, Great General of Agile Cavalry, and Opening Office with Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies.

entries.zh: 封衡陽郡王。
entries.en: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Hengyang Commandery.
entries.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Hengyang Commandery.

entries.zh: 諡曰宣。
entries.en: His posthumous title was Xuan.
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Xuan.

entries.zh: 象容止閒雅，善於交遊，事所生母以孝聞。
entries.en: Xiang had an easy, refined bearing and was skilled in society. In caring for his birth mother he was renowned for filial devotion.
entries.literal: Xiang's bearing and deportment were easy and refined; he was skilled at social intercourse, and in serving the mother who bore him he was famed for filial piety.

entries.zh: 起家寧遠將軍、丹陽尹。
entries.en: On entering office he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance and Governor of Danyang.
entries.literal: Upon first taking office he was made General Who Pacifies the Distance and Governor of Danyang.

entries.zh: 到官未幾，簡王妃薨，去職。
entries.en: He had not long taken up his post when the Princess of Jian died, and he resigned to observe mourning.
entries.literal: He had not long been in the post when the Princess of Jian died, and he left office.

entries.zh: 服闋，復授明威將軍、丹陽尹。
entries.en: When his mourning period ended he was reappointed General of Bright Might and Governor of Danyang.
entries.literal: When mourning was completed he was again given the title General of Bright Might and Governor of Danyang.

entries.zh: 象生長深宮，始親庶政，舉無失德，朝廷稱之。
entries.en: Xiang had grown up within the palace walls. When he first took up the duties of government, nothing he did fell short of propriety, and the court praised him.
entries.literal: Xiang had grown up in the deep palace; when he first took part in ordinary government affairs, in all he did there was no lapse in virtue, and the court praised him.

entries.zh: 出爲持節、督司霍郢三州諸軍事、征遠將軍、郢州刺史。
entries.en: He was posted with the staff of authority as overseer of Si, Huo, and E, General Who Campaigns Afar, and Governor of Ezhou.
entries.literal: He went out with the staff of authority as overseer of all military affairs of the three provinces Si, Huo, and E, General Who Campaigns Afar, and Governor of Ezhou.

entries.zh: 尋遷湘衡二州諸軍事、輕車將軍、湘州刺史。
entries.en: Soon after he was transferred to oversee military affairs in Xiang and Heng, as General of the Light Carriage and Governor of Xiangzhou.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to oversee military affairs of the two provinces Xiang and Heng, General of the Light Carriage, and Governor of Xiangzhou.

entries.zh: 湘州舊多虎暴，及象在任，爲之靜息，故老咸稱德政所感。
entries.en: Xiangzhou had long been troubled by man-eating tigers. Under Xiang's rule they ceased their depredations, and the elders all attributed it to the power of his virtuous rule.
entries.literal: Xiangzhou in former times had many violent tigers; when Xiang was in office they were stilled and quieted, and the elders all said it was moved by his virtuous government.

entries.zh: 除中書侍郎，俄以本官行石頭戍軍事，轉給事黃門侍郎、兼領軍，又以本官兼宗正卿。
entries.en: He was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, and soon afterward acted in his existing capacity over the military affairs of the Shitou garrison. He was then transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and concurrent General of the Garrison Guards, and concurrently served as Director of the Imperial Clan.
entries.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat; soon, in his present office, he acted in the military affairs of the Shitou garrison; he was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and concurrent General of the Garrison Guards, and again in his present office was made concurrent Director of the Imperial Clan.

entries.zh: 尋遷侍中、太子詹事，未拜，改授持節、督江州諸軍事、信武將軍、江州刺史。
entries.en: Soon after he was promoted to Attendant-in-Chief and Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, but before he could take up those offices he was reassigned with the staff of authority as overseer of Jiangzhou, General of Trustworthy Might, and Governor of Jiangzhou.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Attendant-in-Chief and Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince; he did not assume the posts and was reassigned with the staff of authority as overseer of all military affairs of Jiangzhou, General of Trustworthy Might, and Governor of Jiangzhou.

entries.zh: 以疾免。
entries.en: He resigned on account of illness.
entries.literal: Because of illness he was dismissed from office.

entries.zh: 尋除太常卿，加侍中，遷秘書監、領步兵校尉。
entries.en: Soon after he was appointed Director of the Imperial Sacrifices with the additional title Palace Attendant, and was then made Director of the Imperial Library and concurrently Commandant of Foot Soldiers.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Director of the Imperial Sacrifices, given the additional title Palace Attendant, and transferred to Director of the Imperial Library and concurrently Commandant of Foot Soldiers.

entries.zh: 大同二年，薨，諡曰敦。
entries.en: In the second year of Datong he died and was given the posthumous title Dun.
entries.literal: In the second year of Datong he died; his posthumous title was Dun.

entries.zh: 子慥嗣。
entries.en: His son Cao succeeded him.
entries.literal: His son Cao succeeded.

entries.zh: 梁書卷第二十三 列傳第十七
entries.en: Book of Liang, Volume 23, Biographies 17
entries.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 23, Biographies 17

entries.zh: 蕭景字子昭，高祖從父弟也。
entries.en: Xiao Jing, styled Zizhao, was Emperor Gaozu's cousin on his father's side.
entries.literal: Xiao Jing, courtesy name Zizhao, was a paternal cousin of Emperor Gaozu.

entries.zh: 父崇之字茂敬，卽左光祿大夫道賜之子。
entries.en: His father Chongzhi, styled Maojing, was the son of Daoci, who had held the post of Left Chamberlain for the Imperial Insignia.
entries.literal: His father Chongzhi, courtesy name Maojing, was the son of the Left Chamberlain for the Imperial Insignia Daoci.

entries.zh: 道賜三子：長子尚之，字茂先；
entries.en: Daoci had three sons: the eldest, Shangzhi, styled Maoxian;
entries.literal: Daoci had three sons: the eldest was Shangzhi, courtesy name Maoxian;

entries.zh: 次太祖文皇帝；
entries.en: the second was the Grand Progenitor, Emperor Wen;
entries.literal: the second was the founding Grandfather, the Literary Emperor;

entries.zh: 次崇之。
entries.en: and the third was Chongzhi.
entries.literal: the third was Chongzhi.

entries.zh: 初，左光祿居於鄉里，專行禮讓，爲衆所推。
entries.en: Earlier, while living in his home district, Daoci had devoted himself to ritual propriety and modest deference and was widely respected.
entries.literal: In the beginning, while serving as Left Chamberlain for the Imperial Insignia he lived in his home district, devoted himself to ritual and deference, and was esteemed by the multitude.

entries.zh: 仕歷宋太尉江夏王參軍，終于治書侍御史。
entries.en: He served in office as an aide to the Prince of Jiangxia under the Song Grand Commandant and died as Attending Secretary in the Bureau of Documents.
entries.literal: In office he served successively as aide to the Prince of Jiangxia under the Grand Commandant of Song, and ended as Attending Secretary in the Bureau of Documents.

entries.zh: 齊末，追贈散騎常侍、左光祿大夫。
entries.en: At the end of the Qi dynasty he was posthumously appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Chamberlain for the Imperial Insignia.
entries.literal: At the end of Qi he was posthumously awarded Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Chamberlain for the Imperial Insignia.

entries.zh: 尚之敦厚有德器，爲司徒建安王中兵參軍，一府稱爲長者；
entries.en: Shangzhi was steady and generous, possessed of real moral weight. As Central Army Aide on the staff of the Prince of Jian'an under the Minister of Works, the entire princely establishment called him "the elder";
entries.literal: Shangzhi was solid and generous with moral capacity; he served as Central Army Aide to the Prince of Jian'an under the Minister of Works, and the whole administration called him "the elder";

entries.zh: 琅邪王僧虔尤善之，每事多與議決。
entries.en: Wang Sengqian of Langye held him in particular esteem and frequently consulted him before reaching decisions.
entries.literal: Wang Sengqian of Langye especially favored him; on most affairs he deliberated and decided with him.

entries.zh: 遷步兵校尉，卒官。
entries.en: He was promoted to Commandant of Footsoldiers and died in that post.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Commandant of Footsoldiers and died in office.

entries.zh: 天監初，追諡文宣侯。
entries.en: Early in the Tianjian era he was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Literary Manifestation.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he was posthumously given the title Marquis of Literary Manifestation.

entries.zh: 尚之子靈鈞，仕齊廣德令。
entries.en: Shangzhi's son Lingjun served as magistrate of Guangde in the Qi period.
entries.literal: Shangzhi's son Lingjun served as magistrate of Guangde under Qi.

entries.zh: 高祖義師至，行會稽郡事，頃之卒。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu's righteous army marched east, he took charge of Kuaiji commandery affairs, but died soon afterward.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gaozu's army of righteous campaign arrived, he acted in the affairs of Kuaiji commandery; shortly thereafter he died.

entries.zh: 高祖卽位，追封東昌縣侯，邑一千戶。
entries.en: After Gaozu ascended the throne, Lingjun was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongchang with a fief of one thousand households.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongchang, with a fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 子謇嗣。
entries.en: His son Jian succeeded to the title.
entries.literal: His son Jian succeeded.

entries.zh: 崇之以幹能顯，爲政尚嚴厲，官至冠軍將軍、東陽太守。
entries.en: Chongzhi rose to prominence through ability and resolve; his administration was notably stern, and he eventually reached the posts of Champion General and Administrator of Dongyang.
entries.literal: Chongzhi became prominent for capability and energy; in government he valued severity, and rose to General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Dongyang.

entries.zh: 永明中，錢唐唐㝢之反，別衆破東陽，崇之遇害。
entries.en: During Yongming, Tang Yu of Qiantang rebelled; a rebel detachment overran Dongyang, and Chongzhi was killed in the fighting.
entries.literal: In the Yongming era, Tang Yu of Qiantang rebelled; a separate force defeated Dongyang, and Chongzhi was killed.

entries.zh: 天監初，追諡忠簡侯。
entries.en: Early in Tianjian he was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Loyal Simplicity.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he was posthumously titled Marquis of Loyal Simplicity.

entries.zh: 景八歲隨父在郡，居喪以毀聞。
entries.en: Jing was eight when he accompanied his father to his post; his mourning conduct became renowned for its wrenching austerity.
entries.literal: Jing was eight when he followed his father to the commandery; for his mourning he was famed for self-inflicted ruin.

entries.zh: 旣長好學，才辯能斷。
entries.en: As he grew up he took to learning, showed talent in debate, and had a gift for decisive judgment.
entries.literal: When grown he loved study, was talented in debate, and able to decide.

entries.zh: 齊建武中，除晉安王國左常侍，遷永寧令，政爲百城最。
entries.en: During Jianwu in Qi he was appointed Left Regular Attendant in the Jin'an princedom, then promoted to magistrate of Yongning, where his administration ranked first among all the counties.
entries.literal: In the Jianwu era of Qi he was appointed Left Regular Attendant of the Principality of Jin'an, then transferred to be magistrate of Yongning; his governance was the finest among a hundred cities.

entries.zh: 永嘉太守范述曾居郡，號稱廉平，雅服景爲政，乃牓郡門曰：「諸縣有疑滯者，可就永寧令決。」
entries.en: Fan Shuzeng, Administrator of Yongjia, had governed the commandery with a reputation for integrity and fairness. He admired Jing's administration and posted a notice at the commandery gate: "In any county where a case is doubtful or stalled, take it to the magistrate of Yongning for judgment."
entries.literal: Yongjia Administrator Fan Shuzeng had governed the commandery, famed for integrity and fairness, and held Jing's governance in high regard; he posted at the commandery gate: "Wherever a county has doubtful or stalled cases, they may be taken to the magistrate of Yongning for decision."

entries.zh: 頃之，以疾去官。
entries.en: Before long he resigned his post because of illness.
entries.literal: Before long he left office on account of illness.

entries.zh: 永嘉人胡仲宣等千人詣闕，表請景爲郡，不許。
entries.en: Hu Zhongxuan of Yongjia and a thousand others went to the capital and petitioned to have Jing appointed commandery administrator, but the request was denied.
entries.literal: Hu Zhongxuan of Yongjia and a thousand others went to the capital and submitted a memorial asking that Jing be made administrator of the commandery; it was not granted.

entries.zh: 還爲驃騎行參軍。
entries.en: He returned to the capital as Traveling Aide on the staff of the Rapid Cavalry General.
entries.literal: He returned to serve as Traveling Aide to the Rapid Cavalry General.

entries.zh: 永元二年，以長沙宣武王懿勳，除步兵校尉。
entries.en: In the second year of Yongyuan, in recognition of the merit of Prince Xuanwu of Changsha, Xiao Yi, he was appointed Commandant of Footsoldiers.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yongyuan, on account of the merit of Prince Xuanwu of Changsha, Yi, he was appointed Commandant of Footsoldiers.

entries.zh: 是冬，宣武王遇害，景亦逃難。
entries.en: That winter Prince Xuanwu was murdered, and Jing fled into hiding as well.
entries.literal: That winter Prince Xuanwu was killed, and Jing also fled into hiding.

entries.zh: 高祖義師至，以景爲寧朔將軍、行南兗州軍事。
entries.en: When Gaozu's righteous army arrived, Jing was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and put in charge of Southern Yanzhou affairs.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gaozu's righteous army arrived, Jing was made General Who Pacifies the North and Acting Commander of Southern Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 時天下未定，江北傖楚各據塢壁。
entries.en: The realm was still unsettled; north of the Yangzi, northern settlers and Chu clans each held their own fortified stockades.
entries.literal: At the time the realm was not yet settled; north of the Yangzi the northern migrants and Chu people each held fortified stockades.

entries.zh: 景示以威信，渠帥相率面縛請罪，旬日境內皆平。
entries.en: Jing won them over with authority and good faith; one chieftain after another came forward bound to beg pardon, and within ten days the entire region was pacified.
entries.literal: Jing displayed authority and trust; chieftains came in succession with bound faces to beg forgiveness, and within ten days the whole territory was pacified.

entries.zh: 中興二年，遷督南兗州諸軍事、輔國將軍、監南兗州。
entries.en: In the second year of Zhongxing he was promoted to Supervisor of Military Affairs for Southern Yanzhou, General Who Assists the State, and Inspector of Southern Yanzhou.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhongxing he was transferred to Supervisor of the Military Affairs of Southern Yanzhou, General Who Assists the State, and Inspector of Southern Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 高祖踐阼，封吳平縣侯，食邑一千戶，仍爲使持節、都督南北兗青冀四州諸軍事、冠軍將軍、南兗州刺史。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Jing was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuping with a fief of one thousand households and continued as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief over North and South Yan, Qing, and Ji, Champion General, and Governor of Southern Yanzhou.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuping county, with a fief of one thousand households, and continued as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of the Military Affairs of the four provinces of North and South Yan, Qing, and Ji, General Who Establishes Might, and Governor of Southern Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 詔景母毛氏爲國太夫人，禮如王國太妃，假金章紫綬。
entries.en: An edict made Jing's mother, Lady Mao, Grand Lady of the State, with ceremonial standing equal to a princely grand consort, and granted her the golden seal and purple sash.
entries.literal: An edict made Jing's mother Lady Mao Grand Lady of the State, with ceremony like a princely Grand Consort, and granted her the golden seal and purple sash.

entries.zh: 景居州，清恪有威裁，明解吏職，文案無壅，下不敢欺，吏人畏敬如神。
entries.en: As governor, Jing was pure, scrupulous, and commanding; he understood official duties thoroughly, kept paperwork moving without backlog, and left no room for deception below him. Officials and commoners alike revered him almost as a god.
entries.literal: Jing governed the province with purity, scrupulousness, authority, and judgment; he understood clearly the duties of officials; documents were never blocked; subordinates did not dare deceive; officials and people revered him as a spirit.

entries.zh: 會年荒，計口賑卹，爲饘粥於路以賦之，死者給棺具，人甚賴焉。
entries.en: When famine struck, he counted households to distribute relief, set up gruel kitchens along the roads, and supplied coffins for the dead. The people depended on him heavily.
entries.literal: It happened to be a year of famine; he counted mouths to give relief, set out gruel on the roads to distribute, provided coffins for the dead, and people relied on him greatly.

entries.zh: 景爲人雅有風力，長於辭令。
entries.en: Jing carried himself with elegant force of character and was gifted in formal speech.
entries.literal: Jing as a man had elegant bearing and strength of character, and excelled in rhetoric.

entries.zh: 其在朝廷，爲衆所瞻仰。
entries.en: At court everyone looked up to him.
entries.literal: In court he was looked up to by the multitude.

entries.zh: 於高祖屬雖爲從弟，而禮寄甚隆，軍國大事，皆與議決。
entries.en: Although he was only Gaozu's cousin, the emperor treated him with exceptional honor and consulted him on every major military and state affair.
entries.literal: Although in relation to Emperor Gaozu he was a cousin, the ceremonial regard placed on him was very lofty; on great affairs of army and state he was always consulted for deliberation and decision.

entries.zh: 十五年，加侍中。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year he was given the additional post of Attendant-in-Chief.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year he was given the additional post of Attendant-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 十七年，太尉、揚州刺史臨川王宏坐法免。
entries.en: In the seventeenth year Prince Hong of Linchuan, Grand Commandant and Governor of Yangzhou, was dismissed for an offense.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year the Grand Commandant and Governor of Yangzhou, Prince of Linchuan Hong, was removed from office for an offense.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「揚州應須緝理，宜得其人。
entries.en: An edict said, "Yangzhou must be brought to order, and the right man is needed for the task.
entries.literal: An edict said: "Yangzhou needs to be put in order and should have the right man.

entries.zh: 侍中、領軍將軍吳平侯景才任此舉，可以安右將軍監揚州，並置佐史，侍中如故，卽宅爲府。」
entries.en: Attendant-in-Chief and General of the Palace Guard, Marquis of Wuping Jing, has the talent for it. Let him serve as General of the Right for Pacification overseeing Yangzhou, with a full staff appointed, retain his post as Attendant-in-Chief, and make his residence the administrative seat."
entries.literal: Attendant-in-Chief and General of the Palace Guard, Marquis of Wuping Jing, has the talent to undertake this; he may be made General of the Right for Pacification to oversee Yangzhou, with staff officers appointed, Attendant-in-Chief as before, and his residence made the administrative seat."

entries.zh: 景越親居揚州，辭讓甚懇惻，至于涕泣，高祖不許。
entries.en: Though only a cousin, Jing was now to govern Yangzhou. He declined with deep earnestness, even to tears, but Gaozu would not hear of it.
entries.literal: Jing, though a more distant kinsman, was to govern Yangzhou; his refusal was very earnest, even to tears, but Emperor Gaozu would not allow it.

entries.zh: 在州尤稱明斷，符教嚴整。
entries.en: As governor he was especially famed for clarity and decisiveness; his orders and directives were strict and orderly.
entries.literal: In the province he was especially famed for clarity and decisiveness; his orders and instructions were strict and orderly.

entries.zh: 有田舍老姥嘗訴得符，還至縣，縣吏未卽發，姥語曰：「蕭監州符，火爄汝手，何敢留之！」
entries.en: An old peasant woman once won a writ in a lawsuit; when she returned to the county seat the clerks did not issue it at once. She said, "Supervisor Xiao's writ will burn your hands off—how dare you hold it back!"
entries.literal: An old peasant woman once obtained a writ after suing; returning to the county, the county clerks did not at once issue it; the old woman said: "Supervisor Xiao's writ will burn your hands—how dare you keep it!"

entries.zh: 其爲人所畏敬如此。
entries.en: Such was the awe in which he was held.
entries.literal: Such was the fear and respect in which he was held.

entries.zh: 昱字子真，景第四弟也。
entries.en: Yu, styled Zizhen, was Jing's fourth younger brother.
entries.literal: Yu, courtesy name Zizhen, was Jing's fourth younger brother.

entries.zh: 天監初，除秘書郎，累遷太子舍人，洗馬，中書舍人，中書侍郎。
entries.en: Early in Tianjian he was appointed Secretary and rose in succession to Attendant of the Crown Prince, Groom, Palace Secretary, and Vice Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he was appointed Secretary; he was promoted in succession to Attendant of the Crown Prince, Groom, Palace Secretary, and Vice Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 每求自試，高祖以爲淮南、永嘉、襄陽郡，並不就。
entries.en: He repeatedly asked for a chance to prove himself in office, but when Gaozu offered him Huainan, Yongjia, and Xiangyang commanderies, he declined them all.
entries.literal: He repeatedly asked to prove himself; Emperor Gaozu offered him the commanderies of Huainan, Yongjia, and Xiangyang, but he accepted none.

entries.zh: 志願邊州，高祖以其輕脫無威望，抑而不許。
entries.en: He asked to serve on the frontier, but Gaozu, judging him frivolous and lacking authority, refused.
entries.literal: He wished for a frontier province; Emperor Gaozu, because he was frivolous and without prestige, suppressed and did not grant it.

entries.zh: 遷給事黃門侍郎。
entries.en: He was promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate for Affairs.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate for Affairs.

entries.zh: 上表曰：「夏初陳啓，未垂采照，追懷慚懼，實戰胸心。
entries.en: He submitted a memorial that read, "Early this summer I laid out my petition, yet Your Majesty has not yet looked upon it with favor. Thinking back on this fills me with shame and fear, and my heart trembles within my breast.
entries.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "At the beginning of summer I presented my petition, yet no favoring glance has fallen upon it; recalling this I feel shame and fear, and my heart truly trembles within my breast.

entries.zh: 臣聞暑雨祁寒，小人猶怨；
entries.en: I have heard that in summer rain and bitter winter cold even common people still complain;
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that in summer rain and severe winter cold, even petty men still complain;

entries.zh: 榮枯寵辱，誰能忘懷！
entries.en: how much more when glory turns to decline, or favor to disgrace—who can put such things out of mind!
entries.literal: glory and decline, favor and disgrace—who can forget them from the heart!

entries.zh: 臣藉以往因，得預枝戚之重；
entries.en: Through blessings from former lives I was allowed a place among the imperial kin;
entries.literal: Your servant, relying on causes from the past, was able to share in the weight of the branch kin;

entries.zh: 緣報旣雜，時逢坎鹆稟之運。
entries.en: yet my karmic entanglements were already complex, and the age itself was one of hardship and reversal.
entries.literal: because karmic retribution was already mixed, the times encountered a fate of hardship and setback.

entries.zh: 昔在齊季，義師之始，臣乃幼弱，粗有識慮，東西阻絕，歸赴無由，雖未能負戈擐甲，實銜淚憤懣。
entries.en: In the last years of Qi, when the righteous army first rose, I was still young, with only the beginnings of understanding. East and west were cut off, and I had no way to join the cause. Though I could not take up arms myself, I bore tears and burning indignation in my heart.
entries.literal: Formerly in the closing years of Qi, at the beginning of the righteous army, your servant was still young and weak, with only rough understanding; east and west were cut off, and there was no way to return and join; though unable to bear spear and don armor, I truly held tears and smoldering indignation.

entries.zh: 潛伏東境，備履艱危，首尾三年，亟移數處，雖復饑寒切身，亦不以凍餒爲苦。
entries.en: I hid in the eastern borderlands and endured every hardship and danger. For three years I moved from place to place in haste. Though hunger and cold pressed upon me, I did not count freezing or starvation as suffering.
entries.literal: Hiding in the eastern borderlands, I fully experienced hardship and peril; from beginning to end for three years I moved hurriedly to several places; though hunger and cold pressed on my person, I did not take freezing and starvation as suffering.

entries.zh: 每涉驚疑，惶怖失魄，旣乖致命之節，空有項領之憂，希望開泰，冀蒙共樂；
entries.en: Whenever danger struck I was terrified out of my wits. Having failed the duty of giving my life for the cause, I was left with nothing but the shame of an idle neck. I hoped for a new age of peace and longed to share in its joy.
entries.literal: Whenever I encountered alarm and doubt I was terrified and lost my spirit; having failed the integrity of giving my life, I had only the worry of a neck left idle; I hoped for opening prosperity and wished to share joy together;

entries.zh: 豈期二十餘年，功名無紀，畢此身骸，方填溝壑，丹誠素願，溘至長罷，俯自哀憐，能不傷歎！
entries.en: Who could have foreseen that for more than twenty years I would win no record of merit, and that only when this body is spent will it fill some ditch? My earnest heart and lifelong hopes have suddenly reached their end. Looking down on myself in pity, how could I not grieve and sigh!
entries.literal: Who could have expected that for more than twenty years achievement and fame were unrecorded, and that only when this body is finished will it fill a ditch and gully; red sincerity and plain wishes suddenly reach long cessation—bowing to pity myself, how could I not grieve and sigh!

entries.zh: 夫自媒自衒，誠哉可鄙；
entries.en: Self-promotion and self-display are truly contemptible;
entries.literal: As for self-recommendation and self-display, truly they are contemptible;

entries.zh: 自譽自伐，實在可羞。
entries.en: self-praise and boasting are truly shameful.
entries.literal: self-praise and self-boasting are truly shameful.

entries.zh: 然量己揆分，自知者審，陳力就列，寧敢空言？
entries.en: Yet having measured myself and appraised my place, I know myself clearly enough: to offer my strength and take up a post—how could that be mere empty talk?
entries.literal: Yet measuring myself and appraising my portion, one who knows himself is careful; to display strength and take a place—how would I dare empty words?

entries.zh: 是以常願一試，屢成干請。
entries.en: That is why I have repeatedly asked for a chance to prove myself.
entries.literal: For this reason I have constantly wished for one trial, and repeatedly made importunate requests.

entries.zh: 夫上應玄象，實不易叨；
entries.en: To match Heaven's hidden signs is no easy presumption;
entries.literal: As for matching the dark signs above, it is truly not easy to presume upon;

entries.zh: 錦不輕裁，誠難其制。
entries.en: brocade is not cut lightly, and its making is truly difficult.
entries.literal: brocade is not lightly cut—truly hard to fashion.

entries.zh: 過去業鄣，所以致乖算測。
entries.en: It is past karmic obstacles that have caused me to fall short of what was expected.
entries.literal: Past karmic obstacles are the reason for causing departure from calculated expectation.

entries.zh: 聖監旣謂臣愚短，不可試用，豈容久居顯禁，徒穢黃樞。
entries.en: Since Your Majesty has judged me foolish and inadequate, unfit for trial in office, I cannot remain long in this exalted inner post, merely defiling the imperial pivot.
entries.literal: Since the sage perception already holds your servant foolish and deficient and unfit for trial employment, I cannot long remain in the conspicuous forbidden precinct, vainly defiling the Yellow Pivot.

entries.zh: 忝竊稍積，恐招物議，請解今職，乞摒退私門。
entries.en: My unworthy tenure has gone on too long, and I fear public criticism. I beg to be relieved of my present office and sent back to private life.
entries.literal: My unworthy usurpation has accumulated somewhat; I fear attracting public criticism; I beg to be released from my present office and ask to be cast back to a private gate.

entries.zh: 伏願天照，特垂允許。
entries.en: I prostrate myself and beg Your Majesty's gracious consent.
entries.literal: Prostrate, I wish Heaven's illumination to grant permission especially.

entries.zh: 臣雖叨榮兩宮，報效無地，方違省闥，伏深戀悚。」
entries.en: Though I have enjoyed unearned honor in both palaces, I have had no way to repay it. As I leave the inner court, I prostrate myself in deep attachment and dread."
entries.literal: Your servant, though enjoying unearned glory in both palaces, has no place to repay effectiveness; just now departing the inner gates, I prostrate deep attachment and dread."

entries.zh: 高祖手詔答曰：「昱表如此。
entries.en: Gaozu replied in his own hand: "Yu's memorial reads as follows.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu replied in his own hand: "Yu's memorial is as follows.

entries.zh: 古者用人，必前明試，皆須績用旣立，乃可自退之高。
entries.en: In antiquity, when appointing men to office, rulers always tested them first. Only after they had established a record of achievement could they withdraw to a lofty retirement.
entries.literal: In antiquity when employing men, one must first clearly test them; all must have established achievement in office before they may retire to loftiness on their own.

entries.zh: 昔漢光武兄子章、興二人，並有名宗室，就欲習吏事，不過章爲平陰令，興爲緱氏宰，政事有能，方遷郡守，非直政績見稱，卽是光武猶子。
entries.en: In the past, Emperor Guangwu of Han's nephews Zhang and Xing were both eminent members of the imperial clan. When they wished to learn administration, Zhang was made only magistrate of Pingyin and Xing magistrate of Gou. Only when their governance showed ability were they promoted to commandery administrators. It was not merely that their achievements were praised—they were the emperor's own nephews.
entries.literal: Formerly the Han Emperor Guangwu's brother's sons Zhang and Xing, both famed in the imperial clan, wished to learn administrative affairs; Zhang became no more than magistrate of Pingyin, Xing magistrate of Gou—only when their government affairs showed ability were they promoted to commandery administrators; it was not merely that their administrative achievements were praised, but they were Guangwu's nephews.

entries.zh: 昱之才地，豈得比類焉！
entries.en: How can Yu's talent and standing be compared with theirs!
entries.literal: How can Yu's talent and standing be compared in kind!

entries.zh: 往歲處以淮南郡，旣不肯行；
entries.en: Last year he was offered Huainan commandery, yet refused to go;
entries.literal: In past years he was placed in Huainan commandery, yet refused to go;

entries.zh: 續用爲招遠將軍、鎮北長史、襄陽太守，又以邊外致辭；
entries.en: then he was appointed General Who Summons the Distant, Chief Clerk for Pacifying the North, and Administrator of Xiangyang, and again declined on the grounds that the post was on the frontier;
entries.literal: he was next used as General Who Summons the Distant, Chief Clerk for Pacifying the North, and Administrator of Xiangyang, and again declined on the grounds of the frontier;

entries.zh: 改除招遠將軍、永嘉太守，復云內地非願；
entries.en: he was then reassigned as General Who Summons the Distant and Administrator of Yongjia, and again said the interior was not what he wanted;
entries.literal: he was changed and appointed General Who Summons the Distant and Administrator of Yongjia, and again said the interior was not his wish;

entries.zh: 復問晉安、臨川，隨意所擇，亦復不行。
entries.en: he was then offered Jin'an and Linchuan to choose as he pleased, and again he would not go.
entries.literal: he was again asked about Jin'an and Linchuan, to choose as he wished, yet again would not go.

entries.zh: 解巾臨郡，事不爲薄，數有致辭，意欲何在？
entries.en: To take up office and govern a commandery is no slight honor. He has declined again and again—what does he want?
entries.literal: To unbind the scarf and oversee a commandery is no slight matter; repeatedly he has declined—what is the intent?

entries.zh: 且昱諸兄遞居連率，相繼推轂，未嘗缺歲。
entries.en: Moreover Yu's elder brothers have held regional commands in succession, one after another, without a year's gap.
entries.literal: Moreover Yu's elder brothers in succession have held regional command, one after another pushing the chariot wheel, never missing a year.

entries.zh: 其同產兄景，今正居籓鎮。
entries.en: His full brother Jing now holds a frontier fief and command.
entries.literal: His full brother Jing now holds a frontier fief and command.

entries.zh: 朕豈厚於景而薄於昱，正是朝序物議，次第若斯，於其一門，差自無愧。
entries.en: Do I favor Jing and slight Yu? It is simply that court order and public opinion proceed in due sequence. For one family, the arrangement is not unreasonable.
entries.literal: How would I favor Jing and slight Yu? It is precisely that court order and public opinion proceed in such sequence; for one family, it is rather without shame.

entries.zh: 無論今日不得如此；
entries.en: To say nothing of the present, when such a thing cannot be allowed;
entries.literal: Not to speak of today when it cannot be so;

entries.zh: 昱兄弟昔在布衣，以處成長，於何取立，豈得任情反道，背天違地。
entries.en: the Yu brothers were raised from common life by circumstance. On what basis do they stand? They cannot follow whim against the Way or defy Heaven and earth.
entries.literal: the Yu brothers formerly in plain cloth were raised by circumstance; on what basis do they stand? They cannot follow whim against the Way, turn their backs on Heaven, or violate Earth.

entries.zh: 孰謂朝廷無有憲章，特是未欲致之于理。
entries.en: Who says the court has no laws? I have simply not wished to bring him to judgment.
entries.literal: Who says the court has no statutes and regulations? It is only that I have not wished to bring him to judgment.

entries.zh: 旣表解職，可聽如啓。」
entries.en: Since he has asked to resign, his request may be granted as stated."
entries.literal: Since he has memorialized to resign from office, his request may be granted as stated."

entries.zh: 坐免官。
entries.en: He was dismissed from office.
entries.literal: He was removed from office for the offense.

entries.zh: 因此杜門絕朝覲，國家慶弔不復通。
entries.en: Thereafter he shut his gate and ceased attending court; he no longer took part in state celebrations or mourning.
entries.literal: Because of this he shut his gate and cut off court audiences; he no longer communicated in state celebrations or mourning.

entries.zh: 十八年，累表陳解，高祖未之許。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year he repeatedly petitioned to resign, but Gaozu would not allow it.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year he repeatedly memorialized to resign; Emperor Gaozu did not grant it.

entries.zh: 明年，出爲使持節、散騎常侍、都督郢司霍三州諸軍事、安西將軍、郢州刺史。
entries.en: The following year he was posted out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander-in-Chief over Ying, Si, and Huo, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Ying.
entries.literal: The next year he went out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander-in-Chief of the Military Affairs of the three provinces of Ying, Si, and Huo, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Ying.

entries.zh: 將發，高祖幸建興苑餞別，爲之流涕。
entries.en: Before he departed, Gaozu came to the Jianxing Park to give him a farewell banquet and wept for him.
entries.literal: As he was about to depart, Emperor Gaozu visited the Jianxing Park to give a farewell banquet and wept for him.

entries.zh: 旣還宮，詔給鼓吹一部。
entries.en: After returning to the palace, an edict granted him a full set of martial music.
entries.literal: After returning to the palace, an edict granted him one set of martial music.

entries.zh: 在州復有能名。
entries.en: In Ying he again earned a reputation for capable administration.
entries.literal: In the province he again had a reputation for ability.

entries.zh: 齊安、竟陵郡接魏界，多盜賊，景移書告示，魏卽焚塢戍保境，不復侵略。
entries.en: Qi'an and Jingling bordered Wei territory and were plagued by bandits. Jing sent formal notices across the border, and Wei promptly burned its stockades, held the frontier, and ceased its raids.
entries.literal: Qi'an and Jingling commanderies bordered Wei territory and had many bandits; Jing sent letters of notice, and Wei at once burned the stockades and guarded the border, no longer invading.

entries.zh: 普通四年，卒于州，時年四十七。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Putong he died in office, at the age of forty-seven.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Putong he died in the province, aged forty-seven.

entries.zh: 詔贈侍中、中撫軍、開府儀同三司。
entries.en: An edict posthumously appointed him Attendant-in-Chief, General of the Central Pacification Army, and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Sash with ceremonial privileges equal to the Three Excellencies.
entries.literal: An edict posthumously awarded him Attendant-in-Chief, General of the Central Pacification Army, and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Sash with the same ceremonial privileges as the Three Excellencies.

entries.zh: 諡曰忠。
entries.en: His posthumous title was Loyal.
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Loyal.

entries.zh: 子勱嗣。
entries.en: His son Mai succeeded to the title.
entries.literal: His son Mai succeeded.

entries.zh: 普通五年，坐於宅內鑄錢，爲有司所奏，下廷尉，得免死，徙臨海郡。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Putong he was impeached for casting coin in his home, sent to the Court of Justice, spared death, and banished to Linhai commandery.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Putong, for casting coin within his residence he was impeached by the responsible offices, sent down to the Court of Justice, escaped death, and was banished to Linhai commandery.

entries.zh: 行至上虞，有敕追還，且令受菩薩戒。
entries.en: When he reached Shangyu, an edict recalled him and ordered him to receive the bodhisattva precepts.
entries.literal: Traveling to Shangyu, an edict recalled him and ordered him to receive the bodhisattva precepts.

entries.zh: 昱旣至，恂恂盡禮，改意蹈道，持戒又精潔，高祖甚嘉之，以爲招遠將軍、晉陵太守。
entries.en: When Yu arrived, he was respectful in all ritual observance, turned his heart to the Way, and kept the precepts with pure devotion. Gaozu greatly praised him and appointed him General Who Summons the Distant and Administrator of Jinling.
entries.literal: When Yu arrived, he was respectful and fulfilled all ritual; he changed his intent and followed the Way; his observance of precepts was also pure and scrupulous; Emperor Gaozu greatly praised him and made him General Who Summons the Distant and Administrator of Jinling.

entries.zh: 下車勵名迹，除煩苛，明法憲，嚴於姦吏，優養百姓，旬日之間，郡中大化。
entries.en: Upon taking office he set an example of integrity, removed oppressive regulations, clarified the laws, was stern with corrupt officials, and cared generously for the people. Within ten days the commandery was thoroughly transformed.
entries.literal: Upon taking office he encouraged reputation and conduct, removed troublesome severity, clarified laws and statutes, was stern toward corrupt officials, and generously nurtured the people; within ten days the commandery was greatly transformed.

entries.zh: 俄而暴疾卒，百姓行坐號哭，市里爲之喧沸，設祭奠於郡庭者四百餘人。
entries.en: Soon he died suddenly of illness. The people wept wherever they walked or sat; the marketplaces rang with lamentation, and more than four hundred people set up offerings in the commandery court.
entries.literal: Soon he died suddenly of illness; the people wept and wailed whether walking or sitting; the marketplaces were clamorous for it; more than four hundred set up offerings in the commandery court.

entries.zh: 田舍有女人夏氏，年百餘歲，扶曾孫出郡，悲泣不自勝。
entries.en: In the countryside a woman of the Xia clan, more than a hundred years old, supported her great-grandson to the commandery seat and wept until she could weep no more.
entries.literal: In the countryside there was a woman of the Xia clan, more than a hundred years old, who supported her great-grandson to come out to the commandery seat, weeping in grief beyond control.

entries.zh: 其惠化所感如此。
entries.en: Such was the depth of feeling his benevolent rule inspired.
entries.literal: Such was what his benevolent transformation moved.

entries.zh: 百姓相率爲立廟建碑，以紀其德。
entries.en: The people together built a temple and erected a stele to commemorate his virtue.
entries.literal: The people in succession built a temple and erected a stele to record his virtue.

entries.zh: 又詣京師求贈諡。
entries.en: They also went to the capital to request a posthumous title for him.
entries.literal: They also went to the capital to request a posthumous title.

entries.zh: 詔贈湘州刺史。
entries.en: An edict posthumously appointed him Governor of Xiangzhou.
entries.literal: An edict posthumously awarded him Governor of Xiangzhou.

entries.zh: 諡曰恭。
entries.en: His posthumous title was Respectful.
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Respectful.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：高祖光有天下，慶命傍流，枝戚屬㜕，咸被任遇。
entries.en: The historian writes: When Gaozu came to possess the realm, fortune flowed to his kinsmen on every side, and collateral relatives of the imperial house were all given office and favor.
entries.literal: The historian says: Emperor Gaozu possessed all under Heaven; felicitous mandate flowed to the sides; branch kin and collateral relatives were all given employment and favor.

entries.zh: 蕭景之才辯識斷，益政佐時，蓋梁宗室令望者矣。
entries.en: Xiao Jing's talent, judgment, and debate, and his service in strengthening the government of his time, made him the outstanding figure among the Liang imperial clan.
entries.literal: Xiao Jing's talent in debate and judgment, benefiting government and assisting the age—he was perhaps the eminent hope of the Liang imperial clan.

entries.zh: 梁書卷第二十四 列傳第十八
entries.en: Book of Liang, Volume 24, Biographies 18
entries.literal: Book of Liang, Volume Twenty-four, Biographies Eighteen

entries.zh: 梁臺建，爲奉常丞。
entries.en: When the Liang regime was first set up, he was appointed Vice Director of Court Ceremonial.
entries.literal: When the Liang administration was established, he became Vice Director of Court Ceremonial.

entries.zh: 高祖卽位，博求異能之士。
entries.en: After the High Ancestor acceded, he cast a wide net for men of exceptional talent.
entries.literal: When the High Ancestor took the throne, he broadly sought men of unusual ability.

entries.zh: 吏部尚書范雲與顒素善，重捨才器，言之於高祖，召拜尚書祠部郎。
entries.en: Fan Yun, Minister of Personnel, had long been close to Yan and admired She's ability. He recommended him to the High Ancestor, who summoned She and appointed him Gentleman of the Sacrifices Section in the Secretariat.
entries.literal: Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Fan Yun had long been on good terms with Yan and valued She's talent and capacity; he spoke of him to the High Ancestor, who summoned and appointed him Gentleman of the Department of Sacrifices in the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 時天下草創，禮儀損益，多自捨出。
entries.en: The empire was still being founded, and most revisions to ritual and ceremonial practice came from She.
entries.literal: At that time the realm was newly founded; additions and reductions to ritual and ceremony largely came from She.

entries.zh: 尋爲後軍記室參軍、秣陵令。
entries.en: He was soon made Recorder on the staff of the Rear General and Magistrate of Moling.
entries.literal: Soon he became Recorder of the Rear General's Staff and Magistrate of Moling.

entries.zh: 入爲中書通事舍人，累遷太子洗馬，散騎常侍，中書侍郎，鴻臚卿。
entries.en: He entered central government as an Attendant-in-Ordinary for General Affairs in the Secretariat and rose through the ranks to Groom of the Heir Apparent, Regular Attendant, Secretariat Attendant, and Director of the Court for Dependencies.
entries.literal: He entered the court as Attendant-in-Ordinary for General Affairs in the Secretariat, and was repeatedly promoted to Groom of the Heir Apparent, Regular Attendant, Secretariat Attendant, and Director of the Court for Dependencies.

entries.zh: 時王亮得罪歸家，故人莫有至者，捨獨敦恩舊，及卒，身營殯葬，時人稱之。
entries.en: When Wang Liang fell from favor and retired home, none of his old friends would visit him, but She alone remained loyal to their past friendship. When Wang died, She personally arranged the funeral, and people praised him for it.
entries.literal: At that time Wang Liang had offended and returned home; none of his old friends came to see him, but She alone treated him with the kindness due an old associate, and when he died personally arranged the funeral; people of the time praised him.

entries.zh: 遷尚書吏部郎，太子右衛率，右衛將軍，雖居職屢徙，而常留省內，罕得休下。
entries.en: He was promoted to Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel, Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard, and General of the Right Guard. Though his titles changed often, he remained at court and seldom had a day off.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel in the Secretariat, Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard, and General of the Right Guard; although his posts changed repeatedly, he constantly remained within the Secretariat and rarely had leave to go home.

entries.zh: 國史詔誥，儀體法律，軍旅謀謨，皆兼掌之。
entries.en: He held simultaneous responsibility for the national history, imperial edicts and proclamations, ritual protocol and law, and military planning.
entries.literal: National history, imperial edicts and proclamations, ritual forms and laws, and military strategy and counsel—he held charge of them all.

entries.zh: 日夜侍上，預機密，二十餘年未嘗離左右。
entries.en: Day and night he attended the emperor and shared in state secrets; for more than twenty years he was never far from his side.
entries.literal: Day and night he attended the sovereign and took part in confidential affairs; for more than twenty years he never left his side.

entries.zh: 捨素辯給，與人泛論談謔，終日不絕口，而竟無一言漏泄機事，衆尤嘆服之。
entries.en: She was naturally quick-witted and loved to debate and banter with others, talking without pause all day long, yet he never let a single secret slip. People admired him all the more for it.
entries.literal: She was by nature quick in debate; with others he would discourse broadly and jest, talking without cease all day, yet in the end not a single word of confidential affairs leaked out, and the multitude especially admired and submitted to this.

entries.zh: 性儉素，衣服器用，居處床席，如布衣之貧者。
entries.en: He lived plainly by nature: his clothes, furnishings, room, bed, and bedding were no better than a poor commoner's.
entries.literal: By nature he was frugal and plain; his clothes, implements, dwelling, bed, and mat were like those of a poor commoner.

entries.zh: 每入官府，雖廣廈華堂，閨閤重邃，捨居之則塵埃滿積。
entries.en: Wherever he lodged in government offices, however grand the halls and chambers, his rooms were left thick with dust.
entries.literal: Whenever he entered an official residence, though it had broad halls and splendid chambers with inner apartments deep and secluded, where She dwelt dust would pile up thick.

entries.zh: 以荻爲鄣，壞亦不營。
entries.en: He used reed mats for partitions and did not bother to replace them when they wore out.
entries.literal: He used reeds for screens; when they broke he did not repair them.

entries.zh: 爲右衛，母憂去職，起爲明威將軍、右驍騎將軍。
entries.en: While he was General of the Right Guard, he left office to observe mourning for his mother. When the mourning period ended, he was reappointed General of Illustrious Might and General of the Right Swift Cavalry.
entries.literal: While serving as Right Guard, he left office on his mother's death; on mourning's end he was reappointed General of Illustrious Might and General of the Right Swift Cavalry.

entries.zh: 服闋，除侍中，領步兵校尉，未拜，仍遷員外散騎常侍、太子左衛率。
entries.en: After mourning he was named Palace Attendant and concurrent Colonel of the Footsoldiers, but before he could assume those posts he was transferred to Extraordinary Regular Attendant and Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.
entries.literal: When mourning was complete, he was appointed Palace Attendant and concurrently Colonel of the Footsoldiers; before he could take up the appointment he was transferred to Extraordinary Regular Attendant and Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.

entries.zh: 頃之，加散騎常侍、本州大中正，遷太子詹事。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was given the additional titles Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Grand Rectifier of his home province, and was promoted to Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter he was given the additional titles Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Grand Rectifier of his native province, and was transferred to Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.

entries.zh: 勉幼孤貧，早勵清節。
entries.en: Mian lost his father young and grew up poor, but from an early age he cultivated a life of integrity.
entries.literal: Mian in youth was orphaned and poor and early cultivated pure integrity.

entries.zh: 年六歲，時屬霖雨，家人祈霽，率爾爲文，見稱耆宿。
entries.en: At the age of six, during a long spell of rain, his family prayed for clear weather. He spontaneously composed a piece of writing and was praised by the elders.
entries.literal: At age six, when there was prolonged rain, the family prayed for clear skies; he spontaneously composed a text and was praised by elders.

entries.zh: 及長，篤志好學。
entries.en: As he grew older, he devoted himself wholeheartedly to study.
entries.literal: When he grew up, he was steadfast in will and fond of learning.

entries.zh: 起家國子生。
entries.en: He entered official life as a student of the Imperial University.
entries.literal: He began his career as a student of the Imperial University.

entries.zh: 太尉文憲公王儉時爲祭酒，每稱勉有宰輔之量。
entries.en: Wang Jian, Duke Wenxian and Grand Marshal, was then Libationer of the university and often said that Mian had the makings of a chief minister.
entries.literal: The Grand Marshal, Duke Wenxian Wang Jian, was then Libationer, and often said Mian had the capacity of a chief minister.

entries.zh: 射策舉高第，補西陽王國侍郎。
entries.en: He placed at the top of the archery-and-policy examination and was appointed Attendant to the Prince of Xiyang.
entries.literal: In the target-and-plan examination he achieved a high grade and was appointed Attendant of the Kingdom of Xiyang.

entries.zh: 尋遷太學博士，鎮軍參軍，尚書殿中郎，以公事免。
entries.en: He was soon promoted to Erudite of the Imperial Academy, Staff Member of the Suppressing Army, and Gentleman of the Palace in the Secretariat, but was later dismissed over an official matter.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Erudite of the Imperial Academy, Staff Member of the Suppressing Army, and Gentleman of the Palace in the Secretariat; he was dismissed on account of official business.

entries.zh: 又除中兵郎、領軍長史。
entries.en: He was later appointed Central Troops Officer and Chief Clerk on the staff of the Army Guard.
entries.literal: He was again appointed Central Troops Officer and Chief Clerk of the Army Guard.

entries.zh: 琅邪王元長才名甚盛，嘗欲與勉相識，每託人召之。
entries.en: Wang Yuanchang, Prince of Langye, was then at the height of his fame, and he repeatedly tried to arrange a meeting with Mian through intermediaries.
entries.literal: The Prince of Langye Wang Yuanchang had a very flourishing reputation for talent; he once wished to become acquainted with Mian and repeatedly had others summon him.

entries.zh: 勉謂人曰：「王郎名高望促，難可輕醿衣裾。」
entries.en: Mian told an acquaintance, "Master Wang's fame is high but his prospects are short-lived. One should not lightly trail in his wake."
entries.literal: Mian told someone, "Master Wang's fame is high but his prospects are short; one can hardly lightly wet the hem of one's robe with him."

entries.zh: 俄而元長及禍，時人莫不服其機鑒。
entries.en: Before long Yuanchang met with disaster, and everyone marveled at Mian's foresight.
entries.literal: Before long Yuanchang met with disaster, and people of the time all submitted to his keen foresight.

entries.zh: 初與長沙宣武王游，高祖深器賞之。
entries.en: Early on he became close to Xiao Yi, King of Changsha and King Xuanwu, and the High Ancestor came to think highly of him.
entries.literal: Early on he associated with the King of Changsha, King Xuanwu, and the High Ancestor deeply valued and appreciated him.

entries.zh: 及義兵至京邑，勉於新林謁見，高祖甚加恩禮，使管書記。
entries.en: When the righteous army reached the capital, Mian presented himself at Xinlin. The High Ancestor treated him with special favor and put him in charge of records and correspondence.
entries.literal: When the righteous army reached the capital region, Mian presented himself at Xinlin; the High Ancestor greatly added favor and ceremony and had him manage documents and records.

entries.zh: 高祖踐阼，拜中書侍郎，遷建威將軍、後軍諮議參軍、本邑中正、尚書左丞。
entries.en: When the High Ancestor took the throne, Mian was appointed Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat and soon promoted to General Who Establishes Might, advisory staff officer to the Rear Army, rectifier of his home district, and Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: When the High Ancestor ascended the throne, he was appointed Secretariat Attendant and transferred to General Who Establishes Might, Adviser to the Rear Army, Rectifier of his native district, and Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 自掌樞憲，多所糾舉，時論以爲稱職。
entries.en: Once he held authority over legal discipline, he brought many cases to account, and public opinion held that he was thoroughly fit for the post.
entries.literal: From the time he held the pivot of law and discipline, he impeached many cases; opinion of the time held that he was fit for his post.

entries.zh: 天監二年，除給事黃門侍郎、尚書吏部郎，參掌大選。
entries.en: In the second year of Tianjian he was appointed Supervising Attendant and Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel, sharing responsibility for major appointments.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianjian he was appointed Supervising Attendant and Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel in the Secretariat, participating in the great selection.

entries.zh: 遷侍中。
entries.en: He was promoted to Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 時王師北伐，候驛填委。
entries.en: At that time the imperial army was campaigning in the north, and courier stations were buried under dispatches.
entries.literal: At that time the royal army marched north; courier stations were piled with dispatches.

entries.zh: 勉參掌軍書，劬勞夙夜，動經數旬，乃一還宅。
entries.en: Mian shared responsibility for military correspondence and labored day and night. Weeks would pass before he returned home even once.
entries.literal: Mian participated in managing military documents, toiling from early to late; often several tens of days would pass before he returned home once.

entries.zh: 每還，羣犬驚吠。
entries.en: Whenever he did return, the household dogs barked in alarm at the stranger.
entries.literal: Whenever he returned, the pack of dogs would bark in alarm.

entries.zh: 勉歎曰：「吾憂國忘家，乃至於此。
entries.en: Mian sighed and said, "I have worried for the state until I have forgotten my own home—even to this point.
entries.literal: Mian sighed and said, "I worry for the state and forget my home, even to this point.

entries.zh: 若吾亡後，亦是傳中一事。」
entries.en: When I am gone, this too will be a story worth telling."
entries.literal: After my death, this too will be an incident recorded in my biography."

entries.zh: 六年，除給事中、五兵尚書，遷吏部尚書。
entries.en: In the sixth year he was appointed Supervising Attendant and Minister of the Five Armies, and was then promoted to Minister of Personnel.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Supervising Attendant and Minister of the Five Armies, and transferred to Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 勉居選官，彝倫有序，旣閑尺牘，兼善辭令，雖文案填積，坐客充滿，應對如流，手不停筆。
entries.en: As head of personnel appointments, Mian kept the hierarchy in good order. He was adept at paperwork and equally skilled at formal speech. Though documents piled up and his hall was always full of visitors, he answered with effortless fluency while his brush never stopped moving.
entries.literal: Mian held the post of selection officer; human relations were in order. He was already skilled in documents and also good at formal addresses. Though papers piled up and seated guests filled the room, he responded like flowing water and his hand did not stop the brush.

entries.zh: 又該綜百氏，皆爲避諱。
entries.en: He also possessed comprehensive knowledge of the various clans and took care to avoid all their taboo names.
entries.literal: He also had comprehensive knowledge of the various clans and avoided the taboo names of them all.

entries.zh: 常及閘入夜集，客有虞皓求詹事五官，勉正色答云：「今夕止可談風月，不宜及公事。」
entries.en: He often entertained guests late into the night after the gates had closed. Once a guest named Yu Hao asked him about an appointment as one of the Five Officials under the Grand Tutor. Mian answered sternly, "Tonight we may speak only of poetry and the moon. Official business is out of place."
entries.literal: He often gathered guests after the gate closing into the night; a guest, Yu Hao, sought the Five Officials post under the Grand Tutor. Mian with stern countenance replied, "This evening we may only discuss wind and moon; it is not fitting to touch official business."

entries.zh: 故時人咸服其無私。
entries.en: People admired him all the more for his impartiality.
entries.literal: Therefore people of the time all submitted to his lack of private interest.

entries.zh: 尋授宣惠將軍，置佐史，侍中、僕射如故。
entries.en: He was soon appointed General Who Proclaims Favor with a full staff, while retaining his posts as Palace Attendant and Vice Director.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed General Who Proclaims Favor, with staff officers established; Palace Attendant and Vice Director as before.

entries.zh: 又除尚書僕射、中衛將軍。
entries.en: He was later appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and General of the Central Guard.
entries.literal: He was again appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and General of the Central Guard.

entries.zh: 勉以舊恩，越升重位，盡心奉上，知無不爲。
entries.en: Because of his long service, Mian was promoted beyond the usual measure to high office. He devoted himself wholly to the throne and left nothing undone.
entries.literal: Mian, by reason of old favor, was promoted beyond his rank to a heavy post; he devoted his heart in serving above and there was nothing he knew that he did not do.

entries.zh: 爰自小選，迄於此職，常參掌衡石，甚得士心。
entries.en: From his early work in personnel selection to this highest post, he had long held the scales of appointment, and he won the deep respect of the scholarly class.
entries.literal: From the time of minor selection until this post, he constantly participated in holding the balance and stone, and greatly won the hearts of scholars.

entries.zh: 禁省中事，未嘗漏泄。
entries.en: He never disclosed a single matter from within the palace offices.
entries.literal: Matters within the forbidden precincts, he never leaked.

entries.zh: 每有表奏，輒焚藳草。
entries.en: Whenever he drafted a memorial, he burned the working copy afterward.
entries.literal: Whenever he had memorials submitted, he always burned the draft manuscripts.

entries.zh: 博通經史，多識前載。
entries.en: He was deeply learned in the classics and histories and knew a great deal of earlier historical writing.
entries.literal: He was broadly versed in the classics and histories and knew much of earlier records.

entries.zh: 朝儀國典，婚冠吉凶，勉皆預圖議。
entries.en: Mian took part in drafting and deliberating on court ritual, state institutions, marriage and capping ceremonies, and rites of mourning and celebration.
entries.literal: Court ceremonies, state institutions, marriage and capping, auspicious and inauspicious rites — Mian all participated in planning and discussion.

entries.zh: 普通六年，上修五禮表曰：
entries.en: In the sixth year of the Putong era, Mian submitted a memorial on the revision of the Five Rites, which read:
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Putong, he submitted a memorial on revising the Five Rites, saying:

entries.zh: 除散騎常侍，領遊擊將軍，未拜，改領太子右衛率。
entries.en: He was appointed Regular Attendant and concurrent General of Roaming Attack, but before he could assume the post he was reassigned as Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.
entries.literal: He was appointed Regular Attendant and concurrently General of Roaming Attack; before taking up the appointment he was changed to concurrent Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.

entries.zh: 遷左衛將軍，領太子中庶子，侍東宮。
entries.en: He was promoted to General of the Left Guard and concurrent Chief Steward of the Heir Apparent, serving in the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: He was transferred to General of the Left Guard, concurrently Chief Steward of the Heir Apparent, attending the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 昭明太子尚幼，敕知宮事。
entries.en: The Zhaoming Heir Apparent was still young, and Mian was ordered to manage palace affairs on his behalf.
entries.literal: The Zhaoming Heir Apparent was still young; he was ordered to manage palace affairs.

entries.zh: 太子禮之甚重，每事詢謀。
entries.en: The Heir Apparent treated him with great respect and consulted him on every matter.
entries.literal: The Heir Apparent treated him with great respect and on every matter sought his counsel.

entries.zh: 嘗於殿內講《孝經》，臨川靖惠王、尚書令沈約備二傅，勉與國子祭酒張充爲執經，王瑩、張稷、柳憕、王暕爲侍講。
entries.en: Once, in the palace hall, he lectured on the "Classic of Filial Piety." The King of Linchuan, King Jinghui, and Director of the Secretariat Shen Yue served as the two tutors; Mian and Libationer Zhang Chong held the text; Wang Ying, Zhang Ji, Liu Cong, and Wang Yan served as lecturing attendants.
entries.literal: Once within the hall he lectured on the "Classic of Filial Piety"; the King of Linchuan, King Jinghui, and Director of the Secretariat Shen Yue served as the two tutors; Mian and Libationer of the Imperial University Zhang Chong held the classic; Wang Ying, Zhang Ji, Liu Cong, and Wang Yan served as lecturing attendants.

entries.zh: 時選極親賢，妙盡時譽，勉陳讓數四。
entries.en: The men chosen were the most eminent kinsmen and worthies of the day, and Mian declined the honor four times.
entries.literal: The selection at the time reached the utmost in kinship and worth, wonderfully exhausting the reputation of the age; Mian submitted declining statements four times.

entries.zh: 又與沈約書，求換侍講，詔不許，然後就焉。
entries.en: He also wrote to Shen Yue asking to take the lesser role of lecturing attendant instead, but the emperor refused, and only then did he accept the appointment.
entries.literal: He also wrote to Shen Yue asking to exchange for the post of lecturing attendant; an edict did not permit it, and only then did he take up the post.

entries.zh: 轉太子詹事，領雲騎將軍，尋加散騎常侍，遷尚書右僕射，詹事如故。
entries.en: He was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and concurrent General of Cloud Cavalry, soon given the additional title of Regular Attendant, and promoted to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat while retaining his post as Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently General of Cloud Cavalry; soon he was given the additional title of Regular Attendant and transferred to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, Grand Tutor as before.

entries.zh: 又改授侍中，頻表解宮職，優詔不許。
entries.en: He was later appointed Palace Attendant and repeatedly petitioned to resign, but the emperor's gracious edicts refused each request.
entries.literal: He was again appointed Palace Attendant; he repeatedly submitted memorials resigning office, but gracious edicts did not permit it.

entries.zh: 時人間喪事，多不遵禮，朝終夕殯，相尚以速。
entries.en: At that time many people ignored proper funeral rites, encoffining the dead the same evening they died and competing to see who could bury fastest.
entries.literal: At that time in people's funerals many did not follow ritual; mourning ended in the morning and encoffining came in the evening, and they vied with one another in speed.

entries.zh: 勉上疏曰：「《禮記問喪》云：『三日而後斂者，以俟其生也。
entries.en: Mian submitted a memorial saying: "In the Record of Rites, 'Questions on Mourning,' it says: 'To encoffin only after three days is to wait in case the person may yet live.
entries.literal: Mian submitted a memorial saying: "The Record of Rites, 'Questions on Mourning,' says: 'To encoffin only after three days is to await the person's return to life.

entries.zh: 三日而不生，亦不生矣。』
entries.en: If after three days he has not revived, he will not revive.'
entries.literal: If after three days he does not live, he will not live.

entries.zh: 自頃以來，不遵斯制。
entries.en: In recent times this rule has been ignored.
entries.literal: From recent times onward, this regulation has not been followed.

entries.zh: 送終之禮，殯以期日，潤屋豪家，乃或半晷，衣衾棺槨，以速爲榮，親戚徒隸，各念休反。
entries.en: Funerals are now scheduled for a fixed day, and in wealthy households the encoffining sometimes takes only half a day. Fine shrouds and coffins are prized for how quickly they can be finished. Relatives, servants, and retainers all think only of getting back to their rest.
entries.literal: In the rites of seeing one off at the end, encoffining is set for a fixed day; wealthy households sometimes do it in half a day. Garments, covers, coffin, and outer coffin—taking speed as glory; kin, servants, and retainers each think of rest and return.

entries.zh: 故屬纊才畢，灰釘已具，忘狐鼠之顧步，愧燕雀之徊翔。
entries.en: As soon as the final breath is taken, the lime and nails are already ready. They forget how even foxes and rats pause over the dead, and they would be shamed by the swallows and sparrows that hover and hesitate.
entries.literal: Thus as soon as the last breath is placed, lime and nails are already prepared; they forget the fox and rat's lingering steps and are ashamed before the swallows and sparrows' hovering flight.

entries.zh: 傷情滅理，莫此爲大。
entries.en: Nothing does more violence to human feeling and moral principle than this.
entries.literal: To wound feeling and extinguish principle—nothing is greater than this.

entries.zh: 且人子承衾之時，志懣心絕，喪事所資，悉關他手，愛憎深淺，事實難原。
entries.en: Moreover, when a son receives the death shroud, his heart is broken with grief. Everything needed for the funeral is handled by others, and it is hard to know whether their actions spring from love or from indifference.
entries.literal: Moreover, when a son receives the coverlet, his will is aggrieved and his heart cut off; what the funeral relies on is entirely in others' hands—the depth of love or hate is in fact hard to trace to its source.

entries.zh: 如覘視或爽，存沒違濫，使萬有其一，怨酷已多。
entries.en: If the watching of the body is neglected or the rites for the living and the dead are confused, even if only one case in ten thousand goes wrong, the grief and injustice will be great.
entries.literal: If observation or attendance is neglected, and the living and dead are violated and confused, even if only one in ten thousand suffers this, the grievance and cruelty are already many.

entries.zh: 豈若緩其告斂之晨，申其望生之冀。
entries.en: How much better to delay the morning of encoffinement and preserve the hope that life may yet return?
entries.literal: How does this compare with slowing the morning of announcing encoffinement and extending the hope of return to life?

entries.zh: 請自今士庶，宜悉依古，三日大斂。
entries.en: I ask that from now on gentlemen and commoners alike follow the ancient practice and wait three days before encoffining the body.
entries.literal: I request that from now on gentry and commoners should all follow the ancients and perform great encoffinement after three days.

entries.zh: 如有不奉，加以糾繩。」
entries.en: Those who fail to comply should be subject to investigation and punishment."
entries.literal: If there are those who do not comply, let correction and punishment be applied."

entries.zh: 詔可其奏。
entries.en: The emperor approved his memorial.
entries.literal: An edict approved his memorial.

entries.zh: 洎周室大壞，王道旣衰，官守斯文，日失其序。
entries.en: When the Zhou house collapsed and the royal way declined, the officials charged with preserving these traditions lost their proper order day by day.
entries.literal: When the Zhou house was greatly ruined and the royal way had already declined, officials who guarded this culture daily lost its order.

entries.zh: 禮樂征伐，出自諸侯，《小雅》盡廢，舊章缺矣。
entries.en: Ritual, music, war, and punishment passed from the throne to the feudal lords; the "Lesser Odes of the Kingdom" fell wholly into disuse, and the old regulations were lost.
entries.literal: Ritual, music, campaigns, and punishments issued from the feudal lords; the "Lesser Odes of the Kingdom" were entirely abandoned, and old statutes were lost.

entries.zh: 是以韓宣適魯，知周公之德；
entries.en: Thus when Han Xuan of Jin visited Lu, he came to understand the virtue of the Duke of Zhou;
entries.literal: Therefore when Han Xuan went to Lu, he knew the virtue of the Duke of Zhou;

entries.zh: 叔侯在晉，辨郊勞之儀。
entries.en: and Shu Hou, serving in Jin, was able to explain the rites of suburban welcome.
entries.literal: Shu Hou was in Jin and distinguished the rites of suburban welcome.

entries.zh: 戰國從橫，政教愈泯；
entries.en: In the Warring States period of shifting alliances, government and moral instruction sank ever deeper into obscurity;
entries.literal: In the Warring States era of vertical and horizontal alliances, government and teaching grew ever more extinguished;

entries.zh: 暴秦滅學，掃地無餘。
entries.en: Then tyrannical Qin suppressed learning and swept the ground bare, leaving nothing behind.
entries.literal: Violent Qin destroyed learning, sweeping the ground and leaving nothing.

entries.zh: 漢氏鬱興，日不暇給，猶命叔孫于外野，方知帝王之爲貴。
entries.en: When the Han rose in splendor, its affairs were so pressing that each day left no spare moment; yet the court still had to summon Shusun Tong from the wilderness to devise rites, and only then did men understand how precious imperial dignity truly was.
entries.literal: The Han dynasty flourished abundantly, with days not enough to supply its needs; still it ordered Shusun in the outer wilds, and only then knew how precious being emperor and king was.

entries.zh: 末葉紛綸，遞有興毀，或以武功銳志，或好黃老之言，禮義之式，於焉中止。
entries.en: In the later generations of Han, affairs grew ever more tangled, with one dynasty rising as another fell; some rulers pursued military glory with single-minded zeal, others favored the teachings of Huang-Lao — and the forms of ritual and righteousness came to a halt.
entries.literal: In the late branches, affairs were tangled, successively rising and falling; some were sharp in military achievement, some favored the words of the Yellow Emperor and Laozi — the forms of ritual and righteousness thereupon ceased.

entries.zh: 及東京曹褒，南宮制述，集其散略，百有餘篇，雖寫以尺簡，而終闕平奏。
entries.en: At the Eastern Capital, Cao Bao compiled ritual texts at the Southern Palace, gathering scattered materials into more than a hundred chapters; though copied onto bamboo slips, the work was never brought to completion and formally submitted.
entries.literal: By the Eastern Capital, Cao Bao formulated and compiled at the Southern Palace, gathering scattered outlines into more than a hundred pieces; though written on foot-long slips, in the end they lacked completion and submission.

entries.zh: 其後兵革相尋，異端互起，章句旣淪，俎豆斯輟。
entries.en: After that, war followed upon war, heterodox teachings multiplied, classical commentaries sank into oblivion, and sacrificial vessels fell silent.
entries.literal: Afterward warfare followed in succession, heterodox teachings rose one after another, commentarial passages sank away, and sacrificial vessels ceased.

entries.zh: 方領矩步之容，事滅於旌鼓；
entries.en: The dignified bearing of square collars and measured steps vanished in the clash of banners and drums;
entries.literal: The bearing of square collars and measured steps perished amid banners and drums;

entries.zh: 蘭臺石室之文，用盡於帷蓋。
entries.en: and the texts preserved in the Orchid Terrace and Stone Chamber were consumed to make tent covers.
entries.literal: The texts of the Orchid Terrace and Stone Chamber were entirely used up as tent coverings.

entries.zh: 至乎晉初，爰定新禮，荀顗制之於前，摯虞刪之於末。
entries.en: At the beginning of Jin, a new ritual code was established: Xun Yi drafted it at the outset, and Zhi Yu revised it at the end.
entries.literal: Reaching the beginning of Jin, then the new rites were fixed — Xun Yi formulated them at the start, Zhi Yu edited them at the end.

entries.zh: 旣而中原喪亂，罕有所遺；
entries.en: But when the Central Plains were overrun by chaos, little of it survived;
entries.literal: Soon the Central Plains fell into disorder, and little was left behind;

entries.zh: 江左草創，因循而已。
entries.en: in the southeast the dynasty was newly founded, and men could do no more than follow old precedent.
entries.literal: In the southeast, it was newly established, and they merely followed precedent.

entries.zh: 𨤸革之風，是則未暇。
entries.en: As for the spirit of reform and innovation, there was no time for it at all.
entries.literal: The winds of reform and innovation — for that they had no leisure.

entries.zh: 伏惟陛下睿明啓運，先天改物，撥亂惟武，經世以文。
entries.en: I humbly consider that Your Majesty, wise and discerning, has inaugurated a new age, transformed the realm in accord with Heaven's mandate, quelled disorder through martial power, and governed the world through culture.
entries.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty, wise and bright, inaugurated the destiny, changed things before Heaven, quelled disorder through martial virtue, and ordered the age through culture.

entries.zh: 作樂在乎功成，制禮弘於業定。
entries.en: Music is made when merit is achieved; ritual is established in full when the great enterprise is secure.
entries.literal: Making music lies in accomplishing merit; instituting ritual is magnified when the enterprise is settled.

entries.zh: 光啓二學，皇枝等於貴遊；
entries.en: You opened two imperial academies, placing imperial clansmen on equal footing with the sons of the nobility;
entries.literal: You opened two academies, placing imperial branches on a par with noble scions;

entries.zh: 辟茲五館，草萊升以好爵。
entries.en: and established these five halls of learning, so that men from humble fields might rise to honorable office.
entries.literal: You established these five halls, so men from humble fields rose to fine rank.

entries.zh: 爰自受命，迄于告成，盛德形容備矣，天下能事畢矣。
entries.en: From the moment you received the mandate until the present completion of your work, your great virtue has been fully realized, and every task the realm could undertake has been accomplished.
entries.literal: From accepting the mandate until announcing completion, your abundant virtue has been fully described, and all the world could do is done.

entries.zh: 明明穆穆，無德而稱焉。
entries.en: Bright in wisdom and dignified in bearing, your virtue exceeds what any words can adequately praise.
entries.literal: Bright and dignified, there are no words adequate to praise your virtue.

entries.zh: 至若玄符靈貺之祥，浮溟機山之賮，固亦日書左史，副在司存，今可得而略也。
entries.en: As for the auspicious signs of mystical talismans and divine blessings, and the tribute brought from distant seas and Mount Jishan — these too are recorded daily by the court scribes and preserved in the archives; they may be passed over briefly here.
entries.literal: As for auspicious signs of mysterious talismans and spiritual blessings, tribute from distant seas and Mount Jishan — these too are daily recorded by the left scribe and duplicated in the keeping offices; now they may be briefly noted.

entries.zh: 是以命彼羣才，搜甘泉之法；
entries.en: Therefore Your Majesty summoned many men of talent to search out the ritual precedents of Ganquan;
entries.literal: Therefore you ordered those many talents to search out the methods of Ganquan;

entries.zh: 延茲碩學，闡曲臺之儀。
entries.en: and invited eminent scholars to expound the rites compiled at the Qutai Platform.
entries.literal: and invited these eminent scholars to expound the rites of Qutai Platform.

entries.zh: 淄上淹中之儒，連蹤繼軌；
entries.en: Confucian scholars from Linzi and the Yanzhong academy came in an unbroken stream;
entries.literal: Confucian scholars of Zi River and Yanzhong followed one after another on the same path;

entries.zh: 負笈懷鈆之彥，匪旦伊夕。
entries.en: and learned men bearing book-chests and writing tablets arrived not in a day or a night alone.
entries.literal: Men of talent bearing book-chests and carrying writing styli came not merely overnight.

entries.zh: 諒以化穆三雍，人從五典，秩宗之教，勃焉以興。
entries.en: Surely through the civilizing influence of the Three Yong academies, the people were brought into accord with the Five Classics, and the teachings overseen by the Minister of Rites vigorously revived.
entries.literal: Surely through transforming the Three Yong, people followed the Five Classics — the teachings of the Minister of Rites vigorously arose.

entries.zh: 伏尋所定五禮，起齊永明三年，太子步兵校尉伏曼容表求制一代禮樂，于時參議置新舊學士十人，止修五禮，諮稟衛將軍丹陽尹王儉，學士亦分住郡中，製作歷年，猶未克就。
entries.en: I humbly review the history of the Five Rites now completed: the project began in the third year of Yongming under Qi, when Fu Manrong, Infantry Commandant to the Crown Prince, submitted a memorial requesting the compilation of ritual and music for the age. At that time the court deliberated appointing ten senior and junior academicians to work exclusively on the Five Rites, reporting to Wang Jian, General of the Guard and Intendant of Danyang. The academicians were also dispersed to various commanderies. Years of work passed, yet the project remained unfinished.
entries.literal: I humbly examine the fixed Five Rites: they began in the third year of Yongming of Qi, when the Crown Prince's Infantry Commandant Fu Manrong submitted a memorial requesting the compilation of ritual and music for one generation. At that time it was deliberated to appoint ten old and new academicians, restricting the work to the Five Rites, with consultation and reporting to General of the Guard and Intendant of Danyang Wang Jian. The academicians also dispersed to reside in various commanderies. Production continued for years, yet it was still not completed.

entries.zh: 及文憲薨殂，遺文散逸，後又以事付國子祭酒何胤，經涉九載，猶復未畢。
entries.en: When Wang Jian, posthumously titled Wen Xian, died, his surviving manuscripts were scattered and lost. The task was later entrusted to He Yin, Director of the Imperial Academy; nine more years passed, and the work was still incomplete.
entries.literal: When Wen Xian died, his surviving texts were scattered and lost. Later the task was again entrusted to Director of the Imperial Academy He Yin; nine years passed, and still it was not finished.

entries.zh: 建武四年，胤還東山，齊明帝敕委尚書令徐孝嗣。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Jianwu, Yin retired to East Mountain, and Emperor Ming of Qi ordered that the project be entrusted to Xu Xiaosi, Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Jianwu, Yin returned to East Mountain, and Emperor Ming of Qi ordered that the matter be entrusted to Director of the Secretariat Xu Xiaosi.

entries.zh: 舊事本末，隨在南第。
entries.en: The original materials, with their full history, were kept at his Southern Residence.
entries.literal: The beginning and end of the old affair followed him to the Southern Residence.

entries.zh: 永元中，孝嗣於此遇禍，又多零落。
entries.en: During the Yongyuan era, Xu Xiaosi met with disaster there, and much of the material was again lost.
entries.literal: In the Yongyuan era, Xiaosi met calamity there, and much was again scattered and lost.

entries.zh: 當時鳩斂所餘，權付尚書左丞蔡仲熊、驍騎將軍何佟之，共掌其事。
entries.en: What remained from the earlier collection was provisionally entrusted to Cai Zhongxiong, Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat, and He Tongzhi, General of Valiant Cavalry, who jointly oversaw the work.
