entries.literal: What remained from the collection at that time was provisionally entrusted to Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat Cai Zhongxiong and General of Valiant Cavalry He Tongzhi, who jointly managed the affair.

entries.zh: 時修禮局住在國子學中門外，東昏之代，頻有軍火，其所散失，又逾太半。
entries.en: The ritual revision bureau was then housed outside the middle gate of the Imperial Academy. During the reign of Emperor Hun, repeated military fires broke out, and more than half of what remained was again lost.
entries.literal: At that time the ritual revision bureau was located outside the middle gate of the Imperial Academy. In the reign of Emperor Hun, there were repeated military fires; what was scattered and lost again exceeded more than half.

entries.zh: 天監元年，佟之啓審省置之宜，敕使外詳。
entries.en: In the first year of Tianjian, He Tongzhi submitted a memorial on whether the bureau should be retained or abolished, and an edict ordered the outer offices to deliberate the matter.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianjian, Tongzhi submitted a memorial examining whether it was appropriate to reduce or retain the bureau; an edict ordered the outer offices to deliberate in detail.

entries.zh: 時尚書參詳，以天地初革，庶務權輿，宜俟隆平，徐議刪撰。
entries.en: The Secretariat then deliberated and concluded that, with the realm newly transformed and every branch of government still in its infancy, it would be best to wait until peace was fully established before proceeding with revision and compilation.
entries.literal: At that time the Secretariat deliberated in detail, holding that Heaven and Earth had just been transformed, and numerous affairs were in their beginning; it was appropriate to wait for great peace and then slowly discuss editing and compilation.

entries.zh: 欲且省禮局，並還尚書儀曹。
entries.en: They proposed temporarily abolishing the ritual bureau and returning its functions to the Rites Section of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: They wished temporarily to reduce the ritual bureau and return its functions altogether to the Rites Section of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 詔旨云：「禮壞樂缺，故國異家殊，實宜以時修定，以爲永准。
entries.en: The imperial edict read: "Ritual has fallen into ruin and music into neglect; that is why every state and every house follows different customs. The rites should indeed be revised and fixed in timely fashion, to serve as a permanent standard.
entries.literal: The edict stated: "Ritual is ruined and music is lacking; therefore states differ and families vary. It is truly appropriate to revise and fix them in timely fashion, making them an eternal standard.

entries.zh: 但頃之修撰，以情取人，不以學進；
entries.en: But in recent compilations, men were chosen through personal favor rather than scholarly merit;
entries.literal: But in recent editing and compilation, people were chosen by personal favor, not advanced by learning;

entries.zh: 其掌知者，以貴總一，不以稽古，所以歷年不就，有名無實。
entries.en: those placed in charge were selected for rank rather than knowledge of antiquity. That is why years passed without completion, and the project had a name but no substance.
entries.literal: those in charge were unified by rank, not by investigation of antiquity. Therefore years passed without completion — there was a name but no substance.

entries.zh: 此旣經國所先，外可議其人，人定，便卽撰次。」
entries.en: Since this is a matter of first importance to the ordering of the state, the outer offices should nominate suitable men; once the personnel are settled, compilation should begin at once."
entries.literal: Since this is what ordering the state puts first, the outer offices may discuss the personnel; once the men are fixed, then immediately compile and arrange."

entries.zh: 於是尚書僕射沈約等參議，請五禮各置舊學士一人，人各自舉學士二人，相助抄撰。
entries.en: Thereupon Shen Yue, Vice Director of the Secretariat, and others deliberated and proposed that each of the Five Rites should have one senior academician appointed, each of whom would in turn recommend two academicians to assist in copying and compiling.
entries.literal: Thereupon Vice Director of the Secretariat Shen Yue and others deliberated and requested that for each of the Five Rites one senior academician be appointed, each man himself recommending two academicians to assist in copying and compiling.

entries.zh: 其中有疑者，依前漢石渠、後漢白虎，隨源以聞，請旨斷決。
entries.en: Where doubts arose, following the precedent of the Shiqu and Baihu conferences of Han, the matter would be reported with citations and submitted for imperial decision.
entries.literal: Where there were doubts, following the precedents of Shiqu in Former Han and Baihu in Later Han, they were reported according to source for imperial decision.

entries.zh: 乃以舊學士右軍記室參軍明山賓掌吉禮，中軍騎兵參軍嚴植之掌凶禮，中軍田曹行參軍兼太常丞賀蒨掌賓禮，征虜記室參軍陸璉掌軍禮，右軍參軍司馬裴掌嘉禮，尚書左丞何佟之總參其事。
entries.en: Ming Shanbin, a former academician and Record-Office Aide on the Right Army staff, was placed in charge of auspicious rites; Yan Zhizhi, Cavalry Aide on the Central Army staff, of inauspicious rites; He Qian, acting Field Bureau Aide on the Central Army staff and concurrently Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, of guest rites; Lu Lian, Record-Office Aide to the General Who Conquers the Caitiffs, of military rites; Sima Pei, Staff Officer of the Right Army, of celebratory rites; and He Tongzhi, Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, was given overall supervision of the project.
entries.literal: Thereupon the senior academician Ming Shanbin, Recorder of the Right Army Staff, was put in charge of auspicious rites; Yan Zhizhi, Cavalry Commandant of the Central Army, was put in charge of inauspicious rites; He Qian, Acting Army Field Commandant of the Central Army and concurrently Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was put in charge of guest rites; Lu Lian, Recorder of the General Who Conquers the Barbarians, was put in charge of military rites; Sima Pei, Army Staff Officer of the Right Army, was put in charge of celebratory rites; and Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat He Tongzhi was given overall participation in the affair.

entries.zh: 佟之亡後，以鎮北諮議參軍伏暅代之。
entries.en: After He Tongzhi died, Fu Xiong, Advisory Staff Officer to the General Who Pacifies the North, replaced him.
entries.literal: After Tongzhi died, Fu Xiong, Advisory Staff Officer to the General Who Pacifies the North, replaced him.

entries.zh: 後又以暅代嚴植之掌凶禮。
entries.en: Later Fu Xiong also replaced Yan Zhizhi as overseer of inauspicious rites.
entries.literal: Later Xiong also replaced Yan Zhizhi in charge of inauspicious rites.

entries.zh: 暅尋遷官，以《五經》博士繆昭掌凶禮。
entries.en: Fu Xiong was soon transferred to another post, and Miao Zhao, Erudite of the "Five Classics," was placed in charge of inauspicious rites.
entries.literal: Xiong soon transferred to another post, and Erudite of the Five Classics Miao Zhao was put in charge of inauspicious rites.

entries.zh: 復以禮儀深廣，記載殘缺，宜須博論，共盡其致，更使鎮軍將軍丹陽尹沈約、太常卿張充及臣三人同參厥務。
entries.en: Because ritual propriety was vast in scope and the surviving records were fragmentary, broad deliberation was needed to exhaust its full meaning. Shen Yue, General Who Pacifies the Army and Intendant of Danyang; Zhang Chong, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; and your subject — the three of us — were further appointed jointly to oversee the work.
entries.literal: Again, because ritual propriety was deep and broad and the records were fragmentary and incomplete, broad discussion was needed so that all might exhaust its meaning. Shen Yue, General Who Pacifies the Army and Intendant of Danyang; Zhang Chong, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; and your subject, three men, were further ordered jointly to participate in the task.

entries.zh: 臣又奉別敕，總知其事。
entries.en: Your subject also received a separate edict placing me in overall charge of the project.
entries.literal: Your subject also received a separate edict to oversee the affair in general.

entries.zh: 末又使中書侍郎周捨、庾於陵二人復豫參知。
entries.en: Finally Zhou She, Gentleman Attendant of the Palace Secretariat, and Yu Yuling were also appointed to take part in deliberation.
entries.literal: Finally Zhou She, Gentleman Attendant of the Palace Secretariat, and Yu Yuling were again ordered to participate in the deliberations.

entries.zh: 若有疑義，所掌學士當職先立議，通諮五禮舊學士及參知，各言同異，條牒啓聞，決之制旨。
entries.en: When a doubtful point arose, the academician responsible would first draft a proposal, consult the senior academicians of the Five Rites and the other participants, record each man's agreement or dissent, submit the matter in memorial, and await the emperor's decision.
entries.literal: If there were doubtful points, the academician in charge of the duty would first establish a proposal, consult broadly with the senior academicians of the Five Rites and the participants in consultation, each stating agreement or difference; the items would be submitted in memorial for decision by imperial edict.

entries.zh: 疑事旣多，歲時又積，制旨裁斷，其數不少。
entries.en: The doubtful points were many, and the years accumulated; the number of imperial decisions handed down was considerable.
entries.literal: Doubtful matters were already many, and years also accumulated; imperial edicts deciding them were not a few in number.

entries.zh: 莫不網羅經誥，玉振金聲，義貫幽微，理入神契。
entries.en: Every decision drew upon the canonical texts with the resonance of jade and gold; meaning reached into the subtlest depths, and principle attained a harmony that seemed almost divine.
entries.literal: None failed to gather the canonical teachings, jade vibrating and gold sounding; meaning penetrated the subtle, and principle entered divine accord.

entries.zh: 前儒所不釋，後學所未聞。
entries.en: Points that earlier scholars had left unresolved were settled here; matters that later students had never heard explained were made clear.
entries.literal: What former Confucians did not explain, later students had not heard.

entries.zh: 凡諸奏決，皆載篇首，具列聖旨，爲不刊之則。
entries.en: Every decision submitted and approved was recorded at the head of the relevant section, with the imperial intent fully set forth, to serve as an immutable standard.
entries.literal: All memorial decisions were recorded at the head of each section, fully listing the sage intent, forming an unalterable standard.

entries.zh: 洪規盛範，冠絕百王；
entries.en: These grand regulations and magnificent models surpass those of all the kings of old;
entries.literal: Grand regulations and flourishing models surpass all hundred kings;

entries.zh: 茂實英聲，方垂千載。
entries.en: their substance is rich and their renown splendid, and they will be handed down for a thousand years.
entries.literal: abundant substance and outstanding renown will be handed down for a thousand years.

entries.zh: 寧孝宣之能擬，豈孝章之足云。
entries.en: Even Emperor Xuan of Han could scarcely be compared with this achievement — to say nothing of Emperor Zhang.
entries.literal: Can even Emperor Xiaoxuan be compared? How could Emperor Xiaozhang suffice to mention?

entries.zh: 竊以撰正履禮，歷代罕就，皇明在運，厥功克成。
entries.en: I venture to observe that compiling and establishing ritual has rarely been brought to completion in any age; yet under Your Majesty's enlightened reign this great work has at last been achieved.
entries.literal: I venture to consider that compiling, correcting, and practicing ritual has rarely been accomplished in successive generations; now under imperial brightness the age is in motion, and this merit has been able to succeed.

entries.zh: 周代三千，舉其盈數；
entries.en: In the Zhou, the rites were said to number three thousand, a round total;
entries.literal: The Zhou era had three thousand, taking its full number;

entries.zh: 今之八千，隨事附益。
entries.en: today's eight thousand articles reflect additions made as circumstances required.
entries.literal: today's eight thousand follow affairs in addition and increase.

entries.zh: 質文相變，故其數兼倍，猶如八卦之爻，因而重之，錯綜成六十四也。
entries.en: As substance and form change with the times, the number has naturally doubled — just as the lines of the eight trigrams, when doubled and interwoven, become sixty-four.
entries.literal: Substance and form change each other; therefore the number is doubled — just like the lines of the eight trigrams, which are then doubled and interwoven to form sixty-four.

entries.zh: 昔文武二王，所以綱紀周室，君臨天下，公旦修之，以致太平龍鳳之瑞。
entries.en: In antiquity Kings Wen and Wu used ritual to order the Zhou house and rule the realm; the Duke of Zhou refined it, bringing about the age of peace marked by the auspicious appearances of dragon and phoenix.
entries.literal: Formerly the two kings Wen and Wu thereby regulated the Zhou house, ruled over all under Heaven; the Duke of Zhou refined it, thereby attaining the auspicious signs of peace with dragon and phoenix.

entries.zh: 自斯厥後，甫備茲日。
entries.en: From that age until now, only on this day has such a work been fully completed.
entries.literal: From that time until now, only on this day has it been fully prepared.

entries.zh: 孔子曰：「其有繼周，雖百世可知。」
entries.en: Confucius said: "If there is one to succeed Zhou, even after a hundred generations its way may be foreknown."
entries.literal: Confucius said: "If there is one to succeed Zhou, even after a hundred generations it can be known."

entries.zh: 豈所謂齊功比美者歟！
entries.en: Is this not what is meant by matching Zhou in achievement and in splendor!
entries.literal: Is this not what is called equal in achievement and comparable in beauty!

entries.zh: 臣以庸識，謬司其任，淹留歷稔，允當斯責；
entries.en: Your subject, with my mediocre understanding, was undeservedly entrusted with this charge; I have lingered in the post for many years and have truly borne its weight.
entries.literal: Your subject, with mediocre understanding, was wrongly entrusted with this duty; lingering through accumulated years, I have truly borne this responsibility.

entries.zh: 兼勒成之初，未遑表上，實由才輕務廣，思力不周，永言慚惕，無忘寤寐。
entries.en: When the work was first completed, I had not yet submitted this memorial, truly because my ability was slight and the task vast, and my thought and strength were not equal to it. I remain ashamed and apprehensive, and the matter has never left my mind, waking or sleeping.
entries.literal: Moreover, at the beginning when completion was achieved, I had no leisure to submit a memorial — truly because talent was slight and tasks were broad, thought and strength were not comprehensive. I always speak with shame and caution, never forgetting waking or sleeping.

entries.zh: 自今春輿駕將親六師，搜尋軍禮，閱其條章，靡不該備。
entries.en: Since this spring, as Your Majesty has prepared to lead the Six Armies in person, I have searched the military rites and reviewed their articles and regulations; all are comprehensive and complete.
entries.literal: Since this spring the imperial carriage will personally lead the Six Armies; searching through military rites and examining their articles and regulations, none are not comprehensive and complete.

entries.zh: 所謂郁郁文哉，煥乎洋溢，信可以懸諸日月，頒之天下者矣。
entries.en: Truly it is richly cultured and brilliantly complete — a work that may be displayed beside sun and moon and promulgated throughout the realm.
entries.literal: What is called richly cultured indeed, brilliantly overflowing — truly it can be suspended beside sun and moon and promulgated throughout all under Heaven.

entries.zh: 愚心喜抃，彌思陳述；
entries.en: My humble heart rejoices at this achievement, and I am all the more moved to report it;
entries.literal: My foolish heart rejoices and claps hands; I all the more wish to set forth and state;

entries.zh: 兼前後聯官，一時皆逝，臣雖倖存，耄已將及，慮皇世大典，遂闕騰奏，不任下情，輒具載撰修始末，并職掌人、所成卷秩、條目之數，謹拜表以聞。
entries.en: Moreover, the officials who served before and after me have all passed away; though I alone survive, old age is already upon me. Fearing that this great canon of the imperial age might never be formally reported, and unable to suppress my earnest feeling, I have set forth in full the history of the compilation, the officials in charge, and the number of scrolls and articles completed, and respectfully submit this memorial for Your Majesty's notice.
entries.literal: Moreover, the officials connected before and after all passed away at one time; though your subject survives by fortune, old age is already approaching. Fearing that the great canon of the imperial age would thus lack a submitted memorial, unable to bear my lower feelings, I have fully recorded the beginning and end of compilation and revision, together with the persons in charge, the scroll sections completed, and the number of articles, and respectfully bow with this memorial to report.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「經禮大備，政典載弘，今詔有司，案以行事也。」
entries.en: An edict read: "The canonical rites are now fully complete, and the governmental canon greatly enriched. Let the responsible offices implement them in practice."
entries.literal: An edict stated: "The canonical rites are greatly complete, and the governmental canon is broadly enlarged. Now we order the responsible offices to follow them in conducting affairs."

entries.zh: 又詔曰：「勉表如此。
entries.en: Another edict read: "Mian's memorial is as stated.
entries.literal: Another edict stated: "Mian's memorial is as this.

entries.zh: 因革允𨤸，憲章孔備，功成業定，於是乎在。
entries.en: Reform and preservation duly balanced, statutes and patterns fully complete; the work accomplished and the enterprise settled — all is fulfilled here.
entries.literal: Changing and keeping what is suitable, statutes and patterns fully complete; achievement accomplished and enterprise settled — herein it lies.

entries.zh: 可以光被八表，施諸百代，俾萬世之下，知斯文在斯。
entries.en: It may shine across the eight directions and be handed down through a hundred generations, so that for ten thousand years to come men may know that this civilization endures here.
entries.literal: It can radiate to the eight directions, be applied through a hundred generations, so that beneath ten thousand generations men may know that this culture is here.

entries.zh: 主者其按以遵行，勿有失墜。」
entries.en: Let the responsible officials review it and carry it out; let nothing be allowed to fall away."
entries.literal: Let those in charge examine it and follow it; let nothing be lost or neglected."

entries.zh: 尋加中書令，給親信二十人。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was further appointed Director of the Secretariat and granted twenty personal attendants.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was additionally appointed Director of the Secretariat and granted twenty personal attendants.

entries.zh: 勉以疾自陳，求解內任。
entries.en: Mian pleaded illness in a memorial, asking to be relieved of his duties within the palace.
entries.literal: Mian, citing illness, submitted a memorial requesting release from inner-court duties.

entries.zh: 詔不許，乃令停下省，三日一朝，有事遣主書論決。
entries.en: The edict refused; instead he was told to stay at the Secretariat without daily attendance, appearing at court every three days while routine business was referred to chief clerks for deliberation and decision.
entries.literal: An edict did not permit it; instead he was ordered to remain at the Secretariat but cease daily attendance, coming to court every three days, with matters sent to chief clerks for discussion and decision.

entries.zh: 腳疾轉劇，久闕朝覲，固陳求解，詔乃賚假，須疾差還省。
entries.en: His foot ailment worsened, and after long absence from court he again pressed to resign; the emperor then granted him leave, with orders to return to office once he recovered.
entries.literal: His foot ailment grew worse; having long missed court audience, he repeatedly requested release; an edict then granted him leave, requiring return to the Secretariat once the illness improved.

entries.zh: 五禮之職，事有繁簡，及其列畢，不得同時。
entries.en: The work of the Five Rites varied in complexity, and the sections were completed at different times rather than all at once.
entries.literal: The duties of the Five Rites had affairs both complex and simple; when each was arranged and completed, they could not all be finished at the same time.

entries.zh: 《嘉禮儀注》以天監六年五月七日上尚書，合十有二秩，一百一十六卷，五百三十六條；
entries.en: The "Regulations and Commentaries on Celebratory Rites" was submitted to the Secretariat on the seventh day of the fifth month of the sixth year of Tianjian, comprising twelve sections, one hundred sixteen scrolls, and five hundred thirty-six articles;
entries.literal: "Regulations and Commentaries on Celebratory Rites" was submitted to the Secretariat on the seventh day of the fifth month of the sixth year of Tianjian, totaling twelve sections, one hundred sixteen scrolls, and five hundred thirty-six articles;

entries.zh: 《賓禮儀注》以天監六年五月二十日上尚書，合十有七秩，一百三十三卷，五百四十五條；
entries.en: The "Regulations and Commentaries on Guest Rites" was submitted on the twentieth day of the fifth month of the same year, comprising seventeen sections, one hundred thirty-three scrolls, and five hundred forty-five articles;
entries.literal: "Regulations and Commentaries on Guest Rites" was submitted to the Secretariat on the twentieth day of the fifth month of the sixth year of Tianjian, totaling seventeen sections, one hundred thirty-three scrolls, and five hundred forty-five articles;

entries.zh: 《軍禮儀注》以天監九年十月二十九日上尚書，合十有八秩，一百八十九卷，二百四十條；
entries.en: The "Regulations and Commentaries on Military Rites" was submitted on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth month of the ninth year of Tianjian, comprising eighteen sections, one hundred eighty-nine scrolls, and two hundred forty articles;
entries.literal: "Regulations and Commentaries on Military Rites" was submitted to the Secretariat on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth month of the ninth year of Tianjian, totaling eighteen sections, one hundred eighty-nine scrolls, and two hundred forty articles;

entries.zh: 《吉禮儀注》以天監十一年十一月十日上尚書，合二十有六秩，二百二十四卷，一千五條；
entries.en: The "Regulations and Commentaries on Auspicious Rites" was submitted on the tenth day of the eleventh month of the eleventh year of Tianjian, comprising twenty-six sections, two hundred twenty-four scrolls, and one thousand five articles;
entries.literal: "Regulations and Commentaries on Auspicious Rites" was submitted to the Secretariat on the tenth day of the eleventh month of the eleventh year of Tianjian, totaling twenty-six sections, two hundred twenty-four scrolls, and one thousand five articles;

entries.zh: 《凶禮儀注》以天監十一年十一月十七日上尚書，合四十有七秩，五百一十四卷，五千六百九十三條：大凡一百二十秩，一千一百七十六卷，八千一十九條。
entries.en: The "Regulations and Commentaries on Inauspicious Rites" was submitted on the seventeenth day of the eleventh month of the same year, comprising forty-seven sections, five hundred fourteen scrolls, and five thousand six hundred ninety-three articles — in all one hundred twenty sections, one thousand one hundred seventy-six scrolls, and eight thousand nineteen articles.
entries.literal: "Regulations and Commentaries on Inauspicious Rites" was submitted to the Secretariat on the seventeenth day of the eleventh month of the eleventh year of Tianjian, totaling forty-seven sections, five hundred fourteen scrolls, and five thousand six hundred ninety-three articles: in all one hundred twenty sections, one thousand one hundred seventy-six scrolls, and eight thousand nineteen articles.

entries.zh: 又列副秘閣及《五經》典書各一通，繕寫校定，以普通五年二月始獲洗畢。
entries.en: Duplicate sets were also prepared for the Secret Archive and for the Keeper of the "Five Classics," one copy each. Copying and collation were completed, and fair copies were finally finished in the second month of the fifth year of Putong.
entries.literal: Copies were also arranged for the Secret Archive and for the Keeper of the "Five Classics," one set each; copying, writing, and collation were completed, and in the second month of the fifth year of Putong they were finally finished in clean form.

entries.zh: 余雪泣而答曰：「彭殤之達義，延吳之雅言，亦常聞之矣；
entries.en: I wiped away my tears and replied: "I too have often heard the wisdom of viewing long life and early death alike, and the noble words of Yanling Jizi and Dongmen Wu;
entries.literal: I answered, wiping away my tears: "I too have often heard the enlightened teaching concerning Pengzu and the short-lived, and the refined words of Yanling Jizi and Dongmen Wu;

entries.zh: 顧所以未能弭意者，請陳其說。
entries.en: yet why I cannot calm my heart — let me explain.
entries.literal: yet why I cannot quiet my mind — allow me to set forth my reason.

entries.zh: 夫植樹階庭，欽柯葉之茂；
entries.en: Plant a tree in the courtyard and you delight in its leafy branches;
entries.literal: When one plants a tree in the courtyard, one delights in the fullness of branch and leaf;

entries.zh: 爲山累仞，惜覆簣之功。
entries.en: raise a mountain many ren high and you regret even one basket spilled.
entries.literal: building a mountain to many ren, one cherishes even the work of a basket overturned.

entries.zh: 故秀而不實，尼父爲之歎息；
entries.en: That is why Confucius sighed over 'flowering without fruit';
entries.literal: Thus 'flowering yet bearing no fruit' — the Master sighed for it;

entries.zh: 析彼歧路，楊子所以留連。
entries.en: and why Yangzi lingered at the parting of the roads.
entries.literal: parting at the forked road — Yangzi lingered therefore.

entries.zh: 事有可深，聖賢靡抑。
entries.en: When feeling runs deep, even sages do not forbid it.
entries.literal: When a matter admits of deep feeling, even sages do not restrain it.

entries.zh: 今吾所悲，亦以悱始逾立歲，孝悌之至，自幼而長，文章之美，得之天然，好學不倦，居無塵雜，多所著述，盈帙滿笥，淡然得失之際，不見喜慍之容。
entries.en: What I mourn is that Fei had just passed thirty: filial and fraternal from childhood, gifted in letters by nature, tireless in study, living without worldly clutter, writing until scrolls and cases overflowed, calm in gain and loss, never showing joy or anger on his face.
entries.literal: What I mourn is this: Fei had just passed thirty; filial piety and brotherly respect reached their height, growing from childhood; literary grace came by nature; he loved learning without weariness; his dwelling was free of worldly dust; he wrote extensively, scrolls and cases overflowing; in the face of gain and loss he was tranquil, showing neither joy nor anger.

entries.zh: 及翰飛東朝，參伍盛列，其所遊往，皆一時才俊，賦詩頌詠，終日忘疲。
entries.en: When he rose in the Eastern Court and stood among the foremost, those he kept company with were the finest men of the day; composing and reciting poetry, he forgot weariness from morning to night.
entries.literal: When he took wing in the Eastern Court, ranking among the foremost, those he consorted with were all talents of the age; composing and chanting poetry, he forgot fatigue all day long.

entries.zh: 每從容謂吾以遭逢時來，位隆任要，當應推賢下士，先物後身，然後可以報恩明主，克保元吉。
entries.en: He would calmly tell me that having risen in fortunate times to high rank and heavy responsibility, one must promote the worthy, defer to men of talent, and put others first — only then could one repay the enlightened sovereign and keep fortune secure.
entries.literal: He would calmly tell me that having met with the times and risen to high rank and weighty duty, one should promote the worthy and defer to gentlemen, putting others before oneself — only then could one repay the enlightened lord and secure great fortune.

entries.zh: 俾余二紀之中，忝竊若是，幸無大過者，繄此子之助焉。
entries.en: That in twenty years I have held such rank unworthily yet avoided great fault — I owe to this son.
entries.literal: That in two decades I have undeservedly held such rank yet fortunately committed no great fault — it was through this son's help.

entries.zh: 自出閩區，政存清靜，冀其旋反，少慰衰暮，言念今日，眇然長往。
entries.en: Since he left for Min, his rule was quiet and clean; I hoped for his return to comfort my old age — but today he is gone forever.
entries.literal: Since he left for Min lands, his governance was marked by quiet purity; I hoped for his return to comfort my declining years — thinking of today, he has departed forever.

entries.zh: 加以闔棺千里之外，未知歸骨之期，雖復無情之倫，庸詎不痛於昔！
entries.en: And now the coffin is sealed a thousand li away, with no knowing when his bones will return — even the hardest heart could not but grieve as men have always grieved!
entries.literal: Added to this, the coffin is closed a thousand li away; the day of returning his bones is unknown — though one were utterly without feeling, how could one not grieve as in times past!

entries.zh: 夷甫孩抱中物，尚盡慟以待賓；
entries.en: Wang Yan, for a child still in swaddling clothes, mourned fully before receiving guests;
entries.literal: Xiangfu, for a child still in arms, yet fully mourned to receive guests;

entries.zh: 安仁未及七旬，猶殷勤於詞賦。
entries.en: Pan An, before seventy days had passed, still poured his grief into verse.
entries.literal: Anren, before seventy days had passed, still poured feeling into rhapsodies.

entries.zh: 況夫名立宦成，半途而廢者，亦焉可已已哉。
entries.en: How much more when name and office were established and then cut short midway — how can grief be stilled!
entries.literal: How much more when fame is established and office achieved, yet cut off midway — how can grief be restrained!

entries.zh: 求其此懷，可謂苗實之義。
entries.en: Measured by that feeling, this may be called the grief of the bud that never bore fruit.
entries.literal: Seeking this feeling, one may call it the meaning of the budding and the fruit.

entries.zh: 諸賢旣貽格言，喻以大理，卽日輟哀，命駕修職事焉。」
entries.en: When my friends had offered their wise counsel and explained the larger principle, I ceased mourning that very day, took up my carriage, and returned to my official duties."
entries.literal: The worthies having bestowed maxims and instructed me in the great principle, that very day I ceased mourning, ordered my carriage, and returned to my official duties."

entries.zh: 中大通三年，又以疾自陳，移授特進、右光祿大夫、侍中、中衛將軍，置佐史，餘如故。
entries.en: In Zhongdatong 3, Mian again submitted a statement because of illness, and was transferred to Specially Advanced, Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and General of the Central Guard, with staff officers established for him; the rest remained as before.
entries.literal: In Zhongdatong 3, Mian again submitted a statement because of illness, and was transferred to Specially Advanced, Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and General of the Central Guard, with staff officers established for him; the rest remained as before.

entries.zh: 增親信四十人。
entries.en: His trusted attendants were increased by forty.
entries.literal: His trusted attendants were increased by forty.

entries.zh: 兩宮參問，冠蓋結轍；
entries.en: The two palaces sent inquiries, and the tracks of capped carriages joined one another;
entries.literal: The two palaces sent inquiries, and the tracks of capped carriages joined one another;

entries.zh: 服膳醫藥，皆資天府。
entries.en: his clothing, meals, medicine, and drugs were all supplied from the imperial treasury.
entries.literal: his clothing, meals, medicine, and drugs were all supplied from the imperial treasury.

entries.zh: 有敕每欲臨幸，勉以拜伏有虧，頻啓停出，詔許之，遂停輿駕。
entries.en: Whenever there was an edict intending to visit him, Mian, because he could not properly bow and prostrate himself, repeatedly petitioned that the outing be stopped. The edict permitted it, and the imperial carriage was therefore halted.
entries.literal: Whenever there was an edict intending to visit him, Mian, because he could not properly bow and prostrate himself, repeatedly petitioned that the outing be stopped. The edict permitted it, and the imperial carriage was therefore halted.

entries.zh: 大同元年，卒，時年七十。
entries.en: In Datong 1, he died, aged seventy.
entries.literal: In Datong 1, he died, aged seventy.

entries.zh: 高祖聞而流涕，卽日車駕臨殯，乃詔贈特進、右光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，餘並如故。
entries.en: When Gaozu heard, he shed tears, and that same day the imperial carriage visited the bier. An edict then posthumously granted Mian the offices of Specially Advanced, Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and Opening Office with Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies, with the rest all as before.
entries.literal: When Gaozu heard, he shed tears, and that same day the imperial carriage visited the bier. An edict then posthumously granted Mian the offices of Specially Advanced, Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and Opening Office with Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies, with the rest all as before.

entries.zh: 給東園秘器，朝服一具，衣一襲。
entries.en: He was supplied an imperial coffin from Dongyuan, one set of court robes, and one suit of clothes.
entries.literal: He was supplied an imperial coffin from Dongyuan, one set of court robes, and one suit of clothes.

entries.zh: 贈錢二十萬，布百匹。
entries.en: He was granted two hundred thousand cash and one hundred bolts of cloth.
entries.literal: He was granted two hundred thousand cash and one hundred bolts of cloth.

entries.zh: 皇太子亦舉哀朝堂。
entries.en: The crown prince also held mourning for him in the court hall.
entries.literal: The crown prince also held mourning for him in the court hall.

entries.zh: 諡曰簡肅公。
entries.en: His posthumous title was Duke Jiansu.
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Duke Jiansu.

entries.zh: 梁書卷第二十五 列傳第十九
entries.en: Book of Liang, Volume 25, Biographies, Number 19
entries.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 25, Biographies 19

entries.zh: 先是御史中丞劉休薦昭於武帝，永明初，以昭爲南郡王侍讀。
entries.en: Earlier Censor-in-Chief Liu Xiu had recommended Zhao to Emperor Wu; at the start of Yongming he was made tutor to the Prince of Nanjun.
entries.literal: Earlier the Censor-in-Chief Liu Xiu had recommended Zhao to Emperor Wu; at the beginning of Yongming Zhao was made tutor to the Prince of Nanjun.

entries.zh: 王嗣帝位，故時臣隸爭求權寵，惟昭及南陽宗夬，保身守正，無所參入，竟不罹其禍。
entries.en: When the prince ascended the throne, former retainers fought for favor and power; only Zhao and Zong Que of Nanyang kept their integrity and stayed aloof, and in the end they escaped the purge.
entries.literal: When the prince succeeded to the throne, former retainers scrambled for power and favor; only Zhao and Zong Que of Nanyang kept themselves upright and took no part, and in the end they did not suffer the calamity.

entries.zh: 明帝踐阼，引昭爲中書通事舍人。
entries.en: When Emperor Ming acceded, he brought Zhao in as Secretariat Attendant for Current Affairs.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne he brought Zhao in as Secretariat Attendant for Current Affairs.

entries.zh: 時居此職者，皆勢傾天下，昭獨廉靜，無所干豫。
entries.en: Others in that office wielded power over the realm; Zhao alone remained incorrupt and withdrawn, interfering in nothing.
entries.literal: Those who held this post at the time all bent the world to their power; Zhao alone was pure and quiet, meddling in nothing.

entries.zh: 器服率陋，身安粗糲。
entries.en: His furnishings and dress were plain; he was content with coarse food.
entries.literal: His implements and dress were plain and shabby; he was content with coarse fare.

entries.zh: 常插燭於板床，明帝聞之，賜漆合燭盤等，敕曰：「卿有古人之風，故賜卿古人之物。」
entries.en: He would stick a candle into a plank bed; when Emperor Ming heard of it he sent a lacquered candle box and tray, writing: “You have the spirit of the ancients, so I give you the furnishings of the ancients.”
entries.literal: He would often stick a candle into a plank bed; when Emperor Ming heard of this he granted him a lacquered candle box and tray, with an order saying, “You have the manner of the ancients, so I grant you the things of the ancients.”

entries.zh: 累遷車騎臨海王記室參軍，長水校尉，太子家令，驃騎晉安王諮議參軍。
entries.en: He rose through recorder to the Cavalry General Prince of Linhai, Commandant of the Changshui Guard, Director of the Heir Apparent’s Household, and staff adviser to the Rapid Cavalry Prince of Jin’an.
entries.literal: He was promoted in succession to recorder on the staff of the Cavalry General Prince of Linhai, Commandant of the Changshui Guard, Director of the Heir Apparent’s Household, and staff adviser to the Rapid Cavalry Prince of Jin’an.

entries.zh: 尋除尚書左丞、本州大中正。
entries.en: Soon he was made Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs and chief arbiter of his home province.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs and chief arbiter of his native province.

entries.zh: 高祖素悉昭能，建康城平，引爲驃騎錄事參軍。
entries.en: The High Ancestor had long known Zhao’s gifts; when Jiankang fell he brought him in as recording officer on the Rapid Cavalry staff.
entries.literal: The High Ancestor had long known Zhao’s ability; when Jiankang was pacified he brought him in as recording officer on the staff of the Rapid Cavalry General.

entries.zh: 梁臺建，遷給事黃門侍郎，領著作郎，頃之，兼御史中丞，黃門、著作、中正並如故。
entries.en: When the Liang provisional government was set up he became Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate and Director of the History Office; soon he also served as Censor-in-Chief while keeping his Yellow Gate, History Office, and arbiter posts.
entries.literal: When the Liang headquarters was established he was transferred to Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate and concurrently Director of the History Office; soon after he also served as Censor-in-Chief, retaining his posts at the Yellow Gate, the History Office, and as chief arbiter.

entries.zh: 天監三年，兼五兵尚書，參選事，四年，卽真。
entries.en: In Tianjian year 3 he also served as Minister of the Five Arms and took part in appointments; in year 4 he received the full title.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tianjian he concurrently held the post of Minister of the Five Arms and took part in selections; in the fourth year he received the full appointment.

entries.zh: 六年，徙爲左民尚書，未拜，出爲建威將軍、平南安成王長史、尋陽太守。
entries.en: In year 6 he was transferred to Minister of the Left People; before taking the seal he was sent out as General Who Establishes Might, chief clerk to the Prince of Ancheng (General Who Pacifies the South), and administrator of Xunyang.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he was moved to Minister of the Left People; before he received the seal he went out as General Who Establishes Might, chief clerk to the Prince of Ancheng, General Who Pacifies the South, and Administrator of Xunyang.

entries.zh: 七年，入爲振遠將軍、中權長史。
entries.en: In year 7 he returned as General Who Quells the Distance and chief clerk of the Central Guard.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he entered as General Who Quells the Distance and chief clerk of the Central Guard.

entries.zh: 八年，遷通直散騎常侍，領步兵校尉，復領本州大中正。
entries.en: In year 8 he became Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Commandant of the Footsoldiers, resuming his post as chief arbiter of his home province.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Regular Attendant of Direct Communication, concurrently Commandant of the Footsoldiers, and again held the chief arbiter’s post for his native province.

entries.zh: 十年，復爲左民尚書。
entries.en: In year 10 he again became Minister of the Left People.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he again became Minister of the Left People.

entries.zh: 映字徽遠，昭弟也。
entries.en: Ying, styled Huiyuan, was Zhao’s younger brother.
entries.literal: Ying, courtesy name Huiyuan, was Zhao’s younger brother.

entries.zh: 三歲而孤。
entries.en: He was orphaned at the age of three.
entries.literal: He was orphaned at three.

entries.zh: 兄弟友睦，修身厲行，非禮不行。
entries.en: The brothers lived in warm accord, disciplined in conduct and strict in observance; nothing contrary to ritual was permitted.
entries.literal: The brothers were friendly and harmonious, cultivating the person and strict in conduct; what was not ritual they would not do.

entries.zh: 始昭之守臨海，陸倕餞之，賓主俱歡，日昏不反，映以昭年高，不可連夜極樂，乃自往迎候，同乘而歸，兄弟並已斑白，時人美而服焉。
entries.en: When Zhao first took office at Linhai, Lu Chui gave him a farewell feast; host and guests made merry until dusk, and Zhao did not return. Ying thought his elder brother, at his age, should not carouse all night; he went to fetch him himself, and they rode home together—both already gray-haired. Contemporaries admired and revered the deed.
entries.literal: When Zhao first became administrator of Linhai, Lu Chui gave him a farewell feast; host and guests were all merry, and at dusk he did not return. Ying thought that Zhao, being advanced in years, ought not to revel through the night to excess, and so went himself to meet him; they rode back together. Both brothers’ hair was already streaked with white, and people of the time admired and submitted to this.

entries.zh: 及昭卒，映喪之如父，年逾七十，哀戚過禮，服制雖除，每言輒感慟。
entries.en: When Zhao died, Ying mourned him as a father; though over seventy, his grief exceeded the prescribed rites, and even after the mourning period ended, speech would still move him to tears.
entries.literal: When Zhao died, Ying mourned him as for a father; though past seventy, his grief exceeded the rites; though the mourning garments were laid aside, whenever he spoke he was moved to sorrow.

entries.zh: 映泛涉記傳，有文才，而不以篇什自命。
entries.en: Ying read widely in histories and chronicles and had literary gifts, yet he did not claim the name of poet.
entries.literal: Ying read widely in histories and chronicles, possessed literary talent, yet did not style himself a poet.

entries.zh: 少時與劉繪、蕭琛相友善，繪之爲南康相，映時爲府丞，文教多令具草。
entries.en: In youth he was close to Liu Hui and Xiao Chen; when Hui became administrator of Nankang and Ying served as his commandery aide, Hui often had him draft official documents.
entries.literal: In youth he was close friends with Liu Hui and Xiao Chen; when Hui became Administrator of Nankang, Ying was at the time a commandery aide, and for many documents of culture and instruction Hui had him draft them.

entries.zh: 褚彥回聞而悅之，乃屈與子賁等遊處。
entries.en: Chu Yanhui heard of him with pleasure and allowed him to keep company with his son Ben and the like.
entries.literal: Chu Yanhui heard of this and was pleased; he then condescended to let him associate with his son Ben and others.

entries.zh: 年未弱冠，彥回欲令仕，映以昭未解褐，固辭，須昭仕乃官。
entries.en: Before he was twenty Yanhui wished him to take office, but Ying refused firmly while Zhao had not yet entered service; he would not take rank until his brother did.
entries.literal: Before he had reached twenty, Yanhui wished to have him enter office; Ying, because Zhao had not yet taken up the official robe, firmly declined, saying he must wait until Zhao took office before he himself would serve.

entries.zh: 永元元年，參鎮軍江夏王軍事，出爲武康令。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongyuan he served on the staff of the Pacification General, Prince of Jiangxia, and was sent out as magistrate of Wukang.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan he served on the staff of the Pacification General, Prince of Jiangxia, and went out as magistrate of Wukang.

entries.zh: 及高祖師次建康，吳興太守袁昂自謂門世忠貞，固守誠節，乃訪於映曰：「卿謂時事云何？」
entries.en: When the High Ancestor’s army reached Jiankang, Yuan Ang, administrator of Wuxing, believing his house loyal through generations, clung to his oath of fealty and asked Ying, “What do you make of the times?”
entries.literal: When the High Ancestor’s army halted at Jiankang, Yuan Ang, Administrator of Wuxing, considering his family loyal through generations, held fast to sincere constancy, and so consulted Ying, saying, “What do you think of the present situation?”

entries.zh: 映答曰：「元嘉之末，開闢未有，故太尉殺身以明節，司徒當寄託之重，理無苟全，所以不顧夷險，以殉名義。
entries.en: Ying replied, “At the end of Yuanjia the succession was unsettled; the Grand Marshal gave his life to prove his loyalty, and the Minister over the Masses bore the burden of the realm—there was no saving himself—so he faced every peril for duty and honor.
entries.literal: Ying answered, “At the end of Yuanjia the mandate was not yet settled, and so the Grand Marshal gave his life to clarify integrity; the Minister over the Masses bore the weight of entrustment—reason allowed no selfish preservation—hence he did not regard hardship or ease and died for righteousness and fame.

entries.zh: 今嗣主昏虐，狎近羣小，親賢誅戮，君子道消，外難屢作，曾無悛改。
entries.en: Today the heir is cruel and benighted, fond of petty men, slaying kin and worthies; the way of the gentleman has waned, troubles multiply from without, and he will not mend his ways.
entries.literal: Now the successor lord is benighted and cruel, intimate with petty men, executing kin and worthies; the way of the gentleman has faded; external troubles arise again and again, yet there has never been repentance.

entries.zh: 今荊、雍協舉，乘據上流，背昏向明，勢無不濟。
entries.en: Now Jing and Yong have risen together, holding the upper Yangzi; turning from darkness to light, their cause cannot fail.
entries.literal: Now Jing and Yong rise together, holding the upper reaches of the river; turning from darkness toward light, the momentum cannot fail to succeed.

entries.zh: 百姓思治，天人之意可知；
entries.en: The people yearn for peace—the will of Heaven and of men is plain;
entries.literal: The people long for order; the intent of Heaven and man can be known;

entries.zh: 旣明且哲，忠孝之途無爽。
entries.en: to be clear-sighted and wise is to keep the path of loyalty and filial piety unclouded.
entries.literal: being both bright and wise, the path of loyalty and filial piety is without error.

entries.zh: 願明府更當雅慮，無祇悔也。」
entries.en: May Your Excellency weigh this carefully and not repent too late.”
entries.literal: May Your Excellency reconsider with refined deliberation and not come to regret only afterward.”

entries.zh: 尋以公事免。
entries.en: Soon after he was removed from office on official grounds.
entries.literal: Soon he was dismissed on public grounds.

entries.zh: 天監初，除征虜鄱陽王參軍，建安王中權錄事參軍，領軍長史，烏程令。
entries.en: Early in Tianjian he became staff officer to the Pacification General Prince of Poyang, recording officer on Prince Jian’an’s Central Guard staff, chief clerk of the Army Director, and magistrate of Wucheng.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he was appointed staff officer to the Pacification General Prince of Poyang, recording officer on the staff of the Central Guard of Prince Jian’an, chief clerk of the Army Director, and magistrate of Wucheng.

entries.zh: 所受俸祿，悉歸于兄。
entries.en: Every stipend he received he turned over to his brother.
entries.literal: All salary he received he gave entirely to his elder brother.

entries.zh: 復爲臨川王錄事參軍，南臺治書，安成王錄事，太子翊軍校尉，累遷中散大夫、光祿卿，太中大夫。
entries.en: He later served as recording officer to the Prince of Linchuan, drafter for the Southern Office, recording officer to the Prince of Ancheng, and Commandant of the Heir Apparent’s Guard, rising through Palace Gentleman, Chamberlain for Ceremonials, and Grand Master of the Palace.
entries.literal: He again served as recording officer on the staff of the Prince of Linchuan, drafting documents for the Southern Office, recording officer to the Prince of Ancheng, and Commandant of the Heir Apparent’s Guard; he was promoted in succession to Palace Gentleman, Chamberlain for Ceremonials, and Grand Master of the Palace.

entries.zh: 大同五年，卒，年八十三。
entries.en: In Datong year 5 he died, aged eighty-three.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Datong he died at the age of eighty-three.

entries.zh: 子弘。
entries.en: His son was Hong.
entries.literal: His son was Hong.

entries.zh: 琛少而朗悟，有縱橫才辯。
entries.en: Chen was quick-witted from youth and possessed a debater’s eloquence.
entries.literal: Chen in youth was bright and perceptive, with talent for free-ranging debate.

entries.zh: 起家齊太學博士。
entries.en: He began his career as Erudite of the Qi Imperial University.
entries.literal: He first entered office as Erudite of the Qi Imperial University.

entries.zh: 時王儉當朝，琛年少，未爲儉所識，負其才氣，欲候儉。
entries.en: Wang Jian then dominated the court; Chen was young and unknown to him, but confident in his gifts and determined to seek him out.
entries.literal: At the time Wang Jian held the court; Chen was young and had not yet been noticed by Jian; relying on his talent and spirit, he wished to wait upon Jian.

entries.zh: 時儉宴于樂游苑，琛乃著虎皮靴，策桃枝杖，直造儉坐，儉與語，大悅。
entries.en: When Jian was feasting in the Leyou Gardens, Chen appeared in tiger-skin boots, leaning on a peach-branch staff, and walked straight to Jian’s seat; Jian spoke with him and was delighted.
entries.literal: When Jian was feasting in the Leyou Gardens, Chen put on tiger-skin boots, took a peach-branch staff, and went straight to Jian’s seat; Jian spoke with him and was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 儉爲丹陽尹，辟爲主簿，舉爲南徐州秀才，累遷司徒記室。
entries.en: When Jian became governor of Danyang he made Chen his chief clerk, nominated him as southern Xu’s distinguished graduate, and promoted him to recorder on the Grand Tutor’s staff.
entries.literal: When Jian became Governor of Danyang he appointed Chen chief clerk, recommended him as the distinguished graduate of southern Xu, and promoted him in succession to recorder on the Grand Tutor’s staff.

entries.zh: 東昏初嗣立，時議以無廟見之典，琛議據《周頌烈文》、《閔予》皆爲卽位朝廟之典，於是從之。
entries.en: When Donghun first succeeded to the throne, the court debated that there was no precedent for presenting himself in the ancestral temple. Chen argued on the basis of the Zhou hymns "Liewen" and "Minyu," both of which were precedents for going to court in the temple at accession, and this was followed.
entries.literal: When Donghun first succeeded to the throne, the court debated that there was no precedent for presenting himself in the ancestral temple. Chen argued on the basis of the Zhou hymns "Liewen" and "Minyu," both of which were precedents for going to court in the temple at accession, and this was followed.

entries.zh: 高祖定京邑，引爲驃騎諮議，領錄事，遷給事黃門侍郎。
entries.en: After Gaozu pacified the capital, he brought Chen in as advisory aide to the General of Agile Cavalry, concurrently recorder, and Chen was promoted to Yellow Gate Gentleman for Service.
entries.literal: After Gaozu pacified the capital, he brought Chen in as advisory aide to the General of Agile Cavalry, concurrently recorder, and Chen was promoted to Yellow Gate Gentleman for Service.

entries.zh: 梁臺建，爲御史中丞。
entries.en: When the Liang administration was established, he became Palace Assistant Censor.
entries.literal: When the Liang administration was established, he became Palace Assistant Censor.

entries.zh: 天監元年，遷庶子，出爲宣城太守。
entries.en: In Tianjian 1, he was transferred to crown prince attendant, then went out as administrator of Xuancheng.
entries.literal: In Tianjian 1, he was transferred to crown prince attendant, then went out as administrator of Xuancheng.

entries.zh: 徵爲衛尉卿，俄遷員外散騎常侍。
entries.en: He was summoned as Commandant of the Guards and soon transferred to Supernumerary Regular Attendant.
entries.literal: He was summoned as Commandant of the Guards and soon transferred to Supernumerary Regular Attendant.

entries.zh: 三年，除太子中庶子、散騎常侍。
entries.en: In the third year, he was appointed Household Attendant to the Crown Prince and Regular Attendant.
entries.literal: In the third year, he was appointed Household Attendant to the Crown Prince and Regular Attendant.

entries.zh: 九年，出爲寧遠將軍、平西長史、江夏太守。
entries.en: In the ninth year, he went out as General Who Pacifies the Distant, chief clerk to the General Who Pacifies the West, and administrator of Jiangxia.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, he went out as General Who Pacifies the Distant, chief clerk to the General Who Pacifies the West, and administrator of Jiangxia.

entries.zh: 高祖在西邸，早與琛狎，每朝宴，接以舊恩，呼爲宗老。
entries.en: When the High Ancestor was still in the Western Quarters he had long been close to Chen; at court banquets he treated him with old affection and called him “clan elder.”
entries.literal: When the High Ancestor was in the Western Quarters he had long been intimate with Chen; at every court banquet he received him with old favor and called him “elder of the clan.”

entries.zh: 琛亦奉陳昔恩，以「早簉中陽，夙忝同閈，雖迷興運，猶荷洪慈。」
entries.en: Chen also voiced his gratitude for past kindness: “Long ago I stood in your company at Zhongyang; from the first I was honored to share your household; though I strayed when fortune turned, I still owe your great grace.”
entries.literal: Chen also offered thanks for past kindness, saying, “Long ago I took my place at Zhongyang; from of old I have been honored to share your gate; though I lost my way in the rise of fortune, I still bear your great kindness.”

entries.zh: 上答曰：「雖云早契闊，乃自非同志；
entries.en: The emperor replied, “You speak of an early bond, yet we were never truly kindred spirits;
entries.literal: The emperor answered, “Though you speak of an early bond, we were never truly of one mind;

entries.zh: 勿談興運初，且道狂奴異。」
entries.en: say nothing of how fortune began—tell instead how the mad servant was unlike the rest.”
entries.literal: do not speak of the beginning of the rise of fortune—rather tell how the mad servant was strange.”

entries.zh: 大通二年，爲金紫光祿大夫，加特進，給親信三十人。
entries.en: In Datong 2, Chen became Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, was additionally made Specially Advanced, and was given thirty trusted attendants.
entries.literal: In Datong 2, Chen became Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, was additionally made Specially Advanced, and was given thirty trusted attendants.

entries.zh: 中大通元年，爲雲麾將軍、晉陵太守，秩中二千石。
entries.en: In Zhongdatong 1, he became Cloud Banner General and administrator of Jinling, with rank of middle two-thousand bushels.
entries.literal: In Zhongdatong 1, he became Cloud Banner General and administrator of Jinling, with rank of middle two-thousand bushels.

entries.zh: 以疾自解，改授侍中、特進、金紫光祿大夫。
entries.en: Because of illness he requested release from office and was reassigned as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Specially Advanced, and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
entries.literal: Because of illness he requested release from office and was reassigned as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Specially Advanced, and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.

entries.zh: 卒，年五十二。
entries.en: He died at the age of fifty-two.
entries.literal: He died at the age of fifty-two.

entries.zh: 遺令諸子，與妻同墳異藏，祭以蔬菜，葬日止車十乘，事存率素。
entries.en: In his final instructions to his sons, he ordered that he and his wife share one mound but have separate burials, that sacrifices use vegetables, and that on the burial day there be only ten carriages, keeping the affair simple and plain.
entries.literal: In his final instructions to his sons, he ordered that he and his wife share one mound but have separate burials, that sacrifices use vegetables, and that on the burial day there be only ten carriages, keeping the affair simple and plain.

entries.zh: 乘輿臨哭甚哀。
entries.en: The emperor came to visit and mourn him with deep grief.
entries.literal: The emperor came to visit and mourn him with deep grief.

entries.zh: 詔贈本官，加雲麾將軍，給東園秘器，朝服一具，衣一襲，賻錢二十萬，布百匹。
entries.en: An edict posthumously granted him his former offices, additionally made him Cloud Banner General, and supplied an imperial coffin from Dongyuan, one set of court robes, one suit of clothes, funeral gifts of two hundred thousand cash, and one hundred bolts of cloth.
entries.literal: An edict posthumously granted him his former offices, additionally made him Cloud Banner General, and supplied an imperial coffin from Dongyuan, one set of court robes, one suit of clothes, funeral gifts of two hundred thousand cash, and one hundred bolts of cloth.

entries.zh: 諡曰平子。
entries.en: His posthumous title was Pingzi.
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Pingzi.

entries.zh: 杲少好學，工書畫，舅張融有高名，杲風韻舉動，頗類於融，時稱之曰：「無對日下，惟舅與甥。」
entries.en: Gao loved learning from youth and was skilled at calligraphy and painting. His maternal uncle Zhang Rong had a great reputation, and Gao's style, bearing, and movements much resembled Rong, so people of the time said, "There are no equals under the sun, only uncle and nephew."
entries.literal: Gao loved learning from youth and was skilled at calligraphy and painting. His maternal uncle Zhang Rong had a great reputation, and Gao's style, bearing, and movements much resembled Rong, so people of the time said, "There are no equals under the sun, only uncle and nephew."

entries.zh: 起家齊中軍法曹行參軍，太子舍人，衛軍王儉主簿。
entries.en: He began office as acting law bureau staff officer in Qi's Central Army, then served as crown prince attendant and chief clerk to Wang Jian, General of the Guard.
entries.literal: He began office as acting law bureau staff officer in Qi's Central Army, then served as crown prince attendant and chief clerk to Wang Jian, General of the Guard.

entries.zh: 遷尚書殿中曹郎，拜日，八座丞郎並到上省交禮，而杲至晚，不及時刻，坐免官。
entries.en: He was promoted to gentleman of the Palace Section in the Department of State Affairs. On the day of his appointment, the Eight Seats, assistant directors, and gentlemen all came to the upper office to exchange courtesies, but Gao arrived late and missed the appointed time, and for this he was dismissed from office.
entries.literal: He was promoted to gentleman of the Palace Section in the Department of State Affairs. On the day of his appointment, the Eight Seats, assistant directors, and gentlemen all came to the upper office to exchange courtesies, but Gao arrived late and missed the appointed time, and for this he was dismissed from office.

entries.zh: 久之，以爲司徒竟陵王外兵參軍，遷征虜宜都王功曹史，驃騎晉安王諮議參軍，司徒從事中郎。
entries.en: After a long while, he was made external military aide to the Prince of Jingling, Minister over the Masses, then transferred to merit officer for the Prince of Yidu, General Who Subdues Captives, advisory army aide to the Prince of Jin'an, General of Agile Cavalry, and attendant gentleman to the Minister over the Masses.
entries.literal: After a long while, he was made external military aide to the Prince of Jingling, Minister over the Masses, then transferred to merit officer for the Prince of Yidu, General Who Subdues Captives, advisory army aide to the Prince of Jin'an, General of Agile Cavalry, and attendant gentleman to the Minister over the Masses.

entries.zh: 梁臺建，以爲驃騎記室參軍，遷相國西曹掾。
entries.en: When the Liang administration was established, he was made secretary aide to the General of Agile Cavalry and transferred to western bureau clerk to the Chancellor of State.
entries.literal: When the Liang administration was established, he was made secretary aide to the General of Agile Cavalry and transferred to western bureau clerk to the Chancellor of State.

entries.zh: 天監元年，除撫軍長史，母憂去職。
entries.en: In Tianjian 1, he was appointed chief clerk to the General Who Pacifies the Army, then left office to mourn his mother.
entries.literal: In Tianjian 1, he was appointed chief clerk to the General Who Pacifies the Army, then left office to mourn his mother.

entries.zh: 服闋，拜建威將軍、中軍臨川王諮議參軍，尋遷黃門侍郎，右軍安成王長史。
entries.en: When mourning ended, he was appointed General Who Establishes Might and advisory army aide to the Prince of Linchuan in the Central Army; soon he was transferred to Yellow Gate Gentleman and chief clerk to the Prince of Ancheng in the Right Army.
entries.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed General Who Establishes Might and advisory army aide to the Prince of Linchuan in the Central Army; soon he was transferred to Yellow Gate Gentleman and chief clerk to the Prince of Ancheng in the Right Army.

entries.zh: 五年，遷御史中丞。
entries.en: In the fifth year, he was promoted to Palace Assistant Censor.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, he was promoted to Palace Assistant Censor.

entries.zh: 杲性婞直，無所顧望。
entries.en: Gao was upright and unyielding, bowing to no one’s favor.
entries.literal: Gao’s nature was upright and unyielding; he looked to nothing in fear.

entries.zh: 山陰令虞肩在任，贓污數百萬，杲奏收治。
entries.en: Yu Jian, magistrate of Shanyin, had embezzled millions while in office; Gao memorialized for his arrest and trial.
entries.literal: Yu Jian, magistrate of Shanyin, while in office had embezzled several million; Gao memorialized to have him arrested and tried.

entries.zh: 中書舍人黃睦之以肩事託杲，杲不答。
entries.en: Huang Muzhi, a Secretariat Attendant, asked Gao to intervene in Jian’s case; Gao gave no answer.
entries.literal: Huang Muzhi, Secretariat Attendant, asked Gao to intervene in Jian’s case; Gao did not reply.

entries.zh: 高祖聞之，以問杲，杲答曰「有之」。
entries.en: When the High Ancestor heard of this he questioned Gao, who answered, “That is so.”
entries.literal: When the High Ancestor heard of this he questioned Gao; Gao answered, “It is so.”

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「卿識睦之不？」
entries.en: The High Ancestor asked, “Do you know Muzhi?”
entries.literal: The High Ancestor said, “Do you know Muzhi?”

entries.zh: 杲答曰：「臣不識其人。」
entries.en: Gao replied, “I do not know the man.”
entries.literal: Gao answered, “Your servant does not know the man.”

entries.zh: 時睦之在御側，上指示杲曰：「此人是也。」
entries.en: Muzhi was then at the emperor’s side; the emperor pointed and said, “This is he.”
entries.literal: At the time Muzhi was at the emperor’s side; the emperor pointed him out to Gao and said, “This is the man.”

entries.zh: 杲謂睦之曰：「君小人，何敢以罪人屬南司？」
entries.en: Gao said to Muzhi, “You petty fellow—how dare you hand a criminal over to the censorate?”
entries.literal: Gao said to Muzhi, “Sir, you are a petty man—how dare you entrust a criminal to the Southern Office?”

entries.zh: 睦之失色。
entries.en: Muzhi turned pale.
entries.literal: Muzhi turned pale.

entries.zh: 領軍將軍張稷，是杲從舅，杲嘗以公事彈稷，稷因侍宴訴高祖曰：「陸杲是臣通親，小事彈臣不貸。」
entries.en: Zhang Ji, the Army Director, was Gao’s collateral maternal uncle; Gao once impeached him on official grounds. At a banquet Ji complained to the High Ancestor: “Lu Gao is my close kinsman—over a trifle he impeached me and would show no mercy.”
entries.literal: The Army Director Zhang Ji was Gao’s collateral maternal uncle; Gao once impeached Ji on public grounds. At a banquet Ji complained to the High Ancestor, saying, “Lu Gao is my close kin; on a trifling matter he impeached me and would not spare me.”

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「杲職司其事，卿何得爲嫌！」
entries.en: The High Ancestor said, “Gao was doing his duty—how can you resent it!”
entries.literal: The High Ancestor said, “Gao’s office charged him with this duty—how can you hold a grudge!”

entries.zh: 杲在臺，號稱不畏強禦。
entries.en: At the Censorate Gao was known as one who did not fear the powerful.
entries.literal: At the Censorate Gao was known as one who did not fear the powerful.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：范岫、傅昭，並篤行清慎，善始令終，斯石建、石慶之徒矣。
entries.en: The historian writes: Fan Xiu and Fu Zhao were alike in steadfast conduct, purity, and caution, admirable from first to last—men in the mold of Shi Jian and Shi Qing.
entries.literal: The historian says: Fan Xiu and Fu Zhao alike were steadfast in conduct, pure and cautious, good in beginning and excellent in end—men of the type of Shi Jian and Shi Qing.

entries.zh: 蕭琛、陸杲俱以才學著名。
entries.en: Xiao Chen and Lu Gao were both renowned for talent and learning.
entries.literal: Xiao Chen and Lu Gao were both famed for talent and learning.

entries.zh: 琛朗悟辯捷，加諳究朝典，高祖在田，與琛遊舊，及踐天曆，任遇甚隆，美矣。
entries.en: Chen was quick-witted and eloquent and thoroughly versed in court precedent; the High Ancestor had known him in private life, and when he took the throne his favor was lavish—a fine thing indeed.
entries.literal: Chen was bright, perceptive, and quick in debate, and moreover thoroughly versed in court regulations; when the High Ancestor was still in the fields he had old ties of travel with Chen, and when he ascended the heavenly succession his favor and appointment were very lofty—beautiful indeed.

entries.zh: 杲性婞直，無所忌憚，旣而執法憲臺，糾繩不避權幸，可謂允茲正色。
entries.en: Gao was upright and fearless; at the Censorate he enforced the law without sparing the powerful—truly he wore the face of justice.
entries.literal: Gao’s nature was upright and unyielding, without dread; thereafter, wielding the law at the Censorate, he corrected and bound without avoiding the powerful and favored—one may say he truly bore the upright countenance.

entries.zh: 《詩》云：「彼己之子，邦之司直。」
entries.en: The Book of Songs says, “That man—he is the state’s upright judge.”
entries.literal: The Book of Songs says, “That other man—he is the upright judge of the state.”

entries.zh: 杲其有焉。
entries.en: In this, Gao surely had his part.
entries.literal: In this Gao had his share.

entries.en: [1] Endnote marker.
entries.literal: [1] Endnote marker.

entries.zh: 梁書卷第二十六 列傳第二十
entries.en: Book of Liang, Volume 26, Biographies, Number 20
entries.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 26, Biographies 20

entries.zh: 遷驃騎臨川王東曹掾。
entries.en: He was promoted to eastern bureau aide on the staff of the Rapid Cavalry General, Prince of Linchuan.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Eastern Bureau Aide under the Rapid Cavalry General, Prince of Linchuan.

entries.zh: 是時禮樂制度，多所創革，高祖雅愛倕才，乃敕撰《新漏刻銘》，其文甚美。
entries.en: At that time rites and music were being widely reformed; the emperor greatly valued Chui's talent and ordered him to compose the "Inscription on the New Clepsydra," a work of exceptional beauty.
entries.literal: At that time rites and music institutions were largely created anew and reformed; the High Ancestor greatly cherished Chui's talent and ordered him to compose "Inscription on the New Clepsydra," the text of which was very fine.

entries.zh: 遷太子中舍人，管東宮書記。
entries.en: He was promoted to palace attendant of the heir apparent and oversaw the Eastern Palace records.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant of the Heir Apparent and managed the Eastern Palace records.

entries.zh: 又詔爲《石闕銘記》。
entries.en: He was also ordered to compose the "Record-Inscription of the Stone Que."
entries.literal: He was again ordered to compose "Record-Inscription of the Stone Que."

entries.zh: 奏之。
entries.en: He presented it to the throne.
entries.literal: He presented it.

entries.zh: 敕曰：「太子中舍人陸倕所制《石闕銘》，辭義典雅，足爲佳作。
entries.en: An edict said: "The 'Inscription of the Stone Que' composed by Lu Chui, palace attendant of the heir apparent, is elegant in diction and meaning and fully qualifies as an excellent work.
entries.literal: An edict said: "The 'Inscription of the Stone Que' composed by Lu Chui, Palace Attendant of the Heir Apparent, is elegant in diction and meaning and fully qualifies as an excellent work.

entries.zh: 昔虞丘辨物，邯鄲獻賦，賞以金帛，前史美談，可賜絹三十匹。」
entries.en: Formerly Yuqiu distinguished things and Handan presented a fu, and they were rewarded with gold and silk—a fine tale in former histories. Grant him thirty bolts of silk."
entries.literal: Formerly Yuqiu distinguished things and Handan presented a fu, and they were rewarded with gold and silk—a fine tale in former histories. He may be granted thirty bolts of silk."

entries.zh: 遷太子庶子、國子博士，母憂去職。
entries.en: He was promoted to senior tutor of the heir apparent and erudite of the Imperial University, then left office to observe mourning for his mother.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Senior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Erudite of the Imperial University, then left office on account of his mother's mourning.

entries.zh: 服闋，爲中書侍郎，給事黃門侍郎，揚州別駕從事史，以疾陳解。
entries.en: When mourning ended he served as vice director of the Secretariat, attendant gentleman of the yellow gate, and aide to the Yangzhou administrator, then asked to resign on grounds of illness.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he served as Vice Director of the Secretariat, Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and Aide to the Yangzhou Administrator, then submitted a request to resign on grounds of illness.

entries.zh: 遷鴻臚卿，入爲吏部郎，參選事。
entries.en: He was promoted to grand master of ceremonies, then entered the capital as director of the Ministry of Personnel and took part in official selection.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Grand Master of Ceremonies, entered the capital as Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and participated in selection affairs.

entries.zh: 出爲雲麾晉安王長史、尋陽太守、行江州府州事。
entries.en: He left the capital as chief clerk to the Cloud-Banner General, Prince of Jin'an, as administrator of Xunyang and acting overseer of Jiangzhou affairs.
entries.literal: He went out as Chief Clerk to the Cloud-Banner General, Prince of Jin'an, Administrator of Xunyang, and acting overseer of Jiangzhou prefectural affairs.

entries.zh: 以公事免，左遷中書侍郎、司徒司馬、太子中庶子、廷尉卿。
entries.en: Dismissed over an official matter, he was demoted to Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat, Marshal for the Minister over the Masses, Junior Mentor in the heir apparent's household, and Chamberlain for Law Enforcement.
entries.literal: Dismissed over an official matter, he was demoted to Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat, Marshal for the Minister over the Masses, Junior Mentor in the heir apparent's household, and Chamberlain for Law Enforcement.

entries.zh: 又爲中庶子，加給事中、揚州大中正。
entries.en: He again served as junior tutor, with additional appointment as supervising attendant and senior rectifier of Yangzhou.
entries.literal: He again served as Junior Tutor, with additional appointment as Supervising Attendant and Senior Rectifier of Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 復除國子博士、中庶子、中正並如故。
entries.en: He was again appointed erudite of the Imperial University, junior tutor, and rectifier, all as before.
entries.literal: He was again appointed Erudite of the Imperial University, Junior Tutor, and Rectifier, all as before.

entries.zh: 守太常卿，中正如故。
entries.en: He served as acting minister of ceremonies, retaining his rectifier duties as before.
entries.literal: He served as Acting Minister of Ceremonies, with rectifier duties as before.

entries.zh: 普通七年，卒，年五十七。
entries.en: In the seventh year of Putong he died at the age of fifty-seven.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Putong he died, aged fifty-seven.

entries.zh: 文集二十卷，行於世。
entries.en: His collected writings in twenty fascicles circulated in his day.
entries.literal: His collected writings in twenty juan circulated in the world.

entries.zh: 天監初，沼、溉俱蒙擢用，洽尤見知賞，從弟沆亦相與齊名。
entries.en: Early in the Tianjian era Zhao and Gai were both promoted; Qia was especially favored, and his cousin Hang was equally renowned.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian Zhao and Gai were both promoted and employed; Qia was especially known and rewarded, and his younger cousin of the same clan Hang was likewise famed in equal measure.

entries.zh: 高祖問待詔丘遲曰：「到洽何如沆、溉？」
entries.en: The emperor asked the attendant-in-waiting Qiu Chi, "How does Dao Qia compare with Hang and Gai?"
entries.literal: The High Ancestor asked the Attendant-in-Waiting Qiu Chi, "How does Dao Qia compare with Hang and Gai?"

entries.zh: 遲對曰：「正清過於沆，文章不減溉；
entries.en: Chi replied, "In upright clarity he surpasses Hang; in literary composition he is no less than Gai;
entries.literal: Chi replied, "In upright clarity he surpasses Hang; in literary composition he does not fall short of Gai;

entries.zh: 加以清言，殆將難及。」
entries.en: and with pure talk added, he will perhaps be hard to match."
entries.literal: and with pure talk added, he will perhaps be hard to match."

entries.zh: 卽召爲太子舍人。
entries.en: He was immediately summoned as attendant of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: He was immediately summoned as Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 御華光殿，詔洽及沆、蕭琛、任昉侍讌，賦二十韻詩，以洽辭爲工，賜絹二十匹。
entries.en: At Huaguang Hall the emperor ordered Qia, Hang, Xiao Chen, and Ren Fang to attend a banquet; composing twenty-rhyme poems, the court judged Qia's diction the finest and granted him twenty bolts of silk.
entries.literal: At Huaguang Hall the emperor ordered Qia, Hang, Xiao Chen, and Ren Fang to attend the banquet; composing poems of twenty rhymes, Qia's diction was judged the most accomplished, and he was granted twenty bolts of silk.

entries.zh: 高祖謂昉曰：「諸到可謂才子。」
entries.en: The emperor said to Fang, "The various Daos may truly be called men of talent."
entries.literal: The High Ancestor said to Fang, "The various Daos may be called men of talent."

entries.zh: 昉對曰：「臣常竊議，宋得其武，梁得其文。」
entries.en: Fang replied, "Your servant has often privately remarked that Song obtained their martial men, while Liang obtains their literary men."
entries.literal: Fang replied, "Your servant has often privately remarked that Song obtained their martial men, while Liang obtains their literary men."

entries.zh: 山賓七歲能言名理，十三博通經傳，居喪盡禮。
entries.en: At seven Shanbin could discourse on principles of names; at thirteen he had broadly mastered the classics and their commentaries; in mourning he fulfilled every rite.
entries.literal: At seven Shanbin could discourse on principles of names; at thirteen he broadly mastered the classics and their commentaries; in mourning he fulfilled every rite.

entries.zh: 服闋，州辟從事史。
entries.en: When mourning ended the province summoned him as aide.
entries.literal: When mourning ended the province summoned him as Aide.

entries.zh: 起家奉朝請。
entries.en: He began his career as court gentleman for imperial audience.
entries.literal: He began his career as Court Gentleman for Imperial Audience.

entries.zh: 兄仲璋嬰痼疾，家道屢空，山賓乃行干祿。
entries.en: His elder brother Zhongzhang suffered a chronic illness; the household was repeatedly impoverished, and Shanbin then sought salary by office.
entries.literal: His elder brother Zhongzhang suffered a chronic illness; the household was repeatedly empty, and Shanbin then sought salary by office.

entries.zh: 齊始安王蕭遙光引爲撫軍行參軍，後爲廣陽令，頃之去官。
entries.en: The Prince of Shi'an of Qi, Xiao Yaoguang, brought him in as acting aide of the pacifying army; later he served as magistrate of Guangyang, and shortly left office.
entries.literal: The Prince of Shi'an of Qi, Xiao Yaoguang, brought him in as Acting Aide of the Pacifying Army; later he served as Magistrate of Guangyang, and shortly left office.

entries.zh: 義師至，高祖引爲相府田曹參軍。
entries.en: When the army of righteousness arrived, Emperor Wu brought him in as aide in the Fields Bureau of the Chancellor's Office.
entries.literal: When the army of righteousness arrived, the High Ancestor brought him in as Aide in the Fields Bureau of the Chancellor's Office.

entries.zh: 梁臺建，爲尚書駕部郎，遷治書侍御史，右軍記室參軍，掌治吉禮。
entries.en: When the Liang regime was established he served as director of the carriage section in the Secretariat, was promoted to attending censor, recorder of the right army, and oversaw auspicious rites.
entries.literal: When the Liang regime was established he served as Director of the Carriage Section in the Secretariat, was transferred to Attending Censor, Recorder of the Right Army, and oversaw auspicious rites.

entries.zh: 時初置《五經》博士，山賓首膺其選。
entries.en: At that time the Five Classics erudites were first established, and Shanbin was the first chosen.
entries.literal: At that time the Five Classics erudites were first established, and Shanbin was the first chosen.

entries.zh: 遷北中郎諮議參軍，侍皇太子讀。
entries.en: He was promoted to advisory aide of the north central commandant and attended the heir apparent in study.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Advisory Aide of the North Central Commandant and attended the Heir Apparent in study.

entries.zh: 累遷中書侍郎、國子博士、太子率更令、中庶子，博士如故。
entries.en: He rose through vice director of the Secretariat, erudite of the Imperial University, commandant of the heir apparent's rate regulation, and junior tutor, retaining his erudite duties as before.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat, Erudite of the Imperial University, Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Rate Regulation, and Junior Tutor, with erudite duties as before.

entries.zh: 天監十五年，出爲持節、督緣淮諸軍事、征遠將軍、北兗州刺史。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year of Tianjian he left the capital bearing the staff of authority as supervisor of military affairs along the Huai and as general who subdues the distance and inspector of Northern Yanzhou.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianjian he went out bearing the staff of authority as Supervisor of Military Affairs along the Huai and as General Who Subdues the Distance and Inspector of Northern Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 普通二年，徵爲太子右衛率，加給事中，遷御史中丞。
entries.en: In the second year of Putong he was summoned as right commandant of the heir apparent's guard, with additional appointment as supervising attendant, and promoted to palace censor-in-chief.
entries.literal: In the second year of Putong he was summoned as Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard, with additional appointment as Supervising Attendant, and transferred to Palace Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 以公事左遷黃門侍郎、司農卿。
entries.en: Demoted on account of a public matter, he became attendant of the yellow gate and minister of agriculture.
entries.literal: On account of public business he was demoted to the left as Attendant of the Yellow Gate and Minister of Agriculture.

entries.zh: 四年，遷散騎常侍，領青冀二州大中正。
entries.en: In the fourth year he was promoted to regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and concurrently senior rectifier of Qing and Ji provinces.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and concurrently Senior Rectifier of Qing and Ji provinces.

entries.zh: 東宮新置學士，又以山賓居之，俄以本官兼國子祭酒。
entries.en: The Eastern Palace newly appointed scholars, and Shanbin again held that post; soon, in his existing office, he concurrently served as libationer of the Imperial University.
entries.literal: The Eastern Palace newly appointed scholars, and Shanbin again held that post; soon, in his existing office, he concurrently served as Libationer of the Imperial University.

entries.zh: 七年，出爲鄱陽內史。
entries.en: In the seventh year he left the capital as internal administrator of Poyang.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he went out as Internal Administrator of Poyang.

entries.zh: 先是，郡民鮮于琛服食修道法，嘗入山采藥，拾得五色幡眊，又於地中得石璽，竊怪之。
entries.en: Earlier, a man of the commandery, Xianyu Chen, ingested elixirs and practiced the Way of cultivation; once entering the mountains to gather herbs he picked up a five-colored banner and cap, and also obtained a stone seal from the ground, privately marveling at it.
entries.literal: Earlier, a man of the commandery, Xianyu Chen, ingested elixirs and practiced the Way of cultivation; once entering the mountains to gather herbs he picked up a five-colored banner and cap, and also obtained a stone seal from the ground, privately marveling at it.

entries.zh: 琛先與妻別室，望琛所處，常有異氣，益以爲神。
entries.en: Chen had earlier lived in a separate room from his wife; gazing toward where Chen dwelt there was often a strange aura, and they increasingly regarded him as divine.
entries.literal: Chen had earlier lived in a separate room from his wife; gazing toward where Chen dwelt there was often a strange aura, and they increasingly regarded him as divine.

entries.zh: 大同元年，遂結其門徒，殺廣晉令王筠，號上願元年，署置官屬。
entries.en: In the first year of Datong he then rallied his disciples, killed the magistrate of Guangjin Wang Yun, proclaimed the era name Shangyuan, and appointed official staff.
entries.literal: In the first year of Datong he then rallied his disciples, killed the Magistrate of Guangjin Wang Yun, proclaimed the era name Shangyuan, and appointed official staff.

entries.zh: 其黨轉相誑惑，有衆萬餘人。
entries.en: His faction in turn deceived and misled one another, until they had a host of more than ten thousand men.
entries.literal: His faction in turn deceived and misled one another, until they had a host of more than ten thousand men.

entries.zh: 將出攻郡，襄先已帥民吏修城隍，爲備禦，及賊至，連戰破之，生獲琛，餘衆逃散。
entries.en: About to march out to attack the commandery, Xiang had already led the people and officials in repairing the walls and moat for defense; when the rebels arrived he defeated them in successive battles, captured Chen alive, and the remaining host fled and scattered.
entries.literal: About to march out to attack the commandery, Xiang had already led the people and officials in repairing the walls and moat for defense; when the rebels arrived he defeated them in successive battles, captured Chen alive, and the remaining host fled and scattered.

entries.zh: 時鄰郡豫章、安成等守宰，案治黨與，因求賄貨，皆不得其實，或有善人盡室離禍，惟襄郡部枉直無濫。
entries.en: At that time the defending officials of neighboring commanderies such as Yuzhang and Ancheng, in investigating and punishing accomplices, sought bribes on the pretext and none obtained the truth; sometimes good men had their whole households swept into calamity—only in Xiang's commandery were the wronged and the upright distinguished without excess.
entries.literal: At that time the defending officials of neighboring commanderies such as Yuzhang and Ancheng, in investigating and punishing accomplices, sought bribes on the pretext and none obtained the truth; sometimes good men had their whole households swept into calamity—only in Xiang's commandery were the wronged and the upright distinguished without excess.

entries.zh: 民作歌曰：「鮮于平後善惡分，民無枉死，賴有陸君。」
