entries.zh: 及到九江，安北兄遂溯流更上，全由餼饋懸絕，卒食半菽，阻以菜色，無因進取。
entries.en: When I reached Jiujiang, elder brother Anbei turned upstream again—entirely because supplies were cut off. We ate half beans at the end and were stopped by hunger, with no way to advance.
entries.literal: When I reached Jiujiang, elder brother Anbei turned upstream and went farther upriver—entirely because provisions were cut off; we ate half beans at the end and were blocked by hunger, with no means to advance.

entries.zh: 侯景方延假息，復緩誅刑，信增號憤，啓處無地。
entries.en: Hou Jing was then buying time and deferring punishment—the news only deepened my cries of rage. I had nowhere to turn.
entries.literal: Hou Jing was then prolonging a borrowed respite and deferring execution—indeed this only deepened my cries of rage; I had nowhere to stand or dwell.

entries.zh: 計瀟湘穀粟，猶當紅委，若阻弟嚴兵，唯事交切，至於運轉，恐無暇發遣。
entries.en: I reckon the grain of the Xiao-Xiang region is still abundant in store. If my younger brother's strict blockade continues, matters will only grow urgent—and as for transport, I fear there will be no time to dispatch it.
entries.literal: I reckon the grain of the Xiao-Xiang region is still abundant in storage; if my younger brother's strict military blockade continues, matters will only grow urgent—as for transport, I fear there will be no leisure to dispatch it.

entries.zh: 卽日萬心慊望，唯在民天，若遂等西河，時事殆矣。
entries.en: Today every heart looks with eager hope only to grain, the people's heaven. If you persist as with the Xi River affair, the times will be nearly lost.
entries.literal: Today ten thousand hearts look with eager hope only to the people's heaven; if you persist in equal treatment with the Xi River affair, the times will be nearly lost.

entries.zh: 必希令弟豁照茲途，解汨川之圍，存社稷之計，使其運輸糧儲，應贍軍旅，庶協力一舉，指日寧泰。
entries.en: I earnestly hope my younger brother will see this clearly, lift the siege on the Mil River, preserve the plan for the altars of state, and enable grain transport to supply the armies, so that with combined strength in one thrust peace may come within days.
entries.literal: I earnestly hope my younger brother will open his eyes to this path, lift the siege on the Mil River, preserve the plan for the altars of state, and enable grain transport to supply the armies, so that with combined strength in one thrust peace may come within days.

entries.zh: 宗廟重安，天下清復，推弟之功，豈非幸甚。
entries.en: When the ancestral temples are secure again and the realm restored to order, to credit my younger brother's achievement—would that not be the greatest fortune?
entries.literal: When the ancestral temples are again secure and the realm restored to order, to advance my younger brother's achievement—would that not be most fortunate?

entries.zh: 吾才懦兵寡，安能爲役，所寄令弟，庶得申情，朝聞夕死，萬殞何恨。
entries.en: My talent is weak and my troops few—I cannot serve in this cause. What I entrust to my younger brother is only that he may give voice to my feelings. If I hear his answer in the morning and die by evening, what regret in dying ten thousand deaths?
entries.literal: My talent is weak and my troops few—I cannot serve as a tool in this; what I entrust to my younger brother is only that he may give voice to my feelings—hearing in the morning and dying at evening, what regret in dying ten thousand deaths?

entries.zh: 聊陳聞見，幸無怪焉。
entries.en: I have briefly set forth what I have heard and seen; I hope you will not take offense.
entries.literal: I briefly set forth what I have heard and seen; I hope you will not take offense.

entries.zh: 臨紙號迷，諸失次緒。
entries.en: Facing the paper I cry out in confusion; my words fall out of order.
entries.literal: Facing the paper I cry out in confusion; all is out of order.

entries.zh: 世祖復書，陳河東有罪，不可解圍之狀。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan wrote back, setting forth Prince of Hedong's crimes and explaining why the siege could not be lifted.
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan replied in writing, setting forth Prince of Hedong's crimes and why the siege could not be lifted.

entries.zh: 綸省書流涕曰：「天下之事，一至於斯！」
entries.en: Reading the letter, Xiao Lun wept and said: "Affairs under heaven have come to this!"
entries.literal: Reading the letter, Xiao Lun wept and said: "Affairs under Heaven have come to this!"

entries.zh: 左右聞之，莫不掩泣。
entries.en: His attendants, hearing this, all hid their faces and wept.
entries.literal: Those around him, hearing this, none failed to cover their faces and weep.

entries.zh: 於是大修器甲，將討侯景。
entries.en: Thereupon he greatly refurbished armor and weapons, intending to campaign against Hou Jing.
entries.literal: Thereupon he greatly refurbished armor and weapons, intending to campaign against Hou Jing.

entries.zh: 元帝聞其強盛，乃遣王僧辯帥舟師一萬以逼綸，綸將劉龍武等降僧辯，綸軍潰，遂與子躓等十餘人輕舟走武昌。
entries.en: When Emperor Yuan heard how strong he had become, he dispatched Wang Sengbian with ten thousand river troops to press Xiao Lun. Xiao Lun's general Liu Longwu and others surrendered to Wang Sengbian; Xiao Lun's army collapsed. He fled in a light boat to Wuchang with his son Zhi and more than ten others.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yuan heard of his strength, he dispatched Wang Sengbian at the head of ten thousand river troops to press Xiao Lun. Xiao Lun's general Liu Longwu and others surrendered to Wang Sengbian; Xiao Lun's army collapsed. He then fled in a light boat to Wuchang with his son Zhi and more than ten others.

entries.zh: 時綸長史韋質、司馬薑律先在于外，聞綸敗，馳往迎之。
entries.en: At that time Xiao Lun's chief clerk Wei Zhi and marshal Jiang Lu were already abroad; hearing of his defeat they raced to meet him.
entries.literal: At that time Xiao Lun's chief clerk Wei Zhi and marshal Jiang Lu were already abroad; hearing of Xiao Lun's defeat they raced to meet him.

entries.zh: 於是復收散卒，屯于齊昌郡，將引魏軍共攻南陽。
entries.en: Thereupon he gathered scattered troops again and encamped in Qichang commandery, intending to bring in Northern Wei troops to attack Nanyang jointly.
entries.literal: Thereupon he again gathered scattered troops and encamped in Qichang commandery, intending to lead Wei troops jointly to attack Nanyang.

entries.zh: 侯景將任約聞之，使鐵騎二百襲綸，綸無備，又敗走定州。
entries.en: Hou Jing's general Ren Yue heard of this and sent two hundred armored horsemen to raid Xiao Lun. Unprepared, Xiao Lun was defeated again and fled to Dingzhou.
entries.literal: Hou Jing's general Ren Yue heard of this and sent two hundred iron cavalry to raid Xiao Lun; unprepared, Xiao Lun was again defeated and fled to Dingzhou.

entries.zh: 定州刺史田龍祖迎綸，綸以龍祖荊鎮所任，懼爲所執，復歸齊昌。
entries.en: Dingzhou regional inspector Tian Longzu welcomed Xiao Lun, but Xiao Lun, knowing Longzu had been appointed from the Jing garrison, feared being seized and returned to Qichang.
entries.literal: Dingzhou Regional Inspector Tian Longzu welcomed Xiao Lun; Xiao Lun, because Longzu had been appointed from the Jing circuit garrison, feared being seized and returned to Qichang.

entries.zh: 行至汝南，西魏所署汝南城主李素者，綸之故吏，聞綸敗，開城納之。
entries.en: When he reached Runan, Li Su—commandant of Runan appointed by Western Wei and Xiao Lun's former subordinate—hearing of his defeat, opened the city and received him.
entries.literal: When he reached Runan, Li Su—commandant of Runan city appointed by Western Wei and Xiao Lun's former clerk—hearing of Xiao Lun's defeat, opened the city and received him.

entries.zh: 綸乃脩浚城池，收集士卒，將攻竟陵。
entries.en: Xiao Lun then repaired the walls and moat, gathered troops, and prepared to attack Jingling.
entries.literal: Xiao Lun then repaired and dredged the walls and moat, gathered soldiers, and intended to attack Jingling.

entries.zh: 西魏安州刺史馬岫聞之，報于西魏，西魏遣大將軍楊忠、儀同侯幾通率衆赴焉。
entries.en: Ma Xiu, regional inspector of Anzhou under Western Wei, heard of this and reported to his court. Western Wei sent Grand General Yang Zhong and Yitong Hou Jitong with an army to intervene.
entries.literal: Ma Xiu, Regional Inspector of Anzhou under Western Wei, heard of this and reported to Western Wei. Western Wei sent Grand General Yang Zhong and Yitong Hou Jitong to lead troops there.

entries.zh: 二年二月，忠等至于汝南，綸嬰城自守。
entries.en: In the second month of 551, Yang Zhong and his force reached Runan. Xiao Lun shut the gates and held the city.
entries.literal: In the second month of the second year, Zhong and the others reached Runan. Xiao Lun closed the city and defended himself.

entries.zh: 會天寒大雪，忠等攻不能克，死者甚衆。
entries.en: Bitter cold and heavy snow set in; Yang Zhong could not storm the city, and his losses were very heavy.
entries.literal: It happened that the weather turned bitterly cold with heavy snow. Zhong and the others could not take the city by assault, and very many died.

entries.zh: 後李素中流矢卒，城乃陷。
entries.en: Later Li Su was killed by a stray arrow, and the city fell.
entries.literal: Later Li Su was struck by a stray arrow and died, and the city then fell.

entries.zh: 忠等執綸，綸不爲屈，遂害之。
entries.en: Yang Zhong seized Xiao Lun. He refused to yield and was put to death.
entries.literal: Zhong and the others seized Xiao Lun. He would not submit and was thereupon killed.

entries.zh: 投于江岸，經日顏色不變，鳥獸莫敢近焉。
entries.en: His body was thrown on the riverbank. For a full day his face did not change, and neither bird nor beast dared come near.
entries.literal: His body was cast on the riverbank. For a whole day his complexion did not change, and birds and beasts did not dare approach.

entries.zh: 時年三十三。
entries.en: He was thirty-three.
entries.literal: He was then thirty-three years old.

entries.zh: 百姓憐之，爲立祠廟，後世祖追諡曰攜。
entries.en: The people pitied him and erected a shrine in his honor. Later Emperor Yuan posthumously titled him Xie.
entries.literal: The common people pitied him and built a shrine for him. Later Emperor Yuan posthumously gave him the title Xie.

entries.zh: 長子堅，字長白。
entries.en: His eldest son Jian, styled Changbai.
entries.literal: His eldest son was Jian, styled Changbai.

entries.zh: 大同元年，以例封汝南侯，邑五百戶。
entries.en: In 535, by precedent he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Runan with a fief of five hundred households.
entries.literal: In the first year of Datong, by precedent he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Runan with a fief of five hundred households.

entries.zh: 亦善草隸，性頗庸短。
entries.en: He was also skilled in cursive and clerical script, but by nature he was rather dull and limited.
entries.literal: He also excelled at cursive and clerical script, but his nature was rather mediocre and limited.

entries.zh: 侯景圍城，堅屯太陽門，終日蒲飲，不撫軍政。
entries.en: When Hou Jing besieged the capital, Jian held the Taiyang Gate, drinking all day on rush mats and neglecting military affairs.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing besieged the city, Jian held the Taiyang Gate, drinking all day on rush mats and not attending to military affairs.

entries.zh: 吏士有功，未嘗申理，疫癘所加，亦不存卹，士咸憤怨。
entries.en: He never reported the deeds of deserving officers and men. When plague struck, he offered no relief. The troops were furious.
entries.literal: When officers and soldiers had merit, he never reported it. When plague struck, he showed no care or relief. The troops were all angry and resentful.

entries.zh: 太清三年三月，堅書佐董勛華、白曇朗等以繩引賊登樓，城遂陷，堅遇害。
entries.en: In the third month of 549, Jian's clerks Dong Xunhua, Bai Tanlang, and others used ropes to let the rebels scale the walls. The city fell, and Jian was killed.
entries.literal: In the third month of the third year of Taiqing, Jian's clerical assistants Dong Xunhua, Bai Tanlang, and others used ropes to let the bandits climb the tower. The city then fell, and Jian was killed.

entries.zh: 鐘山之役，確苦戰，所向披靡，羣虜憚之。
entries.en: At the battle on Zhongshan, Que fought fiercely, routing every foe he met; the rebels all feared him.
entries.literal: In the battle at Zhongshan, Que fought bitterly. Wherever he turned, the enemy was swept away, and the bandits all feared him.

entries.zh: 確每臨陣對敵，意氣詳贍。
entries.en: Whenever Que faced the enemy in battle, his bearing was calm and confident.
entries.literal: Whenever Que faced the enemy in battle, his spirit was composed and ample.

entries.zh: 帶甲據鞍，自朝及夕，馳驟往反，不以爲勞，諸將服其壯勇。
entries.en: Armored and in the saddle from dawn to dusk, he rode back and forth without tiring. The generals admired his courage.
entries.literal: Armored and in the saddle from morning to evening, he galloped back and forth and did not count it labor. The generals admired his bold courage.

entries.zh: 及侯景乞盟，確在外，慮爲後患，啓求召確入城。
entries.en: When Hou Jing sued for peace, Que was outside the walls. Fearing he would become a threat later, a memorial asked that Que be recalled into the city.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing begged for a truce, Que was outside the city. Fearing he would become a future threat, someone memorialized asking that Que be summoned into the city.

entries.zh: 詔乃召確爲南中郎將、廣州刺史，增封二千戶。
entries.en: An edict summoned Que as General of the Southern Gentlemen and regional inspector of Guangzhou, with an added fief of two thousand households.
entries.literal: An edict then summoned Que as General of the Southern Gentlemen and Regional Inspector of Guangzhou, with an added fief of two thousand households.

entries.zh: 確知此盟多貳，城必淪沒，因欲南奔。
entries.en: Que knew the truce was treacherous and the city would fall, and he wanted to flee south.
entries.literal: Que knew this truce was full of treachery and that the city would surely be lost, and therefore wished to flee south.

entries.zh: 攜王聞之，逼確使入，確猶不肯。
entries.en: Prince Yo heard of this and pressed Que to enter, but Que still refused.
entries.literal: Prince Yo heard of this and forced Que to enter, but Que still would not agree.

entries.zh: 攜王流涕謂曰：「汝欲反邪！」
entries.en: Prince Yo wept and said, "Are you trying to rebel?"
entries.literal: Prince Yo wept and said, "Do you wish to rebel?"

entries.zh: 時臺使周石珍在坐，確謂石珍曰：「侯景雖云欲去，而不解長圍，以意而推，其事可見。
entries.en: The court envoy Zhou Shizhen was present. Que told him, "Hou Jing says he will leave, but he keeps the long siege intact. That tells you what he really intends.
entries.literal: At that time the capital envoy Zhou Shizhen was present. Que said to Shizhen, "Although Hou Jing says he wishes to leave, he does not lift the long siege. Reasoning from this, his intent is clear.

entries.zh: 今召我入，未見其益也。」
entries.en: Summoning me inside now will do no good."
entries.literal: Now summoning me in, I see no benefit in it."

entries.zh: 石珍曰：「敕旨如此，侯豈得辭？」
entries.en: Shizhen said, "That is the emperor's order. How can you refuse?"
entries.literal: Shizhen said, "The imperial command is thus. How can the marquis decline?"

entries.zh: 確執意猶堅，攜王大怒，謂趙伯超曰：「譙州，卿爲我斬之，當賚首赴闕。」
entries.en: Que would not budge. Prince Xie flew into a rage and told Zhao Bochao, "Qiaozhou, cut him down for me and bring his head to the court."
entries.literal: Que's resolve was still firm. Prince Xie was greatly angered and said to Zhao Bochao, "Qiaozhou, cut him down for me and bring his head to the court."

entries.zh: 伯超揮刃眄確曰：「我識君耳，刀豈識君？」
entries.en: Bochao drew his blade and looked at Que. "I know you," he said, "but does my blade?"
entries.literal: Bochao brandished his blade and glanced at Que, saying, "I know you—but does my blade know you?"

entries.zh: 確於是流涕而出，遂入城。
entries.en: Que wept as he left, then entered the city.
entries.literal: Que thereupon wept as he went out and then entered the city.

entries.zh: 及景背盟復圍城，城陷，確排闥入，啓高祖曰：「城已陷矣。」
entries.en: When Hou Jing broke the truce and besieged the city again, the walls fell. Que burst through the inner gate and told Emperor Wu, "The city is lost."
entries.literal: When Jing broke the truce and again besieged the city, the city fell. Que pushed open the inner gate and reported to Gaozu, "The city has fallen."

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「猶可一戰不？」
entries.en: Emperor Wu asked, "Can we still fight one more battle?"
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "Can we still fight one battle?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「不可。
entries.en: He answered, "No.
entries.literal: He answered, "We cannot.

entries.zh: 臣向者親格戰，勢不能禁，自縋下城，僅得至此。」
entries.en: I was fighting hand to hand and could not hold them. I let myself down from the wall on a rope and barely made it here."
entries.literal: Your subject just now fought hand to hand and could not hold them back. I lowered myself by rope from the wall and barely reached here."

entries.zh: 高祖歎曰：「自我得之，自我失之，亦復何恨。」
entries.en: Emperor Wu sighed and said, "I won it myself and I lose it myself—what is there to regret?"
entries.literal: Gaozu sighed and said, "I gained it myself and I lose it myself—what regret is there?"

entries.zh: 乃使確爲慰勞文。
entries.en: He then had Que draft a letter of consolation to the troops.
entries.literal: He then had Que draft a letter of consolation.

entries.zh: 確旣出見景，景愛其膂力，恒令在左右。
entries.en: When Que went out to see Hou Jing, Hou Jing admired his strength and always kept him close.
entries.literal: When Que went out and saw Jing, Jing admired his physical strength and always kept him at his side.

entries.zh: 後從景行，見天上飛鳶，羣虜爭射不中，確射之，應弦而落。
entries.en: Later, marching with Hou Jing, they saw a kite overhead. The rebels all shot and missed. Que shot once and brought it down.
entries.literal: Later, following Jing on the march, they saw a kite flying in the sky. The bandits all shot at it but missed. Que shot it, and it fell at the twang of the bowstring.

entries.zh: 賊徒忿嫉，咸勸除之。
entries.en: The rebels were jealous and urged that he be killed.
entries.literal: The bandits were resentful and jealous, and all urged that he be eliminated.

entries.zh: 先是攜王遣人密導確，確謂使者曰：「侯景輕佻，可一夫力致，確不惜死，正欲手刃之；
entries.en: Earlier Prince Yo had sent a secret envoy to Que. Que told him, "Hou Jing is reckless and could be brought down by one man. I do not fear death—I mean to kill him with my own hand;
entries.literal: Earlier Prince Yo had sent someone in secret to guide Que. Que told the envoy, "Hou Jing is frivolous and can be brought down by one man's strength. I do not spare my life and mean to kill him with my own hand;

entries.zh: 但未得其便耳。
entries.en: I only lack the chance.
entries.literal: only I have not yet found the opportunity.

entries.zh: 卿還啓家王，願勿以爲念也。」
entries.en: Go back and tell my father not to worry about me."
entries.literal: When you return, report to my prince and ask that he not worry on my account."

entries.zh: 事未遂而爲賊所害。
entries.en: Before he could act, the rebels killed him.
entries.literal: The affair did not succeed, and he was killed by the bandits.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：自周、漢廣樹籓屏，固本深根；
entries.en: The historian remarks: From Zhou and Han onward, feudal princes were widely enfeoffed to secure the dynasty at its roots;
entries.literal: The historian says: From Zhou and Han, feudal screens were widely planted to strengthen the root deep in the soil;

entries.zh: 高祖之封建，將遵古制也。
entries.en: Emperor Wu's enfeoffments were meant to follow that ancient model.
entries.literal: Gaozu's enfeoffments were intended to follow the ancient system.

entries.zh: 南康、廬陵並以宗室之貴，據磐石之重，績以孝著，續以勇聞。
entries.en: Nankang and Luling, as members of the imperial house, held the weight of bedrock posts. Ji was known for filial piety, Xu for courage.
entries.literal: Nankang and Luling both, by the honor of the imperial clan, held the weight of bedrock. Ji was noted for filial piety, Xu for courage.

entries.zh: 綸聰警有才學，性險躁，屢以罪黜，及太清之亂，忠孝獨存，斯可嘉矣。
entries.en: Lun was clever and learned, but rash and volatile; he was repeatedly punished for offenses. Yet amid the Taiqing turmoil he alone kept faith and filial duty—this is praiseworthy.
entries.literal: Lun was clever and alert, with talent and learning, but his nature was dangerous and restless. Repeatedly he was dismissed for offenses. Yet in the chaos of Taiqing, loyalty and filial piety alone remained in him—this is worthy of praise.

entries.zh: 梁書卷第二十九 列傳第二十三
entries.en: Book of Liang, Volume 29, Biography 23
entries.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 29, Biography 23

entries.zh: 裴子野字幾原，河東聞喜人，晉太子左率康八世孫。
entries.en: Pei Ziye, styled Jiyuan, came from Wenxi in Hedong and was the eighth-generation descendant of Pei Kang, who had served Jin as Left Commander of the Heirs Apparent.
entries.literal: Pei Ziye, styled Jiyuan, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong, eighth-generation descendant of Pei Kang, Left Commander of the Heirs Apparent of Jin.

entries.zh: 兄黎，弟楷、綽，並有盛名，所謂「四裴」也。
entries.en: His elder brother Li and his younger brothers Kai and Chuo were all famous, and together they were known as the "Four Peis."
entries.literal: His elder brother Li and younger brothers Kai and Chuo all enjoyed great renown — the so-called "Four Peis."

entries.zh: 曾祖松之，宋太中大夫。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Pei Songzhi had been a Grand Master of the Palace under the Song.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Songzhi was Grand Master of the Palace of Song.

entries.zh: 祖駰，南中郎外兵參軍。
entries.en: His grandfather Pei Yin had served as External Army Aide to the Southern Central Commandant.
entries.literal: His grandfather Yin was an External Army Aide to the Southern Central Commandant.

entries.zh: 父昭明，通直散騎常侍。
entries.en: His father Pei Zhaoming had been Regular Attendant of the Unimpeded Cavalry.
entries.literal: His father Zhaoming was Regular Attendant of the Unimpeded Cavalry.

entries.zh: 初，子野曾祖松之，宋元嘉中受詔續修何承天《宋史》，未及成而卒，子野常欲繼成先業。
entries.en: Earlier, Ziye's great-grandfather Pei Songzhi, in the Yuanjia era of Song, had received an edict to continue He Chengtian's History of Song, but died before finishing it; Ziye had long wished to complete his ancestor's work.
entries.literal: Earlier, Ziye's great-grandfather Songzhi, in the Yuanjia era of Song, received an edict to continue and revise He Chengtian's History of Song, but died before completing it; Ziye had long wished to carry on and finish his ancestor's work.

entries.zh: 及齊永明末，沈約所撰《宋書》旣行，子野更刪撰爲《宋略》二十卷。
entries.en: By the end of the Yongming era of Qi, Shen Yue's History of Song had already appeared; Ziye then abridged and rewrote it as the Song Summary in twenty juan.
entries.literal: By the end of the Yongming era of Qi, Shen Yue's History of Song had already appeared; Ziye further abridged and composed it into the Song Summary in twenty juan.

entries.zh: 其敘事評論多善，約見而歎曰：「吾弗逮也。」
entries.en: Its narrative and commentary were largely excellent. When Shen Yue saw it he sighed and said, "I do not match him."
entries.literal: Its narrative and commentary were largely excellent. When Yue saw it he sighed and said, "I do not match him."

entries.zh: 蘭陵蕭琛、北地傅昭、汝南周捨咸稱重之。
entries.en: Xiao Chen of Lanling, Fu Zhao of Beidi, and Zhou She of Runan all spoke highly of it.
entries.literal: Xiao Chen of Lanling, Fu Zhao of Beidi, and Zhou She of Runan all praised and valued it highly.

entries.zh: 至是，吏部尚書徐勉言之於高祖，以爲著作郎，掌國史及起居注。
entries.en: At this time Director of the Ministry of Personnel Xu Mian spoke of him to Emperor Wu, who appointed him Lang of Composition, in charge of the national history and the records of the ruler's movements.
entries.literal: At this time Director of the Ministry of Personnel Xu Mian spoke of him to Gaozu, and he was made Lang of Composition, in charge of the national history and the records of the ruler's movements.

entries.zh: 頃之，兼中書通事舍人，尋除通直正員郎，著作、舍人如故。
entries.en: Before long he was made concurrent Attendant of General Affairs in the Secretariat; soon afterward he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Unimpeded, while retaining his posts as Lang of Composition and Attendant.
entries.literal: Before long he was made concurrent Attendant of General Affairs in the Secretariat; soon afterward he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Unimpeded, while his posts as Lang of Composition and Attendant remained as before.

entries.zh: 又敕掌中書詔誥。
entries.en: He was also ordered to take charge of edicts and proclamations in the Secretariat.
entries.literal: He was also ordered to take charge of edicts and proclamations in the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 是時西北徼外有白題及滑國，遣使由岷山道入貢。
entries.en: At that time beyond the northwestern frontier were the states of Baiti and Hua, which sent envoys along the Minshan route to offer tribute.
entries.literal: At that time beyond the northwestern frontier were the states of Baiti and Hua; they sent envoys by the Minshan route to offer tribute.

entries.zh: 此二國歷代弗賓，莫知所出。
entries.en: These two states had never submitted in any dynasty, and no one knew where they came from.
entries.literal: These two states had never submitted in any dynasty, and no one knew whence they came.

entries.zh: 子野曰：「漢潁陰侯斬胡白題將一人。
entries.en: Ziye said, "In Han, the Marquis of Yingyin beheaded a Baiti general of the Hu.
entries.literal: Ziye said, "In Han, Marquis of Yingyin beheaded one Baiti general of the Hu.

entries.zh: 服虔《注》云：『白題，胡名也。』
entries.en: Fu Qian's commentary says, 'Baiti is a Hu name.'
entries.literal: Fu Qian's commentary says: 'Baiti is a Hu name.'

entries.zh: 又漢定遠侯擊虜，八滑從之，此其後乎。」
entries.en: Moreover, in Han the Marquis of Dingyuan attacked the barbarians, and the Eight Hua followed him — are these their descendants?"
entries.literal: Moreover, in Han the Marquis of Dingyuan attacked the barbarians, and the Eight Hua followed him — are these their descendants?"

entries.zh: 時人服其博識。
entries.en: Men of the time admired his erudition.
entries.literal: Men of the time admired his broad learning.

entries.zh: 敕仍使撰《方國使圖》，廣述懷來之盛，自要服至于海表，凡二十國。
entries.en: He was further ordered to compose the Atlas of Envoys from the Border States, broadly describing the splendor of those who came in allegiance, from the inner domains to beyond the seas — twenty states in all.
entries.literal: He was further ordered to compose the Atlas of Envoys from the Border States, broadly setting forth the splendor of those who came in allegiance, from the inner domains to beyond the seas — twenty states in all.

entries.zh: 子野與沛國劉顯、南陽劉之遴、陳郡殷芸、陳留阮孝緒、吳郡顧協、京兆韋棱，皆博極羣書，深相賞好，顯尤推重之。
entries.en: Ziye, together with Liu Xian of Peiguo, Liu Zhilin of Nanyang, Yin Yun of Chen commandery, Ruan Xiaoxu of Chenliu, Gu Xie of Wu commandery, and Wei Leng of Jingzhao, had all read exhaustively and were close friends; Xian especially esteemed him.
entries.literal: Ziye, together with Liu Xian of Peiguo, Liu Zhilin of Nanyang, Yin Yun of Chen commandery, Ruan Xiaoxu of Chenliu, Gu Xie of Wu commandery, and Wei Leng of Jingzhao, all ranged to the utmost through the books and deeply admired and befriended one another; Xian especially valued him.

entries.zh: 時吳平侯蕭勱、范陽張纘，每討論墳籍，咸折中於子野焉。
entries.en: At that time Marquis of Wuping Xiao Mai and Zhang Zuan of Fanyang, whenever they discussed the classics and histories, would all defer to Ziye's judgment.
entries.literal: At that time Marquis of Ping of Wu Xiao Mai and Zhang Zuan of Fanyang, whenever they discussed the classics and histories, would all defer to Ziye's judgment.

entries.zh: 普通七年，王師北伐，敕子野爲喻魏文，受詔立成，高祖以其事體大，召尚書僕射徐勉、太子詹事周捨、鴻臚卿劉之遴、中書侍郎朱异，集壽光殿以觀之，時並嘆服。
entries.en: In the seventh year of Putong, the imperial army marched north, and Ziye was ordered to compose a letter admonishing Wei. He received the edict and finished it at once. Because the matter was weighty, Emperor Wu summoned Vice Director of the Secretariat Xu Mian, Supervisor of the Heir Apparent Zhou She, Minister of Ceremonies Liu Zhilin, and Vice Director of the Secretariat Zhu Yi to gather in the Shouguang Hall to read it; all marveled at it.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Putong, the imperial army marched north; Ziye was ordered to compose a letter admonishing Wei. Having received the edict he finished it at once. Gaozu, because the matter was weighty, summoned Vice Director of the Secretariat Xu Mian, Supervisor of the Heir Apparent Zhou She, Minister of Ceremonies Liu Zhilin, and Vice Director of the Secretariat Zhu Yi to gather in the Shouguang Hall to view it; all at once sighed in admiration.

entries.zh: 高祖目子野而言曰：「其形雖弱，其文甚壯。」
entries.en: Emperor Wu looked at Ziye and said, "His body may be slight, but his writing is very strong."
entries.literal: Gaozu looked at Ziye and said, "His form may be frail, but his writing is very strong."

entries.zh: 俄又敕爲書喻魏相元乂，其夜受旨，子野謂可待旦方奏，未之爲也。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was again ordered to compose a letter admonishing Yuan Yi, chief minister of Wei. That night he received the command; Ziye thought he could wait until dawn before presenting it and did not yet write it.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was again ordered to compose a letter admonishing Yuan Yi, chief minister of Wei. That night he received the command; Ziye thought he could wait until dawn before presenting it and did not yet compose it.

entries.zh: 及五鼓，敕催令開齋速上，子野徐起操筆，昧爽便就。
entries.en: By the fifth watch an edict urged him to break his fast and submit it quickly. Ziye rose slowly, took up his brush, and by first light it was finished.
entries.literal: By the fifth watch an edict urged him to open the fast and submit it quickly. Ziye rose slowly, took up his brush, and by first light it was done.

entries.zh: 旣奏，高祖深嘉焉。
entries.en: Once it was presented, Emperor Wu praised it highly.
entries.literal: Once it was presented, Gaozu deeply praised it.

entries.zh: 自是凡諸符檄，皆令草創。
entries.en: From then on, all proclamations and dispatches were entrusted to him for drafting.
entries.literal: From then on, for all proclamations and dispatches, he was ordered to draft them.

entries.zh: 子野爲文典而速，不尚麗靡之詞。
entries.en: Ziye wrote in a classical style and with great speed; he did not favor ornate and florid language.
entries.literal: Ziye's writing was classical and swift; he did not esteem ornate and florid words.

entries.zh: 其制作多法古，與今文體異，當時或有詆訶者，及其末皆翕然重之。
entries.en: His compositions largely followed ancient models and differed from contemporary style; some criticized them at the time, but by the end of his life all came to value them.
entries.literal: His compositions largely followed antiquity and differed from the style of the present day; at the time some criticized them, but by his end all alike came to value them.

entries.zh: 或問其爲文速者，子野答云：「人皆成於手，我獨成於心，雖有見否之異，其於刊改一也。」
entries.en: When someone asked about his swift writing, Ziye answered, "Others complete their work with the hand; I alone complete mine in the mind. Though there is a difference between seeing and not seeing, revision is the same either way."
entries.literal: When someone asked about his swift writing, Ziye answered, "Others complete their work with the hand; I alone complete mine in the mind. Though there is a difference between seeing and not seeing, in revision it is the same."

entries.zh: 二年，吳平侯蕭景爲南兗州刺史，引爲冠軍錄事，府遷職解。
entries.en: In the second year, Marquis of Wuping Xiao Jing became regional inspector of South Yanzhou and took Ziye on as recorder for the Champion General; when the headquarters was transferred, the appointment ended.
entries.literal: In the second year, Marquis of Ping of Wu Xiao Jing became regional inspector of South Yanzhou and took him on as recorder for the Champion General; when the headquarters moved, the post was dissolved.

entries.zh: 時中書范縝與子野未遇，聞其行業而善焉。
entries.en: At that time Fan Zhen of the Secretariat had not yet met Ziye, but having heard of his conduct and accomplishments, he thought well of him.
entries.literal: At that time Fan Zhen of the Secretariat and Ziye had not yet met, but having heard of his conduct and accomplishments, Zhen thought well of him.

entries.zh: 會遷國子博士，乃上表讓之曰：「伏見前冠軍府錄事參軍河東裴子野，年四十，字幾原，幼稟至人之行，長厲國士之風。
entries.en: When he was appointed Erudite of the Imperial Academy, he submitted a memorial yielding the post to another, saying: "I have observed the former recorder of the Champion General's headquarters, Pei Ziye of Hedong, age forty, styled Jiyuan, who from youth embodied the conduct of a sage and in maturity cultivated the bearing of a true gentleman of the state.
entries.literal: When he was transferred to be Erudite of the Imperial Academy, he submitted a memorial yielding the post, saying: "I have observed the former recorder of the Champion General's headquarters, Pei Ziye of Hedong, age forty, styled Jiyuan, who in youth received the conduct of a sage and in maturity cultivated the bearing of a state-worthy man.

entries.zh: 居喪有禮，毀瘠幾滅，免憂之外，蔬水不進。
entries.en: In mourning he observed every rite to the point of wasting away; even after the mourning period ended, he would take in neither vegetables nor water.
entries.literal: In mourning he observed the rites; his emaciation nearly consumed him, and after the mourning period ended he would take in neither vegetables nor water.

entries.zh: 棲遲下位，身賤名微，而性不憛憛，情無汲汲，是以有識嗟推，州閭嘆服。
entries.en: He lingered in humble office, obscure and of little renown, yet his nature was never restless and his heart never grasping; men of discernment praised and recommended him, and his neighbors marveled at him.
entries.literal: He lingered in low office, his person humble and his name obscure, yet his nature was not restless and his heart not grasping; therefore the discerning praised and pushed him forward, and his district sighed in admiration.

entries.zh: 且家傳素業，世習儒史，苑囿經籍，遊息文藝。
entries.en: His family has handed down its scholarly calling for generations, and he has long practiced Confucian learning and history, ranging through the classics and finding his recreation in literature and the arts.
entries.literal: Moreover, his family has handed down its proper calling for generations, and he has long practiced Confucian learning and history, ranging through the classics and finding recreation in letters and the arts.

entries.zh: 著《宋略》二十卷，彌綸首尾，勒成一代，屬辭比事，有足觀者。
entries.en: He has written the Song Summary in twenty juan, spanning a whole age from beginning to end; in arranging words and comparing events, it is well worth reading.
entries.literal: He has composed the Song Summary in twenty juan, spanning beginning to end and binding together a whole age; in arranging words and comparing events, there is much worth viewing.

entries.zh: 且章句洽悉，訓故可傳。
entries.en: His commentarial passages are thorough, and his glosses on ancient terms are fit to be handed down.
entries.literal: Moreover, his commentarial passages are thorough and familiar, and his glosses on old terms can be handed down.

entries.zh: 脫置之膠庠，以弘獎後進，庶一夔之辯可尋，三豕之疑無謬矣。
entries.en: If he were placed in the Academy to encourage younger scholars, perhaps the discernment of a Kui might be found again and errors like the "three pigs" would never arise.
entries.literal: If he were placed in the Academy to encourage and reward the rising generation, perhaps Kui's discernment could be sought again and the error of the three pigs would find no place.

entries.zh: 伏惟皇家淳耀，多士盈庭，官人邁乎有媯，棫朴越於姬氏，苟片善宜錄，無論厚薄，一介可求，不由等級。
entries.en: Your Majesty's house shines with pure brilliance, and talented men fill the court. Its officials surpass those of the age of Gui, and its supply of able men exceeds that of the Zhou. If even the slightest merit deserves record, without regard to high or low station, a single worthy man may be sought without regard to rank.
entries.literal: Your Majesty's house shines with pure brilliance; talented men fill the court. Its officials surpass those of the House of Gui, and its timber for building exceeds that of the House of Ji. If even a fragment of merit should be recorded, regardless of depth or shallowness, a single man of worth may be sought without regard to rank.

entries.zh: 臣歷觀古今人君，欽賢好善，未有聖朝孜孜若是之至也。
entries.en: Your servant has surveyed rulers ancient and modern who honored the worthy and loved goodness, yet none has matched the diligence of this sacred court.
entries.literal: Your servant has surveyed rulers ancient and modern who honored the worthy and loved goodness, yet none has reached the diligence of this sacred court.

entries.zh: 敢緣斯義，輕陳愚瞽，乞以臣斯忝，回授子野。
entries.en: Venturing on this principle, I humbly set forth my dull counsel and beg that the post your unworthy servant now holds may be transferred to Ziye.
entries.literal: I venture on this principle lightly to set forth my dull blindness, begging that the post in which your servant is unworthy may be transferred to Ziye.

entries.zh: 如此，則賢否之宜，各全其所，訊之物議，誰曰不允。
entries.en: If it were so, the worthy and the unworthy would each occupy their proper place, and if one asked public opinion, who would call it unjust?
entries.literal: If it were so, then the fitting place for worthy and unworthy would each be preserved, and if one asked public opinion, who would say it was not acceptable?

entries.zh: 臣與子野雖未嘗銜杯，訪之邑裏，差非虛謬，不勝慺慺微見，冒昧陳聞。
entries.en: Your servant and Ziye have never shared a cup together, yet inquiring in the district, what is said of him is not greatly exaggerated. Unable to restrain my earnest sincerity, I venture this slight view and presumptuously lay it before Your Majesty.
entries.literal: Your servant and Ziye have never shared a cup, yet inquiring in the district, the report is not greatly false. Unable to restrain my earnest sincerity, I venture this slight view and presumptuously report it.

entries.zh: 伏願陛下哀憐悾款，鑒其愚實，干犯之諐，乞垂赦宥。」
entries.en: I bow my head and hope Your Majesty will pity my sincere earnestness, discern my foolish honesty, and extend pardon for this presumptuous offense."
entries.literal: I bow my head and hope Your Majesty will pity my sincere earnestness, discern my foolish truthfulness, and extend pardon for this offense of presumption."

entries.zh: 有司以資歷非次，弗爲通。
entries.en: The relevant offices, holding that his qualifications were out of order, did not approve the request.
entries.literal: The relevant offices, on the grounds that his qualifications were out of order, did not approve it.

entries.zh: 尋除尚書比部郎，仁威記室參軍。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was appointed Lang of the Comparison Bureau in the Secretariat and recorder for Prince Renwei.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Lang of the Comparison Bureau in the Secretariat and recorder for Prince Renwei.

entries.zh: 出爲諸暨令，在縣不行鞭罰，民有爭者，示之以理，百姓稱悅，合境無訟。
entries.en: He was sent out as magistrate of Zhuji. In the county he never used the lash or fines; when the people quarreled, he showed them reason, and they praised him with joy — throughout the whole district there were no lawsuits.
entries.literal: He went out as magistrate of Zhuji. In the county he did not use the lash or fines; when the people had disputes, he showed them reason, and the common folk praised him with joy — throughout the whole district there were no lawsuits.

entries.zh: 徐摛字士秀，東海郯人也。
entries.en: Xu Chi, styled Shixiu, came from Tan in Donghai.
entries.literal: Xu Chi, styled Shixiu, was a native of Tan in Donghai.

entries.zh: 祖憑道，宋海陵太守。
entries.en: His grandfather Xu Pingdao had been governor of Hailing under the Song.
entries.literal: His grandfather Pingdao was governor of Hailing under Song.

entries.zh: 父超之，天監初仕至員外散騎常侍。
entries.en: His father Xu Chaozhi, early in the Tianjian era, rose to Extraordinary Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.
entries.literal: His father Chaozhi, at the beginning of Tianjian, rose in office to Extraordinary Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.

entries.zh: 摛幼而好學，及長，遍覽經史。
entries.en: From youth Chi loved study; when he grew up he read widely in the classics and histories.
entries.literal: Chi from youth loved learning; when he grew up he ranged through the classics and histories.

entries.zh: 屬文好爲新變，不拘舊體。
entries.en: In writing he loved innovation and was not bound by older forms.
entries.literal: In composing texts he loved to make new changes and was not bound by old forms.

entries.zh: 起家太學博士，遷左衛司馬。
entries.en: He entered service as Erudite of the Imperial Academy and was transferred to Marshal of the Left Guard.
entries.literal: He began his career as Erudite of the Imperial Academy and was transferred to Marshal of the Left Guard.

entries.zh: 會晉安王綱出戍石頭，高祖謂周捨曰：「爲我求一人，文學俱長兼有行者，欲令與晉安遊處。」
entries.en: When Prince Jin'an Xiao Gang went out to garrison Shitou, Emperor Wu said to Zhou She, "Find me a man accomplished in both letters and learning who also has proper conduct, to keep company with Jin'an."
entries.literal: When Prince Jin'an Gang went out to garrison Shitou, Gaozu said to Zhou She, "Find me a man accomplished in both letters and learning who also has conduct, whom I wish to have keep company with Jin'an."

entries.zh: 捨曰：「臣外弟徐摛，形質陋小，若不勝衣，而堪此選。」
entries.en: She said, "Your servant's cousin on his mother's side Xu Chi — his frame is slight and homely, as if he could not fill his clothes, yet he is fit for this selection."
entries.literal: She said, "Your servant's cousin on his mother's side Xu Chi — his form and substance are homely and slight, as if he could not fill his clothes, yet he is fit for this selection."

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「必有仲宣之才，亦不簡其容貌。」
entries.en: Emperor Wu said, "If he has the talent of Wang Can, I will not be choosy about his appearance."
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "If he has the talent of Zhongxuan, I will not be choosy about his appearance."

entries.zh: 以摛爲侍讀。
entries.en: Chi was made study companion to the prince.
entries.literal: Chi was made study companion.

entries.zh: 後王出鎮江州，仍補雲麾府記室參軍，又轉平西府中記室。
entries.en: Later the prince went out to govern Jiangzhou; Chi was appointed recorder for the Cloud Pennant headquarters and then transferred to central recorder for the Pacify-the-West headquarters.
entries.literal: Later the prince went out to govern Jiangzhou; Chi was appointed recorder for the Cloud Pennant headquarters and then transferred to central recorder for the Pacify-the-West headquarters.

entries.zh: 王移鎮京口，復隨府轉爲安北中錄事參軍，帶郯令，以母憂去職。
entries.en: When the prince moved his garrison to Jingkou, Chi followed the headquarters and was made recorder for the Pacify-the-North Central Commandant, with concurrent appointment as magistrate of Tan; he resigned when his mother died.
entries.literal: When the prince moved his garrison to Jingkou, Chi again followed the headquarters and was made recorder for the Pacify-the-North Central Commandant, with concurrent appointment as magistrate of Tan; he left office upon his mother's death.

entries.zh: 王爲丹陽尹，起摛爲秣陵令。
entries.en: When the prince became governor of Danyang, Chi was recalled as magistrate of Moling.
entries.literal: When the prince became governor of Danyang, Chi was recalled as magistrate of Moling.

entries.zh: 普通四年，王出鎮襄陽，摛固求隨府西上，遷晉安王諮議參軍。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Putong the prince went out to govern Xiangyang; Chi firmly requested to follow the headquarters west and was promoted to advisory aide to Prince Jin'an.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Putong the prince went out to govern Xiangyang; Chi firmly requested to follow the headquarters west and was promoted to advisory aide to Prince Jin'an.

entries.zh: 大通初，王總戎北伐，以摛兼寧蠻府長史，參贊戎政，教命軍書，多自摛出。
entries.en: At the beginning of Datong the prince took overall command of the northern campaign; Chi was made concurrent Chief Clerk of the Pacify-the-Barbarians headquarters and assisted in military affairs; instructions and military documents mostly came from Chi.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Datong the prince took overall command of the northern campaign; Chi was made concurrent Chief Clerk of the Pacify-the-Barbarians headquarters, assisting in military affairs; instructions and military documents mostly came from Chi.

entries.zh: 王入爲皇太子，轉家令，兼掌管記，尋帶領直。
entries.en: When the prince entered the capital as crown prince, Chi was transferred to Director of the Palace Household, with concurrent charge of records, and soon afterward was placed in command of the direct guard.
entries.literal: When the prince entered the capital as crown prince, Chi was transferred to Director of the Palace Household, with concurrent charge of records, and soon afterward was placed in command of the direct guard.

entries.zh: 先是子野自剋死期，不過庚戌歲。
entries.en: Earlier Ziye had fixed his own term of death, saying he would not live past the gengxu year.
entries.literal: Earlier Ziye had fixed his own term of death, saying it would not pass the gengxu year.

entries.zh: 是年自省移病，謂同官劉之亨曰：「吾其逝矣。」
entries.en: That year he reported himself ill and withdrew, telling his colleague Liu Zhiheng, "I am about to die."
entries.literal: That year he reported himself ill and withdrew, saying to his colleague Liu Zhiheng, "I am about to depart."

entries.zh: 遺命儉約，務在節制。
entries.en: His final instructions were frugal, with restraint in all things.
entries.literal: His final instructions were frugal, striving for restraint.

entries.zh: 高祖悼惜，爲之流涕。
entries.en: Emperor Wu mourned him deeply and wept for him.
entries.literal: Gaozu mourned and cherished his memory, shedding tears for him.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「鴻臚卿、領步兵校尉、知著作郎、兼中書通事舍人裴子野，文史足用，廉白自居，劬勞通事，多歷年所。
entries.en: An edict said: "Minister of Ceremonies Pei Ziye, who also commanded the Footsoldiers, served as Lang of Composition, and was concurrent Attendant of General Affairs in the Secretariat — his letters and histories were fully adequate, he lived in integrity and purity, and labored diligently in general affairs for many years.
entries.literal: An edict said: "Minister of Ceremonies, Colonel of the Footsoldiers in command, Lang of Composition in charge, and concurrent Attendant of General Affairs in the Secretariat Pei Ziye — his letters and histories were fully adequate, he dwelt in integrity and purity, and labored diligently in general affairs for many years.

entries.zh: 奄致喪逝，惻愴空懷。
entries.en: Suddenly he has died, and our hearts are filled with sorrow and grief.
entries.literal: Suddenly he met with death and departure; sorrow and grief fill an empty breast.

entries.zh: 可贈散騎常侍，賻錢五萬，布五十匹，卽日舉哀。
entries.en: Let him be posthumously honored as Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, with funeral gifts of fifty thousand cash and fifty bolts of cloth; mourning is to begin this very day.
entries.literal: He may be posthumously honored as Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, with funeral gifts of fifty thousand cash and fifty bolts of cloth; mourning is to begin this very day.

entries.zh: 諡曰貞子。」
entries.en: His posthumous title is Zhenzi (Upright)."
entries.literal: His posthumous title is Zhenzi (Upright)."

entries.zh: 軍還，會有詔舉士，湘東王表薦協曰：「臣聞貢玉之士，歸之潤山；
entries.en: When the army returned, an edict called for the recommendation of scholars. The Prince of Xiangdong memorialized recommending Xie, saying, "Your servant has heard that one who offers jade returns to Mount Run;
entries.literal: When the army returned, there happened to be an edict calling for the recommendation of scholars. The Prince of Xiangdong memorialized recommending Xie, saying: "Your servant has heard that one who offers jade returns to Mount Run;

entries.zh: 論珠之人，出於枯岸。
entries.en: and one who assesses pearls comes forth from a barren shore.
entries.literal: and one who discusses pearls comes forth from a withered bank.

entries.zh: 是以芻蕘之言，擇於廊廟者也。
entries.en: That is why the humble words of common folk may be chosen in the halls of state.
entries.literal: Therefore the words of hay-cutters and firewood-gatherers are chosen in the court and temple.

entries.zh: 臣府兼記室參軍吳郡顧協，行稱鄉閭，學兼文武，服膺道素，雅量邃遠，安貧守靜，奉公抗直，傍闕知己，志不自營，年方六十，室無妻子。
entries.en: Your servant's headquarters concurrent recorder Gu Xie of Wu commandery — his conduct is praised throughout his district, his learning embraces both civil and military affairs, he embraces the Way in plain simplicity, his generous spirit runs deep, he is content in poverty and keeps to quiet, serves the public with upright integrity, has no patron at his side, and never seeks his own advantage. He is just sixty, and his household has neither wife nor children.
entries.literal: Your servant's headquarters concurrent recorder Gu Xie of Wu commandery — his conduct is praised in village and district, his learning embraces both civil and military affairs, he embraces the Way in plain simplicity, his generous measure is deep and far-reaching, he is content in poverty and keeps to quiet, serves the public with upright integrity, lacks a patron at his side, and his will does not seek its own ends. He is just sixty, and his household has neither wife nor children.

entries.zh: 臣欲言于官人，申其屈滯，協必苦執貞退，立志難奪，可謂東南之遺寶矣。
entries.en: Your servant wished to speak to the officials on his behalf, but Xie would surely cling stubbornly to integrity and withdrawal; his resolve cannot be swayed. He may truly be called a treasure left behind in the southeast.
entries.literal: Your servant wished to speak to the officials and set forth how he has been held back and neglected, but Xie would surely cling bitterly to integrity and withdrawal; his resolve is hard to sway. He may be called a treasure left behind in the southeast.

entries.zh: 伏惟陛下未明求衣，思賢如渴，爰發明詔，各舉所知。
entries.en: I bow my head and consider that Your Majesty, rising before dawn to seek your robes, thirsts for the worthy as for water, and has therefore issued a bright edict that each should recommend those he knows.
entries.literal: I bow my head and consider that Your Majesty, before dawn seeks your robes, thirsts for the worthy as for water, and has therefore issued a bright edict that each should recommend those he knows.

entries.zh: 臣識非許、郭，雖無知人之鑒，若守固無言，懼貽蔽賢之咎。
entries.en: Your servant's discernment does not match that of Xu and Guo; though I lack the eye for knowing men, if I kept stubbornly silent I would fear the fault of concealing the worthy.
entries.literal: Your servant's discernment does not match that of Xu and Guo; though I lack the eye for knowing men, if I kept silent out of stubbornness I would fear the fault of concealing the worthy.

entries.zh: 昔孔愉表韓績之才，庾亮薦翟湯之德，臣雖未齒二臣，協實無慚兩士。」
entries.en: In the past Kong Yu memorialized Han Ji's talent and Yu Liang recommended Zhai Tang's virtue. Your servant, though not equal to those two ministers, finds that Xie would not be shamed before those two gentlemen."
entries.literal: In the past Kong Yu memorialized Han Ji's talent and Yu Liang recommended Zhai Tang's virtue. Your servant, though not equal to those two ministers, finds that Xie is truly not shamed before those two gentlemen."

entries.zh: 卽召拜通直散騎侍郎，兼中書通事舍人。
entries.en: He was at once summoned and appointed Attendant of the Unimpeded Cavalry and made concurrent Attendant of General Affairs in the Secretariat.
entries.literal: He was at once summoned and appointed Attendant of the Unimpeded Cavalry and made concurrent Attendant of General Affairs in the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 累遷步兵校尉，守鴻臚卿，員外散騎常侍，卿、舍人並如故。
entries.en: He was repeatedly promoted to Colonel of the Footsoldiers, acting Minister of Ceremonies, and Extraordinary Regular Attendant of the Cavalry; his posts as minister and attendant remained unchanged.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Colonel of the Footsoldiers, acting Minister of Ceremonies, and Extraordinary Regular Attendant of the Cavalry; his posts as minister and attendant remained as before.

entries.zh: 大同八年，卒，時年七十三。
entries.en: In the eighth year of Datong he died at the age of seventy-three.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Datong he died, age seventy-three.

entries.zh: 高祖悼惜之，手詔曰：「員外散騎常侍、鴻臚卿、兼中書通事舍人顧協，廉潔自居，白首不衰，久在省闥，內外稱善。
entries.en: Emperor Wu mourned him deeply and wrote in his own hand: "Extraordinary Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Gu Xie, who also served as Minister of Ceremonies and concurrent Attendant of General Affairs in the Secretariat — he lived in integrity and purity, which did not fade even in old age. Long in the inner offices, he was praised within and without.
entries.literal: Gaozu mourned and cherished him, writing in his own hand: "Extraordinary Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, Minister of Ceremonies, and concurrent Attendant of General Affairs in the Secretariat Gu Xie — he dwelt in integrity and purity, which did not fade even in white-haired old age. Long in the inner offices, he was praised within and without.

entries.zh: 奄然殞喪，惻怛之懷，不能已已。
entries.en: Suddenly he has died, and sorrow in my breast cannot cease.
entries.literal: Suddenly he has met with death and departure; sorrow and grief in the breast cannot cease.

entries.zh: 傍無近親，彌足哀者。
entries.en: He has no close kin at his side — this makes the grief all the greater.
entries.literal: He has no close kin at his side — this makes the grief all the greater.

entries.zh: 大殮旣畢，卽送其喪柩還鄉，並營冢槨，並皆資給，悉使周辦。
entries.en: Once the encoffinment is complete, send his bier back to his native place at once, provide for his tomb and coffin, supply everything needed, and have it all fully arranged.
entries.literal: Once the great encoffinment is complete, send his bier back to his native place at once, and also provide for his tomb and coffin — supply everything and have it all fully arranged.

entries.zh: 可贈散騎常侍，令便舉哀。
entries.en: Let him be posthumously honored as Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, and let mourning begin at once.
entries.literal: He may be posthumously honored as Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, and mourning is to begin at once.

entries.zh: 諡曰溫子。」
entries.en: His posthumous title is Wenzi (Gentle)."
entries.literal: His posthumous title is Wenzi (Gentle)."

entries.zh: 摛文體旣別，春坊盡學之，「宮體」之號，自斯而起。
entries.en: Chi's literary style was already distinctive; the crown prince's household all studied it, and the name "Palace Style" arose from this.
entries.literal: Chi's literary style was already distinctive; the Eastern Palace all studied it, and the name "Palace Style" arose from this.

entries.zh: 高祖聞之怒，召摛加讓，及見，應對明敏，辭義可觀，高祖意釋。
entries.en: Emperor Wu heard of it and grew angry; he summoned Chi to reproach him, but when he saw him, Chi's replies were clear and keen and his words were impressive; the emperor's anger lifted.
entries.literal: Gaozu heard of it and grew angry; he summoned Chi to reproach him, but when he saw him, Chi's replies were clear and keen and his words and meaning were worth viewing; Gaozu's anger lifted.

entries.zh: 因問《五經》大義，次問歷代史及百家雜說，末論釋教。
entries.en: He then asked about the great meaning of the Five Classics, next about histories of successive dynasties and miscellaneous writings of the hundred schools, and finally discussed Buddhism.
entries.literal: He then asked about the great meaning of the Five Classics, next about histories of successive dynasties and miscellaneous writings of the hundred schools, and finally discussed the Buddhist teaching.

entries.zh: 摛商較縱橫，應答如響，高祖甚加歎異，更被親狎，寵遇日隆。
entries.en: Chi debated freely and answered like an echo; Emperor Wu marveled at him, drew him closer, and his favor grew daily.
entries.literal: Chi weighed and compared freely, answering like an echo; Gaozu greatly sighed in wonder, drew him closer in intimacy, and his favor and treatment grew daily.

entries.zh: 領軍朱异不說，謂所親曰：「徐叟出入兩宮，漸來逼我，須早爲之所。」
entries.en: Commandant-in-Chief Zhu Yi was displeased and said to those close to him, "Old Xu goes in and out of both palaces and is gradually pressing upon me; I must deal with this early."
entries.literal: Commandant-in-Chief Zhu Yi was displeased and said to those close to him, "Old Xu goes in and out of both palaces and is gradually pressing upon me; I must deal with this early."

entries.zh: 遂承間白高祖曰：「摛年老，又愛泉石，意在一郡，以自怡養。」
entries.en: He then seized an opportunity to inform Emperor Wu, saying, "Chi is old and loves springs and rocks; his wish is for one commandery where he may nourish himself in ease."
entries.literal: He then seized an opportunity to inform Gaozu, saying, "Chi is old and also loves springs and rocks; his wish is for one commandery where he may nourish himself in ease."

entries.zh: 高祖謂摛欲之，乃召摛曰：「新安大好山水，任昉等並經爲之，卿爲我臥治此郡。」
entries.en: Emperor Wu thought Chi wished it and summoned him, saying, "Xin'an has excellent mountains and waters; Ren Fang and others have all governed it. You shall govern this commandery for me from your couch."
entries.literal: Gaozu thought Chi wished it and therefore summoned him, saying, "Xin'an has excellent mountains and waters; Ren Fang and others have all governed it. You shall lie abed and govern this commandery for me."

entries.zh: 中大通三年，遂出爲新安太守。
entries.en: In the third year of Zhongdatong he was sent out as governor of Xin'an.
entries.literal: In the third year of Zhongdatong he went out as governor of Xin'an.

entries.zh: 至郡，爲治清靜，教民禮義，勸課農桑，期月之中，風俗便改。
entries.en: On reaching the commandery he governed with purity and quiet, taught the people rites and righteousness, and urged them in agriculture and sericulture; within a month customs were transformed.
entries.literal: On reaching the commandery he governed with purity and quiet, taught the people rites and righteousness, and urged them in agriculture and sericulture; within a full month customs were changed.

entries.zh: 秩滿，還爲中庶子，加戎昭將軍。
entries.en: When his term ended he returned as Central Palace Companion and was given the additional title General Who Displays Martial Resolution.
entries.literal: When his term ended he returned as Central Palace Companion and was given the additional title General Who Displays Martial Resolution.

entries.zh: 子野少時，《集注喪服》、《續裴氏家傳》各二卷，抄合後漢事四十餘卷，又敕撰《衆僧傳》二十卷，《百官九品》二卷，《附益諡法》一卷，《方國使圖》一卷，文集二十卷，並行於世。
entries.en: In his youth Ziye wrote the Collected Commentary on Mourning Garments and the Continuation of the Pei Family Genealogy, each in two juan, and copied and compiled more than forty juan of Later Han affairs. By edict he also composed the Biographies of the Many Monks in twenty juan, the Nine Ranks of the Hundred Officials in two juan, Supplementary Methods of Posthumous Titles in one juan, the Atlas of Envoys from the Border States in one juan, and a collection of writings in twenty juan — all of which circulated in his day.
entries.literal: In his youth Ziye wrote the Collected Commentary on Mourning Garments and the Continuation of the Pei Family Genealogy, each in two juan, and copied and compiled more than forty juan of Later Han affairs. By edict he also composed the Biographies of the Many Monks in twenty juan, the Nine Ranks of the Hundred Officials in two juan, Supplementary Methods of Posthumous Titles in one juan, the Atlas of Envoys from the Border States in one juan, and a collection of writings in twenty juan — all circulated in the world.

entries.zh: 又欲撰《齊梁春秋》，始草創，未就而卒。
entries.en: He also wished to compose the Spring and Autumn of Qi and Liang, but had only begun the draft when he died without finishing it.
entries.literal: He also wished to compose the Spring and Autumn of Qi and Liang, but had only begun the draft when he died before completing it.

entries.zh: 子謇，官至通直郎。
entries.en: His son Pei Jian rose to the office of Attendant of the Unimpeded.
entries.literal: His son Jian reached the office of Attendant of the Unimpeded.

entries.zh: 起家揚州議曹從事史，兼太學博士。
entries.en: He entered service as a clerk in the deliberation office of Yangzhou and as concurrent Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
entries.literal: He began his career as a clerk in the deliberation office of Yangzhou and as concurrent Erudite of the Imperial Academy.

entries.zh: 舉秀才，尚書令沈約覽其策而歎曰：「江左以來，未有此作。」
entries.en: He was recommended as a cultivated talent. When Director of the Secretariat Shen Yue read his examination essay, he sighed and said, "Since the south of the Yangtze, there has been nothing like this."
entries.literal: He was recommended as a cultivated talent. Director of the Secretariat Shen Yue read his examination essay and sighed, "Since the south of the Yangtze, there has been nothing like this composition."

entries.zh: 遷安成王國左常侍，兼廷尉正。
entries.en: He was transferred to Left Regular Attendant in the Kingdom of the Prince of Ancheng and made concurrent Director of the Court of Justice.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Left Regular Attendant in the Kingdom of the Prince of Ancheng and made concurrent Director of the Court of Justice.

entries.zh: 太尉臨川王聞其名，召掌書記，仍侍西豊侯正德讀。
entries.en: The Defender-in-Chief, Prince of Linchuan, heard his name and summoned him to take charge of records, and he also attended upon Marquis of Feng of the West, Xiao Zhengde, in his studies.
entries.literal: The Defender-in-Chief, Prince of Linchuan, heard his name and summoned him to take charge of records, and he also attended upon Marquis of Feng of the West, Xiao Zhengde, in his studies.

entries.zh: 正德爲巴西、梓潼郡，協除所部安都令。
entries.en: Zhengde held the commanderies of Baxi and Zitong; Xie was appointed magistrate of Andu within his jurisdiction.
entries.literal: Zhengde held the commanderies of Baxi and Zitong; Xie was appointed magistrate of Andu within his jurisdiction.

entries.zh: 未至縣，遭母憂。
entries.en: Before he reached the county, his mother died.
entries.literal: Before he reached the county he met with his mother's death.

entries.zh: 服闋，出補西陽郡丞。
entries.en: When mourning ended, he was sent out as assistant administrator of Xiyang commandery.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he went out to fill the post of assistant administrator of Xiyang commandery.

entries.zh: 還除北中郎行參軍，復兼廷尉正。
entries.en: On his return he was appointed acting aide to the Northern Central Commandant and again made concurrent Director of the Court of Justice.
entries.literal: On his return he was appointed acting aide to the Northern Central Commandant and again made concurrent Director of the Court of Justice.

entries.zh: 久之，出爲廬陵郡丞，未拜。
entries.en: After some time he was appointed assistant administrator of Luling commandery but did not assume the post.
entries.literal: After some time he was sent out as assistant administrator of Luling commandery but did not assume the post.

entries.zh: 會西豊侯正德爲吳郡，除中軍參軍，領郡五官，遷輕車湘東王參軍事，兼記室。
entries.en: When Marquis of Feng of the West Zhengde became governor of Wu commandery, Xie was appointed aide in the Central Army and placed in charge of the five officials of the commandery; he was then transferred as aide to the Prince of Xiangdong in the Light Chariots and made concurrent recorder.
entries.literal: When Marquis of Feng of the West Zhengde became governor of Wu commandery, Xie was appointed aide in the Central Army and placed in charge of the five officials of the commandery; he was then transferred as aide to the Prince of Xiangdong in the Light Chariots and made concurrent recorder.

entries.zh: 普通六年，正德受詔北討，引爲府錄事參軍，掌書記。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Putong, Zhengde received an edict for the northern campaign and took Xie on as recorder of the headquarters, in charge of records.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Putong, Zhengde received an edict for the northern campaign and took him on as recorder of the headquarters, in charge of records.

entries.zh: 鮑泉字潤岳，東海人也。
entries.en: Bao Quan, styled Runyue, came from Donghai.
entries.literal: Bao Quan, styled Runyue, was a native of Donghai.

entries.zh: 父機，湘東王諮議參軍。
entries.en: His father Bao Ji was advisory aide to the Prince of Xiangdong.
entries.literal: His father Ji was advisory aide to the Prince of Xiangdong.

entries.zh: 泉博涉史傳，兼有文筆。
entries.en: Quan ranged broadly through histories and biographies and was also accomplished as a writer.
entries.literal: Quan ranged broadly through histories and biographies and was also accomplished with the brush.

entries.zh: 少事元帝，早見擢任。
entries.en: In youth he served Emperor Yuan and was early selected for appointment.
entries.literal: In youth he served Emperor Yuan and was early selected and appointed.

entries.zh: 及元帝承制，累遷至信州刺史。
entries.en: When Emperor Yuan assumed the regency he was repeatedly promoted to regional inspector of Xinzhou.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yuan assumed the regency he was repeatedly promoted to regional inspector of Xinzhou.

entries.zh: 太清三年，元帝命泉征河東王譽於湘州，泉至長沙，作連城以逼之，譽率衆攻泉，泉據柵堅守，譽不能克。
entries.en: In the third year of Taiqing, Emperor Yuan ordered Quan to campaign against Prince Hedong Xiao Yu in Xiangzhou. Quan reached Changsha and built linked ramparts to press him; Yu led his forces to attack Quan, but Quan held the palisade and defended firmly, and Yu could not overcome him.
entries.literal: In the third year of Taiqing, Emperor Yuan ordered Quan to campaign against Prince Hedong Yu in Xiangzhou. Quan reached Changsha and built linked ramparts to press him; Yu led his host to attack Quan, but Quan held the palisade and defended firmly, and Yu could not overcome him.

entries.zh: 泉因其弊出擊之，譽大敗，盡俘其衆，遂圍其城，久未能拔。
entries.en: Quan, taking advantage of his weakness, sallied forth and struck him; Yu was greatly defeated and his entire force was captured. Quan then besieged his city but for a long time could not take it.
entries.literal: Quan, taking advantage of his weakness, sallied forth and struck him; Yu was greatly defeated and his entire host was captured. Quan then besieged his city but for a long time could not take it.

entries.zh: 世祖乃數泉罪，遣平南將軍王僧辯代泉爲都督。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan then enumerated Quan's crimes and sent General Who Pacifies the South Wang Sengbian to replace Quan as commander-in-chief.
entries.literal: Shizu then enumerated Quan's crimes and sent General Who Pacifies the South Wang Sengbian to replace Quan as commander-in-chief.

entries.zh: 僧辯至，泉愕然，顧左右曰：「得王竟陵助我經略，賊不足平矣。」
entries.en: When Sengbian arrived, Quan was startled and, turning to those at his side, said, "With Wang of Jingling to assist me in strategy, the rebels are not worth pacifying."
entries.literal: When Sengbian arrived, Quan was startled and, turning to those at his side, said, "With Wang of Jingling to assist me in strategy, the rebels are not worth pacifying."

entries.zh: 僧辯旣入，乃背泉而坐，曰：「鮑郎有罪，令旨使我鎖卿，卿勿以故意見期。」
entries.en: Once Sengbian had entered, he sat with his back to Quan and said, "Master Bao is guilty; by command I am to lock you up — do not expect old friendship."
entries.literal: Once Sengbian had entered, he sat with his back to Quan and said, "Master Bao is guilty; by command I am to lock you up — do not expect old friendship."

entries.zh: 因出令示泉，鎖之床下。
entries.en: He then produced the order and showed it to Quan, and locked him beneath the bed.
entries.literal: He then produced the order and showed it to Quan, and locked him beneath the bed.

entries.zh: 泉曰：「稽緩王師，甘罪是分，但恐後人更思鮑泉之憒憒耳。」
entries.en: Quan said, "In delaying the imperial army I accept my share of guilt, but I fear later men will again think of Bao Quan's muddle-headedness."
entries.literal: Quan said, "In delaying the imperial army I accept my share of guilt, but I fear later men will again think of Bao Quan's muddle-headedness."

entries.zh: 乃爲啓謝淹遲之罪。
entries.en: He then composed a memorial apologizing for the offense of delay.
entries.literal: He then composed a memorial apologizing for the offense of delay.

entries.zh: 世祖尋復其任，令與僧辯等率舟師東逼邵陵王於郢州。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan soon restored him to his post and ordered him, together with Sengbian and others, to lead the fleet east and press Prince Shaoling at Yingzhou.
entries.literal: Shizu soon restored him to his post and ordered him, together with Sengbian and others, to lead the fleet east and press Prince Shaoling at Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 郢州平，元帝以長子方諸爲刺史，泉爲長史，行府州事。
entries.en: When Yingzhou was pacified, Emperor Yuan appointed his eldest son Fangzhu regional inspector; Quan was made Chief Clerk and administered the headquarters and province.
entries.literal: When Yingzhou was pacified, Emperor Yuan appointed his eldest son Fangzhu regional inspector; Quan was made Chief Clerk and acted in the affairs of the headquarters and province.

entries.zh: 侯景密遣將宋子仙、任約率精騎襲之。
entries.en: Hou Jing secretly sent his generals Song Zixian and Ren Yue to lead picked cavalry in a surprise attack.
entries.literal: Hou Jing secretly sent his generals Song Zixian and Ren Yue to lead picked cavalry in a surprise attack.

entries.zh: 方諸與泉不恤軍政，唯蒲酒自樂，賊騎至，百姓奔告，方諸與泉方雙陸，不信，曰：「徐文盛大軍在東，賊何由得至？」
entries.en: Fangzhu and Quan paid no attention to military affairs and took their pleasure only in gambling and wine. When the rebel cavalry arrived, the common folk ran to report it; Fangzhu and Quan were just playing backgammon and did not believe it, saying, "Xu Wensheng's great army is in the east — how could the rebels get here?"
entries.literal: Fangzhu and Quan did not attend to military affairs and took their pleasure only in gambling and wine. When the rebel cavalry arrived, the common folk ran to report it; Fangzhu and Quan were just playing backgammon and did not believe it, saying, "Xu Wensheng's great army is in the east — how could the rebels get here?"

entries.zh: 旣而傳告者衆，始令闔門。
entries.en: Before long those who came to report were many, and only then did they order the gates closed.
entries.literal: Before long those who came to report were many, and only then did they order the gates closed.

entries.zh: 賊縱火焚之，莫有抗者，賊騎遂入，城乃陷。
entries.en: The rebels set fires to burn the gates; none resisted, the rebel cavalry then entered, and the city fell.
entries.literal: The rebels set fires to burn them; none resisted, the rebel cavalry then entered, and the city fell.

entries.zh: 執方諸及泉送之景所。
entries.en: They seized Fangzhu and Quan and sent them to Hou Jing's headquarters.
entries.literal: They seized Fangzhu and Quan and sent them to Jing's headquarters.

entries.zh: 後景攻王僧辯於巴陵，不克，敗還，乃殺泉於江夏，沉其屍于黃鵠磯。
entries.en: Later Hou Jing attacked Wang Sengbian at Baling but could not overcome him and returned defeated; he then killed Quan at Jiangxia and cast his corpse into the Huanghe Ford.
entries.literal: Later Jing attacked Wang Sengbian at Baling but could not overcome him and returned defeated; he then killed Quan at Jiangxia and cast his corpse into the Huanghe Ford.

entries.zh: 初，泉之爲南討都督也，其友人夢泉得罪于世祖，覺而告之。
entries.en: Earlier, when Quan was commander-in-chief of the southern campaign, a friend dreamed that Quan had offended Emperor Yuan; on waking he told him.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Quan was commander-in-chief of the southern campaign, a friend dreamed that Quan had offended Shizu; on waking he told him.

entries.zh: 後未旬，果見囚執。
entries.en: Within less than ten days afterward, he was indeed imprisoned.
entries.literal: Within less than ten days afterward, he was indeed seen imprisoned.

entries.zh: 頃之，又夢泉著朱衣而行水上，又告泉曰：「君勿憂，尋得免矣。」
entries.en: Before long he again dreamed that Quan wore red robes and walked upon the water, and again told Quan, "Do not worry — you will soon be released."
entries.literal: Before long he again dreamed that Quan wore red robes and walked upon the water, and again told Quan, "Do not worry — you will soon be released."

entries.zh: 因說其夢，泉密記之，俄而復見任，皆如其夢。
entries.en: He then related the dream; Quan secretly recorded it, and soon afterward was again employed — all as in the dream.
entries.literal: He then related the dream; Quan secretly recorded it, and soon afterward was again employed — all as in the dream.

entries.zh: 太清三年，侯景攻陷臺城，時太宗居永福省，賊衆奔入，舉兵上殿，侍衛奔散，莫有存者。
entries.en: In the third year of Taiqing, Hou Jing captured Terrace City. At that time Emperor Jianwen resided in the Yongfu quarter; the rebel host rushed in, raised arms, and ascended the hall. The guards fled and scattered; none remained.
entries.literal: In the third year of Taiqing, Hou Jing captured and overran Terrace City. At that time Taizong resided in the Yongfu quarter; the rebel host rushed in, raised arms, and ascended the hall. The guards fled and scattered; none remained.

entries.zh: 摛獨嶷然侍立不動，徐謂景曰：「侯公當以禮見，何得如此。」
entries.en: Chi alone stood attendant, lofty and unmoving, and slowly said to Jing, "Lord Hou ought to be received with proper ceremony — how can you act like this?"
entries.literal: Chi alone stood attendant, lofty and unmoving, and slowly said to Jing, "Lord Hou ought to be received with rites — how can you act like this?"

entries.zh: 凶威遂折。
entries.en: His fierce authority was thereby broken.
entries.literal: His fierce authority was thereby broken.

entries.zh: 侯景乃拜，由是常憚摛。
entries.en: Hou Jing then bowed; from this he always feared Chi.
entries.literal: Hou Jing then bowed; from this he always feared Chi.

entries.zh: 太宗嗣位，進授左衛將軍，固辭不拜。
entries.en: When Emperor Jianwen succeeded to the throne, Chi was advanced to General of the Left Guard, but he firmly declined and did not accept.
entries.literal: When Taizong succeeded to the throne, Chi was advanced and given the post of General of the Left Guard, but he firmly declined and did not accept.

entries.zh: 太宗後被幽閉，摛不獲朝謁，因感氣疾而卒，年七十八。
entries.en: Later Emperor Jianwen was confined in seclusion; Chi could not attend court and, afflicted by illness, died at the age of seventy-eight.
entries.literal: Later Taizong was confined in seclusion; Chi could not attend court audience and, afflicted by a disorder of the vital breath, died, age seventy-eight.

entries.zh: 長子陵，最知名。
entries.en: His eldest son Xu Ling was the most famous.
entries.literal: His eldest son Ling was the most famous.

entries.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：阮孝緒常言，仲尼論四科，始乎德行，終乎文學。
entries.en: Yao Cha, Director of the Ministry of Personnel of Chen, said: Ruan Xiaoxu often said that in Confucius's discussion of the four categories, he began with virtue and conduct and ended with letters and learning.
entries.literal: Yao Cha, Director of the Ministry of Personnel of Chen, said: Ruan Xiaoxu often said that in Confucius's discussion of the four categories, he began with virtue and conduct and ended with letters and learning.

entries.zh: 有行者多尚質樸，有文者少蹈規矩，故衛、石靡餘論可傳，屈、賈無立德之譽。
entries.en: Those with conduct mostly esteem plain simplicity; those with letters seldom tread within rules. Therefore Wei and Shi have no remaining discourse worth handing down, while Qu Yuan and Jia Yi have no reputation for establishing virtue.
entries.literal: Those with conduct mostly esteem plain simplicity; those with letters seldom tread within rules. Therefore Wei and Shi have no remaining discourse worth handing down, while Qu and Jia have no reputation for establishing virtue.

entries.zh: 若夫憲章游、夏，祖述回、騫，體兼文行，於裴幾原見之矣。
entries.en: In modeling oneself on Ziyou and Zixia, following in the footsteps of Yan Hui and Min Ziqian, and combining literary talent with moral conduct — all of this we see in Pei Jiyuan.
entries.literal: As for taking You and Xia as models, tracing back to Yan and Qian, embodying both letters and conduct — in Pei Jiyuan we have seen it.

entries.zh: 梁書卷第三十 列傳第二十四
entries.en: Book of Liang, Volume 30, Biography 24
entries.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 30, Biography 24

entries.zh: 齊初，起家冠軍安成王行參軍，遷征虜主簿，太子舍人，王儉鎮軍府功曹史。
entries.en: When Qi was founded he began his career as acting aide in the household of the Prince of Ancheng, General Who Conquers Champions, then rose to registrar under the General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, attendant of the heir apparent, and merit clerk on Wang Jian's Pacifying-Army staff.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qi he entered service as Acting Aide to the General Who Conquers Champions, Prince of Ancheng, and was promoted to Registrar of the General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and Clerk in the Merit Office of Wang Jian's Pacifying-Army headquarters.

entries.zh: 儉時爲京尹，經於後堂獨引見昂，指北堂謂昂曰：「卿必居此。」
entries.en: Jian was serving as metropolitan governor. One day, passing through the rear hall, he received Ang alone and, pointing to the north hall, said, "You will surely sit in that seat one day."
entries.literal: Jian was then Metropolitan Governor; passing through the rear hall he summoned Ang alone and, pointing to the north hall, said to him, "You will surely dwell here."

entries.zh: 累遷秘書丞，黃門侍郎。
entries.en: He was promoted in turn to secretary of the palace library and gentleman of the yellow gate.
entries.literal: He was promoted in succession to Secretary of the Palace Library and Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

entries.zh: 昂本名千里，齊永明中，武帝謂之曰：「昂昂千里之駒，在卿有之，今改卿名爲昂，卽千里爲字。」
entries.en: Ang had originally been named Qianli. During Qi's Yongming reign, Emperor Wu told him, "The horse that travels a thousand li in a day — that is what you are. I now change your given name to Ang, and let Qianli be your style."
entries.literal: Ang's original given name was Qianli. In the Yongming era of Qi, Emperor Wu said to him, "A steed that goes a thousand li in a day — you have one in you. I now change your given name to Ang, and Qianli shall be your style."

entries.zh: 出爲安南鄱陽王長史、尋陽公相。
entries.en: He was sent out as chief clerk to the Prince of Poyang, General Who Pacifies the South, and as chancellor to the Duke of Xunyang.
entries.literal: He went out as Chief Clerk to the Prince of Poyang, General Who Pacifies the South, and Chancellor to the Duke of Xunyang.

entries.zh: 還爲太孫中庶子、衛軍武陵王長史。
entries.en: On returning to court he was made junior mentor to the grand heir apparent and chief clerk to the Prince of Wuling, General of the Guard.
entries.literal: On his return he became Junior Mentor to the Grand Heir Apparent and Chief Clerk to the Prince of Wuling, General of the Guard.

entries.zh: 服闋，除右軍邵陵王長史，俄遷御史中丞。
entries.en: When his mourning ended he was made chief clerk to the Prince of Shaoling, General of the Right Army, and soon afterward promoted to imperial censor.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Chief Clerk to the Prince of Shaoling, General of the Right Army, and soon promoted to Imperial Censor.

entries.zh: 時尚書令王晏弟詡爲廣州，多納賕貨，昂依事劾奏，不憚權豪，當時號爲正直。
entries.en: Wang Yan's younger brother Xu was then in Guangzhou and took heavy bribes; Ang impeached him on the facts without fear of the powerful, and men of the day called him upright.
entries.literal: At the time the younger brother of the Director of the Department of State Affairs Wang Yan, Xu, was in Guangzhou and took many bribes; Ang impeached him according to the facts, not fearing the powerful, and at the time was called upright.

entries.zh: 出爲豫章內史，丁所生母憂去職。
entries.en: He was sent out as internal administrator of Yuzhang and left office when his birth mother died.
entries.literal: He went out as Internal Administrator of Yuzhang and left office on the death of his biological mother.

entries.zh: 以喪還，江路風浪暴駭，昂乃縛衣著柩，誓同沉溺。
entries.en: On the journey home with the coffin, violent storms struck the river route; Ang tied his clothes to the bier and swore to drown with it.
entries.literal: Returning with the coffin, the river route was struck by violent wind and waves; Ang bound his garments to the bier and vowed to sink together with it.

entries.zh: 及風止，餘船皆沒，唯昂所乘船獲全，咸謂精誠所致。
entries.en: When the wind died down every other boat had sunk; only Ang's was spared, and all attributed it to his sincerity.
entries.literal: When the wind stopped, the other boats all sank; only the boat Ang was on was spared, and all said it was due to his sincerity.

entries.zh: 葬訖，起爲建武將軍、吳興太守。
entries.en: After the funeral he was recalled as General Who Establishes Might and administrator of Wuxing.
entries.literal: After the burial he was recalled as General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Wuxing.

entries.zh: 永元末，義師至京師，州牧郡守皆望風降款，昂獨拒境不受命。
entries.en: At the end of the Yongyuan reign the army of righteousness reached the capital; governors and administrators everywhere surrendered at the first rumor, but Ang alone closed his borders and refused to obey.
entries.literal: At the end of Yongyuan the righteous army reached the capital; provincial governors and commandery administrators all surrendered at the first rumor, but Ang alone barred his borders and would not accept orders.

entries.zh: 高祖手書喻曰：「夫禍福無門，興亡有數，天之所棄，人孰能匡？
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu wrote to him in his own hand: "Fortune and disaster have no fixed door; rise and fall follow Heaven's reckoning. What Heaven has cast off — who can set right?
entries.literal: The High Ancestor wrote in his own hand to instruct him, saying, "Fortune and misfortune have no fixed gate; rise and fall follow a number. What Heaven abandons — who can set right?

entries.zh: 機來不再，圖之宜早。
entries.en: Opportunity does not come twice; you should act while you can.
entries.literal: Opportunity does not come twice; you should plan early.

entries.zh: 頃藉聽道路，承欲狼顧一隅，旣未悉雅懷，聊申往意。
entries.en: Lately, from what travelers report, I hear you mean to hold one corner and look back in hesitation; since I do not yet know your mind, I briefly state my purpose.
