entries.literal: Recently, relying on what the roads report, I hear you wish to look back like a wolf upon one corner; since I do not yet fully know your refined intent, I briefly set forth my former purpose.

entries.zh: 獨夫狂悖，振古未聞，窮凶極虐，歲月滋甚。
entries.en: The tyrant is mad and perverse beyond anything antiquity records; his cruelty grows worse with every month.
entries.literal: The lone tyrant is mad and perverse, unheard of since antiquity; his extremity of cruelty grows month by month.

entries.zh: 天未絕齊，聖明啟運，兆民有賴，百姓來蘇。
entries.en: Heaven has not abandoned Qi; a sage ruler has begun his mandate; the people have someone to lean on; the common folk are coming back to life.
entries.literal: Heaven has not cut off Qi; a sage and enlightened ruler opens his mandate; the myriad people have one to rely on; the common folk revive.

entries.zh: 吾荷任前驅，掃除京邑，方撥亂反正，伐罪弔民，至止以來，前無橫陣。
entries.en: I bear the charge as vanguard to clear the capital, to set chaos aright, punish the guilty, and comfort the people; since I arrived no force has blocked our advance.
entries.literal: I bear the charge as vanguard, sweeping clean the capital region, now setting chaos aright and returning to the correct, punishing crime and comforting the people; since I arrived, no army has stood in my path.

entries.zh: 今皇威四臨，長圍已合，遐邇畢集，人神同奮。
entries.en: Imperial authority now commands every quarter; the long siege is closed; the near and the far have all gathered; men and spirits fight as one.
entries.literal: Now imperial majesty faces on four sides, the long encirclement is closed; far and near all gather; men and spirits strive together.

entries.zh: 銳卒萬計，鐵馬千羣，以此攻戰，何往不克。
entries.en: Tens of thousands of elite troops, thousands of squadrons of armored horse — with such a force, what could fail to fall?
entries.literal: Keen soldiers by the tens of thousands, iron horses in thousands of squadrons — with these to attack, where would we not conquer?

entries.zh: 況建業孤城，人懷離阻，面縛軍門，日夕相繼，屠潰之期，勢不云遠。
entries.en: Jianye is but a lone city; hearts within are divided; men come day and night to surrender at the camp gate — the day of its fall cannot be far off.
entries.literal: Moreover Jianye is a lone city; men's hearts are divided and blocked; those who bind themselves at the camp gate follow one after another day and night — the day of slaughter and rout cannot be said to be far.

entries.zh: 兼熒惑出端門，太白入氐室，天文表於上，人事符於下，不謀同契，寔在茲辰。
entries.en: Mars has left the Gate of Beginning and Venus has entered the Chamber of Di — Heaven shows the sign above and human affairs match below; to join in one accord needs no further counsel — the moment is now.
entries.literal: Moreover the Sparkling Deluder has left the Gate of Beginning, and the Great White has entered the Chamber of Di — the heavens show it above, human affairs match below; to join in accord without counsel — truly the time is now.

entries.zh: 且范岫、申胄，久薦誠款，各率所由，仍爲掎角，沈法瑀、孫肸、朱端，已先肅清吳會，而足下欲以區區之郡，禦堂堂之師，根本旣傾，枝葉安附？
entries.en: Fan Xiu and Shen Zhou have long pledged their loyalty; each leads his forces and forms a pincer with us. Shen Faying, Sun Xi, and Zhu Duan have already cleared Wu and Kuaiji — yet you would hold one small commandery against a great army? When the root is down, what can the branches cling to?
entries.literal: Moreover Fan Xiu and Shen Zhou have long offered sincere allegiance; each leads his following and still forms pincers. Shen Faying, Sun Xi, and Zhu Duan have already first pacified Wu and Kuaiji — yet you wish to oppose a grand army with one small commandery? When the root is already toppled, how can the branches still cling?

entries.zh: 童兒牧豎，咸謂其非，求之明鑒，實所未達。
entries.en: Even children and herd boys say this is wrong; I ask your clear judgment, for I truly do not see your purpose.
entries.literal: Children and herd boys all say it is wrong; I seek your clear mirror — I truly do not understand.

entries.zh: 今竭力昏主，未足爲忠，家門屠滅，非所謂孝，忠孝俱盡，將欲何依？
entries.en: To exhaust yourself for a benighted ruler is no true loyalty; to see your house destroyed is no filial piety — when both are gone, what will you lean on?
entries.literal: Now to exhaust yourself for a benighted lord is not enough to count as loyalty; to have your clan slaughtered is not what is called filial piety — when loyalty and filial piety are both exhausted, what will you lean on?

entries.zh: 豈若翻然改圖，自招多福，進則遠害全身，退則長守祿位。
entries.en: Better to change course at once and win great fortune — advance and you escape harm with body whole; hold back and you keep rank and stipend for long.
entries.literal: How much better to turn your plan about at once and invite much good fortune — advance and you keep far from harm with body intact; retreat and you long keep rank and stipend.

entries.zh: 去就之宜，幸加詳擇。
entries.en: Whether to stay or go — I hope you will choose with care.
entries.literal: The fitness of staying or going — I hope you will choose with care.

entries.zh: 若執迷遂往，同惡不悛，大軍一臨，誅及三族。
entries.en: If you cling to error and go on with the wicked without repenting, when the great army comes punishment will reach three generations of your kin.
entries.literal: If you cling to error and go on, sharing evil without repentance, when the great army arrives punishment will reach three clans.

entries.zh: 雖貽後悔，寧復云補？
entries.en: Regret afterward will mend nothing.
entries.literal: Though you leave regret behind, can it still be said to mend matters?

entries.zh: 欲布所懷，故致今白。」
entries.en: I write to lay my mind before you."
entries.literal: Wishing to set forth what I feel, I therefore send this present note."

entries.zh: 昂答曰：「都史至，辱誨。
entries.en: Ang replied: "Your envoy from the capital has arrived — I am honored by your letter.
entries.literal: Ang replied, "The capital clerk has arrived — I am honored by your instruction.

entries.zh: 承藉以衆論，謂僕有勤王之舉，兼蒙誚責，獨無送款，循復嚴旨，若臨萬仞。
entries.en: I hear the common talk that I am raising troops to rescue the throne, and your rebuke that I alone have not surrendered. I read your stern command again as if standing before a cliff ten thousand ren high.
entries.literal: I receive, relying on common talk, that people say I have the act of rescuing the king; I am also favored with reproach that I alone have not offered surrender. I follow again your stern command as if facing ten thousand ren.

entries.zh: 三吳內地，非用兵之所，況以偏隅一郡，何能爲役？
entries.en: The Three Wu is heartland, not a field for armies — how could one remote commandery be of any use?
entries.literal: The Three Wu region is inner territory, not a place for deploying troops — how much less could one remote commandery serve as a tool?

entries.zh: 近奉敕，以此境多虞，見使安慰。
entries.en: I have lately received an edict, because this region is troubled, appointing me to reassure the people.
entries.literal: Recently I received an edict that because this region has many troubles, I was sent to offer reassurance.

entries.zh: 自承麾旆屆止，莫不膝袒軍門，惟僕一人敢後至者，政以內揆庸素，文武無施，直是東國賤男子耳。
entries.en: Since your banners arrived, everyone has bared the knee at your camp gate — only I dared to come last, because I know myself mediocre and useless in civil and military matters, a mere low fellow from the east.
entries.literal: Since your banners arrived, none have failed to bare the knee at the camp gate — only I alone dared to come late, truly because inwardly I measure my mediocrity and plainness, with nothing to offer in civil or martial affairs — I am simply a low fellow of the eastern states.

entries.zh: 雖欲獻心，不增大師之勇；
entries.en: Though I wished to offer my loyalty, it would not add to your army's strength;
entries.literal: Though I wished to offer my heart, it would not increase the Grand Master's courage;

entries.zh: 置其愚默，寧沮衆軍之威。
entries.en: and my silence would only damp the army's prestige.
entries.literal: leave my stupidity and silence — would it not rather damp the army's prestige?

entries.zh: 幸藉將軍含弘之大，可得從容以禮。
entries.en: I trust in your breadth of mind and hope to be treated with courtesy.
entries.literal: Fortunately, relying on the general's breadth and forbearance, I may be treated with courtesy at ease.

entries.zh: 竊以一飡微施，尚復投殞，況食人之祿，而頓忘一旦。
entries.en: For a single meal's kindness men will lay down their lives — how then can one who has eaten the ruler's stipend forget it overnight?
entries.literal: I venture that for one meal's small favor men still cast away their lives — how much more when one has eaten another's stipend, to forget it in a morning?

entries.zh: 非惟物議不可，亦恐明公鄙之，所以躊躇，未遑薦璧。
entries.en: Public opinion would not permit it, and I fear you would despise me for it — that is why I hesitate and have not yet come to offer surrender.
entries.literal: It is not only that public opinion would not permit it; I also fear that my lord would despise me for it — therefore I hesitate and have not yet offered the surrender jade.

entries.zh: 遂以輕微，爰降重命，震灼于心，忘其所厝，誠推理鑒，猶懼威臨。」
entries.en: Because I am insignificant you have sent so weighty a command; it burns in my heart and leaves me unsure where I stand — even by your clear judgment I still fear your authority."
entries.literal: Thus because I am slight, you have bestowed a weighty command; it sears my heart and I forget where I stand — truly, reasoning by your mirror, I still fear your majesty descending."

entries.zh: 建康城平，昂束身詣闕，高祖宥之不問也。
entries.en: When Jiankang fell, Ang went to court of his own accord; Emperor Gaozu pardoned him and asked nothing further.
entries.literal: When Jiankang fell, Ang bound himself and went to the palace; the High Ancestor pardoned him and did not question him.

entries.zh: 高祖答曰：「朕遺射鉤，卿無自外。」
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu replied: "I forgive the arrow that struck the hook — do not hold yourself apart."
entries.literal: The High Ancestor replied, "I leave behind the arrow that struck the hook — do not put yourself outside."

entries.zh: 俄除給事黃門侍郎。
entries.en: He was soon appointed attendant gentleman of the yellow gate.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

entries.zh: 其年遷侍中。
entries.en: That same year he was promoted to palace attendant.
entries.literal: That year he was transferred to Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 明年，出爲尋陽太守，行江州事。
entries.en: The following year he was sent out as administrator of Xunyang and acted as inspector of Jiang province.
entries.literal: The next year he went out as Administrator of Xunyang and acted as Inspector of Jiang province.

entries.zh: 六年，徵爲吏部尚書，累表陳讓，徙爲左民尚書，兼右僕射。
entries.en: In the sixth year he was recalled as director of the Ministry of Personnel; he repeatedly memorialized to decline and was transferred to director of the Left Bureau of the People, with an additional appointment as vice director of the right.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he was summoned as Director of the Ministry of Personnel; he submitted memorials repeatedly declining and was moved to Director of the Left Bureau of the People, also serving as Vice Director of the Right.

entries.zh: 七年，除國子祭酒，兼僕射如故，領豫州大中正。
entries.en: In the seventh year he was made libationer of the imperial university while keeping his vice directorship, and headed the grand assessor of Yu province.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Libationer of the Imperial University, retaining his vice directorship as before, and heading the Grand Assessor of Yu province.

entries.zh: 八年，出爲仁威將軍、吳郡太守。
entries.en: In the eighth year he was sent out as General of Humane Might and administrator of Wu commandery.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he went out as General of Humane Might and Administrator of Wu commandery.

entries.zh: 十一年，入爲五兵尚書，復兼右僕射，未拜，有詔卽真封。
entries.en: In the eleventh year he returned as director of the Five Armies and again as vice director of the right; before he could take up the latter post, an edict made the appointment substantive.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year he entered court as Director of the Five Armies, again concurrently Vice Director of the Right; before he had received appointment, an edict made the concurrent post substantive.

entries.zh: 尋以本官領起部尚書，加侍中。
entries.en: Soon he also headed the Ministry of Commencements in addition to his existing post, and was given the additional title of palace attendant.
entries.literal: Soon, on the basis of his present office, he headed the Ministry of Commencements and was given the additional title Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 十四年，馬仙琕破魏軍於朐山，詔權假昂節，往勞軍。
entries.en: In the fourteenth year Ma Xiancai defeated the Wei army at Qushan; Ang was given provisional authority by edict to go and comfort the troops.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year Ma Xiancai defeated the Wei army at Qushan; an edict provisionally granted Ang the staff of authority to go and comfort the troops.

entries.zh: 十五年，遷左僕射，尋爲尚書令、宣惠將軍。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to vice director of the left, and soon became director of the Department of State Affairs and General Who Proclaims Favor.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Left, and soon became Director of the Department of State Affairs and General Who Proclaims Favor.

entries.zh: 普通三年，爲中書監、丹陽尹。
entries.en: In the third year of Putong he was appointed supervisor of the palace secretariat and metropolitan governor of Danyang.
entries.literal: In the third year of Putong he was made Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat and Metropolitan Governor of Danyang.

entries.zh: 其年進號中衛將軍，復爲尚書令，卽本號開府儀同三司，給鼓吹，未拜，又領國子祭酒。
entries.en: That year he was advanced to General of the Central Guard and again made director of the Department of State Affairs; on that basis he was granted the privilege of an office equal to the three excellencies, with martial music; before taking up the latter honor he also headed the imperial university as libationer.
entries.literal: That year his title was advanced to General of the Central Guard; he again became Director of the Department of State Affairs, and on the basis of that title was made Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies with an office of his own, granted martial music; before he had received appointment he also headed the Libationer of the Imperial University.

entries.zh: 大通元年，加中書監，給親信三十人。
entries.en: In the first year of Datong he was given the additional title of supervisor of the palace secretariat and thirty personal attendants.
entries.literal: In the first year of Datong he was given the additional title Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat and granted thirty personal attendants.

entries.zh: 尋表解祭酒，進號中撫軍大將軍，遷司空、侍中、尚書令，親信、鼓吹並如故。
entries.en: Soon he memorialized to resign as libationer, was advanced to grand general who pacifies the central army, and was made minister of works, palace attendant, and director of the Department of State Affairs; his attendants and martial music remained unchanged.
entries.literal: Soon he memorialized to resign as libationer, was advanced to Grand General Who Pacifies the Army of the Center, and was transferred to Minister of Works, Palace Attendant, and Director of the Department of State Affairs; his personal attendants and martial music remained as before.

entries.zh: 五年，加特進、左光祿大夫，增親信爲八十人。
entries.en: In the fifth year he was given the additional titles of exceptional promotion and grand master of splendid happiness of the left, and his personal attendants were increased to eighty.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he was given the additional titles Exceptional Promotion and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Left, and his personal attendants were increased to eighty.

entries.zh: 大同六年，薨，時年八十。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Datong he died, at the age of eighty.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Datong he died; he was then eighty.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「侍中、特進、左光祿大夫、司空昂，奄至薨逝，惻怛於懷。
entries.en: An edict said: "Palace Attendant, Exceptional Promotion, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Left, and Minister of Works Ang has died suddenly — our hearts are pierced with sorrow.
entries.literal: An edict said, "Palace Attendant, Exceptional Promotion, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Left, Minister of Works Ang has suddenly come to his end — our hearts are pierced with sorrow.

entries.zh: 公器珝凝素，志誠貞方，端朝燮理，嘉猷載緝。
entries.en: His talent was bright and unadorned, his will sincere and upright; at court he helped harmonize governance, and good counsel flowed from him in succession.
entries.literal: His public vessel was bright and plain; his will sincere and upright; at court he harmonized governance, and fine plans were gathered in succession.

entries.zh: 追榮表德，實惟令典。
entries.en: To honor him posthumously and display his virtue is indeed the proper precedent.
entries.literal: To pursue honor and display virtue is truly the excellent standard.

entries.zh: 可贈本官，鼓吹一部，給東園秘器，朝服一具，衣一襲，錢二十萬，絹布一百匹，蠟二百斤，卽日舉哀。」
entries.en: Let him be posthumously granted his present offices, one set of martial music, the secret funerary implements of the Eastern Garden, one set of court robes, one suit of garments, two hundred thousand cash, one hundred bolts of silk and cloth, and two hundred jin of wax — mourning is to begin this day."
entries.literal: He may be posthumously granted his present offices, one set of martial music, the secret implements of the Eastern Garden, one set of court robes, one suit of garments, two hundred thousand in cash, one hundred bolts of silk and cloth, two hundred jin of wax — mourning is to begin this day."

entries.zh: 天監二年，以爲後軍臨川王參軍事。
entries.en: In the second year of Tianjian he was appointed aide in the household of the Prince of Linchuan, Rear Army.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianjian he was made Aide to the Rear Army, Prince of Linchuan.

entries.zh: 昂奉啟謝曰：「恩降絕望之辰，慶集寒心之日，焰灰非喻，荑枯未擬，摳衣聚足，顛狽不勝。
entries.en: Ang submitted a memorial of thanks: "Grace has come when I had abandoned hope; joy has gathered on the day my heart was cold — no image of flame and ash, no likeness of sprout and withered stalk — I gather my robe and stand trembling, unable to bear the weight of it.
entries.literal: Ang submitted a memorial of thanks, saying, "Favor descends in the hour of utter hopelessness; joy gathers on the day of a frozen heart — flame and ash are no likeness, sprout and withered stalk no comparison; I gather my robe and stand on tiptoe, overwhelmed and unable to bear up.

entries.zh: 臣遍歷三墳，備詳六典，巡校賞罰之科，調檢生死之律，莫不嚴五辟於明君之朝，峻三章於聖人之世。
entries.en: I have studied the Three Archives and mastered the Six Canons, reviewed the rules of reward and punishment and the laws of life and death — in every enlightened reign the five punishments are strict, and in every sage age the three statutes are severe.
entries.literal: Your servant has gone through the Three Archives and examined in full the Six Canons, reviewing the categories of reward and punishment and adjusting the statutes of life and death — none fail to make strict the five punishments in the court of an enlightened lord and steep the three chapters in the age of a sage.

entries.zh: 是以塗山始會，致防風之誅；
entries.en: At the first assembly at Mount Tu, Fangfeng was executed;
entries.literal: Therefore at the first assembly at Tushan came the execution of Fangfeng;

entries.zh: 酆邑方構，有崇侯之伐。
entries.en: when Feng was first being built, the Marquis of Chong was attacked.
entries.literal: when Feng was just being built, there was the campaign against the Marquis of Chong.

entries.zh: 未有緩憲於斫戮之人，賒刑於耐罪之族，出萬死入一生如臣者也。
entries.en: Never was the law eased for one marked for execution, nor punishment deferred for a lesser offender — to pass from ten thousand deaths into one life, as I have, is without precedent.
entries.literal: Never has the law been relaxed for one marked for the axe, nor punishment deferred for a clan bearing lesser guilt — to pass out of ten thousand deaths into one life, like your servant, has not occurred.

entries.zh: 推恩及罪，在臣實大，披心瀝血，敢乞言之。
entries.en: To extend grace even to the guilty is for me a vast mercy; with heart laid open and blood poured out, I dare speak of it.
entries.literal: To extend grace even to the guilty — for your servant it is truly great; I lay open my heart and drain my blood, and dare beg to speak of it.

entries.zh: 臣東國賤人，學行何取，旣殊鳴雁直木，故無結綬彈冠，徒藉羽儀，易農就仕。
entries.en: I am a low fellow from the east — what learning or conduct can I offer? Unlike the goose that answers the straight timber, I never tied my ribbons or dusted my cap for office; I merely borrowed rank and left farming for service.
entries.literal: Your servant is a low man of the eastern states — what learning or conduct have I to offer? Unlike the calling goose on straight timber, I have no tying of ribbons or flicking of caps; I merely borrowed insignia of office and changed from farming to service.

entries.zh: 往年濫職，守秩東隅，仰屬龔行，風驅電掩。
entries.en: In former years I held office unworthily in the east, looking up to join the righteous march that swept like wind and lightning.
entries.literal: In former years I held office unworthily, keeping rank in the eastern corner, looking up to belong to the righteous march — wind-driven, lightning-swift.

entries.zh: 當其時也，負鼎圖者日至，執玉帛者相望。
entries.en: In those days men bearing tribute came day after day, and envoys with jade and silk were seen in endless succession.
entries.literal: At that time those who bore the cauldron and the map came day by day; those who held jade and silk were seen one after another.

entries.zh: 獨在愚臣，頓昏大義，殉鴻毛之輕，忘同德之重。
entries.en: Alone I, foolish as I am, was suddenly blind to the great cause, ready to die for a feather's weight and forget the bond of shared virtue.
entries.literal: Alone among them was this foolish servant, suddenly blind to the great principle, dying for the lightness of a goose feather and forgetting the weight of shared virtue.

entries.zh: 但三吳險薄，五湖交通，屢起田儋之變，每懼殷通之禍，空慕君魚保境，遂失師涓抱器。
entries.en: But the Three Wu are treacherous and the Five Lakes link by water; revolts like Tian Dan's have risen again and again, and I always feared a disaster like Yin Tong's. I vainly admired those who held their borders and failed to embrace the cause as a true minister should.
entries.literal: But the Three Wu are perilous and shallow, the Five Lakes connect by water — Tian Dan's revolts have risen again and again; I always feared Yin Tong's disaster; I vainly admired Lord Yu's guarding his borders and so failed to embrace the vessel like Master Juan.

entries.zh: 後至者斬，臣甘斯戮。
entries.en: "He who comes late is beheaded" — I willingly accept that sentence.
entries.literal: "He who comes late is beheaded" — your servant willingly accepts that punishment.

entries.zh: 明刑徇衆，誰曰不然。
entries.en: To enforce the law for the sake of the people — who would deny it?
entries.literal: To make clear the punishments and follow the multitude — who would say otherwise?

entries.zh: 幸約法之弘，承解網之宥，猶當降等薪粲，遂乃頓釋鉗赭。
entries.en: By your merciful law I receive the pardon that loosens the net — I ought still to be reduced to the lowest rank, yet suddenly my chains and marks are gone.
entries.literal: Fortunately the contracted law is broad; I receive the pardon that loosens the net — I ought still to be reduced to the rank of fuel and fodder, yet suddenly the fetters and red dye are cast off.

entries.zh: 斂骨吹魂，還編黔庶，濯疵蕩穢，入楚游陳，天波旣洗，雲油遽沐。
entries.en: My bones are gathered and my soul revived; I am enrolled again among the people; my stains are washed away. I enter Chu and wander Chen — Heaven's waves have washed over me, and sudden blessing rains down.
entries.literal: Gathering bones and reviving the soul, I return to the rolls of the black-haired folk; washing flaws and sweeping filth, I enter Chu and wander Chen — Heaven's waves have washed me, cloud oil suddenly anoints me.

entries.zh: 古人有言：『非死之難，處死之難。』
entries.en: The ancients said: "Dying is not the hard part — living afterward is the hard part."
entries.literal: The ancients said, "It is not dying that is hard — it is how one meets death that is hard."

entries.zh: 臣之所荷，曠古不書；
entries.en: What I have received is unrecorded since antiquity;
entries.literal: What your servant bears has not been written since vast antiquity;

entries.zh: 臣之死所，未知何地。」
entries.en: and where I shall die — I do not yet know."
entries.literal: the place where your servant will die — I do not yet know where it is."

entries.zh: 史臣曰：夫天尊地卑，以定君臣之位；
entries.en: The historiographer says: Heaven is honored and earth is low — by this the positions of ruler and minister are fixed;
entries.literal: The historiographer says: Heaven is honored and earth is low — thereby the positions of lord and minister are fixed;

entries.zh: 松筠等質，無革歲寒之心。
entries.en: pine and bamboo are of such substance that they do not change their hearts when the year turns cold.
entries.literal: pine and bamboo share their substance — they have no heart that changes with the cold of the year.

entries.zh: 袁千里命屬崩離，身逢厄季，雖獨夫喪德，臣志不移；
entries.en: Yuan Qianli's fate was bound to collapse; he lived in a time of disaster — though the tyrant had lost virtue, his loyalty as a minister did not waver;
entries.literal: Yuan Qianli's fate belonged to collapse and separation; his person met a season of calamity — though the lone tyrant lost virtue, the minister's will did not shift;

entries.zh: 及抗疏高祖，無虧忠節，斯亦存夷、叔之風矣。
entries.en: when he stood firm in his memorial to Emperor Gaozu without failing in loyalty — this too preserves the spirit of Boyi and Shuqi.
entries.literal: when he resisted in memorial to the High Ancestor without impairing loyal integrity — this too preserves the spirit of Boyi and Shuqi.

entries.zh: 終爲梁室台鼎，何其美焉。
entries.en: In the end he became a pillar of the Liang state — how admirable!
entries.literal: In the end he became the pillar and tripod of the Liang house — how fine!

entries.zh: 子君正，美風儀，善自居處，以貴公子得當世名譽。
entries.en: His son Junzheng had fine bearing and knew how to comport himself; as a nobleman's son he won reputation in his day.
entries.literal: His son Junzheng had fine bearing and deportment, was skilled in conducting himself, and as a nobleman's son gained reputation in his time.

entries.zh: 頃之，兼吏部郎，以母憂去職。
entries.en: Soon he also served as gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel and left office when his mother died.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he concurrently served as Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel and left office on his mother's death.

entries.zh: 服闋，爲邵陵王友、北中郎長史、東陽太守。
entries.en: When mourning ended he was companion to the Prince of Shaoling, chief clerk to the North General of the Center, and administrator of Dongyang.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he became Companion to the Prince of Shaoling, Chief Clerk to the North General of the Center, and Administrator of Dongyang.

entries.zh: 尋徵還都，郡民徵士徐天祐等三百人詣闕乞留一年，詔不許，仍除豫章內史，尋轉吳郡太守。
entries.en: Soon he was recalled to the capital; three hundred men of the commandery, including the scholar Xu Tianyou, went to court asking that he stay another year — the emperor refused; he was appointed internal administrator of Yuzhang and soon transferred to administrator of Wu.
entries.literal: Soon he was summoned back to the capital; three hundred men of the commandery, including the reclusive scholar Xu Tianyou, went to the palace gate asking that he be kept one more year — an edict did not permit it; he was still appointed Internal Administrator of Yuzhang, and soon transferred to Administrator of Wu commandery.

entries.zh: 侯景亂，率數百人隨邵陵王赴援，及京城陷，還郡。
entries.en: When Hou Jing rebelled, he led several hundred men with the Prince of Shaoling to relieve the capital; when the capital fell, he returned to his commandery.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, he led several hundred men following the Prince of Shaoling to the rescue; when the capital fell, he returned to his commandery.

entries.zh: 梁書卷第三十一 列傳第二十五
entries.en: Book of Liang, Volume 31, Biographies 25
entries.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 31, Biographies 25

entries.zh: 陳慶之字子雲，義興國山人也。
entries.en: Chen Qingzhi, styled Ziyun, came from Guoshan in Yixing commandery.
entries.literal: Chen Qingzhi, styled Ziyun, was a native of Guoshan in Yixing.

entries.zh: 幼而隨從高祖。
entries.en: From childhood he attended Emperor Wu.
entries.literal: In his youth he followed and attended the High Ancestor.

entries.zh: 高祖性好棊，每從夜達旦不輟，等輩皆倦寐，惟慶之不寢，聞呼卽至，甚見親賞。
entries.en: Emperor Wu loved weiqi and often played from dusk until dawn. His attendants all fell asleep from exhaustion, but Qingzhi alone stayed awake and answered every summons—behind this lay deep personal regard.
entries.literal: The High Ancestor loved weiqi; he would play from night until dawn without stopping, and his companions all grew weary and slept, but only Qingzhi did not sleep; at a call he would arrive at once, and was greatly favored and prized.

entries.zh: 從高祖東下平建鄴，稍爲主書，散財聚士，常思效用。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu marched east to take Jianye, Qingzhi followed. He rose to chief secretary, spent his fortune gathering followers, and always looked for a chance to prove himself.
entries.literal: Following the High Ancestor east to pacify Jianye, he gradually became Chief Secretary, dispersed his wealth to gather gentlemen, and constantly thought of rendering service.

entries.zh: 除奉朝請。
entries.en: He was made a palace attendant.
entries.literal: He was appointed Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 大通元年，隸領軍曹仲宗伐渦陽。
entries.en: In the first year of Datong he served under Commander-in-Chief Cao Zhongzong in the attack on Guoyang.
entries.literal: In the first year of Datong, he was attached to the army of the Commander-in-Chief Cao Zhongzong in the campaign against Guoyang.

entries.zh: 魏遣征南將軍常山王元昭等率馬步十五萬來援，前軍至駝澗，去渦陽四十里。
entries.en: Wei sent General Who Conquers the South Prince Zhao of Changshan and others with a hundred and fifty thousand cavalry and infantry. The vanguard reached Tuojian, forty li from Guoyang.
entries.literal: Wei sent the General Who Conquers the South, Prince Zhao of Changshan, Yuan Zhao, and others with one hundred fifty thousand horse and foot to relieve the city; the vanguard reached Tuojian, forty li from Guoyang.

entries.zh: 慶之欲逆戰，韋放以賊之前鋒必是輕銳，與戰若捷，不足爲功，如其不利，沮我軍勢，兵法所謂以逸待勞，不如勿擊。
entries.en: Qingzhi wanted to give battle. Wei Fang objected that the enemy vanguard would be picked troops: a victory would count for little, a defeat would sap the army's spirit. Better, as the strategists say, to let the weary come to you—do not engage.
entries.literal: Qingzhi wished to meet them in battle; Wei Fang argued that the enemy vanguard must be light and elite troops—if battle went well it would not be enough for merit, and if it went badly it would damp our army's momentum; as the Art of War says, wait at ease for the weary—better not to strike.

entries.zh: 慶之曰：「魏人遠來，皆已疲倦，去我旣遠，必不見疑，及其未集，須挫其氣，出其不意，必無不敗之理。
entries.en: Qingzhi said, "The Wei troops have marched far and are already tired. They think we are still distant and will not expect a strike. Before they mass, we must break their spirit and hit them unawares—defeat is certain.
entries.literal: Qingzhi said: "The Wei men have come from afar and are all already weary; they are already far from us and surely will not suspect us—before they have gathered, we must blunt their spirit and take them unawares; there is surely no principle by which we would not defeat them.

entries.zh: 且聞虜所據營，林木甚盛，必不夜出。
entries.en: Besides, their camp stands in thick woods—they will not march out at night.
entries.literal: Moreover I hear that the camp the barbarians hold has very dense woods and they surely will not come out at night.

entries.zh: 諸君若疑惑，慶之請獨取之。」
entries.en: If you still doubt me, let me take them alone."
entries.literal: If you gentlemen are in doubt, Qingzhi asks to take it alone."

entries.zh: 於是與麾下二百騎奔擊，破其前軍，魏人震恐。
entries.en: He then led two hundred horsemen in a headlong charge, routed the vanguard, and threw the Wei army into panic.
entries.literal: Thereupon with two hundred horsemen under his command he charged in assault, broke their vanguard, and the Wei men were shaken with terror.

entries.zh: 慶之乃還與諸將連營而進，據渦陽城，與魏軍相持。
entries.en: Qingzhi rejoined the other commanders, advanced in linked camps, took Guoyang, and settled into a standoff with the Wei forces.
entries.literal: Qingzhi then returned and, with the other generals linking camps, advanced and seized Guoyang city, and faced the Wei army in stalemate.

entries.zh: 自春至冬，數十百戰，師老氣衰，魏之援兵復欲築壘於軍後，仲宗等恐腹背受敵，謀欲退師。
entries.en: From spring through winter they fought scores of engagements until the army was worn down. Wei relief columns tried to build fortifications behind the Liang lines. Zhongzong and the others, fearing encirclement, planned to pull back.
entries.literal: From spring to winter there were scores and hundreds of battles; the army grew old and its spirit waned. Wei's relief troops again wished to build stockades behind the army; Zhongzong and the others feared attack from front and rear and planned to withdraw the army.

entries.zh: 慶之杖節軍門曰：「共來至此，涉歷一歲，糜費糧仗，其數極多。
entries.en: Qingzhi stood at the camp gate with his staff of authority and said, "We have all been here a full year. The grain and arms we have spent are beyond counting.
entries.literal: Qingzhi, staff of authority in hand at the army gate, said: "Together we have come to this place and passed a full year; grain and weapons wasted—the number is extremely great.

entries.zh: 諸軍並無鬭心，皆謀退縮，豈是欲立功名，直聚爲抄暴耳。
entries.en: The troops have no will to fight and only want to retreat. You did not come here for glory—you came to loot.
entries.literal: The armies all have no fighting spirit and all plan to shrink back—how could this be wishing to establish merit and fame? You have simply gathered to plunder and ravage.

entries.zh: 吾聞置兵死地，乃可求生，須虜大合，然後與戰。
entries.en: They say armies on deadly ground fight to live. Wait until the enemy masses, then fight.
entries.literal: I have heard that placing troops on deadly ground is how one may seek life; we must wait until the barbarians have gathered in full, and then give battle.

entries.zh: 審欲班師，慶之別有密敕，今日犯者，便依明詔。」
entries.en: If you mean to withdraw, I hold a secret order from the throne: anyone who retreats today dies by imperial command."
entries.literal: If you truly wish to withdraw the army, Qingzhi has a separate secret edict: whoever offends today shall be dealt with according to the clear decree."

entries.zh: 仲宗壯其計，乃從之。
entries.en: Zhongzong was impressed and agreed.
entries.literal: Zhongzong admired his plan and thereupon followed it.

entries.zh: 魏人掎角作十三城，慶之銜枚夜出，陷其四壘，渦陽城主王緯乞降。
entries.en: The Wei built thirteen linked strongpoints. Qingzhi led a silent night sortie, took four of them, and Guoyang's commander Wang Wei surrendered.
entries.literal: The Wei men set up thirteen cities in pincer formation; Qingzhi went out at night with gags in the men's mouths, took four of their stockades, and Wang Wei, lord of Guoyang, begged to surrender.

entries.zh: 所餘九城，兵甲猶盛，乃陳其俘馘，鼓噪而攻之，遂大奔潰，斬獲略盡，渦水咽流，降城中男女三萬餘口。
entries.en: The other nine posts still held strong garrisons. He paraded prisoners and severed heads, stormed them with drum and shout, and drove them into rout. The slaughter filled the Guo River; more than thirty thousand men and women in the surrendered towns came over.
entries.literal: Of the remaining nine cities the armor and weapons were still strong; he then displayed their captives and severed ears, attacked with drums and shouts, and they thereupon fled in great rout; those slain and captured were nearly all, the Guo River choked with the flow, and men and women of the surrendered cities numbered more than thirty thousand.

entries.zh: 詔以渦陽之地置西徐州。
entries.en: The court created Western Xu province on the Guoyang region.
entries.literal: An edict established Western Xu province on the territory of Guoyang.

entries.zh: 衆軍乘勝前頓城父。
entries.en: The victorious army pushed on and encamped at Chengfu.
entries.literal: The mass of armies, riding victory, advanced and encamped at Chengfu.

entries.zh: 高祖嘉焉，賜慶之手詔曰：「本非將種，又非豪家，觖望風雲，以至於此。
entries.en: Emperor Wu was delighted and sent Qingzhi a personal note: "You were born neither to a general's house nor to a great clan, yet you reached for wind and cloud and have come this far.
entries.literal: The High Ancestor praised this and bestowed on Qingzhi a handwritten edict saying: "By origin you were not of a general's line, nor of a great house; you aspired to wind and cloud and have come to this.

entries.zh: 可深思奇略，善克令終。
entries.en: Think hard on bold strategy and see your career through to a worthy end.
entries.literal: You may deeply ponder strange stratagems and well achieve a fine end.

entries.zh: 開朱門而待賓，揚聲名於竹帛，豈非大丈夫哉！」
entries.en: Open your gates to guests and let your name live in the histories—is that not the mark of a true man?"
entries.literal: Open vermilion gates and await guests; raise your name on bamboo and silk—is this not a great man!"

entries.zh: 大通初，魏北海王元顥以本朝大亂，自拔來降，求立爲魏主。
entries.en: Early in Datong, Prince Hao of Beihai under Wei, citing turmoil at home, defected to Liang and asked to be set up as emperor of Wei.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Datong, Yuan Hao, Prince of Beihai under Wei, because his own dynasty was in great disorder, came over of his own accord to surrender and asked to be established as ruler of Wei.

entries.zh: 高祖納之，以慶之爲假節、飆勇將軍，送元顥還北。
entries.en: Emperor Wu agreed and named Qingzhi acting-credentials holder and General of Swift Valor to escort Hao north.
entries.literal: The High Ancestor accepted this and made Qingzhi acting-credentials holder and General of Swift Valor, to escort Yuan Hao back north.

entries.zh: 顥于渙水卽魏帝號，授慶之使持節、鎮北將軍、護軍、前軍大都督，發自銍縣，進拔滎城，遂至睢陽。
entries.en: At the Huan River, Hao took the Wei imperial title and gave Qingzhi full credentials as General Who Pacifies the North, army protector, and grand commander of the vanguard. They marched from Zhi county, took Yingcheng, and reached Suiyang.
entries.literal: Hao at the Huan River assumed the title of Emperor of Wei and invested Qingzhi as bearer of credentials, General Who Pacifies the North, Protector of the Army, and Grand Commander of the Forward Army; setting out from Zhi county, he advanced and took Yingcheng, and then reached Suiyang.

entries.zh: 魏將丘大千有衆七萬，分築九城以相拒。
entries.en: The Wei commander Qiu Daqian had seventy thousand men and ringed the route with nine fortified towns.
entries.literal: The Wei general Qiu Daqian had seventy thousand men and built nine cities in division to resist.

entries.zh: 慶之攻之，自旦至申，陷其三壘，大千乃降。
entries.en: Qingzhi attacked from dawn until mid-afternoon, took three strongpoints, and Daqian surrendered.
entries.literal: Qingzhi attacked him; from dawn to the shen hour he took three stockades, and Daqian then surrendered.

entries.zh: 時魏征東將軍濟陰王元暉業率羽林庶子二萬人來救梁、宋，進屯考城，城四面縈水，守備嚴固。
entries.en: General Who Conquers the East Prince Yuye of Jiyin marched with twenty thousand imperial guards to relieve Liang and Song and encamped at Kaocheng, a town moated on every side and strongly held.
entries.literal: At that time the Wei General Who Conquers the East, Prince Yuye of Jiyin, Yuan Yuye, led twenty thousand Forest Guard cadets to relieve Liang and Song, advanced and encamped at Kaocheng—the city on all four sides was girdled by water and its defenses were strict and solid.

entries.zh: 慶之命浮水築壘，攻陷其城，生擒暉業，獲租車七千八百兩。
entries.en: Qingzhi built floating stockades across the water, stormed the city, took Yuye alive, and seized seventy-eight hundred tax wagons.
entries.literal: Qingzhi ordered floating works to build stockades on the water, attacked and took his city, captured Yuye alive, and obtained seven thousand eight hundred tax carts.

entries.zh: 仍趨大梁，望旗歸款。
entries.en: He pressed on to Daliang, where the defenders surrendered at sight of his banners.
entries.literal: He then pressed on to Daliang; at sight of his banners they submitted.

entries.zh: 顥進慶之衛將軍、徐州刺史、武都公。
entries.en: Hao promoted him to General of the Guard, inspector of Xu province, and Duke of Wudu.
entries.literal: Hao promoted Qingzhi to General of the Guard, Inspector of Xu province, and Duke of Wudu.

entries.zh: 仍率衆而西。
entries.en: The army marched west again.
entries.literal: He still led the masses westward.

entries.zh: 中大通二年，除都督南北司西豫豫四州諸軍事、南北司二州刺史，餘並如故。
entries.en: In the second year of Zhongdatong he was made commander of the four provinces of Southern and Northern Si, Western Yu, and Yu, and inspector of Southern and Northern Si; his other posts remained unchanged.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhongdatong he was appointed Commander of military affairs for the four provinces of Southern and Northern Si, Western Yu, and Yu, and Inspector of the two provinces of Southern and Northern Si; the rest remained as before.

entries.zh: 慶之至鎮，遂圍懸瓠。
entries.en: On reaching his post Qingzhi at once besieged Xuanhu.
entries.literal: When Qingzhi reached his commandery, he thereupon besieged Xuanhu.

entries.zh: 破魏潁州刺史婁起、揚州刺史是云寶於溱水，又破行臺孫騰、大都督侯進、豫州刺史堯雄、梁州刺史司馬恭於楚城。
entries.en: He routed Wei Inspector of Ying Province Lou Qi and Inspector of Yang Province Shiyun Bao on the Qin River, then defeated mobile headquarters commander Sun Teng, Grand Commander Hou Jin, Inspector of Yu Province Yao Xiong, and Inspector of Liang Province Sima Gong at Chucheng.
entries.literal: He defeated Wei Inspector of Ying province Lou Qi and Inspector of Yang province Shiyun Bao at the Qin River, and again defeated Mobile Headquarters Sun Teng, Grand Commander Hou Jin, Inspector of Yu province Yao Xiong, and Inspector of Liang province Sima Gong at Chucheng.

entries.zh: 罷義陽鎮兵，停水陸轉運，江湖諸州並得休息。
entries.en: He stood down the Yiyang garrison, halted supply convoys by land and water, and gave the river provinces a respite.
entries.literal: He dismissed the garrison troops of Yiyang, halted water and land transport of supplies, and the provinces of the rivers and lakes all obtained rest.

entries.zh: 開田六千頃，二年之後，倉廩充實。
entries.en: He opened six thousand qing of farmland; within two years the granaries were full.
entries.literal: He opened six thousand qing of fields; after two years the granaries were full and solid.

entries.zh: 高祖每嘉勞之。
entries.en: Emperor Wu repeatedly praised and rewarded him.
entries.literal: The High Ancestor often praised and comforted him.

entries.zh: 又表省南司州，復安陸郡，置上明郡。
entries.en: He also memorialized to abolish Southern Si province, restore Anlu commandery, and create Shangming commandery.
entries.literal: He also memorialized to abolish Southern Si province, restore Anlu commandery, and establish Shangming commandery.

entries.zh: 太清二年，侯景圍歷陽，敕召昕還，昕啓云：「採石急須重鎮，王質水軍輕弱，恐慮不濟。」
entries.en: In the second year of Taiqing, Hou Jing besieged Liyang. The court recalled Xin, but he reported, "Caishi needs a strong garrison at once. Wang Zhi's fleet is too light—I fear it will fail."
entries.literal: In the second year of Taiqing, Hou Jing besieged Liyang; an edict recalled Xin; Xin reported: "Caishi urgently needs a heavy garrison; Wang Zhi's water army is light and weak—I fear it will not succeed."

entries.zh: 乃板昕爲雲騎將軍，代質，未及下渚，景已渡江，仍遣率所領遊防城外，不得入守。
entries.en: He was hastily named General of Cloud Cavalry to replace Zhi. Before Xin reached Xiazhu, Jing had crossed the Yangzi. Xin was posted outside the walls on patrol and could not enter to defend.
entries.literal: He was then appointed on the board as General of Cloud Cavalry to replace Zhi; before reaching Xiazhu, Jing had already crossed the Yangzi, and Xin was still sent to lead his command in roaming defense outside the walls, unable to enter and hold the defense.

entries.zh: 欲奔京口，乃爲景所擒。
entries.en: He tried to flee to Jingkou but was seized by Jing.
entries.literal: He wished to flee to Jingkou but was captured by Jing.

entries.zh: 景見昕殷勤，因留極飲，曰：「我至此得卿，餘人無能爲也。」
entries.en: Jing found Xin obliging and kept him for a long drinking bout, saying, "With you in hand I need no one else."
entries.literal: Jing saw that Xin was attentive and courteous and therefore detained him for extreme drinking, saying: "In coming here I have obtained you; the rest are incapable of acting."

entries.zh: 令昕收集部曲，將用之，昕誓而不許。
entries.en: He ordered Xin to rally his troops for service. Xin swore he would not comply.
entries.literal: He ordered Xin to gather his troops and intended to use him; Xin swore an oath and would not consent.

entries.zh: 景使其儀同范桃棒嚴禁之，昕因說桃棒令率所領歸降，襲殺王偉、宋子仙爲信。
entries.en: Jing had his officer Fan Taobang guard him closely. Xin persuaded Taobang to lead his men in surrender and kill Wang Wei and Song Zixian as proof of good faith.
entries.literal: Jing had his Protocol Equal Fan Taobang strictly confine him; Xin thereupon persuaded Taobang to lead those under his command to return and surrender, and to attack and kill Wang Wei and Song Zixian as proof of good faith.

entries.zh: 桃棒許之，遂盟約，射啓城中，遣昕夜縋而入。
entries.en: Taobang agreed. They sealed a pact, shot a message into the city, and sent Xin in by rope at night.
entries.literal: Taobang agreed; they then made a covenant, shot a message into the city, and sent Xin in by night on a rope.

entries.zh: 高祖大喜，敕卽受降，太宗遲疑累日不決，外事發洩，昕弗之知，猶依期而下。
entries.en: Emperor Wu was delighted and ordered the surrender accepted at once, but the Heir Apparent hesitated for days. The matter leaked. Xin knew nothing and came down on schedule.
entries.literal: The High Ancestor was greatly pleased and ordered that the surrender be accepted at once; the Heir Apparent hesitated for many days without deciding; the matter leaked outside; Xin did not know of this and still descended according to schedule.

entries.zh: 景邀得之，乃逼昕令更射書城中，云「桃棒且輕將數十人先入。」
entries.en: Jing caught him and forced him to shoot another message into the city: "Taobang will send only a few dozen men inside first."
entries.literal: Jing intercepted and seized him, then forced Xin to shoot another letter into the city saying "Taobang will first send only a few dozen light troops to enter."

entries.zh: 景欲裹甲隨之。
entries.en: Jing meant to follow in armor himself.
entries.literal: Jing wished to wrap his armor and follow after.

entries.zh: 昕旣不肯爲書，期以必死，遂爲景所害，時年三十三。
entries.en: Xin refused to write the letter, accepting death, and Jing killed him. He was thirty-three.
entries.literal: Xin would not write the letter and expected certain death; he was thereupon killed by Jing, at the age of thirty-three.

entries.zh: 出爲持節、都督緣淮諸軍事、奮武將軍、北兗州刺史。
entries.en: He was sent out with credentials as commander of Huai frontier forces, General of Stirring Martiality, and inspector of Northern Yan.
entries.literal: He went out as bearer of credentials, Commander of all military affairs along the Huai, General of Stirring Martiality, and Inspector of Northern Yan province.

entries.zh: 會有妖賊沙門僧強自稱爲帝，土豪蔡伯龍起兵應之。
entries.en: A sorcerer-monk named Seng Qiang declared himself emperor, and the local magnate Cai Bolong rose in his support.
entries.literal: It happened that the demonic bandit monk Seng Qiang declared himself emperor, and the local strongman Cai Bolong raised troops in response to him.

entries.zh: 僧強頗知幻術，更相扇惑，衆至三萬，攻陷北徐州，濟陰太守楊起文棄城走，鐘離太守單希寶見害，使慶之討焉。
entries.en: Seng Qiang knew sleight-of-hand and they whipped each other into frenzy until their host reached thirty thousand. They took Northern Xu. Jiyin administrator Yang Qiwen fled; Zhongli administrator Shan Xibao was killed. Qingzhi was ordered to suppress them.
entries.literal: Seng Qiang was quite skilled in illusion arts and they fanned and deluded one another; the masses reached thirty thousand, attacked and took Northern Xu province, Administrator of Jiyin Yang Qiwen abandoned the city and fled, Administrator of Zhongli Shan Xibao was killed—the court sent Qingzhi to subdue them.

entries.zh: 車駕幸白下，臨餞謂慶之曰：「江、淮兵勁，其鋒難當，卿可以策制之，不宜決戰。」
entries.en: The emperor went to Baixia and, at the farewell feast, told Qingzhi, "Jiang and Huai fighters are fierce and hard to meet head-on. Use strategy, not a pitched battle."
entries.literal: The imperial carriage went to Baixia; at the farewell feast he said to Qingzhi: "Jiang and Huai troops are strong; their edge is hard to meet—you may use stratagem to control them; it is not fitting to decide the matter in pitched battle."

entries.zh: 慶之受命而行。
entries.en: Qingzhi took his orders and marched.
entries.literal: Qingzhi received the command and set out.

entries.zh: 曾未浹辰，斬伯龍、僧強，傳其首。
entries.en: Within ten days he had beheaded Bolong and Seng Qiang and sent their heads to court.
entries.literal: Before a full ten days had passed, he beheaded Bolong and Seng Qiang and sent their heads.

entries.zh: 魏左僕射楊昱、西阿王元慶、撫軍將軍元顯恭率御仗羽林宗子庶子衆凡七萬，據滎陽拒顥。
entries.en: Left Vice Director Yang Yu, Prince Qing of Xi'a, and Pacification Army General Yuan Xiangong led seventy thousand imperial guards and cadets to hold Yingyang against Hao.
entries.literal: Yang Yu, Left Vice Director under Wei, Prince Qing of Xi'a, Yuan Qing, and Pacification Army General Yuan Xiangong led the imperial guard Forest Guard cadets and sons of the clans, in all seventy thousand, and held Yingyang to resist Hao.

entries.zh: 兵旣精強，城又險固，慶之攻未能拔。
entries.en: Their troops were elite and the city formidable; Qingzhi could not break it at first.
entries.literal: The troops were already elite and strong, and the city was also perilous and solid; Qingzhi attacked but could not take it.

entries.zh: 魏將元天穆大軍復將至，先遣其驃騎將軍尒朱吐沒兒領胡騎五千，騎將魯安領夏州步騎九千，援楊昱；
entries.en: Yuan Tianmu's main army was closing in. He first sent Cavalry General Erzhu Tumener with five thousand barbarian horse and Cavalry Commander Lu An with nine thousand mixed troops from Xia province to reinforce Yang Yu;
entries.literal: The Wei general Yuan Tianmu's great army was again about to arrive; he first sent his Cavalry General Erzhu Tumener with five thousand barbarian horsemen, and Cavalry Commander Lu An with nine thousand Xia province foot and horse, to relieve Yang Yu;

entries.zh: 又遣右僕射尒朱世隆、西荊州刺史王羆騎一萬，據虎牢。
entries.en: and Right Vice Director Erzhu Shilong and Western Jing inspector Wang Pi with ten thousand cavalry to hold Hulao.
entries.literal: and also sent Right Vice Director Erzhu Shilong and Inspector of Western Jing Wang Pi with ten thousand horse to hold Hulao.

entries.zh: 天穆、吐沒兒前後繼至，旗鼓相望。
entries.en: Tianmu and Tumener arrived in succession until enemy banners filled the horizon.
entries.literal: Tianmu and Tumener arrived one after another in succession; banners and drums faced one another.

entries.zh: 時滎陽未拔，士衆皆恐，慶之乃解鞍秣馬，宣喻衆曰：「吾至此以來，屠城略地，實爲不少；
entries.en: Yingyang still held, and the men were afraid. Qingzhi had the horses unsaddled and fed, then addressed the army: "Since we crossed the border we have sacked cities and seized land without number;
entries.literal: At that time Yingyang was not yet taken and officers and masses were all afraid; Qingzhi then unslung his saddle and fed his horses, and announced to the masses: "From the time I came here until now, cities slaughtered and territory seized have truly been not a few;

entries.zh: 君等殺人父兄，略人子女，又爲無算。
entries.en: you have killed fathers and elder brothers and taken sons and daughters beyond counting.
entries.literal: you gentlemen have killed men's fathers and elder brothers and seized men's sons and daughters—again beyond counting.

entries.zh: 天穆之衆，並是仇讎。
entries.en: Tianmu's host are nothing but blood enemies.
entries.literal: Tianmu's masses are all blood enemies.

entries.zh: 我等才有七千，虜衆三十餘萬，今日之事，義不圖存。
entries.en: We are seven thousand against more than three hundred thousand. Today we fight with no thought of survival.
entries.literal: We have only seven thousand; the barbarian masses are more than three hundred thousand—today's affair, by right we do not plan to survive.

entries.zh: 吾以虜騎不可爭力平原，及未盡至前，須平其城壘，諸君無假狐疑，自貽屠膾。」
entries.en: Their cavalry cannot match us on open ground, but not until they are all here. Take the city first. Do not hesitate and make yourselves meat for the pot."
entries.literal: I hold that barbarian horse cannot contend for strength on the plain; before they have all arrived, we must level their city and stockades—you gentlemen must not borrow fox-like doubt and bring down slaughter and mince upon yourselves."

entries.zh: 一鼓悉使登城，壯士東陽宋景休、義興魚天湣逾堞而入，遂克之。
entries.en: At a single drumbeat he sent them up the walls. Song Jingxiu of Dongyang and Yu Tianmin of Yixing scrambled over the parapet and broke in; the city fell.
entries.literal: At one drumbeat he had them all mount the wall; the stalwart Song Jingxiu of Dongyang and Yu Tianmin of Yixing crossed the parapet and entered, and thereupon took it.

entries.zh: 俄而魏陣外合，慶之率騎三千背城逆戰，大破之，魯安於陣乞降，元天穆、尒朱吐沒兒單騎獲免。
entries.en: Soon the Wei encirclement closed. Qingzhi led three thousand horse out from the city and shattered them. Lu An surrendered in the field; Tianmu and Tumener fled alone on horseback.
entries.literal: Shortly the Wei battle lines closed from outside; Qingzhi led three thousand horse with the city at his back to meet them in battle and routed them greatly; Lu An begged to surrender on the field, and Yuan Tianmu and Erzhu Tumener escaped on single horses.

entries.zh: 收滎陽儲實，牛馬穀帛不可勝計。
entries.en: They seized Yingyang's stores—cattle, horses, grain, and silk beyond reckoning.
entries.literal: They gathered Yingyang's stored goods; cattle, horses, grain, and silk could not be counted.

entries.zh: 進赴虎牢，尒朱世隆棄城走。
entries.en: They advanced on Hulao; Erzhu Shilong abandoned the town and fled.
entries.literal: Advancing to Hulao, Erzhu Shilong abandoned the city and fled.

entries.zh: 魏主元子攸懼，奔幷州。
entries.en: The Wei emperor Yuan Ziyou fled in fear to Bing province.
entries.literal: The Wei ruler Yuan Ziyou was afraid and fled to Bing province.

entries.zh: 其臨淮王元彧、安豊王元延明率百僚，封府庫，備法駕，奉迎顥入洛陽宮，御前殿，改元大赦。
entries.en: Prince Yu of Linhuai and Prince Yanming of Anfeng led the officials, sealed the treasuries, prepared the imperial train, and ushered Hao into the Luoyang palace. He took the throne hall, changed the reign title, and proclaimed a general amnesty.
entries.literal: His Prince Yu of Linhuai, Yuan Yu, and Prince Yanming of Anfeng, Yuan Yanming, led the hundred officials, sealed the treasuries, prepared the imperial equipage, and welcomed Hao into the Luoyang palace; he took the front hall, changed the era name, and proclaimed a great amnesty.

entries.zh: 顥以慶之爲侍中、車騎大將軍、左光祿大夫，增邑萬戶。
entries.en: Hao made Qingzhi palace attendant, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and left grand master of splendid happiness, adding ten thousand households to his fief.
entries.literal: Hao made Qingzhi Palace Attendant, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and increased his fief by ten thousand households.

entries.zh: 魏大將軍上黨王元天穆、王老生、李叔仁又率衆四萬，攻陷大梁，分遣老生、費穆兵二萬，據虎牢，刁宣、刁雙入梁、宋，慶之隨方掩襲，並皆降款。
entries.en: Grand General Prince Tianmu of Shangdang, Wang Laosheng, and Li Shuren marched again with forty thousand, took Daliang, and sent Laosheng and Fei Mu with twenty thousand to hold Hulao while Diao Xuan and Diao Shuang pushed into Liang and Song. Qingzhi ambushed them wherever they moved, and they all surrendered.
entries.literal: The Wei Grand General Prince Tianmu of Shangdang, Yuan Tianmu, Wang Laosheng, and Li Shuren again led forty thousand men, attacked and took Daliang, and separately sent Laosheng and Fei Mu with twenty thousand troops to hold Hulao; Diao Xuan and Diao Shuang entered Liang and Song—Qingzhi struck by surprise wherever they went, and all submitted.

entries.zh: 天穆與十餘騎北渡河。
entries.en: Tianmu fled north across the river with only a dozen riders.
entries.literal: Tianmu with a dozen or so horsemen crossed the river north.

entries.zh: 高祖復賜手詔稱美焉。
entries.en: Emperor Wu sent another personal note of praise.
entries.literal: The High Ancestor again bestowed a handwritten edict praising him.

entries.zh: 慶之麾下悉著白袍，所向披靡。
entries.en: Qingzhi's men all wore white robes and swept aside everything before them.
entries.literal: All under Qingzhi's command wore white robes; wherever they went, none could stand before them.

entries.zh: 先是洛陽童謠曰：「名師大將莫自牢，千兵萬馬避白袍。」
entries.en: A Luoyang children's rhyme had already run: "Famed commanders, do not think yourselves safe—thousands upon thousands flee the white robes."
entries.literal: Earlier a children's rhyme in Luoyang said: "Famed generals and great commanders, do not hold yourselves secure—thousands of soldiers and ten thousands of horses avoid the white robes."

entries.zh: 自發銍縣至於洛陽，十四旬平三十二城，四十七戰，所向無前。
entries.en: From Zhi county to Luoyang, in a hundred and forty days he took thirty-two cities in forty-seven battles and met no equal.
entries.literal: From setting out at Zhi county until Luoyang, in fourteen tens of days he pacified thirty-two cities and forty-seven battles—wherever he went, none stood before him.

entries.zh: 初，元子攸止單騎奔走，宮衛嬪侍無改於常。
entries.en: At first Ziyou had fled alone on horseback, yet the palace guards and consorts carried on as if nothing had changed.
entries.literal: At first Yuan Ziyou fled on a single horse alone; palace guards and palace women attendants were unchanged from the usual.

entries.zh: 顥旣得志，荒於酒色，乃日夜宴樂，不復視事。
entries.en: Once Hao had his prize, he gave himself to wine and women, feasting day and night and neglecting government.
entries.literal: Once Hao had achieved his aim, he was dissolute in wine and women; then day and night feasting and music, and he no longer attended to affairs.

entries.zh: 與安豊、臨淮共立姦計，將背朝恩，絕賓貢之禮；
entries.en: He and the princes of Anfeng and Linhuai plotted treachery, planning to turn on Liang and end the tribute owed the southern court;
entries.literal: Together with Anfeng and Linhuai he set up a wicked plot, intending to turn against the court's grace and cut off the ritual of guest and tribute;

entries.zh: 直以時事未安，且資慶之之力用，外同內異，言多忌刻。
entries.en: but the realm was not yet secure, so for the moment they still needed Qingzhi's sword—outward allies, inward enemies, their speech sharp with suspicion.
entries.literal: only because the times were not yet settled did they for the moment rely on Qingzhi's strength and use—outwardly the same, inwardly different, their words full of jealousy and harshness.

entries.zh: 慶之心知之，亦密爲其計。
entries.en: Qingzhi saw through them and laid plans of his own in secret.
entries.literal: Qingzhi knew it in his heart and also secretly made plans of his own.

entries.zh: 乃說顥曰：「今遠來至此，未伏尚多，若人知虛實，方更連兵，而安不忘危，須預爲其策。
entries.en: He urged Hao, "We are far from home and many regions are not yet pacified. Once the enemy learns how few we are, they will mass again. In peace one must plan for danger.
entries.literal: He then urged Hao: "Now having come from afar to this place, those not yet subdued are still many; if men know our emptiness and fullness, they will again link armies—in security do not forget peril; we must prepare plans in advance.

entries.zh: 宜啓天子，更請精兵；
entries.en: Ask the Son of Heaven for more elite troops;
entries.literal: We ought to report to the Son of Heaven and request elite troops again;

entries.zh: 並勒諸州，有南人沒此者，悉須部送。」
entries.en: and order every province to send south all southerners held captive in the north."
entries.literal: and also order the provinces that any southerners taken captive here must all be escorted and sent."

entries.zh: 顥欲從之，元延明說顥曰：「陳慶之兵不出數千，已自難制；
entries.en: Hao was inclined to agree, but Yuan Yanming warned him, "Chen Qingzhi commands only a few thousand men, and they are already hard to control.
entries.literal: Hao wished to follow this; Yuan Yanming urged Hao: "Chen Qingzhi's troops do not exceed several thousand, and already by themselves are hard to control;

entries.zh: 今增其衆，寧肯復爲用乎？
entries.en: If you swell his ranks, will he still serve you?
entries.literal: if we now increase his masses, would he willingly again be used by us?

entries.zh: 權柄一去，動轉聽人，魏之宗社，於斯而滅。」
entries.en: Once power slips from your hands, you become everyone's puppet—and Wei's altars fall with you."
entries.literal: Once power and handle are gone, every move listens to others—Wei's altars and state, at this point are destroyed."

entries.zh: 顥由是致疑，稍成疏貳。
entries.en: From that Hao grew suspicious and their alliance frayed.
entries.literal: From this Hao came to doubt, and gradually estrangement and divided loyalty formed.

entries.zh: 慮慶之密啓，乃表高祖曰：「河北、河南一時已定，唯尒朱榮尚敢跋扈，臣與慶之自能擒討。
entries.en: Fearing a secret report from Qingzhi, he wrote Emperor Wu: "Hebei and Henan are pacified for now. Only Erzhu Rong still struts defiantly—your servant and Qingzhi can deal with him ourselves.
entries.literal: Fearing Qingzhi's secret memorial, he then memorialized the High Ancestor: "Hebei and Henan for the moment are all settled; only Erzhu Rong still dares to be overbearing and unruly—your servant and Qingzhi by ourselves can capture and subdue him.

entries.zh: 今州郡新服，正須綏撫，不宜更復加兵，搖動百姓。」
entries.en: The provinces have only just submitted and need gentle rule. More troops would only unsettle the people."
entries.literal: Now the provinces and commanderies have newly submitted and just need soothing settlement—it is not fitting to add troops again and shake the common people."

entries.zh: 高祖遂詔衆軍皆停界首。
entries.en: Emperor Wu ordered all reinforcing armies to halt at the frontier.
entries.literal: The High Ancestor thereupon ordered all armies to halt at the border passes.

entries.zh: 洛下南人不出一萬，羌夷十倍，軍副馬佛念言於慶之曰：「功高不賞，震主身危，二事旣有，將軍豈得無慮？
entries.en: Fewer than ten thousand southerners held Luoyang, while Qiang and other tribesmen outnumbered them tenfold. Vice commander Ma Fonian told Qingzhi, "Great merit goes unrewarded, and power that awes one's lord endangers the man who wields it. With both true, can you have no fears?
entries.literal: Southerners in Luoyang did not reach ten thousand; Qiang and barbarians were ten times that number. Army Vice Commander Ma Fonian said to Qingzhi: "Merit high but unrewarded, shaking the ruler and peril to the person—these two things are already present; how can the general not have concerns?

entries.zh: 自古以來，廢昏立明，扶危定難，鮮有得終。
entries.en: Since antiquity, men who deposed bad rulers, raised good ones, and rescued states in peril have rarely died in their beds.
entries.literal: From antiquity until now, deposing the dim and establishing the bright, supporting peril and settling difficulty—few have had a good end.

entries.zh: 今將軍威震中原，聲動河塞，屠顥據洛，則千載一時也。」
entries.en: Your fame now shakes the central plains and the Yellow River frontier. Kill Hao, take Luoyang, and you seize a moment that comes once in a thousand years."
entries.literal: Now the general's prestige shakes the central plains and his fame moves the river passes and frontier—slay Hao and hold Luoyang, and it is a once-in-a-thousand-years moment."

entries.zh: 慶之不從。
entries.en: Qingzhi refused.
entries.literal: Qingzhi did not follow.

entries.zh: 顥前以慶之爲徐州刺史，因固求之鎮。
entries.en: Hao had already named Qingzhi inspector of Xu, and Qingzhi pressed hard to take up that post.
entries.literal: Hao had earlier made Qingzhi Inspector of Xu province, and Qingzhi therefore firmly requested to garrison there.

entries.zh: 顥心憚之，遂不遣。
entries.en: Hao feared to let him go and refused.
entries.literal: Hao feared him in his heart and therefore did not send him.

entries.zh: 乃曰：「主上以洛陽之地全相任委，忽聞舍此朝寄，欲往彭城，謂君遽取富貴，不爲國計，手敕頻仍，恐成僕責。」
entries.en: He said, "The emperor has entrusted all of Luoyang to you. If he hears you mean to abandon that charge for Pengcheng, he will think you grasp at private gain and ignore the realm. His letters come one after another; I fear we will be blamed as servants who failed their master."
entries.literal: He then said: "The lord above has wholly entrusted you with the Luoyang region; suddenly I hear you would leave this court commission and wish to go to Pengcheng—he will think you are hastily seizing wealth and rank, not planning for the state; handwritten edicts come repeatedly, and I fear it will become a servant's fault."

entries.zh: 慶之不敢復言。
entries.en: Qingzhi said no more.
entries.literal: Qingzhi did not dare speak again.

entries.zh: 魏天柱將軍尒朱榮、右僕射尒朱世隆、大都督元天穆、驃騎將軍尒朱吐沒兒、榮長史高歡、鮮卑、芮芮，勒衆號百萬，挾魏主元子攸來攻顥。
entries.en: Wei's Pillar of Heaven Erzhu Rong, Erzhu Shilong, Grand Commander Yuan Tianmu, Erzhu Tumener, Rong's chief clerk Gao Huan, and Xianbei and Rouran allies marched with a host they claimed numbered a million, bringing Emperor Ziyou along to crush Hao.
entries.literal: Wei's Pillar of Heaven General Erzhu Rong, Right Vice Director Erzhu Shilong, Grand Commander Yuan Tianmu, Cavalry General Erzhu Tumener, Rong's Chief Clerk Gao Huan, Xianbei, and Rouran led masses they called a million, taking the Wei ruler Yuan Ziyou along to attack Hao.

entries.zh: 顥據洛陽六十五日，凡所得城，一時反叛。
entries.en: Hao had held Luoyang sixty-five days when every city he had taken rose against him at once.
entries.literal: Hao had held Luoyang sixty-five days; all the cities he had gained at once rebelled.

entries.zh: 慶之渡河守北中郎城，三日中十有一戰，傷殺甚衆。
entries.en: Qingzhi crossed the river and held Beizhonglang fortress. In three days he fought eleven engagements with heavy casualties on both sides.
entries.literal: Qingzhi crossed the river and guarded Beizhonglang city; in three days there were eleven battles, and the wounded and slain were very many.

entries.zh: 榮將退，時有劉助者，善天文，乃謂榮曰：「不出十日，河南大定。」
entries.en: Rong was ready to pull back when Liu Zhu, an expert in astronomy, told him, "Within ten days Henan will be fully pacified."
entries.literal: Rong was about to withdraw; at that time there was one Liu Zhu, skilled in astronomy, who said to Rong: "Within no more than ten days Henan will be greatly settled."

entries.zh: 榮乃縛木爲筏，濟自硤石，與顥戰於河橋，顥大敗，走至臨潁，遇賊被擒，洛陽陷。
entries.en: Rong lashed logs into rafts, crossed at Xiashi, and met Hao at Heqiao. Hao was routed, fled to Linying, was seized by marauders, and Luoyang fell.
entries.literal: Rong then bound wood into rafts, crossed from Xiashi, and fought Hao at Heqiao; Hao was greatly defeated, fled to Linying, met bandits and was captured, and Luoyang fell.

entries.zh: 慶之馬步數千，結陣東反，榮親自來追，值蒿高山水洪溢，軍人死散。
entries.en: Qingzhi withdrew east with a few thousand horse and foot. Erzhu Rong pursued in person. Floods on the Song and Gaoshan ranges drowned and scattered his army.
entries.literal: Qingzhi had several thousand horse and foot; he formed battle lines and turned east in retreat. Rong came in person to pursue; they met with floods overflowing the Song Mountains and Gaoshan waters, and soldiers died and scattered.

entries.zh: 慶之乃落鬚髮爲沙門，間行至豫州，豫州人程道雍等潛送出汝陰。
entries.en: He shaved his beard, took monk's robes, and stole his way to Yu province, where Cheng Daoyong and others smuggled him out through Ruyin.
entries.literal: Qingzhi then cut off his beard and hair and became a monk, traveling by secret paths to Yu province; Cheng Daoyong and others of Yu province secretly escorted him out through Ruyin.

entries.zh: 至都，仍以功除右衛將軍，封永興縣侯，邑一千五百戶。
entries.en: Back in the capital he was made General of the Right Guard for his service and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongxing with a fief of fifteen hundred households.
entries.literal: On reaching the capital, he was again appointed by merit as General of the Right Guard and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongxing with a fief of one thousand five hundred households.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：陳慶之、蘭欽俱有將略，戰勝攻取，蓋頗、牧、衛、霍之亞歟。
entries.en: The historiographer writes: Chen Qingzhi and Lan Qin both possessed true generalship. In victory and conquest they stand in the company of Lian Po, Li Mu, Wei Qing, and Huo Qubing.
entries.literal: The historiographer says: Chen Qingzhi and Lan Qin both had military strategy; victorious in battle and taking by assault—they were perhaps the peers of Lian Po, Li Mu, Wei Qing, and Huo Qubing.

entries.zh: 慶之警悟，早侍高祖，旣預舊恩，加之謹肅，蟬冕組珮，亦一世之榮矣。
entries.en: Qingzhi was quick-witted and attended Emperor Wu from youth. Old favor, sober conduct, and the regalia of high office were glory enough for one life.
entries.literal: Qingzhi was alert and perceptive; he early attended the High Ancestor, and having shared in old favor, together with his respectful sobriety, cicada cap and ribbon pendant—these too were the glory of a lifetime.

entries.zh: 大同二年，魏遣將侯景率衆七萬寇楚州，刺史桓和陷沒，景仍進軍淮上，貽慶之書使降。
entries.en: In the second year of Datong, Wei sent Hou Jing with seventy thousand men against Chu. Inspector Huan He was overrun. Jing pushed on to the Huai and wrote Qingzhi urging surrender.
entries.literal: In the second year of Datong, Wei sent the general Hou Jing with seventy thousand men to raid Chu province; Inspector Huan He was lost, and Jing still advanced his army on the Huai and sent Qingzhi a letter urging him to surrender.

entries.zh: 敕遣湘潭侯退、右衛夏侯夔等赴援，軍至黎漿，慶之已擊破景。
entries.en: The court sent Marquis Tui of Xiangtan, Xiahou Kui of the Right Guard, and others to reinforce him, but by the time they reached Lijiang Qingzhi had already beaten Jing.
entries.literal: An edict sent Marquis Tui of Xiangtan, Xiahou Kui of the Right Guard, and others to relieve them; when the army reached Lijiang, Qingzhi had already routed Jing.

entries.zh: 時大寒雪，景棄輜重走，慶之收之以歸。
entries.en: In bitter cold and snow Jing abandoned his baggage train and fled. Qingzhi gathered the spoils and returned.
entries.literal: At that time there was great cold and snow; Jing abandoned his baggage train and fled, and Qingzhi gathered it and returned.

entries.zh: 進號仁威將軍。
entries.en: He was promoted to General of Humane Prestige.
entries.literal: His title was advanced to General of Humane Prestige.

entries.zh: 是歲，豫州饑，慶之開倉賑給，多所全濟。
entries.en: That year Yu province suffered famine. Qingzhi opened the granaries and saved many lives.
entries.literal: That year Yu province suffered famine; Qingzhi opened the granaries for relief and distribution, and many were wholly saved.

entries.zh: 州民李升等八百人表請樹碑頌德，詔許焉。
entries.en: Eight hundred residents led by Li Sheng petitioned for a stele in his honor, and the court approved.
entries.literal: Eight hundred common people of the province, Li Sheng and others, submitted a memorial requesting a stele to praise his virtue, and an edict permitted it.

entries.zh: 五年十月，卒，時年五十六。
entries.en: In the tenth month of the fifth year he died, aged fifty-six.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of the fifth year he died, at the age of fifty-six.

entries.zh: 贈散騎常侍、左衛將軍，鼓吹一部。
entries.en: He was posthumously made attendant cavalier at large and general of the left guard, with a full military band for his funeral.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was given Attendant Cavalier at Large and General of the Left Guard, and one set of martial music.

entries.zh: 諡曰武。
entries.en: His posthumous title was Martial.
entries.literal: His posthumous name was Martial.

entries.zh: 敕義興郡發五百丁會喪。
entries.en: The court ordered Yixing commandery to send five hundred laborers for the funeral.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Yixing commandery to dispatch five hundred corvée laborers to attend the funeral.

entries.zh: 子夏禮，侯景至歷陽，率其部曲邀擊景，兵敗死之。
entries.en: His son Xiali, when Hou Jing reached Liyang, led his troops to ambush Jing, was defeated, and died.
entries.literal: His son Xiali—when Hou Jing reached Liyang, he led his troops to intercept and strike Jing, was defeated in battle, and died.

entries.zh: 梁書卷第三十二 列傳第二十六
entries.en: Book of Liang, Volume 32, Biography 26
entries.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 32, Biographies 26

entries.zh: 蕭子恪 弟子範 子顯 子雲
entries.en: Xiao Zike; his younger brother Zifan; Xiao Zixian; Xiao Ziyun
entries.literal: Xiao Zike; his younger brother Zifan; Zixian; Ziyun

entries.zh: 蕭子恪，字景沖，蘭陵人，齊豫章文獻王嶷第二子也。
entries.en: Xiao Zike, styled Jingchong, came from Lanling and was the second son of Yi, Prince Wenxian of Yuzhang under Qi.
entries.literal: Xiao Zike, styled Jingchong, came from Lanling and was the second son of Yi, Prince Wenxian of Yuzhang under Qi.

entries.zh: 永明中，以王子封南康縣侯。
entries.en: During Yongming, as a prince's son he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Nankang county.
entries.literal: During Yongming, as a prince's son he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Nankang county.

entries.zh: 年十二，和從兄司徒竟陵王《高松賦》，衛軍王儉見而奇之。
entries.en: At twelve, he wrote a matching piece to his elder cousin the Prince of Jingling, Minister over the Masses, on the "Rhapsody on Tall Pines"; Wang Jian, General of the Guard, saw it and marveled.
entries.literal: At twelve, he wrote a matching piece to his elder cousin the Prince of Jingling, Minister over the Masses, on the "Rhapsody on Tall Pines"; Wang Jian, General of the Guard, saw it and marveled.

entries.zh: 初爲寧朔將軍、淮陵太守，建武中，遷輔國將軍、吳郡太守。
entries.en: He first served as General Who Pacifies the North and administrator of Huailing; during Jianwu he was transferred to General Who Supports the State and administrator of Wu Commandery.
entries.literal: He first served as General Who Pacifies the North and administrator of Huailing; during Jianwu he was transferred to General Who Supports the State and administrator of Wu Commandery.

entries.zh: 大司馬王敬則於會稽舉兵反，以奉子恪爲名，明帝悉召子恪兄弟親從七十餘人入西省，至夜當害之。
entries.en: When Grand Marshal Wang Jingze raised troops in rebellion at Kuaiji, claiming he would uphold Zike, Emperor Ming summoned Zike, his brothers, and more than seventy close followers into the Western Office, intending to kill them that night.
entries.literal: When Grand Marshal Wang Jingze raised troops in rebellion at Kuaiji, claiming he would uphold Zike, Emperor Ming summoned Zike, his brothers, and more than seventy close followers into the Western Office, intending to kill them that night.

entries.zh: 會子恪棄郡奔歸，是日亦至，明帝乃止，以子恪爲太子中庶子。
entries.en: As it happened, Zike abandoned his commandery and rushed back, arriving that same day; Emperor Ming then stopped and made Zike Household Attendant to the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: As it happened, Zike abandoned his commandery and rushed back, arriving that same day; Emperor Ming then stopped and made Zike Household Attendant to the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 東昏卽位，遷秘書監，領右軍將軍，俄爲侍中。
entries.en: When Donghun took the throne, Zike was promoted to Palace Library Director, concurrently General of the Right Army, and soon became Attendant-in-Ordinary.
entries.literal: When Donghun took the throne, Zike was promoted to Palace Library Director, concurrently General of the Right Army, and soon became Attendant-in-Ordinary.

entries.zh: 中興二年，遷輔國諮議參軍。
entries.en: In Zhongxing 2, he was transferred to advisory army aide to the General Who Supports the State.
entries.literal: In Zhongxing 2, he was transferred to advisory army aide to the General Who Supports the State.

entries.zh: 天監元年，降爵爲子，除散騎常侍，領步兵校尉，以疾不拜，徙爲光祿大夫，俄爲司徒左長史。
entries.en: In Tianjian 1, his title was reduced to viscount; he was appointed Regular Attendant, concurrently Infantry Colonel, but did not take office because of illness. He was shifted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and soon became left chief clerk to the Minister over the Masses.
entries.literal: In Tianjian 1, his title was reduced to viscount; he was appointed Regular Attendant, concurrently Infantry Colonel, but did not take office because of illness. He was shifted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and soon became left chief clerk to the Minister over the Masses.

entries.zh: 子恪與弟子範等，嘗因事入謝，高祖在文德殿引見之，從容謂曰：「我欲與卿兄弟有言。
entries.en: Zike and his younger brother Zifan and the others once came to court to offer thanks on official business. Emperor Wu received them in the Wende Hall and said at his ease, "I wish to speak with you brothers.
entries.literal: Zike and his younger brother Zifan and others once entered to give thanks on an affair; the High Ancestor received them in the Wende Hall and said at ease, "I wish to have words with you brothers.

entries.zh: 夫天下之寶，本是公器，非可力得。
entries.en: The treasures of the realm are by nature the common property of all; they cannot be seized by force.
entries.literal: Now, the treasures of All-under-Heaven are by nature public instruments; they cannot be obtained by force.

entries.zh: 苟無期運，雖有項籍之力，終亦敗亡。
entries.en: Without the proper season of fortune, even with the strength of Xiang Yu, one would in the end be defeated and destroyed.
entries.literal: If one lacks the season of fortune, though one have the strength of Xiang Yu, in the end one will be defeated and perish.

entries.zh: 所以班彪《王命論》云：『所求不過一金，然終轉死溝壑』。
entries.en: Hence Ban Biao's Discourse on the Mandate of Kingship says, "What he sought was no more than a single piece of gold, yet in the end he died in ditches and gullies."
entries.literal: Therefore Ban Biao's "Discourse on the Mandate of Kingship" says, "What he sought was no more than one piece of gold, yet in the end he turned to die in ditches and gullies."

entries.zh: 卿不應不讀此書。
entries.en: You ought to have read this book.
entries.literal: You ought not to have failed to read this book.

entries.zh: 宋孝武爲性猜忌，兄弟粗有令名者，無不因事鴆毒，所遺唯有景和。
entries.en: Emperor Xiaowu of Song was by nature suspicious and jealous. Of his brothers who had any reputation at all, none escaped being poisoned on one pretext or another—only Jinghe was left alive.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Song was by nature suspicious and jealous; of his brothers who roughly had a good name, none failed to be poisoned on some pretext—only Jinghe was left.

entries.zh: 至於朝臣之中，或疑有天命而致害者，枉濫相繼，然而或疑有天命而不能害者，或不知有天命而不疑者，于時雖疑卿祖，而無如之何。
entries.en: Among the court ministers as well, some whom he suspected of possessing the Mandate of Heaven were destroyed, and wrongful killings followed one after another. Yet some whom he suspected of possessing the Mandate of Heaven he could not destroy, and some who did not know they possessed the Mandate of Heaven he did not suspect. At that time he did suspect your grandfather, yet could do nothing about it.
entries.literal: As for the court ministers, some whom he suspected of possessing the Mandate of Heaven he harmed, and wrongful killings followed one after another; yet some whom he suspected of possessing the Mandate of Heaven he could not harm, and some who did not know they possessed the Mandate of Heaven he did not suspect. At that time, though he suspected your grandfather, he could do nothing about it.

entries.zh: 此是疑而不得。
entries.en: This was a case of suspecting but being unable to act.
entries.literal: This was a case of suspecting but not being able to obtain the result.

entries.zh: 又有不疑者，如宋明帝本爲庸常被免，豈疑而得全？
entries.en: There were also those he did not suspect, such as Emperor Ming of Song, who had originally been a mediocre man and was dismissed from office—how could suspicion have preserved him?
entries.literal: There were also those he did not suspect, such as Emperor Ming of Song, who had originally been a mediocre commoner and was dismissed—how could suspicion have preserved him?

entries.zh: 又復我于時已年二歲，彼豈知我應有今日？
entries.en: Moreover, at that time I was already two years old—how could he have known that I was destined for what I have today?
entries.literal: Moreover, at that time I was already two years old—how could he have known that I was destined for what I have today?

entries.zh: 當知有天命者，非人所害，害亦不能得。
entries.en: You should understand that one who possesses the Mandate of Heaven cannot be harmed by men; even if harm is attempted, it cannot succeed.
entries.literal: You should know that one who possesses the Mandate of Heaven cannot be harmed by men; even if harm is attempted, it cannot be obtained.

entries.zh: 我初平建康城，朝廷內外皆勸我云：『時代革異，物心須一，宜行處分。』
entries.en: When I first pacified Jiankang, everyone inside and outside the court urged me, saying, "The age has changed; minds must be unified; you ought to take decisive measures."
entries.literal: When I first pacified Jiankang, everyone inside and outside the court urged me, saying, "The age has changed; minds must be unified; you ought to take decisive measures."

entries.zh: 我于時依此而行，誰謂不可！
entries.en: At the time I acted accordingly—who would say it was wrong!
entries.literal: At the time I acted accordingly—who would say it was not permissible!

entries.zh: 我政言江左以來，代謝必相誅戮，此是傷於和氣，所以國祚例不靈長。
