entries.en: I maintain only that since the establishment of the regime south of the Yangtze, each change of dynasty has been accompanied by mutual slaughter. This wounds the harmony of spirit, and so imperial fortunes as a rule do not last long.
entries.literal: I maintain only that since the establishment of the regime south of the Yangtze, each change of dynasty has necessarily involved mutual slaughter—this wounds the harmony of spirit, and so imperial fortunes as a rule do not last long.

entries.zh: 所謂『殷鑒不遠，在夏後之世』。
entries.en: As the saying goes, "The lesson of Yin is not far off; it is in the age of the Xia descendants."
entries.literal: As the saying goes, "The lesson of Yin is not far off; it is in the age of the Xia descendants."

entries.zh: 此是一義。
entries.en: This is the first point.
entries.literal: This is the first point.

entries.zh: 二者，齊梁雖曰革代，義異往時。
entries.en: Second, although Qi and Liang are called a change of dynasty, the principle differs from times past.
entries.literal: Second, although Qi and Liang are called a change of dynasty, the principle differs from times past.

entries.zh: 我與卿兄弟雖復絕服二世，宗屬未遠。
entries.en: Though you brothers and I are separated by two generations of mourning dress, our kinship is not remote.
entries.literal: Though you brothers and I are separated by two generations of mourning dress, our kinship is not remote.

entries.zh: 卿勿言兄弟是親，人家兄弟自有周旋者，有不周旋者，況五服之屬邪？
entries.en: Do not speak of brothers as being close by nature. Among ordinary families, brothers have those who get along and those who do not—how much more so for kin within five degrees of mourning?
entries.literal: Do not speak of brothers as being close—among ordinary families brothers have those who associate and those who do not; how much more so for kin within five degrees of mourning?

entries.zh: 齊業之初，亦是甘苦共嘗，腹心在我。
entries.en: In the early years of the Qi state, we too shared bitterness and sweetness, and the innermost confidence was placed in me.
entries.literal: In the early years of the Qi enterprise, we too shared bitterness and sweetness; you were trusted as my inner confidants.

entries.zh: 卿兄弟年少，理當不悉。
entries.en: You brothers are young and can scarcely know this fully.
entries.literal: You brothers are young and can scarcely know this fully.

entries.zh: 我與卿兄弟，便是情同一家，豈當都不念此，作行路事。
entries.en: With you brothers I am as close as one family. How could I fail to bear this in mind and treat you as strangers on the road?
entries.literal: With you brothers I am as close as one family—how could I fail to bear this in mind and treat you as strangers on the road?

entries.zh: 此是二義。
entries.en: This is the second point.
entries.literal: This is the second point.

entries.zh: 我有今日，非是本意所求。
entries.en: What I have today was not what I originally sought.
entries.literal: What I have today was not what I originally sought.

entries.zh: 且建武屠滅卿門，致卿兄弟塗炭。
entries.en: Moreover, the Jianwu reign annihilated your clan's households and brought you brothers to ruin.
entries.literal: Moreover, the Jianwu reign annihilated your clan's households and brought you brothers to ruin.

entries.zh: 我起義兵，非惟自雪門恥，亦是爲卿兄弟報仇。
entries.en: When I raised the army of righteousness, it was not only to avenge my own house's shame but also to take revenge for you brothers.
entries.literal: When I raised the army of righteousness, it was not only to avenge my own house's shame but also to take revenge for you brothers.

entries.zh: 卿若能在建武、永元之世，撥亂反正，我雖起樊、鄧，豈得不釋戈推奉；
entries.en: Had you been able in the Jianwu and Yongyuan reigns to restore order and right the wrongs, though I had risen at Fan and Deng, how could I have failed to lay down my weapons and yield the lead?
entries.literal: Had you been able in the Jianwu and Yongyuan reigns to restore order and right the wrongs, though I had risen at Fan and Deng, how could I have failed to lay down my weapons and yield the lead?

entries.zh: 其雖欲不已，亦是師出無名。
entries.en: Even had I wished to continue, it would have been a campaign without righteous cause.
entries.literal: Even had I wished to continue, it would have been a campaign without righteous cause.

entries.zh: 我今爲卿報仇，且時代革異，望卿兄弟盡節報我耳。
entries.en: Now I have avenged you, and the age has changed. I look to you brothers to exhaust your loyalty in serving me.
entries.literal: Now I have avenged you, and the age has changed; I look to you brothers to exhaust your loyalty in serving me.

entries.zh: 且我自藉喪亂，代明帝家天下耳，不取卿家天下。
entries.en: I took advantage of the chaos to inherit Emperor Ming's realm—I did not seize your family's realm.
entries.literal: Moreover, I took advantage of the chaos to inherit Emperor Ming's realm—I did not seize your family's realm.

entries.zh: 昔劉子輿自稱成帝子，光武言『假使成帝更生，天下亦不復可得，況子輿乎』。
entries.en: In former times Liu Ziyu styled himself a son of Emperor Cheng; Emperor Guangwu said, "Suppose even Emperor Cheng were reborn—the realm could no longer be obtained; how much less Liu Ziyu?"
entries.literal: In former times Liu Ziyu styled himself a son of Emperor Cheng; Emperor Guangwu said, "Suppose even Emperor Cheng were reborn—the realm could no longer be obtained; how much less Liu Ziyu?"

entries.zh: 梁初，人勸我相誅滅者，我答之猶如向孝武時事：彼若苟有天命，非我所能殺；
entries.en: Early in the Liang, there were those who urged me to carry out mass slaughter. I answered as in the time of Emperor Xiaowu: if they truly possessed the Mandate of Heaven, I could not kill them;
entries.literal: Early in the Liang, there were those who urged me to carry out mass slaughter; I answered as in the time of Emperor Xiaowu: if they truly possessed the Mandate of Heaven, I could not kill them;

entries.zh: 若其無期運，何忽行此，政足示無度量。
entries.en: if they lacked the season of fortune, why suddenly do this—it would only show a want of magnanimity.
entries.literal: if they lacked the season of fortune, why suddenly do this—it would only show a want of magnanimity.

entries.zh: 曹志親是魏武帝孫，陳思之子，事晉武能爲晉室忠臣，此卽卿事例。
entries.en: Cao Zhi was a close relative of Emperor Wu of Wei and a son of Prince Si of Chen; serving Emperor Wu of Jin he could be a loyal minister to the Jin house—this is exactly your case.
entries.literal: Cao Zhi was a close relative of Emperor Wu of Wei and a son of Prince Si of Chen; serving Emperor Wu of Jin he could be a loyal minister to the Jin house—this is exactly your case.

entries.zh: 卿是宗室，情義異佗，方坦然相期，卿無復懷自外之意。
entries.en: You are of the imperial clan; your bond differs from others. I openly expect much of you—do not harbor thoughts of standing apart.
entries.literal: You are of the imperial clan; your bond differs from others. I openly expect much of you; do not harbor thoughts of standing apart.

entries.zh: 小待，自當知我寸心。」
entries.en: Wait a little—you will come to know my true heart."
entries.literal: Wait a little—you will come to know my true heart."

entries.zh: 又文獻王時，內齋直帳閹人趙叔祖，天監初，入爲臺齋帥，在壽光省，高祖呼叔祖曰：「我本識汝在北第，以汝舊人，故每驅使。
entries.en: Again, in the time of the Literary and Cultivated Prince, Zhao Shuzu was a eunuch attendant in the inner quarters. At the beginning of Tianjian he entered service as Master of the Terrace Quarters in the Shouguang office. The Emperor called Shuzu and said, "I knew you long ago at the Northern Residence, and because you are an old acquaintance I have you run errands often.
entries.literal: Again, in the time of the Literary and Cultivated Prince, Zhao Shuzu was a eunuch attendant in the inner quarters; at the beginning of Tianjian he entered service as Master of the Terrace Quarters, in the Shouguang office. The High Ancestor called Shuzu and said, "I knew you long ago at the Northern Residence, and because you are an old acquaintance I have you run errands often.

entries.zh: 汝比見北第諸郎不？」
entries.en: Have you lately seen the various gentlemen of the Northern Residence?"
entries.literal: Have you lately seen the various gentlemen of the Northern Residence?"

entries.zh: 叔祖奉答云：「比多在直，出外甚疏，假使暫出，亦不能得往。」
entries.en: Shuzu replied, "Of late I have mostly been on duty and have gone out very rarely. Even when I went out briefly I could not get there."
entries.literal: Shuzu replied, "Of late I have mostly been on duty and have gone out very rarely; even when I went out briefly I could not get there."

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「若見北第諸郎，道我此意：我今日雖是革代，情同一家；
entries.en: The Emperor said, "If you see the gentlemen of the Northern Residence, convey my meaning: though today we have changed the dynasty, our feeling is as of one family;
entries.literal: The High Ancestor said, "If you see the gentlemen of the Northern Residence, convey my meaning: though today we have changed the dynasty, our feeling is as of one family;

entries.zh: 但今磐石未立，所以未得用諸郎者，非惟在我未宜，亦是欲使諸郎得安耳。
entries.en: only because the foundation stone is not yet set, I have not been able to employ you gentlemen—not only because it would be improper for me, but also because I wish to let you gentlemen dwell in peace.
entries.literal: only because the foundation stone is not yet set, I have not been able to employ you gentlemen—not only because it would be improper for me, but also because I wish to let you gentlemen dwell in peace.

entries.zh: 但閉門高枕，後自當見我心。」
entries.en: Simply shut your gates and rest your heads on high pillows—you will later come to see my heart."
entries.literal: Simply shut your gates and rest your heads on high pillows—you will later come to see my heart."

entries.zh: 叔祖卽出外具宣敕語。
entries.en: Shuzu went out at once and fully proclaimed the imperial words.
entries.literal: Shuzu went out at once and fully proclaimed the imperial words.

entries.zh: 子顯偉容貌，身長八尺。
entries.en: Zixian had an imposing appearance and stood eight chi tall.
entries.literal: Zixian had an imposing appearance, eight chi in height.

entries.zh: 好學，工屬文。
entries.en: He loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.
entries.literal: He loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.

entries.zh: 嘗著《鴻序賦》，尚書令沈約見而稱曰：「可謂得明道之高致，蓋《幽通》之流也。」
entries.en: He once composed An Ode on the Wild Goose's Preface. Minister of State Shen Yue saw it and praised it, saying, "One may say he has attained the lofty reach of the Way—of the same stream as The Mysterious Communication."
entries.literal: He once composed An Ode on the Wild Goose's Preface; Minister of State Shen Yue saw it and praised it, saying, "One may say he has attained the lofty reach of the Way—of the same stream as The Mysterious Communication."

entries.zh: 又采衆家《後漢》，考正同異，爲一家之書。
entries.en: He also drew on various Later Han histories, reconciled their agreements and differences, and produced a unified work of his own.
entries.literal: He also gathered various families' Later Han histories, corrected agreements and differences, and made them into a single unified book.

entries.zh: 又啟撰《齊史》，書成，表奏之，詔付秘閣。
entries.en: He also memorialized to compile the History of Qi. When the book was complete he submitted it, and an edict ordered it deposited in the secret archive.
entries.literal: He also memorialized to compile the History of Qi; when the book was complete he submitted it, and an edict ordered it deposited in the secret archive.

entries.zh: 累遷太子中舍人，建康令，邵陵王友，丹陽尹丞，中書郎，守宗正卿。
entries.en: He was promoted through posts to Attendant to the Heir Apparent, Magistrate of Jiankang, Friend to the Prince of Shaoling, Assistant Magistrate of Danyang, Palace Secretariat Gentleman, and Acting Director of the Imperial Clan.
entries.literal: He was promoted through posts to Attendant to the Heir Apparent, Magistrate of Jiankang, Friend to the Prince of Shaoling, Assistant Magistrate of Danyang, Palace Secretariat Gentleman, and Acting Director of the Imperial Clan.

entries.zh: 出爲臨川內史，還除黃門郎。
entries.en: He went out as Internal Governor of Linchuan. On his return he was appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
entries.literal: He went out as Internal Governor of Linchuan; on return he was appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

entries.zh: 中大通二年，遷長兼侍中。
entries.en: In the second year of Zhongdatong he was promoted to Senior Palace Attendant with concurrent appointment.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhongdatong he was promoted to Senior Palace Attendant with concurrent appointment.

entries.zh: 高祖雅愛子顯才，又嘉其容止吐納，每御筵侍坐，偏顧訪焉。
entries.en: The Emperor greatly loved Zixian's talent and also admired his bearing and speech. Whenever he held a banquet Zixian sat in attendance and received special attention and inquiry.
entries.literal: The High Ancestor greatly loved Zixian's talent and also admired his bearing and speech; whenever he held a banquet Zixian sat in attendance and received special attention and inquiry.

entries.zh: 嘗從容謂子顯曰：「我造《通史》，此書若成，衆史可廢。」
entries.en: He once said at ease to Zixian, "I am composing the Comprehensive History. If this book is completed, the various histories may be discarded."
entries.literal: He once said at ease to Zixian, "I am composing the Comprehensive History; if this book is completed, the various histories may be discarded."

entries.zh: 子顯對曰：「仲尼贊《易》道，黜《八索》，述職方，除《九丘》，聖制符同，復在茲日。」
entries.en: Zixian replied, "Confucius praised the Way of the Changes, dismissed the Eight Canons, expounded the Regional Officers, and removed the Nine Mounds—sage standards match; again on this day."
entries.literal: Zixian replied, "Confucius praised the Way of the Changes, dismissed the Eight Canons, expounded the Regional Officers, and removed the Nine Mounds—sage standards match; again on this day."

entries.zh: 時以爲名對。
entries.en: At the time this was considered a famous reply.
entries.literal: At the time this was considered a famous reply.

entries.zh: 三年，以本官領國子博士。
entries.en: In the third year, in his existing office he concurrently served as Erudite of the Imperial University.
entries.literal: In the third year, in his existing office he concurrently served as Erudite of the Imperial University.

entries.zh: 高祖所制經義，未列學官，子顯在職，表置助教一人，生十人。
entries.en: The classical exegeses composed by the Emperor had not been listed among the academic officers. Zixian while in office memorialized to appoint one teaching assistant and ten students.
entries.literal: The classical exegeses composed by the High Ancestor had not been listed among the academic officers; Zixian while in office memorialized to appoint one teaching assistant and ten students.

entries.zh: 又啟撰高祖集，并《普通北伐記》。
entries.en: He also memorialized to compile the Emperor's collected writings, together with the Record of the Putong Northern Campaign.
entries.literal: He also memorialized to compile the High Ancestor's collected writings, together with the Record of the Putong Northern Campaign.

entries.zh: 其年遷國子祭酒，又加侍中，於學遞述高祖《五經義》。
entries.en: That year he was promoted to Libationer of the Imperial University and also added as Palace Attendant. At the academy he lectured in succession on the Emperor's Exegeses of the Five Classics.
entries.literal: That year he was promoted to Libationer of the Imperial University and also added as Palace Attendant; at the academy he lectured in succession on the High Ancestor's Exegeses of the Five Classics.

entries.zh: 五年，遷吏部尚書，侍中如故。
entries.en: In the fifth year he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel, retaining his post as Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel, retaining his post as Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 二子序、愷，並少知名。
entries.en: His two sons Xu and Kai both were known from youth.
entries.literal: His two sons Xu and Kai both were known from youth.

entries.zh: 序，太清中歷官太子家令，中庶子，並掌管記。
entries.en: Xu in the Taiqing era held office as Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household, Junior Mentor, and concurrently managed records.
entries.literal: Xu in the Taiqing era held office as Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household, Junior Mentor, and concurrently managed records.

entries.zh: 及亂，於城內卒。
entries.en: When the turmoil came, he died within the city.
entries.literal: When the turmoil came, he died within the city.

entries.zh: 愷，初爲國子生，對策高第，州又舉秀才。
entries.en: Kai at first was a student of the Imperial University, ranked high in the policy examination, and the province also nominated him as Cultivated Talent.
entries.literal: Kai at first was a student of the Imperial University, ranked high in the policy examination, and the province also nominated him as Cultivated Talent.

entries.zh: 起家秘書郎，遷太子中舍人，王府主簿，太子洗馬，父憂去職。
entries.en: He began his career as Secretariat Gentleman, was promoted to Attendant to the Heir Apparent, Chief Clerk of a princely establishment, and Groom of the Heir Apparent, and resigned on his father's mourning.
entries.literal: He began his career as Secretariat Gentleman, was promoted to Attendant to the Heir Apparent, Chief Clerk of a princely establishment, and Groom of the Heir Apparent, and resigned on his father's mourning.

entries.zh: 服闋，復除太子洗馬，遷中舍人，並掌管記。
entries.en: When mourning ended he was again appointed Groom of the Heir Apparent, promoted to Attendant, and concurrently managed records.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he was again appointed Groom of the Heir Apparent, promoted to Attendant, and concurrently managed records.

entries.zh: 累遷宣城王文學，中書郎，太子家令，又掌管記。
entries.en: He was promoted through posts to Literary Scholar to the Prince of Xuancheng, Palace Secretariat Gentleman, and Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household, again managing records.
entries.literal: He was promoted through posts to Literary Scholar to the Prince of Xuancheng, Palace Secretariat Gentleman, and Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household, again managing records.

entries.zh: 愷才學譽望，時論以方其父，太宗在東宮，早引接之。
entries.en: Kai's talent, learning, and reputation led contemporary opinion to compare him with his father. Emperor Jianwen while in the Eastern Palace drew him in early.
entries.literal: Kai's talent, learning, and reputation led contemporary opinion to compare him with his father; the Taizong while in the Eastern Palace drew him in early.

entries.zh: 時中庶子謝嘏出守建安，於宣猷堂宴餞，並召時才賦詩，同用十五劇韻，愷詩先就，其辭又美。
entries.en: At the time Junior Mentor Xie Xia was going out to guard Jian'an. At a farewell banquet in the Xuanyou Hall the talented men of the age were summoned to compose poems, all using the same fifteen rhyme categories. Kai's poem was finished first and its wording was also fine.
entries.literal: At the time Junior Mentor Xie Xia was going out to guard Jian'an; at a farewell banquet in the Xuanyou Hall the talented men of the age were summoned to compose poems, all using the same fifteen rhyme categories; Kai's poem was finished first and its wording was also fine.

entries.zh: 太宗與湘東王令曰：「王筠本自舊手，後進有蕭愷可稱，信爲才子。」
entries.en: Emperor Jianwen wrote to the Prince of Xiangdong, "Wang Yun is an old hand by nature; among the rising generation Xiao Kai may be praised—truly a talented man."
entries.literal: The Taizong wrote to the Prince of Xiangdong, "Wang Yun is an old hand by nature; among the rising generation Xiao Kai may be praised—truly a talented man."

entries.zh: 先是時太學博士顧野王奉令撰《玉篇》，太宗嫌其書詳略未當，以愷博學，於文字尤善，使更與學士刪改。
entries.en: Earlier, Erudite of the Imperial University Gu Yewang had been ordered to compile the Jade Chapters. Emperor Jianwen found the book's detail and brevity not quite right, and because Kai was broadly learned and especially skilled in written characters, had him revise it again with the academicians.
entries.literal: Earlier, Erudite of the Imperial University Gu Yewang had been ordered to compile the Jade Chapters; the Taizong found the book's detail and brevity not quite right, and because Kai was broadly learned and especially skilled in written characters, had him revise it again with the academicians.

entries.zh: 遷中庶子，未拜，徙爲吏部郎。
entries.en: He was transferred to Junior Mentor, but before he was installed he was moved to Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Junior Mentor; not yet installed, he was moved to Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 太清二年，遷御史中丞。
entries.en: In the second year of Taiqing he was promoted to Imperial Censor.
entries.literal: In the second year of Taiqing he was promoted to Imperial Censor.

entries.zh: 頃之，侯景寇亂，愷於城內遷侍中，尋卒官，時年四十四。
entries.en: Shortly afterward Hou Jing raided and brought turmoil. Kai within the city was promoted to Palace Attendant and soon died in office, aged forty-four.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward Hou Jing raided and brought turmoil; Kai within the city was promoted to Palace Attendant and soon died in office, aged forty-four.

entries.zh: 文集並亡逸。
entries.en: His collected works were all lost.
entries.literal: His collected works were all lost.

entries.zh: 子雲善草隸書，爲世楷法。
entries.en: Ziyun was skilled in cursive and clerical script and became the standard for the age.
entries.literal: Ziyun was skilled in cursive and clerical script and became the standard for the age.

entries.zh: 自雲善效鐘元常、王逸少而微變字體。
entries.en: He himself said he was skilled at imitating Zhong You and Wang Xizhi while slightly varying the character forms.
entries.literal: He himself said he was skilled at imitating Zhong You and Wang Xizhi while slightly varying the character forms.

entries.zh: 答敕云：「臣昔不能拔賞，隨世所貴，規摹子敬，多歷年所。
entries.en: Replying to the edict he said, "I formerly could not break free in appreciation and followed what the age valued, modeling myself on Zi Jing for many years.
entries.literal: Replying to the edict he said, "I formerly could not break free in appreciation and followed what the age valued, modeling myself on Zi Jing for many years.

entries.zh: 年二十六，著《晉史》，至《二王列傳》，欲作論語草隸法，言不盡意，遂不能成，略指論飛白一勢而已。
entries.en: At age twenty-six, composing the History of Jin, when I reached the Biographies of the Two Wangs I wished to compose a discourse on cursive and clerical methods, but words could not exhaust the meaning and so I could not complete it—I only sketched a discussion of the flying-white manner.
entries.literal: At age twenty-six, composing the History of Jin, when I reached the Biographies of the Two Wangs I wished to compose a discourse on cursive and clerical methods, but words could not exhaust the meaning and so I could not complete it—I only sketched a discussion of the flying-white manner.

entries.zh: 十許年來，始見敕旨《論書》一卷，商略筆勢，洞澈字體；
entries.en: For some ten years I have only now seen the edict's Treatise on Calligraphy in one juan, weighing brush momentum and penetrating character forms;
entries.literal: For some ten years I have only now seen the edict's Treatise on Calligraphy in one juan, weighing brush momentum and penetrating character forms;

entries.zh: 又以逸少之不及元常，猶子敬之不及逸少。
entries.en: and also that Xizhi does not match You, just as Zi Jing does not match Xizhi.
entries.literal: and also that Xizhi does not match You, just as Zi Jing does not match Xizhi.

entries.zh: 自此研思，方悟隸式，始變子敬，全範元常。
entries.en: From this I studied and reflected and at last understood clerical forms. I began to change from Zi Jing and wholly took You as my model.
entries.literal: From this I studied and reflected and at last understood clerical forms; I began to change from Zi Jing and wholly took You as my model.

entries.zh: 逮爾以來，自覺功進。」
entries.en: Since then I have felt my achievement advance."
entries.literal: Since then I have felt my achievement advance."

entries.zh: 其書迹雅爲高祖所重，嘗論子雲書曰：「筆力勁駿，心手相應，巧逾杜度，美過崔寔，當與元常並驅爭先。」
entries.en: His calligraphic traces were elegantly valued by the Emperor, who once discussed Ziyun's writing, saying, "Brush strength vigorous and fleet, heart and hand in accord; skill surpassing Du Du, beauty exceeding Cui Shi—he ought to race neck and neck with You."
entries.literal: His calligraphic traces were elegantly valued by the High Ancestor, who once discussed Ziyun's writing, saying, "Brush strength vigorous and fleet, heart and hand in accord; skill surpassing Du Du, beauty exceeding Cui Shi—he ought to race neck and neck with You."

entries.zh: 其見賞如此。
entries.en: Thus was he appreciated.
entries.literal: Thus was he appreciated.

entries.zh: 梁初，郊廟未革牲牷，樂辭皆沈約撰，至是承用，子雲始建言宜改。
entries.en: Early in the Liang, the suburban and ancestral temples had not yet reformed the sacrificial victims. The hymn texts were all composed by Shen Yue and were still in use. Ziyun first memorialized that they ought to be changed.
entries.literal: Early in the Liang, the suburban and ancestral temples had not yet reformed the sacrificial victims; the hymn texts were all composed by Shen Yue and were still in use; Ziyun first memorialized that they ought to be changed.

entries.zh: 啟曰：「伏惟聖敬率由，尊嚴郊廟，得西鄰之心，知周、孔之跡，載革牢俎，德通神明，黍稷蘋藻，竭誠嚴配，經國制度，方懸日月，垂訓百王，於是乎在。
entries.en: His memorial said, "I bow to consider that in sacred reverence you follow the constant way, honoring the suburban and ancestral temples, attaining the heart of the western neighbor, knowing the traces of Zhou and Confucius, reforming the victims on the altar, virtue reaching the spirits, millet and offerings presented with full sincerity in solemn matching—statecraft and institutions hang like sun and moon; instruction for a hundred kings lies herein.
entries.literal: His memorial said, "I bow to consider that in sacred reverence you follow the constant way, honoring the suburban and ancestral temples, attaining the heart of the western neighbor, knowing the traces of Zhou and Confucius, reforming the victims on the altar, virtue reaching the spirits, millet and offerings presented with full sincerity in solemn matching—statecraft and institutions hang like sun and moon; instruction for a hundred kings lies herein.

entries.zh: 臣比兼職齋官，見伶人所歌，猶用未革牲前曲。
entries.en: I recently held a concurrent post as fasting officer and saw what the musicians sang—they still used the melodies from before the victims were reformed.
entries.literal: I recently held a concurrent post as fasting officer and saw what the musicians sang—they still used the melodies from before the victims were reformed.

entries.zh: 圜丘視燎，尚言『式備牲牷』；
entries.en: At the Round Mound when viewing the burning offering, they still say, "Thus prepare the sacrificial victims";
entries.literal: At the Round Mound when viewing the burning offering, they still say, "Thus prepare the sacrificial victims";

entries.zh: 北郊《諴雅》，亦奏『牲雲孔備』；
entries.en: the Northern Suburb's Xianya hymn also performs "the victims are fully prepared";
entries.literal: the Northern Suburb's Xianya hymn also performs "the victims are fully prepared";

entries.zh: 清廟登歌，而稱『我牲以潔』；
entries.en: the Clear Temple's ascending hymn calls "our victims are pure";
entries.literal: the Clear Temple's ascending hymn calls "our victims are pure";

entries.zh: 三朝食舉，猶詠『朱尾碧鱗』。
entries.en: at the three mornings' food-raising they still chant "red tails and green scales."
entries.literal: at the three mornings' food-raising they still chant "red tails and green scales."

entries.zh: 聲被鼓鐘，未符盛制。
entries.en: The sounds spread among drums and bells and do not match the flourishing institutions.
entries.literal: The sounds spread among drums and bells and do not match the flourishing institutions.

entries.zh: 臣職司儒訓，意以爲疑，未審應改定樂辭以不？」
entries.en: I hold office in Confucian instruction and consider this doubtful. I do not know whether the hymn texts ought to be revised or not?"
entries.literal: I hold office in Confucian instruction and consider this doubtful; I do not know whether the hymn texts ought to be revised or not?"

entries.zh: 敕答曰：「此是主者守株，宜急改也。」
entries.en: The edict replied, "This is the responsible officer clinging to the stump; it should be changed at once."
entries.literal: The edict replied, "This is the responsible officer clinging to the stump; it should be changed at once."

entries.zh: 仍使子雲撰定。
entries.en: Ziyun was then ordered to draft and fix them.
entries.literal: Ziyun was then ordered to draft and fix them.

entries.zh: 敕曰：「郊廟歌辭，應須典誥大語，不得雜用子史文章淺言；
entries.en: An edict said, "Suburban and temple hymn texts must use the great language of the canonical edicts. One must not mix in shallow words from the Masters and histories;
entries.literal: An edict said, "Suburban and temple hymn texts must use the great language of the canonical edicts; one must not mix in shallow words from the Masters and histories;

entries.zh: 而沈約所撰，亦多舛謬。」
entries.en: and what Shen Yue composed also has many errors."
entries.literal: and what Shen Yue composed also has many errors."

entries.zh: 子雲答敕曰：「殷薦朝饗，樂以雅名，理應正采《五經》，聖人成教。
entries.en: Ziyun replied to the edict, "Yin offerings and morning feasts—music takes its elegant names. By principle one ought rightly to draw on the Five Classics, the completed teaching of the sages.
entries.literal: Ziyun replied to the edict, "Yin offerings and morning feasts—music takes its elegant names; by principle one ought rightly to draw on the Five Classics, the completed teaching of the sages.

entries.zh: 而漢來此制，不全用經典；
entries.en: Yet since Han this institution has not fully used the classics;
entries.literal: Yet since Han this institution has not fully used the classics;

entries.zh: 約之所撰，彌復淺雜。
entries.en: what Yue composed is all the more shallow and miscellaneous.
entries.literal: what Yue composed is all the more shallow and miscellaneous.

entries.zh: 臣前所易約十曲，惟知牲牷旣革，宜改歌辭，而猶承例，不嫌流俗乖體。
entries.en: The ten pieces I earlier revised of Yue's knew only that the victims had been reformed and the hymn texts ought to be changed, yet still followed precedent and did not mind that vulgar custom violated proper form.
entries.literal: The ten pieces I earlier revised of Yue's knew only that the victims had been reformed and the hymn texts ought to be changed, yet still followed precedent and did not mind that vulgar custom violated proper form.

entries.zh: 旣奉令旨，始得發蒙。
entries.en: Having received the command, I have at last been enlightened.
entries.literal: Having received the command, I have at last been enlightened.

entries.zh: 臣夙本庸滯，昭然忽朗，謹依成旨，悉改約制。
entries.en: I have long been dull and slow by nature, but suddenly all became clear. I respectfully follow the completed command and have wholly changed Yue's system.
entries.literal: I have long been dull and slow by nature, but suddenly all became clear; I respectfully follow the completed command and have wholly changed Yue's system.

entries.zh: 惟用《五經》爲本，其次《爾雅》、《周易》、《尚書》、《大戴禮》，卽是經誥之流，愚意亦取兼用。
entries.en: I use only the Five Classics as foundation; next the Erya, Book of Changes, Documents, and Grand Dai Rites—that is, texts of canonical edicts—and in my humble opinion I also take these for combined use.
entries.literal: I use only the Five Classics as foundation; next the Erya, Book of Changes, Documents, and Grand Dai Rites—that is, texts of canonical edicts—and in my humble opinion I also take these for combined use.

entries.zh: 臣又尋唐、虞諸書，殷《頌》周《雅》，稱美是一，而復各述時事。
entries.en: I further examine the books of Tang and Yu, the Yin Odes and Zhou Elegantiae—praise is one, yet each again relates the affairs of its time.
entries.literal: I further examine the books of Tang and Yu, the Yin Odes and Zhou Elegantiae—praise is one, yet each again relates the affairs of its time.

entries.zh: 大梁革服，偃武修文，制禮作樂，義高三正；
entries.en: Great Liang has changed its garments, laid down arms and cultivated letters, established rites and made music—its righteousness surpasses the Three Corrections;
entries.literal: Great Liang has changed its garments, laid down arms and cultivated letters, established rites and made music—its righteousness surpasses the Three Corrections;

entries.zh: 而約撰歌辭，惟浸稱聖德之美，了不序皇朝製作事。
entries.en: yet Yue's composed hymn texts only soak in praise of sacred virtue's beauty and entirely do not narrate the imperial house's creative achievements.
entries.literal: yet Yue's composed hymn texts only soak in praise of sacred virtue's beauty and entirely do not narrate the imperial house's creative achievements.

entries.zh: 《雅》、《頌》前例，於體爲違。
entries.en: The former examples of the Elegantiae and Odes—in form this violates them.
entries.literal: The former examples of the Elegantiae and Odes—in form this violates them.

entries.zh: 伏以聖旨所定《樂論》，鐘律緯緒，文思深微，命世一出，方懸日月，不刊之典，禮樂之教，致治所成。
entries.en: I bow to consider the Treatise on Music fixed by the sacred command—bells, pitch pipes, and their woven principles; literary thought deep and subtle; once in an age; hanging like sun and moon; an unalterable canon; the teaching of rites and music through which good governance is achieved.
entries.literal: I bow to consider the Treatise on Music fixed by the sacred command—bells, pitch pipes, and their woven principles; literary thought deep and subtle; once in an age; hanging like sun and moon; an unalterable canon; the teaching of rites and music through which good governance is achieved.

entries.zh: 謹一二采綴，各隨事顯義，以明製作之美。
entries.en: I respectfully gather and arrange piece by piece, each following its affair to display its meaning, to make clear the beauty of the creative achievements.
entries.literal: I respectfully gather and arrange piece by piece, each following its affair to display its meaning, to make clear the beauty of the creative achievements.

entries.zh: 覃思累日，今始克就，謹以上呈。」
entries.en: Deep thought for many days—today it is at last completed. I respectfully submit it above."
entries.literal: Deep thought for many days—today it is at last completed; I respectfully submit it above."

entries.zh: 敕並施用。
entries.en: The edict ordered all to be put into use.
entries.literal: The edict ordered all to be put into use.

entries.zh: 子雲性沈靜，不樂仕進。
entries.en: Ziyun was quiet and reserved by nature and took no pleasure in pursuing office.
entries.literal: Ziyun was quiet and reserved by nature and took no pleasure in pursuing office.

entries.zh: 年三十，方起家爲秘書郎。
entries.en: Only at thirty did he begin office as Palace Library Gentleman.
entries.literal: Only at thirty did he begin office as Palace Library Gentleman.

entries.zh: 遷太子舍人，撰《東宮新記》，奏之，敕賜束帛。
entries.en: He was transferred to crown prince attendant, compiled New Records of the Eastern Palace, and submitted it; by edict he was granted bundled silk.
entries.literal: He was transferred to crown prince attendant, compiled New Records of the Eastern Palace, and submitted it; by edict he was granted bundled silk.

entries.zh: 累遷北中郎外兵參軍，晉安王文學，司徒主簿，丹陽尹丞。
entries.en: He rose successively to external military aide to the Northern Central Commandant, literary scholar to the Prince of Jin'an, chief clerk to the Minister over the Masses, and assistant Intendant of Danyang.
entries.literal: He rose successively to external military aide to the Northern Central Commandant, literary scholar to the Prince of Jin'an, chief clerk to the Minister over the Masses, and assistant Intendant of Danyang.

entries.zh: 時湘東王爲京尹，深相賞好，如布衣之交。
entries.en: At the time the Prince of Xiangdong was capital intendant and deeply appreciated and liked him, as if they were friends in commoner clothes.
entries.literal: At the time the Prince of Xiangdong was capital intendant and deeply appreciated and liked him, as if they were friends in commoner clothes.

entries.zh: 遷北中郎廬陵王諮議參軍，兼尚書左丞。
entries.en: He was transferred to advisory army aide to the Prince of Luling, Northern Central Commandant, and concurrently Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: He was transferred to advisory army aide to the Prince of Luling, Northern Central Commandant, and concurrently Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 大通元年，除黃門郎，俄遷輕車將軍，兼司徒左長史。
entries.en: In Datong 1, he was appointed Yellow Gate Gentleman and soon transferred to General of Light Chariots, concurrently left chief clerk to the Minister over the Masses.
entries.literal: In Datong 1, he was appointed Yellow Gate Gentleman and soon transferred to General of Light Chariots, concurrently left chief clerk to the Minister over the Masses.

entries.zh: 二年，入爲吏部。
entries.en: In the second year, he entered court to serve in the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: In the second year, he entered court to serve in the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 三年，遷長兼侍中。
entries.en: In the third year, he was transferred to long-term acting Attendant-in-Ordinary.
entries.literal: In the third year, he was transferred to long-term acting Attendant-in-Ordinary.

entries.zh: 中大通元年，轉太府卿。
entries.en: In Zhongdatong 1, he was transferred to Chamberlain of the Imperial Treasury.
entries.literal: In Zhongdatong 1, he was transferred to Chamberlain of the Imperial Treasury.

entries.zh: 三年，出爲貞威將軍、臨川內史。
entries.en: In the third year, he went out as General of Firm Awe and Interior Minister of Linchuan.
entries.literal: In the third year, he went out as General of Firm Awe and Interior Minister of Linchuan.

entries.zh: 在郡以和理稱，民吏悅之。
entries.en: In the commandery he was praised for harmonious administration, and the people and officials were pleased with him.
entries.literal: In the commandery he was praised for harmonious administration, and the people and officials were pleased with him.

entries.zh: 還除散騎常侍，俄復爲侍中。
entries.en: He returned to court as Regular Attendant and soon again became Attendant-in-Ordinary.
entries.literal: He returned to court as Regular Attendant and soon again became Attendant-in-Ordinary.

entries.zh: 大同二年，遷員外散騎常侍、國子祭酒，領南徐州大中正。
entries.en: In Datong 2, he was transferred to Supernumerary Regular Attendant and Libationer of the Imperial Academy, concurrently grand rectifier of South Xuzhou.
entries.literal: In Datong 2, he was transferred to Supernumerary Regular Attendant and Libationer of the Imperial Academy, concurrently grand rectifier of South Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 頃之，復爲侍中，祭酒、中正如故。
entries.en: Before long, he again became Attendant-in-Ordinary, while remaining Libationer and rectifier as before.
entries.literal: Before long, he again became Attendant-in-Ordinary, while remaining Libationer and rectifier as before.

entries.zh: 七年，出爲仁威將軍、東陽太守。
entries.en: In the seventh year, Ziyun went out as General of Benevolent Awe and administrator of Dongyang.
entries.literal: In the seventh year, Ziyun went out as General of Benevolent Awe and administrator of Dongyang.

entries.zh: 中大同元年，還拜宗正卿。
entries.en: In Zhongdatong 1, he returned to court and was appointed Minister of the Imperial Clan.
entries.literal: In Zhongdatong 1, he returned to court and was appointed Minister of the Imperial Clan.

entries.zh: 太清元年，復爲侍中、國子祭酒，領南徐州大中正。
entries.en: In Taiqing 1, he again became Attendant-in-Ordinary and Libationer of the Imperial Academy, concurrently grand rectifier of South Xuzhou.
entries.literal: In Taiqing 1, he again became Attendant-in-Ordinary and Libationer of the Imperial Academy, concurrently grand rectifier of South Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 二年，侯景寇逼，子雲逃民間。
entries.en: In the second year, as Hou Jing's rebels pressed close, Ziyun fled among the common people.
entries.literal: In the second year, as Hou Jing's rebels pressed close, Ziyun fled among the common people.

entries.zh: 三年三月，宮城失守，東奔晉陵，餒卒于顯靈寺僧房，年六十三。
entries.en: In the third month of the third year, when the palace city fell, he fled east to Jinling commandery and died of starvation in a monk's room at Xianling Temple, aged sixty-three.
entries.literal: In the third month of the third year, when the palace city fell, he fled east to Jinling commandery and died of starvation in a monk's room at Xianling Temple, aged sixty-three.

entries.zh: 所著《晉書》一百一十卷，《東宮新記》二十卷。
entries.en: He wrote the Book of Jin in 110 juan and New Records of the Eastern Palace in 20 juan.
entries.literal: He wrote the Book of Jin in 110 juan and New Records of the Eastern Palace in 20 juan.

entries.zh: 第二子特，字世達。
entries.en: His second son Te, style name Shida.
entries.literal: His second son Te, style name Shida.

entries.zh: 早知名，亦善草隸。
entries.en: Known early, he was also skilled in cursive and clerical script.
entries.literal: Known early, he was also skilled in cursive and clerical script.

entries.zh: 高祖嘗謂子雲曰：「子敬之書，不及逸少。
entries.en: The Emperor once said to Ziyun, "Zi Jing's writing does not match Yishao.
entries.literal: The High Ancestor once said to Ziyun, "Zi Jing's writing does not match Yishao.

entries.zh: 近見特跡，遂逼於卿。」
entries.en: Lately seeing Te's traces, they now press close upon yours."
entries.literal: Lately seeing Te's traces, they now press close upon yours."

entries.zh: 歷官著作佐郎，太子舍人，宣惠主簿，中軍記室。
entries.en: He held office as Assistant in the Composition Office, Attendant to the Heir Apparent, Chief Clerk of the Xuanhui Prince, and Recorder of the Central Army.
entries.literal: He held office as Assistant in the Composition Office, Attendant to the Heir Apparent, Chief Clerk of the Xuanhui Prince, and Recorder of the Central Army.

entries.zh: 出爲海鹽令，坐事免。
entries.en: He went out as Magistrate of Haiyan and was dismissed on account of an affair.
entries.literal: He went out as Magistrate of Haiyan and was dismissed on account of an affair.

entries.zh: 年二十五，先子雲卒。
entries.en: At age twenty-five he died before his father Ziyun.
entries.literal: At age twenty-five he died before his father Ziyun.

entries.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：昔魏藉兵威而革漢運，晉因宰輔乃移魏曆，異乎古之禪授，以德相傳，故抑前代宗枝，用絕民望。
entries.en: Yao Cha, Minister of Personnel of Chen, said: In former times Wei relied on military might to change Han's fortune; Jin through its chief ministers shifted Wei's mandate. This differed from ancient abdications where virtue was transmitted, so they suppressed the former dynasty's collateral branches to cut off popular hope.
entries.literal: Yao Cha, Minister of Personnel of Chen, said: In former times Wei relied on military might to change Han's fortune; Jin through its chief ministers shifted Wei's mandate—differing from ancient abdications where virtue was transmitted, they therefore suppressed the former dynasty's collateral branches to cut off popular hope.

entries.zh: 然劉曄、曹志，猶顯於朝；
entries.en: Yet Liu Ye and Cao Zhi still shone at court;
entries.literal: Yet Liu Ye and Cao Zhi still shone at court;

entries.zh: 及宋遂爲廢姓。
entries.en: by the Song they had become an abolished surname.
entries.literal: by Song they had become an abolished surname.

entries.zh: 而齊代，宋之戚屬，一皆殲焉。
entries.en: In the Qi era, Song's kin by marriage were all annihilated.
entries.literal: In the Qi era, Song's kin by marriage were all annihilated.

entries.zh: 其祚不長，抑亦由此。
entries.en: Their fortunes did not last long—this too was a reason.
entries.literal: Their fortunes did not last long—this too was a reason.

entries.zh: 有梁革命，弗取前規，故子恪兄弟及羣從，並隨才任職，通貴滿朝，不失於舊，豈惟魏幽晉顯而已哉。
entries.en: When Liang rose in revolution it did not take the former rule. Therefore Zike, his brothers, and the clan groups all received posts according to talent, filling the court with the eminent without loss compared with old times. Was it only Wei obscure and Jin manifest?
entries.literal: When Liang rose in revolution it did not take the former rule; therefore Zike, his brothers, and the clan groups all received posts according to talent, filling the court with the eminent without loss compared with old times. Was it only Wei obscure and Jin manifest?

entries.zh: 君子以是知高祖之弘量，度越前代矣。
entries.en: The noble person thereby knows the Emperor's broad magnanimity, surpassing former ages.
entries.literal: The noble person thereby knows the High Ancestor's broad magnanimity, surpassing former ages.

entries.zh: 梁書卷第三十五 列傳第二十九
entries.en: Book of Liang, Volume 35, Biography 29
entries.literal: Book of Liang, Volume Thirty-Five, Biography Twenty-Nine

entries.zh: 休源年十一而孤，居喪盡禮，每見父手所寫書，必哀慟流涕，不能自勝，見者莫不爲之垂泣。
entries.en: Orphaned at eleven, he mourned his father with scrupulous ritual. Books in his father's hand always moved him to uncontrollable tears, and even onlookers wept.
entries.literal: At eleven Xiuyuan was orphaned; he observed mourning with full propriety. Whenever he saw books written in his father's own hand, he always wept in grief beyond restraint—and those who saw it never failed to shed tears for him.

entries.zh: 後就吳興沈驎士受經，略通大義。
entries.en: He later studied under Wuxing's Shen Linshi and mastered the classics in broad outline.
entries.literal: Later he studied the classics under Shen Linshi of Wuxing and gained a rough grasp of the essential principles.

entries.zh: 建武四年，州舉秀才，太尉徐孝嗣省其策，深善之，謂同坐曰：「董仲舒、華令思何以尚此，可謂後生之准也。
entries.en: In Jianwu year 4 the province nominated him as xiucai. Grand Marshal Xu Xiaosi read his examination paper and praised it to his companions: "Not even Dong Zhongshu or Hua Lingsi would outshine this youth—he is the standard for his generation.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Jianwu the province recommended him as xiucai; Grand Marshal Xu Xiaosi reviewed his examination answers and deeply approved, saying to those seated with him: "How could Dong Zhongshu or Hua Lingsi surpass this? He may be called the measure of the younger generation.

entries.zh: 觀其此對，足稱王佐之才。」
entries.en: From this answer alone, he clearly has the makings of a king's right-hand man."
entries.literal: Judging from this response, he is fully worthy to be called talent fit to assist a king."

entries.zh: 琅邪王融雅相友善，乃薦之於司徒竟陵王，爲西邸學士。
entries.en: Wang Rong of Langya, who knew him well, recommended him to Minister of Works Prince of Jingling, and he entered the Western Pavilion as a scholar.
entries.literal: Wang Rong of Langya was on friendly terms with him and recommended him to Minister of Works Prince of Jingling, where he became a scholar of the Western Pavilion.

entries.zh: 梁臺建，與南陽劉之遴同爲太學博士，當時以爲美選。
entries.en: When the Liang regime was founded, he and Nanyang's Liu Zhilin were both appointed Masters of the Imperial Academy—an appointment everyone envied.
entries.literal: When the Liang platform was established, he and Liu Zhilin of Nanyang both became Masters of the Imperial Academy—a choice then regarded as fine.

entries.zh: 休源初到京，寓於宗人少府卿孔登宅，曾以祠事入廟，侍中范雲一與相遇，深加褒賞，曰：「不期忽覯清顏，頓袪鄙吝，觀天披霧，驗之今日。」
entries.en: On first reaching the capital he stayed with his kinsman Kong Deng, Junior Director of the Treasury. During a temple visit for sacrifice he met Attendant Fan Yun, who exclaimed: "I never expected to see such a clear face—it sweeps away my vulgarity, like clouds parting to reveal the sky."
entries.literal: When Xiuyuan first arrived in the capital he lodged at the home of his clansman Kong Deng, Junior Director of the Imperial Treasury. Once, entering a temple on sacrificial business, he met Attendant-in-Ordinary Fan Yun, who greatly praised him: "To meet your refined countenance unexpectedly dispels my baseness; parting clouds to see the heavens—verified today."

entries.zh: 後雲命駕到少府門，登便拂筵整帶，謂當詣己，旣而獨造休源，高談盡日，同載還家，登深以爲愧。
entries.en: Later Yun drove to the Junior Director's gate. Deng hurried to set out cushions and straighten his sash, sure the visit was for him. Instead Yun sought out Xiuyuan alone, talked all day, and rode home with him—leaving Deng deeply mortified.
entries.literal: Later Yun ordered his carriage to the Junior Director's gate; Deng hastened to arrange the feast and straighten his sash, expecting Yun had come for him—but Yun went alone to Xiuyuan, talked at length all day, and returned home sharing the same carriage; Deng was deeply ashamed.

entries.zh: 尚書令沈約當朝貴顯，軒蓋盈門，休源或時後來，必虛襟引接，處之坐右，商略文義。
entries.en: Chief Minister Shen Yue, then at the height of power with a constant throng at his gate, always made room for Xiuyuan when he came late, seated him on the right, and debated texts with him.
entries.literal: Chief Minister Shen Yue held great influence at court, his gateway always crowded with visitors; whenever Xiuyuan arrived late, Yue would always receive him with an open mind, seat him at his right hand, and discuss literary meaning.

entries.zh: 其爲通人所推如此。
entries.en: Such was the regard in which men of culture held him.
entries.literal: In this way he was esteemed by those of broad learning.

entries.zh: 革幼而聰敏，早有才思，六歲便解屬文。
entries.en: Clever from childhood and precocious in letters, Ge could write linked prose at six.
entries.literal: Ge was clever and sharp from childhood with early literary talent; at six he could already compose linked prose.

entries.zh: 柔之深加賞器，曰：「此兒必興吾門。」
entries.en: Rouzhi admired him deeply and said, "This child will bring honor to our house."
entries.literal: Rouzhi prized him greatly and said: "This boy will raise our clan."

entries.zh: 九歲丁父艱，與弟觀同生孤貧，傍無師友，兄弟自相訓勖，讀書精力不倦。
entries.en: At nine his father died. He and his younger brother Guan were left alone and poor, with no teachers near at hand; the two brothers pushed each other to study without rest.
entries.literal: At nine he entered mourning for his father; he and his younger brother Guan were together orphaned and poor, without teachers or friends nearby—the brothers urged each other on, reading with tireless energy.

entries.zh: 十六喪母，以孝聞。
entries.en: At sixteen he lost his mother and became known for filial devotion.
entries.literal: At sixteen he lost his mother and became known for filial piety.

entries.zh: 服闋，與觀俱詣太學，補國子生，舉高第。
entries.en: After mourning he and Guan entered the Imperial Academy as National University students and graduated at the top of their class.
entries.literal: When mourning ended, he and Guan both went to the Imperial Academy, enrolled as a student of the National University, and were selected at the top of the class.

entries.zh: 齊中書郎王融、吏部謝朓雅相欽重。
entries.en: Wang Rong, Palace Secretary of Qi, and Xie Tiao, Director of Personnel, both admired him.
entries.literal: Qi Palace Secretary Wang Rong and Personnel Director Xie Tiao both held him in high regard.

entries.zh: 朓嘗宿衛，還過候革，時大雪，見革弊絮單席，而耽學不倦，嗟歎久之，乃脫所著襦，並手割半氈與革充臥具而去。
entries.en: Once, coming off palace guard duty in heavy snow, Tiao visited Ge and found him in patched cotton on a thin mat, still studying without pause. Tiao sighed long, gave him the padded jacket he was wearing, and cut half his felt mat by hand for Ge's bedding before he left.
entries.literal: Tiao once returned from palace guard duty and visited Ge; it was snowing heavily—seeing Ge in worn cotton with only a thin mat yet studying without tiring, Tiao sighed for a long time, took off the padded jacket he wore, and with his own hands cut half a felt mat for Ge's bedding before leaving.

entries.zh: 司徒竟陵王聞其名，引爲西邸學士。
entries.en: Prince of Jingling, Minister of Works, heard of him and made him a Western Pavilion scholar.
entries.literal: Minister of Works Prince of Jingling heard his fame and brought him in as a Western Pavilion scholar.

entries.zh: 弱冠舉南徐州秀才。
entries.en: At twenty he was chosen xiucai of South Xu province.
entries.literal: At weak-cap age he was selected as xiucai of South Xu province.

entries.zh: 時豫章胡諧之行州事，王融與諧之書，令薦革。
entries.en: Hu Xiezhi of Yuzhang was then acting governor; Wang Rong wrote urging him to recommend Ge.
entries.literal: At that time Hu Xiezhi of Yuzhang was acting provincial governor; Wang Rong wrote to Xiezhi instructing him to recommend Ge.

entries.zh: 諧之方貢琅邪王泛，便以革代之。
entries.en: Xiezhi had intended to send up Wang Fan of Langya as the provincial tribute candidate and replaced him with Ge.
entries.literal: Xiezhi was about to present Wang Fan of Langya as tribute and substituted Ge in his place.

entries.zh: 俄除臨川王府行參軍。
entries.en: He was soon made an adjutant in Prince of Linchuan's household.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Adjunct in the Princely Household of Prince of Linchuan.

entries.zh: 高祖嘗問吏部尚書徐勉曰：「今帝業初基，須一人有學藝解朝儀者，爲尚書儀曹郎。
entries.en: Gaozu once asked Xu Mian, Minister of Personnel: "The dynasty is just taking shape. I need a learned man who knows court ceremony for Director of Ritual in the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: The Emperor once asked Minister of Personnel Xu Mian: "Now that imperial enterprise is newly founded, we need someone learned in the arts who understands court rites to serve as Director of Ritual in the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 爲朕思之，誰堪其選？」
entries.en: Think for me—who can fill the post?"
entries.literal: Think for me—who is fit for this choice?"

entries.zh: 勉對曰：「孔休源識具清通，諳練故實，自晉、宋《起居注》誦略上口。」
entries.en: Mian answered: "Kong Xiuyuan is lucid, well grounded in precedent, and can recite the Jin and Song Daily Records almost by heart."
entries.literal: Mian replied: "Kong Xiuyuan has clear, thorough knowledge and is versed in antiquity; the Jin and Song Daily Records he can recite from memory nearly word for word."

entries.zh: 高祖亦素聞之，卽日除兼尚書儀曹郎中。
entries.en: Gaozu had already heard of him and appointed him Acting Director of Ritual that very day.
entries.literal: The Emperor too had long heard of him and the same day appointed him Acting Director of Ritual in the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 是時多所改作，每逮訪前事，休源卽以所誦記隨機斷決，曾無疑滯。
entries.en: The court was then revising many institutions; whenever old precedents were needed, Xiuyuan answered from memory on the spot, never at a loss.
entries.literal: At that time many reforms were underway; whenever they consulted him on past precedents, Xiuyuan decided on the spot from what he had memorized, never hesitating in doubt.

entries.zh: 吏部郎任昉常謂之爲「孔獨誦」。
entries.en: Ren Fang of the Personnel Section nicknamed him "Kong the Sole Reciter."
entries.literal: Personnel Section Director Ren Fang often called him "Kong Who Recites Alone."

entries.zh: 遷建康獄正，及辨訟折獄，時罕冤人。
entries.en: Promoted to Corrector of Jiankang Prison, he heard cases with such care that wrongful convictions were rare.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Corrector of Jiankang Prison; in judging lawsuits and deciding cases, rarely was anyone wrongly convicted.

entries.zh: 後有選人爲獄司者，高祖尚引休源以勵之。
entries.en: When a successor was later chosen for the prison post, Gaozu still held Xiuyuan up as the model.
entries.literal: Later when someone was chosen for prison duty, the Emperor still cited Xiuyuan as an example to encourage them.

entries.zh: 除中書舍人，司徒臨川王府記室參軍，遷尚書左丞，彈肅禮闈，雅允朝望。
entries.en: He became Palace Secretary and secretary to Prince of Linchuan, then Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, where his stern integrity in the examination hall won wide respect.
entries.literal: Appointed Palace Secretary, Secretary to Prince of Linchuan's household, promoted to Left Assistant Director in the Masters of Writing—in the Rites Gate he was stern and upright, fully meeting the court's expectations.

entries.zh: 時太子詹事周舍撰《禮疑義》，自漢魏至于齊梁，並皆搜采，休源所有奏議，咸預編錄。
entries.en: When Crown Prince's Steward Zhou She compiled Doubts on Rites, drawing on Han, Wei, Qi, and Liang, every memorial and opinion Xiuyuan had written was included.
entries.literal: At that time the Crown Prince's Steward Zhou She compiled "Doubts on Rites," searching materials from Han and Wei through Qi and Liang; Xiuyuan's memorials and deliberations were all included in the compilation.

entries.zh: 除給事黃門侍郎，遷長兼御史中丞，正色直繩，無所回避，百僚莫不憚之。
entries.en: Made Supervising Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and then Senior Concurrent Censor, he was unflinching in enforcing the law, and the whole bureaucracy feared him.
entries.literal: Appointed Supervising Gentleman-in-Attendance of the Yellow Gate, promoted to Senior Concurrent Supervisor of Censors—in upright color and straight measure he deferred to nothing; all officials feared him.

entries.zh: 除少府卿，又兼行丹陽尹事。
entries.en: He was appointed Junior Director of the Treasury and also acted as magistrate of Danyang.
entries.literal: Appointed Junior Director of the Imperial Treasury, additionally acting as Magistrate of Danyang.

entries.zh: 出爲宣惠晉安王府長史、南郡太守、行荊州府州事。
entries.en: He left the capital as chief secretary to Propagation and Grace Prince of Jin'an, administrator of Nan commandery, with charge of Jingzhou affairs.
entries.literal: He went out as Chief of the Princely Household of Propagation and Grace Prince of Jin'an, Administrator of Nan commandery, directing Jing province military and civil affairs.

entries.zh: 高祖謂之曰：「荊州總上流沖要，義高分陝，今以十歲兒委卿，善匡翼之，勿憚周昌之舉也。」
entries.en: Gaozu told him: "Jingzhou guards the upper Yangzi and is as vital as the western frontier. I am placing a ten-year-old prince in your hands—guide him well, and do not hesitate to speak bluntly as Zhou Chang did."
entries.literal: The Emperor told him: "Jing province is overall the upper reaches' strategic key; its meaning equals the high divide at Fen. Now I entrust to you a ten-year-old child—well guide and support him; do not shrink from a Zhou Chang's action."

entries.zh: 對曰：「臣以庸鄙，曲荷恩遇，方揣丹誠，效其一割。」
entries.en: He answered: "I am a humble man who has received extraordinary favor; I will give whatever sincerity and effort I possess."
entries.literal: He replied: "Your servant, coarse and lowly, has curiously received your grace; I shall gauge my utmost sincerity and offer what little I can."

entries.zh: 上善其對，乃敕晉安王曰：「孔休源人倫儀錶，汝年尚幼，當每事師之。」
entries.en: Pleased with the answer, Gaozu ordered Prince of Jin'an: "Kong Xiuyuan is a paragon of conduct. You are still young—let him be your teacher in all things."
entries.literal: The Emperor approved his reply and issued an edict to Prince of Jin'an: "Kong Xiuyuan is a model of human relations and deportment. You are still young—take him as teacher in every matter."

entries.zh: 尋而始興王嶦代鎮荊州，復爲憺府長史，南郡太守、行府州事如故。
entries.en: When Prince of Shixing Xiao Dan took over Jingzhou, Xiuyuan stayed on as his chief secretary and Nan commandery administrator with the same duties as before.
entries.literal: Soon Prince of Shixing Xiao Dan replaced him as Jing governor; again he served as Chief of Dan's household, with Nan commandery administrator and directing military and civil affairs as before.

entries.zh: 在州累政，甚有治績，平心決斷，請託不行。
entries.en: Over several tours of duty he governed with real success, judging fairly and refusing every private request.
entries.literal: Through several terms in the province he had very good administrative achievements—deciding cases with an even hand, petitions and entreaties gaining no effect.

entries.zh: 高祖深嘉之。
entries.en: Gaozu praised him warmly for it.
entries.literal: The Emperor deeply commended this.

entries.zh: 除通直散騎常侍，領羽林監，轉秘書監，遷明威將軍，復爲晉安王府長史、南蘭陵太守，別敕專行南徐州事。
entries.en: He became Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and head of the Feathered Forest Guard, then Director of the Secretariat and Bright Might General, again chief secretary to Prince of Jin'an and administrator of South Lanling, with a special commission for South Xu alone.
entries.literal: Appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, overseeing the Feathered Forest Guard, transferred to Director of the Secretariat, promoted to Bright Might General, again Chief of Jin'an's household and Administrator of South Lanling—separate edict put him solely in charge of South Xu affairs.

entries.zh: 休源累佐名籓，甚得民譽，王深相倚仗，軍民機務，動止詢謀。
entries.en: Having served several great princely domains, he enjoyed wide public esteem; the prince leaned on him heavily, consulting him on every military and civil decision.
entries.literal: Xiuyuan had repeatedly assisted famous fiefs, winning great popular repute; the prince deeply relied on him—military and civilian urgent business, every move and halt consulted his counsel.

entries.zh: 常於中齋別施一榻，云「此是孔長史坐」，人莫得預焉。
entries.en: In the inner study he kept a couch set apart, saying, "This seat is for Chief Secretary Kong," and no one else was allowed to sit there.
entries.literal: He often set aside a separate couch in the central study, saying "This is Chief Kong's seat"—no one else might use it.

entries.zh: 其見敬如此。
entries.en: That was the measure of the honor he received.
entries.literal: Such was the respect shown him.

entries.zh: 昭明太子薨，有敕夜召休源入宴居殿，與羣公參定謀議，立晉安王綱爲皇太子。
entries.en: After Crown Prince Zhaoming's death, an edict called Xiuyuan to the palace at night to join the assembled ministers in choosing Prince of Jin'an Gang as heir.
entries.literal: When Crown Prince Zhaoming died, an edict summoned Xiuyuan at night to the dwelling hall for deliberation with the assembled lords on establishing Prince of Jin'an Gang as crown prince.

entries.zh: 四年，遘疾，高祖遣中使候問，並給醫藥，日有十數。
entries.en: In year 4 he fell ill; Gaozu sent palace messengers to inquire after him and sent medicine ten or more times a day.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he fell ill; the Emperor sent palace envoys to inquire and provided medicine—ten or more each day.

entries.zh: 其年五月，卒，時年六十四。
entries.en: He died in the fifth month of that year, at sixty-four.
entries.literal: That year in the fifth month he died, aged sixty-four.

entries.zh: 遺令薄葬，節朔薦蔬菲而已。
entries.en: He left orders for a plain funeral and only modest vegetable offerings at the seasonal rites.
entries.literal: His final instructions: simple burial, only vegetables at the seasonal sacrifices.

entries.zh: 高祖爲之流涕，顧謂謝舉曰：「孔休源奉職清忠，當官正直，方欲共康治道，以隆王化。
entries.en: Gaozu wept and, turning to Xie Ju, said: "Kong Xiuyuan served with pure loyalty and upright integrity. I had hoped to build good government with him and elevate the kingly way.
entries.literal: The Emperor wept for him and, turning to Xie Ju, said: "Kong Xiuyuan served his office with pure loyalty, upright as an official; I had hoped to jointly bring about good government and elevate kingly transformation.

entries.zh: 奄至殞歿，朕甚痛之。」
entries.en: Suddenly he is gone, and I grieve deeply."
entries.literal: Suddenly he is cut off—I grieve deeply."

entries.zh: 舉曰：「此人清介強直，當今罕有，微臣竊爲陛下惜之。」
entries.en: Ju replied: "He was incorruptible and resolute—a man rarely seen today. Your servant grieves for Your Majesty's loss."
entries.literal: Ju said: "This man was pure and upright, strong and straight—rare today; your humble servant privately mourns him for Your Majesty."

entries.zh: 詔曰：「慎終追遠，歷代通規；
entries.en: An edict ran: "To honor the dead and remember the distant is the custom of every age;
entries.literal: An edict proclaimed: "Care in death and remembrance of the distant—the common rule of all dynasties;

entries.zh: 褒德疇庸，先王令典。
entries.en: to praise virtue and reward service is the ancient kings' true law.
entries.literal: honoring virtue and rewarding merit—the worthy precedent of ancient kings.

entries.zh: 宣惠將軍、金紫光祿大夫、監揚州孔休源，風業貞正，雅量沖邈，升榮建禮，譽重搢紳。
entries.en: Propagation and Grace General, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Supervisor of Yangzhou Kong Xiuyuan was upright in character, broad in spirit, honored at the Hall of Establishing Rites, and esteemed among officials.
entries.literal: Propagation and Grace General, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Supervisor of Yangzhou Kong Xiuyuan—his conduct and learning were upright and true, his generous measure serene and far-reaching; rising in honor at the Hall of Establishing Rites, his reputation weighed heavy among the gentry.

entries.zh: 理務神州，化覃歌詠，方興仁壽，穆是髂倫。
entries.en: He governed the central realm, won the people's praise in song, and was on the verge of bringing humane rule and moral order to fruition.
entries.literal: He managed affairs in the heartland; his transforming influence spread to songs of praise; he was just raising benevolent longevity and harmonizing the moral order.

entries.zh: 奄然永逝，倍用悲惻。
entries.en: Now he is gone forever, and our sorrow is doubled.
entries.literal: Suddenly he passed forever—doubly we use grief and sorrow.

entries.zh: 可贈散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫，賻第一材一具，布五十匹，錢五萬，蠟二百斤。
entries.en: Let him be posthumously made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, with one first-grade coffin, fifty bolts of cloth, fifty thousand cash, and two hundred jin of wax.
entries.literal: He may be posthumously granted Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; funeral gifts of one first-grade coffin set, fifty bolts of cloth, fifty thousand cash, and two hundred jin of wax.

entries.zh: 剋日舉哀。
entries.en: Mourning rites shall be held on the appointed day.
entries.literal: Mourning shall be observed on the appointed day.

entries.zh: 喪事所須，隨由資給。
entries.en: All funeral expenses shall be provided as required.
entries.literal: Whatever the funeral requires shall be supplied as needed.

entries.zh: 諡曰貞子。」
entries.en: Posthumous title: Viscount Zhen."
entries.literal: Posthumous title: Viscount of Integrity."

entries.zh: 皇太子手令曰：「金紫光祿大夫孔休源，立身中正，行己清恪。
entries.en: The crown prince wrote: "Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon Kong Xiuyuan was upright in bearing and pure in conduct.
entries.literal: The crown prince's handwritten order said: "Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon Kong Xiuyuan stood upright in person and conducted himself with pure integrity.

entries.zh: 昔歲西浮渚宮，東泊枌壤，毘佐蕃政，實盡厥誠。
entries.en: In recent years he served princes west at Zhugong and east on the Fen borderlands, giving his whole loyalty to their rule.
entries.literal: In past years he served west at Zhugong Palace and east on the Fen frontier, assisting in princely governance with full sincerity.

entries.zh: 安國之詳審，公儀之廉白，無以過之。
entries.en: His careful judgment in governing a realm and his spotless integrity surpass all comparison.
entries.literal: The careful steadiness of one who steadies a state, the clean whiteness of one who balances the scales—none surpass him.

entries.zh: 奄至殞喪，情用惻怛。
entries.en: His sudden death fills me with sorrow.
entries.literal: Suddenly he is cut off in death—my feelings are deeply pained.

entries.zh: 今須舉哀，外可備禮。」
entries.en: Mourning must now be observed; let the proper ceremonies be arranged."
entries.literal: Now mourning must be observed; outwardly let the full rites be prepared."

entries.zh: 徵爲太府卿，俄授都官尚書，頃之，領太子中庶子。
entries.en: He was summoned as Chamberlain of the Imperial Treasury, soon appointed Minister of Justice, and before long concurrently served as Household Attendant to the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: He was summoned as Chamberlain of the Imperial Treasury, soon appointed Minister of Justice, and before long concurrently served as Household Attendant to the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 普通七年，揚州刺史臨川王宏薨，高祖與羣臣議代王居州任者久之，于時貴戚王公，咸望遷授，高祖曰：「朕已得人。
entries.en: In Putong 7, when Hong, Prince of Linchuan and Inspector of Yangzhou, died, Gaozu discussed with his ministers for a long time who should replace the prince in the provincial post. At the time noble relatives and princes all hoped to receive the transfer, but Gaozu said, "I have already found the man.
entries.literal: In Putong 7, when Hong, Prince of Linchuan and Inspector of Yangzhou, died, Gaozu discussed with his ministers for a long time who should replace the prince in the provincial post. At the time noble relatives and princes all hoped to receive the transfer, but Gaozu said, "I have already found the man.

entries.zh: 孔休源才識通敏，實應此選。」
entries.en: Kong Xiuyuan is quick in talent and judgment, and truly suits this selection."
entries.literal: Kong Xiuyuan is quick in talent and judgment, and truly suits this selection."

entries.zh: 乃授宣惠將軍、監揚州。
entries.en: He then appointed him Xuanhui General and supervisor of Yangzhou.
entries.literal: He then appointed him Xuanhui General and supervisor of Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 休源初爲臨川王行佐，及王薨而管州任，時論榮之。
entries.en: Xiuyuan had first served as administrative aide to the Prince of Linchuan; when the prince died and Xiuyuan took charge of the province, opinion at the time considered it an honor.
entries.literal: Xiuyuan had first served as administrative aide to the Prince of Linchuan; when the prince died and Xiuyuan took charge of the province, opinion at the time considered it an honor.

entries.zh: 而神州都會，簿領殷繁，休源割斷如流，傍無私謁。
entries.en: Yet the divine province was the capital region, and its documents and cases were heavy and complex; Xiuyuan made decisions as smoothly as flowing water and allowed no private petitions from the side.
entries.literal: Yet the divine province was the capital region, and its documents and cases were heavy and complex; Xiuyuan made decisions as smoothly as flowing water and allowed no private petitions from the side.

entries.zh: 中大通二年，加授金紫光祿大夫，監揚州如故。
entries.en: In Zhongdatong 2, he was additionally appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, while continuing as supervisor of Yangzhou.
entries.literal: In Zhongdatong 2, he was additionally appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, while continuing as supervisor of Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 累表陳讓，優詔不許。
entries.en: He repeatedly submitted memorials declining, but gracious edicts did not permit it.
entries.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials declining, but gracious edicts did not permit it.

entries.zh: 在州晝決辭訟，夜覽墳籍。
entries.en: While in the province, by day he judged pleadings and lawsuits, and by night he read the ancient texts.
entries.literal: While in the province, by day he judged pleadings and lawsuits, and by night he read the ancient texts.

entries.zh: 每車駕巡幸，常以軍國事委之。
entries.en: Whenever the imperial carriage went on tour, the emperor regularly entrusted him with military and state affairs.
entries.literal: Whenever the imperial carriage went on tour, the emperor regularly entrusted him with military and state affairs.

entries.zh: 除少府卿，出爲貞威將軍、北中郎南康王長史、廣陵太守，改授鎮北豫章王長史，將軍、太守如故。
entries.en: Appointed Minister of the Lesser Treasury, he went out as General of Loyal Might, chief clerk to Prince Nankang of North Central Command and administrator of Guangling, then was reassigned chief clerk to Prince Zhenbei of Yuzhang while keeping the same generalship and magistracy.
entries.literal: He was appointed Minister of the Lesser Treasury, went out as General of Loyal Might, Chief Clerk to Prince Nankang of North Central Command and Administrator of Guangling, then reassigned as Chief Clerk to Prince Zhenbei of Yuzhang; his generalship and administrator's post were unchanged.

entries.zh: 時魏徐州刺史元法僧降附，革被敕隨府王鎮彭城。
entries.en: When Yuan Faseng, Wei governor of Xuzhou, surrendered, Ge was ordered to follow the prince and garrison Pengcheng.
entries.literal: When Wei Governor of Xuzhou Yuan Faseng surrendered and submitted, Ge was ordered to follow the princely household to garrison Pengcheng.

entries.zh: 城旣失守，革素不便馬，乃泛舟而還，途經下邳，遂爲魏人所執。
entries.en: The city fell. Ge had never ridden well; he took to the river instead, and at Xiapi Wei soldiers seized him.
entries.literal: When the city fell, Ge had never been comfortable on horseback; he took boat instead, and passing through Xiapi was seized by Wei men.

entries.zh: 魏徐州刺史元延明聞革才名，厚加接待。
entries.en: Yuan Yanming, Wei governor of Xuzhou, had heard of Ge's fame and received him with deep respect.
entries.literal: Wei Governor of Xuzhou Yuan Yanming, hearing of Ge's literary reputation, treated him with great honor.

entries.zh: 革稱患腳不拜，延明將加害焉，見革辭色嚴正，更相敬重。
entries.en: Ge claimed a bad leg and refused to bow. Yanming meant to punish him, but Ge's stern bearing in word and face won respect instead.
entries.literal: Ge pleaded a lame leg and would not bow; Yanming was about to harm him, but seeing Ge's stern dignity in speech and bearing, treated him with renewed respect.

entries.zh: 時祖𣈶同被拘執，延明使𣈶作《欹器》、《漏刻銘》，革罵𣈶曰：「卿荷國厚恩，已無報答，今乃爲虜立銘，孤負朝廷。」
entries.en: Zu Can was held with him. Yanming had Can write inscriptions for the Tilting Vessel and the Clepsydra. Ge reviled him: "The state heaped grace on you and you never repaid it. Now you write for the captors and betray the court."
entries.literal: At the time Zu Can was also detained; Yanming had Can compose inscriptions for the Tilting Vessel and the Clepsydra. Ge cursed Can: "You received the state's deep grace yet have no repayment; now you write inscriptions for the enemy—betraying the court."

entries.zh: 延明聞之，乃令革作丈八寺碑並祭彭祖文，革辭以囚執旣久，無復心思。
entries.en: Yanming then ordered Ge to compose the Zhangba Temple stele and a sacrifice to Peng Zu. Ge refused: long imprisonment had drained his mind.
entries.literal: Yanming heard and ordered Ge to write the Zhangba Temple stele and a text sacrificing to Peng Zu; Ge refused, saying long captivity had left him no heart for such work.

entries.zh: 延明逼之逾苦，將加箠撲。
entries.en: Yanming pressed harder and was about to have him flogged.
entries.literal: Yanming pressed him harder and would have had him beaten.

entries.zh: 革厲色而言曰：「江革行年六十，不能殺身報主，今日得死爲幸，誓不爲人執筆。」
entries.en: Ge said, face hard: "Jiang Ge is sixty. I could not die for my lord; to die today would be luck. I swear I will never take up the brush for another man."
entries.literal: Ge said with stern countenance: "Jiang Ge is sixty years old; unable to give his life for his lord, today to die would be fortune—I swear never to write at another's command."

entries.zh: 延明知不可屈，乃止。
entries.en: Yanming saw he could not be bent and desisted.
entries.literal: Yanming knew he could not be broken and stopped.

entries.zh: 日給脫粟三升，僅餘性命。
entries.en: Each day he received three sheng of husked millet—just enough to stay alive.
entries.literal: Each day they gave him three sheng of husked millet—barely enough to keep life.

entries.zh: 值魏主討中山王元略反北，乃放革及祖𣈶還朝。
entries.en: When the Wei ruler marched north against Prince Zhongshan Yuan Lue's rebellion, Ge and Zu Can were freed and sent home to court.
entries.literal: It happened the Wei ruler marched north to suppress Prince Zhongshan Yuan Lue's rebellion; Ge and Zu Can were released and sent back to court.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「前貞威將軍、鎮北長史、廣陵太守江革，才思通贍，出內有聞，在朝正色，臨危不撓，首佐台鉉，實允僉諧。
entries.en: An edict ran: "Jiang Ge, former General of Loyal Might, chief clerk of Zhenbei, and administrator of Guangling—gifted in mind and word, known in court and out, upright in office, unbroken in danger, chief aide to the Three Dukes—fully worthy of trust.
entries.literal: An edict said: "Former General of Loyal Might, Chief Clerk of Zhenbei, and Administrator of Guangling Jiang Ge—talented in thought and expression, known inside and outside court, upright in office, unmoved in peril, chief aide to the Three Dukes—all agreed he was fit.

entries.zh: 可太尉臨川王長史。」
entries.en: Let him be chief clerk to the Grand Marshal, Prince Linchuan."
entries.literal: Appoint him Chief Clerk to the Grand Marshal, Prince Linchuan."

entries.zh: 時高祖盛於佛教，朝賢多啓求受戒，革精信因果，而高祖未知，謂革不奉佛教，乃賜革《覺意詩》五百字，云「惟當勤精進，自強行勝脩；
entries.en: Gaozu was then deep in Buddhism; court worthies often asked to take vows. Ge truly believed in karma, but Gaozu did not know and thought he rejected the faith. He gave Ge a five-hundred-character "Awakened Intent Poem," saying, "Only diligence and self-strengthening beat empty practice;
entries.literal: Gaozu was then zealous for Buddhism; court worthies often petitioned to receive ordination. Ge faithfully believed in karma, but Gaozu did not know and thought Ge did not embrace Buddhism; he bestowed on Ge a five-hundred-character "Awakened Intent Poem," saying "Only diligent effort and self-strengthening surpass cultivation;

entries.zh: 豈可作底突，如彼必死囚。
entries.en: Who would be a stubborn bump, like a man already condemned to die?
entries.literal: How can one be a stubborn bump, like those condemned prisoners?

entries.zh: 以此告江革，並及諸貴遊。」
entries.en: Tell this to Jiang Ge, and to the other noble travelers as well."
entries.literal: Let this be told to Jiang Ge, and also to the other noble travelers."

entries.zh: 又手敕云：「世間果報，不可不信，豈得底突如對元延明邪？」
entries.en: A handwritten edict added: "Worldly retribution is real. How can you be a stubborn bump with Yuan Yanming as you were before?"
entries.literal: Also a handwritten edict: "Worldly retribution cannot be disbelieved—how can one be a stubborn bump as before Yuan Yanming?"

entries.zh: 革因啓乞受菩薩戒。
entries.en: Ge then memorialized asking to receive the bodhisattva precepts.
entries.literal: Ge thereupon memorialized requesting to receive the bodhisattva precepts.

entries.zh: 重除少府卿、長史、校尉。
entries.en: He was again made Minister of the Lesser Treasury, chief clerk, and colonel commandant.
entries.literal: Again appointed Minister of the Lesser Treasury, Chief Clerk, and Colonel Commandant.

entries.zh: 時武陵王在東州，頗自驕縱，上召革面敕曰：「武陵王年少，臧盾性弱，不能匡正，欲以卿代爲行事。
entries.en: Prince Wuling held East Yangzhou and had grown proud and loose. The emperor summoned Ge and charged him in person: "Prince Wuling is young. Zang Dun is mild and cannot correct him. I want you to replace him as acting administrator.
entries.literal: Prince Wuling was in East Yangzhou and rather arrogant and unrestrained; the Emperor summoned Ge and personally charged him: "Prince Wuling is young; Zang Dun is timid by nature and cannot correct him—I wish to have you replace him as acting administrator.

entries.zh: 非卿不可，不得有辭。」
entries.en: No one but you will do. You may not refuse."
entries.literal: No one but you will do; you may not refuse."

entries.zh: 乃除折沖將軍、東中郎武陵王長史、會稽郡丞、行府州事。
entries.en: He was made General Who Breaks the Charge, chief clerk to Prince Wuling of East Central Command, assistant administrator of Kuaiji, and acting head of prefectural and commandery affairs.
entries.literal: Appointed General Who Breaks the Charge, Chief Clerk to Prince Wuling of East Central Command, Assistant Administrator of Kuaiji, overseeing prefectural and commandery affairs.

entries.zh: 革門生故吏，家多在東州，聞革應至，並齎持緣道迎候。
entries.en: Many of Ge's former students and subordinates lived in East Yangzhou. Hearing he was coming, they lined the road with gifts to welcome him.
entries.literal: Ge's former students and subordinates, many with homes in East Yangzhou, hearing Ge was coming, all brought gifts along the road to welcome him.

entries.zh: 革曰：「我通不受餉，不容獨當故人筐篚。」
entries.en: Ge said, "I never take gifts. I cannot be the only one to fill my old friends' baskets and boxes."
entries.literal: Ge said: "I have never accepted gifts—I cannot alone take my old friends' baskets and boxes."

entries.zh: 至鎮，惟資公俸，食不兼味。
entries.en: At his post he lived only on official salary and never ate more than one dish at a meal.
entries.literal: On reaching his post he relied only on official salary; his meals had no second dish.

entries.zh: 郡境殷廣，辭訟日數百，革分判辨析，曾無疑滯。
entries.en: The commandery was broad and crowded; lawsuits came by the hundred each day. Ge divided and decided them without a moment's hesitation.
entries.literal: The commandery was vast and populous; lawsuits ran to hundreds per day—Ge divided and judged them, never once stalling in doubt.

entries.zh: 功必賞，過必罰，民安吏畏，百城震恐。
entries.en: Merit was always rewarded and fault always punished. The people rested easy, officials feared him, and every city shook.
entries.literal: Merit always rewarded, fault always punished; the people were at peace, officials feared him, and every city trembled.

entries.zh: 琅邪王騫爲山陰令，贓貨狼藉，望風自解。
entries.en: Wang Qian of Langye, magistrate of Shanyin, was awash in bribes. At Ge's coming he resigned before the wind.
entries.literal: Wang Qian of Langye was magistrate of Shanyin—his bribery was flagrant; at Ge's approach he resigned of his own accord.

entries.zh: 府王憚之，遂雅相欽重。
entries.en: The prince feared him and thereafter held him in deep respect.
entries.literal: The princely household feared him and thereafter held him in deep esteem.

entries.zh: 每至侍宴，言論必以《詩》《書》，王因此耽學好文。
entries.en: At every banquet his talk turned to the Odes and Documents, and the prince came to love learning and letters.
entries.literal: Whenever he attended banquets, his talk always drew on the Odes and Documents; the Prince therefore devoted himself to study and letters.

entries.zh: 典簽沈熾文以王所制詩呈高祖，高祖謂僕射徐勉曰：「江革果能稱職。」
entries.en: Chief of staff Shen Chiwen showed the prince's poems to Gaozu. Gaozu told Vice Director Xu Mian, "Jiang Ge has truly done his duty."
entries.literal: Chief of Staff Shen Chiwen presented the Prince's poems to Gaozu; Gaozu said to Vice Director Xu Mian: "Jiang Ge has indeed proved equal to his charge."

entries.zh: 乃除都官尚書。
entries.en: He was made Minister of Justice.
entries.literal: Appointed Minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 將還，民皆戀惜之，贈遺無所受。
entries.en: When he was about to leave, the people clung to him with grief. He took no parting gifts.
entries.literal: When he was about to leave, the people all cherished him and wished to keep him—he accepted no parting gifts.

entries.zh: 送故依舊訂舫，革並不納，惟乘臺所給一舸。
entries.en: Escorts arranged a boat as always. Ge refused it and took only the single vessel the office gave him.
