entries.literal: Kan then led thirty thousand picked troops to strike him, could not overcome him, and still built more than ten walled camps to hold him.

entries.zh: 朝廷賞授，一與元法僧同。
entries.en: Liang treated him with the same honors it had given Yuan Faseng.
entries.literal: The court’s rewards and appointments were the same as for Yuan Faseng.

entries.zh: 遣羊鴉仁、王弁率軍應接，李元履運給糧仗。
entries.en: Yang Yaren and Wang Bian marched to his aid while Li Yuanlü ran supplies.
entries.literal: Yang Yaren and Wang Bian led armies to support him; Li Yuanlü transported grain and weapons.

entries.zh: 魏帝聞之，使授侃驃騎大將軍、司徒、泰山郡公，長爲兗州刺史，侃斬其使者以徇。
entries.en: Wei tried to buy him with General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry, Minister of Works, Duke of Taishan, and permanent Yanzhou inspector; Kan killed the envoy and exposed the head.
entries.literal: When the Wei emperor heard of it, he sent orders appointing Kan General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry, Minister of Works, Duke of Taishan commandery, and long-term Inspector of Yanzhou; Kan beheaded the envoy and displayed the head.

entries.zh: 魏人大駭，令僕射于暉率衆數十萬，及高歡、尒朱陽都等相繼而至，圍侃十餘重，傷殺甚衆。
entries.en: Wei sent Yu Hui with hundreds of thousands, then Gao Huan and Erzhu Yangdu in waves, wrapping Kan in layer after layer of siege and slaughter.
entries.literal: The Wei were greatly alarmed and sent Vice Director of the Secretariat Yu Hui at the head of several hundred thousand men, while Gao Huan, Erzhu Yangdu, and others came in succession, surrounding Kan in more than a dozen rings and inflicting heavy casualties.

entries.zh: 柵中矢盡，南軍不進，乃夜潰圍而出，且戰且行，一日一夜乃出魏境。
entries.en: When arrows failed and southern relief stalled, he burst out at night, fighting nonstop for a day and a night before he crossed the border.
entries.literal: Arrows in the stockade ran out and the southern armies did not advance; he then broke out by night, fighting as he went, and only after a day and a night did he leave Wei territory.

entries.zh: 至渣口，衆尚萬餘人，馬二千匹，將入南，士卒並竟夜悲歌。
entries.en: At Zhakou ten thousand men and two thousand horses remained; on the eve of crossing south, his troops keened through the night.
entries.literal: At Zhakou he still had more than ten thousand men and two thousand horses; about to enter the south, the soldiers all sang laments through the night.

entries.zh: 侃乃謝曰：「卿等懷土，理不能見隨，幸適去留，於此別異。」
entries.en: Kan told them, “You long for home and need not follow me—stay or go; this is where we divide.”
entries.literal: Kan then said in farewell: “You cherish your homeland and cannot rightly follow me; go or stay as you please—here we part.”

entries.zh: 因各拜辭而去。
entries.en: Each man bowed farewell and went his way.
entries.literal: Thereupon each bowed in leave and departed.

entries.zh: 侃以大通三年至京師，詔授使持節、散騎常侍、都督瑕丘征討諸軍事、安北將軍、徐州刺史，并其兄默及三弟忱、給、元，皆拜爲刺史。
entries.en: He entered the capital in Datong year 3 with staff authority, Regular Attendant, Xiqiu campaign commander, General Who Pacifies the North, and Xuzhou inspector—and his brother Mo and brothers Chen, Ji, and Yuan were all made inspectors too.
entries.literal: Kan reached the capital in the third year of Datong; an edict appointed him Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, Area Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs for the Xiqiu Campaign, General Who Pacifies the North, and Inspector of Xuzhou, and his elder brother Mo and three younger brothers Chen, Ji, and Yuan were all appointed inspectors.

entries.zh: 尋以侃爲都督北討諸軍事，出頓日城，會陳慶之失律，停進。
entries.en: He was soon named northern expedition commander and took post at Richeng, but Chen Qingzhi’s breach of orders stopped the march.
entries.literal: Soon Kan was made Area Commander-in-Chief of all Northern Expedition forces, encamped at Richeng; when Chen Qingzhi lost discipline, the advance halted.

entries.zh: 其年，詔以爲持節、雲麾將軍、青、冀二州刺史。
entries.en: The same year brought staff authority, General of the Cloud Banner, and the Qing-Ji inspectorate.
entries.literal: That year an edict appointed him Bearer of the Staff, General of the Cloud Banner, and Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces.

entries.zh: 羊侃字祖忻，泰山梁甫人，漢南陽太守續之裔也。
entries.en: Yang Kan, styled Zuxin, of Liangfu in Taishan, traced his line to Han’s Yang Xu, grand administrator of Nanyang.
entries.literal: Yang Kan, courtesy name Zuxin, was a native of Liangfu in Taishan, a descendant of Yang Xu, Grand Administrator of Nanyang in Han.

entries.zh: 祖規，宋武帝之臨徐州，辟祭酒從事、大中正。
entries.en: His grandfather Gui was recruited as Libationer-Attendant and Grand Rectifier when the future Emperor Wu of Song governed Xuzhou.
entries.literal: His grandfather Gui, when the future Emperor Wu of Song governed Xuzhou, was recruited as Libationer-Attendant and Grand Rectifier.

entries.zh: 會薛安都舉彭城降北，規由是陷魏，魏授衛將軍、營州刺史。
entries.en: Xue Andu’s surrender of Pengcheng to Northern Wei left Gui on the wrong side of the line; Wei made him General of the Guard and Yingzhou inspector.
entries.literal: When Xue Andu raised Pengcheng and went over to the north, Gui was thereby trapped in Wei; Wei appointed him General of the Guard and Inspector of Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 父祉，魏侍中，金紫光祿大夫。
entries.en: His father Zhi held Wei’s Palace Attendant and golden Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
entries.literal: His father Zhi was Palace Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Ornament in Wei.

entries.zh: 侃少而瑰偉，身長七尺八寸，雅愛文史，博涉書記，尤好《左氏春秋》及《孫吳兵法》。
entries.en: Even young he was imposing, seven feet eight inches tall; he loved literature and history, read widely, and especially favored the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals and the military methods of Sun and Wu.
entries.literal: Kan from youth was magnificent in bearing, seven feet eight inches in height, fond of letters by nature, broadly versed in records and documents, and especially loved the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn and the Art of War of Sun and Wu.

entries.zh: 弱冠隨父在梁州立功。
entries.en: At twenty he campaigned with his father in Liangzhou and earned distinction.
entries.literal: At twenty he followed his father in Liangzhou and won merit.

entries.zh: 魏正光中，稍爲別將。
entries.en: Under Wei’s Zhengguang era he rose to independent command.
entries.literal: In Zhengguang of Wei he gradually became a separate commander.

entries.zh: 時秦州羌有莫遮念生者，據州反，稱帝，仍遣其弟天生率衆攻陷岐州，遂寇雍州。
entries.en: Qinzhou’s Qiang leader Mo Zhaoniansheng rebelled, crowned himself, and sent his brother Tiansheng to seize Qi Province and raid Yong.
entries.literal: At that time among the Qiang of Qinzhou, Mo Zhaoniansheng held the province in revolt, declared himself emperor, and still sent his younger brother Tiansheng at the head of the host to take Qi Province and then raid Yong Province.

entries.zh: 侃爲偏將，隸蕭寶夤往討之，潛身巡緌，伺射天生，應弦卽倒，其衆遂潰。
entries.en: Serving under Xiao Baoyin, Kan stole along the front, drew on Tiansheng, and dropped him with one arrow; the rebels broke.
entries.literal: Kan was a subordinate general under Xiao Baoyin on the punitive expedition; he went in secret along the line of battle, watched for a shot at Tiansheng, and when the arrow flew Tiansheng fell at once and the host collapsed.

entries.zh: 以功遷使持節、征東大將軍、東道行臺，領泰山太守，進爵鉅平侯。
entries.en: The victory won him staff authority, General Who Campaigns East, eastern commissioner, Taishan administrator, and the marquisate of Juping.
entries.literal: For merit he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, General Who Campaigns East, Eastern Expedition Commissioner, concurrent Grand Administrator of Taishan, and advanced in rank to Marquis of Juping.

entries.zh: 梁書卷第三十九 列傳第三十三
entries.en: Book of Liang, Volume 39, Biography 33
entries.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 39, Biography 33

entries.zh: 顯幼而聰敏，當世號曰神童。
entries.en: Xian was bright from childhood; men of his day called him a prodigy.
entries.literal: Xian was clever from childhood; his contemporaries called him a divine child.

entries.zh: 天監初，舉秀才，解褐中軍臨川王行參軍，俄署法曹。
entries.en: When Tianjian opened he was presented as a cultivated talent, entered service as staff officer to the Prince of Linchuan in the Central Army, and soon headed the law bureau.
entries.literal: At the opening of Tianjian he was recommended as a cultivated talent, relieved his clerk’s collar as Administrative Officer on the staff of the Prince of Linchuan in the Central Army, and soon served as Chief of the Law Bureau.

entries.zh: 顯好學，博涉多參通，任昉嘗得一篇缺簡書，文字零落，歷示諸人，莫能識者，顯云是《古文尚書》所刪逸篇，昉檢《周書》，果如其說，昉因大相賞異。
entries.en: Xian loved study and ranged across many disciplines; once Ren Fang had a bamboo slip with characters broken and faded, showed it around, and no one could read it—Xian said it was a lost passage cut from the Old Text Documents; Fang checked the Documents of Zhou and found it exact, and from then held him in wonder.
entries.literal: Xian loved learning and ranged widely in many fields; once Ren Fang obtained a fragmentary bamboo text with characters scattered and eroded, showed it to everyone, and none could read it—Xian said it was a lost passage deleted from the Old Text Documents, and when Fang checked the Documents of Zhou it matched exactly; Fang was thereafter greatly struck by him.

entries.zh: 丁母憂，服闋，尚書令沈約命駕造焉，於坐策顯經史十事，顯對其九。
entries.en: After his mother’s mourning, the Director of the Department of State Affairs Shen Yue came by carriage to call on him and, seated, examined him on ten points of canon and history—Xian answered nine.
entries.literal: When his mother’s mourning ended, the Director of the Department of State Affairs Shen Yue came in his carriage to visit, and at the seat tested Xian on ten matters from the classics and histories—Xian answered nine.

entries.zh: 約曰：「老夫昏忘，不可受策；
entries.en: Yue said, “This old man is dim and forgetful; I cannot sit for your test—
entries.literal: Yue said: “This old man is muddled and forgetful; I cannot submit to examination—

entries.zh: 雖然，聊試數事，不可至十也。」
entries.en: Still, try me on a few—you must not make it ten.”
entries.literal: Even so, let me try a few things—you must not reach ten.”

entries.zh: 顯問其五，約對其二。
entries.en: Xian put five questions to him; Yue answered two.
entries.literal: Xian questioned him on five; Yue answered two.

entries.zh: 陸倕聞之歎曰：「劉郎可謂差人，雖吾家平原詣張壯武，王粲謁伯喈，必無此對。」
entries.en: Lu Chui heard and sighed, “Master Liu is a man apart—even when our Lu Ji sought out Zhang Hua, or Wang Can called on Cai Yong, there was never such an exchange.”
entries.literal: Lu Chui heard of it and sighed: “One may say Master Liu is a man apart—even when our house’s Lu Ji called on Zhang Hua, or when Wang Can visited Cai Yong, there could not have been such parry and riposte.”

entries.zh: 其爲名流推賞如此。
entries.en: So the leading men of the age honored him.
entries.literal: Such was the esteem in which leading minds held him.

entries.zh: 及約爲太子少傅，乃引爲五官掾，俄兼廷尉正。
entries.en: When Yue became mentor to the heir apparent, he drew Xian in as aide in the Five Offices; soon Xian also served as director under the Court of Judicial Review.
entries.literal: When Yue became Mentor to the Heir Apparent, he brought Xian in as Aide in the Five Offices, and soon he also served as Director under the Court of Judicial Review.

entries.zh: 五兵尚書傅昭掌著作，撰國史，引顯爲佐。
entries.en: Fu Zhao, Minister of the Five Armies and overseer of historiography, was compiling the national history and took Xian as his assistant.
entries.literal: Fu Zhao, Minister of the Five Armies and in charge of historiography, was compiling the national history and brought Xian in as assistant.

entries.zh: 九年，始革尚書五都選，顯以本官兼吏部郎，又除司空臨川王外兵參軍，遷尚書儀曹郎。
entries.en: In year nine the five selection directorates were first reformed; Xian kept his post while also serving as director in the Ministry of Personnel, was made external military officer to the Minister of Works, the Prince of Linchuan, and then Gentleman of the Ceremonial Bureau.
entries.literal: In year nine the Ministry system was first reformed for the five directorates of selection; Xian in his existing post also served as Director in the Ministry of Personnel, was further appointed External Military Officer to the Minister of Works, the Prince of Linchuan, and was transferred to Gentleman of the Ceremonial Bureau.

entries.zh: 嘗爲《上朝詩》，沈約見而美之，時約郊居宅新成，因命工書人題之於壁。
entries.en: He once wrote a poem on the morning audience; Shen Yue admired it, and when Yue’s suburban house was newly finished he had a scribe brush it on the wall.
entries.literal: Once he composed a poem on morning audience; Shen Yue read it with admiration, and at the time Yue’s suburban residence was newly built—he had a scribe paint it on the wall.

entries.zh: 出爲臨川王記室參軍。
entries.en: He left the capital as recorder to the Prince of Linchuan.
entries.literal: He went out as Recorder on the staff of the Prince of Linchuan.

entries.zh: 建康平，復入爲尚書儀曹侍郎，兼中書通事舍人。
entries.en: After Jiankang was pacified he returned as vice director of ceremonial affairs and again Master of Documents for Palace Affairs.
entries.literal: When Jiankang was pacified he returned as Vice Director of Ceremonial Affairs in the Ministry of Rites and concurrently Master of Documents for Palace Affairs.

entries.zh: 出爲秣陵令，又除驃騎鄱陽王記室，兼中書舍人，累遷步兵校尉、中書侍郎，舍人如故。
entries.en: He served as magistrate of Moling, then recorder to the Prince of Poyang, Cavalry General, again Master of Documents, and rose to Commandant of Footsoldiers and Secretariat gentleman, keeping the palace post throughout.
entries.literal: He went out as Magistrate of Moling, was again made Recorder to the Prince of Poyang, Cavalry General, with concurrent service as Master of Documents, and was promoted in succession to Commandant of Footsoldiers and Gentleman of the Secretariat, still Master of Documents.

entries.zh: 顯有三子：莠，荏，臻。
entries.en: Xian had three sons—You, Ren, and Zhen.
entries.literal: Xian had three sons: You, Ren, and Zhen.

entries.zh: 臻早著名。
entries.en: Zhen was famed from early on.
entries.literal: Zhen early won renown.

entries.zh: 梁書卷第四十 列傳第三十四
entries.en: Book of Liang, Volume 40, Biography 34
entries.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 40, Biography 34

entries.zh: 孺幼聰敏，七歲能屬文。
entries.en: Ru was bright and sharp as a boy; at seven he could already write.
entries.literal: Ru was clever and keen from childhood; at seven he could compose prose.

entries.zh: 年十四，居父喪，毀瘠骨立，宗黨咸異之。
entries.en: At fourteen he mourned his father until he was skin and bone; kinsmen and neighbors were astonished.
entries.literal: At fourteen, while mourning his father, he wasted away until only bone remained, and all his kin marveled at him.

entries.zh: 服闋，叔父瑱爲義興郡，攜以之官，常置坐側，謂賓客曰：「此兒吾家之明珠也。」
entries.en: When mourning ended his uncle Zhen governed Yixing and brought him along, keeping him always at his side, and said to guests, "This child is the pearl of our clan."
entries.literal: When mourning ended his uncle Zhen was interior minister of Yixing and took him to his post, always seating him at his side, and told guests: "This boy is the pearl of our house."

entries.zh: 旣長，美風采，性通和，雖家人不見其喜慍。
entries.en: Grown handsome in bearing and even-tempered, even his own household never caught him in joy or anger.
entries.literal: When grown he was handsome in bearing, open and harmonious by nature, and even at home none saw him show pleasure or anger.

entries.zh: 本州召迎主簿。
entries.en: His home province called him to be registrar.
entries.literal: The province summoned him to serve as registrar.

entries.zh: 第五弟孝勝，歷官邵陵王法曹、湘東王安西主簿記室、尚書左丞。
entries.en: His fifth brother Xiaosheng served as law aide to the Prince of Shaoling, recorder to the Prince of Xiangdong of the Pacifier of the West, and Left Assistant in the Secretariat.
entries.literal: His fifth younger brother Xiaosheng held office as law aide to the Prince of Shaoling, recorder to the Prince of Xiangdong of the Pacifier of the West, and Left Assistant in the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 出爲信義太守，公事免。
entries.en: He was sent out as administrator of Xinyi and removed for a disciplinary offense.
entries.literal: He went out as administrator of Xinyi and was dismissed for an official offense.

entries.zh: 久之，復爲尚書右丞，兼散騎常侍。
entries.en: Long afterward he again became Right Assistant in the Secretariat and concurrently regular palace attendant.
entries.literal: After a long interval he again became Right Assistant in the Secretariat and concurrently regular palace attendant.

entries.zh: 聘魏還，爲安西武陵王紀長史、蜀郡太守。
entries.en: Back from an embassy to Wei he was chief clerk to Prince Ji of Wuling, Pacifier of the West, and administrator of Shujun.
entries.literal: On return from an embassy to Wei he became chief clerk to the Prince of Wuling of the Pacifier of the West, Ji, and administrator of Shujun.

entries.zh: 太清中，侯景陷京師，紀僭號於蜀，以孝勝爲尚書僕射。
entries.en: During Great Clarity, after Hou Jing seized the capital, Ji set himself up in Shu and made Xiaosheng Minister of the Left.
entries.literal: In the Great Clarity era, when Hou Jing took the capital, Ji declared himself emperor in Shu and made Xiaosheng Minister of the Left.

entries.zh: 承聖中，隨紀出峽口，兵敗，被執下獄。
entries.en: In the Chengsheng period he followed Ji through the gorge; defeated, he was taken and cast into prison.
entries.literal: In the Chengsheng era he followed Ji out through the gorge; the army was defeated and he was seized and thrown into prison.

entries.zh: 世祖尋宥之，起爲司徒右長史。
entries.en: The Founding Emperor soon forgave him and made him right chief clerk of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor soon pardoned him and raised him to right chief clerk of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 第七弟孝先，武陵王法曹、主簿。
entries.en: His seventh brother Xiaoxian was law aide and chief clerk to the Prince of Wuling.
entries.literal: His seventh younger brother Xiaoxian served as law aide and chief clerk to the Prince of Wuling.

entries.zh: 王遷益州，隨府轉安西記室。
entries.en: When the prince moved to Yizhou, he followed the staff and became recorder to the Pacifier of the West.
entries.literal: When the prince was transferred to Yizhou, he followed the prince's staff and became recorder to the Pacifier of the West.

entries.zh: 承聖中，與兄孝勝俱隨紀軍出峽口，兵敗，至江陵，世祖以爲黃門侍郎，遷侍中。
entries.en: In Chengsheng he and Xiaosheng both followed Ji's army through the gorge; beaten, they came to Jiangling, and the Founding Emperor made Xiaoxian Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, then palace attendant.
entries.literal: In the Chengsheng era he and his brother Xiaosheng both followed Ji's army out through the gorge; defeated, they reached Jiangling, and the Founding Emperor made Xiaoxian Gentleman of the Yellow Gates and promoted him to palace attendant.

entries.zh: 兄弟並善五言詩，見重於世。
entries.en: All the brothers excelled at five-character poetry and were held in honor by their age.
entries.literal: The brothers were all skilled at five-character verse and were esteemed in the world.

entries.zh: 文集值亂，今不具存。
entries.en: Their collections were destroyed in the chaos and no longer survive whole.
entries.literal: Their collected writings were lost in the disorders and are not fully preserved today.

entries.zh: 蕭幾字德玄，齊曲江公遙欣子也。
entries.en: Xiao Ji, styled Dexuan, was the son of Duke Yaoxin of Qujiang under Qi.
entries.literal: Xiao Ji, courtesy name Dexuan, was son of the Duke of Qujiang, Yaoxin, of Qi.

entries.zh: 年十歲，能屬文。
entries.en: At ten he could already write prose.
entries.literal: At ten he could compose literary pieces.

entries.zh: 早孤，有弟九人，並皆稚小，幾恩愛篤睦，聞於朝野。
entries.en: Fatherless while young, he had nine younger brothers, all infants; Ji's love among them was warm and close, and word of it reached court and countryside.
entries.literal: Orphaned early, he had nine younger brothers, all still very young; Ji's affection among them was deep and harmonious, and the court and common people heard of it.

entries.zh: 性溫和，與物無競，清貧自立。
entries.en: Gentle by nature, he strove with no one and lived upright in honest poverty.
entries.literal: His nature was mild and gentle; he did not contend with others and upheld himself in clean poverty.

entries.zh: 好學，善草隸書。
entries.en: He loved study and wrote well in cursive and clerical hands.
entries.literal: He loved learning and was skilled at cursive and clerical script.

entries.zh: 湘州刺史楊公則，曲江之故吏也。
entries.en: Yang Gongze, governor of Xiangzhou, had long served the house of Qujiang.
entries.literal: Yang Gongze, governor of Xiangzhou, had been an old retainer of Qujiang.

entries.zh: 每見幾，謂人曰：「康公此子，可謂桓靈寶出。」
entries.en: Whenever he met Ji he would tell others, "Duke Kang's son is truly a Huan Lingbao come again."
entries.literal: Whenever he saw Ji he would say to others, "Duke Kang's son may be called a Huan Lingbao reborn."

entries.zh: 及公則卒，幾爲之誄，時年十五，沈約見而奇之，謂其舅蔡撙曰：「昨見賢甥楊平南誄文，不減希逸之作，始驗康公積善之慶。」
entries.en: When Gongze died, Ji composed his funeral elegy at fifteen. Shen Yue read it with wonder and said to his uncle Cai Bo, "Yesterday I saw your worthy nephew's dirge for Yang, Pacifier of the South—not a step below Xiyi's writing; here is the first sign of Duke Kang's stored grace."
entries.literal: When Gongze died, Ji wrote an elegy for him; he was fifteen. Shen Yue saw it and marveled, saying to his uncle Cai Bo, "Yesterday I read your worthy nephew's elegy for the Pacifier of the South, Yang—it is no whit inferior to Xiyi's work; this is the first proof of Duke Kang's accumulated good fortune."

entries.zh: 釋褐著作佐郎、廬陵王文學、尚書殿中郎、太子舍人、掌管記，遷庶子、中書侍郎、尚書左丞。
entries.en: After his first office he rose through Gentleman of the Palace Library, literary aide to the Prince of Luling, Secretariat gentleman in the palace bureau, crown prince attendant, and keeper of the records, then junior tutor, Secretariat gentleman, and left assistant in the Secretariat.
entries.literal: On leaving the mourning garb he was appointed Gentleman of the Palace Library, literary aide to the Prince of Luling, Secretariat gentleman in the palace bureau, crown prince attendant, and keeper of the records; he was promoted to junior tutor, Secretariat gentleman, and left assistant in the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 末年，專尚釋教。
entries.en: In his last years he gave himself wholly to Buddhist teaching.
entries.literal: In his later years he devoted himself solely to Buddhism.

entries.zh: 爲新安太守，郡多山水，特其所好，適性遊履，遂爲之記。
entries.en: Made magistrate of Xin'an, whose hills and streams were his special delight, he roamed at ease and composed a record of the commandery.
entries.literal: As magistrate of Xin'an, a commandery rich in mountains and rivers that suited his temperament, he wandered as inclination led and wrote an account of the place.

entries.zh: 卒於官。
entries.en: He died while holding office.
entries.literal: He died in office.

entries.zh: 子爲，字元專，亦有文才。
entries.en: His son Wei, styled Yuanzhuan, likewise showed a gift for letters.
entries.literal: His son Wei, courtesy name Yuanzhuan, also had literary talent.

entries.zh: 仕至太子舍人，永康令。
entries.en: He served as crown prince attendant and magistrate of Yongkang.
entries.literal: In office he reached crown prince attendant and magistrate of Yongkang.

entries.zh: 梁書卷第四十一 列傳第三十五
entries.en: Book of Liang, Volume 41, Biography 35
entries.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 41, Biography 35

entries.zh: 臧盾字宣卿，東莞莒人。
entries.en: Zang Dun, styled Xuanqing, came from Ju in Dongguan.
entries.literal: Zang Dun, courtesy name Xuanqing, was a native of Ju in Dongguan.

entries.zh: 高祖燾，宋左光祿大夫。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Tao had served Song as Left Glorious Grand Master.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Tao had been Left Glorious Grand Master under Song.

entries.zh: 祖潭之，左民尚書。
entries.en: His grandfather Tanzhi had been Minister of the Left for the People.
entries.literal: His grandfather Tanzhi had been Minister of the Left for the People.

entries.zh: 父未甄，博涉文史，有才幹，少爲外兄汝南周顒所知。
entries.en: His father Weizhen read widely in letters and history and showed real talent; as a youth he came to the attention of his uncle by marriage, Zhou Yong of Runan.
entries.literal: His father Weizhen was broadly learned in letters and history and gifted in affairs; in youth he won the notice of his maternal cousin Zhou Yong of Runan.

entries.zh: 宋末，起家爲領軍主簿，所奉卽齊武帝。
entries.en: At the end of Song he took his first post as recorder on the staff of the Army of the Capital—the lord he served was Emperor Wu of Qi.
entries.literal: At the end of Song he began office as recorder in the headquarters of the Army of the Capital; the lord he served was Emperor Wu of Qi.

entries.zh: 入齊，歷太尉祭酒、尚書主客郎、建安、廬陵二王府記室、前軍功曹史、通直郎、南徐州中正、丹陽尹丞。
entries.en: Under Qi he served as libationer to the Grand Marshal, gentleman for foreign guests in the Ministry of Rites, secretariat aide to the princes of Jian'an and Luling, merit officer on the Forward Army staff, direct-communication attendant, rectifier of the South Xuzhou central register, and assistant to the governor of Danyang.
entries.literal: Entering Qi he held posts as libationer to the Grand Marshal, gentleman in the Ministry of Rites in charge of foreign guests, secretariat aide to the princes of Jian'an and Luling, merit officer in the Forward Army, palace attendant for direct communication, rectifier of the central register of South Xuzhou, and assistant in the yamen of the governor of Danyang.

entries.zh: 高祖平京邑，霸府建，引爲驃騎刑獄參軍。
entries.en: When the High Ancestor secured the capital and set up his headquarters, Weizhen was brought onto the staff of General of Agile Cavalry as penal and judicial aide.
entries.literal: When the High Ancestor pacified the capital region and established the hegemon's headquarters, Weizhen was brought in as penal and judicial aide on the staff of General of Agile Cavalry.

entries.zh: 天監初，除後軍諮議中郎、南徐州別駕，入拜黃門郎，遷右軍安成王長史、少府卿。
entries.en: At the start of Heavenly Surveillance he became staff adviser and middle director in the Rear Army and chief clerk of South Xuzhou, then entered court as a Yellow Gate gentleman and rose to chief clerk to the Prince of Ancheng of the Right Army and minister of the palace supplies.
entries.literal: At the opening of Heavenly Surveillance he was made staff adviser and middle director in the Rear Army and chief clerk of South Xuzhou, then entered court as gentleman in the Yellow Gate, and was promoted to chief clerk to the Prince of Ancheng of the Right Army and minister of the palace supplies.

entries.zh: 出爲新安太守，有能名。
entries.en: Sent out as magistrate of Xin'an, he earned a reputation for competence.
entries.literal: He went out as magistrate of Xin'an and won a name for ability.

entries.zh: 還爲太子中庶子、司農卿、太尉長史。
entries.en: Recalled, he became Junior Mentor in the heir apparent's household, Chamberlain for the National Granaries, and chief clerk to the Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: Returning he became junior tutor to the crown prince, minister of the national granaries, and chief clerk to the Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 丁所生母憂，三年廬于墓側。
entries.en: He mourned his birth mother and for three years lived in a hut by the grave.
entries.literal: He entered mourning for his birth mother and for three years dwelt in a hut beside the grave.

entries.zh: 服闋，除廷尉卿。
entries.en: When mourning ended he was appointed minister of justice.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he was made minister of justice.

entries.zh: 出爲安成王長史、江夏太守，卒官。
entries.en: He left the capital as chief clerk to the Prince of Ancheng and magistrate of Jiangxia, and died in office.
entries.literal: He went out as chief clerk to the Prince of Ancheng and magistrate of Jiangxia, and died in office.

entries.zh: 盾幼從徵士琅邪諸葛璩受《五經》，通章句。
entries.en: As a youth Dun studied the Five Classics under the recluse Zhuge Huan of Langye and mastered chapter and phrase.
entries.literal: In youth Dun studied the Five Classics from the reclusive scholar Zhuge Huan of Langye, mastering chapter and phrase.

entries.zh: 璩學徒常有數十百人，盾處其間，無所狎比。
entries.en: Huan's pupils often ran to dozens, but Dun kept company with none of them.
entries.literal: Huan's students often numbered in the dozens, yet among them Dun kept close with no one.

entries.zh: 璩異之，歎曰：「此生重器，王佐才也。」
entries.en: Huan marked him out and sighed, "This boy is a heavy vessel—the makings of a king's counselor."
entries.literal: Huan marveled at him and sighed: "This youth is a vessel of weight—the stuff of a king's aide."

entries.zh: 初爲撫軍行參軍，遷尚書中兵郎。
entries.en: He began as traveling aide on the Forward Army staff and was promoted to gentleman in the Secretariat bureau of soldiers.
entries.literal: He first served as traveling aide on the staff of the Forward Army and was promoted to gentleman in the Secretariat bureau of soldiers.

entries.zh: 盾美風姿，善舉止，每趨奏，高祖甚悅焉。
entries.en: Dun was handsome in bearing and graceful in manner; each time he hurried to audience the Founding Emperor took great delight in him.
entries.literal: Dun had a handsome bearing and graceful carriage; whenever he hurried to audience the Founding Emperor was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 入兼中書通事舍人，除安右錄事參軍，舍人如故。
entries.en: He entered court as concurrent communications attendant in the Secretariat, was made recording aide on the right of stability, and kept his attendant post.
entries.literal: He entered court concurrently as communications attendant in the Secretariat, was made recording aide on the right of stability, and kept his post as attendant.

entries.zh: 中大通五年二月，高祖幸同泰寺開講，設四部大會，衆數萬人。
entries.en: In the second month of the fifth year of Zhongdatong, the High Ancestor went to Tongtai Temple to open a lecture and held a great assembly of the four orders, with tens of thousands present.
entries.literal: In the second month of the fifth year of Zhongdatong the Founding Emperor visited Tongtai Temple to open a lecture and held a great assembly in four sections with tens of thousands present.

entries.zh: 南越所獻馴象，忽於衆中狂逸，乘轝羽衛及會皆駭散，惟盾與散騎郎裴之禮嶷然自若，高祖甚嘉焉。
entries.en: A tame elephant from Southern Yue suddenly ran wild in the crowd; the imperial carriage guards, feathered guards, and the whole assembly fled in terror. Only Dun and Scattered Cavalry Gentleman Pei Zhili stood unmoved, to the High Ancestor's great admiration.
entries.literal: A tame elephant presented by Southern Yue suddenly went mad in the crowd; carriage guards and attendants and the assembly all scattered in terror—only Dun and the regular palace attendant Pei Zhili stood unmoved, to the Founding Emperor's great admiration.

entries.zh: 盾有孝性，隨父宿直於廷尉，母劉氏在宅，夜暴亡，左手中指忽痛，不得寢。
entries.en: Dun was deeply filial. He followed his father on night duty at the court of justice while his mother Liu stayed at home. That night she died suddenly; the middle finger of his left hand throbbed with pain and he could not sleep.
entries.literal: Dun was deeply filial; he followed his father on night duty at the court of justice, while his mother Liu remained at home. She died suddenly that night; the middle finger of his left hand throbbed with pain and he could not sleep.

entries.zh: 及曉，宅信果報凶問，其感通如此。
entries.en: At dawn a messenger from home brought word of her death—such was the reach of his feeling.
entries.literal: At dawn a messenger from the house brought word of death—his sensitivities worked thus.

entries.zh: 服制未終，父又卒，盾居喪五年，不出廬戶，形骸枯顇，家人不復識。
entries.en: Before her mourning had ended his father died too; Dun mourned five years without leaving the hut, wasted to bone until his family could no longer know him.
entries.literal: Before the mourning period for her had ended his father also died; Dun kept mourning five years without leaving the hut, his frame wasted to bone until kin could no longer recognize him.

entries.zh: 鄉人王端以狀聞，高祖嘉之，敕累遣抑譬。
entries.en: A townsman, Wang Duan, reported this to the throne; the Founding Emperor praised him and again and again sent orders urging him to moderate his grief.
entries.literal: A townsman named Wang Duan reported this to the throne; the Founding Emperor praised him and repeatedly sent orders urging restraint.

entries.zh: 厥前後居職，所掌之局大事及蘭臺廷尉所不能決者，敕並付厥。
entries.en: Throughout his career the major matters of the bureaus he ran—and cases the Orchid Terrace and court of justice could not settle—were all entrusted to Jue.
entries.literal: Throughout his career the major matters of the bureaus he ran—and cases the Orchid Terrace and court of justice could not decide—were all entrusted to Jue.

entries.zh: 厥辨斷精詳，咸得其理。
entries.en: Jue's judgments were precise and detailed, and all accorded with reason.
entries.literal: Jue's judgments were precise and detailed; all accorded with reason.

entries.zh: 厥卒後，有撾登聞鼓訴者，求付清直舍人。
entries.en: After Jue died someone beat the petition drum at the Gate of Impartial Hearing, asking that his cases be given to a fair and upright attendant.
entries.literal: After Jue died someone beat the petition drum at the Gate of Impartial Hearing, asking that his cases be given to a fair and upright attendant.

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「臧厥旣亡，此事便無可付。」
entries.en: The Founding Emperor said, "Now that Zang Jue is gone, there is no one to whom this can be entrusted."
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor said: "Now that Zang Jue is gone, there is no one to whom this can be entrusted."

entries.zh: 其見知如此。
entries.en: Such was the esteem in which he was held.
entries.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

entries.zh: 岐美容止，博涉能占對。
entries.en: Qi had a fine bearing, read widely, and was skilled in repartee.
entries.literal: Qi had a fine bearing and was broadly learned, skilled in repartee.

entries.zh: 大同中，與魏和親，其使歲中再至，常遣岐接對焉。
entries.en: In Great Unity, when Liang and Wei made peace, Wei envoys came twice a year; Qi was often sent to receive them.
entries.literal: In Great Unity, when Liang and Wei made peace, their envoys came twice a year; Qi was often sent to receive them.

entries.zh: 太清元年，累遷太僕、司農卿，舍人如故。
entries.en: In the first year of Supreme Purity he rose in succession to grand charioteer and minister of the national granaries, keeping his attendant post.
entries.literal: In the first year of Supreme Purity he rose in succession to grand charioteer and minister of the national granaries, attendant as before.

entries.zh: 在禁省十餘年，機事密勿亞於朱异。
entries.en: For more than ten years in the forbidden precinct he handled confidential affairs, second only to Zhu Yi.
entries.literal: For more than ten years in the forbidden precinct he handled confidential affairs, second only to Zhu Yi.

entries.zh: 此年冬，豫州刺史貞陽侯蕭淵明率衆伐彭城，兵敗陷魏。
entries.en: That winter Marquis Zhenyang, Xiao Yuanming, governor of Yuzhou, led troops against Pengcheng; the army was defeated and Yuanming fell into Wei hands.
entries.literal: That winter Marquis Zhenyang of Xiao Yuanming, governor of Yuzhou, led troops to attack Pengcheng; the army was defeated and Yuanming was taken by Wei.

entries.zh: 二年，淵明遣使還，述魏人欲更通和好，敕有司及近臣定議。
entries.en: In the second year Yuanming sent envoys back, saying the Wei wished renewed peace; an edict ordered the relevant offices and nearby ministers to decide.
entries.literal: In the second year Yuanming sent envoys back, reporting that the Wei wished renewed peace and harmony; an edict ordered the relevant offices and nearby ministers to decide.

entries.zh: 左衛朱异曰：「高澄此意，當復欲繼好，不爽前和；
entries.en: Left Guard Zhu Yi said, "Gao Cheng's intent is surely to renew good relations and not break the prior peace;
entries.literal: Left Guard Zhu Yi said: "Gao Cheng's intent is surely to renew the good relations and not break the prior peace;

entries.zh: 邊境且得靜寇息民，於事爲便。」
entries.en: the borders may rest from raiders and the people from harm—for affairs this is convenient."
entries.literal: the borders may rest from raiders and the people from harm—for affairs this is convenient."

entries.zh: 議者並然之。
entries.en: The debaters all agreed with him.
entries.literal: The debaters all agreed with him.

entries.zh: 岐獨曰：「高澄旣新得志，其勢非弱，何事須和？
entries.en: Qi alone said, "Gao Cheng has newly secured his aims; his power is not weak—why should he need peace?
entries.literal: Qi alone said: "Gao Cheng has newly secured his aims; his power is not weak—why should he need peace?

entries.zh: 此必是設間，故令貞陽遣使，令侯景自疑當以貞陽易景。
entries.en: This must be a stratagem: he has Zhenyang send envoys so Hou Jing will suspect he is to be exchanged for Zhenyang.
entries.literal: This must be a stratagem: he has Zhenyang send envoys so that Hou Jing will suspect he is to be exchanged for Zhenyang.

entries.zh: 景意不安，必圖禍亂。
entries.en: Uneasy in mind, Jing is sure to plot rebellion.
entries.literal: Uneasy in mind, Jing is sure to plot rebellion.

entries.zh: 今若許澄通好，正是墮其計中。
entries.en: If we now grant Cheng peace, we fall straight into his scheme.
entries.literal: If we now grant Cheng peace, we fall straight into his scheme.

entries.zh: 且彭城去歲喪師，渦陽新復敗退，令便就和，益示國家之弱。
entries.en: Moreover, last year Pengcheng lost its army and Guoyang has newly suffered defeat and retreat—to make peace now only shows the state's weakness.
entries.literal: Moreover, last year Pengcheng lost its army and Guoyang has newly suffered defeat and retreat—to make peace now only shows the state's weakness.

entries.zh: 若如愚意，此和宜不可許。」
entries.en: In my humble view this peace ought not be granted."
entries.literal: In my humble view this peace ought not be granted."

entries.zh: 朱异等固執，高祖遂從異議。
entries.en: Zhu Yi and the rest held firm; the Founding Emperor followed Yi's counsel.
entries.literal: Zhu Yi and the rest held firm; the Founding Emperor followed Yi's counsel.

entries.zh: 及遣和使，侯景果有此疑，累啟請追使，敕但依違報之。
entries.en: When peace envoys were sent, Hou Jing indeed harbored this suspicion and repeatedly memorialized asking that the envoys be recalled; edicts answered only evasively.
entries.literal: When peace envoys were sent, Hou Jing indeed harbored this suspicion and repeatedly memorialized asking that the envoys be recalled; edicts answered only evasively.

entries.zh: 至八月，遂舉兵反。
entries.en: By the eighth month he had raised troops in rebellion.
entries.literal: By the eighth month he had raised troops in rebellion.

entries.zh: 十月，入寇京師，請誅朱异。
entries.en: In the tenth month he invaded the capital and asked that Zhu Yi be executed.
entries.literal: In the tenth month he invaded the capital and asked that Zhu Yi be executed.

entries.zh: 三年，遷中領軍，舍人如故。
entries.en: In the third year he was promoted to commandant of the central army, keeping his attendant post.
entries.literal: In the third year he was promoted to commandant of the central army, attendant as before.

entries.zh: 二月，景于闕前通表，乞割江右四州，安其部下，當解圍還鎮，敕許之。
entries.en: In the second month Jing submitted a memorial before the palace gate, asking to cede the four prefectures west of the river to settle his followers and promising to lift the siege and return to garrison if granted; an edict approved.
entries.literal: In the second month Jing submitted a memorial before the palace gate, asking to cede the four prefectures west of the river to settle his followers and promising to lift the siege and return to garrison if granted; an edict approved.

entries.zh: 乃於城西立盟，求遣宣城王出送。
entries.en: An oath was then sworn west of the city, and Jing asked that the Prince of Xuancheng be sent out as hostage.
entries.literal: An oath was then sworn west of the city, and Jing asked that the Prince of Xuancheng be sent out as hostage.

entries.zh: 岐固執宣城嫡嗣之重，不宜許，遣石城公大款送之。
entries.en: Qi held firm to the weight of Xuancheng's legitimate heir and said he ought not be granted; the Duke of Stone City, Dakuan, was sent instead.
entries.literal: Qi held firm to the weight of the legitimate heir of Xuancheng and said he ought not be granted; the Duke of Stone City, Dakuan, was sent instead.

entries.zh: 及與景盟訖，城中文武喜躍，望得解圍。
entries.en: When the oath with Jing was finished, civil and military men in the city rejoiced, hoping the siege would be lifted.
entries.literal: When the oath with Jing was finished, civil and military men in the city rejoiced, hoping the siege would be lifted.

entries.zh: 岐獨言於衆曰：「賊舉兵爲逆，未遂求和，夷情獸心，必不可信，此和終爲賊所詐也。」
entries.en: Qi alone said to the assembly, "The bandit raised troops in rebellion and has not yet obtained peace; barbarian hearts and beast natures cannot be trusted—this peace will in the end be the bandit's deceit."
entries.literal: Qi alone said to the assembly: "The bandit raised troops in rebellion and has not yet obtained peace; barbarian hearts and beast natures cannot be trusted—this peace will in the end be the bandit's deceit."

entries.zh: 衆並怨怪之。
entries.en: The crowd all resented and blamed him.
entries.literal: The crowd all resented and blamed him.

entries.zh: 及景背盟，莫不嘆服。
entries.en: When Jing broke the oath, none failed to admire Qi.
entries.literal: When Jing broke the oath, none failed to admire him.

entries.zh: 尋有詔，以岐勤勞，封南豊縣侯，邑五百戶，固辭不受。
entries.en: Soon an edict, for Qi's diligence, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Nanfeng with a fief of five hundred households; he firmly refused and did not accept.
entries.literal: Soon an edict, for Qi's diligence, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Nanfeng with a fief of five hundred households; he firmly refused and did not accept.

entries.zh: 宮城失守，岐帶疾出圍，卒於宅。
entries.en: When the palace city fell, Qi, though ill, broke out of the encirclement and died at his house.
entries.literal: When the palace city fell, Qi, though ill, broke out of the encirclement and died at his house.

entries.zh: 俄有詔，加散騎常侍，未拜，又詔曰：「總一六軍，非才勿授。
entries.en: Soon an edict made him regular palace attendant, but before he took office another edict said, "To command the Six Armies—give the post only to the worthy.
entries.literal: Soon an edict added him as regular palace attendant, but before he took office another edict said: "To command the Six Armies—give the post only to talent.

entries.zh: 御史中丞、新除散騎常侍盾，志懷忠密，識用詳慎，當官平允，處務勤恪，必能緝斯戎政。
entries.en: Censor-in-chief and newly appointed regular palace attendant Dun is loyal at heart and careful in judgment; fair in office and diligent in affairs—surely fit to order these military matters.
entries.literal: Censor-in-chief and newly appointed regular palace attendant Dun is loyal at heart and careful in judgment; in office he is fair and in affairs diligent—surely able to order these military matters.

entries.zh: 可兼領軍，常侍如故。」
entries.en: Let him concurrently command the Army of the Capital while keeping his post as regular attendant."
entries.literal: He may concurrently command the Army of the Capital while keeping his post as regular attendant."

entries.zh: 大同二年，遷中領軍。
entries.en: In the second year of Great Unity he was promoted to commandant of the central army.
entries.literal: In the second year of Great Unity he was promoted to commandant of the central army.

entries.zh: 領軍管天下兵要，監局事多。
entries.en: The commandant controlled the empire's military keys and oversaw many bureaus.
entries.literal: The commandant's post controlled the empire's military keys and supervised many bureaus.

entries.zh: 盾爲人敏贍，有風力，長於撥繁，職事甚理。
entries.en: Dun was quick and capable, forceful in character, and excelled at cutting through complexity; the work ran in good order.
entries.literal: Dun was quick and capable, had force of character, and excelled at cutting through complexity—the work ran in good order.

entries.zh: 天監中，吳平侯蕭景居此職，著聲稱。
entries.en: In Heavenly Surveillance the Marquis of Pingwu, Xiao Jing, had held this post to wide renown.
entries.literal: In Heavenly Surveillance the Marquis of Pingwu Xiao Jing had held this post with famed reputation.

entries.zh: 至是盾復繼之。
entries.en: Now Dun followed him in that line.
entries.literal: Now Dun followed him in succession.

entries.zh: 傅岐字景平，北地靈州人也。
entries.en: Fu Qi, styled Jingping, came from Lingzhou in Beidi.
entries.literal: Fu Qi, courtesy name Jingping, was a native of Lingzhou in Beidi.

entries.zh: 高祖弘仁，宋太常。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Hongren had served Song as grand chamberlain.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Hongren had been grand chamberlain under Song.

entries.zh: 祖琰，齊世爲山陰令，有治能，自縣擢爲益州刺史。
entries.en: His grandfather Yan, in Qi times magistrate of Shanyin, governed well and was raised from that county post to Inspector of Yi Province.
entries.literal: His grandfather Yan, in Qi times magistrate of Shanyin, had governing ability and was promoted from that county post to Inspector of Yi Province.

entries.zh: 父翽，天監中，歷山陰、建康令，亦有能名，官至驃騎諮議。
entries.en: His father Hui, under Heavenly Surveillance, held Shanyin and Jiankang in succession, likewise famed for ability, and reached staff adviser to Rapid Cavalry.
entries.literal: His father Hui, in Heavenly Surveillance, held the magistracies of Shan and Jiankang in succession, likewise famed for ability, and reached staff adviser to Rapid Cavalry.

entries.zh: 梁書卷第四十二 列傳第三十六
entries.en: Book of Liang, Volume 42, Biography 36
entries.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 42, Biography 36

entries.zh: 韋粲字長蒨，車騎將軍叡之孫，北徐州刺史放之子也。
entries.en: Wei Can, styled Changqian, was grandson of Rapid Cavalry General Rui and son of North Xuzhou Inspector Fang.
entries.literal: Wei Can, courtesy name Changqian, was grandson of Rapid Cavalry General Rui and son of North Xuzhou Inspector Fang.

entries.zh: 有父風，好學仗氣，身長八尺，容貌甚偉。
entries.en: He had his father's manner, loved learning and bore himself with spirit; eight chi tall, with a truly imposing presence.
entries.literal: He had his father's manner, loved learning and bore himself with spirit; eight chi tall, his appearance was very imposing.

entries.zh: 初爲雲麾晉安王行參軍，俄署法曹，遷外兵參軍，兼中兵。
entries.en: He began as traveling aide on the staff of the Cloud-Banner Prince of Jin'an, soon held the law bureau, rose to exterior military aide, and concurrently interior military aide.
entries.literal: He first served as traveling aide on the staff of the Cloud-Banner Prince of Jin'an, soon held the law bureau, was promoted to exterior military aide, and concurrently interior military aide.

entries.zh: 時潁川庾仲容、吳郡張率，前輩知名，與粲同府，並忘年交好。
entries.en: Yu Zhongrong of Yingchuan and Zhang Shuai of Wu, famed seniors, shared the same headquarters with Can and became close friends despite the gap in years.
entries.literal: At the time Yu Zhongrong of Yingchuan and Zhang Shuai of Wu commandery, famed seniors of earlier standing, were in the same headquarters and became friends with Can despite the gap in years.

entries.zh: 及王遷鎮雍州，隨轉記室，兼中兵如故。
entries.en: When the prince moved to garrison Yongzhou, Can became secretariat aide and kept his concurrent interior military post.
entries.literal: When the prince was transferred to garrison Yongzhou, Can moved with him to secretariat aide, still concurrently interior military aide as before.

entries.zh: 王立爲皇太子，粲遷步兵校尉，入爲東宮領直，丁父憂去職。
entries.en: When the prince became crown prince, Can rose to colonel of the infantry guard, entered as commander of the Eastern Palace guard, then left office to mourn his father.
entries.literal: When the prince was established as crown prince, Can was promoted to colonel of the infantry guard, entered court as commander of the Eastern Palace guard, and left office for his father's mourning.

entries.zh: 尋起爲招遠將軍，復爲領直。
entries.en: Soon he was recalled as General Who Wins the Distant and again commander of the guard.
entries.literal: Soon he was recalled as General Who Wins the Distant and again commander of the guard.

entries.zh: 服闋，襲爵永昌縣侯，除安西湘東王諮議，累遷太子僕、左衛率，領直並如故。
entries.en: When mourning ended he inherited the marquisate of Yongchang and became staff adviser to the Prince of Xiangdong of the Anxi Army, then rose through crown prince steward and left guard leader while keeping his guard command.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he inherited the marquisate of Yongchang county and was made staff adviser to the Prince of Xiangdong of the Anxi Army, then rose through crown prince steward and left guard leader, keeping his guard command as before.

entries.zh: 粲以舊恩，任寄綢密，雖居職屢徙，常留宿衛，頗擅威名，誕倨，不爲時輩所平。
entries.en: Because of old favor Can was entrusted with intimate duties; though his posts shifted, he regularly remained on night guard, wielded real prestige, and was haughty—men of the day did not regard him as their equal.
entries.literal: Because of old favor Can was entrusted with intimate duties; though his posts often changed, he regularly remained on night guard, wielded considerable reputation for awe, and was haughty and proud—men of the day did not regard him as their equal.

entries.zh: 右衛朱异嘗於酒席厲色謂粲曰：「卿何得已作領軍面向人！」
entries.en: Right Guard Zhu Yi once said to Can at a banquet in harsh tones, "How dare you already act like a commandant of the army before people!"
entries.literal: Right Guard Zhu Yi once said to Can at a banquet in harsh tones: "How dare you already act like a commandant of the army before people!"

entries.zh: 張嵊字四山，鎮北將軍稷之子也。
entries.en: Zhang Sheng, styled Sishan, was son of Pacifying North General Ji.
entries.literal: Zhang Sheng, courtesy name Sishan, was son of Pacifying North General Ji.

entries.zh: 少方雅，有志操，能清言。
entries.en: From youth he was upright and elegant, had resolve, and could speak with clarity.
entries.literal: From youth he was upright and elegant, had resolve, and could speak with clarity.

entries.zh: 父臨青州，爲土民所害，嵊感家禍，終身蔬食布衣，手不執刀刃。
entries.en: His father while inspecting Qing province was killed by locals; Sheng, moved by the family calamity, ate vegetables and wore cloth all his life and never held a blade.
entries.literal: His father while inspecting Qing province was killed by the local people; Sheng, moved by the family calamity, ate vegetables and wore cloth all his life and never held a blade in his hand.

entries.zh: 州舉秀才。
entries.en: The province nominated him as Presented Scholar.
entries.literal: The province nominated him as Presented Scholar.

entries.zh: 起家秘書郎，累遷太子舍人、洗馬、司徒左西掾、中書郎。
entries.en: He began as secretary gentleman and rose through crown prince attendant, steward, left merit officer on the Minister of Education's staff, and Secretariat gentleman.
entries.literal: He began office as secretary gentleman and rose through crown prince attendant, steward, left merit officer on the Minister of Education's staff, and gentleman of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 出爲永陽內史，還除中軍宣城王司馬、散騎常侍。
entries.en: He went out as interior minister of Yongyang, returned as staff major to the Prince of Xuancheng of the Central Army and regular palace attendant.
entries.literal: He went out as interior minister of Yongyang, returned and was made staff major to the Prince of Xuancheng of the Central Army and regular palace attendant.

entries.zh: 又出爲鎮南湘東王長史、尋陽太守。
entries.en: Again he went out as chief clerk to the Prince of Xiangdong of the Pacifying South Army and magistrate of Xunyang.
entries.literal: Again he went out as chief clerk to the Prince of Xiangdong of the Pacifying South Army and magistrate of Xunyang.

entries.zh: 中大同元年，徵爲太府卿，俄遷吳興太守。
entries.en: In the first year of Zhongdatong he was summoned as minister of the palace treasury, soon promoted to magistrate of Wuxing.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhongdatong he was summoned as minister of the palace treasury, soon promoted to magistrate of Wuxing.

entries.zh: 次新亭，賊列陣於中興寺，相持至晚，各解歸。
entries.en: Stopping at Xinting, the bandit drew up lines at Zhongxing Temple; they faced each other until evening, each withdrawing.
entries.literal: Stopping at Xinting, the bandit drew up battle lines at Zhongxing Temple; they faced each other until evening, each withdrawing.

entries.zh: 是夜，仲禮入粲營，部分衆軍，旦日將戰，諸將各有據守，令粲頓青塘。
entries.en: That night Zhongli entered Can's camp and arrayed the armies; at dawn they would fight; each general had his post, and Can was ordered to hold Qingtang.
entries.literal: That night Zhongli entered Can's camp and arrayed the armies; at dawn they would fight; each general had his post, and Can was ordered to hold Qingtang.

entries.zh: 青塘當石頭中路，粲慮柵壘未立，賊必爭之，頗以爲憚，謂仲禮曰：「下官才非禦侮，直欲以身殉國。
entries.en: Qingtang lay on the middle road to Stone City; Can feared the palisade was not yet built and the bandit would contest it, and said to Zhongli, "My talent is not for repelling insults—I only wish to give my body for the state.
entries.literal: Qingtang lay on the middle road to Stone City; Can feared the palisade was not yet built and the bandit would surely contest it, and was much afraid, saying to Zhongli: "This subordinate's talent is not for repelling insults—I only wish to give my body for the state.

entries.zh: 節下善量其宜，不可致有虧喪。」
entries.en: Master, weigh what is fit—do not let there be loss and ruin."
entries.literal: Master, weigh what is fit—do not let there be loss and ruin."

entries.zh: 仲禮曰：「青塘立柵，迫近淮渚，欲以糧儲船乘盡就泊之，此是大事，非兄不可。
entries.en: Zhongli said, "To build a palisade at Qingtang close to the Huai ford is to bring grain stores and boats all to moor there—this is a great matter and cannot be done without you, brother.
entries.literal: Zhongli said: "To build a palisade at Qingtang close to the Huai ford is to bring grain stores and boats all to moor there—this is a great matter and cannot be done without you, brother.

entries.zh: 若疑兵少，當更差軍相助。」
entries.en: If you fear too few troops, more troops can be sent to help."
entries.literal: If you fear too few troops, more troops can be sent to help."

entries.zh: 乃使直閤將軍劉叔胤師助粲，帥所部水陸俱進。
entries.en: He sent direct-gate general Liu Shuyin to assist Can, leading his command by land and water together.
entries.literal: He then sent the direct-gate general Liu Shuyin to assist Can, leading his command by land and water together.

entries.zh: 時值昏霧，軍人迷失道，比及青塘，夜已過半，壘柵至曉未合。
entries.en: Fog and dusk fell; the soldiers lost the road, and by the time they reached Qingtang it was past midnight; the palisade was not closed by dawn.
entries.literal: At the time fog and dusk fell; the soldiers lost the road, and by the time they reached Qingtang it was past midnight; the palisade was not closed by dawn.

entries.zh: 景登禪靈寺門閣，望粲營未立，便率銳卒來攻。
entries.en: Jing climbed the gate-tower of Chanling Temple, saw Can's camp not yet established, and led crack troops to attack.
entries.literal: Jing climbed the gate-tower of Chanling Temple, saw Can's camp not yet established, and led crack troops to attack.

entries.zh: 軍副王長茂勸據柵待之，粲不從，令軍主鄭逸逆擊之，命劉叔胤以水軍截其後。
entries.en: Deputy Wang Changmao urged holding the palisade and waiting; Can would not agree and ordered commander Zheng Yi to meet the attack, commanding Liu Shuyin with the water army to cut the rear.
entries.literal: The deputy Wang Changmao urged holding the palisade and waiting; Can would not agree and ordered the commander Zheng Yi to meet the attack, commanding Liu Shuyin with the water army to cut off the rear.

entries.zh: 叔胤畏懦不敢進，逸遂敗。
entries.en: Shuyin in cowardice dared not advance; Yi was defeated.
entries.literal: Shuyin in cowardice dared not advance; Yi was defeated.

entries.zh: 賊乘勝入營，左右牽粲避賊，粲不動，猶叱子弟力戰，兵死略盡，遂見害，時年五十四。
entries.en: The bandit pressed the victory into the camp; attendants pulled Can away but he did not move, still shouting at his sons and brothers to fight hard; soldiers died almost to the last man, and he was killed at fifty-four.
entries.literal: The bandit pressed the victory into the camp; attendants pulled Can away from the bandit but he did not move, still shouting at his sons and younger brothers to fight hard; soldiers died almost to the last man, and he was killed at age fifty-four.

entries.zh: 粲子尼及三弟助、警、構、從弟昂皆戰死，親戚死者數百人。
entries.en: Can's son Ni and three younger brothers Zhu, Jing, and Gou, and cousin Ang, all died in battle; kin who died numbered in the hundreds.
entries.literal: Can's son Ni and three younger brothers Zhu, Jing, and Gou, and cousin Ang, all died in battle; kin who died numbered in the hundreds.

entries.zh: 賊傳粲首闕下，以示城內，太宗聞之流涕曰：「社稷所寄，惟在韋公，如何不幸，先死行陣。」
entries.en: The bandit displayed Can's head below the gate; when the Heir Apparent heard he wept and said, "The altars' trust rested only in Lord Wei—how could he die first in the ranks."
entries.literal: The bandit displayed Can's head below the gate to show the city; when the Heir Apparent heard he wept and said: "The altars' trust rested only in Lord Wei—how could he, unhappily, die first in the ranks."

entries.zh: 詔贈護軍將軍。
entries.en: An edict posthumously made him General Who Guards the Army.
entries.literal: An edict posthumously made him General Who Guards the Army.

entries.zh: 世祖平侯景，追諡曰忠貞，並追贈助、警、構及尼皆中書郎，昂員外散騎常侍。
entries.en: When Emperor Shizu pacified Hou Jing, he was posthumously titled Loyal and Upright, and Zhu, Jing, Gou, and Ni were posthumously made Secretariat gentlemen, Ang exterior regular palace attendant.
entries.literal: When the Shizu Emperor pacified Hou Jing, he was posthumously titled Loyal and Upright, and Zhu, Jing, Gou, and Ni were all posthumously made gentlemen of the Secretariat, Ang exterior regular palace attendant.

entries.zh: 及侯景反，攻陷歷陽，自橫江將渡，子一帥舟師千餘人，於下流欲邀之，其副董桃生家在江北，因與其黨散走。
entries.en: When Hou Jing rebelled and took Liyang and was about to cross from Hengjiang, Ziyi led more than a thousand boats downstream to intercept him, but deputy Dong Taosheng had family north of the river and fled with his faction.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled and took Liyang, he was about to cross from Hengjiang; Ziyi led more than a thousand boats downstream intending to intercept him, but his deputy Dong Taosheng had family north of the river and with his faction scattered and fled.

entries.zh: 子一乃退還南洲，復收餘衆，步道赴京師。
entries.en: Ziyi withdrew to South Isle, gathered the remainder again, and went on foot toward the capital.
entries.literal: Ziyi then withdrew to South Isle, gathered the remainder again, and went on foot toward the capital.

entries.zh: 賊亦尋至，子一啓太宗曰：「賊圍未合，猶可出蕩，若營柵一固，無所用武。」
entries.en: The bandit soon arrived; Ziyi memorialized the Heir Apparent, "The siege is not yet closed—one can still sally out; once camps are fixed, arms are useless."
entries.literal: The bandit also soon arrived; Ziyi memorialized the Heir Apparent: "The bandit siege is not yet closed—one can still sally out; once camps are fixed, there is no use for arms."

entries.zh: 請與其弟子四、子五帥所領百餘人，開承明門挑賊。
entries.en: He asked with his younger brothers Zisi and Ziwu to lead more than a hundred men to open the Chengming Gate and challenge the bandit.
entries.literal: He asked with his younger brothers Zisi and Ziwu to lead their command of more than a hundred men to open the Chengming Gate and challenge the bandit.

entries.zh: 許之。
entries.en: Permission was granted.
entries.literal: Permission was granted.

entries.zh: 子一乃身先士卒，抽戈獨進，群賊夾攻之，從者莫敢繼。
entries.en: Ziyi took the lead, drew his halberd and advanced alone; bandits attacked from both sides and followers dared not follow.
entries.literal: Ziyi then took the lead before the soldiers, drew his halberd and advanced alone; bandits attacked from both sides and followers dared not follow.

entries.zh: 子四、子五見事急，相引赴賊，並見害。
entries.en: Zisi and Ziwu, seeing affairs urgent, pulled one another toward the bandit and were both killed.
entries.literal: Zisi and Ziwu, seeing affairs urgent, pulled one another toward the bandit and were both killed.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「故戎昭將軍、通直散騎侍郎、南津校尉江子一，前尚書右丞江子四，東宮直殿主帥子五，禍故有聞，良以矜惻，死事加等，抑惟舊章。
entries.en: An edict said, "The late General of Martial Proclamation, regular palace attendant, and colonel of the southern ford Jiang Ziyi; the late right assistant Jiang Zisi; and Eastern Palace direct-hall commander Ziwu—misfortune has brought report and we are deeply moved; to die for the affair merits higher rank by old regulations.
entries.literal: An edict said: "The late General of Martial Proclamation, regular palace attendant for direct communication, and colonel of the southern ford Jiang Ziyi; the late right assistant Jiang Zisi; and the Eastern Palace direct-hall commander Ziwu—misfortune has brought report, and we are deeply moved; to die for the affair merits higher rank, as old regulations provide.

entries.zh: 可贈子一給事黃門侍郎，子四中書侍郎，子五散騎侍郎。」
entries.en: Ziyi may be posthumously made Yellow Gate gentleman; Zisi Secretariat gentleman; Ziwu regular palace attendant."
entries.literal: Ziyi may be posthumously made gentleman in the Yellow Gate; Zisi gentleman in the Secretariat; Ziwu regular palace attendant."

entries.zh: 侯景平，世祖又追贈子一侍中，諡義子；
entries.en: When Hou Jing was pacified Emperor Shizu again posthumously made Ziyi palace attendant with the posthumous title Righteous;
entries.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified the Shizu Emperor again posthumously made Ziyi palace attendant with the posthumous title Righteous;

entries.zh: 子四黃門侍郎，諡毅子；
entries.en: Zisi Yellow Gate gentleman with the posthumous title Resolute;
entries.literal: Zisi gentleman in the Yellow Gate with the posthumous title Resolute;

entries.zh: 子五中書侍郎，諡烈子。
entries.en: Ziwu Secretariat gentleman with the posthumous title Fierce.
entries.literal: Ziwu gentleman in the Secretariat with the posthumous title Fierce.

entries.zh: 太清二年，侯景圍京城，嵊遣弟伊率郡兵數千人赴援。
entries.en: In the second year of Supreme Purity Hou Jing besieged the capital; Sheng sent his younger brother Yi to lead several thousand commandery troops to the rescue.
entries.literal: In the second year of Supreme Purity Hou Jing besieged the capital; Sheng sent his younger brother Yi to lead several thousand commandery troops to the rescue.

entries.zh: 三年，宮城陷，御史中丞沈浚違難東歸。
entries.en: In the third year the palace city fell; censor-in-chief Shen Jun fled east in hardship.
entries.literal: In the third year the palace city fell; censor-in-chief Shen Jun fled east in hardship.

entries.zh: 嵊往見而謂曰：「賊臣憑陵，社稷危恥，正是人臣效命之秋。
entries.en: Sheng went to see him and said, "The traitor towers over us; the altars are in peril—this is the season for ministers to devote their lives.
entries.literal: Sheng went to see him and said: "The traitor minister towers over us; the altars are in peril and shame—this is the season for ministers to devote their lives.

entries.zh: 今欲收集兵力，保據貴鄉。
entries.en: Now I wish to gather troops and hold your noble district.
entries.literal: Now I wish to gather troops and hold your noble district.

entries.zh: 若天道無靈，忠節不展，雖復及死，誠亦無恨。」
entries.en: If Heaven is without spirit and loyal resolve cannot unfold, even if death follows, I have no regret."
entries.literal: If Heaven's way is without spirit and loyal resolve cannot unfold, even if death follows, truly I have no regret."

entries.zh: 浚曰：「鄙郡雖小，仗義拒逆，誰敢不從！」
entries.en: Jun said, "Though my commandery is small, who relying on righteousness to resist the villain dares not follow!"
entries.literal: Jun said: "Though my commandery is small, who relying on righteousness to resist the villain dares not follow!"

entries.zh: 固勸嵊舉義。
entries.en: He firmly urged Sheng to raise righteousness.
entries.literal: He firmly urged Sheng to raise righteousness.

entries.zh: 於是收集士卒，繕築城壘。
entries.en: Thereupon he gathered soldiers and repaired walls and ramparts.
entries.literal: Thereupon he gathered soldiers and repaired walls and ramparts.

entries.zh: 時邵陵王東奔至錢唐，聞之，遣板授嵊征東將軍，加秩中二千石。
entries.en: The Prince of Shaoling had fled east to Qiantang; hearing of it he sent a commission appointing Sheng General Who Pacifies the East with rank equal to two thousand shi.
entries.literal: At the time the Prince of Shaoling had fled east to Qiantang; hearing of it he sent a commission appointing Sheng General Who Pacifies the East with rank equal to two thousand shi.

entries.zh: 嵊曰：「朝廷危迫，天子蒙塵，今日何情，復受榮號。」
entries.en: Sheng said, "The court is in peril and the Son of Heaven suffers dust—what heart today for glory and title."
entries.literal: Sheng said: "The court is in peril and the Son of Heaven suffers dust—what heart today for receiving glory and title."

entries.zh: 留板而已。
entries.en: He kept the commission only.
entries.literal: He kept the commission only.

entries.zh: 賊行台劉神茂攻破義興，遣使說嵊曰：「若早降附，當還以郡相處，復加爵賞。」
entries.en: The bandit field headquarters Liu Shenmao took Yixing and sent a messenger persuading Sheng, "If you surrender early, you will be returned the commandery to govern and receive enfeoffment and reward."
entries.literal: The bandit's field headquarters Liu Shenmao took Yixing and sent a messenger persuading Sheng: "If you surrender early, you will be returned the commandery to govern and further receive enfeoffment and reward."

entries.zh: 嵊命斬其使，仍遣軍主王雄等帥兵於鱧瀆逆擊之，破神茂，神茂退走。
entries.en: Sheng ordered the messenger beheaded and sent commander Wang Xiong and others to meet the attack at Lüdu, defeated Shenmao, and Shenmao retreated.
entries.literal: Sheng ordered the messenger beheaded and sent the commander Wang Xiong and others with troops to meet the attack at Lüdu, defeated Shenmao, and Shenmao retreated.

entries.zh: 侯景聞神茂敗，乃遣其中軍侯子鑒帥精兵二萬人，助神茂以擊嵊。
entries.en: Hou Jing heard Shenmao was defeated and sent his central army Hou Zijian with twenty thousand crack troops to help Shenmao attack Sheng.
entries.literal: Hou Jing heard Shenmao was defeated and sent his central army Hou Zijian with twenty thousand crack troops to help Shenmao attack Sheng.

entries.zh: 嵊遣軍主范智朗出郡西拒戰，爲神茂所敗，退歸。
entries.en: Sheng sent commander Fan Zhilang west of the commandery to meet battle, was defeated by Shenmao, and withdrew.
entries.literal: Sheng sent the commander Fan Zhilang west of the commandery to meet battle, was defeated by Shenmao, and withdrew.

entries.zh: 賊騎乘勝焚柵，柵內衆軍皆土崩。
entries.en: The bandit cavalry pressed the victory and burned the palisade; troops within the palisade all collapsed.
entries.literal: The bandit cavalry pressed the victory and burned the palisade; troops within the palisade all collapsed.

entries.zh: 嵊乃釋戎服，坐於聽事，賊臨之以刃，終不爲屈。
entries.en: Sheng put off military dress and sat in the audience hall; the bandit held blades to him and he was never bent.
entries.literal: Sheng then put off military dress and sat in the audience hall; the bandit held blades to him and he was never bent.

entries.zh: 乃執嵊以送景，景刑之於都市，子弟同遇害者十餘人，時年六十二。
entries.en: They seized Sheng and sent him to Jing; Jing executed him in the market, and sons and brothers who suffered with him numbered more than ten—he was sixty-two.
entries.literal: They seized Sheng and sent him to Jing; Jing executed him in the market, and sons and younger brothers who suffered with him numbered more than ten—he was sixty-two.

entries.zh: 賊平，世祖追贈侍中、中衛將軍、開府儀同三司。
entries.en: When the bandit was pacified Emperor Shizu posthumously made him palace attendant, central army commander, and Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon with the rites of the Three Excellencies.
entries.literal: When the bandit was pacified the Shizu Emperor posthumously made him palace attendant, central army commander, and Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon with the same rites as the Three Excellencies.

entries.zh: 諡曰忠貞子。
entries.en: His posthumous title was Loyal and Upright.
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Loyal and Upright.

entries.zh: 中大同十一年，遷通直散騎常侍，未拜，出爲持節、督衡州諸軍事、安遠將軍、衡州刺史。
entries.en: In the eleventh year of Zhongdatong he was promoted to regular palace attendant for direct communication, did not take office, and went out as bearer of the staff, commander of Hengzhou military affairs, General of Peaceful Distance, and inspector of Hengzhou.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhongdatong he was promoted to regular palace attendant for direct communication, did not take office, and went out as bearer of the staff, commander of military affairs in Hengzhou, General of Peaceful Distance, and inspector of Hengzhou.

entries.zh: 皇太子出餞新亭，執粲手曰：「與卿不爲久別。」
entries.en: The crown prince came out to Xinting to see him off and took his hand, saying, "With you it will not be a long parting."
entries.literal: The crown prince came out to Xinting to see him off and took Can's hand, saying: "With you it will not be a long parting."

entries.zh: 太清元年，粲至州無幾，便表解職。
entries.en: In the first year of Supreme Purity Can had barely reached his post when he memorialized to resign.
entries.literal: In the first year of Supreme Purity Can had been at his post only a short time when he memorialized to resign.

entries.zh: 二年，徵爲散騎常侍。
entries.en: In the second year he was summoned as regular palace attendant.
entries.literal: In the second year he was summoned as regular palace attendant.

entries.zh: 粲還至廬陵，聞侯景作逆，便簡閱部下，得精卒五千，馬百匹，倍道赴援。
entries.en: Can returned as far as Luling, heard Hou Jing had rebelled, reviewed his men, gathered five thousand picked troops and a hundred horses, and hurried to the rescue by forced marches.
entries.literal: Can returned as far as Luling, heard that Hou Jing had rebelled, reviewed his subordinates, got five thousand picked troops and a hundred horses, and hurried by forced marches to the rescue.

entries.zh: 至豫章，奉命報云「賊已出橫江」，粲卽就內史劉孝儀共謀之。
entries.en: Reaching Yuzhang he received orders reporting, "The bandits have already crossed Hengjiang," and at once went to interior minister Liu Xiaoyi to plan.
entries.literal: Reaching Yuzhang he received orders reporting "the bandit has already crossed Hengjiang," and Can at once went to the interior minister Liu Xiaoyi to plan together.

entries.zh: 孝儀曰：「必期如此，當有別敕。
entries.en: Xiaoyi said, "If it must be so, there should be a separate edict.
entries.literal: Xiaoyi said: "If it must be so, there should be a separate edict.

entries.zh: 豈可輕信單使，妄相驚動，或恐不然。」
entries.en: How can we lightly trust a lone messenger and rashly stir alarm—perhaps it is not so after all."
entries.literal: How can we lightly trust a lone messenger and rashly stir alarm—perhaps it is not so after all."

entries.zh: 時孝儀置酒，粲怒，以杯抵地曰：「賊已渡江，便逼宮闕，水陸俱斷，何暇有報；
entries.en: Xiaoyi was setting out wine; Can in anger dashed his cup to the ground and said, "The bandit has crossed the river and presses on the palace gates; land and water are both cut—what leisure is there for reports;
entries.literal: At the time Xiaoyi was setting out wine; Can in anger dashed his cup to the ground and said: "The bandit has crossed the river and presses on the palace gates; land and water routes are both cut—what leisure is there for reports;

entries.zh: 假令無敕，豈得自安？
entries.en: even if there were no edict, how could one rest at ease?
entries.literal: even if there were no edict, how could one rest at ease?

entries.zh: 韋粲今日何情飲酒！」
entries.en: What heart has Wei Can today for drinking wine!"
entries.literal: What heart has Wei Can today for drinking wine!"

entries.zh: 卽馳馬出，部分將發，會江州刺史當陽公大心遣使要粲，粲乃馳往見大心曰：「上游蕃鎮，江州去京最近，殿下情計，實宜在前；
entries.en: He galloped out and arrayed his forces to march, when the Duke of Dangyang, Daxin, governor of Jiangzhou, summoned him; Can galloped to Daxin and said, "The garrison towns upriver are the realm's bulwarks; Jiangzhou is nearest the capital—in intent Your Highness should go first;
entries.literal: He at once galloped out, arrayed his forces to march, when the Duke of Dangyang, Daxin, governor of Jiangzhou, sent a messenger summoning Can; Can galloped to see Daxin and said: "The garrison towns upriver are the realm's bulwarks; Jiangzhou is nearest the capital—in intent Your Highness should surely go first;

entries.zh: 但中流任重，當須應接，不可闕鎮。
entries.en: but the midstream burden is weighty and must be met—one cannot leave the garrison vacant.
entries.literal: but the midstream burden is weighty and must be met—one cannot leave the garrison vacant.

entries.zh: 今直且張聲勢，移鎮湓城，遣偏將賜隨，於事便足。」
entries.en: For now simply raise a great clamor and shift the garrison to Pencheng; send a subordinate general to follow—that will suffice."
entries.literal: For now simply raise a great clamor and shift the garrison to Pencheng; send a subordinate general to follow—that will suffice for affairs."

entries.zh: 大心然之，遣中兵柳昕帥兵二千人隨粲。
entries.en: Daxin agreed and sent middle army officer Liu Xin with two thousand troops to follow Can.
entries.literal: Daxin agreed and sent the middle army officer Liu Xin with two thousand troops to follow Can.

entries.zh: 粲悉留家累於江州，以輕舸就路。
entries.en: Can left all his family in Jiangzhou and took light boats on the road.
entries.literal: Can left all his family dependents in Jiangzhou and took light boats on the road.

entries.zh: 至南州，粲外弟司州刺史柳仲禮亦帥步騎萬餘人至橫江，粲卽送糧仗贍給之，並散私金帛以賞其戰士。
entries.en: Reaching South Prefecture, his cousin by marriage, Sizhou inspector Liu Zhongli, also led more than ten thousand foot and horse to Hengjiang; Can sent grain and weapons to supply him and distributed private gold and silk to reward his warriors.
entries.literal: Reaching South Prefecture, his cousin by marriage, Inspector of Sizhou Liu Zhongli, also led more than ten thousand foot and horse to Hengjiang; Can at once sent grain and weapons to supply him and distributed private gold and silk to reward his warriors.

entries.zh: 先是，安北將軍鄱陽王範亦自合肥遣西豫州刺史裴之高與其長子嗣，帥江西之衆赴京師，屯於張公洲，待上流諸軍至。
entries.en: Earlier Pacifying North General, the Prince of Poyang Fan, had from Hefei sent Western Yuzhou inspector Pei Zhigao with his eldest son Si, leading Jiangxi forces toward the capital, encamped at Zhanggong Isle, waiting for upriver armies.
entries.literal: Earlier the Pacifying North General, the Prince of Poyang Fan, had also from Hefei sent Western Yuzhou Inspector Pei Zhigao with his eldest son Si, leading the Jiangxi forces toward the capital, encamped at Zhanggong Isle, waiting for the upriver armies to arrive.

entries.zh: 是時，之高遣船渡仲禮，與合軍進屯王游苑。
entries.en: Zhigao sent boats to ferry Zhongli; they united and advanced to encamp at Wang You Park.
entries.literal: At that time Zhigao sent boats to ferry Zhongli; they united and advanced to encamp at Wang You Park.

entries.zh: 粲建議推仲禮爲大都督，報下流衆軍。
entries.en: Can proposed making Zhongli grand commander and reported this to the downstream armies.
entries.literal: Can proposed making Zhongli grand commander and reporting this to the downstream armies.

entries.zh: 裴之高自以年位恥居其下，乃云：「柳節下是州將，何須我復鞭板？」
entries.en: Pei Zhigao, ashamed to stand below him in age and rank, said, "Master Liu the prefect is a provincial commander—why need I again wield the whip and board?"
entries.literal: Pei Zhigao, ashamed to stand below him in age and rank, said: "Master Liu the prefect is a provincial commander—why need I again wield the whip and board?"

entries.zh: 累日不決。
entries.en: For days no decision was reached.
entries.literal: For days no decision was reached.

entries.zh: 粲乃抗言於衆曰：「今者同赴國難，義在除賊，所以推柳司州者，政以久捍邊疆，先爲侯景所憚；
entries.en: Can then spoke firmly before the assembly, "Today we share the state's peril; righteousness lies in destroying the bandit—therefore we propose Liu the Sizhou inspector, because he has long defended the frontier and Hou Jing fears him first;
entries.literal: Can then spoke firmly before the assembly: "Today we share in the state's peril; righteousness lies in destroying the bandit—therefore we propose Liu the inspector of Sizhou, because he has long defended the frontier and Hou Jing fears him first;

entries.zh: 且士馬精銳，無出其前。
entries.en: moreover his troops and horses are elite, none surpass him.
entries.literal: moreover his troops and horses are elite, none surpass him.

entries.zh: 若論位次，柳在粲下；
entries.en: If we speak of rank, Liu stands below Can;
entries.literal: If we speak of rank, Liu stands below Can;

entries.zh: 語其年齒，亦少於粲，直以社稷之計，不得復論。
entries.en: if we speak of years, he is younger than Can too—only for the altars' sake we cannot argue further.
entries.literal: if we speak of years, he is younger than Can too—only for the altars' sake we cannot argue further.

entries.zh: 今日形勢，貴在將和；
entries.en: Today's situation values generals in harmony;
entries.literal: Today's situation values generals in harmony;

entries.zh: 若人心不同，大事去矣。
entries.en: if hearts differ, the great affair is lost.
entries.literal: if hearts differ, the great affair is lost.

entries.zh: 裴公朝之舊齒，年德已隆，豈應復挾私情，以沮大計。
entries.en: Lord Pei is a court elder in age and virtue—surely he should not indulge private feeling and thwart the great plan.
entries.literal: Lord Pei is an elder of the court in age and virtue—surely he should not again indulge private feeling and thwart the great plan.

entries.zh: 粲請爲諸君解釋之。」
entries.en: Can asks to explain this for you all."
entries.literal: Can asks to explain this for you all."

entries.zh: 乃單舸至之高營，切讓之曰：「前諸將之議，豫州意所未同，卽二宮危逼，猾寇滔天，臣子當戮力同心，豈可自相矛盾！
entries.en: He took a lone boat to Zhigao's camp and reproached him sharply, "The generals' councils did not accord with Lord Yuzhou's intent—yet the two palaces are in peril and the cunning bandit floods heaven; ministers should join strength—how can we contradict one another!
entries.literal: He took a lone boat to Zhigao's camp and reproached him sharply: "The earlier councils of the generals did not accord with Lord Yuzhou's intent—yet the two palaces are in peril and the cunning bandit floods heaven; ministers should join strength in one heart—how can we contradict one another!

entries.zh: 豫州必欲立異，鋒鏑便有所歸。」
entries.en: If Lord Yuzhou insists on standing apart, blades and arrows will have their target."
entries.literal: If Lord Yuzhou insists on standing apart, blades and arrows will have their target."

entries.zh: 之高垂泣曰：「吾荷國恩榮，自應帥先士卒，顧恨衰老，不能效命，企望柳使君共平凶逆，謂衆議已從，無俟老夫耳。
entries.en: Zhigao wept and said, "I have received the state's grace and should lead the van; I regret my old age and cannot devote my life, and hoped to look to Master Liu to pacify the villain together—I thought the assembly had agreed and had no need of this old man.
entries.literal: Zhigao wept and said: "I have received the state's grace and glory and should myself lead the van; I regret my old age and cannot devote my life, and hoped to look to Master Liu the inspector to pacify the villain together—I thought the assembly had already agreed and had no need of this old man.

entries.zh: 若必有疑，當剖心相示。」
entries.en: If there must be doubt, I will lay open my heart."
entries.literal: If there must be doubt, I will lay open my heart."

entries.zh: 於是諸將定議，仲禮方得進軍。
entries.en: Then the generals fixed their plan and Zhongli was able to advance.
entries.literal: Then the generals fixed their plan and Zhongli was able to advance the army.

entries.zh: 粲長子臧，字君理。
entries.en: Can's eldest son Zang, styled Junli.
entries.literal: Can's eldest son Zang, styled Junli.

entries.zh: 歷官尚書三公郎、太子洗馬、東宮領直。
entries.en: He held posts as gentleman in the three excellencies bureau, crown prince steward, and commander of the Eastern Palace guard.
entries.literal: He held posts as gentleman in the three excellencies bureau, crown prince steward, and commander of the Eastern Palace guard.

entries.zh: 侯景至，帥兵屯西華門。
entries.en: When Hou Jing arrived he led troops to garrison the Western Splendid Gate.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing arrived he led troops to garrison the Western Splendid Gate.

entries.zh: 城陷，奔江州，收舊部曲，據豫章，爲其部下所害。
entries.en: When the city fell he fled to Jiangzhou, gathered his old command, held Yuzhang, and was killed by his subordinates.
entries.literal: When the city fell he fled to Jiangzhou, gathered his old command, held Yuzhang, and was killed by his subordinates.

entries.zh: 浚少博學，有才幹，歷山陰、吳、建康令，並有能名。
entries.en: Jun from youth was broadly learned and gifted; he held Shanyin, Wu, and Jiankang in succession, all with a name for ability.
entries.literal: Jun from youth was broadly learned and gifted in affairs; he held the magistracies of Shanyin, Wu, and Jiankang in succession, all with a name for ability.

entries.zh: 入爲中書郎、尚書左丞。
entries.en: He entered court as Secretariat gentleman and left assistant.
entries.literal: He entered court as gentleman of the Secretariat and left assistant.

entries.zh: 侯景逼京城，遷御史中丞。
entries.en: When Hou Jing pressed the capital he was promoted to censor-in-chief.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing pressed the capital he was promoted to censor-in-chief.

entries.zh: 是時外援並至，侯景表請求和，詔許之。
entries.en: Outside aid all arrived; Hou Jing memorialized asking for peace and an edict granted it.
entries.literal: At that time outside aid all arrived; Hou Jing memorialized asking for peace and an edict granted it.

entries.zh: 旣盟，景知城內疾疫，復懷奸計，遲疑不去。
entries.en: After the oath Jing knew plague raged within the city and again harbored treacherous design, hesitating and not leaving.
entries.literal: After the oath Jing knew plague raged within the city and again harbored treacherous design, hesitating and not leaving.
