entries.zh: 數日，皇太子令浚詣景所，景曰：「卽已向熱，非復行時。
entries.en: After several days the crown prince ordered Jun to Jing's quarters; Jing said, "It has already turned hot—not the season for marching again.
entries.literal: After several days the crown prince ordered Jun to Jing's quarters; Jing said: "It has already turned hot—not the season for marching again.

entries.zh: 十萬之衆，何由可去，還欲立效朝廷，君可見爲申聞。」
entries.en: A host of a hundred thousand—how could they go? I wish again to serve the court; you may report this for me."
entries.literal: A host of a hundred thousand—how could they go? I wish again to render service to the court; you may report this for me."

entries.zh: 浚曰：「將軍此論，意在得城。
entries.en: Jun said, "General, this talk aims at getting the city.
entries.literal: Jun said: "General, this talk of yours aims at getting the city.

entries.zh: 城內兵糧，尚支百日。
entries.en: Within the city troops and grain still last a hundred days.
entries.literal: Within the city troops and grain still last a hundred days.

entries.zh: 將軍儲積內盡，國家援軍外集，十萬之衆，將何所資？
entries.en: General, your stores within are exhausted and rescue armies gather without—a host of a hundred thousand, on what will they rely?
entries.literal: General, your stores within are exhausted and the state's rescue armies gather without—a host of a hundred thousand, on what will they rely?

entries.zh: 而反設此言，欲脅朝廷邪？」
entries.en: Yet you set forth this talk—do you mean to coerce the court?"
entries.literal: Yet you set forth this talk—do you mean to coerce the court?"

entries.zh: 景橫刃於膝，暿真目叱之。
entries.en: Jing laid a blade across his knee, glared angrily, and shouted at him.
entries.literal: Jing laid a blade across his knee and glared angrily and shouted at him.

entries.zh: 浚正色責景曰：「明公親是人臣，舉兵向闕，聖主申恩赦過，已共結盟，口血未乾，而有翻背。
entries.en: Jun in stern color rebuked Jing, "Your Grace is plainly a minister who raised troops against the palace; the sage ruler pardoned past faults and you have sworn alliance—oath blood not yet dry, yet there is treachery.
entries.literal: Jun in stern color rebuked Jing: "Your Grace is plainly a minister who raised troops against the palace; the sage ruler extended grace and pardoned past faults, and you have already sworn alliance—oath blood not yet dry, yet there is treachery.

entries.zh: 沈浚六十之年，且天子之使，死生有命，豈畏逆臣之刀乎！」
entries.en: Shen Jun is sixty and the Son of Heaven's envoy—life and death have their allotment; how would I fear a traitor's blade!"
entries.literal: Shen Jun is sixty years old and moreover the Son of Heaven's envoy—life and death have their allotment; how would I fear a traitor's blade!"

entries.zh: 不顧而出。
entries.en: Without a glance he went out.
entries.literal: Without a glance he went out.

entries.zh: 景曰：「是真司直也。」
entries.en: Jing said, "This is a true upright censor."
entries.literal: Jing said: "This is a true upright censor."

entries.zh: 然密銜之。
entries.en: Yet he secretly harbored resentment.
entries.literal: Yet he secretly harbored resentment.

entries.zh: 及破張嵊，乃求浚以害之。
entries.en: When Zhang Sheng was defeated he asked for Jun to kill him.
entries.literal: When Zhang Sheng was defeated he asked for Jun to kill him.

entries.zh: 敬禮與兄仲禮，皆少以勇烈知名。
entries.en: Jingli and his elder brother Zhongli were both famed from youth for fierce courage.
entries.literal: Jingli and his elder brother Zhongli were both famed from youth for fierce courage.

entries.zh: 起家著作佐郎，稍遷扶風太守。
entries.en: He began as gentleman of the Palace Library and rose to magistrate of Fufeng.
entries.literal: He began office as gentleman of the Palace Library and was gradually promoted to magistrate of Fufeng.

entries.zh: 侯景渡江，敬禮率馬步三千赴援。
entries.en: When Hou Jing crossed the river Jingli led three thousand horse and foot to the rescue.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing crossed the river Jingli led three thousand horse and foot to the rescue.

entries.zh: 至都，據青溪埭，與景頻戰，恒先登陷陳，甚著威名。
entries.en: Reaching the capital he held Qingxi Ford and fought Jing repeatedly, always first to scale and break the line, winning great renown.
entries.literal: Reaching the capital he held Qingxi Ford and fought Jing repeatedly, always first to scale and break the line, winning great renown for martial awe.

entries.zh: 台城沒，敬禮與仲禮俱見於景，景遣仲禮經略上流，留敬禮爲質，以爲護軍。
entries.en: When the terrace city fell Jingli and Zhongli both appeared before Jing; Jing sent Zhongli upriver and kept Jingli as hostage, making him General Who Guards the Army.
entries.literal: When the terrace city fell Jingli and Zhongli both appeared before Jing; Jing sent Zhongli to command the upriver region and kept Jingli as hostage, making him General Who Guards the Army.

entries.zh: 景餞仲禮於後渚，敬禮密謂仲禮曰：「景今來會，敬禮抱之，兄拔佩刀，便可斫殺，敬禮死亦無所恨。」
entries.en: Jing saw Zhongli off at Rear Ford; Jingli secretly said to Zhongli, "Jing comes to this meeting—Jingli will embrace him; brother, draw your sword and you can cut him down; Jingli dies without regret."
entries.literal: Jing saw Zhongli off at Rear Ford; Jingli secretly said to Zhongli: "Jing comes to this meeting today—Jingli will embrace him; brother, draw your sword and you can cut him down; Jingli dies without regret."

entries.zh: 仲禮壯其言，許之。
entries.en: Zhongli admired his words and agreed.
entries.literal: Zhongli admired his words and agreed.

entries.zh: 及酒數行，敬禮目仲禮，仲禮見備衛嚴，不敢動，計遂不果。
entries.en: When cups had gone round several times Jingli signaled Zhongli; Zhongli saw the guards strict and dared not move—the plan did not succeed.
entries.literal: When cups had gone round several times Jingli signaled Zhongli; Zhongli saw the guards strict and dared not move—the plan in the end did not succeed.

entries.zh: 會景征晉熙，敬禮與南康王會理共謀襲其城，剋期將發，建安侯蕭賁知而告之，遂遇害。
entries.en: When Jing campaigned against Jinxing Jingli with the Prince of Nankang Huili plotted to seize his city; the day fixed they were about to rise when the Marquis of Jian'an Xiao Ben reported it, and he was killed.
entries.literal: When Jing campaigned against Jinxing Jingli with the Prince of Nankang Huili plotted to seize his city; the day fixed they were about to rise when the Marquis of Jian'an Xiao Ben learned and reported it, and he was killed.

entries.zh: 江子一字元貞，濟陽考城人，晉散騎常侍統之七世孫也。
entries.en: Jiang Ziyi, styled Yuanchen, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang, seventh-generation descendant of Jin's regular palace attendant Tong.
entries.literal: Jiang Ziyi, styled Yuanchen, was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang, seventh-generation descendant of Regular Palace Attendant Tong under Jin.

entries.zh: 父法成，天監中奉朝請。
entries.en: His father Facheng had been a court gentleman in attendance under Heavenly Surveillance.
entries.literal: His father Facheng had been a court gentleman in attendance under Heavenly Surveillance.

entries.zh: 子一少好學，有志操，以家貧闕養，因蔬食終身。
entries.en: Ziyi from youth loved learning and had resolve; because his family was poor he ate vegetables all his life.
entries.literal: Ziyi from youth loved learning and had resolve; because his family was poor and could not support him, he ate vegetables all his life.

entries.zh: 起家王國侍郎、朝請。
entries.en: He began as gentleman in a princely kingdom and court gentleman in attendance.
entries.literal: He began office as gentleman in a princely kingdom and court gentleman in attendance.

entries.zh: 啓求觀書秘閣，高祖許之，有敕直華林省。
entries.en: He memorialized to view books in the secret archive; the Founding Emperor granted it and ordered him to attend directly at the Orchard of Splendor.
entries.literal: He memorialized asking to view books in the secret archive; the Founding Emperor granted it and issued an edict that he attend directly at the Orchard of Splendor.

entries.zh: 其姑夫右衛將軍朱异，權要當朝，休下之日，賓客輻湊，子一未嘗造門，其高潔如此。
entries.en: His uncle by marriage, Right Guard Zhu Yi, held power; on days off guests crowded in—but Ziyi never came to his gate; such was his lofty purity.
entries.literal: His uncle by marriage, Right Guard General Zhu Yi, held power in his day; on his days off guests crowded in—but Ziyi never once came to his gate; such was his lofty purity.

entries.zh: 稍遷尚書儀曹郎，出爲遂昌、曲阿令，皆著美績。
entries.en: He rose to gentleman in the ritual bureau, went out as magistrate of Suichang and Qu'a, and in both showed fine achievement.
entries.literal: He was gradually promoted to gentleman in the ritual bureau of the Secretariat, went out as magistrate of Suichang and Qu'a, and in both showed fine achievement.

entries.zh: 除通直散騎侍郎，出爲戎昭將軍、南津校尉。
entries.en: He was made regular palace attendant for direct communication, went out as General of Martial Proclamation and colonel of the southern ford.
entries.literal: He was made regular palace attendant for direct communication, went out as General of Martial Proclamation and colonel of the southern ford.

entries.zh: 弟子四，歷尚書金部郎。
entries.en: His younger brother Zisi had held gentleman in the treasury bureau of gold.
entries.literal: His younger brother Zisi had held the post of gentleman in the treasury bureau of gold.

entries.zh: 大同初，遷右丞。
entries.en: At the opening of Great Unity he was promoted to right assistant.
entries.literal: At the opening of Great Unity he was promoted to right assistant.

entries.zh: 兄弟性並剛烈。
entries.en: The brothers were all fierce by nature.
entries.literal: The brothers were all fierce by nature.

entries.zh: 子四自右丞上封事，極言得失，高祖甚善之，詔尚書詳擇施行焉。
entries.en: From his post as right assistant Zisi submitted a memorial on gains and losses; the Founding Emperor greatly approved and ordered the Secretariat to examine and carry out what was fit.
entries.literal: From his post as right assistant Zisi submitted a memorial stating gains and losses to the full; the Founding Emperor greatly approved and ordered the Secretariat to examine and carry out what was fit.

entries.zh: 左民郎沈炯、少府丞顧璵嘗奏事不允，高祖厲色呵責之；
entries.en: Left People Gentleman Shen Jiong and junior palace supplies aide Gu Yu once memorialized without approval; the Founding Emperor shouted and rebuked them in anger;
entries.literal: Left People Gentleman Shen Jiong and junior palace supplies aide Gu Yu once memorialized on affairs without approval; the Founding Emperor in anger shouted and rebuked them;

entries.zh: 子四乃趨前代炯等對，言甚激切，高祖怒呼縛之，子四據地不受，高祖怒亦止，乃釋之。
entries.en: Zisi hurried forward to answer for Jiong and the rest in fierce words; the Founding Emperor ordered him bound; Zisi sat on the ground and would not submit; the emperor's anger ceased and he released him.
entries.literal: Zisi then hurried forward to answer for Jiong and the rest in words very fierce; the Founding Emperor in rage ordered him bound; Zisi sat on the ground and would not submit; the Founding Emperor's anger also ceased, and he released him.

entries.zh: 猶坐免職。
entries.en: He was still demoted and removed from office.
entries.literal: He was still demoted and removed from office.

entries.zh: 韋粲 江子一 弟子四 子五 張嵊 沈浚 柳敬禮
entries.en: Wei Can; Jiang Ziyi; his younger brothers Zisi and Ziwu; Zhang Sheng; Shen Jun; Liu Jingli
entries.literal: Wei Can; Jiang Ziyi; younger brother Zisi; younger brother Ziwu; Zhang Sheng; Shen Jun; Liu Jingli

entries.zh: 史臣曰：若夫義重於生，前典垂誥，斯蓋先哲之所貴也。
entries.en: The historian writes: When righteousness outweighs life, former canons leave instruction—this is what the sages prized.
entries.literal: The historian says: When righteousness outweighs life, former canons leave instruction—this is what the sages prized.

entries.zh: 故孟子稱生者我所欲，義亦我所欲，二事必不可兼得，寧捨生而取義。
entries.en: Thus Mencius said life is what I desire and righteousness is also what I desire; the two cannot be grasped together—I would rather relinquish life and take righteousness.
entries.literal: Thus Mencius said life is what I desire and righteousness is also what I desire; the two cannot be grasped together—I would rather relinquish life and take righteousness.

entries.zh: 至如張嵊二三子之徒，捐軀殉節，赴死如歸，英風勁氣，籠罩今古，君子知梁代之有忠臣焉。
entries.en: Men such as Zhang Sheng and the two or three like him gave their bodies and died for integrity, going to death like returning home—their heroic wind and firm spirit cover past and present; the gentleman knows the Liang had loyal ministers.
entries.literal: As for men such as Zhang Sheng and the two or three like him, who gave their bodies and died for integrity, going to death like returning home—their heroic wind and firm spirit cover past and present; the gentleman knows the Liang had loyal ministers.

entries.zh: 梁書卷第四十三 列傳第三十七
entries.en: Book of Liang, Volume 43, Biography 37
entries.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 43, Biography 37

entries.zh: 太宗十一王 世祖二子
entries.en: The eleven sons of Heir Apparent Taizong; the two sons of Emperor Shizu
entries.literal: The eleven sons of the Heir Apparent Taizong; the two sons of Emperor Shizu

entries.zh: 世祖諸男：徐妃生忠壯世子方等，王夫人生貞惠世子方諸，其愍懷太子方矩
entries.en: Emperor Shizu's sons: Lady Xu bore Loyal and Upright Heir Fang Deng; Lady Wang bore Upright and Gracious Heir Fang Zhu; Lamented and Cherished Crown Prince Fang Ju
entries.literal: The sons of Emperor Shizu: Lady Xu bore the Loyal and Upright Heir Fang Deng; Lady Wang bore the Upright and Gracious Heir Fang Zhu; the Lamented and Cherished Crown Prince Fang Ju

entries.zh: 〈（本書不載所生，別有傳）〉，
entries.en: (His birth mother is not recorded in this book; he has a separate biography.)
entries.literal: (his birth mother is not recorded in this book; he has a separate biography)〉

entries.zh: 夏賢妃生敬皇帝。
entries.en: Lady Xia the Worthy bore Emperor Jing.
entries.literal: Lady Xia the Worthy bore Emperor Jing.

entries.zh: 自餘諸子，並本書無傳。
entries.en: The remaining sons have no biography in this book.
entries.literal: The remaining sons all have no biography in this book.

entries.zh: 忠壯世子方等，字實相，世祖長子也。
entries.en: Loyal and Upright Heir Fang Deng, styled Shixiang, was Emperor Shizu's eldest son.
entries.literal: The Loyal and Upright Heir Fang Deng, courtesy name Shixiang, was the eldest son of Emperor Shizu.

entries.zh: 母曰徐妃。
entries.en: His mother was Lady Xu.
entries.literal: His mother was Lady Xu.

entries.zh: 少聰敏，有俊才，善騎射，尤長巧思。
entries.en: From youth clever and keen, with outstanding talent, skilled at riding and shooting, especially gifted in ingenious design.
entries.literal: From youth clever and keen, with outstanding talent, skilled at riding and shooting, especially gifted in ingenious design.

entries.zh: 性愛林泉，特好散逸。
entries.en: By nature he loved forests and springs and favored untrammeled wandering.
entries.literal: By nature he loved forests and springs and especially favored untrammeled wandering.

entries.zh: 嘗著論曰：「人生處世，如白駒過隙耳。
entries.en: He once wrote, "Life in the world is like a white colt crossing a crack.
entries.literal: He once composed a discourse saying: "Life in the world is like a white colt crossing a crack.

entries.zh: 一壺之酒，足以養性；
entries.en: One jug of wine is enough to nurture the nature;
entries.literal: One jug of wine is enough to nurture the nature;

entries.zh: 一簞之食，足以怡形。
entries.en: one basket of food is enough to delight the form.
entries.literal: one basket of food is enough to delight the form.

entries.zh: 生在蓬蒿，死葬溝壑，瓦棺石槨，何以異茲？
entries.en: Born among weeds, buried in ditches—how do tile coffin and stone outer coffin differ?
entries.literal: Born among weeds, buried in ditches—how do tile coffin and stone outer coffin differ from this?

entries.zh: 吾嘗夢爲魚，因化爲鳥。
entries.en: I once dreamed I was a fish and then became a bird.
entries.literal: I once dreamed I was a fish and then transformed into a bird.

entries.zh: 當其夢也，何樂如之；
entries.en: While dreaming, what joy could match it;
entries.literal: While dreaming, what joy could match it;

entries.zh: 及其覺也，何憂斯類；
entries.en: when I awoke, what sorrow of that kind;
entries.literal: when I awoke, what sorrow of that kind;

entries.zh: 良由吾之不及魚鳥者，遠矣。
entries.en: truly because I fall far short of fish and birds.
entries.literal: truly because I fall far short of fish and birds.

entries.zh: 故魚鳥飛浮，任其志性；
entries.en: Thus fish and birds fly and float, following their nature and will;
entries.literal: Thus fish and birds fly and float, following their nature and will;

entries.zh: 吾之進退，恒存掌握。
entries.en: my advance and retreat always rest in another's grasp.
entries.literal: my advance and retreat always rest in another's grasp.

entries.zh: 舉手懼觸，搖足恐墮。
entries.en: Raising a hand I fear to touch; moving a foot I fear to fall.
entries.literal: Raising a hand I fear to touch; moving a foot I fear to fall.

entries.zh: 若使吾終得與魚鳥同遊，則去人間如脫屣耳。」
entries.en: If I could roam with fish and birds at last, leaving the human world would be like doffing shoes."
entries.literal: If I could at last roam with fish and birds, leaving the human world would be like doffing shoes."

entries.zh: 初，徐妃以嫉妒失寵，方等意不自安。
entries.en: Earlier Lady Xu had lost favor through jealousy; Fang Deng felt ill at ease.
entries.literal: Earlier Lady Xu had lost favor through jealousy; Fang Deng felt ill at ease.

entries.zh: 世祖聞之，又惡方等，方等益懼，故述論以申其志焉。
entries.en: Shizu heard and also disliked Fang Deng; he grew more afraid and set forth this discourse to declare his intent.
entries.literal: Emperor Shizu heard and also disliked Fang Deng; Fang Deng grew more afraid and therefore set forth this discourse to declare his intent.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：太宗、世祖諸子，雖開土宇，運屬亂離；
entries.en: The historian writes: The sons of Taizong and Shizu, though they opened territories, met chaos and separation;
entries.literal: The historian says: The sons of the Heir Apparent Taizong and Emperor Shizu, though they opened territories, met a time of chaos and separation;

entries.zh: 旣拘寇賊，多殞非命。
entries.en: once seized by bandits, most died untimely deaths.
entries.literal: once seized by bandits, most died untimely deaths.

entries.zh: 籲！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 可嗟矣。
entries.en: Lamentable indeed.
entries.literal: Lamentable indeed.

entries.zh: 會高祖欲見諸王長子，世祖遣方等入侍，方等欣然升舟，冀免憂辱。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor wished to see princes' eldest sons, Shizu sent Fang Deng to attend; he gladly boarded the boat, hoping to escape worry and disgrace.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor wished to see the eldest sons of the princes, Shizu sent Fang Deng to attend; Fang Deng gladly boarded the boat, hoping to escape worry and disgrace.

entries.zh: 行至繇水，值侯景亂，世祖召之，方等啓曰：「昔申生不愛其死，方等豈顧其生？」
entries.en: Reaching Yaoshui he met Hou Jing's rebellion; Shizu summoned him; Fang Deng memorialized, "Formerly Shensheng did not love his life—how would I cherish mine?"
entries.literal: Reaching Yaoshui he met Hou Jing's rebellion; Shizu summoned him; Fang Deng memorialized: "Formerly Shensheng did not love his life—how would Fang Deng cherish his?"

entries.zh: 世祖省書歎息，知無還意，乃配步騎一萬，使援京都。
entries.en: Shizu read the letter, sighed, knew he had no mind to return, and assigned him ten thousand foot and horse to relieve the capital.
entries.literal: Shizu read the letter, sighed, knew he had no mind to return, and assigned him ten thousand foot and horse to relieve the capital.

entries.zh: 賊每來攻，方等必身當矢石。
entries.en: Whenever the bandit attacked Fang Deng always met arrows and stones in person.
entries.literal: Whenever the bandit came to attack Fang Deng always met arrows and stones in person.

entries.zh: 宮城陷，方等歸荊州，收集士馬，甚得衆和，世祖始歎其能。
entries.en: When the palace city fell he returned to Jingzhou, gathered soldiers and horses, and won great harmony among the host—Shizu then sighed at his ability.
entries.literal: When the palace city fell Fang Deng returned to Jingzhou, gathered soldiers and horses, and won great harmony among the host—Shizu then sighed at his ability.

entries.zh: 方等又勸修築城柵，以備不虞。
entries.en: He also urged building walls and palisades against the unforeseen.
entries.literal: Fang Deng also urged building walls and palisades against the unforeseen.

entries.zh: 旣成，樓雉相望，周回七十餘里。
entries.en: When finished, towers and battlements faced one another for more than seventy li.
entries.literal: When finished, towers and battlements faced one another, the circuit more than seventy li.

entries.zh: 世祖觀之甚悅，入謂徐妃曰：「若更有一子如此，吾復何憂！」
entries.en: Shizu viewed it with great pleasure and said to Lady Xu, "If I had another son like this, what more would I worry about!"
entries.literal: Shizu viewed it with great pleasure, entered and said to Lady Xu: "If I had another son like this, what more would I worry about!"

entries.zh: 徐妃不答，垂泣而退。
entries.en: Lady Xu did not answer, wept, and withdrew.
entries.literal: Lady Xu did not answer, wept, and withdrew.

entries.zh: 世祖忿之，因疏其穢行，榜於大閣。
entries.en: Shizu in anger set forth her shameful conduct and posted it on the great gate.
entries.literal: Shizu in anger therefore set forth her shameful conduct and posted it on the great gate.

entries.zh: 方等入見，益以自危。
entries.en: Fang Deng came to audience and felt still more endangered.
entries.literal: Fang Deng came to audience and felt still more endangered.

entries.zh: 時河東王爲湘州刺史，不受督府之令，方等乃乞征之，世祖許焉。
entries.en: The Prince of Hedong was inspector of Xiangzhou and did not accept headquarters orders; Fang Deng begged to campaign against him and Shizu granted it.
entries.literal: At the time the Prince of Hedong was inspector of Xiangzhou and did not accept the headquarters' orders; Fang Deng begged to campaign against him and Shizu granted it.

entries.zh: 拜爲都督，令帥精卒二萬南討。
entries.en: He was made commander and ordered to lead twenty thousand picked troops south.
entries.literal: He was made commander and ordered to lead twenty thousand picked troops south to attack.

entries.zh: 方等臨行，謂所親曰：「吾此段出征，必死無二；
entries.en: Setting out he told those close to him, "On this campaign I shall surely die without second thought;
entries.literal: As Fang Deng set out he told those close to him: "On this campaign I shall surely die without second thought;

entries.zh: 死而獲所，吾豈愛生。」
entries.en: if in death I gain my aim, how would I love life."
entries.literal: if in death I gain my aim, how would I love life."

entries.zh: 及至麻溪，河東王率軍逆戰，方等擊之，軍敗，遂溺死，時年二十二。
entries.en: Reaching Maxi, the Prince of Hedong met him in battle; Fang Deng attacked; the army was defeated and he drowned at twenty-two.
entries.literal: Reaching Maxi, the Prince of Hedong led his army to meet battle; Fang Deng attacked; the army was defeated and he drowned; he was twenty-two.

entries.zh: 世祖聞之，不以爲慼。
entries.en: Shizu heard and did not grieve.
entries.literal: Shizu heard and did not grieve.

entries.zh: 後追思其才，贈侍中、中軍將軍、揚州刺史，諡曰忠壯世子，幷爲招魂以哀之。
entries.en: Later, recalling his talent, he posthumously made him palace attendant, central army commander, and inspector of Yangzhou, titled Loyal and Upright Heir, and performed a soul-summoning rite to mourn him.
entries.literal: Later, recalling his talent, he posthumously made him palace attendant, central army commander, and inspector of Yangzhou, titled Loyal and Upright Heir, and also performed a soul-summoning rite to mourn him.

entries.zh: 梁書卷第四十四 列傳第三十八
entries.en: Book of Liang, Volume 44, Biography 38
entries.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 44, Biography 38

entries.zh: 貞惠世子方諸，字智相，世祖第二子。
entries.en: Upright and Gracious Heir Fang Zhu, styled Zhixiang, was Shizu's second son.
entries.literal: The Upright and Gracious Heir Fang Zhu, courtesy name Zhixiang, was Emperor Shizu's second son.

entries.zh: 母王夫人。
entries.en: His mother was Lady Wang.
entries.literal: His mother was Lady Wang.

entries.zh: 幼聰警博學，明《老》、《易》，善談玄，風采清越，辭辯鋒生，特爲世祖所愛，母王氏又有寵。
entries.en: From youth clever and broadly learned, he understood the Laozi and Changes, was skilled in Dark Learning, clear in bearing, sharp in argument—especially loved by Shizu, and his mother Lady Wang also held favor.
entries.literal: From youth clever, alert, and broadly learned, he understood the Laozi and Changes, was skilled in Dark Learning discourse, his bearing clear and surpassing, his argument sharp as a blade—he was especially loved by Shizu, and his mother Lady Wang also held favor.

entries.zh: 及方等敗沒，世祖謂之曰：「不有所廢，其何以興。」
entries.en: When Fang Deng was destroyed Shizu said to him, "Without casting something aside, how can anything rise."
entries.literal: When Fang Deng was destroyed Shizu said to him: "Without casting something aside, how can anything rise."

entries.zh: 因拜爲中撫軍以自副，又出爲郢州刺史，鎮江夏，以鮑泉爲行事，防遏下流。
entries.en: He was made Pacifying Central Army as Shizu's deputy, went out as inspector of E, garrisoned Jiangxia, with Bao Quan as acting officer to block downstream.
entries.literal: He was made Pacifying Central Army as Shizu's deputy, went out as inspector of E prefecture, garrisoned Jiangxia, with Bao Quan as acting officer to block the downstream route.

entries.zh: 時世祖遣徐文盛督衆軍，與侯景將任約相持未決。
entries.en: Shizu sent Xu Wensheng to command armies in stalemate with Hou Jing's general Ren Yue.
entries.literal: At the time Shizu sent Xu Wensheng to command the armies in stalemate with Hou Jing's general Ren Yue.

entries.zh: 方諸恃文盛在近，不恤軍政，日與鮑泉蒲酒爲樂。
entries.en: Fang Zhu relied on Wensheng being near and neglected military affairs, daily drinking with Bao Quan.
entries.literal: Fang Zhu relied on Wensheng being near and did not tend military affairs, daily drinking and making merry with Bao Quan.

entries.zh: 侯景知之，乃遣其將宋子仙率輕騎數百，從間道襲之。
entries.en: Hou Jing learned of it and sent general Song Zixian with several hundred light horse by a bypath to strike.
entries.literal: Hou Jing learned of it and sent his general Song Zixian with several hundred light horse by a bypath to strike.

entries.zh: 屬風雨晦冥，子仙至，百姓奔告，方諸與鮑泉猶不信，曰：「徐文盛大軍在下，虜安得來？」
entries.en: Wind and rain darkened the sky; when Zixian arrived the people ran to report, yet Fang Zhu and Bao Quan still did not believe and said, "Xu Wensheng's great army is below—how could the barbarian come?"
entries.literal: Wind and rain made the sky dark; when Zixian arrived the people ran to report, yet Fang Zhu and Bao Quan still did not believe it and said: "Lord Xu Wensheng's great army is below—how could the barbarian come?"

entries.zh: 始命閉門，賊騎已入，城遂陷，子仙執方諸以歸。
entries.en: Only then were they ordered to shut the gate; bandit horse had already entered and the city fell; Zixian seized Fang Zhu and returned.
entries.literal: Only then were they ordered to shut the gate; the bandit horse had already entered and the city fell; Zixian seized Fang Zhu and returned.

entries.zh: 王僧辯軍至蔡洲，景遂害之。
entries.en: When Wang Sengbian's army reached Cai Isle, Jing killed him.
entries.literal: When Wang Sengbian's army reached Cai Isle, Jing then killed him.

entries.zh: 世祖追贈侍中、大將軍。
entries.en: Shizu posthumously made him palace attendant and grand general.
entries.literal: Shizu posthumously made him palace attendant and grand general.

entries.zh: 諡曰貞惠世子。
entries.en: His posthumous title was Upright and Gracious Heir.
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Upright and Gracious Heir.

entries.zh: 尋陽王大心字仁恕。
entries.en: Prince of Xunyang Daxin, styled Renshu.
entries.literal: The Prince of Xunyang, Daxin, courtesy name Renshu.

entries.zh: 幼而聰朗，善屬文。
entries.en: From youth he was clever and bright and wrote well.
entries.literal: From youth he was clever and bright and skilled at literary composition.

entries.zh: 中大通四年，以皇孫封當陽公，邑一千五百戶。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Zhongdatong he was enfeoffed Duke of Dangyang with a fief of fifteen hundred households.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Zhongdatong, as imperial grandson he was enfeoffed Duke of Dangyang with a fief of one thousand five hundred households.

entries.zh: 大同元年，出爲使持節、都督郢南北司定新五州諸軍事、輕車將軍、郢州刺史。
entries.en: In the first year of Great Unity he went out as bearer of the staff, commander of the five E-region prefectures, General of Light Chariots, and inspector of E.
entries.literal: In the first year of Great Unity he went out as bearer of the staff, commander of military affairs in the five prefectures of E, north and south of Si, Ding, and Xin, General of Light Chariots, and inspector of E prefecture.

entries.zh: 時年十三，太宗以其幼，恐未達民情，戒之曰：「事無大小，悉委行事，纖毫不須措懷。」
entries.en: He was thirteen; Taizong, fearing he had not grasped the people's hearts, admonished him, "In affairs great or small, entrust all to your staff—do not let a thread of worry touch your mind."
entries.literal: He was thirteen; the Heir Apparent Taizong, because he was young, feared he had not yet grasped the people's hearts and admonished him: "In affairs great or small, entrust all to your staff—do not let a thread of worry touch your mind."

entries.zh: 大心雖不親州務，發言每合於理，衆皆驚服。
entries.en: Though he did not handle prefectural affairs himself, whenever he spoke it accorded with reason and all were struck and submitted.
entries.literal: Though Daxin did not personally handle prefectural affairs, whenever he spoke it accorded with reason and all were struck and submitted.

entries.zh: 七年，征爲侍中、兼石頭戍軍事。
entries.en: In the seventh year he was summoned as palace attendant and concurrently commander of the Stone City garrison.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he was summoned as palace attendant and concurrently commander of the Stone City garrison.

entries.zh: 太清元年，出爲雲麾將軍、江州刺史。
entries.en: In the first year of Supreme Purity he went out as General of the Cloud Banner and inspector of Jiangzhou.
entries.literal: In the first year of Supreme Purity he went out as General of the Cloud Banner and inspector of Jiangzhou.

entries.zh: 二年，侯景寇京邑。
entries.en: In the second year Hou Jing raided the capital region.
entries.literal: In the second year Hou Jing raided the capital region.

entries.zh: 大心招集士卒，遠近歸之，衆至數萬，與上流諸軍赴援宮闕。
entries.en: Daxin gathered soldiers; men near and far joined until his force reached tens of thousands, and with upriver armies he hurried to relieve the palace.
entries.literal: Daxin gathered soldiers; men near and far came to him until his force reached tens of thousands, and with the upriver armies he hurried to relieve the palace.

entries.zh: 三年，城陷，上甲侯蕭韶南奔，宣密詔，加散騎常侍，進號平南將軍。
entries.en: In the third year the city fell; Marquis of Shangjia Xiao Shao fled south and proclaimed a secret edict making Daxin regular palace attendant and General Who Pacifies the South.
entries.literal: In the third year the city fell; Marquis of Shangjia Xiao Shao fled south and proclaimed a secret edict adding Daxin as regular palace attendant and promoting his title to General Who Pacifies the South.

entries.zh: 大寶元年，封尋陽王，邑二千戶。
entries.en: In the first year of Great Treasure he was enfeoffed Prince of Xunyang with a fief of two thousand households.
entries.literal: In the first year of Great Treasure he was enfeoffed Prince of Xunyang with a fief of two thousand households.

entries.zh: 初，歷陽太守莊鐵以城降侯景，旣而又奉其母來奔，大心以鐵舊將，厚爲其禮，軍旅之事，悉以委之，仍以爲豫章內史。
entries.en: Earlier Liyang magistrate Zhuang Tie had surrendered to Hou Jing, then brought his mother to defect; Daxin, because Tie was an old general, treated him generously and entrusted all military affairs to him, and made him interior minister of Yuzhang.
entries.literal: Earlier Liyang magistrate Zhuang Tie had surrendered the city to Hou Jing, then brought his mother to defect; Daxin, because Tie was an old general, treated him with great courtesy and entrusted all military affairs to him, and also made him interior minister of Yuzhang.

entries.zh: 侯景數遣軍西上寇抄，大心輒令鐵擊破之，賊不能進。
entries.en: Hou Jing repeatedly sent armies west to raid; Daxin always had Tie defeat them and the bandit could not advance.
entries.literal: Hou Jing repeatedly sent armies west to raid; Daxin always had Tie defeat them and the bandit could not advance.

entries.zh: 時鄱陽王範率衆棄合肥，屯于柵口，待援兵總集，欲俱進。
entries.en: The Prince of Poyang Fan had abandoned Hefei and encamped at Zhakou, waiting for relief armies before advancing together.
entries.literal: At the time the Prince of Poyang Fan led his host abandoning Hefei and encamped at Zhakou, waiting for relief armies to gather before advancing together.

entries.zh: 大心聞之，遣要範西上，以湓城處之，廩饋甚厚，與戮力共除禍難。
entries.en: Daxin summoned Fan west, lodged him at Pencheng with rich grain supplies, to join strength against the calamity.
entries.literal: Daxin heard and summoned Fan west, lodging him at Pencheng with very rich grain supplies, to join strength in removing the calamity.

entries.zh: 會莊鐵據豫章反，大心令中兵參軍韋約等將軍擊之，鐵敗績，又乞降。
entries.en: Then Zhuang Tie held Yuzhang in rebellion; Daxin sent middle army aide Wei Yue and others to attack; Tie was defeated and again begged surrender.
entries.literal: Then Zhuang Tie held Yuzhang in rebellion; Daxin sent the middle army aide Wei Yue and others with troops to attack; Tie was defeated and again begged surrender.

entries.zh: 鄱陽世子嗣先與鐵遊處，因稱其人才略從橫，且舊將也，欲舉大事，當資其力，若降江州，必不全其首領，嗣請援之。
entries.en: Poyang's heir Si had traveled with Tie and praised his talent, saying that as an old general he should be used in a great affair; if he surrendered to Jiangzhou his head would not be spared—Si asked to rescue him.
entries.literal: The Prince of Poyang's heir Si had earlier traveled with Tie and therefore praised his talent and stratagem, and that as an old general he should be used in a great affair; if he surrendered to Jiangzhou his head would surely not be spared—Si asked to rescue him.

entries.zh: 範從之，乃遣將侯瑱率精甲五千往救鐵，夜襲破韋約等營。
entries.en: Fan agreed and sent general Hou Zhen with five thousand picked armor to save Tie; by night they stormed and broke Wei Yue's camp.
entries.literal: Fan agreed and sent the general Hou Zhen with five thousand picked armor to save Tie; by night they stormed and broke Wei Yue's camp.

entries.zh: 大心聞之大懼，於是二籓釁起，人心離貳。
entries.en: Daxin heard and was greatly afraid; the two fiefs raised strife and hearts turned divided.
entries.literal: Daxin heard and was greatly afraid; then the two fiefs raised strife and hearts turned divided.

entries.zh: 景將任約略地至于湓城，大心遣司馬韋質拒戰，敗績。
entries.en: Jing's general Ren Yue overran the land to Pencheng; Daxin sent marshal Wei Zhi to meet battle and was defeated.
entries.literal: Jing's general Ren Yue overran the land as far as Pencheng; Daxin sent the marshal Wei Zhi to meet battle and was defeated.

entries.zh: 時帳下猶有勇士千餘人，咸說曰：「旣無糧儲，難以守固。
entries.en: There were still more than a thousand warriors in the tent, who all said, "Without grain stores we cannot hold firm.
entries.literal: At the time there were still more than a thousand warriors in the tent, who all said: "Without grain stores we cannot hold firm.

entries.zh: 若輕騎往建州，以圖後舉，策之上者也。」
entries.en: If with light horse we go to Jianzhou to plan a later rising, that is the best stratagem."
entries.literal: If with light horse we go to Jianzhou to plan a later rising, that is the best stratagem."

entries.zh: 大心未決，其母陳淑容曰：「卽日聖御年尊，儲宮萬福，汝久奉違顏色，不念拜謁闕庭，且吾已老，而欲遠涉險路，糧儲不給，豈謂孝子？
entries.en: Daxin had not decided when his mother Lady Chen said, "Today the sage ruler is old and the heir blessed—you have long been absent and do not think to bow at the palace gate; I am old, and you would cross a perilous road with no grain—can this be filial?
entries.literal: Daxin had not decided when his mother Lady Chen the Shure said: "Today the sage ruler is advanced in years and the heir ten thousandfold blessed—you have long been absent from his face and do not think to bow at the palace gate; moreover I am old, and you would cross a perilous road with no grain—can this be called filial?

entries.zh: 吾終不行。」
entries.en: I will never go."
entries.literal: I will never go."

entries.zh: 因撫胸慟哭，大心乃止。
entries.en: She clutched her breast and wept bitterly; Daxin then stopped.
entries.literal: She clutched her breast and wept bitterly; Daxin then stopped.

entries.zh: 遂與約和。
entries.en: He then made peace with Yue.
entries.literal: He then made peace with Yue.

entries.zh: 二年秋，遇害，時年二十九。
entries.en: In the autumn of the second year he was killed at twenty-nine.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the second year he was killed; he was twenty-nine.

entries.zh: 南海王大臨，字仁宣。
entries.en: Prince of Nanhai Dalin, styled Renxuan.
entries.literal: The Prince of Nanhai, Dalin, courtesy name Renxuan.

entries.zh: 大同二年，封寧國縣公，邑一千五百戶。
entries.en: In the second year of Great Unity he was enfeoffed Duke of Ningguo with fifteen hundred households.
entries.literal: In the second year of Great Unity he was enfeoffed Duke of Ningguo with a fief of one thousand five hundred households.

entries.zh: 少而敏慧。
entries.en: From youth he was quick and clever.
entries.literal: From youth he was quick and clever.

entries.zh: 年十一，遭左夫人憂，哭泣毀瘠，以孝聞。
entries.en: At eleven he mourned the left lady, wept until wasted, and was famed for filial piety.
entries.literal: At eleven he suffered mourning for the left lady; he wept until wasted and was famed for filial piety.

entries.zh: 後入國學，明經射策甲科，拜中書侍郎，遷給事黃門侍郎。
entries.en: Later he entered the National University, placed first in classics and policy, became Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat, and rose to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
entries.literal: Later he entered the National University, placed first in the classics examination and policy shooting, was made gentleman of the Secretariat, and promoted to gentleman in the Yellow Gate.

entries.zh: 十一年，爲長兼侍中。
entries.en: In the eleventh year he was made acting long-term palace attendant.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year he was made acting long-term palace attendant.

entries.zh: 出爲輕車將軍，琅邪、彭城二郡太守。
entries.en: He went out as General of Light Chariots and magistrate of Langye and Pengcheng.
entries.literal: He went out as General of Light Chariots and magistrate of Langye and Pengcheng commanderies.

entries.zh: 侯景亂，爲使持節、宣惠將軍，屯新亭。
entries.en: When Hou Jing rebelled he was made bearer of the staff and General of Proclaimed Grace, encamped at Xinting.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled he was made bearer of the staff and General of Proclaimed Grace, encamped at Xinting.

entries.zh: 俄又徵還，屯端門，都督城南諸軍事。
entries.en: Soon he was summoned back to garrison the Duan Gate and command military affairs south of the city.
entries.literal: Soon he was summoned back to garrison the Duan Gate and command military affairs south of the city.

entries.zh: 時議者皆勸收外財物，擬供賞賜，大臨獨曰：「物乃賞士，而牛可犒軍。」
entries.en: Men of the day urged seizing outside goods for rewards; Dalin alone said, "Goods reward warriors—but cattle can feed the army."
entries.literal: Men of the day all urged seizing outside goods to supply rewards; Dalin alone said: "Goods are for rewarding warriors—but cattle can feed the army."

entries.zh: 命取牛，得千餘頭，城內賴以饗士。
entries.en: He ordered cattle taken and got more than a thousand head; the city relied on this to feast the troops.
entries.literal: He ordered cattle taken and got more than a thousand head; within the city they relied on this to feast the troops.

entries.zh: 大寶元年，封南海郡王，邑二千戶。
entries.en: In the first year of Great Treasure he was enfeoffed Prince of Nanhai with two thousand households.
entries.literal: In the first year of Great Treasure he was enfeoffed Prince of Nanhai commandery with a fief of two thousand households.

entries.zh: 出爲使持節、都督揚、南徐二州諸軍事、安南將軍、揚州刺史。
entries.en: He went out as bearer of the staff, commander of Yang and South Xu, General Who Pacifies the South, and inspector of Yangzhou.
entries.literal: He went out as bearer of the staff, commander of military affairs in Yang and South Xu prefectures, General Who Pacifies the South, and inspector of Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 又除安東將軍、吳郡太守。
entries.en: He was also made General Who Pacifies the East and magistrate of Wu commandery.
entries.literal: He was also made General Who Pacifies the East and magistrate of Wu commandery.

entries.zh: 時張彪起義於會稽，吳人陸令公、潁川庾孟卿等勸大臨走投彪。
entries.en: Zhang Biao raised righteousness in Kuaiji; Wu men Lu Linggong and Yingchuan Yu Mengqing urged Dalin to flee to Biao.
entries.literal: At the time Zhang Biao raised righteousness in Kuaiji; Wu men Lu Linggong and Yingchuan Yu Mengqing and others urged Dalin to flee to Biao.

entries.zh: 大臨曰：「彪若成功，不資我力；
entries.en: Dalin said, "If Biao succeeds, he will not need my strength;
entries.literal: Dalin said: "If Biao succeeds, he will not need my strength;

entries.zh: 如其撓敗，以我說焉。
entries.en: if he is broken and defeated, they will blame my persuasion.
entries.literal: if he is broken and defeated, they will blame it on my persuasion.

entries.zh: 不可往也。」
entries.en: I cannot go."
entries.literal: I cannot go."

entries.zh: 二年秋，遇害于郡，時年二十五。
entries.en: In the autumn of the second year he was killed in the commandery at twenty-five.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the second year he was killed in the commandery; he was twenty-five.

entries.zh: 南郡王大連，字仁靖。
entries.en: Prince of Nan commandery Dalian, styled Renjing.
entries.literal: The Prince of Nan commandery, Dalian, courtesy name Renjing.

entries.zh: 少俊爽，能屬文，舉止風流，雅有巧思，妙達音樂，兼善丹青。
entries.en: From youth handsome and bright, he wrote well, bore himself gracefully, had a gift for design, mastered music, and painted well.
entries.literal: From youth handsome and bright, skilled at literary composition, his bearing and carriage graceful; he had a subtle gift for design, was masterly in music, and also good at painting.

entries.zh: 大同二年，封臨城縣公，邑一千五百戶。
entries.en: In the second year of Great Unity he was enfeoffed Duke of Lincheng with fifteen hundred households.
entries.literal: In the second year of Great Unity he was enfeoffed Duke of Lincheng with a fief of one thousand five hundred households.

entries.zh: 七年，與南海王俱入國學，射策甲科，拜中書侍郎。
entries.en: In the seventh year he and the Prince of Nanhai together entered the National University, placed first in policy, and became Gentlemen of the Palace Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he and the Prince of Nanhai together entered the National University, placed first in policy shooting, and were made gentlemen of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 十年，高祖幸朱方，大連與兄大臨並從。
entries.en: In the tenth year the Founding Emperor visited Zhufang; Dalian and his brother Dalin both followed.
entries.literal: In the tenth year the Founding Emperor visited Zhufang; Dalian and his elder brother Dalin both followed.

entries.zh: 高祖問曰：「汝等習騎不？」
entries.en: The Founding Emperor asked, "Have you practiced riding?"
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor asked: "Have you practiced riding?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「臣等未奉詔，不敢輒習。」
entries.en: They answered, "We have not received edict and dare not practice on our own."
entries.literal: They answered: "We have not received edict and dare not practice on our own."

entries.zh: 敕各給馬試之，大連兄弟據鞍往還，各得馳驟之節，高祖大悅，卽賜所乘馬。
entries.en: He ordered each given a horse; the brothers mounted and circled, each showing the rhythm of the gallop; the Founding Emperor was greatly pleased and gave them the horses they rode.
entries.literal: He ordered each given a horse to try; the Dalian brothers mounted and circled, each showing the rhythm of the gallop; the Founding Emperor was greatly pleased and at once gave them the horses they rode.

entries.zh: 及爲啓謝，詞又甚美。
entries.en: When they memorialized thanks the wording was also very fine.
entries.literal: When they memorialized thanks the wording was also very fine.

entries.zh: 高祖佗日謂太宗曰：「昨見大臨、大連，風韻可愛，足以慰吾年老。」
entries.en: Another day the Founding Emperor said to Taizong, "Yesterday seeing Dalin and Dalian—their bearing is lovable and enough to comfort me in my old age."
entries.literal: Another day the Founding Emperor said to the Heir Apparent Taizong: "Yesterday seeing Dalin and Dalian—their bearing is lovable and enough to comfort me in my old age."

entries.zh: 遷給事黃門侍郎，轉侍中，尋兼石頭戍軍事。
entries.en: He rose to Yellow Gate gentleman, then palace attendant, soon concurrently commander of the Stone City garrison.
entries.literal: He was promoted to gentleman in the Yellow Gate, then palace attendant, soon concurrently commander of the Stone City garrison.

entries.zh: 太清元年，出爲使持節、輕車將軍、東揚州刺史。
entries.en: In the first year of Supreme Purity he went out as bearer of the staff, General of Light Chariots, and inspector of East Yangzhou.
entries.literal: In the first year of Supreme Purity he went out as bearer of the staff, General of Light Chariots, and inspector of East Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 侯景入寇京師，大連率衆四萬來赴。
entries.en: When Hou Jing invaded the capital Dalian led forty thousand men to the rescue.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing invaded the capital Dalian led forty thousand men to the rescue.

entries.zh: 及臺城沒，援軍散，復還揚州。
entries.en: When the terrace city fell the relief armies scattered and he returned to Yangzhou.
entries.literal: When the terrace city fell the relief armies scattered and he returned to Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 三年，會稽山賊田領群聚黨數萬來攻，大連命中兵參軍張彪擊斬之。
entries.en: In the third year Kuaiji bandits led by Tian Lingqun gathered tens of thousands and attacked; Dalian ordered middle army aide Zhang Biao to strike and behead them.
entries.literal: In the third year bandits of Kuaiji led by Tian Ling gathered tens of thousands in party and attacked; Dalian ordered the middle army aide Zhang Biao to strike and behead them.

entries.zh: 大寶元年，封爲南郡王，邑二千戶。
entries.en: In the first year of Great Treasure he was enfeoffed Prince of Nan commandery with two thousand households.
entries.literal: In the first year of Great Treasure he was enfeoffed Prince of Nan commandery with a fief of two thousand households.

entries.zh: 景仍遣其將趙伯超、劉神茂來討，大連設備以待之。
entries.en: Jing again sent generals Zhao Bochao and Liu Shenmao to attack; Dalian prepared to await them.
entries.literal: Jing again sent his generals Zhao Bochao and Liu Shenmao to attack; Dalian made preparations to await them.

entries.zh: 會將留異以城應賊，大連棄城走，至信安，爲賊所獲。
entries.en: Then general Liu Yi surrendered the city to the bandit; Dalian abandoned the city and fled; at Xin'an he was taken.
entries.literal: Then the general Liu Yi surrendered the city to the bandit; Dalian abandoned the city and fled; reaching Xin'an he was taken by the bandit.

entries.zh: 侯景以爲輕車將軍、行揚州事，遷平南將軍、江州刺史。
entries.en: Hou Jing made him General of Light Chariots with acting charge of Yangzhou, then General Who Pacifies the South and inspector of Jiangzhou.
entries.literal: Hou Jing made him General of Light Chariots with acting charge of Yangzhou affairs, then promoted to General Who Pacifies the South and inspector of Jiangzhou.

entries.zh: 大連旣迫寇手，恒思逃竄，乃與賊約曰：「軍民之事，吾不預焉。
entries.en: Pressed in the bandit's grip, Dalian always thought of escape and made a pact, "In military and civil affairs I take no part.
entries.literal: Dalian, pressed in the bandit's grip, always thought of escape, and made a pact with the bandit: "In military and civil affairs I take no part.

entries.zh: 候我存亡，但聽鐘響。」
entries.en: Wait for my life or death—only listen for the bell."
entries.literal: Wait for my life or death—only listen for the bell."

entries.zh: 欲簡與相見，因得亡逸，賊亦信之。
entries.en: He wished to meet the bandit with few attendants and slip away; the bandit also trusted him.
entries.literal: He wished to meet the bandit with few attendants and thus slip away; the bandit also trusted him.

entries.zh: 事未果。
entries.en: The affair did not succeed.
entries.literal: The affair did not succeed.

entries.zh: 二年秋，遇害，時年二十五。
entries.en: In the autumn of the second year he was killed at twenty-five.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the second year he was killed; he was twenty-five.

entries.zh: 安陸王大春，字仁經。
entries.en: Prince of Anlu Dachun, styled Renjing.
entries.literal: The Prince of Anlu, Dachun, courtesy name Renjing.

entries.zh: 少博涉書記。
entries.en: From youth he read widely in letters and records.
entries.literal: From youth he read widely in letters and records.

entries.zh: 天性孝謹，體貌環偉，腰帶十圍。
entries.en: By nature filial and careful, his build imposing, his belt ten arm-spans around.
entries.literal: By nature filial and careful, his build round and imposing, his belt ten arm-spans around.

entries.zh: 大同六年，封西豊縣公，邑一千五百戶。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Great Unity he was enfeoffed Duke of Xifeng with fifteen hundred households.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Great Unity he was enfeoffed Duke of Xifeng with a fief of one thousand five hundred households.

entries.zh: 拜中書侍郎。
entries.en: He was made Secretariat gentleman.
entries.literal: He was made gentleman of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 後爲寧遠將軍，知石頭戍軍事。
entries.en: Later he was General of Peaceful Distance and in charge of Stone City garrison affairs.
entries.literal: Later he was General of Peaceful Distance and in charge of Stone City garrison affairs.

entries.zh: 侯景內寇，大春奔京口，隨邵陵王入援，戰于鐘山，爲賊所獲。
entries.en: When Hou Jing invaded Dachun fled to Jingkou and followed the Prince of Shaoling to the rescue, fought at Zhongshan, and was taken.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing invaded within the passes Dachun fled to Jingkou and followed the Prince of Shaoling to the rescue, fought at Zhongshan, and was taken by the bandit.

entries.zh: 京城旣陷，大寶元年，封安陸郡王，邑二千戶。
entries.en: When the capital fell, in the first year of Great Treasure he was enfeoffed Prince of Anlu with two thousand households.
entries.literal: When the capital fell, in the first year of Great Treasure he was enfeoffed Prince of Anlu commandery with a fief of two thousand households.

entries.zh: 出爲使持節、雲麾將軍、東揚州刺史。
entries.en: He went out as bearer of the staff, General of the Cloud Banner, and inspector of East Yangzhou.
entries.literal: He went out as bearer of the staff, General of the Cloud Banner, and inspector of East Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 二年秋，遇害，時年二十二。
entries.en: In the autumn of the second year he was killed at twenty-two.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the second year he was killed; he was twenty-two.

entries.zh: 建平王大球字仁珽。
entries.en: Prince of Jianping Daqiu, styled Renting.
entries.literal: The Prince of Jianping, Daqiu, courtesy name Renting.

entries.zh: 大寶元年，封建平郡王，邑二千戶。
entries.en: In the first year of Great Treasure he was enfeoffed Prince of Jianping with two thousand households.
entries.literal: In the first year of Great Treasure he was enfeoffed Prince of Jianping commandery with a fief of two thousand households.

entries.zh: 性明慧夙成。
entries.en: By nature bright and clever from early youth.
entries.literal: By nature bright and clever from early youth.

entries.zh: 初，侯景圍京城，高祖素歸心釋教，每發誓願，恒云：「若有衆生應受諸苦，悉衍身代當。」
entries.en: When Hou Jing besieged the capital, the Founding Emperor had long turned to Buddhism; whenever he vowed he said, "If living beings should suffer every pain, let it all pass to my body in their stead."
entries.literal: Earlier, when Hou Jing besieged the capital, the Founding Emperor had long turned his heart to Buddhism; whenever he made a vow he always said: "If there are living beings who should suffer every pain, let it all be transferred to my body in their stead."

entries.zh: 時大球年甫七歲，聞而驚謂母曰：「官家尚爾，兒安敢辭？」
entries.en: Daqiu was just seven; hearing this he said to his mother, "If the ruler is still like this, how dare I refuse?"
entries.literal: Daqiu was just seven; hearing this he was startled and said to his mother: "If the ruler is still like this, how dare I refuse?"

entries.zh: 乃六時禮佛，亦云：「凡有衆生應獲苦報，悉大球代受。」
entries.en: He worshiped Buddha at the six hours and said, "Whatever living beings should receive bitter retribution, let Daqiu receive it all in their stead."
entries.literal: He then worshiped Buddha at the six hours and likewise said: "Whatever living beings should receive bitter retribution, let Daqiu receive it all in their stead."

entries.zh: 其早慧如此。
entries.en: Such was his early wisdom.
entries.literal: Such was his early wisdom.

entries.zh: 二年，出爲輕車將軍、兼石頭戍軍事。
entries.en: In the second year he went out as General of Light Chariots and concurrently commander of the Stone City garrison.
entries.literal: In the second year he went out as General of Light Chariots and concurrently commander of the Stone City garrison.

entries.zh: 其年秋，遇害，時年十一。
entries.en: That autumn he was killed at eleven.
entries.literal: That autumn he was killed; he was eleven.

entries.zh: 義安王大昕，字仁朗。
entries.en: Prince Daxin of Yi'an was styled Renlang.
entries.literal: Prince Daxin of Yi'an was styled Renlang.

entries.zh: 年四歲，母陳夫人卒，便哀慕毀悴，有若成人。
entries.en: When he was four, his mother, Lady Chen, died; he grieved and wasted away in longing, as though he were an adult.
entries.literal: When he was four, his mother, Lady Chen, died; he grieved and wasted away in longing, as though he were an adult.

entries.zh: 及高祖崩，大昕奉慰太宗，嗚咽不能自勝。
entries.en: When Gaozu died, Daxin offered consolation to Taizong, sobbing so hard he could not control himself.
entries.literal: When Gaozu died, Daxin offered consolation to Taizong, sobbing so hard he could not control himself.

entries.zh: 左右見之，莫不掩泣。
entries.en: Those attending at the sides saw him, and none failed to cover their faces and weep.
entries.literal: Those attending at the sides saw him, and none failed to cover their faces and weep.

entries.zh: 大寶元年，封義安郡王，邑二千戶。
entries.en: In Dabao 1, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yi'an Commandery with a fief of two thousand households.
entries.literal: In Dabao 1, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yi'an Commandery with a fief of two thousand households.

entries.zh: 二年，出爲寧遠將軍、琅邪、彭城二郡太守，未之鎮，遇害，時年十一。
entries.en: In the second year, he went out as General of Peaceful Distance and administrator of Langye and Pengcheng commanderies, but before reaching his post he was killed, aged eleven.
entries.literal: In the second year, he went out as General Who Pacifies the Distant and administrator of Langye and Pengcheng commanderies, but before reaching his post he was killed, aged eleven.

entries.zh: 瀏陽公大雅字仁風。
entries.en: Duke of Liuyang Daya, styled Renfeng.
entries.literal: The Duke of Liuyang, Daya, courtesy name Renfeng.

entries.zh: 大同九年，封瀏陽縣公，邑一千五百戶。
entries.en: In the ninth year of Great Unity he was enfeoffed Duke of Liuyang with fifteen hundred households.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Great Unity he was enfeoffed Duke of Liuyang with a fief of one thousand five hundred households.

entries.zh: 少聰警，美姿儀，特爲高祖所愛。
entries.en: From youth clever and handsome, he was especially loved by the Founding Emperor.
entries.literal: From youth clever and alert, handsome in bearing, he was especially loved by the Founding Emperor.

entries.zh: 太清三年，京城陷，賊已乘城，大雅猶命左右格戰，賊至漸衆，乃自縋而下。
entries.en: In the third year of Supreme Purity the capital fell; the bandit had scaled the wall, yet Daya still ordered his men to fight; the bandit grew numerous and he lowered himself by rope.
entries.literal: In the third year of Supreme Purity the capital fell; the bandit had already scaled the wall, yet Daya still ordered his attendants to fight at the barrier; the bandit grew numerous and he lowered himself by rope.

entries.zh: 因發憤感疾，薨，時年十七。
entries.en: He then fell ill from indignation and died at seventeen.
entries.literal: He then fell ill from indignation and died; he was seventeen.

entries.zh: 西陽王大鈞字仁輔。
entries.en: Prince of Xiyang Dajun, styled Renfu.
entries.literal: The Prince of Xiyang, Dajun, courtesy name Renfu.

entries.zh: 性厚重，不妄戲弄。
entries.en: By nature grave and steady, he did not play rashly.
entries.literal: By nature grave and steady, he did not play rashly.

entries.zh: 年七歲，高祖嘗問讀何書，對曰「學《詩》」。
entries.en: At seven the Founding Emperor asked what book he read; he answered, "Studying the Odes."
entries.literal: At seven the Founding Emperor once asked what book he was reading; he answered: "Studying the Odes."

entries.zh: 因命諷誦，音韻清雅，高祖因賜王羲之書一卷。
entries.en: Ordered to recite, his tones were clear and elegant, and the Founding Emperor gave him one scroll of Wang Xizhi's calligraphy.
entries.literal: He was then ordered to recite; his tones were clear and elegant, and the Founding Emperor gave him one scroll of Wang Xizhi's calligraphy.

entries.zh: 大寶元年，封西陽郡王，邑二千戶。
entries.en: In the first year of Great Treasure he was enfeoffed Prince of Xiyang with two thousand households.
entries.literal: In the first year of Great Treasure he was enfeoffed Prince of Xiyang commandery with a fief of two thousand households.

entries.zh: 出爲宣惠將軍、丹陽尹。
entries.en: He went out as General of Proclaimed Grace and governor of Danyang.
entries.literal: He went out as General of Proclaimed Grace and governor of Danyang.

entries.zh: 二年，監揚州，將軍如故。
entries.en: In the second year he supervised Yangzhou, keeping his general's title.
entries.literal: In the second year he supervised Yangzhou, general as before.

entries.zh: 至秋遇害，時年十三。
entries.en: By autumn he was killed at thirteen.
entries.literal: By autumn he was killed; he was thirteen.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：自侯景寇逆，世祖據有上游，以全楚之兵委僧辯將率之任。
entries.en: The historian writes: From Hou Jing's rebellion, Yuan held the upper reaches and entrusted all Chu's troops to Sengbian.
entries.literal: The historian says: From the time Hou Jing rebelled, Emperor Yuan held the upper reaches and entrusted the troops of all Chu to Sengbian's command.

entries.zh: 及克平禍亂，功亦著焉，在乎策勳，當上臺之賞。
entries.en: When he crushed the calamity his merit was manifest; in recording merit he ought to have received the highest reward.
entries.literal: When he had crushed the calamity his merit too was manifest; in recording merit he ought to have received reward on the highest terrace.

entries.zh: 敬帝以高祖貽厥之重，世祖繼體之尊，洎渚宮淪覆，理膺寶祚。
entries.en: Emperor Jing bore Gaozu's legacy and Yuan's succession; when Zhugong fell, by right he should have received the throne.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing bore the weight of Emperor Gaozu's legacy and Emperor Yuan's succession in the line; when Zhugong Palace was submerged, by right he should have received the precious throne.

entries.zh: 僧辯位當將相，義存伊、霍，乃受脅齊師，傍立支庶。
entries.en: Sengbian stood as general and minister with Yi Yin and Huo Guang's righteousness—yet he accepted Qi's coercion and set up a collateral scion.
entries.literal: Sengbian stood in the place of general and minister with the righteousness of Yi Yin and Huo Guang—yet he accepted coercion from Qi's army and set up a collateral scion at the side.

entries.zh: 苟欲行夫忠義，何忠義之遠矣？
entries.en: If he wished loyalty and righteousness, how far they had fled!
entries.literal: If he wished to practice loyalty and righteousness, how far loyalty and righteousness had fled!

entries.zh: 樹國之道旣虧，謀身之計不足，自致殲滅，悲矣！
entries.en: The way of establishing a state was lost; the plan for himself insufficient—he brought on his own destruction. Lamentable!
entries.literal: The way of establishing a state was already lost; the plan for preserving himself was insufficient—he brought on his own destruction. Lamentable!

entries.zh: 梁書卷第四十五 列傳第三十九
entries.en: Book of Liang, Volume 45, Biography 39
entries.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 45, Biography 39

entries.zh: 胡僧祐 徐文盛 杜崱 兄岸 弟幼安 兄子龕 陰子春
entries.en: Hu Sengyou; Xu Wensheng; Du Ze; Du An; Du You'an; Du Kan; Yin Zichun
entries.literal: Hu Sengyou, Xu Wensheng, Du Ze, elder brother An, younger brother You'an, elder brother's son Kan, Yin Zichun

entries.zh: 胡僧祐字願果，南陽冠軍人。
entries.en: Hu Sengyou, styled Yuanguo, came from Guanjun in Nanyang.
entries.literal: Hu Sengyou, styled Yuanguo, came from Guanjun in Nanyang.

entries.zh: 少勇決，有武幹。
entries.en: In youth he was brave and resolute and had military ability.
entries.literal: In youth he was brave and resolute and had military ability.

entries.zh: 仕魏至銀青光祿大夫，以大通二年歸國，頻上封事，高祖器之，拜假節、超武將軍、文德主帥，使戍項城。
entries.en: He served Wei, reaching Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon. In Datong 2 he returned to Liang and repeatedly submitted sealed memorials. Gaozu valued him and appointed him acting staff-bearer, General Who Surpasses Martial Might, and commander of the Wende guard, sending him to garrison Xiangcheng.
entries.literal: He served Wei, reaching Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon. In Datong 2 he returned to Liang and repeatedly submitted sealed memorials. Gaozu valued him and appointed him acting staff-bearer, General Who Surpasses Martial Might, and commander of the Wende guard, sending him to garrison Xiangcheng.

entries.zh: 城陷，復沒于魏。
entries.en: When the city fell, he was again lost to Wei.
entries.literal: When the city fell, he was again lost to Wei.

entries.zh: 中大通元年，陳慶之送魏北海王元顥入洛陽，僧祐又得還國，除南天水、天門二郡太守，有善政。
entries.en: In Zhongdatong 1, when Chen Qingzhi escorted Yuan Hao, Prince of Beihai of Wei, into Luoyang, Sengyou again managed to return to Liang. He was appointed administrator of South Tianshui and Tianmen commanderies and governed well.
entries.literal: In Zhongdatong 1, when Chen Qingzhi escorted Yuan Hao, Prince of Beihai of Wei, into Luoyang, Sengyou again managed to return to Liang. He was appointed administrator of South Tianshui and Tianmen commanderies and governed well.

entries.zh: 性好讀書，不解緝綴。
entries.en: By nature he loved reading, but he did not understand literary composition.
entries.literal: By nature he loved reading, but he did not understand literary composition.

entries.zh: 然每在公宴，必強賦詩，文辭鄙俚，多被嘲謔，僧祐怡然自若，謂己實工，矜伐愈甚。
entries.en: Yet whenever he attended public banquets, he always forced himself to compose poems. His wording was crude and rustic, and he was often mocked, but Sengyou remained perfectly at ease, believed himself truly skilled, and boasted all the more.
entries.literal: Yet whenever he attended public banquets, he always forced himself to compose poems. His wording was crude and rustic, and he was often mocked, but Sengyou remained perfectly at ease, believed himself truly skilled, and boasted all the more.

entries.zh: 徐文盛，字道茂，彭城人也。
entries.en: Xu Wensheng, styled Daomao, was from Pengcheng.
entries.literal: Xu Wensheng, styled Daomao, was a man of Pengcheng.

entries.zh: 世仕魏爲將。
entries.en: His family had served Wei as generals for generations.
entries.literal: For generations his family served Wei as generals.

entries.zh: 父慶之，天監初，率千餘人自北歸款，未至道卒。
entries.en: His father Qingzhi, early in Heavenly Surveillance, led over a thousand men south to defect but died on the way.
entries.literal: His father Qingzhi, at the beginning of Heavenly Surveillance, led more than a thousand men to surrender from the north but died on the road before arriving.

entries.zh: 文盛仍統其衆，稍立功績，高祖甚優寵之。
entries.en: Wensheng took over the troops, won merit step by step, and Gaozu favored him greatly.
entries.literal: Wensheng then took command of his force, gradually achieved merit, and Gaozu favored him exceedingly.

entries.zh: 大同末，以爲持節、督寧州刺史。
entries.en: At the end of Great Unity he became staff bearer and inspector of Ning.
entries.literal: At the end of Great Unity he was made bearer of the staff and inspector of Ning prefecture.

entries.zh: 先是，州在僻遠，所管羣蠻不識教義，貪欲財賄，劫篡相尋，前後刺史莫能制。
entries.en: The prefecture was remote; the tribes knew no law, only greed and raiding—no earlier governor had controlled them.
entries.literal: Earlier the prefecture lay in remote borderland; the tribal barbarians it governed knew no civil teaching, coveted bribes and goods, and plundered one another in succession—no former inspector could control them.

entries.zh: 文盛推心撫慰，示以威德，夷獠感之，風俗遂改。
entries.en: Wensheng won them with sincerity and awed them with strength; the tribes were moved and manners changed.
entries.literal: Wensheng opened his heart to soothe them, showed them might and virtue; the Yi and Liao were moved, and custom was reformed.

entries.zh: 杜崱，京兆杜陵人也。
entries.en: Du Ze was from Dulings in Jingzhao.
entries.literal: Du Ze, of Dulings in Jingzhao commandery.

entries.zh: 其先自北歸南，居於雍州之襄陽，子孫因家焉。
entries.en: His forebears came south from the north and settled at Xiangyang in Yong; the family remained there.
entries.literal: His ancestors had returned south from the north and settled at Xiangyang in Yong province; descendants made their home there.

entries.zh: 祖靈啓，齊給事中。
entries.en: Grandfather Lingqi was a Qi court attendant.
entries.literal: Grandfather Lingqi served Qi as attendant within the court.

entries.zh: 父懷寶，少有志節，常邀際會。
entries.en: His father Huaibao had spirit and principle from youth and waited for his hour.
entries.literal: Father Huaibao from youth had resolve and integrity, always awaiting the right moment.

entries.zh: 高祖義師東下，隨南平王偉留鎮襄陽。
entries.en: When Gaozu's army marched east he stayed with Prince of Nanping Wei to hold Xiangyang.
entries.literal: When Gaozu's righteous army marched east, he followed Prince of Nanping Wei remaining to garrison Xiangyang.

entries.zh: 天監中，稍立功績，官至驍猛將軍、梁州刺史。
entries.en: Under Heavenly Surveillance he rose through merit to General of Fierce Valor and Liang inspector.
entries.literal: In Heavenly Surveillance he gradually achieved merit and reached General of Fierce Valor and inspector of Liang prefecture.

entries.zh: 大同初，魏梁州刺史元羅舉州內附，懷寶復進督華州。
entries.en: Early in Great Unity Yuan Luo, Wei inspector of Liang, surrendered; Huaibao was also made commander of Hua.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Great Unity Wei inspector of Liang Yuan Luo surrendered the prefecture inward; Huaibao was further made superintending commander of Hua prefecture.

entries.zh: 值秦州所部武興氐王楊紹反，懷寶擊破之。
entries.en: Yang Shao, Di king of Wu Xing in Qin, rebelled; Huaibao defeated him.
entries.literal: Qin prefecture's dependent Wu Xing had Di king Yang Shao rebel; Huaibao defeated and broke him.

entries.zh: 五年，卒於鎮。
entries.en: In the fifth year he died in office.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he died at his post.

entries.zh: 崱卽懷寶第七子也。
entries.en: Ze was Huaibao's seventh son.
entries.literal: Ze was Huaibao's seventh son.

entries.zh: 幼有志氣，居鄉里以膽勇稱。
entries.en: From youth he had nerve and was known at home for boldness.
entries.literal: From youth he had fighting spirit and was known in his hometown for courage and daring.

entries.zh: 釋褐廬江驃騎府中兵參軍。
entries.en: He began as army recorder on the Lujiang Rapid Cavalry staff.
entries.literal: On leaving the office he became army recorder in the Rapid Cavalry command of Lujiang.

entries.zh: 世祖臨荊州，仍參幕府，後爲新興太守。
entries.en: When Shizu held Jingzhou he served on his staff, later becoming governor of Xinxing.
entries.literal: When Shizu governed Jingzhou he still served on his staff, later becoming governor of Xinxing.

entries.zh: 陰子春，字幼文，武威姑臧人也。
entries.en: Yin Zichun, styled Youwen, was from Guzang in Wuwei.
entries.literal: Yin Zichun, styled Youwen, was a man of Guzang in Wuwei commandery.

entries.zh: 晉義熙末，曾祖襲，隨宋高祖南遷，至南平，因家焉。
entries.en: At the end of Jin Yixi his great-grandfather Xi followed Song Gaozu south to Nanping and settled there.
entries.literal: At the end of Yixi in Jin, his great-grandfather Xi followed Song Gaozu south, reaching Nanping, and there made home.

entries.zh: 父智伯，與高祖鄰居，少相友善，嘗入高祖臥內，見有異光成五色，因握高祖手曰：「公後必大貴，非人臣也。
entries.en: His father Zhibo lived next to Gaozu; they were friends from youth; once he entered Gaozu's bedchamber and saw a five-colored light; he took Gaozu's hand and said, "You are destined for greatness—not the fate of a subject.
entries.literal: Father Zhibo was Gaozu's neighbor; from youth they were friendly; he once entered Gaozu's sleeping chamber and saw a strange light in five colors; he grasped Gaozu's hand and said: "Your Grace will surely rise to great nobility—not the lot of a subject.

entries.zh: 天下方亂，安蒼生者，其在君乎！」
entries.en: The realm is in chaos; will you not be the one to save the people?"
entries.literal: The realm is in disorder; he who settles the black-haired folk—is it not you?"

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「幸勿多言。」
entries.en: Gaozu said, "Say no more."
entries.literal: Gaozu said: "Pray speak no more."

entries.zh: 於是情好轉密，高祖每有求索，如外府焉。
entries.en: Their bond deepened; whenever Gaozu needed anything it was as if he had another treasury.
entries.literal: Thereupon their affection grew still closer; whenever Gaozu had need it was as from an outer treasury.

entries.zh: 及高祖踐阼，官至梁、秦二州刺史。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne he rose to inspector of Liang and Qin.
entries.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne he reached inspector of Liang and Qin.

entries.zh: 晚事世祖，爲鎮西錄事參軍。
entries.en: Later he served Shizu as recorder on the Pacifying West staff.
entries.literal: In his later years he served Emperor Shizu as staff recorder in the Pacifying West headquarters.

entries.zh: 侯景亂，西沮蠻反，世祖令僧祐討之，使盡誅其渠帥，僧祐諫，忤旨下獄。
entries.en: When Hou Jing rebelled the Western Ju rose; Shizu ordered Sengyou to put them down and kill every chieftain; Sengyou remonstrated, offended the throne, and was jailed.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, the Western Ju barbarians revolted; Shizu ordered Sengyou to suppress them and to execute all their chieftains; Sengyou remonstrated and, defying the edict, was thrown into prison.

entries.zh: 大寶二年，侯景寇荊陝，圍王僧辯于巴陵，世祖乃引僧祐於獄，拜爲假節、武猛將軍，封新市縣侯，令赴援。
entries.en: In Great Treasure year two Hou Jing raided Jing-Shan and besieged Wang Sengbian at Baling; Shizu freed Sengyou, made him acting staff bearer, General of Martial Ferocity, and Marquis of Xinshi, and sent him to relieve the siege.
entries.literal: In the second year of Great Treasure, when Hou Jing raided Jing and Shan and besieged Wang Sengbian at Baling, Shizu brought Sengyou out of prison, made him acting bearer of the staff, General of Martial Ferocity, and Marquis of Xinshi county, and ordered him to relieve the siege.

entries.zh: 僧祐將發，謂其子曰：「汝可開兩門，一門擬朱，一門擬白。
entries.en: As he was about to march he told his son, "Prepare two gates—one for red, one for white.
entries.literal: As Sengyou was about to set out he told his son: "You may prepare two gates—one gate for red, one gate for white.

entries.zh: 吉則由朱門，凶則由白門。
entries.en: If I win, come in by the red gate; if I lose, by the white.
entries.literal: If fortune comes, enter by the red gate; if misfortune, by the white gate.

entries.zh: 吾不捷不歸也。」
entries.en: I will not come home unless I win."
entries.literal: I shall not return unless victorious."

entries.zh: 世祖聞而壯之。
entries.en: Shizu heard and was stirred.
entries.literal: When Shizu heard this he admired his spirit.

entries.zh: 至楊浦，景遣其將任約率銳卒五千，據白塉，遙以待之。
entries.en: At Yangpu, Jing sent Ren Yue with five thousand elites to hold White Embankment and wait for him.
entries.literal: Reaching Yangpu, Jing sent his general Ren Yue with five thousand crack troops to hold White Embankment, watching for him from afar.

entries.zh: 僧祐由別路西上，約謂畏己而退，急追之，及於南安芊口，呼僧祐曰：「吳兒，何爲不早降？
entries.en: Sengyou took a side road west; Yue thought he had fled in fear and chased hard; at Nan'an Qian Ford he shouted to Sengyou, "Wu whelp—why not surrender now?
entries.literal: Sengyou took a bypath westward; Yue thought he had feared him and retreated, and pursued urgently; at Nan'an Qian Ford he called to Sengyou: "Wu boy—why do you not surrender early?

entries.zh: 走何處去。」
entries.en: Where can you run?"
entries.literal: Where will you run?"

entries.zh: 僧祐不與之言，潛引卻，至赤砂亭，會陸法和至，乃與幷軍擊約，大破之，擒約送于江陵。
entries.en: Sengyou would not answer but quietly withdrew; at Red Sand Pavilion Lu Fahe came up, and together they attacked Yue, broke him utterly, captured him, and sent him to Jiangling.
entries.literal: Sengyou did not speak with him but secretly drew back; at Red Sand Pavilion layman Lu Fahe arrived, and together they joined armies and struck Yue, routing him greatly; they captured Yue and sent him to Jiangling.

entries.zh: 侯景聞之遂遁。
entries.en: Hou Jing heard and fled.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing heard of it he fled.

entries.zh: 世祖以僧祐爲侍中、領軍將軍，徵還荊州。
entries.en: Shizu made him palace attendant and commanding general and recalled him to Jingzhou.
entries.literal: Shizu made Sengyou palace attendant and General Who Commands the Army, and summoned him back to Jingzhou.

entries.zh: 承聖二年，進爲車騎將軍、開府儀同三司，餘悉如故。
entries.en: In Chengsheng year two he was promoted General of Chariots and Cavalry and Opening-the-Fortress with Three Staffs Equals; the rest unchanged.
entries.literal: In the second year of Chengsheng he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Opening-the-Fortress with Three Staffs Equals, all else unchanged.

entries.zh: 西魏寇至，以僧祐爲都督城東諸軍事。
entries.en: When Western Wei attacked, Shizu made him commander east of the city.
entries.literal: When Western Wei raided, Shizu made Sengyou commander of military affairs east of the city.

entries.zh: 魏軍四面起攻，百道齊舉，僧祐親當矢石，晝夜督戰，獎勵將士，明於賞罰，衆皆感之，咸爲致死，所向摧殄，賊莫敢前。
entries.en: Wei forces assaulted from every side, a hundred lines at once; Sengyou took arrows and stones himself, fighting day and night, clear in rewards and punishments—the men were stirred and died where they stood; nothing could stand before him; the enemy dared not come forward.
entries.literal: Wei armies attacked from all four sides, a hundred routes rising together; Sengyou himself met arrows and stones, supervising battle day and night, rewarding soldiers, clear in reward and punishment—all were moved and fought to the death; wherever he turned he crushed and destroyed; the bandits dared not advance.

entries.zh: 俄而中流矢卒，時年六十三。
entries.en: Soon he was hit by a stray arrow and died at sixty-three.
entries.literal: Before long he was struck by a stray arrow and died, aged sixty-three.

entries.zh: 世祖聞之，馳往臨哭。
entries.en: Shizu heard and rushed to mourn over the body.
entries.literal: When Shizu heard, he raced to attend and weep over the corpse.

entries.zh: 於是內外惶駭，城遂陷。
entries.en: Inside and outside panicked, and the city fell.
entries.literal: Thereupon inside and outside were terrified and alarmed, and the city fell.

entries.zh: 太清二年，聞國難，乃召募得數萬人來赴。
entries.en: In Supreme Clarity year two, hearing the capital was in peril, he raised tens of thousands and marched east.
entries.literal: In the second year of Supreme Clarity, hearing of the state's calamity, he mustered and recruited several tens of thousands to come to the relief.

entries.zh: 世祖嘉之，以爲持節、散騎常侍、左衛將軍、督梁、南秦、沙、東益、巴、北巴六州諸軍事、仁威將軍、秦州刺史，授以東討之略。
entries.en: Shizu praised him and made him staff bearer, palace attendant, Left Guard general, commander of six prefectures' forces, General of Benevolent Might, and Qin inspector, with the eastern campaign plan.
entries.literal: Shizu praised this and made him bearer of the staff, regular palace attendant, Left Guard general, commander of military affairs in Liang, South Qin, Sha, East Yi, Ba, and North Ba—six prefectures—General of Benevolent Might, and inspector of Qin prefecture, entrusting him with the eastern campaign plan.

entries.zh: 於是文盛督衆軍東下，至武昌，遇侯景將任約，遂與相持。
entries.en: Wensheng led his host east; at Wuchang he met Ren Yue and stood locked.
entries.literal: Thereupon Wensheng led the armies east; reaching Wuchang he met Hou Jing's general Ren Yue and locked in stalemate.

entries.zh: 久之，世祖又命護軍將軍尹悅、平東將軍杜幼安、巴州刺史王珣等會之，並受文盛節度。
entries.en: After long delay Shizu sent Yin Yue, Du You'an, Wang Xun, and others to join him, all under Wensheng.
entries.literal: After a long while Shizu again ordered Protector of the Army Yin Yue, Pacifying East general Du You'an, Ba prefecture governor Wang Xun and others to join him, all under Wensheng's command.

entries.zh: 擊任約於貝磯，約大敗，退保西陽。
entries.en: They fought Ren Yue at Shell Ford; Yue was routed and fell back on Xiyang.
entries.literal: They struck Ren Yue at Shell Ford; Yue was greatly defeated and withdrew to hold Xiyang.

entries.zh: 文盛進據蘆洲，又與相持。
entries.en: Wensheng took Reed Islet and faced him again.
entries.literal: Wensheng advanced and held Reed Islet, again in stalemate.

entries.zh: 侯景聞之，乃率大衆西上援約，至西陽。
entries.en: Hou Jing heard and led a great force west to save Yue, reaching Xiyang.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing heard, he led a great host west to relieve Yue, reaching Xiyang.

entries.zh: 文盛不敢戰。
entries.en: Wensheng would not give battle.
entries.literal: Wensheng did not dare fight.

entries.zh: 諸將咸曰：「景水軍輕進，又甚饑疲，可因此擊之，必大捷。」
entries.en: The generals said, "Jing's fleet came fast and is starving—we can strike now and win a great victory."
entries.literal: The generals all said: "Jing's river army advanced lightly and is very hungry and weary—we can strike now and surely win a great victory."

entries.zh: 文盛不許。
entries.en: Wensheng refused.
entries.literal: Wensheng did not permit it.

entries.zh: 文盛妻石氏，先在建鄴，至是，景載以還之。
entries.en: Wensheng's wife Lady Shi had been in Jiankang; Jing now sent her back to him.
entries.literal: Wensheng's wife the Lady Shi had been in Jiankang; at this time Jing conveyed her back to him.

entries.zh: 文盛深德景，遂密通信使，都無戰心，衆咸憤怨。
entries.en: Wensheng felt beholden to Jing and began secret correspondence; he would not fight—the army seethed with anger.
entries.literal: Wensheng felt deep obligation to Jing and then secretly exchanged envoys; he had no will to fight at all—the host was furious and resentful.

entries.zh: 杜幼安、守簉等乃率所領獨進，與景戰，大破之，獲其舟艦以歸。
entries.en: Du You'an, Shouzao, and others led their men out alone, fought Jing, smashed him, and brought back his ships.
entries.literal: Du You'an, the garrison officer Shouzao and others then led their detachments forward alone, fought Jing, and routed him greatly, capturing his boats and returning.

entries.zh: 會景密遣騎從間道襲陷郢州，軍中兇懼，遂大潰。
entries.en: Then Jing sent cavalry by a hidden road, took E prefecture, and the army collapsed in terror.
entries.literal: Just then Jing secretly sent cavalry by a hidden path to raid and seize E prefecture; the army was panic-stricken and utterly routed.

entries.zh: 文盛奔還荊州，世祖仍以爲城北面都督。
entries.en: Wensheng fled to Jingzhou; Shizu still made him commander of the north wall.
entries.literal: Wensheng fled back to Jingzhou; Shizu still made him commander of the north face of the city.

entries.zh: 又聚贓汚甚多，世祖大怒，下令責之，數其十罪，除其官爵。
entries.en: He had also piled up loot; Shizu raged, rebuked him, listed ten crimes, and stripped his titles.
entries.literal: He had also amassed much corrupt booty; Shizu was greatly angered, issued orders to reproach him, counted his ten crimes, and stripped rank and title.

entries.zh: 文盛旣失兵權，私懷怨望，世祖聞之，乃以下獄。
entries.en: Stripped of command, he nursed grievance; Shizu heard and jailed him.
entries.literal: Having lost military authority, he harbored private resentment; when Shizu heard, he was thrown into prison.

entries.zh: 時任約被擒，與文盛同禁。
entries.en: Ren Yue had been captured and shared his cell.
entries.literal: At the time Ren Yue had been captured and was imprisoned with Wensheng.

entries.zh: 文盛謂約曰：「汝何不早降，令我至此。」
entries.en: Wensheng said to Yue, "Why did you not surrender sooner and spare me this?"
entries.literal: Wensheng said to Yue: "Why did you not surrender early and put me in this plight?"

entries.zh: 約曰：「門外不見卿馬跡，使我何遽得降？」
entries.en: Yue said, "I saw no hoofprints of yours outside the gate—how could I surrender so soon?"
entries.literal: Yue said: "Outside the gate one saw no trace of your horses—how was I to surrender at once?"

entries.zh: 文盛無以答，遂死獄中。
entries.en: Wensheng had no reply and died in prison.
entries.literal: Wensheng had nothing to answer and died in prison.

entries.zh: 太清二年，隨岳陽王來襲荊州，世祖以與之有舊，密邀之。
entries.en: In Supreme Clarity year two he came with the Prince of Yueyang to attack Jingzhou; Shizu, who knew him of old, secretly called him over.
entries.literal: In the second year of Supreme Clarity he followed the Prince of Yueyang in coming to raid Jingzhou; Shizu, having old ties with him, secretly invited him.

entries.zh: 崱乃與兄岸、弟幼安、兄子龕等夜歸于世祖，世祖以爲持節、信威將軍、武州刺史。
entries.en: Ze came by night with his brother An, younger brother You'an, and nephew Kan; Shizu made him staff bearer, General of Trustworthy Might, and Wu inspector.
entries.literal: Ze then with his elder brother An, younger brother You'an, and nephew Kan by night returned to Shizu; Shizu made him bearer of the staff, General of Trustworthy Might, and inspector of Wu prefecture.

entries.zh: 俄遷宣毅將軍，領鎮蠻護軍、武陵內史，枝江縣侯，邑千戶。
entries.en: Soon he became General Who Chastises the Yi, Barbarian-quelling Protector, interior minister of Wuling, and Marquis of Zhijiang with a thousand households.
entries.literal: Before long he was transferred General Who Chastises the Yi, concurrently Barbarian-quelling Protector, interior minister of Wuling, and Marquis of Zhijiang with a fief of a thousand households.

entries.zh: 令隨王僧辯東討侯景。
entries.en: He was ordered to follow Wang Sengbian east against Hou Jing.
entries.literal: He was ordered to follow Wang Sengbian east to campaign against Hou Jing.

entries.zh: 至巴陵，會景來攻，數十日不剋而遁。
entries.en: At Baling Hou Jing attacked; after many days he could not win and fled.
