entries.literal: Reaching Baling, Jing came to attack; for many days he could not take it and fled.

entries.zh: 加侍中、左衛將軍，進爵爲公，增邑五百戶。
entries.en: He was made palace attendant and Left Guard general, raised to duke, fief increased five hundred households.
entries.literal: He was added palace attendant and Left Guard general, promoted in rank to duke, fief increased five hundred households.

entries.zh: 仍隨僧辯追景至石頭，與賊相持橫嶺。
entries.en: He followed Sengbian in pursuit to Stonehead and faced the bandit at Heng Ridge.
entries.literal: He still followed Sengbian pursuing Jing to Stonehead, stalemate with the bandit at Heng Ridge.

entries.zh: 及戰，景親率精銳，左右衝突，崱從嶺後橫截之，景乃大敗，東奔晉陵，崱入據城。
entries.en: In the fight Jing led his best men in person; Ze struck from behind the ridge; Jing was shattered and fled east to Jinling; Ze took the city.
entries.literal: In battle Jing personally led elites, charging left and right; Ze cut in from behind the ridge and Jing was greatly defeated, fleeing east to Jinling; Ze entered and held the city.

entries.zh: 景平，加散騎常侍、持節、督江州諸軍事、江州刺史，增邑千戶。
entries.en: When Jing fell he was added palace attendant, staff bearer, Jiang commander, and Jiang inspector—fief increased a thousand households.
entries.literal: When Jing was pacified he was added regular palace attendant, bearer of the staff, commander of Jiang military affairs, inspector of Jiang—fief increased a thousand households.

entries.zh: 是月，齊將郭元建攻秦州刺史嚴超遠於秦郡，王僧辯令崱赴援。
entries.en: That month Qi general Guo Yuanjian besieged Yan Chaoyuan at Qin; Wang Sengbian sent Ze to relieve him.
entries.literal: That month Qi general Guo Yuanjian attacked Qin prefecture inspector Yan Chaoyuan at Qin commandery; Wang Sengbian ordered Ze to relieve him.

entries.zh: 陳霸先亦自歐陽來會，與元建大戰于士林，霸先令強弩射，元建衆卻。
entries.en: Chen Baxian came from Ouyang to join; at Shilin they fought Guo Yuanjian; Baxian ordered heavy crossbows and Yuanjian's men fell back.
entries.literal: Chen Baxian also came from Ouyang to join; with Yuanjian they fought a great battle at Shilin; Baxian ordered strong crossbowmen to shoot and Yuanjian's host withdrew.

entries.zh: 崱因縱兵擊，大破之，斬首萬餘級，生擒千餘人，元建收餘衆而遁。
entries.en: Ze charged and broke them—ten thousand heads, a thousand prisoners; Yuanjian gathered what was left and fled.
entries.literal: Ze then released his troops to strike, routing them greatly—more than ten thousand heads cut, more than a thousand captured alive; Yuanjian gathered the remnant and fled.

entries.zh: 時世祖執王琳於江陵，其長史陸納等遂于長沙反，世祖徵崱與王僧辯討之。
entries.en: Shizu held Wang Lin at Jiangling; Lu Na rebelled at Changsha; Shizu called Ze and Wang Sengbian to suppress him.
entries.literal: At the time Shizu held Wang Lin at Jiangling; his chief clerk Lu Na and others then rebelled at Changsha; Shizu summoned Ze and Wang Sengbian to suppress them.

entries.zh: 承聖二年，及納等戰於車輪，大敗，陷其二壘，納等走保長沙，崱等圍之。
entries.en: In Chengsheng year two they fought Lu Na at Wheel Ford, took two forts, and drove him to Changsha; Ze besieged the city.
entries.literal: In Chengsheng year two they fought Na and others at Wheel Ford, were greatly victorious, took two of their forts; Na and others fled to hold Changsha; Ze and the others besieged them.

entries.zh: 後納等降，崱又與王僧辯西討武陵王於硤口，至卽破平之。
entries.en: When Na surrendered Ze went west with Wang Sengbian against the Prince of Wuling at Gorge Mouth and broke him at once.
entries.literal: Later Na and others surrendered; Ze again with Wang Sengbian campaigned west against the Prince of Wuling at Gorge Mouth—reaching there they broke and pacified him at once.

entries.zh: 於是旋鎮，遘疾卒。
entries.en: He returned to his post, fell ill, and died.
entries.literal: Thereupon he returned to his command but met illness and died.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「崱，京兆舊姓，元凱苗裔。
entries.en: The edict said, "Ze, of the ancient house of Jingzhao, line of Yuan Kai.
entries.literal: An edict said: "Ze—of the old surname of Jingzhao, descendant of Yuan Kai.

entries.zh: 家傳學業，世載忠貞。
entries.en: His clan carried learning; generation after generation served in loyalty.
entries.literal: His family transmitted learning; generation after generation bore loyal fidelity.

entries.zh: 自驅傳江渚，政號廉能。
entries.en: From service on the river isles his rule was called clean and capable.
entries.literal: From driving the relay-chariot on the river isles, his rule was called incorrupt and able.

entries.zh: 推轂淺原，實聞清靜。
entries.en: On the shallow fords of command one heard only of his quiet rule.
entries.literal: Pushing the chariot-wheel on the shallow ford, one truly heard of his quiet governance.

entries.zh: 奄致殞喪，惻愴于懷。
entries.en: Suddenly he is gone—grief pierces the heart.
entries.literal: Suddenly he met ruin and death—grief pierces the breast.

entries.zh: 可贈車騎將軍，加鼓吹一部。
entries.en: Let him be posthumously made General of Chariots and Cavalry, with martial music.
entries.literal: He may be posthumously made General of Chariots and Cavalry, with one suite of martial music added.

entries.zh: 諡曰武。」
entries.en: Posthumous title: Martial."
entries.literal: His posthumous title shall be Martial."

entries.zh: 岸，字公衡。
entries.en: An, styled Gongheng.
entries.literal: An, styled Gongheng.

entries.zh: 少有武幹，好從橫之術。
entries.en: From youth he had martial talent and loved bold stratagems.
entries.literal: From youth he had martial capacity and loved schemes of alliance and pressure.

entries.zh: 太清中，與崱同歸世祖，世祖以爲持節、平北將軍、北梁州刺史，封江陵縣侯，邑一千戶。
entries.en: In Supreme Clarity he returned with Ze; Shizu made him staff bearer, Pacifying North general, North Liang inspector, and Marquis of Jiangling with a thousand households.
entries.literal: In Supreme Clarity he returned with Ze to Shizu; Shizu made him bearer of the staff, Pacifying North general, inspector of North Liang, Marquis of Jiangling, fief a thousand households.

entries.zh: 岸因請襲襄陽，世祖許之。
entries.en: An asked to strike Xiangyang; Shizu agreed.
entries.literal: An thereupon requested to raid Xiangyang; Shizu granted it.

entries.zh: 岸乃晝夜兼行，先往攻其城，不剋。
entries.en: He marched day and night and struck the city first—but could not take it.
entries.literal: He marched day and night, first going to attack the city—but could not take it.

entries.zh: 岳陽至，遂走依其兄巘于南陽，巘時爲南陽太守。
entries.en: When the Prince of Yueyang came he fled to his brother Yan at Nanyang, who was then Nanyang governor.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Yueyang arrived he fled to rely on his brother Yan at Nanyang—Yan was then governor of Nanyang.

entries.zh: 岳陽尋遣攻陷其城，岸及巘俱遇害。
entries.en: The prince soon took the city; An and Yan both perished.
entries.literal: The Prince of Yueyang soon sent troops to take the city; An and Yan both met disaster.

entries.zh: 幼安性至孝，寬厚，雄勇過人。
entries.en: You'an was deeply filial, open-handed and mild, yet fiercer than most in battle.
entries.literal: You'an was utterly filial by nature, generous and mild, and surpassed others in fierce courage.

entries.zh: 太清中，與兄崱同歸世祖，世祖以爲雲麾將軍、西荊州刺史，封華容縣侯，邑一千戶。
entries.en: In Supreme Clarity he returned with Ze; Shizu made him Cloud Banner general, West Jing inspector, and Marquis of Huarong with a thousand households.
entries.literal: In Supreme Clarity he returned with his brother Ze to Shizu; Shizu made him Cloud Banner general, inspector of West Jing, Marquis of Huarong, fief a thousand households.

entries.zh: 令與平南將軍王僧辯討河東王譽於長沙，平之。
entries.en: He was ordered with Wang Sengbian to campaign against the Prince of Hedong at Changsha and pacify him.
entries.literal: He was ordered with Pacifying South general Wang Sengbian to campaign against the Prince of Hedong Yu at Changsha and pacify him.

entries.zh: 又命率精甲一萬，助左衛將軍徐文盛東討侯景。
entries.en: He was also told to lead ten thousand armored men to aid Xu Wensheng against Hou Jing.
entries.literal: He was also ordered to lead ten thousand picked armored troops to aid Left Guard general Xu Wensheng in the eastern campaign against Hou Jing.

entries.zh: 至貝磯，遇景將任約來逆，遂與戰，大敗之。
entries.en: At Shell Ford he met Ren Yue; they fought and broke him.
entries.literal: Reaching Shell Ford he met Jing's general Ren Yue coming to resist; they fought and routed him greatly.

entries.zh: 斬其儀同叱羅子通、湘州刺史趙威方等，傳首江陵。
entries.en: They cut off Chiluo Zitong, Zhao Weifang of Xiangzhou, and others, and sent the heads to Jiangling.
entries.literal: They beheaded his Staff Equal Chiluo Zitong, Xiangzhou inspector Zhao Weifang and others, and sent the heads to Jiangling.

entries.zh: 乃進軍大舉，因與景相持。
entries.en: Then the host pushed forward and faced Jing in stalemate.
entries.literal: Thereupon the army advanced in force and stalemate with Jing.

entries.zh: 別攻武昌，拔之。
entries.en: He also attacked Wuchang and took it.
entries.literal: Separately he attacked Wuchang and took it.

entries.zh: 景渡蘆洲上流以壓文盛等，幼安與衆軍攻之，景大敗，盡獲其舟艦。
entries.en: Jing moved above Reed Islet to crush Wensheng; You'an attacked with the army, shattered Jing, and seized every ship.
entries.literal: Jing crossed upstream of Reed Islet to press Wensheng and the others; You'an with the host attacked and Jing was greatly defeated, all his boats captured.

entries.zh: 會景密遣襲陷郢州，執刺史方諸等以歸，人情大駭，徐文盛由漢口遁歸，衆軍大敗，幼安遂降于景。
entries.en: Then Jing sent raiders by a hidden road, took E prefecture, and captured Fang Zhu; panic spread; Wensheng fled up the Han; the army collapsed; You'an surrendered to Jing.
entries.literal: Just then Jing secretly sent a raid that seized E prefecture, capturing inspector Fang Zhu and others and returning; morale was greatly shaken; Xu Wensheng fled by Hankou; the armies were utterly routed; You'an then surrendered to Jing.

entries.zh: 景殺之，以其多反覆故也。
entries.en: Jing killed him for his repeated betrayals.
entries.literal: Jing killed him—for his many vacillations.

entries.zh: 龕，崱第二兄岑之子。
entries.en: Kan was son of Ze's second brother Cen.
entries.literal: Kan was son of Ze's second elder brother Cen.

entries.zh: 少驍勇，善用兵，亦太清中與諸父同歸世祖，世祖以爲持節、忠武將軍、鄖州刺史，中廬縣侯，邑一千戶。
entries.en: From youth he was fierce and knew war; in Supreme Clarity he returned with his uncles; Shizu made him staff bearer, General of Loyal Martial, Yun inspector, and Marquis of Zhonglu with a thousand households.
entries.literal: From youth fierce and brave, skilled at using troops; also in Supreme Clarity he returned with his uncles to Shizu; Shizu made him bearer of the staff, General of Loyal Martial, inspector of Yun, Marquis of Zhonglu, fief a thousand households.

entries.zh: 與叔幼安俱隨王僧辯討河東王，平之。
entries.en: With his uncle You'an he followed Wang Sengbian against the Prince of Hedong and pacified him.
entries.literal: With his uncle You'an he followed Wang Sengbian to campaign against the Prince of Hedong and pacified him.

entries.zh: 又隨僧辯下，繼徐文盛軍至巴陵，聞侯景襲陷郢州，西上將至，乃與僧辯等守巴陵以待之。
entries.en: Following Sengbian downriver he took over Wensheng's line at Baling; hearing Jing had taken E and was coming west, he and Sengbian held Baling to meet him.
entries.literal: Again following Sengbian downstream he continued Xu Wensheng's army to Baling; hearing Hou Jing had raided and seized E prefecture and was coming west, he with Sengbian and the others held Baling to await him.

entries.zh: 景至，圍之數旬，不剋而遁。
entries.en: Jing besieged it for weeks, failed, and fled.
entries.literal: When Jing arrived he besieged it many weeks, could not take it, and fled.

entries.zh: 遷太府卿、安北將軍、督定州諸軍事、定州刺史，加通直散騎常侍，增邑五百戶。
entries.en: He became Grand Treasurer, Pacifying North general, Ding commander and inspector, Direct and Regular Palace Attendant, fief up five hundred households.
entries.literal: He was transferred Grand Treasurer, Pacifying North general, commander of Ding military affairs, inspector of Ding, added Direct and Regular Palace Attendant, fief increased five hundred households.

entries.zh: 仍隨僧辯追景至江夏，圍其城。
entries.en: He followed Sengbian in pursuit to Jiangxia and besieged the city.
entries.literal: He still followed Sengbian pursuing Jing to Jiangxia and besieged the city.

entries.zh: 景將宋子仙棄城遁，龕追至楊浦，生擒之。
entries.en: Song Zixian abandoned the city and fled; Kan chased to Yangpu and took him alive.
entries.literal: Jing's general Song Zixian abandoned the city and fled; Kan pursued to Yangpu and captured him alive.

entries.zh: 大寶三年，衆軍至姑孰，景將侯子鑒逆戰，龕與陳霸先、王琳等率精銳擊之，大敗子鑒，遂至於石頭。
entries.en: In Great Treasure year three the armies reached Gushu; Hou Zijian met them; Kan with Chen Baxian and Wang Lin led elites, broke Zijian, and pushed on to Stonehead.
entries.literal: In the third year of Great Treasure the armies reached Gushu; Jing's general Hou Zijian met them in battle; Kan with Chen Baxian, Wang Lin and others led crack troops to strike, routing Zijian greatly, and reached Stonehead.

entries.zh: 景親率其黨會戰，龕與衆軍奮擊，大破景，景遂東奔。
entries.en: Jing fought in person; Kan and the host struck hard, shattered him, and Jing fled east.
entries.literal: Jing personally led his faction to join battle; Kan with the armies fought fiercely, routing Jing greatly; Jing fled east.

entries.zh: 論功爲最，授平東將軍、東揚州刺史，益封一千戶。
entries.en: His merit ranked first; he was made Pacifying East general, East Yang inspector, fief up a thousand households.
entries.literal: For merit he was first; he was made Pacifying East general, inspector of East Yang, fief increased a thousand households.

entries.zh: 子春，天監初，起家宣惠將軍、西陽太守。
entries.en: Zichun began under Heavenly Surveillance as General of Manifest Grace and Xiyang governor.
entries.literal: Zichun, at the beginning of Heavenly Surveillance, began office as General of Manifest Grace and governor of Xiyang.

entries.zh: 普通中，累遷至明威將軍、南梁州刺史；
entries.en: In the Ordinary era he rose to General of Bright Might and South Liang inspector;
entries.literal: In the Ordinary era he was repeatedly promoted to General of Bright Might and inspector of South Liang;

entries.zh: 又遷信威將軍、都督梁、秦、華三州諸軍事、梁、秦二州刺史。
entries.en: then General of Trustworthy Might, commander of Liang, Qin, and Hua, and inspector of Liang and Qin.
entries.literal: also transferred General of Trustworthy Might, commander of Liang, Qin, and Hua military affairs, inspector of Liang and Qin.

entries.zh: 太清二年，討峽中叛蠻，平之。
entries.en: In Supreme Clarity year two he put down rebel tribes in the gorges.
entries.literal: In the second year of Supreme Clarity he campaigned against rebel barbarians in the gorges and pacified them.

entries.zh: 徵爲左衛將軍，又遷侍中。
entries.en: He was summoned as Left Guard general, then made palace attendant.
entries.literal: He was summoned as Left Guard general, then transferred palace attendant.

entries.zh: 屬侯景亂，世祖令子春隨領軍將軍王僧辯攻邵陵王於郢州，平之。
entries.en: When Hou Jing rebelled Shizu ordered Zichun to follow Wang Sengbian against the Prince of Shaoling at E and pacify him.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled Shizu ordered Zichun to follow General Who Commands the Army Wang Sengbian in attacking the Prince of Shaoling at E prefecture and pacifying him.

entries.zh: 又與左衛將軍徐文盛東討侯景，至貝磯，與景遇，子春力戰，恒冠諸軍，頻敗景。
entries.en: Again with Xu Wensheng he marched east against Hou Jing; at Shell Ford they met Jing; Zichun fought at the fore and beat him again and again.
entries.literal: Again with Left Guard general Xu Wensheng he campaigned east against Hou Jing; reaching Shell Ford they met Jing; Zichun fought fiercely, always foremost among the armies, repeatedly defeating Jing.

entries.zh: 值郢州陷沒，軍遂退敗。
entries.en: When E prefecture fell the army retreated in rout.
entries.literal: When E prefecture fell the armies then retreated in defeat.

entries.zh: 大寶二年，卒於江陵。
entries.en: In Great Treasure year two he died at Jiangling.
entries.literal: In the second year of Great Treasure he died at Jiangling.

entries.zh: 承聖二年，又與王僧辯討陸納等於長沙，降之。
entries.en: In Chengsheng year two he again followed Wang Sengbian against Lu Na at Changsha and forced surrender.
entries.literal: In Chengsheng year two he again with Wang Sengbian suppressed Lu Na and others at Changsha and made them surrender.

entries.zh: 又征武陵王於西陵，亦平之。
entries.en: He also campaigned against the Prince of Wuling at Xiling and pacified him.
entries.literal: Again he campaigned against the Prince of Wuling at Xiling and likewise pacified him.

entries.zh: 後江陵陷，齊納貞陽侯以紹梁嗣，以龕爲震州刺史、吳興太守。
entries.en: After Jiangling fell Qi set up the True Yang Marquis to continue Liang; Kan became Zhen inspector and Wuxing governor.
entries.literal: Later Jiangling fell; Qi installed the True Yang Marquis to continue Liang; Kan was made inspector of Zhen and governor of Wuxing.

entries.zh: 又除鎮南將軍、都督南豫州諸軍事、南豫州刺史、溧陽縣侯，給鼓吹一部。
entries.en: He was also made Pacifying South general, South Yu commander and inspector, Marquis of Liyang, with martial music.
entries.literal: Also made Pacifying South general, commander of South Yu military affairs, inspector of South Yu, Marquis of Liyang, given a suite of martial music.

entries.zh: 又加散騎常侍、鎮東大將軍。
entries.en: He was also made Regular Palace Attendant and Great General Who Pacifies the East.
entries.literal: Also added Regular Palace Attendant and Great General Who Pacifies the East.

entries.zh: 會陳霸先襲陷京師，執王僧辯殺之。
entries.en: Then Chen Baxian seized the capital, took Wang Sengbian, and killed him.
entries.literal: Just then Chen Baxian raided and seized the capital, seized Wang Sengbian and killed him.

entries.zh: 龕，僧辯之婿也，爲吳興太守。
entries.en: Kan was Sengbian's son-in-law and governor of Wuxing.
entries.literal: Kan, Sengbian's son-in-law, was governor of Wuxing.

entries.zh: 以霸先旣非貴素，兵又猥雜，在軍府日，都不以霸先經心；
entries.en: Baxian was low-born and his troops were a rabble; in headquarters days Kan never took him seriously;
entries.literal: Because Baxian was not of noble birth and his troops were crude and mixed, in headquarters days Kan never took Baxian to heart;

entries.zh: 及爲本郡，每以法繩其宗門，無所縱捨，霸先銜之切齒。
entries.en: as home governor he bound his clan by law without mercy—Baxian hated him to the bone.
entries.literal: when he became governor of his home commandery he constantly bound his clan by law without indulgence—Baxian hated him to the teeth.

entries.zh: 及僧辯敗，龕乃據吳興以距之，遣軍副杜泰攻陳蒨於長城，反爲蒨所敗。
entries.en: When Sengbian fell Kan held Wuxing against him and sent Du Tai to strike Chen Qian at Changcheng—but Qian beat him.
entries.literal: When Sengbian was defeated Kan then held Wuxing to resist him, sending deputy Du Tai to attack Chen Qian at Changcheng—but was in turn defeated by Qian.

entries.zh: 霸先乃遣將周文育討龕，龕令從弟北叟出距，又爲文育所破，走義興，霸先親率衆圍之。
entries.en: Baxian sent Zhou Wenyun against him; Kan sent his cousin Beisou out and was beaten again; he fled to Yixing and Baxian besieged him in person.
entries.literal: Baxian then sent general Zhou Wenyun to campaign against Kan; Kan sent his cousin Beisou out to resist and was again broken by Wenyun; he fled to Yixing and Baxian personally led troops to besiege him.

entries.zh: 會齊將柳達摩等襲京師，霸先恐，遂還與齊人連和。
entries.en: Then Liu Damo of Qi struck the capital; Baxian feared and turned back to treat with Qi.
entries.literal: Just then Qi general Liu Damo and others raided the capital; Baxian was afraid and returned to ally with the Qi men.

entries.zh: 龕聞齊兵還，乃降，遂遇害。
entries.en: When Kan heard Qi had withdrawn he surrendered—and was killed.
entries.literal: When Kan heard the Qi army had withdrawn he surrendered and then met disaster.

entries.zh: 梁書卷第四十六 列傳第四十
entries.en: Book of Liang, Volume 46, Biography 40
entries.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 46, Biography 40

entries.zh: 滕曇恭，豫章南昌人也。
entries.en: Teng Tangong came from Nanchang in Yuzhang.
entries.literal: Teng Tangong came from Nanchang in Yuzhang.

entries.zh: 年五歲，母楊氏患熱，思食寒瓜，土俗所不產。
entries.en: When he was five, his mother, Lady Yang, suffered from a fever and longed to eat cold melon, but the local custom did not produce it.
entries.literal: When he was five, his mother, Lady Yang, suffered from a fever and longed to eat cold melon, but the local custom did not produce it.

entries.zh: 曇恭歷訪不能得，銜悲哀切。
entries.en: Tangong searched everywhere but could not obtain any, and he held grief in his heart with deep sorrow.
entries.literal: Tangong searched everywhere but could not obtain any, and he held grief in his heart with deep sorrow.

entries.zh: 俄值一桑門問其故，曇恭具以告。
entries.en: Soon he encountered a Buddhist monk who asked the reason, and Tangong told him everything.
entries.literal: Soon he encountered a Buddhist monk who asked the reason, and Tangong told him everything.

entries.zh: 桑門曰：「我有兩瓜，分一相遺。」
entries.en: The monk said, "I have two melons; I will give you one of them."
entries.literal: The monk said, "I have two melons; I will give you one of them."

entries.zh: 曇恭拜謝，因捧瓜還，以薦其母。
entries.en: Tangong bowed in thanks, then carried the melon home and presented it to his mother.
entries.literal: Tangong bowed in thanks, then carried the melon home and presented it to his mother.

entries.zh: 舉室驚異。
entries.en: The whole household was amazed.
entries.literal: The whole household was amazed.

entries.zh: 尋訪桑門，莫知所在。
entries.en: When they soon searched for the monk, no one knew where he was.
entries.literal: When they soon searched for the monk, no one knew where he was.

entries.zh: 及父母卒，曇恭水漿不入口者旬日，感慟嘔血，絕而復蘇。
entries.en: When his parents died, Tangong took neither water nor gruel for ten days; overcome with grief, he vomited blood, lost consciousness, and then revived.
entries.literal: When his parents died, Tangong took neither water nor gruel for ten days; overcome with grief, he vomited blood, lost consciousness, and then revived.

entries.zh: 隆冬不著繭絮，蔬食終身。
entries.en: In the depth of winter he wore no padded silk or floss, and he ate vegetables for the rest of his life.
entries.literal: In the depth of winter he wore no padded silk or floss, and he ate vegetables for the rest of his life.

entries.zh: 每至忌日，思慕不自堪，晝夜哀慟。
entries.en: Whenever the death anniversaries arrived, longing overcame him, and he wailed in grief day and night.
entries.literal: Whenever the death anniversaries arrived, longing overcame him, and he wailed in grief day and night.

entries.zh: 其門外有冬生樹二株，時忽有神光自樹而起，俄見佛像及夾侍之儀，容光顯著，自門而入。
entries.en: Outside his gate stood two winter-growing trees. At one point divine light suddenly rose from the trees, and soon a Buddha image and attendant figures appeared, their radiant forms clearly visible, entering through the gate.
entries.literal: Outside his gate stood two winter-growing trees. At one point divine light suddenly rose from the trees, and soon a Buddha image and attendant figures appeared, their radiant forms clearly visible, entering through the gate.

entries.zh: 曇恭家人大小，咸共禮拜，久之乃滅，遠近道俗咸傳之。
entries.en: All the members of Tangong's household, great and small, bowed in worship together; after a long while it vanished, and Daoists, Buddhists, and laypeople far and near all passed on the story.
entries.literal: All the members of Tangong's household, great and small, bowed in worship together; after a long while it vanished, and Daoists, Buddhists, and laypeople far and near all passed on the story.

entries.zh: 太守王僧度引曇恭爲功曹，固辭不就。
entries.en: Administrator Wang Sengdu summoned Tangong to serve as merit officer, but he firmly declined and did not take the post.
entries.literal: Administrator Wang Sengdu summoned Tangong to serve as merit officer, but he firmly declined and did not take the post.

entries.zh: 王儉時隨僧度在郡，號爲滕曾子。
entries.en: Wang Jian was then in the commandery with Sengdu and called him Teng Zengzi.
entries.literal: Wang Jian was then in the commandery with Sengdu and called him Teng Zengzi.

entries.zh: 天監元年，陸璉奉使巡行風俗，表言其狀。
entries.en: In Tianjian 1, Lu Lian received an imperial mission to inspect local customs and submitted a memorial describing Tangong's conduct.
entries.literal: In Tianjian 1, Lu Lian received an imperial mission to inspect local customs and submitted a memorial describing Tangong's conduct.

entries.zh: 曇恭有子三人，皆有行業。
entries.en: Tangong had three sons, all of whom had virtuous conduct.
entries.literal: Tangong had three sons, all of whom had virtuous conduct.

entries.zh: 沈崇傃字思整，吳興武康人也。
entries.en: Shen Chongsu, styled Si Zheng, was from Wukang in Wuxing.
entries.literal: Shen Chongsu, courtesy name Si Zheng, was a man of Wukang in Wuxing.

entries.zh: 父懷明，宋兗州刺史。
entries.en: His father Huaiming had been Song Inspector of Yanzhou.
entries.literal: His father Huaiming had been Inspector of Yanzhou under Song.

entries.zh: 崇傃六歲丁父憂，哭踴過禮。
entries.en: At six he lost his father and mourned beyond propriety.
entries.literal: At six Chongsu suffered his father's death and wept and stamped beyond the rites.

entries.zh: 及長，傭書以養母焉。
entries.en: Grown, he copied books to feed his mother.
entries.literal: When grown he copied books to support his mother.

entries.zh: 齊建武初，起家爲奉朝請。
entries.en: In early Jianwu he entered service as Attendant at Court.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Jianwu era he first took office as Attendant at Court.

entries.zh: 永元末，遷司徒行參軍。
entries.en: At Yongyuan's end he became staff aide to the Minister of Education.
entries.literal: At the end of the Yongyuan era he was promoted to staff aide in the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 天監初，爲前軍鄱陽王參軍事。
entries.en: Early in Tianjian he was staff officer to the Forward Army's Prince of Poyang.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Tianjian era he served as staff officer to the Prince of Poyang in the Forward Army.

entries.zh: 三年，太守柳惲辟爲主簿。
entries.en: In year three Prefect Liu Yun made him chief clerk.
entries.literal: In the third year the prefect Liu Yun engaged him as chief clerk.

entries.zh: 崇傃從惲到郡，還迎其母，母卒。
entries.en: Chongsu went with Yun to the prefecture, then went back for his mother; she died on the way.
entries.literal: Chongsu followed Yun to the commandery, then returned to fetch his mother; his mother died.

entries.zh: 崇傃以不及侍疾，將欲致死，水漿不入口，晝夜號哭，旬日殆將絕氣。
entries.en: Having missed her sickbed, he meant to die: no food or drink, weeping day and night until in ten days he was all but gone.
entries.literal: Chongsu, because he had not been able to tend her in her illness, was about to die himself: he would not take water or food and wept day and night; in ten days he was nearly dead.

entries.zh: 兄弟謂之曰：「殯葬未申，遽自毀滅，非全孝之道也。」
entries.en: His brothers said, "The funeral is not settled—if you kill yourself now, that is not complete filial duty."
entries.literal: His brothers said to him: "The burial is not yet arranged—if you destroy yourself in haste, that is not the full way of filial piety."

entries.zh: 崇傃之瘞所，不避雨雪，倚墳哀慟。
entries.en: He would not leave the grave in rain or snow and leaned on the mound wailing.
entries.literal: At the burial ground Chongsu did not avoid rain or snow but leaned on the mound in grief.

entries.zh: 每夜恒有猛獸來望之，有聲狀如歎息者。
entries.en: Nightly wild beasts came to watch him, sighing as they came.
entries.literal: Each night fierce beasts would come to look upon him, with sounds like sighing.

entries.zh: 家貧無以遷窆，乃行乞經年，始獲葬焉。
entries.en: Too poor to rebury her, he begged a full year before he could lay her to rest.
entries.literal: The family was poor and could not move the grave; he begged for a year before he could bury her.

entries.zh: 旣而廬於墓側，自以初行喪禮不備，復以葬後更治服三年。
entries.en: Then he hutched beside the tomb; thinking the first mourning rites incomplete, he wore mourning again for three years after burial.
entries.literal: Thereafter he built a hut beside the tomb; because he felt his first mourning had been incomplete, after the burial he observed mourning dress again for three years.

entries.zh: 久食麥屑，不啖鹽酢，坐臥于單薦，因虛腫不能起。
entries.en: He lived on bran without salt or vinegar, sat and slept on one thin mat, and swelled so weak he could not stand.
entries.literal: For long he ate only wheat bran and would not touch salt or vinegar; he sat and lay on a single mat until, from emaciation, he could not rise.

entries.zh: 郡縣舉其至孝。
entries.en: Commandery and county commended his extreme filiality.
entries.literal: The commandery and county reported his utmost filial piety.

entries.zh: 高祖聞，卽遣中書舍人慰勉之，乃下詔曰：「前軍沈崇傃，少有志行，居喪逾禮。
entries.en: Gaozu heard and sent a Secretariat Attendant to comfort him, then issued an edict: "Forward Army Shen Chongsu showed resolve young and mourning beyond measure.
entries.literal: When Gaozu heard, he at once sent a Secretariat Attendant to comfort and encourage him, and issued an edict saying: "Shen Chongsu of the Forward Army, in youth had resolve and conduct; in mourning he exceeded the rites.

entries.zh: 齋制不終，未得大葬，自以行乞淹年，哀典多闕，方欲以永慕之晨，更爲再朞之始。
entries.en: His fast was unfinished and the great burial undone; after a year of begging the rites still lacked, and he would begin another mourning cycle from that dawn of grief.
entries.literal: His fast was not finished and the great burial had not been performed; he himself felt that a year of begging had left the funeral rites much wanting, and he meant to begin a second mourning term from the morning of everlasting longing.

entries.zh: 雖卽情可矜，禮有明斷。
entries.en: Pity his heart, but rites have limits.
entries.literal: Though feeling may be pitiable, the rites have clear limits.

entries.zh: 可便令除釋，擢補太子洗馬。
entries.en: Release him from mourning and appoint Crown Prince's Household Steward.
entries.literal: Let him at once be released from mourning dress and promoted to fill the post of Crown Prince's Household Steward.

entries.zh: 旌彼門閭，敦茲風教。」
entries.en: Honor his household and strengthen this custom."
entries.literal: Honor his gate and lane and thicken this teaching of custom."

entries.zh: 崇傃奉詔釋服，而涕泣如居喪，固辭不受官，苦自陳讓，經年乃得爲永寧令。
entries.en: He obeyed and doffed mourning but wept as in bereavement, refused the post, pleaded hard, and only after a year took Yongning magistracy.
entries.literal: Chongsu received the edict and put off mourning dress, yet wept as if still in mourning; he firmly refused the office, pleaded bitterly, and only after a year did he become magistrate of Yongning.

entries.zh: 自以祿不及養，怛恨愈甚，哀思不自堪，至縣卒，時年三十九。
entries.en: His stipend could no longer feed his mother; grief overwhelmed him and he died in office at thirty-nine.
entries.literal: He felt that his salary could no longer nourish his mother; regret and grief grew worse, his sorrow unbearable, and at the county he died, aged thirty-nine.

entries.zh: 荀匠字文師，潁陰人，晉太保勗九世孫也。
entries.en: Xun Jiang, styled Wen Shi, of Yingyin, was ninth generation from Jin Grand Tutor Xun Xu.
entries.literal: Xun Jiang, courtesy name Wen Shi, was a man of Yingyin, ninth-generation descendant of Jin Grand Tutor Xun Xu.

entries.zh: 祖瓊，年十五，復父仇於成都市，以孝聞。
entries.en: His grandfather Qiong at fifteen avenged his father in Chengdu market and won fame for filial piety.
entries.literal: His grandfather Qiong, at fifteen, avenged his father's death in Chengdu market and was known for filial piety.

entries.zh: 宋元嘉末，渡淮赴武陵王義，爲元凶追兵所殺，贈員外散騎侍郎。
entries.en: Late in Song Yuanjia he crossed the Huai for Prince of Wuling Yi, was killed by the crown prince's pursuers, and was posthumously made Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
entries.literal: At the end of the Yuanjia era of Song he crossed the Huai to join Prince of Wuling Yi and was killed by the crown prince's pursuing troops; posthumously he was given the title Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

entries.zh: 父法超，齊中興末爲安復令，卒於官。
entries.en: His father Fachao, late in Qi Zhongxing, was Anfu magistrate and died in office.
entries.literal: His father Fachao, at the end of the Zhongxing era of Qi, was magistrate of Anfu and died in office.

entries.zh: 凶問至，匠號慟氣絕，身體皆冷，至夜乃蘇。
entries.en: When word came he wailed himself breathless and cold; only at night did he wake.
entries.literal: When the dire news arrived Jiang wailed until his breath stopped and his whole body was cold; only at night did he revive.

entries.zh: 旣而奔喪，每宿江渚，商旅皆不忍聞其哭聲。
entries.en: Rushing to the funeral he lodged nightly on the river sandbars; travelers could not bear his crying.
entries.literal: Then he hurried to the mourning; each night he lodged on the river islets, and travelers could not bear to hear his weeping.

entries.zh: 服未闋，兄斐起家爲鬰林太守，征俚賊，爲流矢所中，死於陣。
entries.en: Mourning unfinished, his brother Fei became Yulin governor, fought the Liao raiders, took a stray arrow, and died on the field.
entries.literal: Before mourning was finished his elder brother Fei first took office as governor of Yulin, campaigned against the Liao bandits, was struck by a stray arrow, and died in battle.

entries.zh: 喪還，匠迎于豫章，望舟投水，傍人赴救，僅而得全。
entries.en: The bier returning, he met it at Yuzhang, saw the boat, and leapt into the river; bystanders barely saved him.
entries.literal: When the coffin returned Jiang met it at Yuzhang, saw the boat, and threw himself into the water; those beside him rescued him and he barely survived.

entries.zh: 旣至，家貧不得時葬。
entries.en: Home again, they were too poor to bury on time.
entries.literal: When he arrived, the family was poor and could not bury in season.

entries.zh: 居父憂並兄服，歷四年不出廬戶。
entries.en: He mourned father and brother together—four years without leaving the mourning hut.
entries.literal: He observed mourning for his father together with mourning for his brother—four years without leaving the hut door.

entries.zh: 自括發後，不復櫛沐，髮皆禿落。
entries.en: From binding his hair he never combed or bathed, and his hair fell out.
entries.literal: After he bound up his hair he never combed or washed again, and his hair all fell out.

entries.zh: 哭無時，聲盡則係之以泣，目眥皆爛，形體枯顇，皮骨裁連，雖家人不復識。
entries.en: He wept without cease; when voice failed he sobbed on; his eyelids rotted, his body skeletal; kin scarcely knew him.
entries.literal: He wept without fixed times; when his voice was gone he tied on sobbing, his eyelids all ulcerated, his form withered and gaunt, skin and bone barely joined—even his family no longer knew him.

entries.zh: 郡縣以狀言，高祖詔遣中書舍人爲其除服，擢爲豫章王國左常侍。
entries.en: Commandery and county reported; Gaozu sent a Secretariat Attendant to release mourning and make him Left Regular Attendant in Prince of Yuzhang's kingdom.
entries.literal: The commandery and county reported the facts; Gaozu issued an edict that a Secretariat Attendant should release him from mourning and promote him to Left Regular Attendant in the Kingdom of the Prince of Yuzhang.

entries.zh: 匠雖卽吉，毀顇逾甚。
entries.en: Though he left mourning, his wasting grew worse.
entries.literal: Though Jiang had returned to the ordinary calendar, his devastation grew worse.

entries.zh: 外祖孫謙誡之曰：「主上以孝治天下，汝行過古人，故發明詔，擢汝此職。
entries.en: His maternal grandfather Sun Qian warned him: "The throne rules by filial piety; your conduct exceeds the ancients, hence the edict and this appointment.
entries.literal: His maternal grandfather Sun Qian admonished him, saying: "The sovereign rules the realm by filial piety; your conduct surpasses the ancients, and therefore the bright edict was issued and you were raised to this post.

entries.zh: 非唯君父之命難拒，故亦揚名後世，所顯豈獨汝身哉！」
entries.en: You cannot only refuse a lord-father's command—you will win fame for ages; the glory is not yours alone!"
entries.literal: It is not only that a lord and father's command is hard to refuse—you will also make a name for later ages; the glory shown is not yours alone!"

entries.zh: 匠於是乃拜。
entries.en: Then Jiang accepted the post.
entries.literal: Thereupon Jiang bowed in acceptance.

entries.zh: 竟以毀卒於家，時年二十一。
entries.en: He died at home of grief at twenty-one.
entries.literal: In the end, from devastation he died at home, aged twenty-one.

entries.zh: 吉翂字彥霄，馮翊蓮勺人也。
entries.en: Ji Bin, styled Yan Xiao, was from Lianzhao in Fengyi.
entries.literal: Ji Bin, courtesy name Yan Xiao, was a man of Lianzhao in Fengyi.

entries.zh: 世居襄陽。
entries.en: The clan had long lived in Xiangyang.
entries.literal: For generations the family dwelt in Xiangyang.

entries.zh: 翂幼有孝性。
entries.en: From childhood Bin was filial.
entries.literal: Bin from childhood had a filial nature.

entries.zh: 年十一，遭所生母憂，水漿不入口，殆將滅性，親黨異之。
entries.en: At eleven he mourned his birth mother, took no food or drink, nearly died of grief, and kin marveled.
entries.literal: At eleven he suffered mourning for his birth mother; he would not take water or broth and was nearly destroyed in nature; kin and neighbors marveled at him.

entries.zh: 天監初，父爲吳興原鄉令，爲姦吏所誣，逮詣廷尉。
entries.en: Early in Tianjian his father was Yuan township magistrate in Wuxing, was framed by a corrupt clerk, and was sent to the Court of Justice.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Tianjian era his father was magistrate of Yuan township in Wuxing and was slandered by a corrupt clerk and seized and sent to the Court of Justice.

entries.zh: 翂年十五，號泣衢路，祈請公卿，行人見者，皆爲隕涕。
entries.en: Bin at fifteen wailed in the streets, pleading with high officials; every passerby wept.
entries.literal: Bin, aged fifteen, wept and wailed in the public streets, begging the high ministers; passersby who saw him all shed tears.

entries.zh: 其父理雖清白，恥爲吏訊，乃虛自引咎，罪當大辟。
entries.en: Though his father was innocent, he was shamed to be examined as a criminal and falsely confessed; the penalty was death.
entries.literal: Though his father's case was in truth innocent, he was ashamed to be questioned as a criminal and therefore falsely confessed guilt himself; the crime called for the great execution.

entries.zh: 翂乃撾登聞鼓，乞代父命。
entries.en: Bin then struck the petition drum and begged to die for his father.
entries.literal: Bin then beat the petition drum at the palace gate and begged to die in his father's place.

entries.zh: 高祖異之，敕廷尉卿蔡法度曰：「吉翂請死贖父，義誠可嘉；
entries.en: Gaozu was moved and ordered Minister of Justice Cai Fadu: "Ji Bin asks to die for his father—his loyalty is admirable;
entries.literal: Gaozu marveled at it and ordered the Minister of Justice Cai Fadu, saying: "Ji Bin asks to die to redeem his father—the righteousness and sincerity are truly admirable;

entries.zh: 但其幼童，未必自能造意。
entries.en: but he is a child and may not have thought of this himself.
entries.literal: but he is still a young child and may not himself have formed the intent.

entries.zh: 卿可嚴加脅誘，取其款實。」
entries.en: Coerce and entice him strictly and get the full truth."
entries.literal: You may strictly coerce and entice him and obtain his full confession."

entries.zh: 法度受敕還寺，盛陳徽纏，備列官司，厲色問翂曰：「爾求代父死，敕已相許，便應伏法。
entries.en: Fadu took the order, returned to court, spread out chains and fetters, lined up the officials, and sternly asked Bin: "You ask to die for your father—the edict already grants it; you should submit to execution.
entries.literal: Fadu received the order and returned to his office; he displayed fetters and chains in profusion, arrayed the officials in full, and with stern countenance questioned Bin, saying: "You ask to die in your father's place—the edict has already granted it, and you ought to submit to the law.

entries.zh: 然刀鋸至劇，審能死不？
entries.en: But blade and saw are cruel—can you truly die?
entries.literal: Yet knife and saw are most severe—can you in truth face death?

entries.zh: 且爾童孺，志不及此，必爲人所教。
entries.en: You are only a boy; your heart cannot reach here—you were taught by someone.
entries.literal: Moreover you are a mere child; your will does not reach to this—you must have been taught by someone.

entries.zh: 姓名是誰，可具列答。
entries.en: Name him—answer fully.
entries.literal: What is his name—give a full list in answer.

entries.zh: 若有悔異，亦相聽許。」
entries.en: If you repent, we will hear it."
entries.literal: If you repent and change your mind, that too will be allowed."

entries.zh: 翂對曰：「囚雖蒙弱，豈不知死可畏憚？
entries.en: Bin answered: "Though I am weak, do I not know death is fearful?
entries.literal: Bin answered: "Though the prisoner is feeble and weak, does he not know that death is to be feared?

entries.zh: 顧諸弟稚藐，唯囚爲長，不忍見父極刑，自延視息。
entries.en: My brothers are small; I alone am eldest—I cannot watch my father die while I live on.
entries.literal: But my younger brothers are young and small; only the prisoner is the eldest—I cannot bear to see my father suffer the extreme penalty and myself prolong my breath.

entries.zh: 所以內斷胸臆，上干萬乘。
entries.en: So I broke my heart within and troubled the throne above.
entries.literal: Therefore I cut off my heart within and troubled the Son of Heaven above.

entries.zh: 今欲殉身不測，委骨泉壤，此非細故，奈何受人教邪！
entries.en: Now I would throw my body into the unknown and leave my bones underground—this is no small thing; how could another teach me!
entries.literal: Now I wish to cast away my body into the unknown and leave my bones in the springs and mounds—this is no small matter; how could I accept another's teaching!

entries.zh: 明詔聽代，不異登仙，豈有回貳！」
entries.en: The clear edict lets me substitute—it is like ascending to immortality; how could I waver!"
entries.literal: The bright edict permits substitution—no different from ascending as an immortal; how could there be second thoughts!"

entries.zh: 法度知翂至心有在，不可屈撓，乃更和顏誘語之曰：「主上知尊侯無罪，行當釋亮。
entries.en: Fadu saw Bin's heart could not be broken; he softened and said, "The throne knows your father is innocent and will free him soon.
entries.literal: Fadu knew Bin's resolve was fixed and could not be bent; he changed to gentle persuasion and said, "The emperor knows your honored father is guiltless and will soon release him.

entries.zh: 觀君神儀明秀，足稱佳童，今若轉辭，幸父子同濟。
entries.en: You are bright and handsome, a model youth—turn back now and father and son may yet be spared.
entries.literal: You look bright and noble—truly a fine youth. If you change your plea now, perhaps father and son may both be saved.

entries.zh: 奚以此妙年，苦求湯鑊？」
entries.en: Why at this tender age court the boiling cauldron?"
entries.literal: Why in the flower of youth do you seek the cauldron and blade so bitterly?"

entries.zh: 翂對曰：「凡鯤鮞螻蟻，尚惜其生；
entries.en: Bin answered, "Even minnows and ants cling to life;
entries.literal: Bin replied, "Even fish fry and ants cherish their lives;

entries.zh: 況在人斯，豈願齏粉？
entries.en: how much more a man—who would choose to be pulverized?
entries.literal: how much more a man—who would wish to be ground to dust?

entries.zh: 但囚父掛深劾，必正刑書，故思殞仆，冀延父命。
entries.en: But my father faces capital charge; I offer my life to prolong his.
entries.literal: Yet my father hangs under grave accusation and must face the full penalty; I mean to throw away my life hoping to extend his.

entries.zh: 今瞑目引領，以聽大戮，情殫意極，無言復對。」
entries.en: I shut my eyes and await the blade—heart and words are spent; I will not answer again."
entries.literal: Now I close my eyes and stretch my neck for the great execution—feeling and will are spent; I have nothing more to say."

entries.zh: 翂初見囚，獄掾依法備加桎梏；
entries.en: When Bin entered prison the clerks, by statute, fitted him with every bond;
entries.literal: When Bin was first imprisoned the jailers, by law, loaded him with full shackles;

entries.zh: 法度矜之，命脫其二械，更令著一小者。
entries.en: Fadu took pity and had two removed, leaving only a lighter set.
entries.literal: Fadu pitied him and ordered two bonds removed, allowing a lighter pair.

entries.zh: 翂弗聽，曰：「翂求代父死，死罪之囚，唯宜增益，豈可減乎？」
entries.en: Bin refused: "I seek to die for my father—a man under death sentence should wear more, not less?"
entries.literal: Bin would not agree and said, "I ask to die for my father—a capital convict should only have bonds added; how may they be lessened?"

entries.zh: 竟不脫械。
entries.en: and he would not let them be taken off.
entries.literal: In the end he would not remove them.

entries.zh: 法度具以奏聞，高祖乃宥其父。
entries.en: Fadu memorialized all of it; Gaozu then spared his father.
entries.literal: Fadu reported everything in full; Gaozu then pardoned his father.

entries.zh: 丹陽尹王志求其在廷尉故事，幷請鄉居，欲於歲首，舉充純孝之選。
entries.en: Dan'yang magistrate Wang Zhi looked up his file at the Court of Justice and asked his home place too, planning to nominate him for pure filial piety at the new year.
entries.literal: Dan'yang magistrate Wang Zhi sought his case in the Court of Justice records and asked his township as well, intending at year's start to recommend him for the pure filial selection.

entries.zh: 翂曰：「異哉王尹，何量翂之薄乎！
entries.en: Bin said, "Strange, Magistrate Wang—how little you think of Bin!
entries.literal: Bin said, "How strange, Magistrate Wang—how shallow you judge Bin!

entries.zh: 夫父辱子死，斯道固然。
entries.en: When a father is disgraced, a son should die—that is the way.
entries.literal: When a father is shamed, a son dies—that is right and proper.

entries.zh: 若翂有靦面目，當其此舉，則是因父買名，一何甚辱！」
entries.en: Had I any shame left after this, it would mean buying a name at my father's cost—how vile!"
entries.literal: If Bin had face to live, having done this act, it would be buying fame through one's father—how shameful!"

entries.zh: 拒之而止。
entries.en: He declined and would hear no more.
entries.literal: He refused and put a stop to it.

entries.zh: 年十七，應辟爲本州主簿。
entries.en: At seventeen he was summoned as the province's chief clerk.
entries.literal: At seventeen he answered summons as chief clerk of his province.

entries.zh: 出監萬年縣，攝官朞月，風化大行。
entries.en: He supervised Wannian county; in one month as acting magistrate custom was greatly reformed.
entries.literal: He went out to supervise Wannian county; as acting magistrate for one cycle customs were greatly transformed.

entries.zh: 自雍還至郢，湘州刺史柳悅復召爲主簿。
entries.en: From Yong he came back to Ying; Liu Yue, inspector of Xiangzhou, again made him chief clerk.
entries.literal: From Yong he returned to Ying; Xiangzhou inspector Liu Yue again summoned him as chief clerk.

entries.zh: 後鄉人裴儉、丹陽尹丞臧盾、揚州中正張仄連名薦翂，以爲孝行純至，明通《易》、《老》。
entries.en: Later Pei Jian of his town, Zang Dun of Dan'yang, and Zhang Ze, Yangzhou rectifier, jointly praised Bin's pure filiality and clear grasp of the Changes and Laozi.
entries.literal: Later townsman Pei Jian, Dan'yang assistant magistrate Zang Dun, and Yangzhou rectifier Zhang Ze jointly recommended Bin, finding his filial conduct pure and his mastery of the Changes and Laozi clear.

entries.zh: 敕付太常旌舉。
entries.en: An edict sent the matter to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for public commendation.
entries.literal: An edict ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to proclaim and recommend him.

entries.zh: 初，翂以父陷罪，因成悸疾，後因發而卒。
entries.en: From his father's ordeal he had taken a trembling sickness; later he died when it broke out.
entries.literal: Earlier, because his father fell into guilt, he developed a trembling illness; later he died when it flared.

entries.zh: 劉曇淨字元光，彭城呂人也。
entries.en: Liu Tanjing, styled Yuanguang, was from Lyu in Pengcheng.
entries.literal: Liu Tanjing, styled Yuanguang, was a man of Lyu in Pengcheng.

entries.zh: 祖元真，淮南太守，居郡得罪；
entries.en: His grandfather Yuanzhen was governor of Huainan and committed an offense in the commandery;
entries.literal: His grandfather Yuanzhen had been Huainan governor and offended while in office;

entries.zh: 父慧鏡，歷詣朝士乞哀，懇惻甚至，遂以孝聞。
entries.en: his father Huijing went again and again to court notables pleading mercy, utterly earnest, and won fame for filial piety.
entries.literal: his father Huijing went repeatedly to court officials begging pity, sincere to the utmost, and became known for filial piety.

entries.zh: 曇淨篤行有父風。
entries.en: Tanjing's devoted ways matched his father's.
entries.literal: Tanjing's steadfast conduct had his father's spirit.

entries.zh: 解褐安成王國左常侍。
entries.en: He first served as left palace attendant in the Kingdom of Ancheng.
entries.literal: On first office he was left palace attendant of the Kingdom of Ancheng.

entries.zh: 父卒於郡，曇淨奔喪，不食飲者累日，絕而又蘇。
entries.en: His father died in office; Tanjing ran to the funeral and for days took no food or drink, fainting and waking.
entries.literal: His father died in the prefecture; Tanjing rushed to mourning and for days ate and drank nothing, dying and reviving.

entries.zh: 每哭輒嘔血。
entries.en: Every bout of weeping brought up blood.
entries.literal: Each time he wept he vomited blood.

entries.zh: 服闋，因毀瘠成疾。
entries.en: After mourning he sickened from grief-wasting.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he fell ill from wasting grief.

entries.zh: 會有詔，士姓各舉四科，曇淨叔父慧斐舉以應孝行，高祖用爲海寧令。
entries.en: When an edict bade each clan recommend four kinds of men, his uncle Huifei nominated him for filial conduct and Gaozu appointed him Haining magistrate.
entries.literal: An edict came for gentry and commoners each to recommend four categories; his uncle Huifei recommended him for filial conduct and Gaozu made him Haining magistrate.

entries.zh: 曇淨以兄未爲縣，因以讓兄，乃除安西行參軍。
entries.en: His elder brother had no county post yet, so Tanjing yielded the magistracy and was made staff officer on the Pacifying West staff.
entries.literal: Tanjing's elder brother had not yet held a county post, so he yielded; he was then made staff officer of the Pacifying West campaign.

entries.zh: 父亡後，事母尤淳至，身營飧粥，不以委人。
entries.en: After his father died he served his mother with deepest devotion, cooking gruel himself and trusting no one else.
entries.literal: After his father's death he served his mother with utmost purity, cooking porridge himself and entrusting it to none.

entries.zh: 母疾，衣不解帶。
entries.en: When she was ill he never loosened his belt.
entries.literal: When his mother fell ill he did not unfasten his belt.

entries.zh: 及母亡，水漿不入口者殆一旬。
entries.en: When she died he took no food or drink for nearly ten days.
entries.literal: When she died he nearly ten days took no food or drink.

entries.zh: 母喪權瘞藥王寺。
entries.en: His mother was provisionally buried at Medicine King Temple.
entries.literal: His mother's coffin was temporarily interred at Medicine King Temple.

entries.zh: 時天寒，曇淨身衣單布，廬於瘞所，晝夜哭泣不絕聲，哀感行路，未及朞而卒。
entries.en: It was bitter cold; Tanjing wore a single layer, hutted at the grave, weeping day and night—passersby wept; before the year ended he died.
entries.literal: The weather was cold; Tanjing wore only thin cloth, hutted at the burial place, weeping day and night without pause—travelers were moved; before the year was out he died.

entries.zh: 庾沙彌，潁陰人也。
entries.en: Yu Shamí was from Yingyin.
entries.literal: Yu Shamí was a man of Yingyin.

entries.zh: 晉司空冰六世孫。
entries.en: He was sixth in descent from Jin Minister of Works Bing.
entries.literal: He was sixth-generation descendant of Jin Minister of Works Bing.

entries.zh: 父佩玉，輔國長史、長沙內史，宋昇明中坐沈攸之事誅，沙彌時始生。
entries.en: His father Peiyu was chief aide to the Pacifying-the-State general and Changsha administrator; in Song Shengming he was killed in Shen Youzhi's rebellion—Shamí was a newborn.
entries.literal: His father Peiyu had been Pacifying the State chief aide and Changsha administrator; in Song's Shengming he was executed for Shen Youzhi's affair—Shamí had just been born.

entries.zh: 年至五歲，所生母爲制采衣，輒不肯服。
entries.en: At five his birth mother made him bright clothes; he refused to put them on.
entries.literal: At five his birth mother had a colored garment made for him; he would not wear it.

entries.zh: 母問其故，流涕對曰：「家門禍酷，用是何爲！」
entries.en: Asked the reason, he wept and said, "Our clan suffered bitter ruin—what is this for?"
entries.literal: When she asked why, he wept and said, "Our house met cruel disaster—of what use is this?"

entries.zh: 旣長，終身布衣蔬食。
entries.en: Grown, he wore coarse cloth and ate vegetables for life.
entries.literal: Grown, he wore plain cloth and ate vegetables all his life.

entries.zh: 起家臨川王國左常侍，遷中軍田曹行參軍。
entries.en: He started as left palace attendant in the Kingdom of Linchuan, then field-accounts staff officer of the Central Army.
entries.literal: He began as left palace attendant of the Kingdom of Linchuan and became acting field-accounts staff officer of the Central Army.

entries.zh: 嫡母劉氏寢疾，沙彌晨昏侍側，衣不解帶，或應針灸，輒以身先試之。
entries.en: When his stepmother Lady Liu was sick Shamí waited dawn and dusk, belt never loosened; if needles were used he tested them on himself first.
entries.literal: When his stepmother Lady Liu lay ill Shamí attended morning and evening, belt unfastened; if acupuncture was needed he tried it on himself first.

entries.zh: 及母亡，水漿不入口累日，終喪不解衰絰，不出廬戶，晝夜號慟，鄰人不忍聞。
entries.en: When she died he fasted for days, never left his mourning garb or hut, wailing day and night till neighbors could not listen.
entries.literal: When she died he took no food or drink for days, through the whole mourning never removing his hemp, never leaving the hut, wailing day and night—neighbors could not bear to hear.

entries.zh: 墓在新林，因有旅松百餘株，自生墳側。
entries.en: The grave was at Xinlin; over a hundred pines grew by themselves beside the tomb.
entries.literal: The tomb was at Xinlin; more than a hundred traveler pines sprang up on their own beside the mound.

entries.zh: 族兄都官尚書詠表言其狀，應純孝之舉，高祖召見嘉之，以補歙令。
entries.en: His kinsman Yu Yong, Minister President of Justice, reported him for pure filial piety; Gaozu received him, praised him, and made him magistrate of She.
entries.literal: His clan elder, Minister President of Justice Yong, memorialized his case for the pure filial recommendation; Gaozu summoned and praised him and appointed him She magistrate.

entries.zh: 還除輕車邵陵王參軍事，隨府會稽，復丁所生母憂。
entries.en: He returned to office as staff equal to the Prince of Shaoling of Light Chariots, followed the headquarters to Kuaiji, and again mourned his birth mother.
entries.literal: He was transferred back and made staff equal on the staff of the Prince of Shaoling, Light Chariots; he followed the prince's headquarters to Kuaiji and again entered mourning for his birth mother.

entries.zh: 喪還都，濟浙江，中流遇風，舫將覆沒，沙彌抱柩號哭，俄而風靜，蓋孝感所致。
entries.en: On the homeward crossing of the Zhe the boat nearly capsized in a squall; Shami clung to the coffin and wailed, and soon the wind died—men took it as filial feeling answered from Heaven.
entries.literal: Returning from mourning to the capital, he crossed the Zhe River; midstream he met wind and the boat was about to capsize—Shami embraced the coffin and wailed, and presently the wind fell still—thought to be moved by filial response.

entries.zh: 服闋，除信威刑獄參軍，兼丹陽郡囗囗囗累遷寧遠錄事參軍，轉司馬。
entries.en: After mourning he became Trustworthy Might criminal judge staff equal and concurrently [text lost] in Danyang; he rose to Ningyuan recording secretary, then marshal.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he was made staff equal of Trustworthy Might criminal judge, concurrently [lacuna] of Danyang commandery; he was promoted in succession recording secretary of Ningyuan and transferred to marshal.

entries.zh: 出爲長城令，卒。
entries.en: He served as magistrate of Changcheng and died in office.
entries.literal: He went out as magistrate of Changcheng and died.

entries.zh: 恬數歲喪父，哀感有若成人。
entries.en: Tian lost his father as a small child, mourning like a grown man.
entries.literal: Tian lost his father at several years old, grief like an adult's.

entries.zh: 家人矜其小，以肉汁和飯飼之，恬不肯食。
entries.en: Kin, pitying his age, mixed broth into his rice; Tian refused it.
entries.literal: The family pitied his youth and fed him rice mixed with broth; Tian would not eat.

entries.zh: 年八歲，問其母，恨生不識父，遂悲泣累日，忽若有見，言其形貌，則其父也，時以爲孝感。
entries.en: At eight he told his mother he hated never knowing his father, wept for days, then seemed to see someone and described his looks—it was his father; men called it filial portent.
entries.literal: At eight he asked his mother, grieving he had never known his father; he wept for days until suddenly he seemed to see one and spoke his features—it was his father; at the time this was deemed filial response.

entries.zh: 家貧，養母常得珍羞。
entries.en: Poor as they were, he always found fine food for his mother.
entries.literal: Though the household was poor, in nurturing his mother he always obtained delicacies.

entries.zh: 及居喪，廬於墓側，恒有鳥玄黃雜色，集於廬樹，恬哭則鳴，哭止則止。
entries.en: Mourning at the grave he built a hut; black-and-yellow birds always perched on its tree—when Tian wept they called, when he ceased they ceased.
entries.literal: In mourning he hutted by the tomb; constantly birds of mixed black and yellow gathered on the hut tree—when Tian wept they cried, when he stopped they stopped.

entries.zh: 又有白雀栖宿其廬。
entries.en: A white sparrow roosted on the hut as well.
entries.literal: A white sparrow also roosted on his hut.

entries.zh: 州將始興王憺表其行狀。
entries.en: Xiao Dan, Prince of Shixing and provincial commander, reported his conduct.
entries.literal: The provincial commander, Prince of Shixing Xiao Dan, memorialized his conduct.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「朕虛己欽賢，寤寐盈想。
entries.en: The edict read, "We humble ourselves before the worthy and think of them waking and sleeping.
entries.literal: Edict said, "We empty ourselves to honor the worthy, longing day and night.

entries.zh: 詔彼群岳，務盡搜揚。
entries.en: We command the high officials to seek and raise them without fail.
entries.literal: We charge the mountain peaks to search and lift all they can.

entries.zh: 恬旣孝行殊異，聲著邦壤，敦風厲俗，弘益茲多。
entries.en: Tian's filiality is extraordinary, his name known in every district—he steels the folk and brings great good.
entries.literal: Tian's filial conduct is truly rare, his fame filling the land—he ennobles custom and profits the realm greatly.

entries.zh: 牧守騰聞，義同親覽。
entries.en: The governors have sent word; We receive it as if with Our own eyes.
entries.literal: The shepherds and guards have reported up; it is as if We read it ourselves.

entries.zh: 可旌表室閭，加以爵位。」
entries.en: Let his gate and lane be honored and rank be granted."
entries.literal: He may be marked at his gate and lane and given rank."

entries.zh: 恬官至安南行參軍。
entries.en: Tian rose to acting staff officer on the Pacifying South staff.
entries.literal: Tian reached the post of acting staff officer on the Pacifying South campaign.

entries.zh: 韓懷明，上黨人也，客居荊州。
entries.en: Han Huaiming was from Shangdang and lived as a guest in Jingzhou.
entries.literal: Han Huaiming was a man of Shangdang who resided as a guest in Jingzhou.

entries.zh: 年十歲，母患屍疰，每發輒危殆。
entries.en: At ten his mother had corpse-consumption sickness; every bout nearly took her life.
entries.literal: At ten his mother suffered corpse-consumption malady; each attack nearly killed her.

entries.zh: 懷明夜於星下稽顙祈禱，時寒甚切，忽聞香氣，空中有人語曰：「童子母須臾永差，無勞自苦。」
entries.en: Huaiming knelt under the stars in bitter cold; suddenly fragrance came and a voice above said, "The boy's mother will soon be wholly well—do not torture yourself."
entries.literal: Huaiming knelt and prayed under the stars; the cold was piercing—suddenly he smelled fragrance and a voice in the air said, "Your mother's illness will soon be cured for good—do not torment yourself."

entries.zh: 未曉，而母豁然平復。
entries.en: Before daybreak his mother was completely healed.
entries.literal: Before dawn his mother was wholly restored.

entries.zh: 鄉里異之。
entries.en: Neighbors were astonished.
entries.literal: The countryside marveled.

entries.zh: 十五喪父，幾至滅性，負土成墳，贈助無所受。
entries.en: At fifteen his father died; he nearly perished from grief, piled the grave himself, and took no aid offered.
entries.literal: At fifteen he lost his father, nearly wasting away; he carried earth for the mound and accepted no gifts of help.

entries.zh: 免喪，與鄉人郭瑀俱師事南陽劉虬。
entries.en: After mourning he and Guo Yu of his town studied with Liu Qiu of Nanyang.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he and townsman Guo Yu both studied under Liu Qiu of Nanyang.

entries.zh: 虬嘗一日廢講，獨居涕泣。
entries.en: Once Qiu canceled class for a day and wept by himself.
entries.literal: Once Qiu suspended lecture for a day and wept alone.

entries.zh: 懷明竊問其故，虬家人答云：「是外祖亡日。」
entries.en: Huaiming asked the reason in private; the household said, "It is the day his mother's father died."
entries.literal: Huaiming quietly asked why; Qiu's household answered, "It is his maternal grandfather's death-day."

entries.zh: 時虬母亦亡矣。
entries.en: His own mother was already gone as well.
entries.literal: By then Qiu's mother was also dead.

entries.zh: 懷明聞之，卽日罷學，還家就養。
entries.en: Hearing this, Huaiming quit school the same day and went home to tend her.
entries.literal: Huaiming heard and that day left study to return home and serve.

entries.zh: 虬歎曰：「韓生無虞丘之恨矣。」
entries.en: Qiu sighed, "Han need not bear Yu Qiu's remorse."
entries.literal: Qiu sighed, "Master Han need have no regret like Yu Qiu's."

entries.zh: 家貧，常肆力以供甘脆，嬉怡膝下，朝夕不離母側。
entries.en: The house was poor; he toiled for dainties, merry at her knee, never leaving her side dawn to dusk.
entries.literal: Poor at home, he often hired out labor for sweet and tender foods, delighting under his mother's knees, never leaving her day or night.

entries.zh: 母年九十一，以壽終，懷明水漿不入口一旬，號哭不絕聲。
entries.en: His mother died at ninety-one; Huaiming took no food or drink for ten days and wailed without stopping.
entries.literal: His mother died at ninety-one of old age; Huaiming took neither food nor drink for ten days, wailing without cease.

entries.zh: 有雙白鳩巢其廬上，字乳馴狎，若家禽焉，服釋乃去。
entries.en: Two white doves nested on his hut, rearing young as tame as poultry; they left only when mourning was done.
entries.literal: A pair of white doves nested on his mourning hut, feeding their young tamely like barn birds; only when mourning ended did they leave.

entries.zh: 旣除喪，蔬食終身，衣衾無改。
entries.en: After mourning he ate only vegetables for life and never changed his clothes.
entries.literal: After mourning he ate vegetables all his life and never changed his garments.

entries.zh: 天監初，刺史始興王憺表言之。
entries.en: At the start of Tianjian, Xiao Dan, Prince of Shixing and inspector, reported him.
entries.literal: Early in Tianjian the inspector, Prince of Shixing Xiao Dan, memorialized him.

entries.zh: 州累辟不就，卒于家。
entries.en: The province called him many times; he would not go, and died at home.
entries.literal: The province repeatedly summoned him but he would not accept; he died at home.

entries.zh: 江紑字含潔，濟陽考城人也。
entries.en: Jiang Fou, styled Hanjie, was from Kaocheng in Jiyang.
entries.literal: Jiang Fou, styled Hanjie, was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang.

entries.zh: 父蒨，光祿大夫。
entries.en: His father Qian was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
entries.literal: His father Qian was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

entries.zh: 紑幼有孝性。
entries.en: Gou was filial from childhood.
entries.literal: From childhood Gou had a filial nature.

entries.zh: 年十三，父患眼，紑侍疾將朞月，衣不解帶。
entries.en: At thirteen, when his father had eye trouble, Gou nursed him nearly a month without leaving his side.
entries.literal: At thirteen his father suffered eye disease; Gou attended the illness for nearly a month without undoing his belt.

entries.zh: 夜夢一僧云：「患眼者，飲慧眼水必差。」
entries.en: In a dream a monk told him, "For eye disease, drink Wisdom-Eye water and it will heal."
entries.literal: One night he dreamed a monk said, "For eye disease, drink Wisdom-Eye water and you will be cured."

entries.zh: 及覺說之，莫能解者。
entries.en: He told the dream at dawn, but no one could explain it.
entries.literal: When he woke and told it, no one could explain it.

entries.zh: 紑第三叔祿與草堂寺智者法師善，往訪之。
entries.en: His third uncle Lu was close to the Wise One of Caotang Temple and went to ask him.
entries.literal: Gou's third uncle Lu was on good terms with the Wise One of Caotang Temple; he went to visit him.

entries.zh: 智者曰：「《無量壽經》云：慧眼見真，能渡彼岸。」
entries.en: The Wise One said, "The Infinite Life Sutra says, 'The wisdom-eye sees truth and can ferry to the farther shore.'"
entries.literal: The Wise One said, "The Infinite Life Sutra says: the wisdom-eye sees truth and can ferry to the farther shore."

entries.zh: 蒨乃因智者啓捨同夏縣界牛屯里舍爲寺，乞賜嘉名。
entries.en: Qian then asked the Wise One to petition donating the Niutun estate in Tongxia as a monastery and to grant it a worthy name.
entries.literal: Qian thereupon through the Wise One petitioned to donate the house and land at Niutun in Tongxia county as a monastery and begged a fine name.

entries.zh: 敕答云：「純臣孝子，往往感應。
entries.en: The reply edict said, "Pure ministers and filial sons often meet with response.
entries.literal: The edict in reply said, "Pure ministers and filial sons often meet with response.

entries.zh: 晉世顏含，遂見冥中送藥。
entries.en: In Jin times Yan Han likewise saw medicine sent from the shades.
entries.literal: In Jin times Yan Han thus saw medicine sent from the shades.

entries.zh: 近見智者，知卿第二息感夢，云飲慧眼水。
entries.en: Recently the Wise One told me your second son dreamed of drinking wisdom-eye water.
entries.literal: Recently seeing the Wise One, I know your second son was moved in a dream, saying to drink wisdom-eye water.

entries.zh: 慧眼則是五眼之一號，若欲造寺，可以慧眼爲名。」
entries.en: Wisdom-eye is one of the five eyes; if you build a monastery, call it Wisdom-Eye."
entries.literal: Wisdom-eye is the name of one of the five eyes; if you wish to build a monastery, you may take Wisdom-Eye as its name."

entries.zh: 及就創造，泄故井，井水清冽，異於常泉。
entries.en: When they built, they cleared an old well whose water was clear and sweet, unlike ordinary springs.
entries.literal: When construction was undertaken they opened an old well; the well water was clear and sweet, unlike ordinary springs.

entries.zh: 依夢取水洗眼及煮藥，稍覺有瘳，因此遂差。
entries.en: As the dream directed they washed his eyes and boiled medicine in it; he improved and was cured.
entries.literal: Following the dream they took the water to wash the eyes and boil medicine; he felt somewhat better, and thereby was cured.

entries.zh: 時人謂之孝感。
entries.en: People called it filial feeling answered.
entries.literal: Men of the time called it filial feeling answered.

entries.zh: 南康王爲南州，召爲迎主簿。
entries.en: When the Prince of Nankang governed the south he made Gou reception chief clerk.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Nankang was southern inspector he summoned Gou as reception chief clerk.

entries.zh: 紑性靜，好《老》、《莊》玄言，尤善佛義，不樂進仕。
entries.en: Quiet by nature, he loved Laozi and Zhuangzi and Buddhist teaching and did not care to advance in office.
entries.literal: Gou's nature was quiet; he loved the dark learning of Laozi and Zhuangzi and was especially skilled in Buddhist meaning, and did not delight in advancing in office.

entries.zh: 及父卒，紑廬于墓，終日號慟不絕聲，月餘卒。
entries.en: When his father died he lodged at the tomb and wailed without cease; after more than a month he died.
entries.literal: When his father died Gou built a hut at the tomb and wailed without cease all day; after more than a month he died.

entries.zh: 謝藺字希如，陳郡陽夏人也。
entries.en: Xie Lan, styled Xiru, was from Yangxia in Chen commandery.
entries.literal: Xie Lan, styled Xiru, was a man of Yangxia in Chen commandery.

entries.zh: 晉太傅安八世孫。
entries.en: He was eighth-generation descendant of Jin Grand Tutor An.
entries.literal: He was eighth-generation descendant of Jin Grand Tutor An.

entries.zh: 父經，中郎諮議參軍。
entries.en: His father Jing was staff equal for consultation in the Central Guard.
entries.literal: His father Jing was staff equal for consultation in the Central Guard.

entries.zh: 藺五歲，每父母未飯，乳媼欲令藺先飯，藺曰：「旣不覺饑。」
entries.en: At five, if his parents had not eaten the nurse would feed Lan first; he said, "I do not yet feel hungry."
entries.literal: At five, whenever his parents had not yet eaten, the wet nurse wished to let Lan eat first; Lan said, "I am not yet aware of hunger."

entries.zh: 強食終不進。
entries.en: Pressed, he still would not eat.
entries.literal: Though pressed he would in the end not eat.

entries.zh: 舅阮孝緒聞之，歎曰：「此兒在家則曾子之流，事君則藺生之匹。」
entries.en: His uncle Ruan Xiaoxu sighed, "At home this boy is like Zengzi; in serving a lord he would match young Lan."
entries.literal: His maternal uncle Ruan Xiaoxu heard of it and sighed, "This child at home is of Zengzi's sort; in serving his lord he would match the lad Lan."

entries.zh: 因名之曰藺。
entries.en: So he was named Lan.
entries.literal: He therefore gave him the name Lan.

entries.zh: 稍受以經史，過目便能諷誦。
entries.en: Taught the classics and histories, he could chant from memory whatever he read.
entries.literal: Gradually he received instruction in the classics and histories; what passed before his eyes he could chant from memory.

entries.zh: 孝緒每曰「吾家陽元也」。
entries.en: Xiaoxu often said, "He is our house's Yangyuan."
entries.literal: Xiaoxu often said, "He is the Yangyuan of our house."

entries.zh: 及丁父憂，晝夜號慟，毀瘠骨立，母阮氏常自守視譬抑之。
entries.en: After his father's death he wailed day and night until only bone remained; his mother Lady Ruan constantly watched and restrained him.
entries.literal: When he entered mourning for his father he wailed day and night, wasted away until only bone stood, and his mother Lady Ruan constantly watched over him herself to restrain and comfort him.

entries.zh: 服闋後，吏部尚書蕭子顯表其至行，擢爲王府法曹行參軍，累遷外兵記室參軍。
entries.en: When mourning ended Minister Xiao Zixian recommended his utmost conduct; he became princely legal affairs gentleman, then outer staff recorder.
entries.literal: After mourning he was recommended for utmost conduct by Minister of Personnel Xiao Zixian and was promoted court gentleman for legal affairs on the prince's staff, then in succession outer staff recorder.

entries.zh: 時甘露降士林館，藺獻頌，高祖嘉之，因有詔使制《北兗州刺史蕭楷德政碑》，又奉令制《宣城王奉述中庸頌》。
entries.en: When sweet dew fell on the Scholars' Grove, Lan presented a eulogy the emperor praised; he was ordered to compose the stele on Xiao Kai's virtuous rule in North Yanzhou and the eulogy on the Prince of Xuancheng presenting the Mean.
entries.literal: At that time sweet dew fell on the Scholars' Grove; Lan presented a eulogy and Gaozu praised it, whereupon an edict ordered him to compose the Stele on the Virtuous Government of Xiao Kai, Inspector of North Yanzhou, and he was also ordered to compose the "Eulogy on the Prince of Xuancheng's Presentation of the Mean."

entries.zh: 太清元年，遷散騎侍郎，兼散騎常侍，使於魏。
entries.en: In Taiqing year one he became Gentleman Attendant and Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and envoy to Wei.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taiqing he was promoted Gentleman Attendant of the Palace Secretariat and concurrently Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and sent as envoy to Wei.

entries.zh: 會侯景舉地入附，境上交兵，藺母慮不得還，感氣卒。
entries.en: When Hou Jing defected and border fighting broke out, Lan's mother feared he would not return and died of grief.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing surrendered territory and came over, fighting broke out on the borders; Lan's mother feared he could not return and died of grief.

entries.zh: 及藺還入境，爾夕夢不祥，旦便投劾馳歸。
entries.en: On re-entering the realm that night he dreamed ill omens; at dawn he resigned and raced home.
entries.literal: When Lan returned and entered the realm, that very evening he dreamed ill omens; at dawn he submitted his resignation and raced home.

entries.zh: 旣至，號慟嘔血，氣絕久之，水漿不入口。
entries.en: Arriving, he wailed until he vomited blood and long lost breath, and took no food.
entries.literal: When he arrived he wailed and vomited blood and long lost breath; he would not take water or gruel.

entries.zh: 親友慮其不全，相對悲慟，強勸以飲粥。
entries.en: Kin feared he would not live and wept together, forcing thin gruel on him.
entries.literal: Kin and friends feared he would not survive and mourned together; they forced him to take thin gruel.

entries.zh: 藺初勉強受之，終不能進，經月餘日，因夜臨而卒，時年三十八。
entries.en: He forced himself at first but could not swallow; after more than a month he died one night at the tomb, aged thirty-eight.
entries.literal: At first Lan forced himself to accept it but in the end could not swallow; after more than a month, one night at the tomb he died, aged thirty-eight.

entries.zh: 藺所制詩賦碑頌數十篇。
entries.en: Lan composed several tens of poems, rhapsodies, steles, and eulogies.
entries.literal: Lan composed several tens of pieces of poetry, fu, steles, and eulogies.

entries.zh: 滕曇恭
entries.en: Teng Tangong
entries.literal: Teng Tangong

entries.zh: 肩吾字子慎。
entries.en: Jianwu, styled Zishen.
entries.literal: Jianwu, courtesy name Zishen.

entries.zh: 八歲能賦詩，特爲兄於陵所友愛。
entries.en: At eight he wrote verse and was Yuling's favorite brother.
entries.literal: At eight he could compose poetry and was especially loved by his elder brother Yuling.

entries.zh: 初爲晉安王國常侍，仍遷王宣惠府行參軍。
entries.en: He began as Jin'an regular attendant, then prince Xuanhui army aide.
entries.literal: He first served as Regular Attendant of the Jin'an princedom, then was promoted to Army Aide of the Prince's Xuanhui office.

entries.zh: 自是每王徙鎮，肩吾常隨府。
entries.en: Whenever the prince moved fief Jianwu followed.
entries.literal: From then on whenever the prince moved his fief Jianwu followed the headquarters.

entries.zh: 歷王府中郎、雲麾參軍，並兼記室參軍。
entries.en: He was princely middle attendant, cloud-banner aide, and chief secretary.
entries.literal: He served as princely middle attendant, Cloud Banner army aide, and chief secretary throughout.

entries.zh: 中大通三年，王爲皇太子，兼東宮通事舍人，除安西湘東王錄事參軍，俄以本官領荊州大中正。
entries.en: Zhongdatong year three the prince became heir; Jianwu was Eastern Palace courier and Xiangdong recorder, soon Jingzhou chief.
entries.literal: In the third year of Zhongdatong the prince became crown prince; Jianwu was Eastern Palace courier while also Jin'an-Xiangdong recorder, and soon headed Jingzhou as chief.

entries.zh: 累遷中錄事諮議參軍、太子率更令、中庶子。
entries.en: He rose to central records consulting colonel, crown prince commissioner of seasons, and household vice-supervisor.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to consulting colonel of the central records, Crown Prince Commissioner for Increasing the Seasons, and Household Vice-Supervisor.

entries.zh: 初，太宗在籓，雅好文章士，時肩吾與東海徐摛、吳郡陸杲、彭城劉遵、劉孝儀、儀弟孝威，同被賞接。
entries.en: In the fief Taizong loved writers; Jianwu, Xu Chi, Lu Guo, Liu Zun, Xiaoyi, and Xiaowei were favored.
entries.literal: When Taizong was still in the fief he loved men of letters; then Jianwu with Xu Chi of Donghai, Lu Guo of Wu, Liu Zun and Liu Xiaoyi of Pengcheng, and Xiaoyi's brother Xiaowei were all favored.

entries.zh: 及居東宮，又開文德省，置學士，肩吾子信、摛子陵、吳郡張長公、北地傅弘、東海鮑至等充其選。
entries.en: As crown prince he reopened Wende scholars—Jianwu's Xin, Chi's Ling, Zhang Changgong, Fu Hong, and Bao Zhi among them.
entries.literal: When he dwelt in the Eastern Palace he again opened the Wende office and placed scholars; Jianwu's son Xin, Chi's son Ling, Zhang Changgong of Wu, Fu Hong of Beidi, and Bao Zhi of Donghai were chosen.

entries.zh: 齊永明中，文士王融、謝朓、沈約文章始用四聲，以爲新變，至是轉拘聲韻，彌尚麗靡，復逾於往時。
entries.en: Qi Yongming brought four-tone verse; now rhyme grew tighter and ornament surpassed the past.
entries.literal: In Qi Yongming, Wang Rong, Xie Tiao, and Shen Yue first used the four tones in writing as a new change; by now sound and rhyme grew stricter and ornate beauty exceeded the past.

entries.zh: 時太子與湘東王書論之曰：
entries.en: The crown prince then wrote Prince Xiangdong, saying:
entries.literal: Then the crown prince wrote to the Prince of Xiangdong discussing it, saying:

entries.zh: 劉昭字宣卿，平原高唐人，晉太尉實九世孫也。
entries.en: Liu Zhao, styled Xuanqing, of Pingyuan Gaotang, ninth generation from Jin's Liu Shi.
entries.literal: Liu Zhao, courtesy name Xuanqing, was from Gaotang in Pingyuan, ninth-generation descendant of Jin Grand Marshal Shi.

entries.zh: 祖伯龍，居父憂以孝聞，宋武帝敕皇太子諸王並往吊慰，官至少府卿。
entries.en: Grandfather Bolong was famed for mourning filial piety; Wudi sent princes to condole; he reached vice director of the palace bureau.
entries.literal: His grandfather Bolong was famed for filial piety in mourning for his father; Song Wudi ordered the crown prince and princes to condole and he reached Vice Director of the Palace Bureau.

entries.zh: 父彪，齊征虜晉安王記室。
entries.en: His father Biao was Qi Jin'an prince chief secretary.
entries.literal: His father Biao was staff chief secretary to the Qi expeditionary Prince Jin'an.

entries.zh: 氣之動物，物之感人，故搖盪性情，形諸舞詠。
entries.en: Qi moves things; things move people—so feeling stirs and finds form in dance and song.
entries.literal: When qi stirs things, things move people; thus feelings sway and take shape in dance and song.

entries.zh: 欲以照燭三才，輝麗萬有，靈祇待之以致饗，幽微藉之以昭告。
entries.en: It lights the three powers and adorns the myriad; spirits wait on it for sacrifice, the hidden use it to declare.
entries.literal: It means to illuminate the three realms and shed glory on the myriad beings; spirits await it for offerings, and the hidden and subtle rely on it for proclamation.

entries.zh: 動天地，感鬼神，莫近於詩。
entries.en: To move Heaven and Earth and touch gods and ghosts, nothing nears poetry.
entries.literal: Moving Heaven and Earth, touching spirits and ghosts—nothing comes nearer than poetry.

entries.zh: 昔《南風》之辭，《卿雲》之頌，厥義夐矣。
entries.en: Of old Southern Winds and Cloud-Coach—their meaning was already vast.
entries.literal: Of old the words of the *Southern Winds* and the hymn *Cloud-Coach*—their meaning was already far-reaching.

entries.zh: 《夏歌》曰「郁陶乎予心」，楚謠云「名余曰正則」，雖詩體未全，然略是五言之濫觴也。
entries.en: Xia Songs have "deeply troubled in heart"; Chu songs name "Zhengze"—verse form was incomplete, yet these were the springs of five-character poetry.
entries.literal: The *Xia Songs* say "I am deeply troubled in heart"; a Chu song says "They named me Zhengze"—though the poetic form was not yet complete, they were roughly the source of five-character verse.

entries.zh: 逮漢李陵，始著五言之目。
entries.en: By Han, Li Ling first established five-character verse as a category.
entries.literal: Down to Han's Li Ling, the category of five-character verse was first set forth.

entries.zh: 古詩眇邈，人代難詳，推其文體，固是炎漢之制，非衰周之倡也。
entries.en: Ancient poems are distant and ages obscure; by form they belong to Han, not late Zhou.
entries.literal: Ancient poems are remote and ages hard to trace; judging their form, they are truly products of blazing Han, not songs of declining Zhou.

entries.zh: 自王、揚、枚、馬之徒，辭賦競爽，而吟詠靡聞。
entries.en: From Wang Bao, Yang Xiong, Mei Cheng, and Sima Xiangru on, fu competed in brilliance while lyric verse was rarely heard.
entries.literal: From Wang, Yang, Mei, and Ma onward, rhapsodies vied in brilliance, yet lyric singing was scarcely heard.

entries.zh: 從李都尉訖班婕妤，將百年間，有婦人焉，一人而已。
entries.en: From Li Ling to Lady Ban, nearly a century held one woman poet—and only one.
entries.literal: From Commandant Li to Lady Ban, in nearly a hundred years there was a woman—and only one.

entries.zh: 詩人之風，頓已缺喪。
entries.en: The poets' wind had suddenly died away.
entries.literal: The poets' tradition had suddenly perished.

entries.zh: 東京二百載中，唯有班固《詠史》，質木無文致。
entries.en: Eastern Han's two centuries held only Ban Gu's Ode on History—plain and without literary grace.
entries.literal: In the two hundred years of Eastern Han there was only Ban Gu's *Ode on History*—plain wood without literary grace.

entries.zh: 降及建安，曹公父子，篤好斯文；
entries.en: By Jian'an, the Cao lord and his sons deeply loved letters;
entries.literal: Down to the Jian'an period, Lord Cao and his sons deeply loved this craft;

entries.zh: 平原兄弟，鬱爲文棟；
entries.en: the Pingyuan brothers rose as literary pillars;
entries.literal: the brothers of Pingyuan flourished as literary pillars;

entries.zh: 劉楨、王粲，爲其羽冀。
entries.en: Liu Zhen and Wang Can were their wings.
entries.literal: Liu Zhen and Wang Can were their wings.

entries.zh: 次有攀龍託鳳，自致於屬車者，蓋將百計。
entries.en: Next came nearly a hundred who clung to dragons and phoenixes and joined the train.
entries.literal: Next came those who, clinging to dragons and nesting phoenixes, attached themselves to the rear train—nearly a hundred in number.

entries.zh: 彬彬之盛，大備於時矣！
entries.en: Such abundant flowering was complete in that age!
entries.literal: Such abundant flourishing was fully prepared in that age!

entries.zh: 爾後陵遲衰微，訖於有晉。
entries.en: Afterward it declined to Jin.
entries.literal: Afterward it declined and weakened, down to Jin.

entries.zh: 太康中，三張二陸，兩潘一左，勃爾復興，踵武前王，風流未沫，亦文章之中興也。
entries.en: Taikang saw the three Zhangs, two Lus, two Pans, and Zuo Zuo revive the art—wind not yet spent, a literary revival.
entries.literal: In the Taikang era the three Zhangs, two Lus, two Pans, and one Zuo suddenly flourished again, following the martial ways of former kings; the breeze had not yet dried—this too was a literary revival.

entries.zh: 永嘉時，貴黃、老，尚虛談，于時篇什，理過其辭，淡乎寡味。
entries.en: Yongjia honored Huang-Lao and pure talk; verse reasoned past its words—thin and flavorless.
entries.literal: In the Yongjia era Yellow Lao and empty talk were honored; poems of the time reasoned beyond their words and were thin and tasteless.

entries.zh: 爰及江表，微波尚傳，孫綽、許詢、桓、庾諸公，皆平典似《道德論》，建安之風盡矣。
entries.en: South of the river slight ripples remained; Sun Chuo, Xu Xun, Huan, and Yu wrote level pieces like the Dao De Lun—Jian'an's wind was gone.
