entries.literal: Reaching the lands south of the Yangtze, slight ripples still passed on; Sun Chuo, Xu Xun, Huan, Yu, and the gentlemen were all level and canonical like the *Dao De Lun*—Jian'an's wind was wholly gone.

entries.zh: 先是郭景純用俊上之才，創變其體；
entries.en: Earlier Guo Jingchun, with lofty talent, changed the form;
entries.literal: Earlier Guo Pu, with lofty talent, innovated and changed the form;

entries.zh: 劉越石仗清剛之氣，贊成厥美。
entries.en: Liu Yueshi, with pure firm spirit, helped perfect that beauty.
entries.literal: Liu Kun, relying on pure firmness, helped perfect that beauty.

entries.zh: 然彼衆我寡，未能動俗。
entries.en: Yet the many outweighed the few and could not shift custom.
entries.literal: Yet they were many against few and could not move custom.

entries.zh: 逮義熙中，謝益壽斐然繼作；
entries.en: By Yixi Xie Lingyun flourished and continued writing;
entries.literal: By the Yixi era Xie Lingyun flourished and continued the work;

entries.zh: 元嘉初，有謝靈運，才高辭盛，富豔難蹤，固已含跨劉、郭，陵轢潘、左。
entries.en: Early Yuanjia brought Xie Lingyun—great talent, rich diction, splendor hard to follow; he spanned Liu and Guo and towered over Pan and Zuo.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia there was Xie Lingyun—talent high, diction rich, splendor hard to track; he already spanned Liu and Guo and towered over Pan and Zuo.

entries.zh: 故知陳思爲建安之傑，公幹、仲宣爲輔；
entries.en: Thus Prince Si was Jian'an's crown, Gonggan and Zhongxuan his aides;
entries.literal: Thus we know Prince Si was Jian'an's paragon, with Gonggan and Zhongxuan as aides;

entries.zh: 陸機爲太康之英，安仁、景陽爲輔；
entries.en: Lu Ji was Taikang's hero, Anren and Jingyang his aides;
entries.literal: Lu Ji was Taikang's hero, with Anren and Jingyang as aides;

entries.zh: 謝客爲元嘉之雄，顏延年爲輔：此皆五言之冠冕，文辭之命世。
entries.en: Guest Xie was Yuanjia's champion, Yan Yannian his aide—these crown five-character verse and master an age of letters.
entries.literal: Guest Xie was Yuanjia's champion, with Yan Yannian as aide: these are the crowns of five-character verse, fated masters of letters.

entries.zh: 興嗣世居姑孰。
entries.en: The Xingsi clan lived at Gushu for generations.
entries.literal: The Xingsi family for generations lived at Gushu.

entries.zh: 年十三，遊學京師，積十餘載，遂博通記傳，善屬文。
entries.en: At thirteen he studied in the capital; after ten-plus years he mastered records and wrote well.
entries.literal: At thirteen he traveled to study in the capital; over more than ten years he came to master records broadly and was skilled at literary composition.

entries.zh: 嘗步自姑孰，投宿逆旅，夜有人謂之曰：「子才學邁世，初當見識貴臣，卒被知英主。」
entries.en: Walking from Gushu he lodged at an inn; at night a voice said: "Your learning surpasses the age; first eminent ministers will know you, then an outstanding lord."
entries.literal: Once walking from Gushu he lodged at an inn; at night someone said to him: "Sir, your learning surpasses the age; at first you will be known to eminent ministers, and in the end favored by an outstanding lord."

entries.zh: 言終，不測所之。
entries.en: When it ended he could not tell where the man went.
entries.literal: When the speech ended, he could not tell where the man went.

entries.zh: 齊隆昌中，侍中謝朏爲吳興太守，唯與興嗣談文史而已。
entries.en: In Qi's Longchang, Xie Tiao as Wuxing grand administrator discussed only literature and history with Xingsi.
entries.literal: In Qi's Longchang era Attendant-in-ordinary Xie Tiao was Grand Administrator of Wuxing and discussed literature and history with Xingsi alone.

entries.zh: 及罷郡還，因大相稱薦。
entries.en: Leaving office he greatly praised and recommended him.
entries.literal: When he left his post and returned, he greatly commended and recommended him.

entries.zh: 本州舉秀才，除桂陽郡丞，太守王嶸素相賞好，禮之甚厚。
entries.en: Recommended as Outstanding Talent, he became Guiyang assistant; Grand Administrator Wang Rong long admired him and treated him generously.
entries.literal: The commandery recommended him as Outstanding Talent; he was appointed Assistant Administrator of Guiyang. Grand Administrator Wang Rong had long admired him and treated him with very thick courtesy.

entries.zh: 高祖革命，興嗣奏《休平賦》，其文甚美，高祖嘉之。
entries.en: When Gaozu took power, Xingsi submitted "Ode on Rest and Peace"—very fine, and Gaozu praised it.
entries.literal: When Gaozu overthrew the old regime, Xingsi submitted "Ode on Rest and Peace"; its writing was very fine and Gaozu praised it.

entries.zh: 拜安成王國侍郎，直華林省。
entries.en: He became Prince Ancheng's gentleman and served straight at Hualin.
entries.literal: He was appointed Gentleman of the Prince of Ancheng's state and served straight at the Hualin Office.

entries.zh: 其年，河南獻儛馬，詔興嗣與待詔到沆、張率爲賦，高祖以興嗣爲工。
entries.en: That year Henan sent tribute horses; Gaozu had Xingsi, Dao Hong, and Zhang Shuai compose fu and judged Xingsi best.
entries.literal: That year Henan presented tribute horses; an edict had Xingsi and Attendant-at-Draft Dao Hong and Zhang Shuai compose fu; Gaozu regarded Xingsi's as best.

entries.zh: 擢員外散騎侍郎，進直文德、壽光省。
entries.en: He rose to cadet-attendant emeritus and served straight in Wende and Shouguang.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Cadet-Attendant Emeritus and advanced to serve straight in the Wende and Shouguang offices.

entries.zh: 是時，高祖以三橋舊宅爲光宅寺，敕興嗣與陸倕各制寺碑。
entries.en: Gaozu made the Three Bridges old residence Guangzai Temple and ordered Xingsi and Lu Yan each to write a stele.
entries.literal: At that time Gaozu made the old residence at Three Bridges into Guangzai Temple and ordered Xingsi and Lu Yan each to compose a temple stele.

entries.zh: 及成俱奏，高祖用興嗣所制者。
entries.en: Both were submitted; Gaozu used Xingsi's.
entries.literal: When both were submitted Gaozu used the one Xingsi composed.

entries.zh: 自是《銅表銘》、《柵塘碣》、《北伐檄》、《次韻王羲之書千字》，並使興嗣爲文；
entries.en: Thence the bronze-column inscription, barrier-pond stele, northern expedition proclamation, and verse matching Wang Xizhi's Thousand Characters all went to Xingsi;
entries.literal: From then on the Bronze Column Inscription, Barrier Pond Stele, Northern Expedition Proclamation, and verse matching Wang Xizhi's Thousand Characters were all entrusted to Xingsi for the text;

entries.zh: 每奏，高祖輒稱善，加賜金帛。
entries.en: each submission won praise and gifts of gold and silk.
entries.literal: each time he submitted, Gaozu would praise it and add gifts of gold and silk.

entries.zh: 九年，除新安郡丞，秩滿，復爲員外散騎侍郎，佐撰國史。
entries.en: Year nine he became Xin'an assistant; after his term he again became cadet-attendant emeritus and helped compile national history.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Assistant Administrator of Xin'an; when his term expired he again became Cadet-Attendant Emeritus and assisted in compiling the National History.

entries.zh: 十二年，遷給事中，撰文如故。
entries.en: Year twelve he became supervisor of attendants, writing as before.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to Supervisor of Attendants, composing documents as before.

entries.zh: 興嗣兩手先患風疽，是年又染癘疾，左目盲，高祖撫其手，嗟曰：「斯人也而有斯疾也！」
entries.en: Xingsi long had wind sores in both hands; that year plague came and his left eye went blind; Gaozu stroked his hand: "That such a man should have such illness!"
entries.literal: Xingsi had long suffered wind sores in both hands; that year he also caught plague, his left eye went blind; Gaozu stroked his hand and sighed: "That a man like this should have such an illness!"

entries.zh: 手疏治疽方以賜之。
entries.en: Gaozu drafted a sore-treatment prescription by hand and gave it him.
entries.literal: By hand he drafted a prescription for treating sores and bestowed it on him.

entries.zh: 其見惜如此。
entries.en: He was cherished thus.
entries.literal: He was cherished thus.

entries.zh: 任昉又愛其才，常言曰：「周興嗣若無疾，旬日當至御史中丞。」
entries.en: Ren Fang loved his talent and said: "Without Zhou Xingsi's illness, within ten days he would reach vice censor-in-chief."
entries.literal: Ren Fang also loved his talent and often said: "Were it not for Zhou Xingsi's illness, within ten days he would reach Vice Director of the Secretariat Censorate."

entries.zh: 十四年，除臨川郡丞。
entries.en: Year fourteen he became Linchuan assistant.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Assistant Administrator of Linchuan.

entries.zh: 十七年，復爲給事中，直西省。
entries.en: Year seventeen he again became supervisor of attendants, serving straight in the Western Office.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year he again became Supervisor of Attendants, serving straight in the Western Office.

entries.zh: 左衛率周捨奉敕注高祖所制歷代賦，啓興嗣助焉。
entries.en: Zhou She of the Left Guard received an edict to annotate imperial fu and asked Xingsi to assist.
entries.literal: Leader of the Left Guard Zhou She received an edict to annotate the various fu composed by successive emperors as ordered by Gaozu, and memorialized that Xingsi should assist.

entries.zh: 普通二年，卒。
entries.en: In Putong year two he died.
entries.literal: In the second year of Putong he died.

entries.zh: 所撰《皇帝實錄》、《皇德記》、《起居注》、《職儀》等百餘卷，文集十卷。
entries.en: He compiled Imperial Veritable Records, Record of Imperial Virtue, Daily Records, Rites of Office, and more—over a hundred juan—and ten juan of collected writings.
entries.literal: What he compiled—*Imperial Veritable Records*, *Record of Imperial Virtue*, *Daily Records*, *Rites of Office*, and the like—totaled over a hundred juan, and his collected writings ten juan.

entries.zh: 到沆 丘遲 劉苞 袁峻 庾於陵 弟肩吾 劉昭 何遜 鍾嶸 周興嗣 吳均
entries.en: Dao Hang · Qiu Chi · Liu Bao · Yuan Jun · Yu Yuling · Jianwu (brother) · Liu Zhao · He Xun · Zhong Rong · Zhou Xingsi · Wu Jun
entries.literal: Dao Hang, Qiu Chi, Liu Bao, Yuan Jun, Yu Yuling, younger brother Jianwu, Liu Zhao, He Xun, Zhong Rong, Zhou Xingsi, Wu Jun

entries.zh: 《易》曰：「亢之爲言也，知進而不知退，知存而不知亡。
entries.en: The Changes says: "Excess" means knowing when to advance but not when to retreat, knowing how to preserve but not how to perish.
entries.literal: The Changes says: "Excess means knowing advance but not retreat, knowing preservation but not loss.

entries.zh: 知進退存亡而不失其正者，其唯聖人乎！」
entries.en: Only the sage knows advance, retreat, preservation, and loss without losing the Mean!"
entries.literal: Knowing advance, retreat, preservation, and loss without losing the Mean—surely only the sage can do this!"

entries.zh: 《傳》曰：「知足不辱，知止不殆。」
entries.en: The Tradition says: "Knowing sufficiency brings no disgrace; knowing when to stop brings no danger."
entries.literal: The Tradition says: "Knowing sufficiency brings no disgrace; knowing when to stop brings no danger."

entries.zh: 然則不知夫進退，不達乎止足，殆辱之累，期月而至矣。
entries.en: Yet those who misjudge advance and retreat and never grasp sufficiency and stopping invite disgrace and danger within a month.
entries.literal: Yet if one does not understand advance and retreat, and does not grasp sufficiency and stopping, the burden of disgrace and danger arrives within a month.

entries.zh: 古人之進也，以康世濟務也，以弘道厲俗也。
entries.en: Men of old advanced to comfort the age, aid affairs, spread the Way, and sharpen custom.
entries.literal: When men of old advanced, it was to bring peace to the age and aid affairs, to spread the Way and sharpen custom.

entries.zh: 然其進也，光寵夷易，故愚夫之所乾沒；
entries.en: Advance brought easy glory and favor, so fools scrambled for them;
entries.literal: When they advanced, glory and favor came easily, so fools scrambled for them;

entries.zh: 其退也，苦節艱貞，故庸曹之所忌憚。
entries.en: withdrawal meant bitter integrity and hard constancy that vulgar men feared and resented.
entries.literal: when they withdrew, bitter integrity and hard constancy made vulgar men fear and resent them.

entries.zh: 雖禍敗危亡，陳乎耳目，而輕舉高蹈，寡乎前史。
entries.en: Though disaster and ruin lay before their eyes, few in earlier histories lightly rose and walked away.
entries.literal: Though disaster, defeat, peril, and ruin lay before their eyes, lightly to rise and walk high—few in earlier histories did so.

entries.zh: 漢世張良功成身退，病臥卻粒，比於樂毅、范蠡至乎顛狽，斯爲優矣。
entries.en: In Han, Zhang Liang achieved merit and withdrew, took to his bed and ceased grain—compared with Yue Yi and Fan Li, even to their ruin, he was the better case.
entries.literal: In Han, Zhang Liang achieved merit and withdrew his person, took to his bed and ceased grain—compared with Yue Yi and Fan Li, down to their ruin, he was the better case.

entries.zh: 其後薛廣德及二疏等，去就以禮，有可稱焉。
entries.en: Later Xue Guangde and the two Shus withdrew according to ritual—there is something to praise in that.
entries.literal: Afterward Xue Guangde and the two Shus and others withdrew and took office according to ritual—there is something to praise in that.

entries.zh: 魚豢《魏略·知足傳》，方田、徐於管、胡，則其道本異。
entries.en: Yu Huan's "Biography of Knowing Sufficiency" in the Wei Summary pairs Tian and Xu with Guan and Hu—their Ways were fundamentally different.
entries.literal: Yu Huan's "Biography of Knowing Sufficiency" in the Wei Summary pairs Tian and Xu with Guan and Hu—their Ways were fundamentally different.

entries.zh: 謝靈運《晉書·止足傳》，先論晉世文士之避亂者，殆非其人；
entries.en: Xie Lingyun's Jin History "Biography of Knowing When to Stop" discusses literary men fleeing disorder—hardly the right men;
entries.literal: Xie Lingyun's "Biography of Knowing When to Stop" in the Jin History first discusses Jin-era literary men who fled disorder—hardly the right men;

entries.zh: 唯阮思曠遺榮好遁，遠殆辱矣。
entries.en: only Ruan Sixiao left glory and loved withdrawal, far from nearly suffering disgrace.
entries.literal: only Ruan Sixiao left glory and loved withdrawal, far from nearly suffering disgrace.

entries.zh: 《宋書·止足傳》有羊欣、王微，咸其流亞。
entries.en: The Song History "Biography of Knowing Sufficiency" has Yang Xin and Wang Wei—both of that stream.
entries.literal: The Song History "Biography of Knowing Sufficiency" has Yang Xin and Wang Wei—both of that stream.

entries.zh: 齊時沛國劉瓛，字子珪，辭祿懷道，棲遲養志，不戚戚於貧賤，不耽耽於富貴，儒行之高者也。
entries.en: In Qi, Liu Huan of Pei, styled Zigui, declined salary and cherished the Way, lingered to nourish his will—neither fretful in poverty nor greedy in wealth: a Confucian of the highest conduct.
entries.literal: In Qi times Liu Huan of Pei, courtesy name Zigui, declined salary and cherished the Way, lingered and nourished his will—neither fretful in poverty nor greedy in wealth: a Confucian of the highest conduct.

entries.zh: 梁有天下，小人道消，賢士大夫相招在位，其量力守志，則當世罔聞，時或有致事告老，或有寡志少欲，國史書之，亦以爲《止足傳》云。
entries.en: When Liang possessed the realm, petty ways faded and worthy men took office together. Those who measured strength and kept resolve went unmentioned; some reported illness and retired, some had few desires—the state history records them in this Biography of Knowing Sufficiency as well.
entries.literal: When Liang possessed the realm, the way of petty men faded; worthy scholar-officials summoned one another to office. Those who measured their strength and kept their resolve went unmentioned in their day; sometimes men reported illness and retired, or had few desires— the state history records them in this "Biography of Knowing Sufficiency" as well.

entries.zh: 遷車騎功曹、晉熙王友。
entries.en: He was transferred to Registrar of the Chariots and Cavalry and Friend of the Prince of Jinxi.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Registrar of the Chariots and Cavalry and Friend of the Prince of Jinxi.

entries.zh: 齊高帝執政，以爲驃騎錄事參軍，遷太尉西曹掾。
entries.en: When Qi Gaozu held the government, he made him Recorder of the Rapid Cavalry and transferred him to Western Section Clerk of the Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: When Qi Gaozu held the government, he made him Recorder of the Rapid Cavalry and transferred him to Western Section Clerk of the Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 齊臺建，爲中書侍郎。
entries.en: When the Qi regime was established, he became Attendant of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: When the Qi regime was established, he became Attendant of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 齊高帝卽位，除衡陽內史。
entries.en: When Qi Gaozu took the throne, he was appointed administrator of Hengyang.
entries.literal: When Qi Gaozu took the throne, he was appointed Administrator of Hengyang.

entries.zh: 先是，郡境連歲疾疫，死者太半，棺木尤貴，悉裹以葦席，棄之路傍。
entries.en: Before this, plague had struck year after year and more than half died; coffin wood was costly, and corpses were wrapped in reed mats and cast beside the road.
entries.literal: Before this, within the commandery plague had struck year after year and more than half had died; coffin wood was especially costly, and corpses were wrapped only in reed mats and cast beside the road.

entries.zh: 憲之下車，分告屬縣，求其親黨，悉令殯葬。
entries.en: When Xianzhi took office, he sent word to subordinate counties to seek kin and had them all buried properly.
entries.literal: When Xianzhi took office, he sent word to the subordinate counties to seek kin and had them all buried properly.

entries.zh: 其家人絕滅者，憲之爲出公祿，使綱紀營護之。
entries.en: For families whose line was extinguished, Xianzhi paid from public salary and had clerks arrange care.
entries.literal: For families whose line was extinguished, Xianzhi paid from public salary and had the clerks arrange care.

entries.zh: 又土俗，山民有病，輒云先人爲禍，皆開塚剖棺，水洗枯骨，名爲除祟。
entries.en: Again, by local custom when mountain folk fell ill they said ancestors were the harm, opening tombs and washing dry bones—called "removing the curse."
entries.literal: Again, by local custom when mountain folk fell ill they would say the ancestors were the harm, all opening tombs and coffins, washing dry bones—called "removing the curse."

entries.zh: 憲之曉喻，爲陳生死之別，事不相由，風俗遂改。
entries.en: Xianzhi enlightened them on life and death and that the affairs do not bear on one another—the custom changed.
entries.literal: Xianzhi enlightened them, setting forth the distinction of life and death and that the affairs do not bear on one another—the custom was thus changed.

entries.zh: 時刺史王奐新至，唯衡陽獨無訟者，乃歎曰：「顧衡陽之化至矣。
entries.en: Inspector Wang Huan had newly arrived; only Hengyang had no litigation, and he sighed: "Administrator Gu of Hengyang's transformation has reached the utmost.
entries.literal: At the time Inspector Wang Huan had newly arrived; only in Hengyang was there no litigation, and he sighed: "Administrator Gu of Hengyang's transformation has reached the utmost.

entries.zh: 若九郡率然，吾將何事！」
entries.en: If the nine commanderies were all like this, what would I have to do!"
entries.literal: If the nine commanderies were all like this, what would I have to do!"

entries.zh: 及長，好學，淡於榮利。
entries.en: When grown he loved learning and was indifferent to glory and profit.
entries.literal: When grown he loved learning and was indifferent to glory and profit.

entries.zh: 起家桂陽王國侍郎、北中郎鎮西行參軍，並不起，時人號曰「聘君」。
entries.en: He began as Gentleman of the Kingdom of Guiyang and Army Aide on the Western Campaign of the Northern General of the Gentlemen, and did not take office—people called him "the Invited Gentleman."
entries.literal: He began his career as Gentleman of the Kingdom of Guiyang and Army Aide on the Western Campaign of the Northern General of the Gentlemen, and did not take office—people of the time called him "the Invited Gentleman."

entries.zh: 父憂服闋，尚書令劉秉領丹陽尹，引爲後軍主簿、領郡功曹。
entries.en: When mourning for his father ended, Liu Bing, concurrently administrator of Danyang, appointed him Chief Clerk of the Rear Army and concurrently Commandery Merit Officer.
entries.literal: When mourning for his father ended, Liu Bing, who was concurrently Administrator of Danyang, appointed him Chief Clerk of the Rear Army and concurrently Commandery Merit Officer.

entries.zh: 出爲望蔡令，頃之以病免。
entries.en: He went out as magistrate of Wangcai; shortly afterward he was excused on grounds of illness.
entries.literal: He went out as Magistrate of Wangcai; shortly afterward he was excused on grounds of illness.

entries.zh: 時劉秉、袁粲以齊高帝權勢日盛，將圖之，秉素重季直，欲與之定策。
entries.en: At the time Liu Bing and Yuan Can, because Qi Gaozu's power grew daily, were about to plot against him; Bing had always esteemed Jizhi and wished to settle strategy with him.
entries.literal: At the time Liu Bing and Yuan Can, because Qi Gaozu's power grew daily, were about to plot against him; Bing had always esteemed Jizhi and wished to settle strategy with him.

entries.zh: 季直以袁、劉儒者，必致顛殞，固辭不赴。
entries.en: Jizhi held that Yuan and Liu were Confucians and would surely come to ruin, and firmly declined to go.
entries.literal: Jizhi held that Yuan and Liu were Confucians and would surely come to ruin, and firmly declined to go.

entries.zh: 俄而秉等伏誅。
entries.en: Shortly afterward Bing and the others were executed.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward Bing and the others were executed.

entries.zh: 還爲太尉從事中郎。
entries.en: He returned as Retainer of the Masters of Affairs in the Grand Marshal's office.
entries.literal: He returned to serve as Retainer of the Masters of Affairs in the Grand Marshal's office.

entries.zh: 出爲東中郎長史、行會稽郡事。
entries.en: He went out as Chief Clerk of the Eastern General of the Gentlemen and acting administrator of Kuaiji.
entries.literal: He went out as Chief Clerk of the Eastern General of the Gentlemen and Acting Administrator of Kuaiji commandery.

entries.zh: 山陰人呂文度有寵於齊武帝，於餘姚立邸，頗縱橫。
entries.en: Lü Wendu of Shanyin had favor with Qi Wudi and established a lodge in Yuyao, behaving overbearingly.
entries.literal: Lü Wendu of Shanyin had favor with Qi Wudi and established a lodge in Yuyao, behaving quite overbearingly.

entries.zh: 憲之至郡，卽表除之。
entries.en: When Xianzhi reached the commandery, he memorialized at once to remove it.
entries.literal: When Xianzhi reached the commandery, he memorialized at once to remove it.

entries.zh: 文度後還葬母，郡縣爭赴弔，憲之不與相聞。
entries.en: Wendu later returned to bury his mother; commandery and county competed to attend mourning, but Xianzhi did not acknowledge it.
entries.literal: Wendu later returned to bury his mother; commandery and county competed to attend the mourning, but Xianzhi did not acknowledge it.

entries.zh: 文度深銜之，卒不能傷也。
entries.en: Wendu deeply resented this but in the end could not harm him.
entries.literal: Wendu deeply resented this but in the end could not harm him.

entries.zh: 遷南中郎巴陵王長史，加建威將軍、行婺州事。
entries.en: He was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Prince of Baling in the Southern General of the Gentlemen, with additional title General Who Establishes Might and acting governor of Wuzhou.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Prince of Baling in the Southern General of the Gentlemen, with additional title General Who Establishes Might and Acting Governor of Wuzhou.

entries.zh: 時司徒、竟陵王於宣城、臨成、定陵三縣界立屯，封山澤數百里，禁民樵采，憲之固陳不可，言甚切直。
entries.en: The Minister of Works, Prince of Jingling, enclosed mountains and marshes for hundreds of li and forbade firewood—Xianzhi firmly memorialized that this could not be, his words very blunt.
entries.literal: At the time the Minister of Works, Prince of Jingling, established garrisons on the borders of Xuancheng, Lincheng, and Dingling counties, enclosing mountains and marshes for hundreds of li and forbidding the people firewood and gathering—Xianzhi firmly memorialized that this could not be, his words very blunt and direct.

entries.zh: 王答之曰：「非君無以聞此德音。」
entries.en: The Prince replied: "Without you I would not have heard this virtuous word."
entries.literal: The Prince replied: "Without you I would not have heard this virtuous word."

entries.zh: 卽命無禁。
entries.en: He at once ordered no prohibition.
entries.literal: He at once ordered no prohibition.

entries.zh: 遷太尉記室參軍。
entries.en: He was transferred to Retainer of the Masters of Affairs in the Grand Marshal's office.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Retainer of the Masters of Affairs in the Grand Marshal's office.

entries.zh: 出爲冠軍司馬、東莞太守，在郡號爲清和。
entries.en: He went out as Army Aide to the Champion and administrator of Dongguan; in the commandery he was known as pure and harmonious.
entries.literal: He went out as Army Aide to the Champion and Administrator of Dongguan; in the commandery he was known as pure and harmonious.

entries.zh: 還除散騎侍郎，領左衛司馬，轉鎮西諮議參軍。
entries.en: On return he was appointed Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Colonel of the Left Guard, then transferred to Army Adviser on the Western Campaign.
entries.literal: On return he was appointed Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and concurrently Colonel of the Left Guard, then transferred to Army Adviser on the Western Campaign.

entries.zh: 齊武帝崩，明帝作相，誅鋤異己，季直不能阿意，明帝頗忌之，乃出爲輔國長史、北海太守。
entries.en: When Qi Wudi died, Mingdi became regent and purged dissenters; Jizhi could not flatter him and Mingdi feared him, sending him out as Chief Clerk Who Assists the State and administrator of Beihai.
entries.literal: When Qi Wudi died, Mingdi became regent, executed and purged those unlike himself; Jizhi could not flatter his intent and Mingdi quite feared him, so he sent him out as Chief Clerk Who Assists the State and Administrator of Beihai.

entries.zh: 邊職上佐，素士罕爲之者。
entries.en: Chief aide on a frontier post—plain scholars rarely held it.
entries.literal: Chief aide on a frontier post—plain scholars rarely held it.

entries.zh: 或勸季直造門致謝，明帝旣見，便留之，以爲驃騎諮議參軍，兼尚書左丞。
entries.en: Some urged Jizhi to call at his gate and apologize; once Mingdi saw him he kept him, making him Army Adviser on the Rapid Cavalry and Director of the Left in the Secretariat.
entries.literal: Some urged Jizhi to call at his gate and apologize; once Mingdi saw him he kept him, making him Army Adviser on the Rapid Cavalry and concurrently Director of the Left in the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 仍遷建安太守，政尚清靜，百姓便之。
entries.en: He was then transferred to administrator of Jian'an; his government prized quiet purity and the people found it easy.
entries.literal: He was then transferred to Administrator of Jian'an; his government prized quiet purity and the people found it easy.

entries.zh: 還爲中書侍郎，遷遊擊將軍、兼廷尉。
entries.en: On return he was Attendant of the Secretariat and transferred to General Who Strikes the Foe and minister of justice.
entries.literal: On return he was Attendant of the Secretariat and transferred to General Who Strikes the Foe and concurrently Minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 中興二年，義師平建康，高祖爲揚州牧，徵憲之爲別駕從事史。
entries.en: In the second year of Zhongxing, when the righteous army pacified Jiankang, Gaozu was governor of Yangzhou and summoned Xianzhi as Retainer of the Separate Chariot.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhongxing, when the righteous army pacified Jiankang, Gaozu was Governor of Yangzhou and summoned Xianzhi as Retainer of the Separate Chariot.

entries.zh: 比至，高祖已受禪，憲之風疾漸篤，固求還吳。
entries.en: By the time he arrived, Gaozu had already received the abdication; Xianzhi's wind ailment grew severe and he firmly asked to return to Wu.
entries.literal: By the time he arrived, Gaozu had already received the abdication; Xianzhi's wind ailment grew severe and he firmly asked to return to Wu.

entries.zh: 天監二年，就家授太中大夫。
entries.en: In the second year of Tianjian, he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace at his home.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianjian, he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace at his home.

entries.zh: 憲之雖累經宰郡，資無擔石。
entries.en: Though Xianzhi had repeatedly governed commanderies, his assets did not amount to a dan of grain.
entries.literal: Though Xianzhi had repeatedly governed commanderies, his assets did not amount to a dan of grain.

entries.zh: 及歸，環堵，不免饑寒。
entries.en: When he returned, his ring of walls could not keep out hunger and cold.
entries.literal: When he returned, his ring of walls could not keep out hunger and cold.

entries.zh: 八年，卒於家，年七十四。
entries.en: In the eighth year he died at home, aged seventy-four.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he died at home, aged seventy-four.

entries.zh: 臨終爲制，以敕其子曰：
entries.en: On his deathbed he made regulations and charged his sons, saying:
entries.literal: On his deathbed he made regulations and charged his sons, saying:

entries.zh: 梁臺建，遷給事黃門侍郎。
entries.en: When the Liang regime was established, he was transferred to Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
entries.literal: When the Liang regime was established, he was transferred to Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

entries.zh: 常稱仕至二千石，始願畢矣，無爲務人間之事，乃辭疾還鄉里。
entries.en: He often said that serving to two-thousand-dan salary fulfilled his original wish, and he would not busy himself with worldly affairs—then he pleaded illness and returned home.
entries.literal: He often said that serving to the rank of two-thousand-dan salary fulfilled his original wish, and he would not busy himself with worldly affairs—then he pleaded illness and returned to his home village.

entries.zh: 天監初，就家拜太中大夫。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tianjian he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace at his home.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace at his home.

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「梁有天下，遂不見此人。」
entries.en: Gaozu said: "Liang has possessed the realm, yet I never saw this man."
entries.literal: Gaozu said: "Liang has possessed the realm, yet I never saw this man."

entries.zh: 十年，卒於家，時年七十五。
entries.en: In the tenth year he died at home, aged seventy-five.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he died at home, aged seventy-five.

entries.zh: 季直素清苦絕倫，又屏居十餘載，及死，家徒四壁，子孫無以殯斂，聞者莫不傷其志焉。
entries.en: Jizhi was pure and bitter beyond compare; he lived in seclusion more than ten years, and at death his house had only bare walls—descendants had no means for burial; hearers grieved for his resolve.
entries.literal: Jizhi was by nature pure and bitter beyond compare; he also lived in seclusion for more than ten years, and at death his house had only bare walls—sons and grandsons had no means for burial; hearers all grieved for his resolve.

entries.zh: 眎素早孤貧，爲叔父惠休所收卹。
entries.en: Shisu was orphaned young and poor and was taken in by his uncle Huixiu.
entries.literal: Shisu was orphaned young and poor and was taken in and supported by his uncle Huixiu.

entries.zh: 起家爲齊司徒法曹行參軍，遷著作佐郎、太子舍人、尚書三公郎。
entries.en: He began as Army Aide in the Law Section of the Qi Minister of Works, transferred to Assistant Gentleman of the Secretariat, Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and Director of the Three Excellencies Section.
entries.literal: He began his career as Army Aide in the Law Section of the Qi Minister of Works, transferred to Assistant Gentleman of the Secretariat, Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and Director of the Three Excellencies Section in the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 永元末，爲太子洗馬。
entries.en: At the end of Yongyuan he was Groom of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: At the end of Yongyuan he was Groom of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 梁臺建，高祖引爲中尉驃騎記室參軍。
entries.en: When the Liang regime was established, Gaozu appointed him Retainer of the Masters of Affairs in the Rapid Cavalry and Central Commandant.
entries.literal: When the Liang regime was established, Gaozu appointed him Retainer of the Masters of Affairs in the Rapid Cavalry and Central Commandant.

entries.zh: 天監初，爲臨川王友，復爲太子中舍人、丹陽尹丞。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tianjian he was Friend of the Prince of Linchuan, then Cadet of the Heir Apparent and assistant to the administrator of Danyang.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he was Friend of the Prince of Linchuan, then again Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Assistant to the Administrator of Danyang.

entries.zh: 初拜，高祖賜錢八萬，眎素一朝散之親友。
entries.en: On first taking office Gaozu bestowed eighty thousand cash; Shisu in one morning scattered it among kin and friends.
entries.literal: On first taking office Gaozu bestowed eighty thousand cash; Shisu in one morning scattered it among kin and friends.

entries.zh: 又遷司徒左西屬、南徐州治中。
entries.en: He was again transferred to Western Section Clerk of the Left in the Minister of Works and concurrent administrator of Southern Xuzhou.
entries.literal: He was again transferred to Western Section Clerk of the Left in the Minister of Works and Concurrent Administrator of Southern Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 莊周、澹臺，達生者也；
entries.en: Zhuang Zhou and Tantai Mieming had attained life;
entries.literal: Zhuang Zhou and Tantai Mieming were men who had attained life;

entries.zh: 王孫、士安，矯俗者也。
entries.en: Wang Sun and Shi An corrected vulgar custom.
entries.literal: Wang Sun and Shi An were men who had corrected vulgar custom.

entries.zh: 吾進不及達，退無所矯。
entries.en: In advance I do not reach attainment; in withdrawal I have nothing to correct.
entries.literal: In advance I do not reach attainment; in withdrawal I have nothing to correct.

entries.zh: 常謂中都之制，允理愜情。
entries.en: I have always held that the mid-dynasty system accords with reason and satisfies feeling.
entries.literal: I have always held that the mid-dynasty system accords with reason and satisfies feeling.

entries.zh: 衣周於身，示不違禮；
entries.en: Clothing sufficient for the body shows one does not violate ritual;
entries.literal: Clothing sufficient for the body shows one does not violate ritual;

entries.zh: 棺周於衣，足以蔽臭。
entries.en: a coffin sufficient for the clothing is enough to cover stench.
entries.literal: a coffin sufficient for the clothing is enough to cover stench.

entries.zh: 入棺之物，一無所須。
entries.en: What goes into the coffin—nothing is needed.
entries.literal: What goes into the coffin—nothing is needed.

entries.zh: 載以輴車，覆以粗布，爲使人勿惡也。
entries.en: Carry on a bier-cart, cover with coarse cloth—so people will not be disgusted.
entries.literal: Carry on a bier-cart, cover with coarse cloth—so people will not be disgusted.

entries.zh: 漢明帝天子之尊，猶祭以杅水脯糗；
entries.en: Emperor Ming of Han, though Son of Heaven, still sacrificed with ladle-water, dried meat, and parched grain;
entries.literal: Emperor Ming of Han, though honored as Son of Heaven, still sacrificed with ladle-water, dried meat, and parched grain;

entries.zh: 范史雲烈士之高，亦奠以寒水乾飯。
entries.en: Fan Shiyun, lofty as a martyr, also offered cold water and dry rice.
entries.literal: Fan Shiyun, lofty as a martyr, also offered cold water and dry rice.

entries.zh: 況吾卑庸之人，其可不節衷也？
entries.en: How much more for a low and mediocre man like me—can he not restrain his feelings?
entries.literal: How much more for a man low and mediocre like me—can he not restrain his feelings?

entries.zh: 喪易寧戚，自是親親之情；
entries.en: Mourning is easy but dwelling in grief is hard—this is kin affection;
entries.literal: Mourning is easy but dwelling in grief is hard—this is the affection of kin for kin;

entries.zh: 禮奢寧儉，差可得由吾意。
entries.en: ritual extravagant but dwelling in frugality is somewhat attainable according to my will.
entries.literal: ritual extravagant but dwelling in frugality is somewhat attainable according to my will.

entries.zh: 不須常施靈筵，可止設香燈，使致哀者有憑耳。
entries.en: Do not constantly set out spirit mats; stop at lighting incense lamps, so mourners have something to rely on.
entries.literal: Do not constantly set out spirit mats; stop at lighting incense lamps, so those who would mourn have something to rely on.

entries.zh: 朔望祥忌，可權安小床，暫設幾席，唯下素饌，勿用牲牢。
entries.en: On the first and fifteenth and mourning anniversaries, provisionally set a small couch and briefly place mats, offering only plain food—do not use sacrificial animals.
entries.literal: On the first and fifteenth and on mourning anniversaries, one may provisionally set a small couch and briefly place mats and seats, offering only plain food—do not use sacrificial animals.

entries.zh: 蒸嘗之祠，貴賤罔替。
entries.en: Seasonal sacrifices to ancestors—noble and base alike do not omit them.
entries.literal: Seasonal sacrifices to ancestors—noble and base alike do not omit them.

entries.zh: 備物難辦，多致疏怠。
entries.en: Full provision is hard to prepare and often leads to neglect.
entries.literal: Full provision is hard to prepare and often leads to neglect.

entries.zh: 祠先人自有舊典，不可有闕。
entries.en: Sacrificing to forebears has its old canon—it cannot be wanting.
entries.literal: Sacrificing to forebears has its old canon—it cannot be wanting.

entries.zh: 自吾以下，祠止用蔬食時果，勿同於上世也。
entries.en: From me downward, sacrifice only with vegetables, grain, and seasonal fruit—do not be like upper generations.
entries.literal: From me downward, sacrifice only with vegetables, grain, seasonal fruit—do not be like the upper generations.

entries.zh: 示令子孫，四時不忘其親耳。
entries.en: Show sons and grandsons so the four seasons do not forget their kin.
entries.literal: Show the sons and grandsons so the four seasons do not forget their kin.

entries.zh: 孔子云：「雖菜羹瓜祭，必齊如也。」
entries.en: Confucius said: "Even with vegetable broth and melon sacrifice, one must be as if present."
entries.literal: Confucius said: "Even with vegetable broth and melon sacrifice, one must be as if present."

entries.zh: 本貴誠敬，豈求備物哉？
entries.en: The root values sincere reverence—how could one seek full provision?
entries.literal: The root values sincere reverence—how could one seek full provision?

entries.zh: 齊初，爲尚書比部郎，時褚淵爲尚書令，與季直素善，頻以爲司空司徒主簿，委以府事。
entries.en: At the beginning of Qi he was Director of the Ministry of Justice Comparison Section; Chu Yuan was Director of the Imperial Secretariat and was on good terms with Jizhi, repeatedly making him Registrar to the Minister of Works and Minister of Education, entrusting him with bureau affairs.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qi he was Director of the Ministry of Justice Comparison Section; at the time Chu Yuan was Minister of Works and was on good terms with Jizhi, repeatedly making him Registrar of the Masters of Works and Minister of Works, entrusting him with bureau affairs.

entries.zh: 淵卒，尚書令王儉以淵有至行，欲諡爲文孝公，季直請曰：「文孝是司馬道子諡，恐其人非具美，不如文簡。」
entries.en: When Yuan died, Wang Jian wished to posthumously title him Duke Wenxiao; Jizhi petitioned: "Wenxiao was Sima Daozi's posthumous title—I fear the man was not wholly good; better Wenjian."
entries.literal: When Yuan died, Director of the Imperial Secretariat Wang Jian, because Yuan had utmost conduct, wished to posthumously title him Duke Wenxiao; Jizhi petitioned: "Wenxiao was Sima Daozi's posthumous title—I fear the man was not wholly good; better Wenjian."

entries.zh: 儉從之。
entries.en: Jian followed this.
entries.literal: Jian followed this.

entries.zh: 季直又請儉爲淵立碑，終始營護，甚有吏節，時人美之。
entries.en: Jizhi also asked Jian to erect a stele for Yuan and saw to it from start to finish—very much official conduct; people praised this.
entries.literal: Jizhi also asked Jian to erect a stele for Yuan and saw to it from start to finish—very much the conduct of an official; people of the time praised this.

entries.zh: 性靜退，少嗜欲，好學，能清言，榮利不關於口，喜怒不形於色。
entries.en: Quiet and retiring by nature, with few desires; he loved learning, spoke with pure refinement, and profit and glory did not touch his lips—joy and anger did not show on his face.
entries.literal: By nature he was quiet and retiring, with few desires; he loved learning, could speak with pure refinement, and profit and glory did not touch his lips—joy and anger did not show on his face.

entries.zh: 在人間及居職，並任情通率，不自矜高，天然簡素，士人以此咸敬之。
entries.en: Among people and in office he was open and direct, never proud; naturally plain and simple—scholars all honored him for this.
entries.literal: Among people and in office he was always according to feeling, open and direct, never proud of himself; naturally plain and simple—scholar-gentry all honored him for this.

entries.zh: 及在京口，便有終焉之志，乃於攝山築室。
entries.en: When at Jingkou he already had the will to end his days there and built a house on Mt She.
entries.literal: When at Jingkou he already had the will to end his days there and built a house on Mt She.

entries.zh: 會徵爲中書侍郎，遂辭不就，因還山宅，獨居屏事，非親戚不得至其籬門。
entries.en: Summoned as Attendant of the Secretariat, he declined; he returned to his mountain dwelling, lived alone, and kin and friends could not reach his hedge gate.
entries.literal: He was summoned as Attendant of the Secretariat and then declined and did not go; he returned to his mountain dwelling, lived alone and screened affairs, and kin and friends could not reach his hedge gate.

entries.zh: 妻，太尉王儉女，久與別居，遂無子。
entries.en: His wife was the daughter of Grand Marshal Wang Jian; long separated from him, in the end there were no sons.
entries.literal: His wife was the daughter of Grand Marshal Wang Jian; long separated from him, in the end there were no sons.

entries.zh: 八年，卒。
entries.en: In the eighth year he died.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he died.

entries.zh: 親故迹其事行，諡曰貞文先生。
entries.en: Kin and friends traced his conduct and gave the posthumous title Recluse Zhenwen.
entries.literal: Kin and friends traced his conduct and deeds and gave the posthumous title Recluse Zhenwen.

entries.zh: 豫章王綜 武陵王紀 臨賀王正德 河東王譽
entries.en: Prince Xiao Zong of Yuzhang; Prince Xiao Ji of Wuling; Prince Zhengde of Linhe; Prince Yu of Hedong
entries.literal: Prince Xiao Zong of Yuzhang; Prince Xiao Ji of Wuling; Prince Zhengde of Linhe; Prince Yu of Hedong

entries.zh: 武陵王紀字世詢，高祖第八子也。
entries.en: Prince Xiao Ji of Wuling, styled Shixun, was Gaozu's eighth son.
entries.literal: Prince Xiao Ji of Wuling, styled Shixun, was Gaozu's eighth son.

entries.zh: 少勤學，有文才，屬辭不好輕華，甚有骨氣。
entries.en: In youth he studied diligently; he had literary talent, disliked frivolous ornament in composition, and possessed considerable backbone.
entries.literal: In youth he studied diligently; he had literary talent, disliked frivolous ornament in composition, and possessed considerable backbone.

entries.zh: 天監十三年，封爲武陵郡王，邑二千戶。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year of Tianjian he was enfeoffed as Prince of Wuling commandery, fief of two thousand households.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianjian he was enfeoffed as Prince of Wuling commandery, fief of two thousand households.

entries.zh: 歷位寧遠將軍、琅邪彭城二郡太守、輕車將軍、丹陽尹。
entries.en: He held in succession General Who Calms the Distance, administrator of the two commanderies Langye and Pengcheng, Light Chariot General, and governor of Danyang.
entries.literal: He held in succession General Who Calms the Distance, Administrator of the two commanderies Langye and Pengcheng, Light Chariot General, and Governor of Danyang.

entries.zh: 出爲會稽太守，尋以其郡爲東揚州，仍爲刺史，加使持節、東中郎將。
entries.en: He went out as administrator of Kuaiji; soon that commandery became East Yangzhou, and he remained as inspector, additionally bearer of the staff and East Central General.
entries.literal: He went out as Administrator of Kuaiji; soon that commandery became East Yangzhou, and he remained as Inspector, additionally Bearer of the Staff and East Central General.

entries.zh: 徵爲侍中，領石頭戍軍事。
entries.en: He was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary, overseeing Stone Fort garrison affairs.
entries.literal: He was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary, overseeing Stone Fort garrison affairs.

entries.zh: 出爲宣惠將軍、江州刺史。
entries.en: He went out as Propagation and Grace General and inspector of Jiangzhou.
entries.literal: He went out as Propagation and Grace General and Inspector of Jiangzhou.

entries.zh: 徵爲使持節、宣惠將軍、都督揚南徐二州諸軍事、揚州刺史。
entries.en: He was summoned as bearer of the staff, Propagation and Grace General, commander of Yang and South Xu military affairs, and inspector of Yangzhou.
entries.literal: He was summoned as Bearer of the Staff, Propagation and Grace General, Commander of military affairs of Yang and South Xu provinces, and Inspector of Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 尋改授持節、都督益梁等十三州諸軍事、安西將軍、益州刺史，加鼓吹一部。
entries.en: Soon he was reassigned bearer of the staff, commander of Yi, Liang, and eleven other provinces, Pacification West General, and inspector of Yizhou, granted one suite of martial music.
entries.literal: Soon he was reassigned Bearer of the Staff, Commander of military affairs of Yi, Liang, and eleven other provinces, Pacification West General, and Inspector of Yizhou, granted one suite of martial music.

entries.zh: 大同十一年，授散騎常侍、征西大將軍、開府儀同三司。
entries.en: In the eleventh year of Datong he was granted Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, Great General Who Conquers the West, and the privilege of establishing a separate office with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Dukes.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year of Datong he was granted Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, Great General Who Conquers the West, and [the right of] opening an office with ceremony equal to the Three Dukes.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：蕭綜、蕭正德並悖逆倡狂，自致夷滅，宜矣。
entries.en: The historian writes: Xiao Zong and Xiao Zhengde were rebels and madmen who destroyed themselves—no more than they deserved.
entries.literal: The historian writes: Xiao Zong and Xiao Zhengde both rebelled and raved in treason, bringing extinction on themselves—as they deserved.

entries.zh: 太清之寇，蕭紀據庸、蜀之資，遂不勤王赴難，申臣子之節；
entries.en: In the Taiqing disaster Xiao Ji held the wealth of Yong and Shu yet never rushed to the throne's rescue or kept a son's or subject's duty;
entries.literal: In the Taiqing calamity, Xiao Ji held the resources of Yong and Shu, yet did not hasten to the king's aid in crisis or fulfill a subject's and son's duty;

entries.zh: 及賊景誅剪，方始起兵，師出無名，成其釁禍。
entries.en: only after Hou Jing was destroyed did he march—an army without just cause, sealing his own ruin.
entries.literal: only after the bandit Jing was cut down did he at last raise troops—an army setting out without cause, completing his stain of disaster.

entries.zh: 嗚呼！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 身當管、蔡之罰，蓋自貽哉。
entries.en: He suffered the fate of Guan and Cai—and had only himself to blame.
entries.literal: Bearing punishment like Guan and Cai—he brought it on himself.

entries.zh: 初，天監中，震太陽門，成字曰「紹宗梁位唯武王」，解者以爲武王者，武陵王也，於是朝野屬意焉。
entries.en: At first, in the Tianjian era, the Sun Gate was struck by earthquake; a sign formed that read, "To continue the Liang throne, only the Martial Prince." Interpreters held that "Martial Prince" meant the Prince of Wuling, and court and commoners looked to him.
entries.literal: At first, in the Tianjian era, the Sun Gate was struck by earthquake; a sign read "The Liang throne belongs only to the Prince of Wu"—interpreters held that the Prince of Wu meant Prince Ji of Wuling, and court and commoners looked to him.

entries.zh: 及太清中，侯景亂，紀不赴援。
entries.en: During the Taiqing era, when Hou Jing rebelled, Ji did not come to the rescue.
entries.literal: During the Taiqing era, when Hou Jing rebelled, Ji did not come to the rescue.

entries.zh: 高祖崩後，紀乃僭號於蜀，改年曰天正。
entries.en: After Gaozu died, Ji seized imperial title in Shu, changing the era name to Tianzheng.
entries.literal: After Gaozu died, Ji seized imperial title in Shu, changing the era name to Tianzheng.

entries.zh: 立子圓照爲皇太子，圓正爲西陽王，圓滿竟陵王，圓普南譙王，圓肅宜都王。
entries.en: He made his son Yuanzhao crown prince, Yuanzheng Prince of Xiyang, Yuanman Prince of Jingling, Yuanpu Prince of Nanqiao, and Yuansu Prince of Yidu.
entries.literal: He made his son Yuanzhao crown prince, Yuanzheng Prince of Xiyang, Yuanman Prince of Jingling, Yuanpu Prince of Nanqiao, and Yuansu Prince of Yidu.

entries.zh: 以巴西、梓潼二郡太守永豊侯撝征西大將軍、益州刺史，封秦郡王。
entries.en: Marquis Huo of Yongfeng, administrator of Baxi and Zitong, was appointed Great General Who Conquers the West and inspector of Yizhou, enfeoffed as Prince of Qin commandery.
entries.literal: Marquis Huo of Yongfeng, Administrator of Baxi and Zitong, was appointed Great General Who Conquers the West and Inspector of Yizhou, enfeoffed as Prince of Qin commandery.

entries.zh: 司馬王僧略、直兵參軍徐怦並固諫，紀以爲貳於己，皆殺之。
entries.en: Master of Affairs Wang Senglue and Direct Service Army Officer Xu Ping both remonstrated firmly; Ji took this as disloyalty and had both killed.
entries.literal: Master of Affairs Wang Senglue and Direct Service Army Officer Xu Ping both remonstrated firmly; Ji took this as disloyalty and had both killed.

entries.zh: 永豊侯撝歎曰：「王不免矣！
entries.en: Marquis Huo of Yongfeng sighed, "The prince is doomed!
entries.literal: Marquis Huo of Yongfeng sighed: "The prince is doomed!

entries.zh: 夫善人、國之基也，今反誅之，不亡何待！」
entries.en: good men are the foundation of a state; now he kills them—how can it not perish!"
entries.literal: Good men are the foundation of a state; now he kills them—how can it not perish!"

entries.zh: 又謂所親曰：「昔桓玄年號大亨，識者謂之『二月了』，而玄之敗實在仲春。
entries.en: he also told his intimates, "In the past Huan Xuan took the era name Daheng; interpreters called it 'the second month is done,' and his defeat indeed came in the second month.
entries.literal: He also told his intimates: "In the past Huan Xuan took the era name Daheng; interpreters called it 'the second month is done,' and his defeat indeed came in the second month.

entries.zh: 今年曰天正，在文爲『一止』，其能久乎？」
entries.en: this year is called Tianzheng—in writing it is 'one stop'—how long can it last?"
entries.literal: This year is called Tianzheng—in writing it is 'one stop'—how long can it last?"

entries.zh: 太清五年夏四月，紀帥軍東下至巴郡，以討侯景爲名，將圖荊陝。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer in the fifth year of Taiqing, Ji led his army east to Ba commandery, claiming to attack Hou Jing but intending to seize Jing and Shan.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of summer in the fifth year of Taiqing, Ji led his army east to Ba commandery, claiming to attack Hou Jing but intending to seize Jing and Shan.

entries.zh: 聞西魏侵蜀，遣其將南梁州刺史譙淹迴軍赴援。
entries.en: Hearing Western Wei invade Shu, he sent his general Qiao Yan, inspector of Southern Liangzhou, to turn the army back for relief.
entries.literal: Hearing Western Wei invade Shu, he sent his general Qiao Yan, Inspector of Southern Liangzhou, to turn the army back for relief.

entries.zh: 五月日，西魏將尉遲迥帥衆逼涪水，潼州刺史楊乾運以城降之，迥分軍據守，卽趨成都。
entries.en: On the fifth month day, Western Wei general Yuchi Tong led troops to press the Fu River; Tongzhou inspector Yang Qianyun surrendered the city, and Tong divided his forces to hold it and rushed straight for Chengdu.
entries.literal: On the fifth month day, Western Wei general Yuchi Tong led troops to press the Fu River; Tongzhou Inspector Yang Qianyun surrendered the city, and Tong divided his forces to hold it and rushed straight for Chengdu.

entries.zh: 丁丑，紀次于西陵，舳艫翳川，旌甲曜日，軍容甚盛。
entries.en: On day dingchou, Ji halted at Xiling; warships crowded the river, banners and armor dazzled the sun—the army's appearance was very grand.
entries.literal: On day dingchou, Ji halted at Xiling; warships crowded the river, banners and armor dazzled the sun—the army's appearance was very grand.

entries.zh: 世祖命護軍將軍陸法和於硤口夾岸築二壘，鎮江以斷之。
entries.en: Shizu ordered Protector General Lu Fahe to build two ramparts on both banks at the Gorge Mouth to hold the river and block him.
entries.literal: Shizu ordered Protector General Lu Fahe to build two ramparts on both banks at the Gorge Mouth to hold the river and block him.

entries.zh: 時陸納未平，蜀軍復逼，物情恇擾，世祖憂焉。
entries.en: At the time Lu Na was not yet pacified and the Shu army pressed again; public sentiment was alarmed and Shizu worried.
entries.literal: At the time Lu Na was not yet pacified and the Shu army pressed again; public sentiment was alarmed and Shizu worried.

entries.zh: 法和告急，旬日相繼。
entries.en: Lu Fahe's urgent reports came one after another for ten days.
entries.literal: Lu Fahe's urgent reports came one after another for ten days.

entries.zh: 世祖乃拔任約於獄，以爲晉安王司馬，撤禁兵以配之；
entries.en: Shizu then pulled Ren Yue from prison and made him Master of Affairs to Prince Jin'an, assigning palace guard troops to him;
entries.literal: Shizu then pulled Ren Yue from prison and made him Master of Affairs to Prince Jin'an, assigning palace guard troops to him;

entries.zh: 幷遣宣猛將軍劉棻共約西赴。
entries.en: and also sent Fierce Attack General Liu Fen to go west with Yue.
entries.literal: and also sent Fierce Attack General Liu Fen to go west with Yue.

entries.zh: 六月，紀築連城，攻絕鐵鏁。
entries.en: In the sixth month, Ji built linked ramparts and attacked, severing the iron chains.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, Ji built linked ramparts and attacked, severing the iron chains.

entries.zh: 世祖復於獄拔謝答仁爲步兵校尉，配衆一旅，上赴法和。
entries.en: Shizu again pulled Xie Daren from prison and made him Colonel of Footsoldiers, assigning him a brigade to go up and relieve Lu Fahe.
entries.literal: Shizu again pulled Xie Daren from prison and made him Colonel of Footsoldiers, assigning him a brigade to go up and relieve Lu Fahe.

entries.zh: 世祖與紀書曰：「皇帝敬問假黃鉞太尉武陵王：自九黎侵軼，三苗寇擾，天長喪亂，獯醜馮陵，虔劉象魏，黍離王室。
entries.en: Shizu wrote Ji a letter: "The Emperor respectfully inquires of the Acting Holder of the Yellow Battle-Axe, Grand Commandant, Prince of Wuling: Since the Nine Li raided our borders and the Three Miao harassed us, Heaven long abandoned order, barbarians pressed against the capital, devoutly laid waste to the realm, and the royal house knew the sorrows of millet and thorn—
entries.literal: Shizu wrote Ji a letter: "The Emperor respectfully inquires of the Acting Holder of the Yellow Battle-Axe, Grand Commandant, Prince of Wuling: Since the Nine Li raided our borders and the Three Miao harassed us, Heaven long abandoned order, barbarians pressed against the capital, devoutly laid waste to the realm, and the royal house knew the sorrows of millet and thorn—

entries.zh: 朕枕戈東望，泣血西浮，殞愛子於二方，無諸侯之八百，身被屬甲，手貫流矢。
entries.en: I sleep with my spear at my pillow looking east, weeping blood as I float west; I lost my beloved sons in two directions, without the eight hundred feudal lords; I wore armor myself and pierced flowing arrows with my hand.
entries.literal: I sleep with my spear at my pillow looking east, weeping blood as I float west; I lost my beloved sons in two directions, without the eight hundred feudal lords; I wore armor myself and pierced flowing arrows with my hand.

entries.zh: 俄而風樹之酷，萬恨始纏，霜露之悲，百憂繼集，扣心飲膽，志不圖全。
entries.en: suddenly the cruelty of wind and tree came—ten thousand hates first entwined; frost and dew griefs piled on by the hundred; I beat my heart and swallowed gall, my will no longer to preserve myself whole.
entries.literal: Suddenly the cruelty of wind and tree came—ten thousand hates first entwined; frost and dew griefs piled on by the hundred; I beat my heart and swallowed gall, my will no longer to preserve myself whole.

entries.zh: 直以宗社綴旒，鯨鯢未剪，嘗膽待旦，龔行天罰，獨運四聰，坐揮八柄。
entries.en: only because the altar and temple hang by a thread, the whale and crocodile are not yet cut down, I tasted gall awaiting dawn, marched Heaven's punishment, alone wielded the four keen ears, sat and commanded the eight handles.
entries.literal: Only because the altar and temple hang by a thread, the whale and crocodile are not yet cut down, I tasted gall awaiting dawn, marched Heaven's punishment, alone wielded the four keen ears, sat and commanded the eight handles.

entries.zh: 雖復結壇待將，褰帷納士，拒赤壁之兵，無謀於魯肅；
entries.en: though again I raised an altar awaiting generals, lifted the curtain to welcome scholars, and repelled the Red Cliffs army—without Lu Su's counsel;
entries.literal: Though again I raised an altar awaiting generals, lifted the curtain to welcome scholars, and repelled the Red Cliffs army—without Lu Su's counsel;

entries.zh: 燒烏巢之米，不訪於荀攸；
entries.en: burned the grain at Wuchao—without consulting Xun You;
entries.literal: burned the grain at Wuchao—without consulting Xun You;

entries.zh: 才智將殫，金貝殆竭，傍無寸助，險阻備嘗。
entries.en: talent and wisdom nearly spent, gold and shell nearly exhausted, not a fingerbreadth of aid beside me, dangers and hardships all tasted.
entries.literal: talent and wisdom nearly spent, gold and shell nearly exhausted, not a fingerbreadth of aid beside me, dangers and hardships all tasted.

entries.zh: 遂得斬長狄於駒門，挫蚩尤於楓木。
entries.en: yet I was able to behead the long Di at Jumen and humble Chiyou at Maplewood.
entries.literal: Yet I was able to behead the long Di at Jumen and humble Chiyou at Maplewood.

entries.zh: 怨恥旣雪，天下無塵，經營四方，專資一力，方與岳牧，同茲清靜。
entries.en: shame and grievance now washed, the realm without dust; I manage the four directions, relying on one strength alone; I shall with the peaks and pastors share this clarity and quiet.
entries.literal: Shame and grievance now washed, the realm without dust; I manage the four directions, relying on one strength alone; I shall with the peaks and pastors share this clarity and quiet.

entries.zh: 隆暑炎赫，弟比何如？
entries.en: in this fierce summer heat, how fares my younger brother?
entries.literal: In this fierce summer heat, how fares my younger brother?

entries.zh: 文武具僚，當有勞弊。
entries.en: civil and military officials must be worn and weary.
entries.literal: Civil and military officials must be worn and weary.

entries.zh: 今遣散騎常侍、光州刺史鄭安忠，指宣往懷。」
entries.en: now I send Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry and inspector of Guangzhou Zheng Anzhong to declare this and carry my embrace."
entries.literal: Now I send Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry and Inspector of Guangzhou Zheng Anzhong to declare this and carry my embrace."

entries.zh: 仍令喻意於紀，許其還蜀，專制岷方。
entries.en: he still had him convey his intent to Ji, promising his return to Shu and sole rule over Minfang.
entries.literal: He still had him convey his intent to Ji, promising his return to Shu and sole rule over Minfang.

entries.zh: 紀不從命，報書如家人禮。
entries.en: Ji refused and replied as between kin.
entries.literal: Ji would not obey and replied in the manner of family correspondence.

entries.zh: 庚申，紀將侯叡率衆緣山將規進取，任約、謝答仁與戰，破之。
entries.en: On gengshen day, Ji's general Hou Rui led men along the ridges to push forward; Ren Yue and Xie Daren met them in battle and broke them.
entries.literal: On gengshen day, Ji's general Hou Rui led troops along the mountains intending to advance and seize ground; Ren Yue and Xie Daren fought them and defeated them.

entries.zh: 旣而陸納平，諸軍並西赴，世祖又與紀書曰：「甚苦大智！
entries.en: Soon Lu Na was subdued and every army marched west; Emperor Yuan wrote again to Ji: "How you must suffer, Great Wisdom!
entries.literal: Shortly afterward Lu Na was pacified; all armies advanced west together, and Emperor Yuan again wrote to Ji: "Great hardship, Great Wisdom!

entries.zh: 季月煩暑，流金爍石，聚蚊成雷，封狐千里，以茲玉體，辛苦行陣。
entries.en: Late summer scorches until metal runs and stone glows; mosquitoes swarm like thunder and foxes haunt the hills for a thousand li—yet you wear this royal frame through the camps.
entries.literal: Late-season oppressive heat, flowing gold and burning stone, gathered mosquitoes becoming thunder, foxes in abundance for a thousand li—with this jade body, hard labor in the battle lines.

entries.zh: 乃眷西顧，我勞如何？
entries.en: I look west and wonder—what toll has this taken on me?
entries.literal: Turning my gaze west, what is my weariness?

entries.zh: 自獯醜憑陵，羯胡叛換，吾年爲一日之長，屬有平亂之功，膺此樂推，事歸當璧。
entries.en: Since the northern scourge overran the land and the Jie turned traitor, I am the elder by a day and was given the work of quelling chaos—heaven's choice fell to me, and the jade scepter is mine to hold.
entries.literal: Since the Xiongnu scoundrels overran the realm and the Jie barbarians rebelled and defected, I am a day older in years, and fate gave me the merit of pacifying disorder—bearing this willing elevation, the matter belongs to the one who should receive the jade disk.

entries.zh: 儻遣使乎，良所遲也。
entries.en: If you would send envoys, that is what I have waited for.
entries.literal: If you would send envoys, that is what I have long awaited.

entries.zh: 如曰不然，於此投筆。
entries.en: If not, I set down my brush here and say no more.
entries.literal: If you say otherwise, I lay down my brush here.

entries.zh: 友于兄弟，分形共氣。
entries.en: Brothers should be friends—one body, one breath.
entries.literal: Brotherly affection among brothers, shared form and common breath.

entries.zh: 兄肥弟瘦，無復相代之期；
entries.en: One brother grows stout while the other wastes away—we shall never take turns again;
entries.literal: The elder brother fat, the younger thin—no more season of taking turns;

entries.zh: 讓棗推梨，長罷歡愉之日。
entries.en: No more yielding jujubes or pushing pears—the days of shared delight are gone.
entries.literal: Yielding jujubes and pushing pears—forever ended days of joy.

entries.zh: 上林靜拱，聞四鳥之哀鳴；
entries.en: In Shanglin I sit in stillness and hear four birds cry in mourning;
entries.literal: In Shanglin Park, quietly seated, hearing the mournful cries of four birds;

entries.zh: 宣室披圖，嗟萬始之長逝。
entries.en: In the Xuan Chamber I unroll the maps and grieve that our Founder's life has long fled.
entries.literal: In the Xuan Chamber unrolling the scrolls, sighing at the Founder's long departure.

entries.zh: 心乎愛矣，書不盡言。」
entries.en: My heart is full of love, yet ink cannot say it all."
entries.literal: The heart loves indeed—the letter cannot exhaust the words."

entries.zh: 大智，紀之別字也。
entries.en: "Great Wisdom" was Ji's courtesy name.
entries.literal: Great Wisdom was Ji's alternate style.

entries.zh: 紀遣所署度支尚書樂奉業至于江陵，論和緝之計，依前旨還蜀。
entries.en: Ji sent his Minister of Revenue Le Fengye to Jiangling to negotiate peace and return to Shu on the old terms.
entries.literal: Ji sent his appointed Minister of Revenue Le Fengye to Jiangling to discuss plans for reconciliation, intending to return to Shu according to the earlier terms.

entries.zh: 世祖知紀必破，遂拒而不許。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan knew Ji was doomed and refused outright.
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan knew Ji would surely be defeated, and so refused and would not agree.

entries.zh: 丙戌，巴興民苻昇、徐子初等斬紀硤口城主公孫晃，降于衆軍。
entries.en: On bingxu day, Fu Sheng and Xu Zichu of Baxiing cut down Xiakou commander Gongsun Huang and surrendered to the host.
entries.literal: On bingxu day, the people of Baxiing Fu Sheng, Xu Zichu, and others beheaded Ji's Xiakou garrison commander Gongsun Huang and surrendered to the allied armies.

entries.zh: 王琳、宋簉、任約、謝答仁等因進攻侯叡，陷其三壘，於是兩岸十餘城遂俱降。
entries.en: Wang Lin, Song Zao, Ren Yue, and Xie Daren pressed Hou Rui, took his three ramparts, and more than ten cities on both shores submitted at once.
entries.literal: Wang Lin, Song Zao, Ren Yue, Xie Daren, and others then advanced against Hou Rui, captured his three forts, and more than ten cities on both banks then all surrendered.

entries.zh: 將軍樊猛獲紀及其第三子圓滿，俱殺之於硤口，時年四十六。
entries.en: General Fan Meng seized Ji and his third son Yuanman and killed them both at Xiakou; Ji was forty-six.
entries.literal: General Fan Meng captured Ji and his third son Yuanman, and both were killed at Xiakou—aged forty-six.

entries.zh: 有司奏請絕其屬籍，世祖許之，賜姓饕餮氏。
entries.en: The court memorialized to strike him from the clan register; Emperor Yuan assented and gave the surname Taotie.
entries.literal: The relevant offices memorialized requesting severance from the clan register; Emperor Yuan granted it and bestowed the surname Taotie.

entries.zh: 初，紀將僭號，妖怪非一。
entries.en: When Ji first planned to take the throne, omens multiplied.
entries.literal: At first, when Ji was about to usurp the title, portents were not one alone.

entries.zh: 其最異者，內寢柏殿柱繞節生花，其莖四十有六，靃靡可愛，狀似荷花。
entries.en: Strangest of all, in the Cypress Hall's inner chamber the pillars put forth flowers at every joint—forty-six stems, soft and lovely as lotus blooms.
entries.literal: The strangest: in the inner chamber of the Cypress Hall, nodes around pillar joints sprouted flowers—forty-six stems, luxuriant and lovely, shaped like lotus blossoms.

entries.zh: 識者曰：「王敦杖花，非佳事也。」
entries.en: Men versed in such things said, "When Wang Dun's staff bloomed, it foretold ruin."
entries.literal: Those who understood said: "When Wang Dun's staff flowered, it was no good sign."

entries.zh: 紀年號天正，與蕭棟暗合，僉曰「天」字「二人」也，「正」字「一止」也。
entries.en: Ji's reign era was Tianzheng, echoing Xiao Dong's in secret; people read tian as "two men" and zheng as "one halt."
entries.literal: Ji's era name was Tianzheng, covertly matching Xiao Dong's; all said the character tian means "two men," and zheng means "one stop."

entries.zh: 棟、紀僭號，各一年而滅。
entries.en: Dong and Ji each reigned a single year before they perished.
entries.literal: Dong and Ji each usurped titles for one year and were destroyed.

entries.zh: 豫章王綜字世謙，高祖第二子也。
entries.en: Prince Xiao Zong of Yuzhang, styled Shiqian, was Gaozu's second son.
entries.literal: Prince Xiao Zong of Yuzhang, styled Shiqian, was Gaozu's second son.

entries.zh: 天監三年，封豫章郡王，邑二千戶。
entries.en: In the third year of Tianjian he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yuzhang commandery, fief of two thousand households.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tianjian he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yuzhang commandery, fief of two thousand households.

entries.zh: 五年，出爲使持節、都督南徐州諸軍事、仁威將軍、南徐州刺史，尋進號北中郎將。
entries.en: In the fifth year he went out as bearer of the staff, commander of South Xuzhou military affairs, General of Benevolent Might, and inspector of South Xuzhou; soon he was advanced to North Central General.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he went out as Bearer of the Staff with discretionary powers, Commander of all military affairs of South Xuzhou, General of Benevolent Might, and Inspector of South Xuzhou; soon he was advanced to North Central General.

entries.zh: 十年，遷都督郢、司、霍三州諸軍事、雲麾將軍、郢州刺史。
entries.en: In the tenth year he was transferred to commander of E, Si, and Huo military affairs, Cloud Command General, and inspector of E.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Commander of military affairs of E, Si, and Huo provinces, Cloud Command General, and Inspector of E.

entries.zh: 十三年，遷安右將軍、領石頭戍軍事。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to Secure Right General, overseeing Stone Fort garrison affairs.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to Secure Right General, overseeing Stone Fort garrison affairs.

entries.zh: 十五年，遷西中郎將，兼護軍將軍，又遷安前將軍、丹陽尹。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to Western Central General, concurrently Protector General, then to Secure Front General and governor of Danyang.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to Western Central General, concurrently Protector General, then to Secure Front General and Governor of Danyang.

entries.zh: 十六年，復爲北中郎將、南徐州刺史。
entries.en: In the sixteenth year he again became North Central General and inspector of South Xuzhou.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year he again became North Central General and Inspector of South Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 普通二年，入爲侍中、鎮右將軍，置佐史。
entries.en: In the second year of Putong he entered court as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Secure Right General, with staff officers appointed.
entries.literal: In the second year of Putong he entered court as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Secure Right General, with staff officers appointed.

entries.zh: 初，其母吳淑媛自齊東昏宮得幸於高祖，七月而生綜，宮中多疑之者。
entries.en: At first his mother Lady Wu Shuyuan, favored by Gaozu after leaving the palace of Qi Emperor Dong Hun, gave birth to Zong in the seventh month; many in the palace doubted him.
entries.literal: At first his mother Lady Wu Shuyuan, favored by Gaozu after leaving the palace of Qi Emperor Dong Hun, gave birth to Zong in the seventh month; many in the palace doubted him.

entries.zh: 及淑媛寵衰怨望，遂陳疑似之說，故綜懷之。
entries.en: When Shuyuan's favor waned and she nursed resentment, she put forward the suspicion—and so Zong harbored it.
entries.literal: When Shuyuan's favor waned and she nursed resentment, she put forward the suspicion—and so Zong harbored it.

entries.zh: 旣長，有才學，善屬文。
entries.en: When grown he had talent in learning and skill in literary composition.
entries.literal: When grown he had talent in learning and skill in literary composition.

entries.zh: 高祖御諸子以禮，朝見不甚數，綜恒怨不見知。
entries.en: Gaozu governed his sons by ritual propriety and summoned them to court infrequently; Zong constantly resented that he was not recognized.
entries.literal: Gaozu governed his sons by ritual propriety and summoned them to court infrequently; Zong constantly resented that he was not recognized.

entries.zh: 每出籓，淑媛恒隨之鎮。
entries.en: Whenever he went out to a fief, Shuyuan always accompanied him to his post.
entries.literal: Whenever he went out to a fief, Shuyuan always accompanied him to his post.

entries.zh: 至年十五六，尚躶袒嬉戲於前，晝夜無別，內外咸有穢議。
entries.en: By fifteen or sixteen he still played naked before her, day and night undistinguished—inside and outside there was filthy talk.
entries.literal: By fifteen or sixteen he still played naked before her, day and night undistinguished—inside and outside there was filthy talk.

entries.zh: 綜在徐州，政刑酷暴。
entries.en: When Zong was in Xuzhou, his government and punishments were cruel and violent.
entries.literal: When Zong was in Xuzhou, his government and punishments were cruel and violent.

entries.zh: 又有勇力，手制奔馬。
entries.en: He also had courage and strength, and could by hand subdue a galloping horse.
entries.literal: He also had courage and strength, and could by hand subdue a galloping horse.

entries.zh: 常微行夜出，無有期度。
entries.en: He often went out in disguise at night, without any fixed schedule.
entries.literal: He often went out in disguise at night, without any fixed schedule.

entries.zh: 每高祖有敕疏至，輒忿恚形於顏色，羣臣莫敢言者。
entries.en: Whenever Gaozu's edicts or letters arrived, rage showed on his face; no minister dared speak.
entries.literal: Whenever Gaozu's edicts or letters arrived, rage showed on his face; no minister dared speak.

entries.zh: 恒於別室祠齊氏七廟，又微服至曲阿拜齊明帝陵。
entries.en: He constantly worshipped the Qi line's seven ancestral temples in a separate chamber, and in plain dress went to Qu'e to pay respects at Emperor Ming of Qi's tomb.
entries.literal: He constantly worshipped the Qi line's seven ancestral temples in a separate chamber, and in plain dress went to Qu'e to pay respects at Emperor Ming of Qi's tomb.

entries.zh: 然猶無以自信，聞俗說以生者血瀝死者骨，滲，卽爲父子。
entries.en: Yet he still could not trust himself; he heard a folk saying that if living blood dripped on a dead man's bone and seeped in, they were father and son.
entries.literal: Yet he still could not trust himself; he heard a folk saying that if living blood dripped on a dead man's bone and seeped in, they were father and son.

entries.zh: 綜乃私發齊東昏墓，出骨，瀝臂血試之。
entries.en: Zong then privately opened the tomb of Dong Hun of Qi, took out the bone, and dripped blood from his arm to test it.
entries.literal: Zong then privately opened the tomb of Dong Hun of Qi, took out the bone, and dripped blood from his arm to test it.

entries.zh: 幷殺一男，取其骨試之，皆有驗，自此常懷異志。
entries.en: He also killed a boy and tested with his bone—the results all matched; from then he constantly harbored disloyal intent.
entries.literal: He also killed a boy and tested with his bone—the results all matched; from then he constantly harbored disloyal intent.

entries.zh: 中大通四年，爲信武將軍、吳郡太守。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Zhongdatong he served as Trustworthy Martial General and administrator of Wu commandery.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Zhongdatong he was Trustworthy Martial General and Administrator of Wu commandery.

entries.zh: 徵爲侍中、撫軍將軍，置佐史，封臨賀郡王，邑二千戶，又加左衛將軍。
entries.en: He was recalled as Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Pacifies the Army, enfeoffed Prince of Linhe with two thousand households, and made Left Guard General besides.
entries.literal: He was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the Army with staff, enfeoffed as Prince of Linhe commandery with two thousand households, and additionally made Left Guard General.

entries.zh: 而凶暴日甚，招聚亡命。
entries.en: His cruelty deepened by the day as he gathered fugitives and desperate men.
entries.literal: Yet his ferocity and violence grew daily worse; he gathered fugitives and outlaws.

entries.zh: 侯景知其有姦心，乃密令誘說，厚相要結。
entries.en: Hou Jing sensed his treachery and secretly wooed him with lavish pledges.
entries.literal: Hou Jing knew he had treacherous intent and secretly sent men to entice and persuade him, binding him with rich promises.

entries.zh: 遺正德書曰：「今天子年尊，姦臣亂國，憲章錯謬，政令顛倒，以景觀之，計日必敗。
entries.en: He wrote to Zhengde: "The Son of Heaven is old, corrupt ministers ruin the realm, law and order are upside down—in my reading, collapse comes within days.
entries.literal: He sent Zhengde a letter: "Today the Son of Heaven is aged, wicked ministers disorder the state, statutes err and edicts overturn—from Jing's view, defeat is counted in days.

entries.zh: 況大王屬當儲貳，中被廢辱，天下義士，竊所痛心，在景愚忠，能無忿慨？
entries.en: You were born to the succession yet cast aside in shame—righteous men everywhere ache at it; can even my blunt loyalty stay cold?
entries.literal: Moreover the Great King by lineage should be heir, mid-course cast down in disgrace—the world's men of righteousness all secretly grieve; can Jing's dull loyalty fail to burn with indignation?

entries.zh: 今四海業業，歸心大王，大王豈得顧此私情，棄茲億兆！
entries.en: The realm trembles and hearts turn to you—will you choose private feeling over a hundred million lives?
entries.literal: Now the four seas tremble in fear and hearts turn to the Great King—can the Great King cling to private feeling and abandon these hundred millions!

entries.zh: 景雖不武，實思自奮。
entries.en: I am no soldier, yet I mean to fight.
entries.literal: Though Jing is no warrior, he truly means to rouse himself.

entries.zh: 願王允副蒼生，鑒斯誠款。」
entries.en: Grant my plea, serve the people, and read this as honest intent."
entries.literal: May the King grant this and match the people's need—discern this sincere pledge."

entries.zh: 正德覽書大喜曰：「侯景意暗與我同，此天贊也。」
entries.en: Zhengde read it and exulted: "Hou Jing thinks as I do—Heaven is with us."
entries.literal: Zhengde read the letter and rejoiced greatly: "Hou Jing's intent secretly matches mine—Heaven approves."

entries.zh: 遂許之。
entries.en: He agreed.
entries.literal: He then agreed.

entries.zh: 及景至江，正德潛運空舫，詐稱迎荻，以濟景焉。
entries.en: When Jing reached the river, Zhengde sent empty boats under the pretense of collecting reeds and ferried him across.
entries.literal: When Jing reached the Yangtze, Zhengde secretly dispatched empty boats, falsely claiming to gather reeds, to ferry Jing across.

entries.zh: 朝廷未知其謀，猶遣正德守朱雀航。
entries.en: The court still knew nothing of the plot and sent Zhengde to hold the Zhuque crossing.
entries.literal: The court did not yet know his plot and still sent Zhengde to guard the Zhuque Bridge crossing.

entries.zh: 景至，正德乃引軍與景俱進，景推正德爲天子，改年爲正平元年，景爲丞相。
entries.en: Jing came; Zhengde opened the gates and marched with him. Jing proclaimed Zhengde emperor, named the era Zhengping year one, and took the chancellorship himself.
entries.literal: When Jing arrived, Zhengde led his army to advance with Jing; Jing set up Zhengde as Son of Heaven, changed the era to Zhengping year one, and made himself Chancellor.

entries.zh: 臺城沒，復太清之號，降正德爲大司馬。
entries.en: When the palace city fell, the Taiqing era was restored and Zhengde was reduced to Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: When the capital fortress fell, the Taiqing era name was restored and Zhengde was demoted to Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 正德有怨言，景聞之，慮其爲變，矯詔殺之。
entries.en: Zhengde grumbled; Jing, fearing betrayal, forged an edict and had him killed.
entries.literal: Zhengde had resentful words; Jing heard and, fearing he might turn, forged an edict and killed him.

entries.zh: 臨賀王正德字公和，臨川靖惠王第三子也。
entries.en: Prince of Linhe Zhengde, styled Gonghe, was the third son of Prince Jinghui of Linchuan.
entries.literal: Prince of Linhe Zhengde, styled Gonghe, was the third son of Prince Jinghui of Linchuan.

entries.zh: 少粗險，不拘禮節。
entries.en: As a youth he was rough and reckless and cared nothing for propriety.
entries.literal: In youth he was coarse and dangerous, not bound by ritual propriety.

entries.zh: 初，高祖未有男，養之爲子。
entries.en: Early on, before Gaozu had a son of his own, he adopted Zhengde.
entries.literal: At first, when Gaozu had no sons, he adopted him as a son.

entries.zh: 及高祖踐極，便希儲貳，後立昭明太子，封正德爲西豊侯，邑五百戶。
entries.en: Once Gaozu took the throne, Zhengde coveted the heirship; when the Zhaoming Heir Apparent was named, Zhengde received only the marquisate of Xifeng—five hundred households.
entries.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Zhengde at once hoped for the heirship; later when the Zhaoming Heir Apparent was established, Zhengde was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xifeng with five hundred households.

entries.zh: 自此怨望，恒懷不軌，䁹睨宮扆，覬幸災變。
entries.en: Thereafter he brooded on slights, plotted treason, eyed the palace throne, and prayed for disaster.
entries.literal: From then he nursed resentment, constantly harboring rebellious intent, casting sidelong glances at the palace throne, hoping for calamity and change.

entries.zh: 普通六年，以黃門侍郎爲輕車將軍，置佐史。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Putong he rose from Gentleman at the Yellow Gate to General of Light Chariots with a staff.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Putong, as Gentleman in Attendance at the Yellow Gate he became General of Light Chariots with a staff.

entries.zh: 頃之，遂逃奔于魏，有司奏削封爵。
entries.en: Soon he fled to Wei; the court moved to strip his rank and fief.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he fled to Wei; the relevant offices memorialized to strip his titles and fiefs.

entries.zh: 七年，又自魏逃歸，高祖不之過也。
entries.en: In the seventh year he slipped back from Wei; Gaozu let the matter pass.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he again fled back from Wei; Gaozu did not punish him.

entries.zh: 復其封爵，仍除征虜將軍。
entries.en: His honors were restored and he was made General Who Pacifies the Barbarians.
entries.literal: His titles and fiefs were restored, and he was additionally made General Who Pacifies the Barbarians.

entries.zh: 四年，出爲使持節、都督南兗兗徐青冀五州諸軍事、平北將軍、南兗州刺史，給鼓吹一部。
entries.en: In the fourth year he went out as bearer of the staff, commander of South Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji military affairs, Pacification North General, and inspector of South Yan, granted one suite of martial music.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he went out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander of military affairs of South Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji provinces, Pacification North General, and Inspector of South Yan, granted one suite of martial music.

entries.zh: 聞齊建安王蕭寶寅在魏，遂使人入北與之相知，謂爲叔父，許舉鎮歸之。
entries.en: Hearing that Xiao Baoyin, Prince of Jian'an of Qi, was in Wei, he sent men north to establish contact, called him uncle, and promised to raise his post in surrender to him.
entries.literal: Hearing that Xiao Baoyin, Prince of Jian'an of Qi, was in Wei, he sent men north to establish contact, called him uncle, and promised to raise his post in surrender to him.

entries.zh: 會大舉北伐。
entries.en: It happened that a great northern campaign was mounted.
entries.literal: It happened that a great northern campaign was mounted.

entries.zh: 六年，魏將元法僧以彭城降，高祖乃令綜都督衆軍，鎮于彭城，與魏將安豊王元延明相持。
entries.en: In the sixth year, Wei general Yuan Faseng surrendered Pengcheng; Gaozu then had Zong command the armies, garrison at Pengcheng, and stand off against Wei general Prince Yuan Yanming of Anfeng.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, Wei general Yuan Faseng surrendered Pengcheng; Gaozu then had Zong command the armies, garrison at Pengcheng, and stand off against Wei general Prince Yuan Yanming of Anfeng.

entries.zh: 高祖以連兵旣久，慮有釁生，敕綜退軍。
entries.en: Gaozu, because the campaign had dragged on, feared trouble would arise and ordered Zong to withdraw the army.
entries.literal: Gaozu, because the campaign had dragged on, feared trouble would arise and ordered Zong to withdraw the army.

entries.zh: 綜懼南歸則無因復與寶寅相見，乃與數騎夜奔于延明，魏以爲侍中、太尉、高平公、丹陽王，邑七千戶，錢三百萬，布絹三千匹，雜彩千匹，馬五十匹，羊五百口，奴婢一百人。
entries.en: Zong feared that returning south would leave him no chance to see Baoyin again; with several horsemen he fled by night to Yanming. Wei made him Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Commandant, Duke of Gaoping, Prince of Danyang, fief of seven thousand households, three million cash, three thousand bolts of cloth and silk, one thousand bolts of mixed brocade, fifty horses, five hundred sheep, and a hundred male and female servants.
entries.literal: Zong feared that returning south would leave him no chance to see Baoyin again; with several horsemen he fled by night to Yanming. Wei made him Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Commandant, Duke of Gaoping, Prince of Danyang, fief of seven thousand households, three million cash, three thousand bolts of cloth and silk, one thousand bolts of mixed brocade, fifty horses, five hundred sheep, and a hundred male and female servants.

entries.zh: 綜乃改名纘，字德文，追爲齊東昏服斬衰。
entries.en: Zong then changed his name to Zuan, styled Dewen, and went into the one-year mourning hemp for Dong Hun of Qi.
entries.literal: Zong then changed his name to Zuan, styled Dewen, and went into the one-year mourning hemp for Dong Hun of Qi.

entries.zh: 於是有司奏削爵土，絕屬籍，改其姓爲悖氏。
