entries.en: Thereupon the relevant offices memorialized to strip his rank and fief, cut him from the genealogical register, and change his surname to the Bo clan.
entries.literal: Thereupon the relevant offices memorialized to strip his rank and fief, cut him from the genealogical register, and change his surname to the Bo clan.

entries.zh: 俄有詔復之，封其子直爲永新侯，邑千戶。
entries.en: Soon an edict restored him; his son Zhi was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongxin, fief of a thousand households.
entries.literal: Soon an edict restored him; his son Zhi was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongxin, fief of a thousand households.

entries.zh: 大通二年，蕭寶寅在魏據長安反，綜自洛陽北遁，將赴之，爲津吏所執，魏人殺之，時年四十九。
entries.en: In the second year of Datong, Xiao Baoyin held Chang'an in rebellion within Wei; Zuan fled north from Luoyang intending to join him, was seized by the ferry clerk, and the Wei people killed him—aged forty-nine.
entries.literal: In the second year of Datong, Xiao Baoyin held Chang'an in rebellion within Wei; Zuan fled north from Luoyang intending to join him, was seized by the ferry clerk, and the Wei people killed him—aged forty-nine.

entries.zh: 未幾，侯景寇京邑，譽率軍入援，至青草湖，臺城沒，有詔班師，譽還湘鎮。
entries.en: Soon Hou Jing struck the capital; Yu marched to relieve it, reached Qingcao Lake, then heard the city had fallen, received orders to withdraw, and returned to his post in Xiang.
entries.literal: Before long Hou Jing raided the capital; Yu led troops to rescue, reached Qingcao Lake; the fortress fell, an edict ordered withdrawal, and Yu returned to his Xiang post.

entries.zh: 時世祖軍于武城，新除雍州刺史張纘密報世祖曰：「河東起兵，岳陽聚米，共爲不逞，將襲江陵。」
entries.en: Emperor Yuan was then at Wucheng; the new inspector of Yongzhou, Zhang Zuan, secretly warned him: "Hedong has risen and Yueyang is hoarding grain—they plot mischief and mean to strike Jiangling."
entries.literal: At the time Emperor Yuan's army was at Wucheng; the newly appointed Inspector of Yongzhou Zhang Zuan secretly reported to Emperor Yuan: "Hedong has raised troops and Yueyang is stockpiling grain—together they are unrestrained and will strike Jiangling."

entries.zh: 世祖甚懼，因步道間還，遣諮議周弘直至譽所，督其糧衆。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan was terrified; he slipped back by side roads and sent Adviser Zhou Hongzhi to Yu's camp to take command of grain and troops.
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan was greatly afraid; he returned by land routes, sent Adviser Zhou Hongzhi to Yu's headquarters to oversee his grain and troops.

entries.zh: 譽曰：「各自軍府，何忽隸人？」
entries.en: Yu said, "Each man has his own command—why suddenly place me under another?"
entries.literal: Yu said: "Each has his own army headquarters—why suddenly make one subordinate to another?"

entries.zh: 前後使三反，譽並不從。
entries.en: Three envoys came and went; Yu refused each time.
entries.literal: Envoys went back and forth three times; Yu would not obey.

entries.zh: 世祖大怒，乃遣世子方等征之，反爲譽所敗死。
entries.en: Enraged, Emperor Yuan sent his heir Fangdeng against him; Yu defeated and killed him.
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan in great anger sent the Heir Fangdeng to campaign against him; instead Fangdeng was defeated and killed by Yu.

entries.zh: 又令信州刺史鮑泉討譽，幷與書陳示禍福，許其遷善。
entries.en: He then ordered Bao Quan, inspector of Xinzhou, to attack Yu, writing to show reward and ruin and offering a path to repentance.
entries.literal: He again ordered Inspector of Xinzhou Bao Quan to attack Yu, and with a letter set forth fortune and disaster, promising he could turn to good.

entries.zh: 譽不答，修浚城池，爲拒守之計。
entries.en: Yu made no answer; he strengthened walls and moats and prepared to stand siege.
entries.literal: Yu did not reply; he repaired and dredged the walls and moats, planning to resist and hold.

entries.zh: 謂鮑泉曰：「敗軍之將，勢豈語勇？
entries.en: He told Bao Quan, "A beaten general has no right to speak of courage.
entries.literal: He said to Bao Quan: "A defeated general—where is the talk of bravery?

entries.zh: 欲前卽前，無所多說。」
entries.en: Advance if you will—say no more."
entries.literal: If you wish to advance, advance—nothing more need be said."

entries.zh: 泉軍于石槨寺，譽帥衆逆擊之，不利而還。
entries.en: Quan camped at Shigu Temple; Yu led a counterattack, failed, and pulled back.
entries.literal: Quan encamped at Shigu Temple; Yu led troops to strike him head-on, did not succeed and withdrew.

entries.zh: 泉進軍于橘洲，譽又盡銳攻之，不剋。
entries.en: Quan moved on Juzhou; Yu threw in every crack soldier and still could not break him.
entries.literal: Quan advanced to Juzhou; Yu again attacked with all his elite troops and could not overcome him.

entries.zh: 會已暮，士卒疲弊，泉因出擊，大敗之，斬首三千級，溺死者萬餘人。
entries.en: At dusk, with Yu's men spent, Quan counterstruck and shattered them—three thousand heads taken and more than ten thousand drowned.
entries.literal: When evening came the soldiers were worn and exhausted; Quan then sallied forth and routed them—three thousand heads cut, over ten thousand drowned.

entries.zh: 譽於是焚長沙郭邑，驅居民於城內，鮑泉度軍圍之。
entries.en: Yu burned Changsha's outer suburbs, herded the people within the walls, and Bao Quan brought his army across to invest the city.
entries.literal: Yu then burned the outer walls of Changsha, drove the residents inside the city, and Bao Quan crossed the army to besiege it.

entries.zh: 譽幼而驍勇，兼有膽氣，能撫循士卒，甚得衆心。
entries.en: Yu had been bold since boyhood, fearless and skilled at winning soldiers' hearts.
entries.literal: Yu from youth was fierce and brave, possessed daring as well; he could comfort and lead soldiers and greatly won the troops' hearts.

entries.zh: 及被圍旣久，雖外內斷絕，而備守猶固。
entries.en: Besieged for months, cut off within and without, he still held firm.
entries.literal: Though besieged long, though inner and outer were cut off, defenses and holding remained firm.

entries.zh: 後世祖又遣領軍將軍王僧辯代鮑泉攻譽，僧辯築土山以臨城內，日夕苦攻，矢石如雨，城中將士死傷者太半。
entries.en: Later Shizu also sent Commandant of the Army Wang Sengbian to replace Bao Quan in attacking Yu. Sengbian raised earthworks overlooking the city and assaulted bitterly day and night until arrows and stones fell like rain and more than half the soldiers in the city were dead or wounded.
entries.literal: Later Emperor Yuan again sent Commandant of the Army Wang Sengbian to replace Bao Quan in attacking Yu; Sengbian built earthen mounds overlooking the inner city, attacked bitterly day and night—arrows and stones like rain—more than half the officers and soldiers in the city were killed or wounded.

entries.zh: 譽窘急，乃潛裝海船，將潰圍而出。
entries.en: Desperate, Yu secretly prepared sea boats to burst the siege and flee.
entries.literal: Yu in dire straits secretly fitted out sea boats, intending to break the siege and escape.

entries.zh: 會其麾下將慕容華引僧辯入城，譽顧左右皆散，遂被執，謂守者曰：「勿殺我！
entries.en: Then his officer Murong Hua admitted Sengbian into the city; Yu's followers scattered and he was taken. He cried to his guards, "Do not kill me!
entries.literal: Just then his subordinate general Murong Hua led Sengbian into the city; Yu looked—his attendants had all scattered—he was seized, and said to his guards: "Do not kill me!

entries.zh: 得一見七官，申此讒賊，死亦無恨。」
entries.en: Let me see the Seventh Officer once and denounce this slanderer—then I can die without regret."
entries.literal: Let me see the Seventh Officer once and expose this slanderous villain—even death would hold no regret."

entries.zh: 主者曰：「奉命不許。」
entries.en: The officer said, "My orders forbid it."
entries.literal: The officer in charge said: "By order it is not permitted."

entries.zh: 遂斬之，傳首荊鎮，世祖反其首以葬焉。
entries.en: He was beheaded; the head was sent to the Jing garrison, and Emperor Yuan returned it for burial.
entries.literal: He was then beheaded; the head was sent to the Jing post and Emperor Yuan returned the head for burial.

entries.zh: 河東王譽字重孫，昭明太子第二子也。
entries.en: Prince of Hedong Yu, styled Chongsun, was the second son of the Zhaoming Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: Prince of Hedong Yu, styled Chongsun, was the Zhaoming Heir Apparent's second son.

entries.zh: 普通二年，封枝江縣公。
entries.en: In the second year of Putong he was made Duke of Zhijiang county.
entries.literal: In the second year of Putong he was enfeoffed as Duke of Zhijiang county.

entries.zh: 中大通三年，改封河東郡王，邑二千戶。
entries.en: In the third year of Zhongdatong he was re-enfeoffed Prince of Hedong commandery with two thousand households.
entries.literal: In the third year of Zhongdatong his fief was changed to Prince of Hedong commandery with two thousand households.

entries.zh: 除寧遠將軍、石頭戍軍事。
entries.en: He was appointed General of Distant Peace and put in charge of the Shitou garrison.
entries.literal: He was made General of Distant Peace and charged with the garrison affairs at Shitou.

entries.zh: 出爲琅邪、彭城二郡太守。
entries.en: He went out to govern Langye and Pengcheng commanderies.
entries.literal: He went out as Administrator of the two commanderies Langye and Pengcheng.

entries.zh: 還除侍中、輕車將軍，置佐史。
entries.en: On return he became Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of Light Chariots with a staff.
entries.literal: Returning he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Light Chariots with staff.

entries.zh: 出爲南中郎將、湘州刺史。
entries.en: He went out as General of the Southern Center and inspector of Xiangzhou.
entries.literal: He went out as General of the Southern Center and Inspector of Xiangzhou.

entries.zh: 梁書卷第五十五 列傳第四十九
entries.en: Book of Liang, Volume 55, Biography 49
entries.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 55, Biography 49

entries.zh: 太祖耶律阿保機上
entries.en: Annals of Taizu Yelü Abaoji, Part One
entries.literal: Taizu Yelü Abaoji, Part One

entries.zh: 太祖大聖大明神烈天皇帝，姓耶律氏，諱億，字阿保機，小字啜里只，契丹迭剌部霞瀨益石烈鄉耶律彌里人。
entries.en: Taizu, styled the Great Sage and Bright Divine Martial Heavenly Emperor, bore the surname Yelü; his given name was Yi, his courtesy name Abaoji, and his childhood name Chuilizhi. He came from Yelü Mili in the Xiasiyishi Lie of the Khitan Diela branch.
entries.literal: The Taizu, Great Sage, Great Brightness, Divine Martial, Heavenly Emperor — surname Yelü, taboo name Yi, courtesy name Abaoji, childhood name Chuilizhi — was a native of Yelü Mili village, Xiasiyishi Lie, Diela Department of the Khitan.

entries.zh: 德祖皇帝長子，母曰宣簡皇后蕭氏。
entries.en: He was the eldest son of Emperor Dezu, born to Empress Xuanjian of the Xiao clan.
entries.literal: He was the eldest son of Emperor Dezu; his mother was Empress Xuanjian, née Xiao.

entries.zh: 唐咸通十三年生。
entries.en: He was born in the thirteenth year of Emperor Yizong's Xiantong era (872).
entries.literal: He was born in the thirteenth year of the Tang Xiantong reign.

entries.zh: 初，母夢日墮懷中，有娠。
entries.en: Before his birth, his mother dreamed that the sun dropped into her breast, and afterward she became pregnant.
entries.literal: At the beginning, his mother dreamed that the sun fell into her bosom, and she conceived.

entries.zh: 及生，室有神光異香，體如三歲兒，即能匍匐。
entries.en: At his birth, divine light filled the room and a strange fragrance hung in the air. His body was already like a three-year-old's, and he could crawl immediately.
entries.literal: When he was born, the room had divine light and strange fragrance; his body was like that of a three-year-old child, and he could crawl at once.

entries.zh: 祖母簡獻皇后異之，鞠為己子。
entries.en: His grandmother Empress Jianxian took him for a prodigy and raised him as if he were her own child.
entries.literal: His grandmother, Empress Jianxian, regarded him as extraordinary and reared him as her own son.

entries.zh: 常匿於別幕，塗其面，不令他人見。
entries.en: She kept him hidden in a separate tent, darkened his face with ash, and forbade anyone else to look upon him.
entries.literal: She often hid him in a separate tent, smeared his face, and did not allow others to see him.

entries.zh: 三月能行；
entries.en: By three months he could walk;
entries.literal: At three months he could walk;

entries.zh: 而能言，知未然事。
entries.en: and soon he could speak and foretell events yet to come.
entries.literal: and he could speak, and knew things before they happened.

entries.zh: 自謂左右若有神人翼衛。
entries.en: He said that divine guardians seemed to hover at his sides, winged and vigilant.
entries.literal: He claimed that on his left and right there seemed to be divine beings guarding him with wings.

entries.zh: 雖齠齔，言必及世務。
entries.en: Even as a child with baby teeth, he spoke always of public affairs.
entries.literal: Although he was still in childhood, his words always touched upon affairs of state.

entries.zh: 時伯父當國，疑輒咨焉。
entries.en: His uncle then governed the Khitan, and whenever uncertain he sought the boy's counsel.
entries.literal: At that time his uncle held power over the state; whenever in doubt he would consult him.

entries.zh: 既長，身長九尺，豐上銳下，目光射人，關弓三百斤。
entries.en: Grown to manhood, he stood nine chi in height — broad-shouldered above, lean below — with a gaze that struck men like an arrow and strength enough to draw a three-hundred-jin bow.
entries.literal: When he had grown up, he stood nine chi tall, broad above and tapering below; his gaze pierced people, and he could draw a bow of three hundred jin.

entries.zh: 為撻馬狘沙里。
entries.en: He held the office of tamagh boshuli.
entries.literal: He served as tamagh boshuli.

entries.zh: 時小黃室韋不附，太祖以計降之。
entries.en: When the Lesser Yellow Shiwei refused submission, Taizu took them by strategy.
entries.literal: At that time the Lesser Yellow Shiwei did not submit; Taizu subdued them by stratagem.
